Kao Corporation is a consumer products company, manufacturing beauty care, human health care, fabric and home care, and chemical products, for both industrial and consumer markets.  Founded in 1887, the company is headquartered in Japan. Kao Corporation has a global presence, although its operations are most heavily concentrated in Asia. In 2014, 67% of sales occurred in Japan.
The company's Beauty Care business encompasses a wide range of cosmetics, including skin and hair care products under a number of global brands such as Molton Brown and John Frieda. The Human Health Care business is primarily focused on the sanitary napkin brand, Laurier, which is sold in Asia, and the disposable diaper brand, Merries, which is also primarily targeted at the Japanese consumer market. The Fabric and Home Care business manufactures products such as laundry detergents and household cleaners for Asian and Japanese consumer market. The Chemical business manufactures products for a diverse range of industries, including paper and pulp, food products, pharmaceutical products, engineering and electronics. Kao Corporation uses palm and palm kernel oil as a raw material, using 96,100 tonnes of palm oil in 2013/14. Pulp is also used in the manufacture of its products.

Nestle is a Swiss food manufacturer with more than 2,000 brands being sold in more than 185 countries. Its products include beverages, confectionary, chilled foods, nutrition and pet care with well-known brands such as Maggi, KitKat, Milo and Nescafe. The company is a major manufacturer and retailer of packaged foods in Indonesia, Brazil the US and Western Europe. Its products also use a high amount of palm oil, with over 400,000 metric tons of palm oil and palm oil derivatives being used in 2015.

News Corporation (News Corp) is a media conglomerate with a network of companies in media, news, education and information services. In June 2013, News Corp's shareholders gave formal approval for the company to split its publishing and entertainment divisions, creating two new companies: News Corp, housing the company's publishing segment; 21st Century Fox housing the entertainment division. News Corp is now specifically a publishing company, producing newspaper, magazines, books and promotional inserts and coupons. The company was established in Australia in 1954, when Rupert Murdoch took control of the Australian corporation, News Limited, which had a majority interest in one of Adelaide's top daily newspapers. Since then, the company has grown dramatically and acquired numerous assets, beginning with newspapers in the UK: 'The Sun' and 'News of the World.' Established in Australia, News Corp is now based in the US and is the largest newspaper publishing company globally.
As of 2014, News Corp is comprised of the following businesses, with each housing several brands: News Corp Australia, News UK, Dow Jones & Company, New York Post, Harper Collins Publishers, Amplify, News America Marketing, and Storyful. News Corp Australia, for example, claims to be Australia's leading media and publishing company, selling over 10 million papers weekly, with titles including The Daily Telegraph, The Australian, and Herald Sun. News UK also publishes some of the UK's most well-known newspapers, including The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times. Dow Jones & Company publishes The Wall Street Journal and specialises in the provision of news and business information via a variety of media outlets.  Finally, News Corp's subsidiary HarperCollins is one of the world's most prominent book publishing companies. In May 2014, HarperCollins acquired book publisher Harlequin; the acquisition of the Canadian company is the biggest deal in book publishing since the merger of two other publishing giants, Penguin and Random House in 2013.

Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (Reckitt Benckiser) manufactures and markets a wide range of branded home, health and personal care products. The group comprises around 60 companies and sells its products in nearly 200 countries, giving it a global presence. The company markets products under several well-known brands, including health products, such as Strepsils, Gaviscon and Nurofen; hygiene products Clearasil, Dettol, and Harpic; and home products, Calgon and Vanish.
Reckitt Benckiser is headquartered in the UK and has its origins in the 1800s, when Benckiser was founded in 1823. However, Reckitt Benckiser in its current form was established in 1999 through a merger between Reckitt & Colman and Benckiser. Since then, the company has undergone rapid expansion, with numerous acquisitions, including Korean household company Oxy in 2000; over-the-counter healthcare business, Boots Healthcare International, in 2006; and SSL International in 2010. More recently, in 2013, Reckitt Benckiser further strengthened its global position through collaboration with Bristol-Myers Squibb, a leading health company in Brazil and Mexico, and the acquisition of Manyanshuning, China's leading sore throat brand.
The company is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil and reported the use of around 107,000 MT of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. Palm oil is used principally in the company's manufacturing of home and personal care goods, for example, in cleaning agents, laundry detergents, and soap tablets.

initiatives: SOY " To demonstrate that the soya we procure is sourced responsibly, our partner Proforest undertakes site assessments against our requirements. We accept certification against approved sustainability schemes and initiatives that are consistent with our requirements. For example, we consider the use of credits from the Roundtable on Responsible Soy (RTRS) – a multi-stakeholder initiative that aims to facilitate a global dialogue on economically viable, socially equitable and environmentally sound soya production – to be an interim solution until assessments can be more widely deployed. We also accept traceable soy from smallholders and growers who have an action plan and timeline in place for meeting our requirements." (http://www.nestle.com/asset-library/documents/library/documents/corporate_social_responsibility/nestle-csv-full-report-2014-en.pdf, page 115) The Soy policy does not seem to require all of its suppliers follow its policy - "We also accept traceable soy", especially when compared to the other two policies (palm and pulp and paper) and how explicit they are. 2/3 policies therefore gets awarded 3/4 points.

Mars Inc. (Mars) is a global leader in the confectionery industry, and also a significant player in the market for dried processed foods, sauces and condiments. The company was originally founded in 1891, and has its origins in the confectionery business, for which it remains most well-known. Headquartered in the state of Virginia in the US, Mars is the third largest private company in the America and employs over 65,000 'associates.' These associates work in 230 locations and factories in 68 countries worldwide. The company's operations are divided between six divisions: pet care products, chocolate, a variety of packaged food, chewing gum and candy under the Wrigley business segment, drinks and finally, scientific research under Mars Symbioscience.
Mars manufactures goods under numerous well-known global brands, including ready meal brands, Uncle Ben's and Suzi Wan, and chocolates brands including Maltesers, Bounty, Galaxy, M&Ms, Twix, Snickers and many more.  Mars sources a variety of raw materials to manufacture its diverse product range. Several forest risk commodities are among these, including beef, which comprises 3.6% of Mars' raw materials purchased by volume, as well as palm oil, soya and pulp and paper. In 2012/2013, Mars reported use of over 77,000 tonnes of palm oil, making its palm oil consumption higher than many other manufacturers.
Mars continues to increase its manufacturing capacity, opening a new $270 million chocolate plant in Kansas, America.  The company is also aiming to improve its market position in petcare through the planned acquisition of the IAMS, Eukanuba and Natura brands from Procter and Gamble for $2.9 billion. The company is also strong in its research and development with a new £6 million facility in Slough, United Kingdom that opened in 2012.

Marks & Spencer Group PLC is the holding company for the Marks & Spencer Group (M&S). The company was established in 1884 as a single market stall in Leeds, UK and has since become a leading UK retailer, with 852 stores in the UK and a further 480 internationally in 59 territories. The company employs over 83,000 individuals. Further to this, M&S sells products online and through its franchise partners.
M&S sells a range of products, including food, homeware, and clothing for men, women and children, which it sources from around 2,000 suppliers globally. In the UK, the food segment comprises the majority of total sales, accounting for 57%, with the remainder made up of the general merchandise department. M&S' food division sells around 6,300 products, from everyday products, such as under the 'Simply M&S' brand range, to food for special occasions.
As a retailer, M&S is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. Palm oil and soya are found in some M&S food products. For example, palm oil and its derivatives are used as a vegetable oil, as a coating for dried fruit, and as a carrier for flavourings. The company also sells beef and has a commitment to source this commodity as well as palm oil and soya from sources that do not contribute to deforestation. Within M&S' women's and men's departments, the company sells a number of leather goods, such as leather boots and bags. M&S is also involved in the wood products industry and stocks a range of furniture items, including wooden garden furniture.

The Danone Group was formed following the merger of BSN and Gervais Danone in 1972; however, the company's origins can be traced back to Spain, where Danone was founded in 1919 in Barcelona, specialising in yogurt products to treat intestinal disorders. The company then expanded to France and the US. BSN was founded later in 1966, and following a series of acquisitions became a top producer of mineral water, beer and baby food. Once merged, the Danone Group conducted numerous acquisitions and embarked on a global expansion, acquiring companies in Eastern Europe, Latin America, and Asia; Danone Group's first acquisition in Asia was the soy sauce and frozen food manufacturer, Amoy, in 1991.
Today the Group's portfolio is based on the company's mission to  "bring health through food to as many people as possible", with the group having divested in its operations in beer, biscuits and sauces in favour of a focus on fresh dairy products, early life nutrition, medical nutrition and water . It operates in more than 140 countries worldwide, with its top markets being France, Russia, the US and China.
Sales in the Fresh Dairy Products range account for just under 60% of the group's consolidated sales, and Danone Group ranks as the global leader in the dairy products industry worldwide. Sales in the Early Life Nutrition range make up around one fifth of the group's total sales, and Danone therefore also occupies a similarly high market share of the global baby food market, ranking in second place overall . Further to this, Danone Group is among the top five packaged food manufacturers globally.
Several forest risk commodities are relevant to Danone's operations, with the company using soya upstream in their supply chain in the form of animal feed for dairy operations as well as paper and packaging for their products. The group uses palm oil in a variety of its nutrition products, and in 2014, reported to the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil total use of 25,000 tonnes of refined palm oil or RBD palm oil and around 500 tonnes of palm kernel oil.

Procter & Gamble Co (P&G) is one of the world's largest consumer packaged goods companies, with operations in approximately 70 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Ohio in the US, P&G manufactures and markets consumer products throughout the world, with its branded products such as Head & Shoulders and Oral-B being sold in over 180 countries. P&G's products are primarily sold through mass merchandisers, grocery stores and drug stores and are approximated to serve around 4.8 billion people worldwide.
P&G divides its operations between four main business segments: Beauty; Health and Grooming; Fabric and Home Care; and Baby, Feminine and Family Care.  Palm kernel oil and, to a lesser extent, palm oil  are used in the manufacture of its products, including in its beauty and household care products such as soaps and detergents. The combined use of palm kernel oil, palm oil and its derivatives was over 532,000 MT in 2013/14. P&G purchases from a variety of suppliers, typically four or five supply chain levels above the source plantation. Over 70% of palm oil and derivatives are sourced from Malaysia, supplemented by procurement from Indonesia, and Central and South America. P&G also purchases wood pulp for absorbent hygiene and tissue products. In the financial year 2013/14, P&G bought approximately 1.7 million air dried metric tons of pulp for use in these products, sourcing pulp from Latin America (34%), Canada (30%) and the US (36%).

Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Aside from their cereal products, Kellogg Co also manufactures a number of snacks and frozen foods, including crisps, ready-meals, meat alternatives and biscuits. These products are sold through several well-known brands including Kellogg's, Fruit loops, Kashi, Pringles and Keebler. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. Notably, the company is building a new facility in Malaysia to take advantage of the rapidly growing Asia Pacific market.  This facility, due to be operational from mid-2015, is set to produce halal Pringles and other snacks, and will create over 300 jobs. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.
As a major manufacturer of packaged food, Kellogg Co uses both soya and palm oil. For example, palm oil is used in a variety of the company's branded products, such as in its cookies and waffles, and soya is used in cereal, such as in Kellogg's Smart Start Soy Protein.

The Sime Darby Group is a Malaysian conglomerate involved in diverse industries, including logistics, industrial equipment, property and plantations. Sime Darby Plantation is the agribusiness arm of the group which has a landbank of approximately 1 million hectares with 600,000 hectares of planted oil palm. This is one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. In 2015, the group processed more than 10 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches and produced more than 2 million metric tons of crude palm oil. It also produces products such as oleochemicals, fats, biodiesel and other derivatives.

Orkla Group (Orkla) is a Norwegian based manufacturer of consumer goods, with other interests including hydropower and real estate. The group began over 350 years ago as a mining operation and through acquisitions and divestments the group has changed very dramatically; its focus is now on branded consumer goods including food and cleaning products, although the group does retain operations in hydro power aluminium products and paint manufacture.  In 2013, the group employed around 17,000 staff and had a turnover of NOK 33 Billion ($5.3 Billion).
Orkla branded consumer goods business accounts for around 86% of revenue and is divided into five business units: Orkla Foods, which operates in Nordic and Baltic regions and concentrates on Orkla's own brand products (which generally hold number 1 or 2 positions in their markets); Orkla Confectionary and Snacks, which owns the brands KIMs Danmark and the Estonian Kalev; the Home and Personal Division, which owns cleaning and comestic brands such as Jif, Comfort and Vaseline Intensive Care; the Orkla International Division, which operates in Russia, Poland, Austria and India; and Orkla Food Ingredients, which produces baking products such as yeast and butter blends.
Orkla Confectionary and Snacks and Orkla Foods are both RSPO members since 2007 and 2013, respectively, following the acquisition of the Swedish companies Goteborgs Kex and Procordia, which were RSPO members. In 2014, the company started a new initiative to reduce deforestation through palm oil use and aims to use traceable and sustainable sources by the end of 2017. They also released a policy for sustainable palm oil use.

Procter & Gamble Co (P&G) is one of the world's largest consumer packaged goods companies, with operations in approximately 70 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Ohio in the US, P&G manufactures and markets consumer products throughout the world, with its branded products such as Head & Shoulders and Oral-B being sold in over 180 countries. P&G's products are primarily sold through mass merchandisers, grocery stores and drug stores and are approximated to serve around 4.8 billion people worldwide.
P&G divides its operations between four main business segments: Beauty; Health and Grooming; Fabric and Home Care; and Baby, Feminine and Family Care.  Palm kernel oil and, to a lesser extent, palm oil  are used in the manufacture of its products, including in its beauty and household care products such as soaps and detergents. The combined use of palm kernel oil, palm oil and its derivatives was over 532,000 MT in 2013/14. P&G purchases from a variety of suppliers, typically four or five supply chain levels above the source plantation. Over 70% of palm oil and derivatives are sourced from Malaysia, supplemented by procurement from Indonesia, and Central and South America. P&G also purchases wood pulp for absorbent hygiene and tissue products. In the financial year 2013/14, P&G bought approximately 1.7 million air dried metric tons of pulp for use in these products, sourcing pulp from Latin America (34%), Canada (30%) and the US (36%).

Its products include oral, personal and home care, as well as pet nutrition products. Brands include Colgate, Palmolive and Sanex. It is a major global player across all its products areas. Globally, Colgate-Palmolive is one of the ten largest home care companies, and ranks among the top five for beauty and personal care and bath and shower products. Palm oil is a major ingredient in many products, with over 170,000 metric tons of palm oil products being used in 2015.

Marks & Spencer Group PLC is the holding company for the Marks & Spencer Group (M&S). The company was established in 1884 as a single market stall in Leeds, UK and has since become a leading UK retailer, with 852 stores in the UK and a further 480 internationally in 59 territories. The company employs over 83,000 individuals. Further to this, M&S sells products online and through its franchise partners.
M&S sells a range of products, including food, homeware, and clothing for men, women and children, which it sources from around 2,000 suppliers globally. In the UK, the food segment comprises the majority of total sales, accounting for 57%, with the remainder made up of the general merchandise department. M&S' food division sells around 6,300 products, from everyday products, such as under the 'Simply M&S' brand range, to food for special occasions.
As a retailer, M&S is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. Palm oil and soya are found in some M&S food products. For example, palm oil and its derivatives are used as a vegetable oil, as a coating for dried fruit, and as a carrier for flavourings. The company also sells beef and has a commitment to source this commodity as well as palm oil and soya from sources that do not contribute to deforestation. Within M&S' women's and men's departments, the company sells a number of leather goods, such as leather boots and bags. M&S is also involved in the wood products industry and stocks a range of furniture items, including wooden garden furniture.

Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.

P&G's products are primarily sold through mass merchandisers, grocery stores and drug stores and are approximated to serve around 4.8 billion people worldwide.
P&G divides its operations between four main business segments: Beauty; Health and Grooming; Fabric and Home Care; and Baby, Feminine and Family Care.  Palm kernel oil and, to a lesser extent, palm oil  are used in the manufacture of its products, including in its beauty and household care products such as soaps and detergents. The combined use of palm kernel oil, palm oil and its derivatives was over 532,000 MT in 2013/14. P&G purchases from a variety of suppliers, typically four or five supply chain levels above the source plantation. Over 70% of palm oil and derivatives are sourced from Malaysia, supplemented by procurement from Indonesia, and Central and South America. P&G also purchases wood pulp for absorbent hygiene and tissue products. In the financial year 2013/14, P&G bought approximately 1.7 million air dried metric tons of pulp for use in these products, sourcing pulp from Latin America (34%), Canada (30%) and the US (36%).

Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (Reckitt Benckiser) manufactures and markets a wide range of branded home, health and personal care products. The group comprises around 60 companies and sells its products in nearly 200 countries, giving it a global presence. The company markets products under several well-known brands, including health products, such as Strepsils, Gaviscon and Nurofen; hygiene products Clearasil, Dettol, and Harpic; and home products, Calgon and Vanish.
Reckitt Benckiser is headquartered in the UK and has its origins in the 1800s, when Benckiser was founded in 1823. However, Reckitt Benckiser in its current form was established in 1999 through a merger between Reckitt & Colman and Benckiser. Since then, the company has undergone rapid expansion, with numerous acquisitions, including Korean household company Oxy in 2000; over-the-counter healthcare business, Boots Healthcare International, in 2006; and SSL International in 2010. More recently, in 2013, Reckitt Benckiser further strengthened its global position through collaboration with Bristol-Myers Squibb, a leading health company in Brazil and Mexico, and the acquisition of Manyanshuning, China's leading sore throat brand.
The company is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil and reported the use of around 107,000 MT of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. Palm oil is used principally in the company's manufacturing of home and personal care goods, for example, in cleaning agents, laundry detergents, and soap tablets.

Kao Corporation is a consumer products company, manufacturing beauty care, human health care, fabric and home care, and chemical products, for both industrial and consumer markets.  Founded in 1887, the company is headquartered in Japan. Kao Corporation has a global presence, although its operations are most heavily concentrated in Asia. In 2014, 67% of sales occurred in Japan.
The company's Beauty Care business encompasses a wide range of cosmetics, including skin and hair care products under a number of global brands such as Molton Brown and John Frieda. The Human Health Care business is primarily focused on the sanitary napkin brand, Laurier, which is sold in Asia, and the disposable diaper brand, Merries, which is also primarily targeted at the Japanese consumer market. The Fabric and Home Care business manufactures products such as laundry detergents and household cleaners for Asian and Japanese consumer market. The Chemical business manufactures products for a diverse range of industries, including paper and pulp, food products, pharmaceutical products, engineering and electronics. Kao Corporation uses palm and palm kernel oil as a raw material, using 96,100 tonnes of palm oil in 2013/14. Pulp is also used in the manufacture of its products.
initiatives: Explicit mention of the importance of forests

rows.coprofile: Colgate-Palmolive is an American consumer goods company with products sold in over 200 countries around the world. Its products include oral, personal and home care, as well as pet nutrition products. Brands include Colgate, Palmolive and Sanex. It is a major global player across all its products areas. Globally, Colgate-Palmolive is one of the ten largest home care companies, and ranks among the top five for beauty and personal care and bath and shower products. Palm oil is a major ingredient in many products, with over 170,000 metric tons of palm oil products being used in 2015.

Amaggi (Grupo André Maggi) is a Brazilian agribusiness company active in the production, processing and trading of agricultural commodities. Its operations are primarily in Brazil, but it also has an important presence in Argentina and Paraguay, as well as being present in Holland, Norway and Poland. It is a major player in the soy market.  It has three soy crushing facilities with an annual production capacity of over 2 million metric tons.  Amaggi is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Grupo Andre Maggi (AMAGGI) is a Brazilian agribusiness company active in the production, processing and trading of agricultural commodities. Its operations are primarily focussed in Brazil, but it also has an important presence in Argentina and Paraguay, as well as being present in Holland, Norway and Poland. It is a major player in the soya market. In 2014, the group had a planted area of over 130,000 hectares for soy and produced more than 450,000 metric tons of soya. It has three soya crushing facilities with an annual production capacity of over 2 million metric tons. In 2016, AMAGGI was among the top five Brazilian exporters of soya.

Orkla Group (Orkla) is a Norwegian based manufacturer of consumer goods, with other interests including hydropower and real estate. The group began over 350 years ago as a mining operation and through acquisitions and divestments the group has changed very dramatically; its focus is now on branded consumer goods including food and cleaning products, although the group does retain operations in hydro power aluminium products and paint manufacture.  In 2013, the group employed around 17,000 staff and had a turnover of NOK 33 Billion ($5.3 Billion).
Orkla branded consumer goods business accounts for around 86% of revenue and is divided into five business units: Orkla Foods, which operates in Nordic and Baltic regions and concentrates on Orkla's own brand products (which generally hold number 1 or 2 positions in their markets); Orkla Confectionary and Snacks, which owns the brands KIMs Danmark and the Estonian Kalev; the Home and Personal Division, which owns cleaning and comestic brands such as Jif, Comfort and Vaseline Intensive Care; the Orkla International Division, which operates in Russia, Poland, Austria and India; and Orkla Food Ingredients, which produces baking products such as yeast and butter blends.
Orkla Confectionary and Snacks and Orkla Foods are both RSPO members since 2007 and 2013, respectively, following the acquisition of the Swedish companies Goteborgs Kex and Procordia, which were RSPO members. In 2014, the company started a new initiative to reduce deforestation through palm oil use and aims to use traceable and sustainable sources by the end of 2017. They also released a policy for sustainable palm oil use.

Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. The company's landbank is one of the ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with approximately 300,000 hectares across Indonesia. It also owns a palm oil refinery and has a 50% stake in another, alongside several processing and crushing facilities. In 2015, the company processed more than 1.7 million metric tons of crude palm oil.

Nestlé is a Swiss food manufacturer with more than 2,000 brands being sold in more than 185 countries. Its products include beverages, confectionary, chilled foods, nutrition and pet care with well-known brands such as Maggi, KitKat, Milo and Nescafé. The company is a major manufacturer and retailer of packaged foods in Indonesia, Brazil the US and Western Europe. Its products use palm oil and soy is used in animal feed for dairy products.  Nestlé S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

General Mills Inc. is a global food business with net sales of $19.2 billion in fiscal 2014. The company's foundations can be traced back to two flour mills built in Minneapolis, US, in the 1860s, and General Mills Inc. was established in its current form when it listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 1928. General Mills Inc. sells its products in over 100 countries, with approximately two thirds of sales originating domestically in the US. The company offers cereals, baking products, snacks, frozen foods, ready meals, dairy and vegetables.
General Mills Inc. owns a number of globally recognised brands, including ice cream brand Hagen-Dazs, breakfast products brands Nature Valley and Cheerios, and Brazilian food brand, Yoki. Its operations in the dairy market include those through its business Yoplait, in which General Mills Inc. gained a controlling stake (51%) in 2011. The company also has a joint venture with Nestle, called Cereal Partners Worldwide, which markets cereals produced by General Mills Inc. in 130 countries worldwide. As of 2008, General Mills Inc. manufactures its products in 79 plants, employing a workforce of 43,000 people in 2014. The company continues to focus on expansion, particularly in emerging markets including India, the Middle East, Indonesia and North Africa. For example, in June 2015 the Yoplait brand was expanded into China. General Mills uses palm oil and soya in the production of their food products such as snacks and cereal, with 61,148 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derivatives utilised by the company in 2013/14.
initiatives: The are several quotes in the reports and on the website that show how the company recognise the value of forests in biodiversity, climate change ect…

On the CDP website no Forest report has been produced. On the Climate Change report 2014 there are no quantitative data about the commodities we are analysing. The ACOP 2013/2114 reports both the entire volume of produced palm oil and the sustainable part of it.

The pulp packaging (quote 1) and palm oil (quote2) policies do not mention any limits so we can assume it applies to all suppliers. The same happens for the soy policy: "General Mills is committed to sustainable soy production practices. We adhere to the Consumer Goods Forum soy sourcing guidelines to help meet industry commitments to stop deforestation by 2020. We also support the Soy Moratorium commitment to not purchase soy from lands that have been deforested in the Amazon biome after July 2006." (http://www.generalmills.com/en/Responsibility/~/media/4588CAEA15604E0C91DE2D29F198FA08.ashx p47)

Pearson Plc (Pearson) is a London-based international media and education company, with key operations in the publishing industry. The company develops and publishes educational and entertainment materials in the form of books, newspapers and online. Pearson provides educational materials to teachers and students across 70 countries.  It also runs the Financial Times Group, a leading provider of business and financial news and analysis, both in print and online. Finally, Pearson is also the parent company of Penguin Random House, which claims to be the first truly global trade book publisher, and comprises the various publishing enterprises of the previously separate Penguin and Random House companies. Penguin Random House was formed in July 2013 after a merger was agreed between the respective publishing enterprises' parent companies, Pearson and Bertelsmann. The joint venture is based in New York and is jointly controlled by the two companies, with 53% owned by Bertelsmann, based in Germany, and 47% by Pearson.
In 2013, the book publishing operations of Pearson, the Penguin Group and Penguin Random House, individually ranked as the top two players in the book publishing industry globally. Only a very small proportion of Pearson's products are printed in-house, with the company instead sourcing from a number of suppliers around the world. For example, commercial printing company R. R. Donnelley, which is the leading company of its kind globally in terms of market share, is an important supplier of Pearson.

Kimberly-Clark Group, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, in the US, is a leading international company in the personal care, health and hygiene industry. It has a long history in supplying paper products for personal care, having been founded over 140 years ago in the state of Wisconsin in the US in 1870. The company produces feminine, adult, family, baby and child care products, as well as products for the professional and health care sectors, including diapers, facial and bathroom tissue, and paper towels. Its well-known brands include Kleenex, which was the world's pioneering facial tissue, and Huggies, a leading brand of diaper that is central to the company's multi-billion dollar baby-care business. It is the leading company in the retail tissue industry globally, and also occupies the second place amongst the top 100 forestry, paper and packaging companies globally, ranked by sales, in 2013.
The company has manufacturing facilities in 37 countries, including in India, Indonesia, Brazil, China and the Republic of Korea and its brands are sold in 175 countries worldwide. The company claims that almost 25% of the world's population purchase Kimberly-Clark Group products on a daily basis. Kimberly-Clark Group's branded tissue products consume significant amounts of wood fibre and pulp. In 2012, the company's manufacturing operations were responsible for the consumption of 4.4% of the total market pulp produced that year, and its products absorbed around 2.36 million air-dried metric tons of virgin wood fibre.

Donnelley, which is the leading company of its kind globally in terms of market share, is an important supplier of Pearson.

Mars Inc. (Mars) is a global leader in the confectionery industry, and also a significant player in the market for dried processed foods, sauces and condiments. The company was originally founded in 1891, and has its origins in the confectionery business, for which it remains most well-known. Headquartered in the state of Virginia in the US, Mars is the third largest private company in the America and employs over 65,000 'associates.' These associates work in 230 locations and factories in 68 countries worldwide. The company's operations are divided between six divisions: pet care products, chocolate, a variety of packaged food, chewing gum and candy under the Wrigley business segment, drinks and finally, scientific research under Mars Symbioscience.
Mars manufactures goods under numerous well-known global brands, including ready meal brands, Uncle Ben's and Suzi Wan, and chocolates brands including Maltesers, Bounty, Galaxy, M&Ms, Twix, Snickers and many more.  Mars sources a variety of raw materials to manufacture its diverse product range. Several forest risk commodities are among these, including beef, which comprises 3.6% of Mars' raw materials purchased by volume, as well as palm oil, soya and pulp and paper. In 2012/2013, Mars reported use of over 77,000 tonnes of palm oil, making its palm oil consumption higher than many other manufacturers.
Mars continues to increase its manufacturing capacity, opening a new $270 million chocolate plant in Kansas, America.  The company is also aiming to improve its market position in petcare through the planned acquisition of the IAMS, Eukanuba and Natura brands from Procter and Gamble for $2.9 billion. The company is also strong in its research and development with a new £6 million facility in Slough, United Kingdom that opened in 2012.

General Mills Inc. is a global food business with net sales of $19.2 billion in fiscal 2014. The company's foundations can be traced back to two flour mills built in Minneapolis, US, in the 1860s, and General Mills Inc. was established in its current form when it listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 1928. General Mills Inc. sells its products in over 100 countries, with approximately two thirds of sales originating domestically in the US. The company offers cereals, baking products, snacks, frozen foods, ready meals, dairy and vegetables.
General Mills Inc. owns a number of globally recognised brands, including ice cream brand Hagen-Dazs, breakfast products brands Nature Valley and Cheerios, and Brazilian food brand, Yoki. Its operations in the dairy market include those through its business Yoplait, in which General Mills Inc. gained a controlling stake (51%) in 2011. The company also has a joint venture with Nestle, called Cereal Partners Worldwide, which markets cereals produced by General Mills Inc. in 130 countries worldwide. As of 2008, General Mills Inc. manufactures its products in 79 plants, employing a workforce of 43,000 people in 2014. The company continues to focus on expansion, particularly in emerging markets including India, the Middle East, Indonesia and North Africa. For example, in June 2015 the Yoplait brand was expanded into China. General Mills uses palm oil and soya in the production of their food products such as snacks and cereal, with 61,148 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derivatives utilised by the company in 2013/14.

Henkel AG & Co. KGaA (Henkel) is a manufacturing company, headquartered in Germany, which operates in both the consumer and business markets. It operates worldwide in three key areas: Laundry and Home Care; Beauty Care; and Adhesive Technologies. Famous brands include Persil and Schwarzkopf. Products sold under these brands (such as laundry detergents, household cleaners and cosmetic products) commonly contain surfactants that consist of palm oil derivatives. Surfactants are an active substance, not produced by Henkel directly but purchased from third party suppliers €“ mineral oils, natural gas, coconut oil, and palm kernel oil are currently the only ingredients able to produce surfactants on an industrial scale. According to Henkel, in 2013, through surfactant and other raw material purchasing, the company used around 71,608 tonnes of palm oil products, mostly comprising palm kernel oil.

News Corporation (News Corp) is a media conglomerate with a network of companies in media, news, education and information services. In June 2013, News Corp's shareholders gave formal approval for the company to split its publishing and entertainment divisions, creating two new companies: News Corp, housing the company's publishing segment; 21st Century Fox housing the entertainment division. News Corp is now specifically a publishing company, producing newspaper, magazines, books and promotional inserts and coupons. The company was established in Australia in 1954, when Rupert Murdoch took control of the Australian corporation, News Limited, which had a majority interest in one of Adelaide's top daily newspapers. Since then, the company has grown dramatically and acquired numerous assets, beginning with newspapers in the UK: 'The Sun' and 'News of the World.' Established in Australia, News Corp is now based in the US and is the largest newspaper publishing company globally.
As of 2014, News Corp is comprised of the following businesses, with each housing several brands: News Corp Australia, News UK, Dow Jones & Company, New York Post, Harper Collins Publishers, Amplify, News America Marketing, and Storyful. News Corp Australia, for example, claims to be Australia's leading media and publishing company, selling over 10 million papers weekly, with titles including The Daily Telegraph, The Australian, and Herald Sun. News UK also publishes some of the UK's most well-known newspapers, including The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times. Dow Jones & Company publishes The Wall Street Journal and specialises in the provision of news and business information via a variety of media outlets.  Finally, News Corp's subsidiary HarperCollins is one of the world's most prominent book publishing companies. In May 2014, HarperCollins acquired book publisher Harlequin; the acquisition of the Canadian company is the biggest deal in book publishing since the merger of two other publishing giants, Penguin and Random House in 2013.

Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Aside from their cereal products, Kellogg Co also manufactures a number of snacks and frozen foods, including crisps, ready-meals, meat alternatives and biscuits. These products are sold through several well-known brands including Kellogg's, Fruit loops, Kashi, Pringles and Keebler. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. Notably, the company is building a new facility in Malaysia to take advantage of the rapidly growing Asia Pacific market.  This facility, due to be operational from mid-2015, is set to produce halal Pringles and other snacks, and will create over 300 jobs. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.
As a major manufacturer of packaged food, Kellogg Co uses both soya and palm oil. For example, palm oil is used in a variety of the company's branded products, such as in its cookies and waffles, and soya is used in cereal, such as in Kellogg's Smart Start Soy Protein.

Oji Holdings is a corporation involved in the pulp and paper industry at a producing, processing and manufacturing level. Its products include packaging materials, household products, print materials and more. In 2014, it was among the top five largest companies for forest, paper and packaging products by annual sales value globally, with a supply capacity of 2.4 million metric tons of pulp to market. Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A, which was one of the largest timber, paper and packaging companies in Brazil in 2014. There were also plans announced in 2015 to establish operations in Myanmar.

rows.coprofile: Bumitama Agri is an Indonesian palm oil company involved in the cultivation and processing of oil palm. At the end of 2014, the company had a planted area of about 150,000 hectares, predominantly on Indonesian Borneo, out of a total landbank of just under 200,000. This is among the fifteen largest landbanks amongst global palm oil producers. Its annual capacity for crude palm oil and palm kernel oil with its 10 mills is about 3.4 million metric tons.

Kimberly-Clark Group, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, in the US, is a leading international company in the personal care, health and hygiene industry. It has a long history in supplying paper products for personal care, having been founded over 140 years ago in the state of Wisconsin in the US in 1870. The company produces feminine, adult, family, baby and child care products, as well as products for the professional and health care sectors, including diapers, facial and bathroom tissue, and paper towels. Its well-known brands include Kleenex, which was the world's pioneering facial tissue, and Huggies, a leading brand of diaper that is central to the company's multi-billion dollar baby-care business. It is the leading company in the retail tissue industry globally, and also occupies the second place amongst the top 100 forestry, paper and packaging companies globally, ranked by sales, in 2013.
The company has manufacturing facilities in 37 countries, including in India, Indonesia, Brazil, China and the Republic of Korea and its brands are sold in 175 countries worldwide. The company claims that almost 25% of the world's population purchase Kimberly-Clark Group products on a daily basis. Kimberly-Clark Group's branded tissue products consume significant amounts of wood fibre and pulp. In 2012, the company's manufacturing operations were responsible for the consumption of 4.4% of the total market pulp produced that year, and its products absorbed around 2.36 million air-dried metric tons of virgin wood fibre.

Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio with the RTL group, publishing with Penguin Random House, and magazines with Gruner + Jahr. The most important markets are the US and Western Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.

Unilever is one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies, with operations across a wide range of market segments. The company has over 400 brands, including many household names such as Lipton, Knorr, Dove and Hellman’s. Its range of products leaves it exposed to a variety of forest risk commodities.  Unilever PLC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

The McDonald's menu of burgers, sandwiches, sides and beverages involves significant amounts of beef, soya and palm oil, as well as paper in packaging. In 2015, for example, over 120,000 metric tons of palm oil were used by McDonald's.

Kimberly-Clark Group, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, in the US, is a leading international company in the personal care, health and hygiene industry. It has a long history in supplying paper products for personal care, having been founded over 140 years ago in the state of Wisconsin in the US in 1870. The company produces feminine, adult, family, baby and child care products, as well as products for the professional and health care sectors, including diapers, facial and bathroom tissue, and paper towels. Its well-known brands include Kleenex, which was the world's pioneering facial tissue, and Huggies, a leading brand of diaper that is central to the company's multi-billion dollar baby-care business. It is the leading company in the retail tissue industry globally, and also occupies the second place amongst the top 100 forestry, paper and packaging companies globally, ranked by sales, in 2013.
The company has manufacturing facilities in 37 countries, including in India, Indonesia, Brazil, China and the Republic of Korea and its brands are sold in 175 countries worldwide. The company claims that almost 25% of the world's population purchase Kimberly-Clark Group products on a daily basis. Kimberly-Clark Group's branded tissue products consume significant amounts of wood fibre and pulp. In 2012, the company's manufacturing operations were responsible for the consumption of 4.4% of the total market pulp produced that year, and its products absorbed around 2.36 million air-dried metric tons of virgin wood fibre.

Pearson Plc (Pearson) is a London-based international media and education company, with key operations in the publishing industry. The company develops and publishes educational and entertainment materials in the form of books, newspapers and online. Pearson provides educational materials to teachers and students across 70 countries.  It also runs the Financial Times Group, a leading provider of business and financial news and analysis, both in print and online. Finally, Pearson is also the parent company of Penguin Random House, which claims to be the first truly global trade book publisher, and comprises the various publishing enterprises of the previously separate Penguin and Random House companies. Penguin Random House was formed in July 2013 after a merger was agreed between the respective publishing enterprises' parent companies, Pearson and Bertelsmann. The joint venture is based in New York and is jointly controlled by the two companies, with 53% owned by Bertelsmann, based in Germany, and 47% by Pearson.
In 2013, the book publishing operations of Pearson, the Penguin Group and Penguin Random House, individually ranked as the top two players in the book publishing industry globally. Only a very small proportion of Pearson's products are printed in-house, with the company instead sourcing from a number of suppliers around the world. For example, commercial printing company R. R. Donnelley, which is the leading company of its kind globally in terms of market share, is an important supplier of Pearson.

Johnson & Johnson is a global family of companies manufacturing health care products for the consumer market and also providing diagnostic and surgical equipment for healthcare services around the world. The company is headquartered in the United States but has a truly global presence, with over 250 companies located in 60 countries worldwide.
Johnson & Johnson's consumer health care products division includes baby care, skin and hair care, and over-the-counter pharmaceutical products, amongst others. Its skin and hair care product brands include Aveeno, Neutrogena, Clean & Clear, and Piz Buin. In 2013, the Johnson & Johnson family of companies used 77,800 tonnes of palm oil and palm kernel oil, which are used in Johnson & Johnson's soap, shampoo, cream and lotion products. These are not bought directly from palm plantations but purchased as oleo chemicals (surfactants, conditioners and emulsifiers) derived from palm oil from other suppliers.

Kering SA is a French company engaged in the retail and distribution of luxury goods, primarily apparel and accessories. Until 2013, the company was known as PPR, short for Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, which in turn was its official name until 2005.  Established in 1963, the company has its origins in the building materials industry and in particular in the timber trade. It then became a leader in the retail sector, before entering into the world of luxury goods with the purchase of the Gucci brand in 1999. Today the company has 22 brands operating in two core divisions: Luxury, which designs, manufactures and markets luxury apparel, leather goods, accessories, watches, jewellery, fragrances and cosmetics; and Sport and Lifestyle, which designs and produces footwear, apparel and accessories under the company's sporting brands.
Kering SA is headquartered in Paris, France and its brands in its luxury and sports and lifestyle segments, include several world famous brands including Puma, Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga and Stella McCartney, many of which have leather goods among their principal products,. Kering SA therefore plays a prominent role in the global trade in leather and animal skins, with several of the company's brands designing and selling leather goods. For example, it produces leather wallets and handbags under Saint Laurent  and Balenciaga. Through these and its numerous other brands, Kering SA holds the second largest market share in the bags and luggage sector globally. It also produces large amount s of leather footwear, for example under Sergio Rossi; a leading Italian shoe brand. Kering SA is among the top five manufacturers of footwear globally, occupying the fourth largest share of the global market in 2013, and in particular holding a leading position in the footwear market of Western Europe, especially in Italy. Kering SA is placing increasing emphasis on the direct sourcing of its raw materials, including leather. In 2013, it bought a majority stake in one the world's biggest producers of tanned skins and it has plans to build a new tanning facility in France, which could be operational by 2016.

Bumitama Agri is an Indonesian palm oil company involved in the cultivation and processing of oil palm. At the end of 2014, the company had a planted area of about 150,000 hectares, predominantly on Indonesian Borneo, out of a total landbank of just under 200,000. This is among the fifteen largest landbanks amongst global palm oil producers. Its annual capacity for crude palm oil and palm kernel oil with its 10 mills is about 3.4 million metric tons.

rows.coprofile: Henkel AG & Co. KGaA (Henkel) is a manufacturing company, headquartered in Germany, which operates in both the consumer and business markets. It operates worldwide in three key areas: Laundry and Home Care; Beauty Care; and Adhesive Technologies. Famous brands include Persil and Schwarzkopf. Products sold under these brands (such as laundry detergents, household cleaners and cosmetic products) commonly contain surfactants that consist of palm oil derivatives. Surfactants are an active substance, not produced by Henkel directly but purchased from third party suppliers €“ mineral oils, natural gas, coconut oil, and palm kernel oil are currently the only ingredients able to produce surfactants on an industrial scale. According to Henkel, in 2013, through surfactant and other raw material purchasing, the company used around 71,608 tonnes of palm oil products, mostly comprising palm kernel oil.

Precious Woods is a Swiss based company involved in the cultivation, processing and trading of tropical timber. It manages forests in both Brazil and Gabon. The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.  Precious Woods Holding AG is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

Oji Holdings is a corporation involved in the pulp and paper industry at a producing, processing and manufacturing level. Its products include packaging materials, household products, print materials and more. In 2014, it was among the top five largest companies for forest, paper and packaging products by annual sales value globally, with a supply capacity of 2.4 million metric tons of pulp to market. Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A, which was one of the largest timber, paper and packaging companies in Brazil in 2014. There were also plans announced in 2015 to establish operations in Myanmar.

Nestlé is a Swiss food manufacturer with more than 2,000 brands being sold in 188 countries. Its products include beverages, confectionary, chilled foods, nutrition and pet care with well-known brands such as Maggi, KitKat, Milo and Nescafé. The company is a major manufacturer and retailer of packaged foods in Indonesia, Brazil the US and Western Europe. Its products use palm oil and soy is used in animal feed for dairy products. Globally, Colgate-Palmolive is one of the ten largest home care companies, and ranks among the top five for beauty and personal care and bath and shower products. rows.coprofile: Sipef Group is a Belgian company, with subsidaries located in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and the Ivory Coast. It operates agro-industrial activities primarily in the production of oil palm products, as well as natural rubber, tea, bananas, flowers and foliage.

McDonald's is an American fast food retailer with more than 36,000 locations in over 100 countries. It is one of the largest fast food restaurant companies globally with a major market share. Additionally, it has one of the largest market shares in the US, China, Western Europe, and in India. The McDonald's menu of burgers, sandwiches, sides and beverages involves significant amounts of beef, soya and palm oil, as well as paper in packaging. In 2015, for example, over 120,000 metric tons of palm oil were used by McDonald's.

Westpac are an Australian-based banking group providing banking and financial services to private, corporate and institutional customers. Their services include retail banking, corporate financing, wealth management, capital markets, investments and insurance. As of 2017, Westpac's total assets amounted to more than 830 billion AUD with more than 660 billion AUD in gross loans to customers. Westpac are among the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 4 billion USD of loans in companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Kingfisher PLC (Kingfisher) is a home improvement company, operating chains of retail stores. Kingfisher is based in the UK and though its domestic market dominates its operations, it is also active overseas, with a presence throughout Europe and in China. 
The company is Europe's leading retailer in the DIY sector and it is the third largest globally. Kingfisher's operations date back to 1982, with the acquisition of FW Woolworth, with which came a small chain of B&Q DIY retail outlets. B&Q is now one of Kingfisher's main retail brands, along with Castorama, Brico Dept, Screwfix, and Koçta?. B&Q supplies DIY and garden products and stocks a number of wooden products, including garden sheds and indoor and outdoor furniture, wooden flooring, and construction, finishing and decorative timber. It has over 350 stores in the UK and Ireland, and 39 in China. B&Q opened its first stores in China in 1999, however after some initial problems in entering the market the company scaled back and restructured its operations to better adapt to the Chinese market, involving a focus on the local preference for 'Do-it-for-me' rather than the traditional 'Do-it-yourself' (DIY), which has stabilised its position as a leader in the somewhat fragmented market. 
Castorama is similarly a chain of home and garden stores, with over 100 outlets in France, 72 stores in Poland, and 20 in Russia. Brico Dept is a more specialist chain of stores, providing products for professional builders and more experienced consumers. The majority of Brico Dept's business is in France, where it has over 100 stores, but it also has stores in Spain and Romania. Screwfix has stores in the UK and provides tools and hardware products. Finally, Koçta? is Turkey's leading home improvement retailer, with 46 stores.

Its operations are primarily in Brazil, but it also has an important presence in Argentina and Paraguay, as well as being present in Holland, Norway and Poland. It is a major player in the soy market.  It has three soy crushing facilities with an annual production capacity of over 2 million metric tons.  Amaggi is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Bunge is a global agribusiness operating in about 40 countries and involved in the processing, manufacture and trading of agricultural commodities. The company is one of the major players in the South American soya industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is one of the largest soya processors in Brazil and one of the market leaders in Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. The company also has facilities in China and India. Globally it has 40 million tons of annual soy crush capacity. Bunge is also among the top five exporters of soya from Argentina and Paraguay, and is one of the largest in Brazil.

Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) is a leading processor and trader in agricultural commodities active in more than 100 countries. The company has significant oilseed crushing facilities in Brazil and Argentina, as well as having an annual capacity of several million metric tons in China. The company's palm oil operations are also significant with the company handling over 2 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in 2015. It is also a major producer of biodiesel.

Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Aside from their cereal products, Kellogg Co also manufactures a number of snacks and frozen foods, including crisps, ready-meals, meat alternatives and biscuits. These products are sold through several well-known brands including Kellogg's, Fruit loops, Kashi, Pringles and Keebler. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. Notably, the company is building a new facility in Malaysia to take advantage of the rapidly growing Asia Pacific market.  This facility, due to be operational from mid-2015, is set to produce halal Pringles and other snacks, and will create over 300 jobs. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.
As a major manufacturer of packaged food, Kellogg Co uses both soya and palm oil. For example, palm oil is used in a variety of the company's branded products, such as in its cookies and waffles, and soya is used in cereal, such as in Kellogg's Smart Start Soy Protein.

The company is Europe's leading retailer in the DIY sector and it is the third largest globally. Kingfisher's operations date back to 1982, with the acquisition of FW Woolworth, with which came a small chain of B&Q DIY retail outlets. B&Q is now one of Kingfisher's main retail brands, along with Castorama, Brico Dept, Screwfix, and Koçta?. B&Q supplies DIY and garden products and stocks a number of wooden products, including garden sheds and indoor and outdoor furniture, wooden flooring, and construction, finishing and decorative timber. It has over 350 stores in the UK and Ireland, and 39 in China. B&Q opened its first stores in China in 1999, however after some initial problems in entering the market the company scaled back and restructured its operations to better adapt to the Chinese market, involving a focus on the local preference for 'Do-it-for-me' rather than the traditional 'Do-it-yourself' (DIY), which has stabilised its position as a leader in the somewhat fragmented market. 
Castorama is similarly a chain of home and garden stores, with over 100 outlets in France, 72 stores in Poland, and 20 in Russia. Brico Dept is a more specialist chain of stores, providing products for professional builders and more experienced consumers. The majority of Brico Dept's business is in France, where it has over 100 stores, but it also has stores in Spain and Romania. Screwfix has stores in the UK and provides tools and hardware products. Finally, Koçta? is Turkey's leading home improvement retailer, with 46 stores.

Mars Inc. (Mars) is a global leader in the confectionery industry, and also a significant player in the market for dried processed foods, sauces and condiments. The company was originally founded in 1891, and has its origins in the confectionery business, for which it remains most well-known. Headquartered in the state of Virginia in the US, Mars is the third largest private company in the America and employs over 65,000 'associates.' These associates work in 230 locations and factories in 68 countries worldwide. The company's operations are divided between six divisions: pet care products, chocolate, a variety of packaged food, chewing gum and candy under the Wrigley business segment, drinks and finally, scientific research under Mars Symbioscience.
Mars manufactures goods under numerous well-known global brands, including ready meal brands, Uncle Ben's and Suzi Wan, and chocolates brands including Maltesers, Bounty, Galaxy, M&Ms, Twix, Snickers and many more.  Mars sources a variety of raw materials to manufacture its diverse product range. Several forest risk commodities are among these, including beef, which comprises 3.6% of Mars' raw materials purchased by volume, as well as palm oil, soya and pulp and paper. In 2012/2013, Mars reported use of over 77,000 tonnes of palm oil, making its palm oil consumption higher than many other manufacturers.
Mars continues to increase its manufacturing capacity, opening a new $270 million chocolate plant in Kansas, America.  The company is also aiming to improve its market position in petcare through the planned acquisition of the IAMS, Eukanuba and Natura brands from Procter and Gamble for $2.9 billion. The company is also strong in its research and development with a new £6 million facility in Slough, United Kingdom that opened in 2012.

Precious Woods is a Swiss based company involved in the cultivation, processing and trading of tropical timber. It manages forests in both Brazil and Gabon. In 2016, its Brazilian forestry concessions amounted to more than 500,000 hectares, making Precious Woods one of the largest Brazilian forestry companies. In Gabon, Precious Woods' forestry concessions total more than 600,000 hectares as of 2016. The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, which processed more than 200,000 cubic metres of timber in 2015. Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.

Johnson & Johnson is a global family of companies manufacturing health care products for the consumer market and also providing diagnostic and surgical equipment for healthcare services around the world. The company is headquartered in the United States but has a truly global presence, with over 250 companies located in 60 countries worldwide.
Johnson & Johnson's consumer health care products division includes baby care, skin and hair care, and over-the-counter pharmaceutical products, amongst others. Its skin and hair care product brands include Aveeno, Neutrogena, Clean & Clear, and Piz Buin. In 2013, the Johnson & Johnson family of companies used 77,800 tonnes of palm oil and palm kernel oil, which are used in Johnson & Johnson's soap, shampoo, cream and lotion products. These are not bought directly from palm plantations but purchased as oleo chemicals (surfactants, conditioners and emulsifiers) derived from palm oil from other suppliers.

PepsiCo Inc (PepsiCo) was formed in 1965 when Frito-Lay Inc. merged with Pepsi-Cola Company. The company now contributes significantly to the food and beverage markets globally, with its products sold on every continent. The company's 2013 revenue was split roughly equally between its food and beverages sectors.
It is through PepsiCo's wholly owned subsidiary, Frito Lay, that it operates in the snack market. Through this subsidiary, PepsiCo has over 35% of the United States savoury snack market and Frito-Lay accounts for approximately a third of PepsiCo's annual sales. PepsiCo owns a total of 22 brands that generate more than $1 billion annually, including Lays, Pepsi, Tropicana, Quaker and Gatorade; its products include a variety of snacks, soft drinks and breakfast cereals. Aside from producing goods for its own brands, PepsiCo also manufactures and distributes a number of products under license from Starbucks, Lipton and Dole. PepsiCo operates a global network of manufacturing facilities, employing nearly 275,000 people and generating over $66 billion in net revenue in 2013. These manufacturing facilities consumed over 450,000 tones of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in 2012-2013. PepsiCo continues to develop its infrastructure, particularly in fast-growth economies. For example, it is committed to investing Rs 1,230 crore in a new beverage factory sited on 80 acres in Andhra Pradesh, India.

Kering SA is a French company engaged in the retail and distribution of luxury goods, primarily apparel and accessories. Until 2013, the company was known as PPR, short for Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, which in turn was its official name until 2005.  Established in 1963, the company has its origins in the building materials industry and in particular in the timber trade. It then became a leader in the retail sector, before entering into the world of luxury goods with the purchase of the Gucci brand in 1999. Today the company has 22 brands operating in two core divisions: Luxury, which designs, manufactures and markets luxury apparel, leather goods, accessories, watches, jewellery, fragrances and cosmetics; and Sport and Lifestyle, which designs and produces footwear, apparel and accessories under the company's sporting brands.
Kering SA is headquartered in Paris, France and its brands in its luxury and sports and lifestyle segments, include several world famous brands including Puma, Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga and Stella McCartney, many of which have leather goods among their principal products,. Kering SA therefore plays a prominent role in the global trade in leather and animal skins, with several of the company's brands designing and selling leather goods. For example, it produces leather wallets and handbags under Saint Laurent  and Balenciaga. Through these and its numerous other brands, Kering SA holds the second largest market share in the bags and luggage sector globally. It also produces large amount s of leather footwear, for example under Sergio Rossi; a leading Italian shoe brand. Kering SA is among the top five manufacturers of footwear globally, occupying the fourth largest share of the global market in 2013, and in particular holding a leading position in the footwear market of Western Europe, especially in Italy. Kering SA is placing increasing emphasis on the direct sourcing of its raw materials, including leather. In 2013, it bought a majority stake in one the world's biggest producers of tanned skins and it has plans to build a new tanning facility in France, which could be operational by 2016.

General Mills Inc. is a global food business with net sales of $19.2 billion in fiscal 2014. The company's foundations can be traced back to two flour mills built in Minneapolis, US, in the 1860s, and General Mills Inc. was established in its current form when it listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 1928. General Mills Inc. sells its products in over 100 countries, with approximately two thirds of sales originating domestically in the US. The company offers cereals, baking products, snacks, frozen foods, ready meals, dairy and vegetables.
General Mills Inc. owns a number of globally recognised brands, including ice cream brand Hagen-Dazs, breakfast products brands Nature Valley and Cheerios, and Brazilian food brand, Yoki. Its operations in the dairy market include those through its business Yoplait, in which General Mills Inc. gained a controlling stake (51%) in 2011. The company also has a joint venture with Nestle, called Cereal Partners Worldwide, which markets cereals produced by General Mills Inc. in 130 countries worldwide. As of 2008, General Mills Inc. manufactures its products in 79 plants, employing a workforce of 43,000 people in 2014. The company continues to focus on expansion, particularly in emerging markets including India, the Middle East, Indonesia and North Africa. For example, in June 2015 the Yoplait brand was expanded into China. General Mills uses palm oil and soya in the production of their food products such as snacks and cereal, with 61,148 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derivatives utilised by the company in 2013/14.

Standard Chartered are an international banking group headquartered in London, providing banking products and services for both personal and business customers. Their services include commercial banking and corporate finance, as well as retail banking, insurance, investment and wealth management. As of 2017, Standard Chartered's total assets stand at over 650 billion USD, their lending amounts to more than 260 billion USD, and they have nearly 60 billion USD in assets under management for private customers. Standard Chartered are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 30 billion dollars of loans to companies exposed to forest risk commodities, predominantly in the food products and agriculture sectors.

Oji Holdings is a corporation involved in the pulp and paper industry at a producing, processing and manufacturing level. Its products include packaging materials, household products, print materials and more. In 2014, it was among the top five largest companies for forest, paper and packaging products by annual sales value globally, with a supply capacity of 2.4 million metric tons of pulp to market. Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A, which was one of the largest timber, paper and packaging companies in Brazil in 2014. There were also plans announced in 2015 to establish operations in Myanmar.

Henkel AG & Co. KGaA (Henkel) is a manufacturing company, headquartered in Germany, which operates in both the consumer and business markets. It operates worldwide in three key areas: Laundry and Home Care; Beauty Care; and Adhesive Technologies. Famous brands include Persil and Schwarzkopf. Products sold under these brands (such as laundry detergents, household cleaners and cosmetic products) commonly contain surfactants that consist of palm oil derivatives. Surfactants are an active substance, not produced by Henkel directly but purchased from third party suppliers €“ mineral oils, natural gas, coconut oil, and palm kernel oil are currently the only ingredients able to produce surfactants on an industrial scale. According to Henkel, in 2013, through surfactant and other raw material purchasing, the company used around 71,608 tonnes of palm oil products, mostly comprising palm kernel oil.

Kao Corporation has a global presence, although its operations are most heavily concentrated in Asia. In 2014, 67% of sales occurred in Japan.
The company's Beauty Care business encompasses a wide range of cosmetics, including skin and hair care products under a number of global brands such as Molton Brown and John Frieda. The Chemical business manufactures products for a diverse range of industries, including paper and pulp, food products, pharmaceutical products, engineering and electronics. Kao Corporation uses palm and palm kernel oil as a raw material, using 96,100 tonnes of palm oil in 2013/14. Pulp is also used in the manufacture of its products.

Its operations are primarily in Brazil, but it also has an important presence in Argentina and Paraguay, as well as being present in Holland, Norway and Poland. It is a major player in the soy market.  It has three soy crushing facilities with an annual production capacity of over 2 million metric tons.  Amaggi is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Oji Holdings is a corporation involved in the pulp and paper industry at a producing, processing and manufacturing level. Its products include packaging materials, household products, print materials and more. In 2014, it was among the top five largest companies for forest, paper and packaging products by annual sales value globally, with a supply capacity of 2.4 million metric tons of pulp to market. Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A, which was one of the largest timber, paper and packaging companies in Brazil in 2014. There were also plans announced in 2015 to establish operations in Myanmar.

It is through PepsiCo's wholly owned subsidiary, Frito Lay, that it operates in the snack market. Through this subsidiary, PepsiCo has over 35% of the United States savoury snack market and Frito-Lay accounts for approximately a third of PepsiCo's annual sales. Kimberly-Clark Group, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, in the US, is a leading international company in the personal care, health and hygiene industry. It has a long history in supplying paper products for personal care, having been founded over 140 years ago in the state of Wisconsin in the US in 1870. The company produces feminine, adult, family, baby and child care products, as well as products for the professional and health care sectors, including diapers, facial and bathroom tissue, and paper towels. Its well-known brands include Kleenex, which was the world's pioneering facial tissue, and Huggies, a leading brand of diaper that is central to the company's multi-billion dollar baby-care business. It is the leading company in the retail tissue industry globally, and also occupies the second place amongst the top 100 forestry, paper and packaging companies globally, ranked by sales, in 2013.
The company has manufacturing facilities in 37 countries, including in India, Indonesia, Brazil, China and the Republic of Korea and its brands are sold in 175 countries worldwide. The company claims that almost 25% of the world's population purchase Kimberly-Clark Group products on a daily basis. Kimberly-Clark Group's branded tissue products consume significant amounts of wood fibre and pulp. In 2012, the company's manufacturing operations were responsible for the consumption of 4.4% of the total market pulp produced that year, and its products absorbed around 2.36 million air-dried metric tons of virgin wood fibre.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum, UN Global Compact

Koninklijke FrieslandCampina NV (Friesland) is a Dutch international dairy company. The company has four sections: Consumer Products Europe, Middle East and Africa; Consumer Products Asia; Cheese, Butter and Milk Powder; and finally Ingredients. It produces a wide range of products, including butter, cheese, condensed milk, cream, lactose, whey proteins, yoghurt and many others.
The company advertises itself as one of the top five dairy companies in the world. It is also the largest in Indonesia and Thailand, is in the top 5 for Malaysia and Western Europe and is in the global top 10 for baby food and dairy. It is also among the top 20 packaged food companies overall in the world.
Friesland operates 141 sites in over 26 countries, with the strongest presence in the Netherlands, where it can be found at 59 sites. The company employs 20,000 people and is supplied by 15,300 dairy farmers. Some it its most notable brands are Campina, Chocomel, Completa, Dutch Lady, Frisian Flag, Foremost, Betagen, Friesche Vlag and Fruttis, amongst others. Friesland used 90,000 tonnes of palm oil in its products in 2013. It has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2007.

PT Rajawali Corp. is an Indonesian investment holding company with diverse business interests including hospitality, media, logistics, mining, and agriculture.
