Kingfisher PLC (Kingfisher) is a home improvement company, operating chains of retail stores. Kingfisher is based in the UK and though its domestic market dominates its operations, it is also active overseas, with a presence throughout Europe and in China. 
The company is Europe's leading retailer in the DIY sector and it is the third largest globally. Kingfisher's operations date back to 1982, with the acquisition of FW Woolworth, with which came a small chain of B&Q DIY retail outlets. B&Q is now one of Kingfisher's main retail brands, along with Castorama, Brico Dept, Screwfix, and Koçta?. B&Q supplies DIY and garden products and stocks a number of wooden products, including garden sheds and indoor and outdoor furniture, wooden flooring, and construction, finishing and decorative timber. It has over 350 stores in the UK and Ireland, and 39 in China. B&Q opened its first stores in China in 1999, however after some initial problems in entering the market the company scaled back and restructured its operations to better adapt to the Chinese market, involving a focus on the local preference for 'Do-it-for-me' rather than the traditional 'Do-it-yourself' (DIY), which has stabilised its position as a leader in the somewhat fragmented market. 
Castorama is similarly a chain of home and garden stores, with over 100 outlets in France, 72 stores in Poland, and 20 in Russia. Brico Dept is a more specialist chain of stores, providing products for professional builders and more experienced consumers. The majority of Brico Dept's business is in France, where it has over 100 stores, but it also has stores in Spain and Romania. Screwfix has stores in the UK and provides tools and hardware products. Finally, Koçta? is Turkey's leading home improvement retailer, with 46 stores.

Avon Products (Avon) is a global manufacturer and marketer of beauty and cosmetic products. Through its representatives system, it sells skincare products, fragrances, hair products, and fashion items. In 2015, the company had sales operations in 57 countries, excluding the US where it owns a minority stake in New Avon, with top markets including Brazil, Mexico, Russia and the United Kingdom. It was among the top ten beauty and personal care companies in the world by market share. In 2015, Avon used 20,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

Carrefour is a large French retail group operating over 12,000 hypermarkets, supermarkets, and convenience stores in more than 30 countries in Europe, Latin America, and Asia. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Carrefour is one of the largest retailers globally, ranking among the top five by edible grocery sales. It is also among the five largest retailers in Europe and in Latin America.

Kering SA is a French company engaged in the retail and distribution of luxury goods, primarily apparel and accessories. Until 2013, the company was known as PPR, short for Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, which in turn was its official name until 2005.  Established in 1963, the company has its origins in the building materials industry and in particular in the timber trade. It then became a leader in the retail sector, before entering into the world of luxury goods with the purchase of the Gucci brand in 1999. Today the company has 22 brands operating in two core divisions: Luxury, which designs, manufactures and markets luxury apparel, leather goods, accessories, watches, jewellery, fragrances and cosmetics; and Sport and Lifestyle, which designs and produces footwear, apparel and accessories under the company's sporting brands.
Kering SA is headquartered in Paris, France and its brands in its luxury and sports and lifestyle segments, include several world famous brands including Puma, Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga and Stella McCartney, many of which have leather goods among their principal products,. Kering SA therefore plays a prominent role in the global trade in leather and animal skins, with several of the company's brands designing and selling leather goods. For example, it produces leather wallets and handbags under Saint Laurent  and Balenciaga. Through these and its numerous other brands, Kering SA holds the second largest market share in the bags and luggage sector globally. It also produces large amount s of leather footwear, for example under Sergio Rossi; a leading Italian shoe brand. Kering SA is among the top five manufacturers of footwear globally, occupying the fourth largest share of the global market in 2013, and in particular holding a leading position in the footwear market of Western Europe, especially in Italy. Kering SA is placing increasing emphasis on the direct sourcing of its raw materials, including leather. In 2013, it bought a majority stake in one the world's biggest producers of tanned skins and it has plans to build a new tanning facility in France, which could be operational by 2016.
initiatives: Company recognises the disastrous impacts of deforestation

rows.coprofile: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) is a leading processor and trader in agricultural commodities active in more than 100 countries. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soya in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company has significant oilseed crushing facilities in Brazil and Argentina, as well as having an annual capacity of several million metric tons in China. LDC is among the top ten soya exporters in Argentina and among the top five in Paraguay and Brazil. The company's palm oil operations are also significant with the company handling over 2 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in 2015. It is also a major producer of biodiesel.

Marks & Spencer Group PLC is the holding company for the Marks & Spencer Group (M&S). The company was established in 1884 as a single market stall in Leeds, UK and has since become a leading UK retailer, with 852 stores in the UK and a further 480 internationally in 59 territories. The company employs over 83,000 individuals. Further to this, M&S sells products online and through its franchise partners.
M&S sells a range of products, including food, homeware, and clothing for men, women and children, which it sources from around 2,000 suppliers globally. In the UK, the food segment comprises the majority of total sales, accounting for 57%, with the remainder made up of the general merchandise department. M&S' food division sells around 6,300 products, from everyday products, such as under the 'Simply M&S' brand range, to food for special occasions.
As a retailer, M&S is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. Palm oil and soya are found in some M&S food products. For example, palm oil and its derivatives are used as a vegetable oil, as a coating for dried fruit, and as a carrier for flavourings. The company also sells beef and has a commitment to source this commodity as well as palm oil and soya from sources that do not contribute to deforestation. Within M&S' women's and men's departments, the company sells a number of leather goods, such as leather boots and bags. M&S is also involved in the wood products industry and stocks a range of furniture items, including wooden garden furniture.

Standard Chartered are an international banking group headquartered in London, providing banking products and services for both personal and business customers. Their services include commercial banking and corporate finance, as well as retail banking, insurance, investment and wealth management. As of 2017, Standard Chartered's total assets stand at over 650 billion USD, their lending amounts to more than 260 billion USD, and they have nearly 60 billion USD in assets under management for private customers. Standard Chartered are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 30 billion dollars of loans to companies exposed to forest risk commodities, predominantly in the food products and agriculture sectors.

Mars Inc. (Mars) is a global leader in the confectionery industry, and also a significant player in the market for dried processed foods, sauces and condiments. The company was originally founded in 1891, and has its origins in the confectionery business, for which it remains most well-known. Headquartered in the state of Virginia in the US, Mars is the third largest private company in the America and employs over 65,000 'associates.' These associates work in 230 locations and factories in 68 countries worldwide. The company's operations are divided between six divisions: pet care products, chocolate, a variety of packaged food, chewing gum and candy under the Wrigley business segment, drinks and finally, scientific research under Mars Symbioscience.
Mars manufactures goods under numerous well-known global brands, including ready meal brands, Uncle Ben's and Suzi Wan, and chocolates brands including Maltesers, Bounty, Galaxy, M&Ms, Twix, Snickers and many more.  Mars sources a variety of raw materials to manufacture its diverse product range. Several forest risk commodities are among these, including beef, which comprises 3.6% of Mars' raw materials purchased by volume, as well as palm oil, soya and pulp and paper. In 2012/2013, Mars reported use of over 77,000 tonnes of palm oil, making its palm oil consumption higher than many other manufacturers.
Mars continues to increase its manufacturing capacity, opening a new $270 million chocolate plant in Kansas, America.  The company is also aiming to improve its market position in petcare through the planned acquisition of the IAMS, Eukanuba and Natura brands from Procter and Gamble for $2.9 billion. The company is also strong in its research and development with a new £6 million facility in Slough, United Kingdom that opened in 2012.

Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. The company’s landbank is one of the largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with approximately 300,000 hectares across Indonesia. It also owns a palm oil refinery alongside several processing and crushing facilities.   PT Astra International TBK is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Precious Woods is a Swiss based company involved in the cultivation, processing and trading of tropical timber. It manages forests in both Brazil and Gabon. In 2016, its Brazilian forestry concessions amounted to more than 500,000 hectares, making Precious Woods one of the largest Brazilian forestry companies. In Gabon, Precious Woods' forestry concessions total more than 600,000 hectares as of 2016. The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, which processed more than 200,000 cubic metres of timber in 2015. Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.

Proctor & Gamble is an American consumer goods manufacturer. The company produces laundry detergents, personal hygiene products, toilet paper, and toothpaste among many other products. Proctor & Gamble owns several well-known brands, such as Ariel, Head & Shoulders, Gillette, Tide, and Herbal Essence.   Procter & Gamble Co, The is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, pulp & paper and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Unilever is one of the largest consumer goods companies in the world, with 2 billion consumers using its products every day. Unilever's products are sold in more than 190 countries, reaching over 8.5 million shops. In 2014, the company had a turnover of $48.4 billion, with expanding sales in emerging markets contributing 57% of business. Unilever operates in a number of markets including food and beverages, and home and personal care. Its foods business generated 45% of operating profit in 2014, while personal care contributed 41%.
Unilever owns a number of well-known brands, notably Dove, Axe, Vaseline, Flora and Domestos. Through the manufacturing of these products, Unilever used 1.5 million MT of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in 2013-2014, equivalent to 2.6% of global production. 95% of its palm oil is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia. The company recognises the need to source its palm oil sustainably and currently purchases 100% of its palm oil as Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) certified, mainly via GreenPalm certificates. Further to this, the company's manufacturing facilities consume 1% of the world's soy, mostly procured from North America.
Unilever continues to focus on gaining a foothold in new and emerging markets. During 2014, the company launched new brands Lifebuoy and Omo in China and Saudi Arabia respectively, while new manufacturing facilities were established in Indonesia, China, the Philippines, and parts of Africa. In parallel, Unilever is consolidating business operations in North America to form more integrated, efficient supply chains.

Campbell Soup Co was founded in New Jersey, US, in 1869, when it began producing canned vegetables, soups, condiments and minced meats. The company now has annual sales of $8 billion and employs over 20,000 people. Its main business operations are divided into three divisions: simple meals (ready-made foods and soups); baked snacks; and health beverages and it has manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
The company's products are marketed under various brands, including Pepperidge Farms, which is the US division for cookies, crackers, bakery and frozen products and is led by 'Goldfish' crackers. However, the flagship Campbell's brand is the company's main source of revenue and is worth around US$2 billion. Through this brand, the company sells almost 2 billion cans of soup each year, accounting for 60% of the United States' market for canned soup. Campbell Soup Co continues to expand its range of products through investments into, and acquisitions of, other companies. For example, in 2013, the company acquired Bolthouse Farms, Plum Organics and Kelsen Group. During 2015, Campbell Soup Co. also plans to launch 200 new products, including protein drinks and bars.

IKEA Group is a leading company in the home furnishings industry that manufactures and sells affordable furniture and other goods for the home. Most of its furniture products are flat-packed and ready to be assembled at home by the customer. It operates throughout the supply chain, and is involved in the development, manufacturing, distribution and retail of products. The majority of the company's operations are in the retail sector, and though it sources products from external suppliers, it also produces many of its own products through Swedwood, the Group's industrial arm.
IKEA Group is based in Sweden and was established in 1943. It has a complicated corporate structure and since 1982, has been privately held by a foundation in the Netherlands, Stichting INGKA Foundation, which owns INGKA Holding B.V., the parent company of IKEA Group. The IKEA Group companies include Swedwood, IKEA of Sweden, and other departments, such as Purchasing and Distribution.
IKEA Group operates about 290 IKEA stores across 26 countries, in a franchise system under Inter IKEA Systems B.V. (Inter IKEA Systems B.V. officially owns the IKEA concept and is part of the Inter IKEA Group, which is a separate group of companies and under different ownership to the IKEA Group.) Added to these, IKEA has 40 stores in a further 15 countries, which are also operated under franchise but are owned outside of the IKEA Group.
IKEA Group operates internationally and is the leading home furnishings company and furniture retailer globally, occupying the leading position in the markets of Western Europe and the second place in the United States. IKEA Group is also the number one home furnishings company and furniture retailer in China and has plans to build upon its already significant position in the Chinese market by opening its first shopping mall there in 2014, with further stores planned for 2015. It also has a strong presence in Japan, Thailand and Taiwan, as well as in other regions worldwide.
As a leading manufacturer and retailer of furniture, IKEA uses large amounts of wood in its products. It is also a significant user of leather, which is used in sofas, rugs and some other products. The company used around four and half million square metres in furniture upholstering in 2013, over 40% of which was sourced from Brazil. It is also a significant user of palm oil, reporting total use of around 34,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. In an attempt to reduce its carbon footprint, IKEA replaced the paraffin used in its candles with palm stearin. The majority (80%) of the company's palm oil use is accounted for by its candles, with the remainder found in its food products.

The Hershey Company (Hershey's) was incorporated in Delaware, US in 1927, as a successor to a business founded in Philadelphia in 1894 by Milton S. Hershey. Today, the company sells and distributes its products in around 70 countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia. It claims to be the top chocolate and confectionary company in US by market share, where over 85% of Hershey's consolidated revenue is generated. Outside the US, the company's main countries of operation are Canada, Mexico, Brazil, China, India, Korea, and Japan. The company has 22,000 employees around the world and an annual turnover of over $7.4 billion. Hershey's has more than 80 brands  including Reese's, Mound, Almond Joy, Twizzlers , and it also shares a licensing agreement with Nestle to produce KitKat in America .  It has been a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member since 2011 and used 23,967 tonnes of palm oil in 2014, 100% of which is RSPO certified. Hershey's is focusing on expanding its business both through entry into new markets, such as the meat snack market through the acquisition of KRAVE Pure Foods, Inc., in March 2015, and through consolidating its operations in markets outside the US, such as through its acquisition in September 2015 of the remaining 49% of shares in its Bauducco/Pandurata Alimentos SA distribution joint venture in Brazil.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. In 2015, the group processed and traded more than 1.6 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.

Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio with the RTL group, publishing with Penguin Random House, and magazines with Gruner + Jahr. The most important markets are the US and Western Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.

Precious Woods is a Swiss based company involved in the cultivation, processing and trading of tropical timber. It manages forests in both Brazil and Gabon. In 2016, its Brazilian forestry concessions amounted to more than 500,000 hectares, making Precious Woods one of the largest Brazilian forestry companies. In Gabon, Precious Woods' forestry concessions total more than 600,000 hectares as of 2016. The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, which processed more than 200,000 cubic metres of timber in 2015. Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.

Deutsche Bank are a major bank based in Germany serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, securities, wealth management, asset management, and retail banking services. As of 2017, the bank's total assets amount to more than 1.5 trillion EUR, with approximately 400 billion EUR in net loans. Deutsche Bank is among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Mars is a global leader in the confectionary industry, and also a significant player in the market for processed food, drinks and pet care. It manufactures goods under well-known global brands including M&Ms, Uncle Ben’s and Royal Canin. The company uses significant quantities of palm oil in its confectionary items and food products. It is also exposed to the forest risk commodity soy through dairy ingredients and in its pet food products.  Mars Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Cargill is a US-based agribusiness company operating in 70 countries. Its business operations include the procurement, processing and trading of agricultural commodities, food products and industrial products, and it also offers financial solutions. It is one of the major players in the South American soya industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. Cargill is one of the major soya processors in Argentina and Brazil. It also has processing facilities in Paraguay, India and China. Cargill is one of the largest exporters of soya in South America, being especially prominent in Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay. The company also has significant palm oil operations, with about 60,000 hectares in Indonesia and a global annual fresh fruit bunch processing capacity of over 1.5 million tons as of 2015.

The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.

Sipef Group is a Belgian company, with subsidaries located in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and the Ivory Coast. It operates agro-industrial activities primarily in the production of oil palm products, as well as natural rubber, tea, bananas, flowers and foliage. Sipef Group is selected as powerbroker for palm oil.

Tesco started as a market stall in London in 1919, selling surplus groceries; its first store was opened ten years later in 1929. Following growth in the UK, Tesco floated on the London Stock Exchange in 1947. Today, Tesco is a multichannel grocery retailer active in eleven countries across Europe and Asia and also provides consumer financial services through its subsidiary, Tesco Bank. The company employs over 510,000 individuals and receives over 80 million shopping trips per week globally. In addition to its core grocery offering, in which it sells own branded and private label goods, Tesco sell a very broad range of other products including clothing, electronics, books and furniture. As a result of its large size and broad product range Tesco uses a range of forest risk commodities including, soy, beef, timber, paper and palm oil. In 2014, Tesco used 32,503 tons palm oil used in own brand products.

rows.coprofile: Sinar Mas is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including pulp and paper, agriculture and food, energy, financial services, and real estate. The group's agricultural business operates about 480,000 hectares of palm oil plantation as of 2016 and has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It also has an annual processing capacity of more than 12 million fresh fruit bunches and is one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.

Colgate-Palmolive is an American consumer goods company with products sold in over 200 countries around the world. Its products include oral, personal and home care, as well as pet nutrition products. Brands include Colgate, Palmolive and Sanex. It is a major global player across all its products areas. Globally, Colgate-Palmolive is one of the ten largest home care companies, and ranks among the top five for beauty and personal care and bath and shower products. Palm oil is a major ingredient in many products, with over 170,000 metric tons of palm oil products being used in 2015.

Estee Lauder is an American cosmetics company with products sold in 50 countries around the world. Products include skin care, hair care, makeup, and fragrances with well-known brands including Aveda, Jo Malone, and Estee Lauder itself. It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

The company has over 400 brands with products sold in over 190 countries, including many household names such as Lipton, Knorr, Dove and Hellman’s. Their brands include Flora, Rama, Blue Band, Proactiv, and Country Crock and own the vegan cheese brand Violife. They have been selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and soy.

Their services include an array of insurance solutions, as well as a significant asset management business. As of 2017, AXA's total assets amount to more than 870 billion EUR, with more than 1.1 trillion EUR of assets under management. They are among the top 15 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 2 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. AXA are also among the top 30 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 13 billion USD worth of shares.

Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. It also owns a palm oil refinery and has a 50% stake in another, alongside several processing and crushing facilities. In 2015, the company processed more than 1.7 million metric tons of crude palm oil.

Ferrero Group (Ferrero) is a family-owned confectionary business formally established in 1946 out of Pietro Ferrero's thriving factory in Piedmont, Italy. The company was one of the earliest in the Italian confectionery industry to expand overseas, with Michele Ferrero and his wife Maria Franca being the first Italians to open manufacturing operations in the confectionery business abroad after World War II. Until he passed away in February 2015, Michele Ferrero ranked 22nd on the Forbes list of billionaires and was the wealthiest man in Italy, worth $27 billion (though living in Monaco). His son Giovanni now runs the company, which operates in 51 countries worldwide and on every continent. The company has over 22,000 employees at 20 production and 3 research and development sites. In addition, the Ferrero Group has 8 agricultural companies for both direct cultivation and manufacturing purposes.
Ferrero is the fourth largest confectionary company in the world and in the past five years has rapidly expanded its sales in China and Russia. It owns many famous brands, including Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella, which was one of the company's first products in the 1940s. Ferrero uses palm oil in its confectionary to give products the right consistency. The company sources palm oil from Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and Brazil, using 150,000 tonnes annually.

Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

Precious Woods is a Swiss based company involved in the cultivation, processing and trading of tropical timber. It manages forests in both Brazil and Gabon. The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.  Precious Woods Holding AG is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

The first Walmart store opened in 1962 in Arkansas, US. The company floated in 1970 and since then has grown within the US and internationally. Now, in 2014, Walmart operates 11,500 stores, under 65 banners, in 28 countries and employs 2.2 million members of staff. Walmart is one of the world's largest retailers.
Walmart operates in four segments: Walmart US, Walmart International, Sam's Club and Global e-Commerce. Within the US, Walmart operates stores in a variety of different formats, the largest is the Supercenter. The approximately 180,000 square foot Supercenters provide grocery, fresh produce, clothing, electronics and home furnishings. Some Supercenters also include pharmacies, health clinics, restaurants and banks. At the other end of the scale Walmart's smallest format, Express stores, focus on groceries and general merchandise. Sam's Club is a wholesaler catering to consumer and small business members who want to buy both groceries and general merchandise in bulk. Sam's Club operates in the US and internationally.
Walmart is present in 27 countries outside of the US, operating grocery and retail operations both through wholly owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. Stores operate under Walmart and other banners: in the UK Walmart operates through ASDA; and in Asia (India, Japan and China) Walmart operates under banners such as Walmart and Seiyu. Walmart's 2011 acquisition of a majority stake of in Massmart Holdings Limited also gives it a presence in sub-Saharan Africa; the majority of its 350 stores are in South Africa. Walmart also operates throughout Latin America, again under both Walmart and local banners.
Walmart sells both private label and international brand goods. As one of the world's largest retailers,  Walmart uses significant volumes of forest risk commodities including beef, leather, pulp and paper, timber, soy and palm oil. In 2014, Walmart used 96,411 MT of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in its own brand products.
initiatives: PALM OIL, PULP & PAPER, SOYA, BEEF, TIMBER

Campbell Soup Co was founded in New Jersey, US, in 1869, when it began producing canned vegetables, soups, condiments and minced meats. The company now has annual sales of $8 billion and employs over 20,000 people. Its main business operations are divided into three divisions: simple meals (ready-made foods and soups); baked snacks; and health beverages and it has manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
The company's products are marketed under various brands, including Pepperidge Farms, which is the US division for cookies, crackers, bakery and frozen products and is led by 'Goldfish' crackers. However, the flagship Campbell's brand is the company's main source of revenue and is worth around US$2 billion. Through this brand, the company sells almost 2 billion cans of soup each year, accounting for 60% of the United States' market for canned soup. Campbell Soup Co continues to expand its range of products through investments into, and acquisitions of, other companies. For example, in 2013, the company acquired Bolthouse Farms, Plum Organics and Kelsen Group. During 2015, Campbell Soup Co. also plans to launch 200 new products, including protein drinks and bars.

Mars Inc. (Mars) is a global leader in the confectionery industry, and also a significant player in the market for dried processed foods, sauces and condiments. The company was originally founded in 1891, and has its origins in the confectionery business, for which it remains most well-known. Headquartered in the state of Virginia in the US, Mars is the third largest private company in the America and employs over 65,000 'associates.' These associates work in 230 locations and factories in 68 countries worldwide. The company's operations are divided between six divisions: pet care products, chocolate, a variety of packaged food, chewing gum and candy under the Wrigley business segment, drinks and finally, scientific research under Mars Symbioscience.
Mars manufactures goods under numerous well-known global brands, including ready meal brands, Uncle Ben's and Suzi Wan, and chocolates brands including Maltesers, Bounty, Galaxy, M&Ms, Twix, Snickers and many more.  Mars sources a variety of raw materials to manufacture its diverse product range. Several forest risk commodities are among these, including beef, which comprises 3.6% of Mars' raw materials purchased by volume, as well as palm oil, soya and pulp and paper. In 2012/2013, Mars reported use of over 77,000 tonnes of palm oil, making its palm oil consumption higher than many other manufacturers.
Mars continues to increase its manufacturing capacity, opening a new $270 million chocolate plant in Kansas, America.  The company is also aiming to improve its market position in petcare through the planned acquisition of the IAMS, Eukanuba and Natura brands from Procter and Gamble for $2.9 billion. The company is also strong in its research and development with a new £6 million facility in Slough, United Kingdom that opened in 2012.

Arla Foods is a dairy cooperative with activities around the world. The company's most prominent markets are the United Kingdom, Central Europe and Asia. Its products include milk, cheese, butter and cooking ingredients with brands such as Lurpak, Castello and Apetina. Arla Foods claimed to be among the top ten dairy companies in the world by revenue in 2015 and is one of the world's largest ingredient producers. Soya plays an important role in the cooperative's animal feed and palm oil is also used in its products, with about 25,000 metric tons being used in 2015.

BNP Paribas are a European banking group headquartered in France serving private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, capital markets, asset management, insurance and retail banking services. As of 2017, the group's total assets amount to more than 2 trillion EUR with approximately 700 billion EUR worth of loans and receivables. BNP Paribas are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 38 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 70 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 5 billion USD worth of shares.

Standard Chartered are an international banking group headquartered in London, providing banking products and services for both personal and business customers. Their services include commercial banking and corporate finance, as well as retail banking, insurance, investment and wealth management. As of 2017, Standard Chartered's total assets stand at over 650 billion USD, their lending amounts to more than 260 billion USD, and they have nearly 60 billion USD in assets under management for private customers. Standard Chartered are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, predominantly in the food products and agriculture sectors.

JBS is a global company involved in the beef, lamb and poultry processing, and in pork production.  It is among the largest producer of protein products worldwide, and is also involved in the production of leather, hygiene and cleaning products, collagen, metal packaging, biodiesel and other goods. JBS has operations spanning 24 countries and serves around 300,000 customers in 150 countries. 
Initially, the company was a small operation, with the capacity of processing five head of cattle per day. However, since 1953, JBS has expanded hugely, with major acquisitions in South America, the US, Australia and Europe. In 2007 JBS was floated on the Brazilian stock exchange, making it the first meat processing company in Brazil to do so. Today it is headquartered in Sao Paulo and employs around 185,000 people in total. Its operations are split between the following business divisions: JBS Mercosul, which comprises the company's beef and leather and related industries in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay; JBS USA, which is responsible for overseeing JBS' activities in Australia, Canada, the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico; and finally, JBS Foods, which was established in 2013 and covers the company's poultry, pork and value-added products in Brazil. 
The variety of products, which include fresh and frozen cuts to ready meals and processed foods service a variety of markets, including the catering, supermarket and export markets. These are marketed under several brands, including Bertin, Swift, and Friboi, and packaged foods, including ready meals under the Seara brand.
As well as its extensive operations in the global meat production and processing industries, which make beef of obvious significance, soya is also important, given its use in animal feed. For example, JBS operates 13 poultry farms, two pig farms and over 40 hatcheries, which use large amounts of animal feed. On top of its own operations, JBS also has around 5000 pig and poultry partner producers, which it provides with technical support and materials including all feed. Similarly within its beef operations, JBS operates cattle feedlots in Brazil the US and Australia where it provides all feed. Further to this, JBS is a significant player in the global leather industry, and with a daily processing capacity of one hundred thousand hides, leather processing is one of JBS' primary activities.

Carrefour is a large French retail group operating over 12,000 hypermarkets, supermarkets, and convenience stores in more than 30 countries in Europe, Latin America, and Asia. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Carrefour is one of the largest retailers globally, ranking among the top five by edible grocery sales. It is also among the five largest retailers in Europe and in Latin America.
initiatives: No mention of suppliers for beef, soy, or paper, so points only awarded for palm

rows.coprofile: Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio with the RTL group, publishing with Penguin Random House, and magazines with Gruner + Jahr. The most important markets are the US and Western Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.

Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd is a holding company for the Nippon Paper Group, which is comprised of around 180 affiliates and subsidiaries. The Group ranks among the top forest, paper and packaging companies globally, occupying sixth place in a worldwide ranking of the top 100 and the second position of such companies in Japan. The Group produces a variety of paper products, including newsprint, printing paper, copy paper, wrapping paper, linerboard, paperboard, tissue products, and healthcare products. For example, through its subsidiary Nippon Paper Crecia Co Ltd, the Group manufactures family care, personal care and professional products under a license agreement with leading hygiene products company, Kimberly-Clark.
The Group has diverse business interests on top of its activities in the paper sector, and several of Nippon Paper Groups's other operations also make use of wood products. For example, it has several subsidiaries active in the wood products and construction industry; in the procurement of lumber and the manufacture of construction materials. These subsidiaries include Nippon Paper Lumber Co., Ltd., PAL Co., Ltd., and Daishowa Uniboard Co., Ltd. Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd has a global network supplying logs and lumber from a variety of sources, including domestically and from the United States, Canada, Europe, New Zealand and some tropical regions. As well as supplying raw and sawn timber, Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd also manufactures plywood and laminated lumber products. Pal Co Ltd and Daishowa Uniboard Co Ltd manufacture products for use in the construction industry, such as doors, staircases, flooring and decorative laminates.

The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.

The L'Oreal Group is a French cosmetics company present in 140 countries. It is active in all branches of cosmetics, such as make-up, skin care, hair care and perfume, and its major brands include Garnier, Maybelline New York and Ralph Lauren. The group is one of the largest manufacturers of beauty and personal care products globally and is high up the list in many other categories. The group is especially prominent in Western Europe, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, and Brazil. In 2015, L'Oreal used about 55,000 metric tons of palm oil in its products.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, Palm Oil Innovation Group, Consumer Goods Forum

rows.coprofile: Lowe's Companies is a major home improvement company based in the US with operations in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. In 2015, Lowe's had one of largest market shares for DIY, furniture, and homeware in the world. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and is one of the top four leading home improvement companies worldwide.

Proctor & Gamble is an American consumer goods manufacturer. The company produces laundry detergents, personal hygiene products, toilet paper, and toothpaste among many other products. Proctor & Gamble owns several well-known brands, such as Ariel, Head & Shoulders, Gillette, Tide, and Herbal Essence.   Procter & Gamble Co, The is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, pulp & paper and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.

Marks & Spencer Group PLC is the holding company for the Marks & Spencer Group (M&S). The company was established in 1884 as a single market stall in Leeds, UK and has since become a leading UK retailer, with 852 stores in the UK and a further 480 internationally in 59 territories. The company employs over 83,000 individuals. Further to this, M&S sells products online and through its franchise partners.
M&S sells a range of products, including food, homeware, and clothing for men, women and children, which it sources from around 2,000 suppliers globally. In the UK, the food segment comprises the majority of total sales, accounting for 57%, with the remainder made up of the general merchandise department. M&S' food division sells around 6,300 products, from everyday products, such as under the 'Simply M&S' brand range, to food for special occasions.
As a retailer, M&S is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. Palm oil and soya are found in some M&S food products. For example, palm oil and its derivatives are used as a vegetable oil, as a coating for dried fruit, and as a carrier for flavourings. The company also sells beef and has a commitment to source this commodity as well as palm oil and soya from sources that do not contribute to deforestation. Within M&S' women's and men's departments, the company sells a number of leather goods, such as leather boots and bags. M&S is also involved in the wood products industry and stocks a range of furniture items, including wooden garden furniture.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum, New York Declaration on Forests, Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, UN Global Compact, Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including agribusiness, manufacturing, mining, and trading. The group’s palm oil subsidiary has one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers, it also has 5 palm oil mills and produces crude palm oil and palm kernel oil.  Triputra Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Cargill is a US-based agribusiness company operating in 70 countries. Its business operations include the procurement, processing and trading of agricultural commodities, food products and industrial products, and it also offers financial solutions. It is one of the major players in the South American soy industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company also has significant palm oil operations.  Cargill is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
initiatives:
United Nations Development Programme’s (UNDP)
Green Commodities Programme, Cerrado Working Group

rows.coprofile: Estee Lauder is an American cosmetics company with products sold in 50 countries around the world. Products include skin care, hair care, makeup, and fragrances with well-known brands including Aveda, Jo Malone, and Estee Lauder itself. It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

H&M Hennes and Mauritz AB is a Swedish clothing company operating under several brands, including its flagship brand H&M, as well as COS, Monki, Cheap Monday, and & Other Stories . The company, headquartered in Sweden, is involved in designing, manufacturing and marketing apparel, accessories and home textiles.  It was established in 1947, with the opening of its first Hennes store in Västerås, Sweden, which exclusively sold women's clothing. With the acquisition of hunting and fishing equipment store Mauritz Widforss in 1968, the company changed its name to Hennes & Mauritz and expanded its product range to also cover apparel for men and children. Since then, the company has expanded, opening stores throughout Europe as well as worldwide. For example, it expanded into the US in 2000, and opened stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2007. Further to this, the company established a new brand, COS, in 2007 and acquired the fashion firm, FaBric Scandinavien AB, in 2008, which holds the Weekday, Monki and Cheap Monday brands . In 2010, the full incorporation of FaBric Scandinavien was completed, when Hennes & Mauritz acquired the remaining 40% of shares.

Procter & Gamble Co (P&G) is one of the world's largest consumer packaged goods companies, with operations in approximately 70 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Ohio in the US, P&G manufactures and markets consumer products throughout the world, with its branded products such as Head & Shoulders and Oral-B being sold in over 180 countries. P&G's products are primarily sold through mass merchandisers, grocery stores and drug stores and are approximated to serve around 4.8 billion people worldwide.
P&G divides its operations between four main business segments: Beauty; Health and Grooming; Fabric and Home Care; and Baby, Feminine and Family Care.  Palm kernel oil and, to a lesser extent, palm oil  are used in the manufacture of its products, including in its beauty and household care products such as soaps and detergents. The combined use of palm kernel oil, palm oil and its derivatives was over 532,000 MT in 2013/14. P&G purchases from a variety of suppliers, typically four or five supply chain levels above the source plantation. Over 70% of palm oil and derivatives are sourced from Malaysia, supplemented by procurement from Indonesia, and Central and South America. P&G also purchases wood pulp for absorbent hygiene and tissue products. In the financial year 2013/14, P&G bought approximately 1.7 million air dried metric tons of pulp for use in these products, sourcing pulp from Latin America (34%), Canada (30%) and the US (36%).
initiatives: New York Declaration on Forests, WWF Global Forest & Trade Network, Consumer Goods Forum

rows.coprofile: Rabobank are a global banking group based in the Netherlands serving private and corporate clients. Their services include private banking, corporate finance, leasing, real estate, capital markets, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2021, Rabobank's total assets amount to more than 639 billion EUR. Rabobank are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans primarily in the agriculture, agricultural commodities, packaged food and food retail sectors. In the 2022 selection, Rabobank was providing 21 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

IKEA Group is a leading company in the home furnishings industry that manufactures and sells affordable furniture and other goods for the home. Most of its furniture products are flat-packed and ready to be assembled at home by the customer. It operates throughout the supply chain, and is involved in the development, manufacturing, distribution and retail of products. The majority of the company's operations are in the retail sector, and though it sources products from external suppliers, it also produces many of its own products through Swedwood, the Group's industrial arm.
IKEA Group is based in Sweden and was established in 1943. It has a complicated corporate structure and since 1982, has been privately held by a foundation in the Netherlands, Stichting INGKA Foundation, which owns INGKA Holding B.V., the parent company of IKEA Group. The IKEA Group companies include Swedwood, IKEA of Sweden, and other departments, such as Purchasing and Distribution.
IKEA Group operates about 290 IKEA stores across 26 countries, in a franchise system under Inter IKEA Systems B.V. (Inter IKEA Systems B.V. officially owns the IKEA concept and is part of the Inter IKEA Group, which is a separate group of companies and under different ownership to the IKEA Group.) Added to these, IKEA has 40 stores in a further 15 countries, which are also operated under franchise but are owned outside of the IKEA Group.
IKEA Group operates internationally and is the leading home furnishings company and furniture retailer globally, occupying the leading position in the markets of Western Europe and the second place in the United States. IKEA Group is also the number one home furnishings company and furniture retailer in China and has plans to build upon its already significant position in the Chinese market by opening its first shopping mall there in 2014, with further stores planned for 2015. It also has a strong presence in Japan, Thailand and Taiwan, as well as in other regions worldwide.
As a leading manufacturer and retailer of furniture, IKEA uses large amounts of wood in its products. It is also a significant user of leather, which is used in sofas, rugs and some other products. The company used around four and half million square metres in furniture upholstering in 2013, over 40% of which was sourced from Brazil. It is also a significant user of palm oil, reporting total use of around 34,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. In an attempt to reduce its carbon footprint, IKEA replaced the paraffin used in its candles with palm stearin. The majority (80%) of the company's palm oil use is accounted for by its candles, with the remainder found in its food products.
initiatives: PALM OIL, PULP & PAPER, TIMBER, LEATHER

General Mills Inc. is a global food business with net sales of $19.2 billion in fiscal 2014. The company's foundations can be traced back to two flour mills built in Minneapolis, US, in the 1860s, and General Mills Inc. was established in its current form when it listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 1928. General Mills Inc. sells its products in over 100 countries, with approximately two thirds of sales originating domestically in the US. The company offers cereals, baking products, snacks, frozen foods, ready meals, dairy and vegetables.
General Mills Inc. owns a number of globally recognised brands, including ice cream brand Hagen-Dazs, breakfast products brands Nature Valley and Cheerios, and Brazilian food brand, Yoki. Its operations in the dairy market include those through its business Yoplait, in which General Mills Inc. gained a controlling stake (51%) in 2011. The company also has a joint venture with Nestle, called Cereal Partners Worldwide, which markets cereals produced by General Mills Inc. in 130 countries worldwide. As of 2008, General Mills Inc. manufactures its products in 79 plants, employing a workforce of 43,000 people in 2014. The company continues to focus on expansion, particularly in emerging markets including India, the Middle East, Indonesia and North Africa. For example, in June 2015 the Yoplait brand was expanded into China. General Mills uses palm oil and soya in the production of their food products such as snacks and cereal, with 61,148 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derivatives utilised by the company in 2013/14.

Grupo Jari, founded in 1994, is a prominent company in the forestry, paper and packaging sectors in Brazil. It claims to be one of the largest producers of corrugated cardboard packaging in Brazil and is responsible for 3% of eucalyptus pulp on the international market.
In 2010, the Group reported that it was responsible for 1.3 million hectares of forest in the Brazilian Amazon, including 545,000 hectares of native forest and 120,000 hectares authorised for plantations. The Group's native forests are located in the Vale do Jari, on the border of the states of ParÃ¡ and AmapÃ¡. According to Brazil's National Confederation of Industry (CNI), Grupo Jari is responsible for the largest area of natural forests under sustainable management in the Brazilian Amazon and is one of the country's principal producers of sawnwood. Grupo Jari produces sawn timber for the furniture and construction industries. Although it represented just 0.3% of total sawnwood production from the Brazilian Amazon in 2010, this is significant given that Brazil is the top producer of tropical sawnwood globally, responsible for 37.54% of total production from all ITTO producer countries (2007-2012). 
Jari was initially made up of three companies: Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A.; Jari Florestal; and Ouro Verde Amazonia. In 2012, however, Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A. and US-based firm, International Paper, formed a joint corrugated packaging venture: Orsa International Paper Embalagens S.A. Having originally owned 75% of the joint venture, International Paper acquired the remainder in 2014 and is therefore is now in charge of Jari Celulose's packaging assets. Groupo Jari also partners with a number of companies manufacturing construction materials, such as wooden decks and flooring, for overseas retailers.

The Danone Group was formed following the merger of BSN and Gervais Danone in 1972; however, the company's origins can be traced back to Spain, where Danone was founded in 1919 in Barcelona, specialising in yogurt products to treat intestinal disorders. The company then expanded to France and the US. BSN was founded later in 1966, and following a series of acquisitions became a top producer of mineral water, beer and baby food. Once merged, the Danone Group conducted numerous acquisitions and embarked on a global expansion, acquiring companies in Eastern Europe, Latin America, and Asia; Danone Group's first acquisition in Asia was the soy sauce and frozen food manufacturer, Amoy, in 1991.
Today the Group's portfolio is based on the company's mission to  "bring health through food to as many people as possible", with the group having divested in its operations in beer, biscuits and sauces in favour of a focus on fresh dairy products, early life nutrition, medical nutrition and water . It operates in more than 140 countries worldwide, with its top markets being France, Russia, the US and China.
Sales in the Fresh Dairy Products range account for just under 60% of the group's consolidated sales, and Danone Group ranks as the global leader in the dairy products industry worldwide. Sales in the Early Life Nutrition range make up around one fifth of the group's total sales, and Danone therefore also occupies a similarly high market share of the global baby food market, ranking in second place overall . Further to this, Danone Group is among the top five packaged food manufacturers globally.
Several forest risk commodities are relevant to Danone's operations, with the company using soya upstream in their supply chain in the form of animal feed for dairy operations as well as paper and packaging for their products. The group uses palm oil in a variety of its nutrition products, and in 2014, reported to the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil total use of 25,000 tonnes of refined palm oil or RBD palm oil and around 500 tonnes of palm kernel oil.

Sinar Mas is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including pulp and paper, agriculture and food, energy, financial services, and real estate. The group's agricultural business operates about 480,000 hectares of palm oil plantation as of 2016 and has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It also has an annual processing capacity of more than 12 million fresh fruit bunches and is one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Its products include cooking oil and margarine. Additionally, the group crushes soya, with an annual capacity of 2.3 million metric tons. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.

Colgate-Palmolive is an American consumer goods company with products sold in over 200 countries around the world. Its products include oral, personal and home care, as well as pet nutrition products. Brands include Colgate, Palmolive and Sanex. It is a major global player across all its products areas. Globally, Colgate-Palmolive is one of the largest home care and beauty and personal care companies.   Colgate-Palmolive Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and beef.

Ferrero Group (Ferrero) is a family-owned confectionary business formally established in 1946 out of Pietro Ferrero's thriving factory in Piedmont, Italy. The company was one of the earliest in the Italian confectionery industry to expand overseas, with Michele Ferrero and his wife Maria Franca being the first Italians to open manufacturing operations in the confectionery business abroad after World War II. Until he passed away in February 2015, Michele Ferrero ranked 22nd on the Forbes list of billionaires and was the wealthiest man in Italy, worth $27 billion (though living in Monaco). His son Giovanni now runs the company, which operates in 51 countries worldwide and on every continent. The company has over 22,000 employees at 20 production and 3 research and development sites. In addition, the Ferrero Group has 8 agricultural companies for both direct cultivation and manufacturing purposes.
Ferrero is the fourth largest confectionary company in the world and in the past five years has rapidly expanded its sales in China and Russia. It owns many famous brands, including Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella, which was one of the company's first products in the 1940s. Ferrero uses palm oil in its confectionary to give products the right consistency. The company sources palm oil from Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and Brazil, using 150,000 tonnes annually.

The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.

It is one of the major players in the South American soya industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. Cargill is one of the major soya processors in Argentina and Brazil. It also has processing facilities in Paraguay, India and China. Cargill is one of the largest exporters of soya in South America, being especially prominent in Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay. The company also has significant palm oil operations, with about 60,000 hectares in Indonesia and a global annual fresh fruit bunch processing capacity of over 1.5 million tons as of 2015.

Marks & Spencer Group PLC is the holding company for the Marks & Spencer Group (M&S). The company was established in 1884 as a single market stall in Leeds, UK and has since become a leading UK retailer, with 852 stores in the UK and a further 480 internationally in 59 territories. The company employs over 83,000 individuals. Further to this, M&S sells products online and through its franchise partners.
M&S sells a range of products, including food, homeware, and clothing for men, women and children, which it sources from around 2,000 suppliers globally. In the UK, the food segment comprises the majority of total sales, accounting for 57%, with the remainder made up of the general merchandise department. M&S' food division sells around 6,300 products, from everyday products, such as under the 'Simply M&S' brand range, to food for special occasions.
As a retailer, M&S is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. Palm oil and soya are found in some M&S food products. For example, palm oil and its derivatives are used as a vegetable oil, as a coating for dried fruit, and as a carrier for flavourings. The company also sells beef and has a commitment to source this commodity as well as palm oil and soya from sources that do not contribute to deforestation. Within M&S' women's and men's departments, the company sells a number of leather goods, such as leather boots and bags. M&S is also involved in the wood products industry and stocks a range of furniture items, including wooden garden furniture.

Kimberly-Clark Group, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, in the US, is a leading international company in the personal care, health and hygiene industry. It has a long history in supplying paper products for personal care, having been founded over 140 years ago in the state of Wisconsin in the US in 1870. The company produces feminine, adult, family, baby and child care products, as well as products for the professional and health care sectors, including diapers, facial and bathroom tissue, and paper towels. Its well-known brands include Kleenex, which was the world's pioneering facial tissue, and Huggies, a leading brand of diaper that is central to the company's multi-billion dollar baby-care business. It is the leading company in the retail tissue industry globally, and also occupies the second place amongst the top 100 forestry, paper and packaging companies globally, ranked by sales, in 2013.
The company has manufacturing facilities in 37 countries, including in India, Indonesia, Brazil, China and the Republic of Korea and its brands are sold in 175 countries worldwide. The company claims that almost 25% of the world's population purchase Kimberly-Clark Group products on a daily basis. Kimberly-Clark Group's branded tissue products consume significant amounts of wood fibre and pulp. In 2012, the company's manufacturing operations were responsible for the consumption of 4.4% of the total market pulp produced that year, and its products absorbed around 2.36 million air-dried metric tons of virgin wood fibre.

General Mills Inc. is a global food business with net sales of $19.2 billion in fiscal 2014. The company's foundations can be traced back to two flour mills built in Minneapolis, US, in the 1860s, and General Mills Inc. was established in its current form when it listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 1928. General Mills Inc. sells its products in over 100 countries, with approximately two thirds of sales originating domestically in the US. The company offers cereals, baking products, snacks, frozen foods, ready meals, dairy and vegetables.
General Mills Inc. owns a number of globally recognised brands, including ice cream brand Hagen-Dazs, breakfast products brands Nature Valley and Cheerios, and Brazilian food brand, Yoki. Its operations in the dairy market include those through its business Yoplait, in which General Mills Inc. gained a controlling stake (51%) in 2011. The company also has a joint venture with Nestle, called Cereal Partners Worldwide, which markets cereals produced by General Mills Inc. in 130 countries worldwide. As of 2008, General Mills Inc. manufactures its products in 79 plants, employing a workforce of 43,000 people in 2014. The company continues to focus on expansion, particularly in emerging markets including India, the Middle East, Indonesia and North Africa. For example, in June 2015 the Yoplait brand was expanded into China. General Mills uses palm oil and soya in the production of their food products such as snacks and cereal, with 61,148 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derivatives utilised by the company in 2013/14.

rows.coprofile: Henkel AG & Co. KGaA (Henkel) is a manufacturing company, headquartered in Germany, which operates in both the consumer and business markets. It operates worldwide in three key areas: Laundry and Home Care; Beauty Care; and Adhesive Technologies. Famous brands include Persil and Schwarzkopf. Products sold under these brands (such as laundry detergents, household cleaners and cosmetic products) commonly contain surfactants that consist of palm oil derivatives. Surfactants are an active substance, not produced by Henkel directly but purchased from third party suppliers €“ mineral oils, natural gas, coconut oil, and palm kernel oil are currently the only ingredients able to produce surfactants on an industrial scale. According to Henkel, in 2013, through surfactant and other raw material purchasing, the company used around 71,608 tonnes of palm oil products, mostly comprising palm kernel oil.

IOI Corporation is a global, vertically integrated palm oil company active throughout the supply chain from cultivation to manufacturing. The company has one of the top ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with more than 225,000 hectares of plantation land in Indonesia and Malaysia. Its 15 mills have an annual capacity for more than 4.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches. Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Aside from their cereal products, Kellogg Co also manufactures a number of snacks and frozen foods, including crisps, ready-meals, meat alternatives and biscuits. These products are sold through several well-known brands including Kellogg's, Fruit loops, Kashi, Pringles and Keebler. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. Notably, the company is building a new facility in Malaysia to take advantage of the rapidly growing Asia Pacific market.  This facility, due to be operational from mid-2015, is set to produce halal Pringles and other snacks, and will create over 300 jobs. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.
As a major manufacturer of packaged food, Kellogg Co uses both soya and palm oil. For example, palm oil is used in a variety of the company's branded products, such as in its cookies and waffles, and soya is used in cereal, such as in Kellogg's Smart Start Soy Protein.

Ferrero Group (Ferrero) is a family-owned confectionary business formally established in 1946 out of Pietro Ferrero's thriving factory in Piedmont, Italy. The company was one of the earliest in the Italian confectionery industry to expand overseas, with Michele Ferrero and his wife Maria Franca being the first Italians to open manufacturing operations in the confectionery business abroad after World War II. Until he passed away in February 2015, Michele Ferrero ranked 22nd on the Forbes list of billionaires and was the wealthiest man in Italy, worth $27 billion (though living in Monaco). His son Giovanni now runs the company, which operates in 51 countries worldwide and on every continent. The company has over 22,000 employees at 20 production and 3 research and development sites. In addition, the Ferrero Group has 8 agricultural companies for both direct cultivation and manufacturing purposes.
Ferrero is the fourth largest confectionary company in the world and in the past five years has rapidly expanded its sales in China and Russia. It owns many famous brands, including Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella, which was one of the company's first products in the 1940s. Ferrero uses palm oil in its confectionary to give products the right consistency. The company sources palm oil from Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and Brazil, using 150,000 tonnes annually.

The company claims to be the world's leading manufacturer of specialty vegetable fats and is a major company in the global bakery ingredients market. Soya sourced from South America as well as palm oil and its derivatives sourced from Central America and Southeast Asia are used in these products by the company. In 2015, AAK used over 950,000 metric tons of palm oil and its derivatives in its products.

IOI Corporation is a global, vertically integrated palm oil company active throughout the supply chain from cultivation to manufacturing. The company has one of the top ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with more than 225,000 hectares of plantation land in Indonesia and Malaysia. Its 15 mills have an annual capacity for more than 4.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches. IOI also owns four refineries in Malaysia and the Netherlands with an annual capacity of more than 3 million metric tons. Its products include oleochemicals and specialty oils and fats for the food industry.

The Danone Group was formed following the merger of BSN and Gervais Danone in 1972; however, the company's origins can be traced back to Spain, where Danone was founded in 1919 in Barcelona, specialising in yogurt products to treat intestinal disorders. The company then expanded to France and the US. BSN was founded later in 1966, and following a series of acquisitions became a top producer of mineral water, beer and baby food. Once merged, the Danone Group conducted numerous acquisitions and embarked on a global expansion, acquiring companies in Eastern Europe, Latin America, and Asia; Danone Group's first acquisition in Asia was the soy sauce and frozen food manufacturer, Amoy, in 1991.
Today the Group's portfolio is based on the company's mission to  "bring health through food to as many people as possible", with the group having divested in its operations in beer, biscuits and sauces in favour of a focus on fresh dairy products, early life nutrition, medical nutrition and water . It operates in more than 140 countries worldwide, with its top markets being France, Russia, the US and China.
Sales in the Fresh Dairy Products range account for just under 60% of the group's consolidated sales, and Danone Group ranks as the global leader in the dairy products industry worldwide. Sales in the Early Life Nutrition range make up around one fifth of the group's total sales, and Danone therefore also occupies a similarly high market share of the global baby food market, ranking in second place overall . Further to this, Danone Group is among the top five packaged food manufacturers globally.
Several forest risk commodities are relevant to Danone's operations, with the company using soya upstream in their supply chain in the form of animal feed for dairy operations as well as paper and packaging for their products. The group uses palm oil in a variety of its nutrition products, and in 2014, reported to the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil total use of 25,000 tonnes of refined palm oil or RBD palm oil and around 500 tonnes of palm kernel oil.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.  Permata Hijau Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Kellogg Co was originally established in 1906 as the Battle Creek Toasted Corn Flake Company. They are now the world's largest cereal company, manufacturing around 1,600 products in 18 countries, and marketing these in more than 180 countries worldwide. Aside from their cereal products, Kellogg Co also manufactures a number of snacks and frozen foods, including crisps, ready-meals, meat alternatives and biscuits. These products are sold through several well-known brands including Kellogg's, Fruit loops, Kashi, Pringles and Keebler. Despite already operating a number of manufacturing facilities across the globe, Kellogg Co continues to expand its supply chain into new areas. Notably, the company is building a new facility in Malaysia to take advantage of the rapidly growing Asia Pacific market.  This facility, due to be operational from mid-2015, is set to produce halal Pringles and other snacks, and will create over 300 jobs. In total, they currently operate manufacturing, distribution and warehouse facilities totalling more than 35 million square feet, both in the US and internationally.
As a major manufacturer of packaged food, Kellogg Co uses both soya and palm oil. For example, palm oil is used in a variety of the company's branded products, such as in its cookies and waffles, and soya is used in cereal, such as in Kellogg's Smart Start Soy Protein.

Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV (Grupo Bimbo) was founded by Lorenzo Servitje in Mexico in 1945. International expansion began in 1989, resulting in Grupo Bimbo becoming the largest bakery company in the world in terms of sales and production volume. The company's main markets are the US and Mexico but it also operates in Central and Latin America, Canada, Asia and Europe. In 2014, net sales were $14.1 billion. The company has 167 manufacturing plants located largely in its key markets, with 85 plants in the US and 39 in Mexico. In addition to its global manufacturing facilities, the company operates a distribution network with over 52,000 routes, feeding into 2.2 million points of sale in 19 countries. Today, Grupo Bimbo employs over 21,000 individuals.
Grupo Bimbo produces more than 10,000 different products under 100 umbrella brands including Bimbo, New York Bakery Co., Marisela and Ricolino. It manufactures bread, potato crisps, pastries and a variety of other snacks, many of which contain palm oil. The company continues to expand its business in international markets; it recently completed the acquisition of the previously public-listed company, Canada Bread, for $1.83 billion.

Its business is located in Africa and Asia, with plantations in Sierra Leone, the Ivory Coast, Nigeria, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ghana, São Tomé and Indonesia.  Socfin Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Mars is a global leader in the confectionary industry, and also a significant player in the market for processed food, drinks and pet care. It manufactures goods under well-known global brands including M&Ms, Uncle Ben’s and Royal Canin. The company uses significant quantities of palm oil in its confectionary items and food products. It is also exposed to the forest risk commodity soy through dairy ingredients and in its pet food products.  Mars Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Rabobank are a global banking group based in the Netherlands serving private and corporate clients. Their services include private banking, corporate finance, leasing, real estate, capital markets, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2017, Rabobank's total assets amount to more than 620 billion EUR, with private sector loans of more than 410 billion EUR. Rabobank are among the top 25 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 15 billion USD primarily in the agriculture, agricultural commodities, packaged food and food retail sectors.

Musim Mas is a fully integrated palm oil corporation involved throughout the palm oil supply chain, from cultivation to processing, manufacturing and trading. The company has one of the largest landbanks globally for oil palm and is among the top five importers and exporters of palm oil from Indonesia.  MUSIM MAS is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.
initiatives: Fire Free Alliance (FFA), Decent Rural Living Initiative, High Carbon Stock (HCS) Approach Steering Group

rows.coprofile: The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.
Danone, Groupe was selected as a powerbroker for Soy (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Cocoa (Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer)
initiatives: Forest Positive Coalition (FPC), SBTN Corporate Engagement Program,
