IKEA Group is a leading company in the home furnishings industry that manufactures and sells affordable furniture and other goods for the home. Most of its furniture products are flat-packed and ready to be assembled at home by the customer. It operates throughout the supply chain, and is involved in the development, manufacturing, distribution and retail of products. The majority of the company's operations are in the retail sector, and though it sources products from external suppliers, it also produces many of its own products through Swedwood, the Group's industrial arm.
IKEA Group is based in Sweden and was established in 1943. It has a complicated corporate structure and since 1982, has been privately held by a foundation in the Netherlands, Stichting INGKA Foundation, which owns INGKA Holding B.V., the parent company of IKEA Group. The IKEA Group companies include Swedwood, IKEA of Sweden, and other departments, such as Purchasing and Distribution.
IKEA Group operates about 290 IKEA stores across 26 countries, in a franchise system under Inter IKEA Systems B.V. (Inter IKEA Systems B.V. officially owns the IKEA concept and is part of the Inter IKEA Group, which is a separate group of companies and under different ownership to the IKEA Group.) Added to these, IKEA has 40 stores in a further 15 countries, which are also operated under franchise but are owned outside of the IKEA Group.
IKEA Group operates internationally and is the leading home furnishings company and furniture retailer globally, occupying the leading position in the markets of Western Europe and the second place in the United States. IKEA Group is also the number one home furnishings company and furniture retailer in China and has plans to build upon its already significant position in the Chinese market by opening its first shopping mall there in 2014, with further stores planned for 2015. It also has a strong presence in Japan, Thailand and Taiwan, as well as in other regions worldwide.
As a leading manufacturer and retailer of furniture, IKEA uses large amounts of wood in its products. It is also a significant user of leather, which is used in sofas, rugs and some other products. The company used around four and half million square metres in furniture upholstering in 2013, over 40% of which was sourced from Brazil. It is also a significant user of palm oil, reporting total use of around 34,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. In an attempt to reduce its carbon footprint, IKEA replaced the paraffin used in its candles with palm stearin. The majority (80%) of the company's palm oil use is accounted for by its candles, with the remainder found in its food products.
initiatives: Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group, UN Global Compact

rows.coprofile: BASF is one of the world’s leading chemical companies, operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF’s home and personal care offerings.  BASF Personal Care and Nutrition GmbH is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group's two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.6 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.

The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.
In addition to its major Starbucks brand the company also operates: Seattles Best Coffee, Teavana, Tazo, Evolution Fresh, La Boulange (bakery brand) and Torrefazione Italia Coffee. Starbucks is the largest cafe/bar owner in the world with revenues of $14.9bn. Starbucks uses paper in its packaging, soya (in milk) and palm oil (in its food products).

Neste Oil OYJ (Neste) is an oil refining company producing traditional fuels such as gasoline and diesel as well as renewable products. The company's main market is the Baltic region and it has refineries in Finland, the Netherlands and Singapore. The Singapore refinery was claimed to be the world's largest for palm oil when it was opened in 2010. Neste is one of the world's largest producers of biodiesel. Palm oil is a major ingredient of the company's biofuels with more than 850,000 metric tons of crude palm oil being used in 2015.

The Société Financière des Caoutchoucs (SOCFIN) is an agribusiness group active in the cultivation, processing and trading of palm oil. This means SOCFIN's landbank is among the top fifteen largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. The group has 26 processing facilities in numerous countries which produced about 360,000 metric tons of palm oil in 2015.

Danone is a French company known to be one of the largest producers of dairy food and water in the world. The company is present in over 140 countries selling fresh dairy products, waters, baby nutrition, and medical nutrition. Some of its well-known brands include Activia, Oikos, Danonino, and Evian. The company is exposed to palm oil as an ingredient and soy as a key component of animal feed.  Danone is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Kering SA is a luxury goods group comprising fashion houses, leather goods companies and jewellery makers. The group’s brands include Gucci, Bottega Veneta, Saint Laurent and Alexander McQueen, amongst many others.  As a leading producer of apparel, luggage and footwear products, Kering SA plays a prominent role in the global trade of leather and animal skins. Kering S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is an American company involved in the global cultivation, processing, manufacturing and trading of agricultural commodities, ingredients for food and animal feed, as well as biofuels. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soya in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is among the top five  processors of soya in Brazil with an annual capacity of around 4 million metric tons in 2016, and is a leading player in Bolivia and Paraguay. Additionally, ADM is one of the world's major biodiesel producers with a reported production capacity of more than 135 million barrels per day. It is also involved in the palm oil supply chain and has an ownership interest in Wilmar International.

Neste Oyj is a Finland-based company engaged in the refining and marketing of petroleum and petroleum related products. The company’s main market is the Baltic region and it has refineries in Finland, the Netherlands and Singapore and also exports oil and renewable fuels to other markets, which include the US, Sweden, Canada, Germany, and the UK. Neste is one of the world’s largest producers of biodiesel. Palm oil is a major ingredient of the company’s biofuels.  Neste Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and soy.

rows.coprofile: Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. The company’s landbank is one of the largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with approximately 300,000 hectares across Indonesia. It also owns a palm oil refinery alongside several processing and crushing facilities.   PT Astra International TBK is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Grupo Jari, founded in 1994, is a prominent company in the forestry, paper and packaging sectors in Brazil. It claims to be one of the largest producers of corrugated cardboard packaging in Brazil and is responsible for 3% of eucalyptus pulp on the international market.
In 2010, the Group reported that it was responsible for 1.3 million hectares of forest in the Brazilian Amazon, including 545,000 hectares of native forest and 120,000 hectares authorised for plantations. The Group's native forests are located in the Vale do Jari, on the border of the states of ParÃ¡ and AmapÃ¡. According to Brazil's National Confederation of Industry (CNI), Grupo Jari is responsible for the largest area of natural forests under sustainable management in the Brazilian Amazon and is one of the country's principal producers of sawnwood. Grupo Jari produces sawn timber for the furniture and construction industries. Although it represented just 0.3% of total sawnwood production from the Brazilian Amazon in 2010, this is significant given that Brazil is the top producer of tropical sawnwood globally, responsible for 37.54% of total production from all ITTO producer countries (2007-2012). 
Jari was initially made up of three companies: Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A.; Jari Florestal; and Ouro Verde Amazonia. In 2012, however, Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A. and US-based firm, International Paper, formed a joint corrugated packaging venture: Orsa International Paper Embalagens S.A. Having originally owned 75% of the joint venture, International Paper acquired the remainder in 2014 and is therefore is now in charge of Jari Celulose's packaging assets. Groupo Jari also partners with a number of companies manufacturing construction materials, such as wooden decks and flooring, for overseas retailers.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. In 2015, the group processed and traded more than 1.6 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.

The L'Oreal Group is a French cosmetics company present in 140 countries. It is active in all branches of cosmetics, such as make-up, skin care, hair care and perfume, and its major brands include Garnier, Maybelline New York and Ralph Lauren. The group is one of the largest manufacturers of beauty and personal care products globally and is high up the list in many other categories. The group is especially prominent in Western Europe, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, and Brazil. In 2015, L'Oreal used about 55,000 metric tons of palm oil in its products.

The Société Financière des Caoutchoucs (SOCFIN) is an agribusiness group active in the cultivation, processing and trading of palm oil. Its business is located in Africa and Asia, with plantations in Sierra Leone, the Ivory Coast, Nigeria, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ghana, São Tomé and Indonesia.  Socfin Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Marks & Spencer Group PLC is the holding company for the Marks & Spencer Group (M&S). The company was established in 1884 as a single market stall in Leeds, UK and has since become a leading UK retailer, with 852 stores in the UK and a further 480 internationally in 59 territories. The company employs over 83,000 individuals. Further to this, M&S sells products online and through its franchise partners.
M&S sells a range of products, including food, homeware, and clothing for men, women and children, which it sources from around 2,000 suppliers globally. In the UK, the food segment comprises the majority of total sales, accounting for 57%, with the remainder made up of the general merchandise department. M&S' food division sells around 6,300 products, from everyday products, such as under the 'Simply M&S' brand range, to food for special occasions.
As a retailer, M&S is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. Palm oil and soya are found in some M&S food products. For example, palm oil and its derivatives are used as a vegetable oil, as a coating for dried fruit, and as a carrier for flavourings. The company also sells beef and has a commitment to source this commodity as well as palm oil and soya from sources that do not contribute to deforestation. Within M&S' women's and men's departments, the company sells a number of leather goods, such as leather boots and bags. M&S is also involved in the wood products industry and stocks a range of furniture items, including wooden garden furniture.

Koninklijke FrieslandCampina NV (Friesland) is a Dutch international dairy company. The company has four sections: Consumer Products Europe, Middle East and Africa; Consumer Products Asia; Cheese, Butter and Milk Powder; and finally Ingredients. It produces a wide range of products, including butter, cheese, condensed milk, cream, lactose, whey proteins, yoghurt and many others.
The company advertises itself as one of the top five dairy companies in the world. It is also the largest in Indonesia and Thailand, is in the top 5 for Malaysia and Western Europe and is in the global top 10 for baby food and dairy. It is also among the top 20 packaged food companies overall in the world.
Friesland operates 141 sites in over 26 countries, with the strongest presence in the Netherlands, where it can be found at 59 sites. The company employs 20,000 people and is supplied by 15,300 dairy farmers. Some it its most notable brands are Campina, Chocomel, Completa, Dutch Lady, Frisian Flag, Foremost, Betagen, Friesche Vlag and Fruttis, amongst others. Friesland used 90,000 tonnes of palm oil in its products in 2013. It has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2007.

The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.  Precious Woods Holding AG is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

Schroders are a financial services company headquartered in the UK offering wealth management and asset management services for private, corporate and institutional clients. As of 2021, Schroders have more than £615 billion of assets under management. They are one of the top shareholders in Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, Schroders was providing 18.5 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

It has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. Eagle High Plantations also has an annual processing capacity of 2.3 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches.  PT Rajawali Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Hershey is an American chocolate manufacturer. Hershey has many well-known brands, including Kit Kat, Reese’s, ROLO, and Twizzlers. The company have operations in more than 70 countries, and is one of the largest chocolate manufacturers in North America. Hershey is exposed to palm oil and soy as ingredients and to soy hidden in the animal feed for dairy products.    Hershey Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

PepsiCo is a global food and beverage company. The company’s products are being sold in more than 200 countries, through famous brands such as Pepsi, Lays, Tropicana, Quaker, Walkers, Starbucks, and Doritos. Products include beverages, snacks, cereals, and biscuits.   PepsiCo Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Home Depot Inc. is a leading home improvement retailer, selling construction materials and products for the home and garden. It was founded in 1978 in Atlanta, Georgia in the US, where the company now has its headquarters. Since the opening of its first two stores in Atlanta in 1979, the company has grown to become the largest retailer in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector both in the US and globally. According to Home Depot, it is the fourth largest retailer in the US and the fifth largest in the world. Home Depot provides a range of products, including building materials, home improvement supplies, indoor and outdoor furniture, tools, and garden products for customers undertaking DIY activities.
The company has over 2,200 specialist stores throughout the US, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, China, Canada and Mexico. It entered the Canadian market in 1994 and now has 182 stores in ten of Canada's provinces. It entered the Mexican market in 2011, and has since become Mexico's largest home improvement retailer, with a total of 114 stores in the country. Home Depot's presence in China increased through its acquisition of The Home Way; China's first home improvement retailer. However, the company experienced slow growth in the Chinese market due to a low consumer appetite for DIY products and since then it has folded its store operations, closing its last store in Beijing in 2013.

BASF is one of the world's leading chemical companies, operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF's home and personal care offerings. It is one of the top ten users of palm oil worldwide, using over 380,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products in 2015.

Home Depot Inc. is a leading home improvement retailer, selling construction materials and products for the home and garden. It was founded in 1978 in Atlanta, Georgia in the US, where the company now has its headquarters. Since the opening of its first two stores in Atlanta in 1979, the company has grown to become the largest retailer in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector both in the US and globally. According to Home Depot, it is the fourth largest retailer in the US and the fifth largest in the world. Home Depot provides a range of products, including building materials, home improvement supplies, indoor and outdoor furniture, tools, and garden products for customers undertaking DIY activities.
The company has over 2,200 specialist stores throughout the US, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, China, Canada and Mexico. It entered the Canadian market in 1994 and now has 182 stores in ten of Canada's provinces. It entered the Mexican market in 2011, and has since become Mexico's largest home improvement retailer, with a total of 114 stores in the country. Home Depot's presence in China increased through its acquisition of The Home Way; China's first home improvement retailer. However, the company experienced slow growth in the Chinese market due to a low consumer appetite for DIY products and since then it has folded its store operations, closing its last store in Beijing in 2013.

BASF is one of the world's leading chemical companies, operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF's home and personal care offerings. It is one of the top ten users of palm oil worldwide, using over 380,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products in 2015.

Target Corporation is a general merchandise retailer operating in the US. Established in 1902 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, it is one of North America's retail giants, ranking among the top fifty in the Fortune 500. Target offers a variety of products including: food, beauty and personal care items; cleaning and paper products; as well as apparel and furniture, among other products. The company operates over 1,792 stores in the US as well as 38 distribution centres. Target began operating stores in Canada in 2011 through the acquisition of Zellers; however in 2015 the company planned to discontinue operating stores in the country.
A significant component of Target's sales are made up of its owned and exclusive branded products, which account for around one third of the company's total sales. Its owned branded products include: Archers Farms groceries; luggage; travel accessories; furniture; other goods sold under the Embark brand; Smith & Hawken outdoor furniture; Sutton & Dodge meat products; and up & up health and beauty products.

Campbell Soup Co was founded in New Jersey, US, in 1869, when it began producing canned vegetables, soups, condiments and minced meats. The company now has annual sales of $8 billion and employs over 20,000 people. Its main business operations are divided into three divisions: simple meals (ready-made foods and soups); baked snacks; and health beverages and it has manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
The company's products are marketed under various brands, including Pepperidge Farms, which is the US division for cookies, crackers, bakery and frozen products and is led by 'Goldfish' crackers. However, the flagship Campbell's brand is the company's main source of revenue and is worth around US$2 billion. Through this brand, the company sells almost 2 billion cans of soup each year, accounting for 60% of the United States' market for canned soup. Campbell Soup Co continues to expand its range of products through investments into, and acquisitions of, other companies. For example, in 2013, the company acquired Bolthouse Farms, Plum Organics and Kelsen Group. During 2015, Campbell Soup Co. also plans to launch 200 new products, including protein drinks and bars.

Deutsche Bank are a major bank based in Germany serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, securities, wealth management, asset management, and retail banking services. As of 2017, the bank's total assets amount to more than 1.5 trillion EUR, with approximately 400 billion EUR in net loans. IOI Corporation is a global, vertically integrated palm oil company active throughout the supply chain from cultivation to manufacturing. The company has one of the top ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with more than 225,000 hectares of plantation land in Indonesia and Malaysia. Its 15 mills have an annual capacity for more than 4.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches. IOI also owns four refineries in Malaysia and the Netherlands with an annual capacity of more than 3 million metric tons. Its products include oleochemicals and specialty oils and fats for the food industry.

AAK is a Swedish agricultural processor and manufacturer of food ingredients, lipids, technical products, and animal feed with 19 production facilities and sales offices in over 25 countries. The company claims to be the world's leading manufacturer of specialty vegetable fats and is a major company in the global bakery ingredients market. Soya sourced from South America as well as palm oil and its derivatives sourced from Central America and Southeast Asia are used in these products by the company. In 2015, AAK used over 950,000 metric tons of palm oil and its derivatives in its products.

Musim Mas is a fully integrated palm oil corporation involved throughout the palm oil supply chain, from cultivation to processing, manufacturing and trading. The company has one of the largest landbanks globally for oil palm, is among the top five importers and exporters of palm oil from Indonesia and is present in 13 countries. Musim Mas is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

AXA are a financial services company headquartered in France serving private, corporate and institutional clients. As of 2017, AXA's total assets amount to more than 870 billion EUR, with more than 1.1 trillion EUR of assets under management. Kering SA is a French company engaged in the retail and distribution of luxury goods, primarily apparel and accessories. Until 2013, the company was known as PPR, short for Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, which in turn was its official name until 2005.  Established in 1963, the company has its origins in the building materials industry and in particular in the timber trade. It then became a leader in the retail sector, before entering into the world of luxury goods with the purchase of the Gucci brand in 1999. Today the company has 22 brands operating in two core divisions: Luxury, which designs, manufactures and markets luxury apparel, leather goods, accessories, watches, jewellery, fragrances and cosmetics; and Sport and Lifestyle, which designs and produces footwear, apparel and accessories under the company's sporting brands.
Kering SA is headquartered in Paris, France and its brands in its luxury and sports and lifestyle segments, include several world famous brands including Puma, Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga and Stella McCartney, many of which have leather goods among their principal products,. Kering SA therefore plays a prominent role in the global trade in leather and animal skins, with several of the company's brands designing and selling leather goods. For example, it produces leather wallets and handbags under Saint Laurent  and Balenciaga. Through these and its numerous other brands, Kering SA holds the second largest market share in the bags and luggage sector globally. It also produces large amount s of leather footwear, for example under Sergio Rossi; a leading Italian shoe brand. Kering SA is among the top five manufacturers of footwear globally, occupying the fourth largest share of the global market in 2013, and in particular holding a leading position in the footwear market of Western Europe, especially in Italy. Kering SA is placing increasing emphasis on the direct sourcing of its raw materials, including leather. In 2013, it bought a majority stake in one the world's biggest producers of tanned skins and it has plans to build a new tanning facility in France, which could be operational by 2016.

Mondelez International (Mondleez) was formed in 2012 as a spinoff of Kraft International. Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack companies with global net revenues of approximately $35 billion in 2013. 60% of the 2013 net revenue originated from biscuit and chocolate sales, with 40% of these sales in Europe and 20% in North Americai. It has over 100,000 employees and manufactures products for consumption in around 165 countries around the worldi.  In total, it has nine billion dollar brands, including Tang, Cadbury, Nabisco and Oreo biscuits. Further to that, the company also owns another 53 brands with annual revenues greater than $100 millioni. Through these brands, the company produces beverages, biscuits, cheese, chocolate and chewing gum. It also invests strongly in research and development, with numerous facilities across Europe, such as the chocolate centre for excellence in Bournville, UK, and its biscuits research and development centre in Saclay, France. The company is now focusing its attention on emerging markets through the expansion of existing manufacturing plants and the building of new ones. For example, Mondelez has expanded its chocolate factory in Curitiba, Brazil and spent $350 million on the construction of a new biscuit factory in Monteray, Mexicoi.
Mondelez International (formerly known as Kraft International) has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011. In 2012, the company used 285732 m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products. Of this 200,653 m3 was RSPO certified (crude palm oil plus palm kernel oil).

rows.coprofile: Marks & Spencer is a leading British retail company with over 1,000 stores worldwide. Through its diverse product range it is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. M&S Food sells products containing palm oil, soy and beef. Meanwhile the company’s apparel and luggage products use leather. M&S also sells home and garden furniture, for which timber is often used.  Marks & Spencer Group PLC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef, leather, timber and paper packaging.

H&M Hennes and Mauritz AB is a Swedish clothing company operating under several brands, including its flagship brand H&M, as well as COS, Monki, Cheap Monday, and & Other Stories . The company, headquartered in Sweden, is involved in designing, manufacturing and marketing apparel, accessories and home textiles.  It was established in 1947, with the opening of its first Hennes store in VÃ¤sterÃ¥s, Sweden, which exclusively sold women's clothing. With the acquisition of hunting and fishing equipment store Mauritz Widforss in 1968, the company changed its name to Hennes & Mauritz and expanded its product range to also cover apparel for men and children. Since then, the company has expanded, opening stores throughout Europe as well as worldwide. For example, it expanded into the US in 2000, and opened stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2007. Further to this, the company established a new brand, COS, in 2007 and acquired the fashion firm, FaBric Scandinavien AB, in 2008, which holds the Weekday, Monki and Cheap Monday brands . In 2010, the full incorporation of FaBric Scandinavien was completed, when Hennes & Mauritz acquired the remaining 40% of shares.

Unilever is one of the largest consumer goods companies in the world, with 2 billion consumers using its products every day. Unilever's products are sold in more than 190 countries, reaching over 8.5 million shops. In 2014, the company had a turnover of $48.4 billion, with expanding sales in emerging markets contributing 57% of business. Unilever operates in a number of markets including food and beverages, and home and personal care. Its foods business generated 45% of operating profit in 2014, while personal care contributed 41%.
Unilever owns a number of well-known brands, notably Dove, Axe, Vaseline, Flora and Domestos. Through the manufacturing of these products, Unilever used 1.5 million MT of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in 2013-2014, equivalent to 2.6% of global production. 95% of its palm oil is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia. The company recognises the need to source its palm oil sustainably and currently purchases 100% of its palm oil as Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) certified, mainly via GreenPalm certificates. Further to this, the company's manufacturing facilities consume 1% of the world's soy, mostly procured from North America.
Unilever continues to focus on gaining a foothold in new and emerging markets. During 2014, the company launched new brands Lifebuoy and Omo in China and Saudi Arabia respectively, while new manufacturing facilities were established in Indonesia, China, the Philippines, and parts of Africa. In parallel, Unilever is consolidating business operations in North America to form more integrated, efficient supply chains.

Shiseido Co Ltd is a multi-brand company comprising 105 companies in the following business divisions: Cosmetics; Healthcare; Professional; Frontier Sciences (manufactures raw materials for cosmetics and drugs); Food (restaurant operations); and Other (education/welfare). It was founded in Japan in 1872 and has grown into a global business; today it operates a domestic line and a global line of products. The global line operates in Europe, the US and Asia and consists of the cosmetics business, which manufactures and sells cosmetics, cosmetic tools and toiletry products; and the professional business, which manufactures and sells products to hair and beauty salons in Japan and overseas. Shiseido Co Ltd products are sold in over 89 overseas territories.
In addition to brands bearing the Shiseido name, the group also has other brands (each with its own brand values) that have been obtained through acquisitions and licensing agreements. These include bareEssentials (mineral make-up), NARS (make-up), Jean Paul-Gautier (fragrance) and Issey Mayake (fragrance).

Bunge is a global agribusiness operating in about 40 countries and involved in the processing, manufacture and trading of agricultural commodities. The company is one of the major players in the South American soya industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is one of the largest soya processors in Brazil and one of the market leaders in Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. The company also has facilities in China and India. Globally it has 40 million tons of annual soy crush capacity. Bunge is also among the top five exporters of soya from Argentina and Paraguay, and is one of the largest in Brazil.

Estee Lauder is an American cosmetics company with products sold in 50 countries around the world. Products include skin care, hair care, makeup, and fragrances with well-known brands including Aveda, Jo Malone, and Estee Lauder itself. It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

rows.coprofile: Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. The company’s landbank is one of the largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with approximately 300,000 hectares across Indonesia. It also owns a palm oil refinery alongside several processing and crushing facilities.   PT Astra International TBK is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (Reckitt Benckiser) manufactures and markets a wide range of branded home, health and personal care products. The group comprises around 60 companies and sells its products in nearly 200 countries, giving it a global presence. The company markets products under several well-known brands, including health products, such as Strepsils, Gaviscon and Nurofen; hygiene products Clearasil, Dettol, and Harpic; and home products, Calgon and Vanish.
Reckitt Benckiser is headquartered in the UK and has its origins in the 1800s, when Benckiser was founded in 1823. However, Reckitt Benckiser in its current form was established in 1999 through a merger between Reckitt & Colman and Benckiser. Since then, the company has undergone rapid expansion, with numerous acquisitions, including Korean household company Oxy in 2000; over-the-counter healthcare business, Boots Healthcare International, in 2006; and SSL International in 2010. More recently, in 2013, Reckitt Benckiser further strengthened its global position through collaboration with Bristol-Myers Squibb, a leading health company in Brazil and Mexico, and the acquisition of Manyanshuning, China's leading sore throat brand.
The company is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil and reported the use of around 107,000 MT of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. Palm oil is used principally in the company's manufacturing of home and personal care goods, for example, in cleaning agents, laundry detergents, and soap tablets.

Procter & Gamble Co (P&G) is one of the world's largest consumer packaged goods companies, with operations in approximately 70 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Ohio in the US, P&G manufactures and markets consumer products throughout the world, with its branded products such as Head & Shoulders and Oral-B being sold in over 180 countries. P&G's products are primarily sold through mass merchandisers, grocery stores and drug stores and are approximated to serve around 4.8 billion people worldwide.
P&G divides its operations between four main business segments: Beauty; Health and Grooming; Fabric and Home Care; and Baby, Feminine and Family Care.  Palm kernel oil and, to a lesser extent, palm oil  are used in the manufacture of its products, including in its beauty and household care products such as soaps and detergents. The combined use of palm kernel oil, palm oil and its derivatives was over 532,000 MT in 2013/14. P&G purchases from a variety of suppliers, typically four or five supply chain levels above the source plantation. Over 70% of palm oil and derivatives are sourced from Malaysia, supplemented by procurement from Indonesia, and Central and South America. P&G also purchases wood pulp for absorbent hygiene and tissue products. In the financial year 2013/14, P&G bought approximately 1.7 million air dried metric tons of pulp for use in these products, sourcing pulp from Latin America (34%), Canada (30%) and the US (36%).

The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.

Koninklijke FrieslandCampina NV (Friesland) is a Dutch international dairy company. The company has four sections: Consumer Products Europe, Middle East and Africa; Consumer Products Asia; Cheese, Butter and Milk Powder; and finally Ingredients. It produces a wide range of products, including butter, cheese, condensed milk, cream, lactose, whey proteins, yoghurt and many others.
The company advertises itself as one of the top five dairy companies in the world. It is also the largest in Indonesia and Thailand, is in the top 5 for Malaysia and Western Europe and is in the global top 10 for baby food and dairy. It is also among the top 20 packaged food companies overall in the world.
Friesland operates 141 sites in over 26 countries, with the strongest presence in the Netherlands, where it can be found at 59 sites. The company employs 20,000 people and is supplied by 15,300 dairy farmers. Some it its most notable brands are Campina, Chocomel, Completa, Dutch Lady, Frisian Flag, Foremost, Betagen, Friesche Vlag and Fruttis, amongst others. Friesland used 90,000 tonnes of palm oil in its products in 2013. It has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2007.

Socfin Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Cargill is a US-based agribusiness company operating in 70 countries. Its business operations include the procurement, processing and trading of agricultural commodities, food products and industrial products, and it also offers financial solutions. It is one of the major players in the South American soy industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company also has significant palm oil operations. Ferrero Group (Ferrero) is a family-owned confectionary business formally established in 1946 out of Pietro Ferrero's thriving factory in Piedmont, Italy. The company was one of the earliest in the Italian confectionery industry to expand overseas, with Michele Ferrero and his wife Maria Franca being the first Italians to open manufacturing operations in the confectionery business abroad after World War II. Until he passed away in February 2015, Michele Ferrero ranked 22nd on the Forbes list of billionaires and was the wealthiest man in Italy, worth $27 billion (though living in Monaco). His son Giovanni now runs the company, which operates in 51 countries worldwide and on every continent. The company has over 22,000 employees at 20 production and 3 research and development sites. In addition, the Ferrero Group has 8 agricultural companies for both direct cultivation and manufacturing purposes.
Ferrero is the fourth largest confectionary company in the world and in the past five years has rapidly expanded its sales in China and Russia. It owns many famous brands, including Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella, which was one of the company's first products in the 1940s. Ferrero uses palm oil in its confectionary to give products the right consistency. The company sources palm oil from Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and Brazil, using 150,000 tonnes annually.

Orkla Group (Orkla) is a Norwegian based manufacturer of consumer goods, with other interests including hydropower and real estate. The group began over 350 years ago as a mining operation and through acquisitions and divestments the group has changed very dramatically; its focus is now on branded consumer goods including food and cleaning products, although the group does retain operations in hydro power aluminium products and paint manufacture.  In 2013, the group employed around 17,000 staff and had a turnover of NOK 33 Billion ($5.3 Billion).
Orkla branded consumer goods business accounts for around 86% of revenue and is divided into five business units: Orkla Foods, which operates in Nordic and Baltic regions and concentrates on Orkla's own brand products (which generally hold number 1 or 2 positions in their markets); Orkla Confectionary and Snacks, which owns the brands KIMs Danmark and the Estonian Kalev; the Home and Personal Division, which owns cleaning and comestic brands such as Jif, Comfort and Vaseline Intensive Care; the Orkla International Division, which operates in Russia, Poland, Austria and India; and Orkla Food Ingredients, which produces baking products such as yeast and butter blends.
Orkla Confectionary and Snacks and Orkla Foods are both RSPO members since 2007 and 2013, respectively, following the acquisition of the Swedish companies Goteborgs Kex and Procordia, which were RSPO members. In 2014, the company started a new initiative to reduce deforestation through palm oil use and aims to use traceable and sustainable sources by the end of 2017. They also released a policy for sustainable palm oil use.

Home Depot Inc. is a leading home improvement retailer, selling construction materials and products for the home and garden. It was founded in 1978 in Atlanta, Georgia in the US, where the company now has its headquarters. Since the opening of its first two stores in Atlanta in 1979, the company has grown to become the largest retailer in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector both in the US and globally. According to Home Depot, it is the fourth largest retailer in the US and the fifth largest in the world. Home Depot provides a range of products, including building materials, home improvement supplies, indoor and outdoor furniture, tools, and garden products for customers undertaking DIY activities.
The company has over 2,200 specialist stores throughout the US, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, China, Canada and Mexico. It entered the Canadian market in 1994 and now has 182 stores in ten of Canada's provinces. It entered the Mexican market in 2011, and has since become Mexico's largest home improvement retailer, with a total of 114 stores in the country. Home Depot's presence in China increased through its acquisition of The Home Way; China's first home improvement retailer. However, the company experienced slow growth in the Chinese market due to a low consumer appetite for DIY products and since then it has folded its store operations, closing its last store in Beijing in 2013.

HSBC are an international banking group headquartered in London serving private and commercial clients. Their services include corporate finance, insurance, and investments, securities, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2017, HSBC's total assets amount to more than 2.4 trillion USD, with approximately 1 trillion USD in loans. HSBC are among the top 10 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 68 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 80 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 4 billion USD worth of shares.

The company is one of the top ten footwear retailers globally by brandshare. It is also among the top ten in China and Hong Kong, as well as in the US.

rows.coprofile: Kao Corporation is a Japanese consumer goods company that manufactures beauty, health and home care products, whilst also providing chemicals to industrial markets. The company owns well-known brands such as Molton Brown, John Freida and Merries. Kao Corp is exposed to palm oil and soy, which are used in its consumer products, and also to pulp and paper which feature in both the company’s products and its packaging.  Kao Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Henkel AG & Co. KGaA (Henkel) is a manufacturing company, headquartered in Germany, which operates in both the consumer and business markets. It operates worldwide in three key areas: Laundry and Home Care; Beauty Care; and Adhesive Technologies. Famous brands include Persil and Schwarzkopf. Products sold under these brands (such as laundry detergents, household cleaners and cosmetic products) commonly contain surfactants that consist of palm oil derivatives. Surfactants are an active substance, not produced by Henkel directly but purchased from third party suppliers €“ mineral oils, natural gas, coconut oil, and palm kernel oil are currently the only ingredients able to produce surfactants on an industrial scale. According to Henkel, in 2013, through surfactant and other raw material purchasing, the company used around 71,608 tonnes of palm oil products, mostly comprising palm kernel oil.

IOI Corporation is a global, vertically integrated palm oil company active throughout the supply chain from cultivation to manufacturing. The company has one of the top ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with more than 225,000 hectares of plantation land in Indonesia and Malaysia. Its 15 mills have an annual capacity for more than 4.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches. IOI also owns four refineries in Malaysia and the Netherlands with an annual capacity of more than 3 million metric tons. Its products include oleochemicals and specialty oils and fats for the food industry.  IOI Corporation Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Westpac are an Australian-based banking group providing banking and financial services to private, corporate and institutional customers. Their services include retail banking, corporate financing, wealth management, capital markets, investments and insurance. As of 2017, Westpac's total assets amounted to more than 830 billion AUD with more than 660 billion AUD in gross loans to customers. Westpac are among the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 4 billion USD of loans in companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Felda Global Ventures (FGV) is a Malaysian group of agribusiness companies active in the palm, rubber, sugar, and agri-services industries. The group is involved in both the cultivation and processing of oil palm as well as in the manufacturing of palm oil goods.  Felda Global Ventures Holdings Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Colgate-Palmolive is an American consumer goods company with products sold in over 200 countries around the world. Its products include oral, personal and home care, as well as pet nutrition products. Brands include Colgate, Palmolive and Sanex. It is a major global player across all its products areas. Globally, Colgate-Palmolive is one of the largest home care and beauty and personal care companies. Colgate-Palmolive Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and beef.

Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV (Grupo Bimbo) was founded by Lorenzo Servitje in Mexico in 1945. International expansion began in 1989, resulting in Grupo Bimbo becoming the largest bakery company in the world in terms of sales and production volume. The company's main markets are the US and Mexico but it also operates in Central and Latin America, Canada, Asia and Europe. In 2014, net sales were $14.1 billion. The company has 167 manufacturing plants located largely in its key markets, with 85 plants in the US and 39 in Mexico. In addition to its global manufacturing facilities, the company operates a distribution network with over 52,000 routes, feeding into 2.2 million points of sale in 19 countries. Today, Grupo Bimbo employs over 21,000 individuals.
Grupo Bimbo produces more than 10,000 different products under 100 umbrella brands including Bimbo, New York Bakery Co., Marisela and Ricolino. It manufactures bread, potato crisps, pastries and a variety of other snacks, many of which contain palm oil. The company continues to expand its business in international markets; it recently completed the acquisition of the previously public-listed company, Canada Bread, for $1.83 billion.

Johnson & Johnson is a global family of companies manufacturing medical devices, pharmaceuticals and consumer healthcare products. Its consumer range contains well-known beauty brands such as Aveeno, Neutrogena, Clean & Clear and Le Petit Marseillais. Amongst its soaps, shampoos, lotions and creams, Johnson & Johnson uses palm oil derivatives as emollients and emulsifiers.  Johnson & Johnson is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) is a leading processor and trader in agricultural commodities active in more than 100 countries. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soy in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company has significant oilseed crushing facilities in Brazil and Argentina, as well as having an annual capacity of several million metric tons in China. LDC is among the top soy exporters in Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil. The company’s palm oil operations are also significant and it is a major producer of biodiesel.  LOUIS DREYFUS is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and soy.

It is also among the five largest retailers in Europe and in Latin America.

Shiseido Co Ltd is a multi-brand company comprising 105 companies in the following business divisions: Cosmetics; Healthcare; Professional; Frontier Sciences (manufactures raw materials for cosmetics and drugs); Food (restaurant operations); and Other (education/welfare). It was founded in Japan in 1872 and has grown into a global business; today it operates a domestic line and a global line of products. The global line operates in Europe, the US and Asia and consists of the cosmetics business, which manufactures and sells cosmetics, cosmetic tools and toiletry products; and the professional business, which manufactures and sells products to hair and beauty salons in Japan and overseas. Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (Reckitt Benckiser) manufactures and markets a wide range of branded home, health and personal care products. The group comprises around 60 companies and sells its products in nearly 200 countries, giving it a global presence. The company markets products under several well-known brands, including health products, such as Strepsils, Gaviscon and Nurofen; hygiene products Clearasil, Dettol, and Harpic; and home products, Calgon and Vanish.
Reckitt Benckiser is headquartered in the UK and has its origins in the 1800s, when Benckiser was founded in 1823. However, Reckitt Benckiser in its current form was established in 1999 through a merger between Reckitt & Colman and Benckiser. Since then, the company has undergone rapid expansion, with numerous acquisitions, including Korean household company Oxy in 2000; over-the-counter healthcare business, Boots Healthcare International, in 2006; and SSL International in 2010. More recently, in 2013, Reckitt Benckiser further strengthened its global position through collaboration with Bristol-Myers Squibb, a leading health company in Brazil and Mexico, and the acquisition of Manyanshuning, China's leading sore throat brand.
The company is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil and reported the use of around 107,000 MT of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. Palm oil is used principally in the company's manufacturing of home and personal care goods, for example, in cleaning agents, laundry detergents, and soap tablets.

Mondelez International (Mondleez) was formed in 2012 as a spinoff of Kraft International. Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack companies with global net revenues of approximately $35 billion in 2013. 60% of the 2013 net revenue originated from biscuit and chocolate sales, with 40% of these sales in Europe and 20% in North Americai. It has over 100,000 employees and manufactures products for consumption in around 165 countries around the worldi.  In total, it has nine billion dollar brands, including Tang, Cadbury, Nabisco and Oreo biscuits. Further to that, the company also owns another 53 brands with annual revenues greater than $100 millioni. Through these brands, the company produces beverages, biscuits, cheese, chocolate and chewing gum. It also invests strongly in research and development, with numerous facilities across Europe, such as the chocolate centre for excellence in Bournville, UK, and its biscuits research and development centre in Saclay, France. The company is now focusing its attention on emerging markets through the expansion of existing manufacturing plants and the building of new ones. For example, Mondelez has expanded its chocolate factory in Curitiba, Brazil and spent $350 million on the construction of a new biscuit factory in Monteray, Mexicoi.
Mondelez International (formerly known as Kraft International) has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011. In 2012, the company used 285732 m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products. Of this 200,653 m3 was RSPO certified (crude palm oil plus palm kernel oil).

Yum! Brands Inc. develops franchises, operates and licenses restaurants. It is one of the world's largest restaurant companies, with over 42,500 companies in more than 130 countries and territories. The three globally recognised chains under the Yum! umbrella are KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell; which are the global leaders in their respective food categories of chicken, pizza and Mexican-style food .
Since its spinoff from PepsiCo. in 1997, Yum! Brands has expanded significantly internationally, with 65% of its profits now coming from non-US markets in 2015 compared to just 20% in 1997. In 2016, Yum! Brands opens on average over six new restaurants a day worldwide.
Yum! Brands' chicken restaurant chain, KFC, has 18,000 outlets in 115 countries and territories, serving over 12 million customers each day. Taco Bell serves Mexican style food through around 6,100 outlets in the US, serving more than 40 million customers each week. However, Yum! Brands is looking to expand the chain globally and currently has around 300 stores in 20 countries outside the US. By the end of 2014, there were over 15,600 Pizza Hut restaurants around the world.
Yum! Brands franchisees and company operated restaurants are significant purchasers of chicken, cheese, beef and pork products as well as paper and packaging materials. All three restaurant brands use palm oil, soy and beef in a variety of different products.

rows.coprofile: The Hershey Company (Hershey's) was incorporated in Delaware, US in 1927, as a successor to a business founded in Philadelphia in 1894 by Milton S. Hershey. Today, the company sells and distributes its products in around 70 countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia. It claims to be the top chocolate and confectionary company in US by market share, where over 85% of Hershey's consolidated revenue is generated. Outside the US, the company's main countries of operation are Canada, Mexico, Brazil, China, India, Korea, and Japan. The company has 22,000 employees around the world and an annual turnover of over $7.4 billion. Hershey's has more than 80 brands  including Reese's, Mound, Almond Joy, Twizzlers , and it also shares a licensing agreement with Nestle to produce KitKat in America .  It has been a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member since 2011 and used 23,967 tonnes of palm oil in 2014, 100% of which is RSPO certified. Hershey's is focusing on expanding its business both through entry into new markets, such as the meat snack market through the acquisition of KRAVE Pure Foods, Inc., in March 2015, and through consolidating its operations in markets outside the US, such as through its acquisition in September 2015 of the remaining 49% of shares in its Bauducco/Pandurata Alimentos SA distribution joint venture in Brazil.

Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A.  Oji Holdings corporation is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

News Corporation (News Corp) is a media conglomerate with a network of companies in media, news, education and information services. In June 2013, News Corp's shareholders gave formal approval for the company to split its publishing and entertainment divisions, creating two new companies: News Corp, housing the company's publishing segment; 21st Century Fox housing the entertainment division. News Corp is now specifically a publishing company, producing newspaper, magazines, books and promotional inserts and coupons. The company was established in Australia in 1954, when Rupert Murdoch took control of the Australian corporation, News Limited, which had a majority interest in one of Adelaide's top daily newspapers. Since then, the company has grown dramatically and acquired numerous assets, beginning with newspapers in the UK: 'The Sun' and 'News of the World.' Established in Australia, News Corp is now based in the US and is the largest newspaper publishing company globally.
As of 2014, News Corp is comprised of the following businesses, with each housing several brands: News Corp Australia, News UK, Dow Jones & Company, New York Post, Harper Collins Publishers, Amplify, News America Marketing, and Storyful. News Corp Australia, for example, claims to be Australia's leading media and publishing company, selling over 10 million papers weekly, with titles including The Daily Telegraph, The Australian, and Herald Sun. News UK also publishes some of the UK's most well-known newspapers, including The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times. Dow Jones & Company publishes The Wall Street Journal and specialises in the provision of news and business information via a variety of media outlets.  Finally, News Corp's subsidiary HarperCollins is one of the world's most prominent book publishing companies. In May 2014, HarperCollins acquired book publisher Harlequin; the acquisition of the Canadian company is the biggest deal in book publishing since the merger of two other publishing giants, Penguin and Random House in 2013.

Home Depot Inc. is a leading home improvement retailer, selling construction materials and products for the home and garden. It was founded in 1978 in Atlanta, Georgia in the US, where the company now has its headquarters. Since the opening of its first two stores in Atlanta in 1979, the company has grown to become the largest retailer in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector both in the US and globally. According to Home Depot, it is the fourth largest retailer in the US and the fifth largest in the world. Home Depot provides a range of products, including building materials, home improvement supplies, indoor and outdoor furniture, tools, and garden products for customers undertaking DIY activities.
The company has over 2,200 specialist stores throughout the US, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, China, Canada and Mexico. It entered the Canadian market in 1994 and now has 182 stores in ten of Canada's provinces. It entered the Mexican market in 2011, and has since become Mexico's largest home improvement retailer, with a total of 114 stores in the country. Home Depot's presence in China increased through its acquisition of The Home Way; China's first home improvement retailer. However, the company experienced slow growth in the Chinese market due to a low consumer appetite for DIY products and since then it has folded its store operations, closing its last store in Beijing in 2013.

PepsiCo Inc (PepsiCo) was formed in 1965 when Frito-Lay Inc. merged with Pepsi-Cola Company. The company now contributes significantly to the food and beverage markets globally, with its products sold on every continent. The company's 2013 revenue was split roughly equally between its food and beverages sectors.
It is through PepsiCo's wholly owned subsidiary, Frito Lay, that it operates in the snack market. Through this subsidiary, PepsiCo has over 35% of the United States savoury snack market and Frito-Lay accounts for approximately a third of PepsiCo's annual sales. PepsiCo owns a total of 22 brands that generate more than $1 billion annually, including Lays, Pepsi, Tropicana, Quaker and Gatorade; its products include a variety of snacks, soft drinks and breakfast cereals. Aside from producing goods for its own brands, PepsiCo also manufactures and distributes a number of products under license from Starbucks, Lipton and Dole. PepsiCo operates a global network of manufacturing facilities, employing nearly 275,000 people and generating over $66 billion in net revenue in 2013. These manufacturing facilities consumed over 450,000 tones of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in 2012-2013. PepsiCo continues to develop its infrastructure, particularly in fast-growth economies. For example, it is committed to investing Rs 1,230 crore in a new beverage factory sited on 80 acres in Andhra Pradesh, India.

Triputra Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Pearson Plc (Pearson) is a London-based international media and education company, with key operations in the publishing industry. The company develops and publishes educational and entertainment materials in the form of books, newspapers and online. Pearson provides educational materials to teachers and students across 70 countries.  It also runs the Financial Times Group, a leading provider of business and financial news and analysis, both in print and online. Finally, Pearson is also the parent company of Penguin Random House, which claims to be the first truly global trade book publisher, and comprises the various publishing enterprises of the previously separate Penguin and Random House companies. Penguin Random House was formed in July 2013 after a merger was agreed between the respective publishing enterprises' parent companies, Pearson and Bertelsmann. The joint venture is based in New York and is jointly controlled by the two companies, with 53% owned by Bertelsmann, based in Germany, and 47% by Pearson.
In 2013, the book publishing operations of Pearson, the Penguin Group and Penguin Random House, individually ranked as the top two players in the book publishing industry globally. Only a very small proportion of Pearson's products are printed in-house, with the company instead sourcing from a number of suppliers around the world. For example, commercial printing company R. R. Donnelley, which is the leading company of its kind globally in terms of market share, is an important supplier of Pearson.

Campbell Soup Co was founded in New Jersey, US, in 1869, when it began producing canned vegetables, soups, condiments and minced meats. The company now has annual sales of $8 billion and employs over 20,000 people. Its main business operations are divided into three divisions: simple meals (ready-made foods and soups); baked snacks; and health beverages and it has manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
The company's products are marketed under various brands, including Pepperidge Farms, which is the US division for cookies, crackers, bakery and frozen products and is led by 'Goldfish' crackers. However, the flagship Campbell's brand is the company's main source of revenue and is worth around US$2 billion. Through this brand, the company sells almost 2 billion cans of soup each year, accounting for 60% of the United States' market for canned soup. Campbell Soup Co continues to expand its range of products through investments into, and acquisitions of, other companies. For example, in 2013, the company acquired Bolthouse Farms, Plum Organics and Kelsen Group. During 2015, Campbell Soup Co. also plans to launch 200 new products, including protein drinks and bars.

VF Corp (VF) is a US-based global apparel company, manufacturing and supplying apparel, footwear and accessories. Headquartered in North Carolina, in the US, VF's products are sold in more than 150 countries worldwide, through 47,000 retail outlets and 1,100 of the company's own stores.
Its products are marketed principally under the company's own brands, within five business divisions: Outdoor and Action Sports, Jeanswear, Imagewear, Sportswear and Contemporary Brands. VF has a diverse portfolio of brands, including well-known names, such as outdoor apparel brand, The North Face, footwear, apparel and accessories brand, Timberland, and luggage and bag brands, Eastpak, JanSport and Kipling. The company produces around 450 million items per year, and operates manufacturing facilities in the Middle East, Europe, Mexico, and Central and South America. As these facilities meet only a proportion of the company's production needs, especially for the company's footwear production, VF sources products from around 1,900 independently and company-run facilities. VF sources raw materials, including leather, from multiple international suppliers.
VF Corp is a leader in the global bags and luggage market, ranking in the top ten globally and occupying a leading position in the US, where it ranks third by market share. It is also a top player in the more fragmented footwear industry, ranking as the third largest in the US by market share, and where it also holds the third position, and is in the top ten globally.

R. R. Donnelley is a commercial printing company founded in 1864. It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. Their customers include some of the world's most well known companies including; Accenture, Barclays, IBM, and Microsoft. Despite offering a number of digital communication strategies, they are primarily known as a supplier of print material and is the leading company of its kind globally.  R. R. Donnelley also prints products for other companies involved in the printing and publishing sector. For example, it supplies print products to Pearson PLC and to HarperCollins, two of the world's largest publishers. In 2013 it employed roughly 57,000 people across four continents, in nearly 40 countries, leading to sales of $10.5 billion. It continues to expand through strategic acquisitions of companies specialising in both digital and commercial print. For example, in 2011, it acquired LibreDigital, a pioneering digital publishing and distribution company, and in 2014 acquired Consolidated Graphics in a deal worth over $600 million.

Mondelez International (Mondleez) was formed in 2012 as a spinoff of Kraft International. Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack companies with global net revenues of approximately $35 billion in 2013. 60% of the 2013 net revenue originated from biscuit and chocolate sales, with 40% of these sales in Europe and 20% in North Americai. It has over 100,000 employees and manufactures products for consumption in around 165 countries around the worldi.  In total, it has nine billion dollar brands, including Tang, Cadbury, Nabisco and Oreo biscuits. Further to that, the company also owns another 53 brands with annual revenues greater than $100 millioni. Through these brands, the company produces beverages, biscuits, cheese, chocolate and chewing gum. It also invests strongly in research and development, with numerous facilities across Europe, such as the chocolate centre for excellence in Bournville, UK, and its biscuits research and development centre in Saclay, France. The company is now focusing its attention on emerging markets through the expansion of existing manufacturing plants and the building of new ones. For example, Mondelez has expanded its chocolate factory in Curitiba, Brazil and spent $350 million on the construction of a new biscuit factory in Monteray, Mexicoi.
Mondelez International (formerly known as Kraft International) has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011. In 2012, the company used 285732 m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products. Of this 200,653 m3 was RSPO certified (crude palm oil plus palm kernel oil).

The Hershey Company (Hershey's) was incorporated in Delaware, US in 1927, as a successor to a business founded in Philadelphia in 1894 by Milton S. Hershey. Today, the company sells and distributes its products in around 70 countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia. It claims to be the top chocolate and confectionary company in US by market share, where over 85% of Hershey's consolidated revenue is generated. Outside the US, the company's main countries of operation are Canada, Mexico, Brazil, China, India, Korea, and Japan. The company has 22,000 employees around the world and an annual turnover of over $7.4 billion. Hershey's has more than 80 brands  including Reese's, Mound, Almond Joy, Twizzlers , and it also shares a licensing agreement with Nestle to produce KitKat in America .  It has been a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member since 2011 and used 23,967 tonnes of palm oil in 2014, 100% of which is RSPO certified. Hershey's is focusing on expanding its business both through entry into new markets, such as the meat snack market through the acquisition of KRAVE Pure Foods, Inc., in March 2015, and through consolidating its operations in markets outside the US, such as through its acquisition in September 2015 of the remaining 49% of shares in its Bauducco/Pandurata Alimentos SA distribution joint venture in Brazil.

Mondelez International (Mondleez) was formed in 2012 as a spinoff of Kraft International. Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack companies with global net revenues of approximately $35 billion in 2013. 60% of the 2013 net revenue originated from biscuit and chocolate sales, with 40% of these sales in Europe and 20% in North Americai. It has over 100,000 employees and manufactures products for consumption in around 165 countries around the worldi.  In total, it has nine billion dollar brands, including Tang, Cadbury, Nabisco and Oreo biscuits. Further to that, the company also owns another 53 brands with annual revenues greater than $100 millioni. Through these brands, the company produces beverages, biscuits, cheese, chocolate and chewing gum. It also invests strongly in research and development, with numerous facilities across Europe, such as the chocolate centre for excellence in Bournville, UK, and its biscuits research and development centre in Saclay, France. The company is now focusing its attention on emerging markets through the expansion of existing manufacturing plants and the building of new ones. For example, Mondelez has expanded its chocolate factory in Curitiba, Brazil and spent $350 million on the construction of a new biscuit factory in Monteray, Mexicoi.
Mondelez International (formerly known as Kraft International) has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011. In 2012, the company used 285732 m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products. Of this 200,653 m3 was RSPO certified (crude palm oil plus palm kernel oil).

Kering SA is a luxury goods group comprising fashion houses, leather goods companies and jewellery makers. The group’s brands include Gucci, Bottega Veneta, Saint Laurent and Alexander McQueen, amongst many others.  As a leading producer of apparel, luggage and footwear products, Kering SA plays a prominent role in the global trade of leather and animal skins.  Kering S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Empresas CMPC S.A. is a Chilean-based producer of forest products. The company operates in the businesses of forestry, pulp and paper, tissue and other products, including the production of paper-manufacture products.  Empresas CMPC S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Schroders are a financial services company headquartered in the UK offering wealth management and asset management services for private, corporate and institutional clients. As of 2021, Schroders have more than £615 billion of assets under management. They are one of the top shareholders in Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, Schroders was providing 18.5 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Sumitomo Forestry Co. Ltd, is a timber company with operations in forestry, processing, materials provision and construction. The company is one of the world’s largest forestry companies and has subsidiaries operating across East and Southeast Asia, Oceania and North America.  Sumitomo Forestry is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Societe Generale are a banking group headquartered in France that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services span corporate finance, capital markets, insurance, wealth management, investments, securities and retail banking services. As of 2017, Societe Generale's total assets amount to more than 1.3 trillion EUR, with more than 410 billion EUR worth of loans. Societe Generale are among the top 20 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 20 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Inditex SA owns the clothing and accessories retail brands Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Uterque and Zara Home. This Spanish company, formed by Amancio Ortega Gaona in 1963, is amongst the largest fashion retailers in the world, with a revenue of over €16 billion 2013.
Inditex SA started business with Zara in 1963, which is the largest and best known of all the company's brands; selling leather shoes and handbags, as well as mid-range clothes to men, women and children. Inditex was incorporated as the group's holding company in 1985 and in 1991 other brands were incorporated into the group. Today, Inditex has more than 6,000 stores in 88 countries around the world, with recent expansions into China and Russia. Outside of Zara, its other brands cover a wide range of markets, for example, Uterque is a dedicated accessory store, and Berksha and Pull&Bear target younger audiences.
Almost 90% of Inditex' suppliers come from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, India, South East Asia, Bangladesh, China, Brazil and Argentina, with over half of the company's manufacturing taking place in Spain or nearby countries, including Turkey and Morocco. This allows the company to respond to in-store demands and trends quickly, a model that has been dubbed 'Fast Fashion'. The company sells a range of apparel and accessories, including leather products, and notably, ranks in the top ten footwear companies in the western European market.

Morgan Stanley are an international investment bank and financial services provider headquartered in the US that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Services include wealth management, investment banking, capital markets, sales and trading, and research and investment management. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 850 billion USD, with more than 130 billion USD worth of loans. Morgan Stanley are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 36 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 20 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 19 billion USD worth of shares.

BASF is a German-based chemical company operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF’s home and personal care offerings.  BASF Personal Care and Nutrition GmbH is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.
