rows.coprofile: Genting is a large investment and management company with major operations in hospitality, energy, and palm oil, especially in palm oil processing. The company's landbank is one of the ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with about 240,000 hectares located in Malaysia and Indonesia as of 2015. It also owns several processing facilities with the capacity in 2015 to process more than 1.5 million fresh fruit bunches annually. Genting claims this makes them one of the leading and lowest cost palm oil producers in Malaysia.

The Clorox Company, headquartered in the US, specialises in manufacturing consumer and professional cleaning products, as well as personal care products. The Clorox Company has operations in 25 countries, with brand names including Burt’s Bees, Clorox and Glad.  Clorox Co, The is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.

Barclays PLC are a financial services group headquartered in the UK serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services cover personal, corporate, offshore, private, and investment banking, wealth management, loans and mortgages, and corporate lending. As of 2017, Barclays PLC's total assets amount to more than 1.1 trillion GBP with over 420 billion GBP in loans. They are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

IKEA Group is a leading company in the home furnishings industry that manufactures and sells affordable furniture and other goods for the home. Most of its furniture products are flat-packed and ready to be assembled at home by the customer. It operates throughout the supply chain, and is involved in the development, manufacturing, distribution and retail of products. The majority of the company's operations are in the retail sector, and though it sources products from external suppliers, it also produces many of its own products through Swedwood, the Group's industrial arm.
IKEA Group is based in Sweden and was established in 1943. It has a complicated corporate structure and since 1982, has been privately held by a foundation in the Netherlands, Stichting INGKA Foundation, which owns INGKA Holding B.V., the parent company of IKEA Group. The IKEA Group companies include Swedwood, IKEA of Sweden, and other departments, such as Purchasing and Distribution.
IKEA Group operates about 290 IKEA stores across 26 countries, in a franchise system under Inter IKEA Systems B.V. (Inter IKEA Systems B.V. officially owns the IKEA concept and is part of the Inter IKEA Group, which is a separate group of companies and under different ownership to the IKEA Group.) Added to these, IKEA has 40 stores in a further 15 countries, which are also operated under franchise but are owned outside of the IKEA Group.
IKEA Group operates internationally and is the leading home furnishings company and furniture retailer globally, occupying the leading position in the markets of Western Europe and the second place in the United States. IKEA Group is also the number one home furnishings company and furniture retailer in China and has plans to build upon its already significant position in the Chinese market by opening its first shopping mall there in 2014, with further stores planned for 2015. It also has a strong presence in Japan, Thailand and Taiwan, as well as in other regions worldwide.
As a leading manufacturer and retailer of furniture, IKEA uses large amounts of wood in its products. It is also a significant user of leather, which is used in sofas, rugs and some other products. The company used around four and half million square metres in furniture upholstering in 2013, over 40% of which was sourced from Brazil. It is also a significant user of palm oil, reporting total use of around 34,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm oil derived products in 2013. In an attempt to reduce its carbon footprint, IKEA replaced the paraffin used in its candles with palm stearin. The majority (80%) of the company's palm oil use is accounted for by its candles, with the remainder found in its food products.

rows.coprofile: Arla Foods is a dairy cooperative with activities around the world. The company's most prominent markets are the United Kingdom, Central Europe and Asia. Its products include milk, cheese, butter and cooking ingredients with brands such as Lurpak, Castello and Apetina. Arla Foods claimed to be among the top ten dairy companies in the world by revenue in 2015 and is one of the world's largest ingredient producers. Soya plays an important role in the cooperative's animal feed and palm oil is also used in its products, with about 25,000 metric tons being used in 2015.
initiatives: Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, UN Global Compact

Wilmar International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Salim Group is a large Indonesian conglomerate. Its subsidiary Indofood Agri is a vertically integrated agribusiness company spanning the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivation to product manufacturing and marketing. Products produced include cooking oils and margarines under several brands which are sold both directly and through retailers.  Salim Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Pearson Plc is a learning and media company based in London. The company operates in more than 65 countries and publishes material online and in book format. The large-scale publishing operations require vast amounts of pulp and paper.  Pearson PLC is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

rows.coprofile: Aegon are an insurance company based in the Netherlands serving private, commercial and institutional customers. Their services include life insurance, pensions, and asset management. As of 2017, Aegon manage a combined value of 840 billion EUR of investments, including more than 325 billion EUR in assets under management. They are one of the top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with approximately 2 billion USD worth of bonds for companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

UPM is a forest industry company based in Finland, with operations in 15 countries including Argentina, Uruguay and Indonesia. UPM produces, processes and trades timber and paper.  UPM is selected as a powerbroker for timber and pulp & paper.

Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group’s two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.8 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.  Royal Golden Eagle is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper.

Yum! Brands Inc. develops franchises, operates and licenses restaurants. It is one of the world's largest restaurant companies, with over 42,500 companies in more than 130 countries and territories. The three globally recognised chains under the Yum! umbrella are KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell; which are the global leaders in their respective food categories of chicken, pizza and Mexican-style food .
Since its spinoff from PepsiCo. in 1997, Yum! Brands has expanded significantly internationally, with 65% of its profits now coming from non-US markets in 2015 compared to just 20% in 1997. In 2016, Yum! Brands opens on average over six new restaurants a day worldwide.
Yum! Brands' chicken restaurant chain, KFC, has 18,000 outlets in 115 countries and territories, serving over 12 million customers each day. Taco Bell serves Mexican style food through around 6,100 outlets in the US, serving more than 40 million customers each week. However, Yum! Brands is looking to expand the chain globally and currently has around 300 stores in 20 countries outside the US. By the end of 2014, there were over 15,600 Pizza Hut restaurants around the world.
Yum! Brands franchisees and company operated restaurants are significant purchasers of chicken, cheese, beef and pork products as well as paper and packaging materials. All three restaurant brands use palm oil, soy and beef in a variety of different products.

Westpac are an Australian-based banking group providing banking and financial services to private, corporate and institutional customers. Their services include retail banking, corporate financing, wealth management, capital markets, investments and insurance. As of 2017, Westpac's total assets amounted to more than 830 billion AUD with more than 660 billion AUD in gross loans to customers. Westpac are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Mondelez International is an American manufacturer of snacks. The company sells chocolate, biscuits, beverages, candy, and meals. Some of the famous brands in Mondelez’s portfolio include Cadbury, Belvita, Mika, Ritz, and Oreo. According to the company, it is are one of the biggest snack companies in the world. Through its products Mondelez are exposed to palm oil and soy.  Mondelez International Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Bunge is a global agribusiness operating in about 40 countries and involved in the processing, manufacture and trading of agricultural commodities. The company is one of the major players in the South American soy industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is one of the largest soy processors in Brazil and one of the market leaders in Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. The company also has facilities in China and India.   Bunge Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

AAK sources Soy from South America and Palm Oil from Southeast Asia and Central America. The Company operates Kamani Oil Industries Pvt Ltd. as a majority owned subsidiary in India. AAK AB is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Koninklijke FrieslandCampina NV (Friesland) is a Dutch international dairy company. The company has four sections: Consumer Products Europe, Middle East and Africa; Consumer Products Asia; Cheese, Butter and Milk Powder; and finally Ingredients. It produces a wide range of products, including butter, cheese, condensed milk, cream, lactose, whey proteins, yoghurt and many others.
The company advertises itself as one of the top five dairy companies in the world. It is also the largest in Indonesia and Thailand, is in the top 5 for Malaysia and Western Europe and is in the global top 10 for baby food and dairy. It is also among the top 20 packaged food companies overall in the world.
Friesland operates 141 sites in over 26 countries, with the strongest presence in the Netherlands, where it can be found at 59 sites. The company employs 20,000 people and is supplied by 15,300 dairy farmers. Some it its most notable brands are Campina, Chocomel, Completa, Dutch Lady, Frisian Flag, Foremost, Betagen, Friesche Vlag and Fruttis, amongst others. Friesland used 90,000 tonnes of palm oil in its products in 2013. It has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2007.

Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.

As a leading producer of apparel, luggage and footwear products, Kering SA plays a prominent role in the global trade of leather and animal skins.  Kering S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Tetra Laval consists of three industry groups, Tetra Pak, Sidel and DeLaval.  The companies' activities focus on systems for the processing, packaging and distribution of food and accessories for dairy production and animal husbandry and are assessed due to their use of pulp and paper.

rows.coprofile: Kao Corporation is a Japanese consumer goods company that manufactures beauty, health and home care products, whilst also providing chemicals to industrial markets. The company owns well-known brands such as Molton Brown, John Freida and Merries. Kao Corp is exposed to palm oil and soy, which are used in its consumer products, and also to pulp and paper which feature in both the company’s products and its packaging.  Kao Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Nippon Paper Industries is a Japanese paper manufacturing company. The company produces newsprint, printing paper, paperboard, wrapping paper, and building materials among other products. rows.coprofile: McDonald’s is an American fast food retailer with more than 36,000 locations in over 100 countries. It is one of the largest fast food restaurant companies globally with a major market share. Additionally, it has one of the largest market shares in the US, China, Western Europe, and in India. The McDonald’s menu of burgers, sandwiches, sides and beverages involves significant amounts of beef, soy and palm oil, as well as paper in packaging.  McDonald's Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Sumitomo Forestry Co. Ltd, is a timber company with operations in forestry, processing, materials provision and construction. The company is one of the world’s largest forestry companies and has subsidiaries operating across East and Southeast Asia, Oceania and North America.  Sumitomo Forestry is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. The company’s landbank is one of the largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with approximately 300,000 hectares across Indonesia. It also owns a palm oil refinery alongside several processing and crushing facilities.   PT Astra International TBK is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Neste Oyj is a Finland-based company engaged in the refining and marketing of petroleum and petroleum related products. The company’s main market is the Baltic region and it has refineries in Finland, the Netherlands and Singapore and also exports oil and renewable fuels to other markets, which include the US, Sweden, Canada, Germany, and the UK. Neste is one of the world’s largest producers of biodiesel. Palm oil is a major ingredient of the company’s biofuels.  Neste Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and soy.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum Deforestation resolution (being a member of the CGF is not sufficient)

rows.coprofile: Olam international is a leading agricultural commodity business operating throughout the supply chain across 70 countries. It is a global market leader in many agricultural commodities such as cocoa and coffee, but also is a major player in African oil palm and forestry. Olam's subsidiary, Congolaise Industrielle de Bois (CIB) operates forestry concessions in the Republic of Congo covering about 2 million hectares in 2016. Olam has a minority stake in the SIFCA group based in Cote d'Ivoire which was managing a total of about 180,000 hectares of oil palm in 2014. Additionally, Olam has a joint venture with the government in Gabon to develop about 50,000 hectares of oil palm plantations with the possibility for further expansion, which began in 2011. The company is also active in soya cultivation and processing in South America and Africa.

Bunge is a global agribusiness operating in about 40 countries and involved in the processing, manufacture and trading of agricultural commodities. The company is one of the major players in the South American soya industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is one of the largest soya processors in Brazil and one of the market leaders in Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. The company also has facilities in China and India. Globally it has 40 million tons of annual soy crush capacity. Bunge is also among the top five exporters of soya from Argentina and Paraguay, and is one of the largest in Brazil.

Marfrig Global Foods SA (Marfrig GF) is a multinational company with operations in Brazil, where it is headquartered, as well as in 15 other countries around the world. The company's main business activities include the production, processing, preparation, sale and distribution of meat (beef, pork, lamb and poultry), pasta and processed foods (including pizzas, lasagnas, breaded products and desserts), ready meals and frozen vegetables, as well as the distribution of other food products (including frozen foods, sausages and fish) and semi-finished and finished leather.
Marfrig GF began distributing meats and imported vegetables in 1986, over the past two decades it has grown rapidly and diversified through organic growth and acquisitions of Brazilian and overseas companies. Marfrig GF operates through a number of wholly and part owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. The largest shareholders are CEO Marcos Antonio Molina dos Santos, and his wife, via a holding company and the Brazilian development bank. In 2013 Marfrig GF sold Seara Brazil and Zenda (non-beef operations) to fellow Brazilian meat processor JBS and refocused on beef and food service in its home market of Brazil. Internationally, however, it retained a broader food focus through its MoyPark and Keystone operations.
Today Marfrig GF is one of Brazil's three largest beef exporters. It employs 46,000 people across its 78 production units and distribution centres, and it has offices in Europe, South America, North America, Asia and Oceania.
Marfrig is divided into three principle segments: Marfrig Beef produces beef and lamb for the South American and export markets, brand include GJ and Aberdeen Angus; the Moy Park segment's primary focus is on Europe where it provides poultry and prepared meals to retailers and food service chains using both the Moy Park and Jamie Oliver brands; and the Keystone segment supplies restaurant chains with meat products, focussing on the US and Asian markets and with a number of joint ventures in China. 
The company has a daily slaughtering capacity of 20,730 head of cattle (as well as numerous chickens, heads of pork and lambs) and also produces 294,000 leather articles per month. In 2013 Marfrig GF launched the world's first Rainforest Alliance Certified beef. The group's poultry and feed operations also use significant amounts of soya within poultry feed.
Marfrig GF claims to participate in the Grupo de Trabalho da Pecuária Sustentável (GTPS) - Sustainable Beef Working Group - a World Bank initiative implemented by IFC - International Finance Corporation with the purpose of promoting the sustainability of the beef and veal commodity supply chain. It is also a member of the Leather Working Group and a signatory to numerous sustainability initiatives, including: the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; the public commitment Criteria for Industrial-Scale Operations with Livestock and Bovine Products in the Amazon Biome, in partnership with Greenpeace; and the Corporate Pact for Sustainable Connections. In addition Marfrig GF has contributed to some reforestation projects, including giving over 9,776,000 eucalyptus saplings to 780 rural producers in order to foster biosafety and the "green barrier" on poultry and pork farms.

Kellogg Company is a global manufacturer of cereal, snack and convenience foods. Under the Kellogg’s brand name and others, including Cheez-It and Pringles, the company markets products in over 180 countries.  As a leading producer of packaged foods, Kellogg uses significant quantities of soy, palm oil, pulp and paper throughout its product range.  Kellogg Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: The L’Oréal Group is a French cosmetics company present in 140 countries. It is active in all branches of cosmetics, such as make-up, skin care, hair care and perfume, and its major brands include Garnier, Maybelline New York and Ralph Lauren. The group is one of the largest manufacturers of beauty and personal care products globally and is high up the list in many other categories. The group is especially prominent in Western Europe, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, and Brazil.  L'Oreal S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Genting is a large investment and management company with major operations in hospitality, energy, and palm oil, especially in palm oil processing. It owns several processing facilities and claim to be one of the leading and lowest cost palm oil producers in Malaysia.  Genting Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

General Mills is an American company that manufactures and distributes baking products, ready meals, ice cream, cereals, snacks, soup, and yoghurt among other products.  With sales in six continents it offers over 100 brands, including Yoplait, Betty Crocker, and Cheerios.  General Mills Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

JBS is one of the world’s largest food companies and exporters of beef from Brazil. Across its meatpacking business it operates over 200 production facilities worldwide, with the capacity to process many tens of thousands of cattle per day. In addition to beef, JBS is exposed to soy, through its use of animal feed in cattle feedlots, poultry and swine farms. The company is also a significant player in the global leather industry, with over twenty tanneries in Brazil alone.  JBS is selected as a powerbroker for soy, beef, leather and paper packaging.

Orkla Group (Orkla) is a Norwegian based manufacturer of consumer goods, with other interests including hydropower and real estate. The group began over 350 years ago as a mining operation and through acquisitions and divestments the group has changed very dramatically; its focus is now on branded consumer goods including food and cleaning products, although the group does retain operations in hydro power aluminium products and paint manufacture.  In 2013, the group employed around 17,000 staff and had a turnover of NOK 33 Billion ($5.3 Billion).
Orkla branded consumer goods business accounts for around 86% of revenue and is divided into five business units: Orkla Foods, which operates in Nordic and Baltic regions and concentrates on Orkla's own brand products (which generally hold number 1 or 2 positions in their markets); Orkla Confectionary and Snacks, which owns the brands KIMs Danmark and the Estonian Kalev; the Home and Personal Division, which owns cleaning and comestic brands such as Jif, Comfort and Vaseline Intensive Care; the Orkla International Division, which operates in Russia, Poland, Austria and India; and Orkla Food Ingredients, which produces baking products such as yeast and butter blends.
Orkla Confectionary and Snacks and Orkla Foods are both RSPO members since 2007 and 2013, respectively, following the acquisition of the Swedish companies Goteborgs Kex and Procordia, which were RSPO members. In 2014, the company started a new initiative to reduce deforestation through palm oil use and aims to use traceable and sustainable sources by the end of 2017. They also released a policy for sustainable palm oil use.

Lindt employs a total of 8,949 people, has eight production sites (six in Europe and two in the USA) and distributes globally (including in China, Australia, South Africa, North America and Europe), with its largest markets being the European and NAFTA countries. The company distributes its products through a variety of avenues, including duty free retail outlets in airports, department stores, its own stores and Chocolate Cafes.
As a confectionery company, Lindt is ranked 7th in the world and 6th in Western Europe, and is also ranked among the top 50 packaged food companies globally. Further to this, Lindt is placed among the Forbes Global 2000 list. As a manufacturer of sweet snacks, Lindt uses palm oil in a number of its products and also includes soya derivatives, such as soya lecithin, as an ingredient in most of its chocolates.
Lindt has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2008. In 2012 it used 2,565m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products; and it aims to be sourcing 100% RSPO-certified sustainable palm oil by 2015.

It was founded and is owned by Peter Sondakh, who is among the richest men in Indonesia and also ranks among the top billionaires globally. 
The company has a growing presence in the agricultural industry. The group began over 350 years ago as a mining operation and through acquisitions and divestments the group has changed very dramatically; its focus is now on branded consumer goods including food and cleaning products, although the group does retain operations in hydro power aluminium products and paint manufacture.  In 2013, the group employed around 17,000 staff and had a turnover of NOK 33 Billion ($5.3 Billion).
Orkla branded consumer goods business accounts for around 86% of revenue and is divided into five business units: Orkla Foods, which operates in Nordic and Baltic regions and concentrates on Orkla's own brand products (which generally hold number 1 or 2 positions in their markets); Orkla Confectionary and Snacks, which owns the brands KIMs Danmark and the Estonian Kalev; the Home and Personal Division, which owns cleaning and comestic brands such as Jif, Comfort and Vaseline Intensive Care; the Orkla International Division, which operates in Russia, Poland, Austria and India; and Orkla Food Ingredients, which produces baking products such as yeast and butter blends.
Orkla Confectionary and Snacks and Orkla Foods are both RSPO members since 2007 and 2013, respectively, following the acquisition of the Swedish companies Goteborgs Kex and Procordia, which were RSPO members. In 2014, the company started a new initiative to reduce deforestation through palm oil use and aims to use traceable and sustainable sources by the end of 2017. They also released a policy for sustainable palm oil use.

Inditex SA owns the clothing and accessories retail brands Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Uterque and Zara Home. This Spanish company, formed by Amancio Ortega Gaona in 1963, is amongst the largest fashion retailers in the world, with a revenue of over €16 billion 2013.
Inditex SA started business with Zara in 1963, which is the largest and best known of all the company's brands; selling leather shoes and handbags, as well as mid-range clothes to men, women and children. Inditex was incorporated as the group's holding company in 1985 and in 1991 other brands were incorporated into the group. Today, Inditex has more than 6,000 stores in 88 countries around the world, with recent expansions into China and Russia. Outside of Zara, its other brands cover a wide range of markets, for example, Uterque is a dedicated accessory store, and Berksha and Pull&Bear target younger audiences.
Almost 90% of Inditex' suppliers come from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, India, South East Asia, Bangladesh, China, Brazil and Argentina, with over half of the company's manufacturing taking place in Spain or nearby countries, including Turkey and Morocco. This allows the company to respond to in-store demands and trends quickly, a model that has been dubbed 'Fast Fashion'. The company sells a range of apparel and accessories, including leather products, and notably, ranks in the top ten footwear companies in the western European market.

VF Corp (VF) is a US-based global apparel company, manufacturing and supplying apparel, footwear and accessories. Headquartered in North Carolina, in the US, VF's products are sold in more than 150 countries worldwide, through 47,000 retail outlets and 1,100 of the company's own stores.
Its products are marketed principally under the company's own brands, within five business divisions: Outdoor and Action Sports, Jeanswear, Imagewear, Sportswear and Contemporary Brands. VF has a diverse portfolio of brands, including well-known names, such as outdoor apparel brand, The North Face, footwear, apparel and accessories brand, Timberland, and luggage and bag brands, Eastpak, JanSport and Kipling. The company produces around 450 million items per year, and operates manufacturing facilities in the Middle East, Europe, Mexico, and Central and South America. As these facilities meet only a proportion of the company's production needs, especially for the company's footwear production, VF sources products from around 1,900 independently and company-run facilities. VF sources raw materials, including leather, from multiple international suppliers.
VF Corp is a leader in the global bags and luggage market, ranking in the top ten globally and occupying a leading position in the US, where it ranks third by market share. It is also a top player in the more fragmented footwear industry, ranking as the third largest in the US by market share, and where it also holds the third position, and is in the top ten globally.

ConAgra Foods is an American manufacturer of packaged food products as well as a provider of commercial products and foodservice. Its products are mostly frozen and refrigerated foods with well-known brands including Banquet, Blue Bonnet and Slim Jim, but it also produces cereals and snacks. ConAgra Foods is a major global player for oils and fats, sweet and savoury snacks, and ready meals.  ConAgra Brands Inc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

JBS is a global company involved in the beef, lamb and poultry processing, and in pork production.  It is among the largest producer of protein products worldwide, and is also involved in the production of leather, hygiene and cleaning products, collagen, metal packaging, biodiesel and other goods. JBS has operations spanning 24 countries and serves around 300,000 customers in 150 countries. 
Initially, the company was a small operation, with the capacity of processing five head of cattle per day. However, since 1953, JBS has expanded hugely, with major acquisitions in South America, the US, Australia and Europe. In 2007 JBS was floated on the Brazilian stock exchange, making it the first meat processing company in Brazil to do so. Today it is headquartered in Sao Paulo and employs around 185,000 people in total. Its operations are split between the following business divisions: JBS Mercosul, which comprises the company's beef and leather and related industries in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay; JBS USA, which is responsible for overseeing JBS' activities in Australia, Canada, the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico; and finally, JBS Foods, which was established in 2013 and covers the company's poultry, pork and value-added products in Brazil. 
The variety of products, which include fresh and frozen cuts to ready meals and processed foods service a variety of markets, including the catering, supermarket and export markets. These are marketed under several brands, including Bertin, Swift, and Friboi, and packaged foods, including ready meals under the Seara brand.
As well as its extensive operations in the global meat production and processing industries, which make beef of obvious significance, soya is also important, given its use in animal feed. For example, JBS operates 13 poultry farms, two pig farms and over 40 hatcheries, which use large amounts of animal feed. On top of its own operations, JBS also has around 5000 pig and poultry partner producers, which it provides with technical support and materials including all feed. Similarly within its beef operations, JBS operates cattle feedlots in Brazil the US and Australia where it provides all feed. Further to this, JBS is a significant player in the global leather industry, and with a daily processing capacity of one hundred thousand hides, leather processing is one of JBS' primary activities.

Cargill is a US-based agribusiness company operating in 70 countries. Its business operations include the procurement, processing and trading of agricultural commodities, food products and industrial products, and it also offers financial solutions. It is one of the major players in the South American soy industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company also has significant palm oil operations.  Cargill is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Tetra Laval consists of three industry groups, Tetra Pak, Sidel and DeLaval.  The companies' activities focus on systems for the processing, packaging and distribution of food and accessories for dairy production and animal husbandry and are assessed due to their use of pulp and paper.

R. R. Donnelley is a commercial printing company founded in 1864. It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. Their customers include some of the world's most well known companies including; Accenture, Barclays, IBM, and Microsoft. Despite offering a number of digital communication strategies, they are primarily known as a supplier of print material and is the leading company of its kind globally.  R. R. Donnelley also prints products for other companies involved in the printing and publishing sector. For example, it supplies print products to Pearson PLC and to HarperCollins, two of the world's largest publishers. In 2013 it employed roughly 57,000 people across four continents, in nearly 40 countries, leading to sales of $10.5 billion. It continues to expand through strategic acquisitions of companies specialising in both digital and commercial print. For example, in 2011, it acquired LibreDigital, a pioneering digital publishing and distribution company, and in 2014 acquired Consolidated Graphics in a deal worth over $600 million.

Prada SpA is the holding company of the Prada Group, which with its subsidiary companies, is involved in the design, manufacture and retail of leather goods, clothing, shoes, and accessories. Prada was founded in Italy in 1913 as a specialist retailer selling accessories, luggage and other luxury items. Today, the Prada brand forms a component of the Prada Group, which has become an international leader in the luxury goods industry. On top of the flagship Prada brand, the Group sells products under the Miu Miu, Car Shoe and Church's brands.  Prada and Miu Miu provide customers with a variety of high-end luxury items, including leatherwear, handbags, apparel, footwear and fragrances. The Car Shoe and Church's brands are more specialist and each offer high-end luxury footwear. Church's is a leading English leather footwear brand that dates back to 1873, while Car Shoe specialises in leather moccasins specifically designed for driving. The Prada Group's brands are sold through its own outlets in stores and online, and through wholesale distribution channels. The Group has a worldwide presence, including in the top fashion markets of London, Milan, Tokyo, Beijing, Hong Kong and New York.
Prada SpA is a significant player in the bags and luggage industry. It ranks among the top five bags and luggage companies globally, and in the top five in China and top three in the Western European market. It also plays an important role in the international footwear industry, particularly in the markets of China, the US and Europe.  Leather goods therefore form an important component of the Prada Group's business; accounting for over 65% of consolidated net sales in the year up to January 2014, totalling over 2 billion Euros.
Fibria are a pulp and paper company based in Brazil. The company are the world’s largest producers of eucalyptus pulp, owning around 1,056,000 hectares of forest across Brazil.

Unicharm Corporation manufactures and sells household care items, including baby, feminine, health and cosmetic products. Unicharm Corporation has operations spanning the globe, and holds the top share of diaper sales in China and Indonesia.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, Consumer Goods Forum

rows.coprofile: McDonald's is an American fast food retailer with more than 36,000 locations in over 100 countries. It is one of the largest fast food restaurant companies globally with a major market share. Additionally, it has one of the largest market shares in the US, China, Western Europe, and in India. The McDonald's menu of burgers, sandwiches, sides and beverages involves significant amounts of beef, soya and palm oil, as well as paper in packaging. In 2015, for example, over 120,000 metric tons of palm oil were used by McDonald's.
initiatives: Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, New York Declaration on Forests, Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner, WWF Global Forest & Trade Network

rows.coprofile: Sainsbury’s is a retail group also active in property, banking, and energy. The company operates supermarkets and convenience stores selling groceries and general merchandise. The company is also the owner of Home Retail Group, the owner of two more retail chains Argos and Habitat, creating one of the UK’s largest food and non-food retailers. The breadth of its retail offerings expose the group to a variety of forest risk commodities.  J Sainsbury's PLC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef, timber and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to leather.
initiatives: Cattle Agreement TAC, Palm Oil Transparency Coalition
Consumer Goods Forum Deforestation resolution (being a member of the CGF is not sufficient)

JBS is a global company involved in the beef, lamb and poultry processing, and in pork production.  It is among the largest producer of protein products worldwide, and is also involved in the production of leather, hygiene and cleaning products, collagen, metal packaging, biodiesel and other goods. JBS has operations spanning 24 countries and serves around 300,000 customers in 150 countries. 
Initially, the company was a small operation, with the capacity of processing five head of cattle per day. However, since 1953, JBS has expanded hugely, with major acquisitions in South America, the US, Australia and Europe. In 2007 JBS was floated on the Brazilian stock exchange, making it the first meat processing company in Brazil to do so. Today it is headquartered in Sao Paulo and employs around 185,000 people in total. Its operations are split between the following business divisions: JBS Mercosul, which comprises the company's beef and leather and related industries in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay; JBS USA, which is responsible for overseeing JBS' activities in Australia, Canada, the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico; and finally, JBS Foods, which was established in 2013 and covers the company's poultry, pork and value-added products in Brazil. 
The variety of products, which include fresh and frozen cuts to ready meals and processed foods service a variety of markets, including the catering, supermarket and export markets. These are marketed under several brands, including Bertin, Swift, and Friboi, and packaged foods, including ready meals under the Seara brand.
As well as its extensive operations in the global meat production and processing industries, which make beef of obvious significance, soya is also important, given its use in animal feed. For example, JBS operates 13 poultry farms, two pig farms and over 40 hatcheries, which use large amounts of animal feed. On top of its own operations, JBS also has around 5000 pig and poultry partner producers, which it provides with technical support and materials including all feed. Similarly within its beef operations, JBS operates cattle feedlots in Brazil the US and Australia where it provides all feed. Further to this, JBS is a significant player in the global leather industry, and with a daily processing capacity of one hundred thousand hides, leather processing is one of JBS' primary activities.

ING Group are a global banking group based in the Netherlands serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, insurance, investments, capital markets and retail banking services. As of 2024, ING Group's total assets amount to more than 200 billion EUR. ING Group are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, ING Group was providing over 59 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
initiatives: Member of the TNFD forum, PRB Nature Target-Setting working group,

rows.coprofile: Tesco started as a market stall in London in 1919, selling surplus groceries; its first store was opened ten years later in 1929. Following growth in the UK, Tesco floated on the London Stock Exchange in 1947. Today, Tesco is a multichannel grocery retailer active in eleven countries across Europe and Asia and also provides consumer financial services through its subsidiary, Tesco Bank. The company employs over 510,000 individuals and receives over 80 million shopping trips per week globally. In addition to its core grocery offering, in which it sells own branded and private label goods, Tesco sell a very broad range of other products including clothing, electronics, books and furniture. As a result of its large size and broad product range Tesco uses a range of forest risk commodities including, soy, beef, timber, paper and palm oil. In 2014, Tesco used 32,503 tons palm oil used in own brand products.

BASF is one of the world's leading chemical companies, operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF's home and personal care offerings. It is one of the top ten users of palm oil worldwide, using over 380,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products in 2015.

Lowe's Companies is a major home improvement company based in the US with operations in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. In 2015, Lowe's had one of largest market shares for DIY, furniture, and homeware in the world. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and is one of the top four leading home improvement companies worldwide.

Staples Inc is an office supplies retailer that sells a variety of products to businesses and individual consumers. It is the world's largest specialist retailer of office supplies with key products lines in stationery, furniture, and technology products. Staples sells a wide variety of paper products, including copy paper, computer paper and POS rolls, photographic paper and letterheads.
Established in 1985, the company is headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts in the United States. The company's three operational segments are: North American Stores & Online; North American Commercial; and International Operations. The company operates around 2,200 stores globally, and also sells products online and via its catalogue service. It also has around 116 distribution centres throughout the US, Canada, Europe, China, South America, and elsewhere, in all serving customers in 26 countries worldwide.
Staples is the world's largest retailer of a wide range of wood- and paper-based office products, sourcing its products from a range of suppliers in different countries, including Argentina, Brazil, Canada, China and the US. In 2013, paper sales accounted for around 9% of Staples' total revenue; office furniture contributed around 5%; and core office supplies, which include paper and other core office products such as writing products, around 30%. Staples sells its own proprietary branded products under the Staples and Quill trademarks and also offers other manufactured branded items.

General Mills is an American company that manufactures and distributes baking products, ready meals, ice cream, cereals, snacks, soup, and yoghurt among other products.  With sales in six continents it offers over 100 brands, including Yoplait, Betty Crocker, and Cheerios.  General Mills Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum Deforestation resolution (being a member of the CGF is not sufficient)

rows.coprofile: Marks & Spencer is a leading British retail company with over 1,000 stores worldwide. Through its diverse product range it is involved in the supply chains of a number of forest risk commodities. M&S Food sells products containing palm oil, soy and beef. Meanwhile the company’s apparel and luggage products use leather. M&S also sells home and garden furniture, for which timber is often used.  Marks & Spencer Group PLC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef, leather, timber and paper packaging.

AAK is a Swedish agricultural processor and manufacturer of food ingredients, lipids, technical products, and animal feed with 19 production facilities and sales offices in over 25 countries. The company claims to be the world's leading manufacturer of specialty vegetable fats and is a major company in the global bakery ingredients market. Soya sourced from South America as well as palm oil and its derivatives sourced from Central America and Southeast Asia are used in these products by the company. In 2015, AAK used over 950,000 metric tons of palm oil and its derivatives in its products.

Grupo Andre Maggi (AMAGGI) is a Brazilian agribusiness company active in the production, processing and trading of agricultural commodities. Its operations are primarily focussed in Brazil, but it also has an important presence in Argentina and Paraguay, as well as being present in Holland, Norway and Poland. It is a major player in the soya market. In 2014, the group had a planted area of over 130,000 hectares for soy and produced more than 450,000 metric tons of soya. It has three soya crushing facilities with an annual production capacity of over 2 million metric tons. In 2016, AMAGGI was among the top five Brazilian exporters of soya.

ABN Amro is a Dutch bank engaged in providing banking products and services. The bank serves the retail, private banking and corporate banking sectors.

Kao Corporation is a Japanese consumer goods company that manufactures beauty, health and home care products, whilst also providing chemicals to industrial markets. The company owns well-known brands such as Molton Brown, John Freida and Merries. Kao Corp is exposed to palm oil and soy, which are used in its consumer products, and also to pulp and paper which feature in both the company’s products and its packaging.  Kao Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Mondi Group is a global packaging and paper group organised across three business units: Corrugated Packaging, Flexible Packaging and Uncoated Fine Paper. Mondi Goup is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

Ferrero Group (Ferrero) is a family-owned confectionary business formally established in 1946 out of Pietro Ferrero's thriving factory in Piedmont, Italy. The company was one of the earliest in the Italian confectionery industry to expand overseas, with Michele Ferrero and his wife Maria Franca being the first Italians to open manufacturing operations in the confectionery business abroad after World War II. Until he passed away in February 2015, Michele Ferrero ranked 22nd on the Forbes list of billionaires and was the wealthiest man in Italy, worth $27 billion (though living in Monaco). His son Giovanni now runs the company, which operates in 51 countries worldwide and on every continent. The company has over 22,000 employees at 20 production and 3 research and development sites. In addition, the Ferrero Group has 8 agricultural companies for both direct cultivation and manufacturing purposes.
Ferrero is the fourth largest confectionary company in the world and in the past five years has rapidly expanded its sales in China and Russia. It owns many famous brands, including Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella, which was one of the company's first products in the 1940s. Ferrero uses palm oil in its confectionary to give products the right consistency. The company sources palm oil from Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and Brazil, using 150,000 tonnes annually.

rows.coprofile: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving individuals and companies. Their services include banking, trust banking, securities, credit cards, and leasing. As of 2017, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group's total assets amount to over 300 trillion Yen with over 100 trillion Yen in loans. They are among the top 10 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 51 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 30 with shares worth more than 13 billion USD.

Their services include retail banking, insurance, pensions, asset management and corporate lending. As of 2017, BBVA'a has more than 690 billion EUR in total assets and more than 416 billion EUR in loans and advances to customers. BBVA are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans to companies across several sectors, including food retail and packaged food.

Stora Enso produces packaging board, biomaterials, wood products and paper. The company is headquartered in Finland with operations in 14 counties including Brazil and China.  Stora Enso is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.  Permata Hijau Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

JP Morgan Chase and Co. are a global financial services firm headquartered in the US serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, wealth management, investments and retail banking services. As of 2017, the firm's total assets amount to over 2.5 trillion USD, with more than 900 billion USD worth of loans. JP Morgan Chase are among the top 5 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 105 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They also among the top 25 bondholders and top 15 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 1.3 billion USD worth of bonds and more than 25 billion USD word of shares.

Dunkin' Donuts has more than 11,500 restaurants in 40 countries worldwide and offers coffee and baked goods including doughnuts and bagels. Baskin-Robbins has more than 7,000 shops in nearly 50 countries offering ice-cream and beverages. The diverse menus of both expose the group to several forest risk commodities. Dunkin' Brands is one of the ten largest food providers globally by market share.

rows.coprofile: The Sime Darby Group is a Malaysian conglomerate involved in diverse industries, including logistics, industrial equipment, property and plantations. Sime Darby Plantation is the agribusiness arm of the group which has one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It also produces products such as oleochemicals, fats, biodiesel and other derivatives.  Sime Darby Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

The first Walmart store opened in 1962 in Arkansas, US. The company floated in 1970 and since then has grown within the US and internationally. Now, in 2014, Walmart operates 11,500 stores, under 65 banners, in 28 countries and employs 2.2 million members of staff. Walmart is one of the world's largest retailers.
Walmart operates in four segments: Walmart US, Walmart International, Sam's Club and Global e-Commerce. Within the US, Walmart operates stores in a variety of different formats, the largest is the Supercenter. The approximately 180,000 square foot Supercenters provide grocery, fresh produce, clothing, electronics and home furnishings. Some Supercenters also include pharmacies, health clinics, restaurants and banks. At the other end of the scale Walmart's smallest format, Express stores, focus on groceries and general merchandise. Pearson Plc (Pearson) is a London-based international media and education company, with key operations in the publishing industry. The company develops and publishes educational and entertainment materials in the form of books, newspapers and online. Pearson provides educational materials to teachers and students across 70 countries.  It also runs the Financial Times Group, a leading provider of business and financial news and analysis, both in print and online. Finally, Pearson is also the parent company of Penguin Random House, which claims to be the first truly global trade book publisher, and comprises the various publishing enterprises of the previously separate Penguin and Random House companies. Penguin Random House was formed in July 2013 after a merger was agreed between the respective publishing enterprises' parent companies, Pearson and Bertelsmann. The joint venture is based in New York and is jointly controlled by the two companies, with 53% owned by Bertelsmann, based in Germany, and 47% by Pearson.
In 2013, the book publishing operations of Pearson, the Penguin Group and Penguin Random House, individually ranked as the top two players in the book publishing industry globally. Only a very small proportion of Pearson's products are printed in-house, with the company instead sourcing from a number of suppliers around the world. For example, commercial printing company R. R. Donnelley, which is the leading company of its kind globally in terms of market share, is an important supplier of Pearson.

Koninklijke FrieslandCampina NV (Friesland) is a Dutch international dairy company. The company has four sections: Consumer Products Europe, Middle East and Africa; Consumer Products Asia; Cheese, Butter and Milk Powder; and finally Ingredients. It produces a wide range of products, including butter, cheese, condensed milk, cream, lactose, whey proteins, yoghurt and many others.
The company advertises itself as one of the top five dairy companies in the world. It is also the largest in Indonesia and Thailand, is in the top 5 for Malaysia and Western Europe and is in the global top 10 for baby food and dairy. It is also among the top 20 packaged food companies overall in the world.
Friesland operates 141 sites in over 26 countries, with the strongest presence in the Netherlands, where it can be found at 59 sites. The company employs 20,000 people and is supplied by 15,300 dairy farmers. Some it its most notable brands are Campina, Chocomel, Completa, Dutch Lady, Frisian Flag, Foremost, Betagen, Friesche Vlag and Fruttis, amongst others. Friesland used 90,000 tonnes of palm oil in its products in 2013. It has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2007.

Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A, which was one of the largest timber, paper and packaging companies in Brazil in 2014. Today, the Prada brand forms a component of the Prada Group, which has become an international leader in the luxury goods industry. On top of the flagship Prada brand, the Group sells products under the Miu Miu, Car Shoe and Church's brands.  Prada and Miu Miu provide customers with a variety of high-end luxury items, including leatherwear, handbags, apparel, footwear and fragrances. Church's is a leading English leather footwear brand that dates back to 1873, while Car Shoe specialises in leather moccasins specifically designed for driving. The Prada Group's brands are sold through its own outlets in stores and online, and through wholesale distribution channels. The Group has a worldwide presence, including in the top fashion markets of London, Milan, Tokyo, Beijing, Hong Kong and New York.

It ranks among the top five bags and luggage companies globally, and in the top five in China and top three in the Western European market. It also plays an important role in the international footwear industry, particularly in the markets of China, the US and Europe.  Leather goods therefore form an important component of the Prada Group's business; accounting for over 65% of consolidated net sales in the year up to January 2014, totalling over 2 billion Euros.

News Corporation (News Corp) is a media conglomerate with a network of companies in media, news, education and information services. In June 2013, News Corp's shareholders gave formal approval for the company to split its publishing and entertainment divisions, creating two new companies: News Corp, housing the company's publishing segment; 21st Century Fox housing the entertainment division. News Corp is now specifically a publishing company, producing newspaper, magazines, books and promotional inserts and coupons. The company was established in Australia in 1954, when Rupert Murdoch took control of the Australian corporation, News Limited, which had a majority interest in one of Adelaide's top daily newspapers. Since then, the company has grown dramatically and acquired numerous assets, beginning with newspapers in the UK: 'The Sun' and 'News of the World.' Established in Australia, News Corp is now based in the US and is the largest newspaper publishing company globally.
As of 2014, News Corp is comprised of the following businesses, with each housing several brands: News Corp Australia, News UK, Dow Jones & Company, New York Post, Harper Collins Publishers, Amplify, News America Marketing, and Storyful. News Corp Australia, for example, claims to be Australia's leading media and publishing company, selling over 10 million papers weekly, with titles including The Daily Telegraph, The Australian, and Herald Sun. News UK also publishes some of the UK's most well-known newspapers, including The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times. Dow Jones & Company publishes The Wall Street Journal and specialises in the provision of news and business information via a variety of media outlets.  Finally, News Corp's subsidiary HarperCollins is one of the world's most prominent book publishing companies. In May 2014, HarperCollins acquired book publisher Harlequin; the acquisition of the Canadian company is the biggest deal in book publishing since the merger of two other publishing giants, Penguin and Random House in 2013.

JBS is a global company involved in the beef, lamb and poultry processing, and in pork production.  It is among the largest producer of protein products worldwide, and is also involved in the production of leather, hygiene and cleaning products, collagen, metal packaging, biodiesel and other goods. JBS has operations spanning 24 countries and serves around 300,000 customers in 150 countries. 
Initially, the company was a small operation, with the capacity of processing five head of cattle per day. However, since 1953, JBS has expanded hugely, with major acquisitions in South America, the US, Australia and Europe. In 2007 JBS was floated on the Brazilian stock exchange, making it the first meat processing company in Brazil to do so. Today it is headquartered in Sao Paulo and employs around 185,000 people in total. Its operations are split between the following business divisions: JBS Mercosul, which comprises the company's beef and leather and related industries in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay; JBS USA, which is responsible for overseeing JBS' activities in Australia, Canada, the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico; and finally, JBS Foods, which was established in 2013 and covers the company's poultry, pork and value-added products in Brazil. 
The variety of products, which include fresh and frozen cuts to ready meals and processed foods service a variety of markets, including the catering, supermarket and export markets. These are marketed under several brands, including Bertin, Swift, and Friboi, and packaged foods, including ready meals under the Seara brand.
As well as its extensive operations in the global meat production and processing industries, which make beef of obvious significance, soya is also important, given its use in animal feed. For example, JBS operates 13 poultry farms, two pig farms and over 40 hatcheries, which use large amounts of animal feed. On top of its own operations, JBS also has around 5000 pig and poultry partner producers, which it provides with technical support and materials including all feed. Similarly within its beef operations, JBS operates cattle feedlots in Brazil the US and Australia where it provides all feed. Further to this, JBS is a significant player in the global leather industry, and with a daily processing capacity of one hundred thousand hides, leather processing is one of JBS' primary activities.

Mewah International Inc. (Mewah) is one of the dominant palm oil traders globally. It started operating in the 1950s with imports of palm oil from Malaysia to Singapore and is now involved in the production and distribution of a range of edible oils and fats. In 1987, Mewah opened its first refinery in Malaysia, producing 400 million tonnes per day, and has now opened a further two refineries, increasing its yearly capacity to 2.8 million tonnes. Mewah sources its raw materials from Malaysia and Indonesia before selling to the consumer and commercial markets in over 100 countries. It sells palm, soya bean, lauric, coconut, canola corn and sunflower oils commercially, and edible oils and fats on the consumer market. Mewah's consumer products are distributed via a range of different regional brands, such as Oki, Mona and Fry-ola, making it the world's leading edible oil company.
Mewah is also a key producer of food grade packaging for commercial and consumer markets. To continue to expand its business, Mewah is aiming to consolidate its position within the palm-based oil and fats business, expand its consumer product range, invest in efficient production facilities and expand its distribution network,. This has involved the construction of a new refinery in Sabah, Malaysia, which will increase Mewah's productivity to 3.5 million tonnes per year, along with the purchase of a new biodiesel facility in Westport, Malaysiaiv. Mewah has complemented these acquisitions with the installation of a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia, costing around $50 million, to produce a range of dairy products.
Mewah has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2006 and it expects to achieve 100% RSPO certification of all supply chains by 2015.

Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd is a holding company for the Nippon Paper Group, which is comprised of around 180 affiliates and subsidiaries. The Group ranks among the top forest, paper and packaging companies globally, occupying sixth place in a worldwide ranking of the top 100 and the second position of such companies in Japan. The Group produces a variety of paper products, including newsprint, printing paper, copy paper, wrapping paper, linerboard, paperboard, tissue products, and healthcare products. For example, through its subsidiary Nippon Paper Crecia Co Ltd, the Group manufactures family care, personal care and professional products under a license agreement with leading hygiene products company, Kimberly-Clark.
The Group has diverse business interests on top of its activities in the paper sector, and several of Nippon Paper Groups's other operations also make use of wood products. For example, it has several subsidiaries active in the wood products and construction industry; in the procurement of lumber and the manufacture of construction materials. These subsidiaries include Nippon Paper Lumber Co., Ltd., PAL Co., Ltd., and Daishowa Uniboard Co., Ltd. Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd has a global network supplying logs and lumber from a variety of sources, including domestically and from the United States, Canada, Europe, New Zealand and some tropical regions. As well as supplying raw and sawn timber, Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd also manufactures plywood and laminated lumber products. Pal Co Ltd and Daishowa Uniboard Co Ltd manufacture products for use in the construction industry, such as doors, staircases, flooring and decorative laminates.

The first Walmart store opened in 1962 in Arkansas, US. The company floated in 1970 and since then has grown within the US and internationally. Now, in 2014, Walmart operates 11,500 stores, under 65 banners, in 28 countries and employs 2.2 million members of staff. Walmart is one of the world's largest retailers.
Walmart operates in four segments: Walmart US, Walmart International, Sam's Club and Global e-Commerce. Within the US, Walmart operates stores in a variety of different formats, the largest is the Supercenter. The approximately 180,000 square foot Supercenters provide grocery, fresh produce, clothing, electronics and home furnishings. Some Supercenters also include pharmacies, health clinics, restaurants and banks. At the other end of the scale Walmart's smallest format, Express stores, focus on groceries and general merchandise. Sam's Club is a wholesaler catering to consumer and small business members who want to buy both groceries and general merchandise in bulk. Sam's Club operates in the US and internationally.
Walmart is present in 27 countries outside of the US, operating grocery and retail operations both through wholly owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. Stores operate under Walmart and other banners: in the UK Walmart operates through ASDA; and in Asia (India, Japan and China) Walmart operates under banners such as Walmart and Seiyu. Walmart's 2011 acquisition of a majority stake of in Massmart Holdings Limited also gives it a presence in sub-Saharan Africa; the majority of its 350 stores are in South Africa. Walmart also operates throughout Latin America, again under both Walmart and local banners.
Walmart sells both private label and international brand goods. As one of the world's largest retailers,  Walmart uses significant volumes of forest risk commodities including beef, leather, pulp and paper, timber, soy and palm oil. In 2014, Walmart used 96,411 MT of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in its own brand products.

Hormel Foods Corp (Hormel) is a manufacturer of food and meat products, based in the US. The company currently has operations in six countries but it markets its thousands of products in over 40 countries from 44 manufacturing facilities, with a total workforce of 19,800 employees. Out of its 48 brands, the group claims that 35 hold either the top or second highest market share.
Since being founded in 1891, Hormel has risen to number 1057 on the Forbes Global 2000 list and is ranked at 311 in the Fortune 500. The business is split into: Grocery products; refrigerated foods; Jennie-O Turkey Store; specialty foods; and all others, each marketed under the wholly-owned subsidiary of Hormel Foods International Corporation (HFIC). HFIC operates in four spheres: the Americas, Asia-Pacific, China and Europe. These are reached through six joint ventures, three licensees and two wholly-owned subsidiaries (Hormel Foods Australia and Jennie-O Turkey Store Inc).
Particularly prevalent in overseas markets are its SPAM (chopped pork and ham) and Stagg (chili) (beef) brands, which both hold the primary market share in the UK and Ireland. Hormel Foods Corp. has recently expanded with the purchase of CytoSport Holdings Inc, which manufactures Muscle Milk, for $450 million in an effort to reach a younger market. In terms of rankings, Hormel is placed in the world top ten for ready meals and chilled processed food, the top five in the world for spreads, and second in the US for spreads and canned/preserved food.

With the acquisition of hunting and fishing equipment store Mauritz Widforss in 1968, the company changed its name to Hennes & Mauritz and expanded its product range to also cover apparel for men and children. Since then, the company has expanded, opening stores throughout Europe as well as worldwide. For example, it expanded into the US in 2000, and opened stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2007. Orkla Group (Orkla) is a Norwegian based manufacturer of consumer goods, with other interests including hydropower and real estate. The group began over 350 years ago as a mining operation and through acquisitions and divestments the group has changed very dramatically; its focus is now on branded consumer goods including food and cleaning products, although the group does retain operations in hydro power aluminium products and paint manufacture.  In 2013, the group employed around 17,000 staff and had a turnover of NOK 33 Billion ($5.3 Billion).
Orkla branded consumer goods business accounts for around 86% of revenue and is divided into five business units: Orkla Foods, which operates in Nordic and Baltic regions and concentrates on Orkla's own brand products (which generally hold number 1 or 2 positions in their markets); Orkla Confectionary and Snacks, which owns the brands KIMs Danmark and the Estonian Kalev; the Home and Personal Division, which owns cleaning and comestic brands such as Jif, Comfort and Vaseline Intensive Care; the Orkla International Division, which operates in Russia, Poland, Austria and India; and Orkla Food Ingredients, which produces baking products such as yeast and butter blends.
Orkla Confectionary and Snacks and Orkla Foods are both RSPO members since 2007 and 2013, respectively, following the acquisition of the Swedish companies Goteborgs Kex and Procordia, which were RSPO members. In 2014, the company started a new initiative to reduce deforestation through palm oil use and aims to use traceable and sustainable sources by the end of 2017. They also released a policy for sustainable palm oil use.

The Rougier Group is an international company, based in France and operating in the timber supply chain. It produces primary timber products, such as sawnwood, plywood and logs; and processed products, such as joists and decking, as well as other materials for the construction, packaging and furniture industries. 
Its main operations consist of natural forest harvesting and wood processing in Africa through Rougier Afrique International; imports and distribution of timber products in France through Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux; and management and investment in industrial forest plantations in Africa, through Lignafrica.
Rougier Group's production and processing operations in Africa through Rougier Afrique International are in the Republic of Congo, Cameroon and Gabon, where it is among the largest forestry companies, managing a total area of around 2 million hectares. In Gabon, Rougier Group exploits around 880,000 hectares of forests under four forest concessions, and also operates one plywood factory and three sawmills. In Cameroon, it operates through its subsidiary Societe ForestiÃ¨re et Industrielle de la Doume (SFID; Doume Forestry Company), which exploits 550,000 hectares of forests and operates two sawmills and a secondary timber processing workshop. Rougier Group also operates in the northern Republic of Congo through its subsidiary, Mokabi SA. Mokabi SA manages 586,000 hectares of forests and operates a sawmill.
Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux imports to France over 40,000 cubic metres per year from Africa, America, Europe and Asia. Rougier Sylvaco Panneax is the result of a merger between Rougier Group's two subsidiaries: Rougier Sylvaco and Rougier Panneaux. The merger aims to position Rougier Group better in the French market, which is experiencing increased concentration among its operators.

The Godrej Group is an Indian conglomerate which, through its subsidiaries, operates in the consumer goods, real estate management, industrial engineering, furniture, appliances, security services, and agricultural products sectors. Established by Ardeshir Godrej in 1897, the Godrej family retain ownership of the group, although its subsidiaries Godrej Industries and Godrej Properties are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The company operates in 28 countries, with around three quarters of its business conducted in India where it is estimated that 500 million people use a Godrej product or service every day. In 2014, the group employed 28,000 people.
The Godrej Group is involved in palm oil through its subsidiaries at multiple stages within the supply chain. Godrej Industries, a holding company within the Godrej Group, is involved in a range of activities and sectors including the manufacture and marketing of oleo-chemicals as well as their precursors and derivatives, edible oils and bakery fats. Godrej International Limited, a subsidiary of Godrej Industries, trades vegetable oils such as palm oil internationally. Godrej Agrovet Ltd is an agribusiness subsidiary of Godrej Industries; it is India's largest animal feed manufacturer, producing over a million tons a year, and is also involved in palm oil production with 51,000 hectares of smallholder cultivation in India, four mills and a total land bank of 235,000 hectares. Finally, Godrej Consumer Products Ltd, the largest Indian personal care company, uses palm oil in its soaps. It is the largest Grade 1 quality soap and second largest toilet soap provider in India with brands such as Cinthol and No.1, and is currently seeking to increase its market share in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

Campbell Soup Co was founded in New Jersey, US, in 1869, when it began producing canned vegetables, soups, condiments and minced meats. The company now has annual sales of $8 billion and employs over 20,000 people. Its main business operations are divided into three divisions: simple meals (ready-made foods and soups); baked snacks; and health beverages and it has manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
The company's products are marketed under various brands, including Pepperidge Farms, which is the US division for cookies, crackers, bakery and frozen products and is led by 'Goldfish' crackers. However, the flagship Campbell's brand is the company's main source of revenue and is worth around US$2 billion. Through this brand, the company sells almost 2 billion cans of soup each year, accounting for 60% of the United States' market for canned soup. Campbell Soup Co continues to expand its range of products through investments into, and acquisitions of, other companies.
