H&M Hennes and Mauritz AB is a Swedish clothing company operating under several brands, including its flagship brand H&M, as well as COS, Monki, Cheap Monday, and & Other Stories . The company, headquartered in Sweden, is involved in designing, manufacturing and marketing apparel, accessories and home textiles.  It was established in 1947, with the opening of its first Hennes store in VÃ¤sterÃ¥s, Sweden, which exclusively sold women's clothing. With the acquisition of hunting and fishing equipment store Mauritz Widforss in 1968, the company changed its name to Hennes & Mauritz and expanded its product range to also cover apparel for men and children. Since then, the company has expanded, opening stores throughout Europe as well as worldwide. For example, it expanded into the US in 2000, and opened stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2007. Further to this, the company established a new brand, COS, in 2007 and acquired the fashion firm, FaBric Scandinavien AB, in 2008, which holds the Weekday, Monki and Cheap Monday brands . In 2010, the full incorporation of FaBric Scandinavien was completed, when Hennes & Mauritz acquired the remaining 40% of shares.

VF Corp (VF) is a US-based global apparel company, manufacturing and supplying apparel, footwear and accessories. Headquartered in North Carolina, in the US, VF's products are sold in more than 150 countries worldwide, through 47,000 retail outlets and 1,100 of the company's own stores.
Its products are marketed principally under the company's own brands, within five business divisions: Outdoor and Action Sports, Jeanswear, Imagewear, Sportswear and Contemporary Brands. VF has a diverse portfolio of brands, including well-known names, such as outdoor apparel brand, The North Face, footwear, apparel and accessories brand, Timberland, and luggage and bag brands, Eastpak, JanSport and Kipling. The company produces around 450 million items per year, and operates manufacturing facilities in the Middle East, Europe, Mexico, and Central and South America. As these facilities meet only a proportion of the company's production needs, especially for the company's footwear production, VF sources products from around 1,900 independently and company-run facilities. VF sources raw materials, including leather, from multiple international suppliers.
VF Corp is a leader in the global bags and luggage market, ranking in the top ten globally and occupying a leading position in the US, where it ranks third by market share. It is also a top player in the more fragmented footwear industry, ranking as the third largest in the US by market share, and where it also holds the third position, and is in the top ten globally.

The first Walmart store opened in 1962 in Arkansas, US. The company floated in 1970 and since then has grown within the US and internationally. Now, in 2014, Walmart operates 11,500 stores, under 65 banners, in 28 countries and employs 2.2 million members of staff. Walmart is one of the world's largest retailers.
Walmart operates in four segments: Walmart US, Walmart International, Sam's Club and Global e-Commerce. Within the US, Walmart operates stores in a variety of different formats, the largest is the Supercenter. The approximately 180,000 square foot Supercenters provide grocery, fresh produce, clothing, electronics and home furnishings. Some Supercenters also include pharmacies, health clinics, restaurants and banks. At the other end of the scale Walmart's smallest format, Express stores, focus on groceries and general merchandise. Sam's Club is a wholesaler catering to consumer and small business members who want to buy both groceries and general merchandise in bulk. Sam's Club operates in the US and internationally.
Walmart is present in 27 countries outside of the US, operating grocery and retail operations both through wholly owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. Stores operate under Walmart and other banners: in the UK Walmart operates through ASDA; and in Asia (India, Japan and China) Walmart operates under banners such as Walmart and Seiyu. Walmart's 2011 acquisition of a majority stake of in Massmart Holdings Limited also gives it a presence in sub-Saharan Africa; the majority of its 350 stores are in South Africa. Walmart also operates throughout Latin America, again under both Walmart and local banners.
Walmart sells both private label and international brand goods. As one of the world's largest retailers,  Walmart uses significant volumes of forest risk commodities including beef, leather, pulp and paper, timber, soy and palm oil. In 2014, Walmart used 96,411 MT of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in its own brand products.

PT Rajawali Corpora is an investment holding company of the Rajawali Group, an Indonesian conglomerate active in a variety of industries, including telecommunications, hotels, consumer goods, retail, transportation, coal, gold and iron mining, and agriculture. The Group's agricultural activities comprise palm, sugar, rubber and corn plantations. Founded in 1984, the company is based in Jakarta and employs some 30,000 people. It was founded and is owned by Peter Sondakh, who is among the richest men in Indonesia and also ranks among the top billionaires globally. 
The company has a growing presence in the agricultural industry. PT Jaya Madiri Sukses (JMS Group) is the plantation arm of the Rajawali Group, and is a holding company comprising of a total of seven plantation companies in South and East Kalimantan. In 2010, Rajawali was reported to begin planting its 200,000 hectare land bank with oil palm. In 2011 Rajawali entered into a joint venture with commodities trader Louis Dreyfus called Green Eagle Plantations Pte Ltd. In 2012, the venture was reported to operate in four regions in Indonesia (South, West and East Kalimantan, and Papua), with concessions of around 50,000 hectares. However, in 2014, Louis Dreyfus Commodities Asia Pte left the joint venture, selling its 50% share of Green Eagle to the Rajawali Group. More recently, in September 2014, through a purchase of two investment firms, Matacuna Group and Pegasus CP One, Rajawali reportedly has acquired a 21% stake in crude palm oil producer, BW Plantation.

The company's main business activities include the production, processing, preparation, sale and distribution of meat (beef, pork, lamb and poultry), pasta and processed foods (including pizzas, lasagnas, breaded products and desserts), ready meals and frozen vegetables, as well as the distribution of other food products (including frozen foods, sausages and fish) and semi-finished and finished leather.
Marfrig GF began distributing meats and imported vegetables in 1986, over the past two decades it has grown rapidly and diversified through organic growth and acquisitions of Brazilian and overseas companies. Marfrig GF operates through a number of wholly and part owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. The largest shareholders are CEO Marcos Antonio Molina dos Santos, and his wife, via a holding company and the Brazilian development bank. In 2013 Marfrig GF sold Seara Brazil and Zenda (non-beef operations) to fellow Brazilian meat processor JBS and refocused on beef and food service in its home market of Brazil. Internationally, however, it retained a broader food focus through its MoyPark and Keystone operations.
Today Marfrig GF is one of Brazil's three largest beef exporters. It employs 46,000 people across its 78 production units and distribution centres, and it has offices in Europe, South America, North America, Asia and Oceania.
Marfrig is divided into three principle segments: Marfrig Beef produces beef and lamb for the South American and export markets, brand include GJ and Aberdeen Angus; the Moy Park segment's primary focus is on Europe where it provides poultry and prepared meals to retailers and food service chains using both the Moy Park and Jamie Oliver brands; and the Keystone segment supplies restaurant chains with meat products, focussing on the US and Asian markets and with a number of joint ventures in China. 
The company has a daily slaughtering capacity of 20,730 head of cattle (as well as numerous chickens, heads of pork and lambs) and also produces 294,000 leather articles per month. In 2013 Marfrig GF launched the world's first Rainforest Alliance Certified beef. The group's poultry and feed operations also use significant amounts of soya within poultry feed.
Marfrig GF claims to participate in the Grupo de Trabalho da Pecuária Sustentável (GTPS) - Sustainable Beef Working Group - a World Bank initiative implemented by IFC - International Finance Corporation with the purpose of promoting the sustainability of the beef and veal commodity supply chain. It is also a member of the Leather Working Group and a signatory to numerous sustainability initiatives, including: the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; the public commitment Criteria for Industrial-Scale Operations with Livestock and Bovine Products in the Amazon Biome, in partnership with Greenpeace; and the Corporate Pact for Sustainable Connections. In addition Marfrig GF has contributed to some reforestation projects, including giving over 9,776,000 eucalyptus saplings to 780 rural producers in order to foster biosafety and the "green barrier" on poultry and pork farms.

News Corp is a media, information, and publishing service. News Corp owns many big newspapers, such as the Times, the Sun, the Wall Street Journal and New York Post. The large-scale publishing operations require vast amounts of pulp and paper.   News Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Unicharm Corporation manufactures and sells household care items, including baby, feminine, health and cosmetic products. Unicharm Corporation has operations spanning the globe, and holds the top share of diaper sales in China and Indonesia.

3M Company is an American manufacturer operating in four areas: safety and industrial, transportation and electronics, health care, and consumer. 3M Company’s safety and industrial segment serves the paper, printing and packaging markets. The company has over 80 manufacturing plants across the United States with more than 120 manufacturing and converting operations worldwide.  3M Company is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

rows.coprofile: Orkla is a Norwegian company supplying consumer goods products. The company sells ready-meals, soups, snacks, confectionary, food ingredients, personal hygiene products, and laundry detergents among other products. Orkla claims to be the leading branded consumer goods company in the Nordic and the Baltic region.   Orkla Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Associated British Foods is a diversified group with operations in food, ingredients and retail. The group's business units include teas, cereals, sugars, and animal feed with such brands such as Twinings, Ryvita, and Blue Dragon. It is also a leading vendor in the baking ingredients market and the owner of the clothing retailer Primark. These diverse businesses expose the group to palm oil and soya in food production, soya in animal feed and leather in apparel. In 2015, for example, it used more than 24,000 metric tons of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in its products. It is also among the top fifteen producers of animal feed in Europe, with a production of over 2.2 million metric tons in 2014.

Kingfisher is a European home improvement company that operates chains of retail stores including B&Q, Castorama and Screwfix. Through its various subsidiaries, Kingfisher trades in a large number of timber products, ranging from garden sheds, to furniture and DIY supplies. It is also exposed to leather in some of its products.  Kingfisher Plc is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Group Ligna is the parent company of Klabin S.A., the largest paper manufacturer and exporter in Brazil, headquartered in Sao Paulo. They manufacture packaging paper and board, corrugated boxes, industrial sacks and timber, with 22 industrial plants in Brazil and one in Argentina. Klabin S.A. are also the largest paper recycler in Brazil, holding 11% of the country's recycling market. They have been selected as a powerbroker for timber and pulp and paper.

Founded in 1927 in Cologne, Germany, the REWE Group employs over 330,000 individuals in 15,000 stores. Germany is REWE Group's largest market, generating 70% of the Group's revenue in 2014, but the company has operations across 11 other European countries.
REWE Group operates in the food sector through multiple chains and formats including; REWE, REWE Center, REWE City, Penny (a discount store) and TEMMA (an organic supermarket). Supermarkets offer a number of store (own) brands such as Penny, ja!, REWE, Muhlenhof and REWE Bio,  whose offerings include meat products, diary and bakery products. In 2014, REWE Group reported using 10,800 tonnes of palm oil in its own brand products.
REWE Group also operates DIY stores under the Toom Baumarkt and B1 Discount Baumarkt brands. Toom Baumarkt stores provide the Toom quality store branded products, with a broad range of items ranging from garden furniture to plant seeds. REWE Group is also active in the Travel & Tourism and Consumer Electronics retail sectors.

Their services include corporate finance, investment management and financial and operating leases, as well as retail banking and consumer finance. SMBC Group is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group. SMBC Group is the banking unit of the organisation. rows.coprofile: The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.  Permata Hijau Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Casino Guichard Perrachon (Casino) is a French retailer with more than 15,000 convenience stores, hypermarkets and supermarkets predominantly in France and Latin America. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Globally, the group is among the top twenty retailers for edible groceries, but it has an especially strong presence in Latin America where it is among the top five. Casino claims to be the top retailer in Brazil, Colombia and Vietnam.

Danzer is a German timber company based in Austria that produces veneer, lumber and other wood products from hardwood. Just under a third of Danzer's raw material comes from Africa where, as of 2016, they own 1.1 million hectares of forestry concessions in the Republic of Congo. Annually, Danzer processes 500,000 cubic metres of wood, with processing facilities in North America and Europe. It claims to be the largest producer of decorative veneer in the world.

rows.coprofile: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is an American company involved in the global cultivation, processing, manufacturing and trading of agricultural commodities, ingredients for food and animal feed, as well as biofuels. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soya in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is among the top five  processors of soya in Brazil with an annual capacity of around 4 million metric tons in 2016, and is a leading player in Bolivia and Paraguay. Additionally, ADM is one of the world's major biodiesel producers with a reported production capacity of more than 135 million barrels per day. It is also involved in the palm oil supply chain and has an ownership interest in Wilmar International.

Hormel Foods Corp (Hormel) is a manufacturer of food and meat products, based in the US. The company currently has operations in six countries but it markets its thousands of products in over 40 countries from 44 manufacturing facilities, with a total workforce of 19,800 employees. Out of its 48 brands, the group claims that 35 hold either the top or second highest market share.
Since being founded in 1891, Hormel has risen to number 1057 on the Forbes Global 2000 list and is ranked at 311 in the Fortune 500. The business is split into: Grocery products; refrigerated foods; Jennie-O Turkey Store; specialty foods; and all others, each marketed under the wholly-owned subsidiary of Hormel Foods International Corporation (HFIC). HFIC operates in four spheres: the Americas, Asia-Pacific, China and Europe. These are reached through six joint ventures, three licensees and two wholly-owned subsidiaries (Hormel Foods Australia and Jennie-O Turkey Store Inc).
Particularly prevalent in overseas markets are its SPAM (chopped pork and ham) and Stagg (chili) (beef) brands, which both hold the primary market share in the UK and Ireland. Hormel Foods Corp. has recently expanded with the purchase of CytoSport Holdings Inc, which manufactures Muscle Milk, for $450 million in an effort to reach a younger market. In terms of rankings, Hormel is placed in the world top ten for ready meals and chilled processed food, the top five in the world for spreads, and second in the US for spreads and canned/preserved food.

Restaurant Brands International Inc. is the third largest fast food company in the world by market share, the second largest in western Europe and the fourth largest in the US. It was created in 2014 through the merging of two companies, Burger King Worldwide Inc. (Burger King) and Tim Hortons. The new company is headquartered in Canada, with 3G Capital being the majority shareholder. 
Burger King is the second largest fast food hamburger chain in the world, with 11 million customers visiting its stores every day. The company was founded in 1954 and in 2010, investment firm 3G Capital became the majority shareholder. The fast food giant is present in over 95 countries and US territories, and as of the end of 2013, comprised 13,667 restaurants, with the majority (54%) in the US and Canada and providing the bulk of the company's revenue. Having said this, Burger King is increasingly targeting expansion elsewhere, especially in high growth emerging markets. Burger King uses palm oil in its baked goods and as frying oil in the Asia/Pacific region and also uses soya in a number of its products, including baked goods.
Tim Hortons, with which Burger King merged to create Restaurant Brands International, is another multinational leader in the fast food industry. Tim Hortons franchises fast food restaurants primarily in Canada and the US. It is well known for its coffee and donuts, and also offers other sandwiches, bagels, cookies, muffins and pastries. Tim Horton's was started in Canada in the 1960s and now has around 4,304 restaurants, 3,468 in Canada, 807 in the US and 29 in the Gulf. Tim Horton's is one of the top ten largest fast food restaurant providers in the world and the largest in Canada. Tim Horton's demonstrates similar use of forest risk commodities to Burger King, purchasing both palm and soya bean oil for use in its products.
Note: In 2014 and 2015 this company was assessed under the name 'Burger King Worldwide Inc.'

rows.coprofile: Sinar Mas is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including pulp and paper, agriculture and food, energy, financial services, and real estate. The group's agricultural business operates about 480,000 hectares of palm oil plantation as of 2016 and has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It also has an annual processing capacity of more than 12 million fresh fruit bunches and is one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Its products include cooking oil and margarine. Additionally, the group crushes soya, with an annual capacity of 2.3 million metric tons. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.

Cargill is a US-based agribusiness company operating in 70 countries. Its business operations include the procurement, processing and trading of agricultural commodities, food products and industrial products, and it also offers financial solutions. It is one of the major players in the South American soy industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company also has significant palm oil operations.  Cargill is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Their services cover personal, corporate, offshore, private, and investment banking, wealth management, loans and mortgages, and corporate lending. As of 2017, Barclays PLC's total assets amount to more than 1.1 trillion GBP with over 420 billion GBP in loans. They are among the top 5 lenders to Forest 500 companies with loans amounting to over 70 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 200 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 1.7 billion USD worth of shares.

Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

Grupo Andre Maggi (AMAGGI) is a Brazilian agribusiness company active in the production, processing and trading of agricultural commodities. Its operations are primarily focussed in Brazil, but it also has an important presence in Argentina and Paraguay, as well as being present in Holland, Norway and Poland. It is a major player in the soya market. In 2014, the group had a planted area of over 130,000 hectares for soy and produced more than 450,000 metric tons of soya. It has three soya crushing facilities with an annual production capacity of over 2 million metric tons. In 2016, AMAGGI was among the top five Brazilian exporters of soya.

Their services include wealth management, insurance, capital markets, investments, commercial banking and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.2 trillion CAD, with net loans worth nearly 480 billion CAD. The Royal Bank of Canada are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 11 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 50 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 7 billion USD worth of shares.

As of 2017, Aegon manage a combined value of 840 billion EUR of investments, including more than 325 billion EUR in assets under management. They are one of the top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with approximately 2 billion USD worth of bonds for companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

UBS are among the top 15 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 26 billion USD worth of shares across a broad range of forest risk sectors. Some of the famous brands in Mondelez’s portfolio include Cadbury, Belvita, Mika, Ritz, and Oreo. According to the company, it is are one of the biggest snack companies in the world. Through its products Mondelez are exposed to palm oil and soy.  Mondelez International Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Lindt & Sprungli AG (Lindt) is a Swiss chocolatier founded in 1845, which describes itself as the market leader in the premium chocolates industry. The company sells in over 100 countries worldwide, with products under the brand names Ghirardelli, Caffarel, Hofbauer and Kufferle. Lindt employs a total of 8,949 people, has eight production sites (six in Europe and two in the USA) and distributes globally (including in China, Australia, South Africa, North America and Europe), with its largest markets being the European and NAFTA countries. The company distributes its products through a variety of avenues, including duty free retail outlets in airports, department stores, its own stores and Chocolate Cafes.
As a confectionery company, Lindt is ranked 7th in the world and 6th in Western Europe, and is also ranked among the top 50 packaged food companies globally. Further to this, Lindt is placed among the Forbes Global 2000 list. As a manufacturer of sweet snacks, Lindt uses palm oil in a number of its products and also includes soya derivatives, such as soya lecithin, as an ingredient in most of its chocolates.
Lindt has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2008. In 2012 it used 2,565m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products; and it aims to be sourcing 100% RSPO-certified sustainable palm oil by 2015.

rows.coprofile: News Corp is a media, information, and publishing service. News Corp owns many big newspapers, such as the Times, the Sun, the Wall Street Journal and New York Post. The large-scale publishing operations require vast amounts of pulp and paper.   News Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

The Sime Darby Group is a Malaysian conglomerate involved in diverse industries, including logistics, industrial equipment, property and plantations. Sime Darby Plantation is the agribusiness arm of the group which has a landbank of approximately 1 million hectares with 600,000 hectares of planted oil palm. This is one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. In 2015, the group processed more than 10 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches and produced more than 2 million metric tons of crude palm oil. It also produces products such as oleochemicals, fats, biodiesel and other derivatives.
initiatives: Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner, New York Declaration on Forests, High Conservation Value Resource Network

rows.coprofile: ABN Amro is a Dutch bank engaged in providing banking products and services. The bank serves the retail, private banking and corporate banking sectors.
initiatives: Statement on deforestation/conversion showing understanding of risks to the financial institution

rows.coprofile: JBS is one of the world’s largest food companies and exporters of beef from Brazil. Across its meatpacking business it operates over 200 production facilities worldwide, with the capacity to process many tens of thousands of cattle per day. In addition to beef, JBS is exposed to soy, through its use of animal feed in cattle feedlots, poultry and swine farms. The company is also a significant player in the global leather industry, with over twenty tanneries in Brazil alone.  JBS is selected as a powerbroker for soy, beef, leather and paper packaging.

The Clorox Company, headquartered in the US, specialises in manufacturing consumer and professional cleaning products, as well as personal care products. The Clorox Company has operations in 25 countries, with brand names including Burt’s Bees, Clorox and Glad.  Clorox Co, The is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.

Mondelez International (Mondleez) was formed in 2012 as a spinoff of Kraft International. Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack companies with global net revenues of approximately $35 billion in 2013. 60% of the 2013 net revenue originated from biscuit and chocolate sales, with 40% of these sales in Europe and 20% in North Americai. It has over 100,000 employees and manufactures products for consumption in around 165 countries around the worldi.  In total, it has nine billion dollar brands, including Tang, Cadbury, Nabisco and Oreo biscuits. Further to that, the company also owns another 53 brands with annual revenues greater than $100 millioni. Through these brands, the company produces beverages, biscuits, cheese, chocolate and chewing gum. It also invests strongly in research and development, with numerous facilities across Europe, such as the chocolate centre for excellence in Bournville, UK, and its biscuits research and development centre in Saclay, France. The company is now focusing its attention on emerging markets through the expansion of existing manufacturing plants and the building of new ones. For example, Mondelez has expanded its chocolate factory in Curitiba, Brazil and spent $350 million on the construction of a new biscuit factory in Monteray, Mexicoi.
Mondelez International (formerly known as Kraft International) has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011. In 2012, the company used 285732 m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products. Of this 200,653 m3 was RSPO certified (crude palm oil plus palm kernel oil).
initiatives: "Data from our 2018 LCA show the contribution to emissions from land-use change for our cocoa, palm oil and soy that we buy directly, based on publicly available scientific datasets of sector averages for each raw material".

rows.coprofile: ABN Amro is a Dutch bank engaged in providing banking products and services. The bank serves the retail, private banking and corporate banking sectors. In the 2022 selection, ABN Amro was providing 4.2 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving individuals and companies. Their services include banking, trust banking, securities, credit cards, and leasing. As of 2024, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial's total assets amount to over 2.6 trillion USD . They are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial was providing 173 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia are a financial services provider headquartered in Australia that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. They offer a range of products and services including retail, premium, business and institutional banking, funds management, pension programmes, insurance, and investment and share-broking products and services. As of 2017, Commonwealth Bank of Australia's total assets amount to over 970 billion AUD with over 730 billion AUD in loans. They are among the top 100 shareholders for Forest 500 Companies, with over 3 billion USD worth of shares.

Arcor is an Argentinian manufacturer of foodstuffs and packaged food operating in five South American countries and selling products in over 120 countries worldwide. Products it produces include confectionary, ice-cream, chocolates, canned food, sugars, and packaging. The company has a worldwide presence, ranking among the ten largest companies for biscuits and snacks by market share, and among the top twenty for packaged food and spreads. It is also an important player in Brazil where it ranks among the top fifteen for packaged foods and among the top ten for biscuits and snacks.

Arcor is an Argentinian manufacturer of foodstuffs and packaged food operating in five South American countries and selling products in over 120 countries worldwide. Products it produces include confectionary, ice-cream, chocolates, canned food, sugars, and packaging. The company has a worldwide presence, ranking among the ten largest companies for biscuits and snacks by market share, and among the top twenty for packaged food and spreads. It is also an important player in Brazil where it ranks among the top fifteen for packaged foods and among the top ten for biscuits and snacks.

Tetra Laval consists of three industry groups, Tetra Pak, Sidel and DeLaval.  The companies' activities focus on systems for the processing, packaging and distribution of food and accessories for dairy production and animal husbandry and are assessed due to their use of pulp and paper.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum Deforestation resolution (being a member of the CGF is not sufficient)

rows.coprofile: Operating across the United States, China and India, Tyson Foods Inc. has business in poultry, beef, pork and processed food products. The company’s poultry business is particularly noteworthy here, because it involves the provision of feed product to a network of independent poultry farmers that in 2015 exceeded 4,000. Animal feed uses significant quantities of soy, and in 2014 Tyson Food Inc’s operations in this field saw it ranked among the top ten feed producers worldwide.   Tyson Foods Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Target Corporation is a leading United States retailer with over 1,800 stores. The company is recognised as an industry leader, and in 2016 was ranked among the top 50 on the Fortune 500. It sells a variety of products including food, personal care items, paper products, furniture and apparel. Amongst these product lines Target sells several own-brand goods under labels including Market Pantry and Archer Farms. Through its retail and production operations Target is exposed to a variety of forest risk commodities.  Target Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef, leather, timber and paper packaging.

Minerva is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.  MINERVA is selected as a powerbroker for beef and leather and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Morgan Stanley are an international investment bank and financial services provider headquartered in the US that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Services include wealth management, investment banking, capital markets, sales and trading, and research and investment management. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 850 billion USD, with more than 130 billion USD worth of loans. Morgan Stanley are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 36 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 20 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 19 billion USD worth of shares.

The Schwarz Group is a German retail group comprised of both wholesalers and multi-format retail stores. Its supermarkets operate under the brands Kaufland, Handelshof and Kaufmarkt, alongside the discount retailer Lidl. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. With the combined weight of these retailers, the Schwarz Group is among the top retailers for edible groceries in Europe and globally. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities.    Schwarz Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong (KLK) is a Malaysian agribusiness company active in the cultivation, processing and manufacturing of palm oil and rubber, as well as being involved in property development. The company has one of the largest landbanks among palm oil producers across Malaysia, Indonesia and Liberia. It also owns several mills and two refineries and is among the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.  Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to timber and paper packaging.

Sumitomo Forestry Co. Ltd, is a timber company with operations in forestry, processing, materials provision and construction. The company is one of the world’s largest forestry companies and has subsidiaries operating across East and Southeast Asia, Oceania and North America.  Sumitomo Forestry is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Harita Group is an Indonesian conglomerate. It's subsidiary Bumitama Agri is a palm oil company involved in the cultivation and processing of oil palm with one of the largest landbanks of global palm oil producers.  Harita Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

rows.coprofile: Essity is a Swedish company which manufacturers paper-based products including personal care, and hygiene products.  Essity is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Kraft Heinz is one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world. Its numerous iconic brands include Kraft, Heinz, Kool-Aid, Capri-Sun and Philadelphia. As one of the leading international food product manufacturers Kraft Heinz is exposed to a range of forest risk commodities. Notably, its product range involves the use of palm oil, soy, pulp and paper. Kraft Heinz Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia are a financial services provider headquartered in Australia that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. They offer a range of products and services including retail, premium, business and institutional banking, funds management, pension programmes, insurance, and investment and share-broking products and services. As of 2017, Commonwealth Bank of Australia's total assets amount to over 970 billion AUD with over 730 billion AUD in loans. They are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 Companies.

Ajinomoto Co Inc is a Japanese multinational food and biotech company based in Tokyo. Ajinomoto Group has products in more than 130 countries and regions and sources raw materials, including beef, from Brazil, Japan, China, Thailand, India, Turkey, the United States, Canada, Mexico, Argentina, Uruguay, Australia and New Zealand. It has been selected as a powerbroker for beef, and is also assessed for it's exposure to palm oil, soy, and pulp and paper.

rows.coprofile: Barclays are a multinational universal bank, headquartered in the UK serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services cover personal, corporate, offshore, private, and investment banking, wealth management, loans and mortgages, and corporate lending. As of 2024, Barclays have over 2 trillion USD in assets under management. They are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Barclays was providing 208 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Tesco is a leading British retailer with over 6,000 stores worldwide. The company specialises in groceries but also sells personal care items, apparel and furniture, as well as offering financial services through its subsidiary Tesco Bank. Amongst its product lines, Tesco sells a range of own brand products including packaged meats, dairy products and confectionary items. The company’s operations leave it exposed to several forest risk commodities.   Tesco plc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.  Permata Hijau Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.
Kencana Agri is a palm oil plantation company based in Indonesia with a planted area of over 65,000 ha.  Kencana Agri Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

AAK refines vegetable oils for specialised products mainly for foodservice, chocolate and confectionery, and technical products.  The Swedish company has 19 production facilities and sales offices in more than 25 countries, and claims to be the world’s leading manufacturer of specialty vegetable fats. AAK sources Soy from South America and Palm Oil from Southeast Asia and Central America.   AAK AB is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Koninklijke FrieslandCampina NV (Friesland) is a Dutch international dairy company. The company has four sections: Consumer Products Europe, Middle East and Africa; Consumer Products Asia; Cheese, Butter and Milk Powder; and finally Ingredients. It produces a wide range of products, including butter, cheese, condensed milk, cream, lactose, whey proteins, yoghurt and many others.
The company advertises itself as one of the top five dairy companies in the world. It is also the largest in Indonesia and Thailand, is in the top 5 for Malaysia and Western Europe and is in the global top 10 for baby food and dairy. It is also among the top 20 packaged food companies overall in the world.
Friesland operates 141 sites in over 26 countries, with the strongest presence in the Netherlands, where it can be found at 59 sites. The company employs 20,000 people and is supplied by 15,300 dairy farmers. Some it its most notable brands are Campina, Chocomel, Completa, Dutch Lady, Frisian Flag, Foremost, Betagen, Friesche Vlag and Fruttis, amongst others. Friesland used 90,000 tonnes of palm oil in its products in 2013. It has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2007.

Musim Mas is a fully integrated palm oil corporation involved throughout the palm oil supply chain, from cultivation to processing, manufacturing and trading. The company's landbank is among the top fifteen largest landbanks globally for oil palm, with over 130,000 hectares of plantations in Indonesia as of 2016. In 2015, Musim Mas' processing facilities had an annual capacity of 900,000 metric tons for fresh fruit bunches and produced over 300,000 metric tons of palm oil products. Furthermore, it is among the top five importers and exporters of palm oil from Indonesia globally and among the top five producers of biodiesel in Indonesia.
initiatives: Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner, Palm Oil Innovation Group, New York Declaration on Forests

rows.coprofile: PT Rajawali Corp. is an Indonesian investment holding company with diverse business interests including hospitality, media, logistics, mining, and agriculture. It has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. Eagle High Plantations also has an annual processing capacity of 2.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches.  PT Rajawali Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Founded in 1927 in Cologne, Germany, the REWE Group employs over 330,000 individuals in 15,000 stores. Germany is REWE Group's largest market, generating 70% of the Group's revenue in 2014, but the company has operations across 11 other European countries.
REWE Group operates in the food sector through multiple chains and formats including; REWE, REWE Center, REWE City, Penny (a discount store) and TEMMA (an organic supermarket). Supermarkets offer a number of store (own) brands such as Penny, ja!, REWE, Muhlenhof and REWE Bio,  whose offerings include meat products, diary and bakery products. In 2014, REWE Group reported using 10,800 tonnes of palm oil in its own brand products.
REWE Group also operates DIY stores under the Toom Baumarkt and B1 Discount Baumarkt brands. Toom Baumarkt stores provide the Toom quality store branded products, with a broad range of items ranging from garden furniture to plant seeds. REWE Group is also active in the Travel & Tourism and Consumer Electronics retail sectors.

R. R. Donnelley is a commercial printing company founded in 1864. It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. Their customers include some of the world's most well known companies including; Accenture, Barclays, IBM, and Microsoft. Despite offering a number of digital communication strategies, they are primarily known as a supplier of print material and is the leading company of its kind globally.  R. R. Donnelley also prints products for other companies involved in the printing and publishing sector. For example, it supplies print products to Pearson PLC and to HarperCollins, two of the world's largest publishers. In 2013 it employed roughly 57,000 people across four continents, in nearly 40 countries, leading to sales of $10.5 billion. It continues to expand through strategic acquisitions of companies specialising in both digital and commercial print. For example, in 2011, it acquired LibreDigital, a pioneering digital publishing and distribution company, and in 2014 acquired Consolidated Graphics in a deal worth over $600 million.

Citigroup are a global banking group headquartered in the US serving private, corporate, government and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, capital markets, securities, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2017, Citigroup's total assets amount to more than 1.8 trillion USD, with more than 600 billion USD worth of loans. Citigroup are among the top 3 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 120 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Marfrig Global Foods SA (Marfrig GF) is a multinational company with operations in Brazil, where it is headquartered, as well as in 15 other countries around the world. The company's main business activities include the production, processing, preparation, sale and distribution of meat (beef, pork, lamb and poultry), pasta and processed foods (including pizzas, lasagnas, breaded products and desserts), ready meals and frozen vegetables, as well as the distribution of other food products (including frozen foods, sausages and fish) and semi-finished and finished leather.
Marfrig GF began distributing meats and imported vegetables in 1986, over the past two decades it has grown rapidly and diversified through organic growth and acquisitions of Brazilian and overseas companies. Marfrig GF operates through a number of wholly and part owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. The largest shareholders are CEO Marcos Antonio Molina dos Santos, and his wife, via a holding company and the Brazilian development bank. In 2013 Marfrig GF sold Seara Brazil and Zenda (non-beef operations) to fellow Brazilian meat processor JBS and refocused on beef and food service in its home market of Brazil. Internationally, however, it retained a broader food focus through its MoyPark and Keystone operations.
Today Marfrig GF is one of Brazil's three largest beef exporters. It employs 46,000 people across its 78 production units and distribution centres, and it has offices in Europe, South America, North America, Asia and Oceania.
Marfrig is divided into three principle segments: Marfrig Beef produces beef and lamb for the South American and export markets, brand include GJ and Aberdeen Angus; the Moy Park segment's primary focus is on Europe where it provides poultry and prepared meals to retailers and food service chains using both the Moy Park and Jamie Oliver brands; and the Keystone segment supplies restaurant chains with meat products, focussing on the US and Asian markets and with a number of joint ventures in China. 
The company has a daily slaughtering capacity of 20,730 head of cattle (as well as numerous chickens, heads of pork and lambs) and also produces 294,000 leather articles per month. In 2013 Marfrig GF launched the world's first Rainforest Alliance Certified beef. The group's poultry and feed operations also use significant amounts of soya within poultry feed.
Marfrig GF claims to participate in the Grupo de Trabalho da Pecuária Sustentável (GTPS) - Sustainable Beef Working Group - a World Bank initiative implemented by IFC - International Finance Corporation with the purpose of promoting the sustainability of the beef and veal commodity supply chain. It is also a member of the Leather Working Group and a signatory to numerous sustainability initiatives, including: the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; the public commitment Criteria for Industrial-Scale Operations with Livestock and Bovine Products in the Amazon Biome, in partnership with Greenpeace; and the Corporate Pact for Sustainable Connections. In addition Marfrig GF has contributed to some reforestation projects, including giving over 9,776,000 eucalyptus saplings to 780 rural producers in order to foster biosafety and the "green barrier" on poultry and pork farms.

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is an American company involved in the global cultivation, processing, manufacturing and trading of agricultural commodities, ingredients for food and animal feed, as well as biofuels. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soy in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is among the largest processors of soy in Brazil, and is a leading player in Bolivia and Paraguay. Additionally, ADM is one of the world's major biodiesel producers.  Archer Daniels Midland Co. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and paper packaging.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Viterra, headquarted in the Netherlands, is a multi-national company producing and trading in the agriculture sectors operating across 38 countries.  Viterra is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

The earliest foundations of the Oetker-Gruppe lie in 1891, when Dr August Oetker developed the baking powder, Backin, in Germany. The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. The Oetker-Gruppe sells its products to the consumer market under the brand, Dr Oetker. Its consumer products include; frozen pizzas, ready desserts and a number of other chilled and frozen products. Through the Martin Braun group, the Oetker-Gruppe sells a number of baking agents, glazes and decorations to baking and confectionary companies. The manufacturing of these products meant that the Oetker-Gruppe used 4,777 tonnes of palm oil or palm oil derivatives in 2013. Oetker-Gruppe has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011 and in 2012, four of its manufacturing facilities in Germany were certified as RSPO supply chain certified (all palm oil and palm oil derivatives used are RSPO-certified).

Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. Together, these facilities have the capacity to slaughter more than 17,000 heads of cattle a day as of 2016. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.

Metro AG is a German wholesaler with operations across the world. The company’s portfolio caters to professional customers, through sales brands including METRO Cash & Carry and different FSD companies. With a diverse product range, Metro AG is exposed to a number of forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy, pulp and paper. Metro AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. The Oetker-Gruppe sells its products to the consumer market under the brand, Dr Oetker. Its consumer products include; frozen pizzas, ready desserts and a number of other chilled and frozen products. Through the Martin Braun group, the Oetker-Gruppe sells a number of baking agents, glazes and decorations to baking and confectionary companies. The manufacturing of these products meant that the Oetker-Gruppe used 4,777 tonnes of palm oil or palm oil derivatives in 2013. Oetker-Gruppe has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011 and in 2012, four of its manufacturing facilities in Germany were certified as RSPO supply chain certified (all palm oil and palm oil derivatives used are RSPO-certified).

As of 2017, Commerzbank has more than 480 billion EUR in total assets, including over 215 billion EUR in claims on customers. Their services include wealth management, insurance, capital markets, investments, commercial banking and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.2 trillion CAD, with net loans worth nearly 480 billion CAD. The Royal Bank of Canada are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 11 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. Shell, headquartered in the Netherlands, is a group of energy and petrochemical companies operating at a global scale. Segments of the business include the development of biofuels, using palm and soy products as a base.

rows.coprofile: Estee Lauder is an American cosmetics company with products sold in 50 countries around the world. Products include skin care, hair care, makeup, and fragrances with well-known brands including Aveda, Jo Malone, and Estee Lauder itself. It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

Lindt & Sprungli AG (Lindt) is a Swiss chocolatier founded in 1845, which describes itself as the market leader in the premium chocolates industry. The company sells in over 100 countries worldwide, with products under the brand names Ghirardelli, Caffarel, Hofbauer and Kufferle. Lindt employs a total of 8,949 people, has eight production sites (six in Europe and two in the USA) and distributes globally (including in China, Australia, South Africa, North America and Europe), with its largest markets being the European and NAFTA countries. The company distributes its products through a variety of avenues, including duty free retail outlets in airports, department stores, its own stores and Chocolate Cafes.
As a confectionery company, Lindt is ranked 7th in the world and 6th in Western Europe, and is also ranked among the top 50 packaged food companies globally. Further to this, Lindt is placed among the Forbes Global 2000 list. As a manufacturer of sweet snacks, Lindt uses palm oil in a number of its products and also includes soya derivatives, such as soya lecithin, as an ingredient in most of its chocolates.
Lindt has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2008. In 2012 it used 2,565m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products; and it aims to be sourcing 100% RSPO-certified sustainable palm oil by 2015.

It is one of the largest homebuilders in Japan, which is an industry that uses large amounts of timber.  Daiwa House Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Santander are a bank headquartered in Spain serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include asset management, corporate finance, securities, insurance and retail banking services. As of 2017, Santander's total assets amount to more than 1.4 trillion EUR, with more than 860 billion EUR in net customer loans. Santander are among the top 20 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 20 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk commodities.

Arcor is an Argentinian manufacturer of foodstuffs and packaged food operating in five South American countries and selling products in over 120 countries worldwide. Products it produces include confectionary, ice-cream, chocolates, canned food, sugars, and packaging. The company has a worldwide presence, ranking among the ten largest companies for biscuits and snacks by market share, and among the top twenty for packaged food and spreads. It is also an important player in Brazil where it ranks among the top fifteen for packaged foods and among the top ten for biscuits and snacks.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

Bunge is a global agribusiness operating in about 40 countries and involved in the processing, manufacture and trading of agricultural commodities. The company is one of the major players in the South American soy industry and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is one of the largest soy processors in Brazil and one of the market leaders in Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. The company also has facilities in China and India.   Bunge Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

Maxingvest is a holding company of subsidiaries Beiersdorf and Tchibo. Beiersdorf is a global cosmetics and skin care company present in more than 65 countries worldwide. The company is a major global player with brands including Nivea, Eucerin and La Prairie. Palm oil is a significant ingredient in its products. Beiersdorf is one of the top global players for sun care, beauty and personal care and skincare.  Maxingvest AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

rows.coprofile: Olam international is a leading agricultural commodity business operating throughout the supply chain across 70 countries. It is a global market leader in many agricultural commodities such as cocoa and coffee, but also is a major player in African oil palm and forestry. Olam's subsidiary, Congolaise Industrielle de Bois (CIB) operates forestry concessions in the Republic of Congo covering about 2 million hectares in 2016. Olam has a minority stake in the SIFCA group based in Cote d'Ivoire which was managing a total of about 180,000 hectares of oil palm in 2014. Additionally, Olam has a joint venture with the government in Gabon to develop about 50,000 hectares of oil palm plantations with the possibility for further expansion, which began in 2011. The company is also active in soya cultivation and processing in South America and Africa.
initiatives: Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner, Soy Moratorium, Global Agribusiness Alliance, UN Global Compact, Natural Capital Coalition, High Conservation Value Resource Network

Arla Foods is a dairy cooperative with activities around the world. The company's most prominent markets are the United Kingdom, Central Europe and Asia. Its products include milk, cheese, butter and cooking ingredients with brands such as Lurpak, Castello and Apetina. Arla Foods claimed to be among the top ten dairy companies in the world by revenue in 2015 and is one of the world's largest ingredient producers. Soya plays an important role in the cooperative's animal feed and palm oil is also used in its products, with about 25,000 metric tons being used in 2015.

Danzer is a German timber company based in Austria that produces veneer, lumber and other wood products from hardwood. Just under a third of Danzer's raw material comes from Africa where, as of 2016, they own 1.1 million hectares of forestry concessions in the Republic of Congo. Annually, Danzer processes 500,000 cubic metres of wood, with processing facilities in North America and Europe. It claims to be the largest producer of decorative veneer in the world.

Staples Inc is an office supplies retailer that sells a variety of products to businesses and individual consumers. It is the world's largest specialist retailer of office supplies with key products lines in stationery, furniture, and technology products. Staples sells a wide variety of paper products, including copy paper, computer paper and POS rolls, photographic paper and letterheads.
Established in 1985, the company is headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts in the United States. The company's three operational segments are: North American Stores & Online; North American Commercial; and International Operations. The company operates around 2,200 stores globally, and also sells products online and via its catalogue service. It also has around 116 distribution centres throughout the US, Canada, Europe, China, South America, and elsewhere, in all serving customers in 26 countries worldwide.
Staples is the world's largest retailer of a wide range of wood- and paper-based office products, sourcing its products from a range of suppliers in different countries, including Argentina, Brazil, Canada, China and the US. In 2013, paper sales accounted for around 9% of Staples' total revenue; office furniture contributed around 5%; and core office supplies, which include paper and other core office products such as writing products, around 30%. Staples sells its own proprietary branded products under the Staples and Quill trademarks and also offers other manufactured branded items.

The Rougier Group is an international company, based in France and operating in the timber supply chain. It produces primary timber products, such as sawnwood, plywood and logs; and processed products, such as joists and decking, as well as other materials for the construction, packaging and furniture industries. 
Its main operations consist of natural forest harvesting and wood processing in Africa through Rougier Afrique International; imports and distribution of timber products in France through Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux; and management and investment in industrial forest plantations in Africa, through Lignafrica.
Rougier Group's production and processing operations in Africa through Rougier Afrique International are in the Republic of Congo, Cameroon and Gabon, where it is among the largest forestry companies, managing a total area of around 2 million hectares. In Gabon, Rougier Group exploits around 880,000 hectares of forests under four forest concessions, and also operates one plywood factory and three sawmills. In Cameroon, it operates through its subsidiary Societe ForestiÃ¨re et Industrielle de la Doume (SFID; Doume Forestry Company), which exploits 550,000 hectares of forests and operates two sawmills and a secondary timber processing workshop. Rougier Group also operates in the northern Republic of Congo through its subsidiary, Mokabi SA. Mokabi SA manages 586,000 hectares of forests and operates a sawmill.
Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux imports to France over 40,000 cubic metres per year from Africa, America, Europe and Asia. Rougier Sylvaco Panneax is the result of a merger between Rougier Group's two subsidiaries: Rougier Sylvaco and Rougier Panneaux. The merger aims to position Rougier Group better in the French market, which is experiencing increased concentration among its operators.

Felda Global Ventures (FGV) is a Malaysian group of agribusiness companies active in the palm, rubber, sugar, and agri-services industries. The group is involved in both the cultivation and processing of oil palm as well as in the manufacturing of palm oil goods. In 2015, FGV had a total oil palm landbank of over 750,000 hectares across Indonesia and Malaysia which is one of the five largest landbanks for palm oil in the world. It also has major processing operations, processing about 15 million fresh fruit bunches in 2015, and claims to be the largest producer of crude palm oil in the world, producing more than 3 million metric tons in the same year.

Ferrero Group (Ferrero) is a family-owned confectionary business formally established in 1946 out of Pietro Ferrero's thriving factory in Piedmont, Italy. The company was one of the earliest in the Italian confectionery industry to expand overseas, with Michele Ferrero and his wife Maria Franca being the first Italians to open manufacturing operations in the confectionery business abroad after World War II. Until he passed away in February 2015, Michele Ferrero ranked 22nd on the Forbes list of billionaires and was the wealthiest man in Italy, worth $27 billion (though living in Monaco). His son Giovanni now runs the company, which operates in 51 countries worldwide and on every continent. The company has over 22,000 employees at 20 production and 3 research and development sites. In addition, the Ferrero Group has 8 agricultural companies for both direct cultivation and manufacturing purposes.
Ferrero is the fourth largest confectionary company in the world and in the past five years has rapidly expanded its sales in China and Russia. It owns many famous brands, including Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Nutella, which was one of the company's first products in the 1940s. Ferrero uses palm oil in its confectionary to give products the right consistency. The company sources palm oil from Malaysia, Papua New Guinea and Brazil, using 150,000 tonnes annually.

The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. VF Corp is an international apparel, footwear and accessories company with product markets in over 170 countries worldwide. The company owns many well-known brands including The North Face, Vans, Wrangler, Timberland and JanSport. As the manufacturer of these leading products, VF Corp is exposed to the forest risk commodity leather, which is used in items such as luggage, footwear and accessories.   VF Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Group Ligna is the parent company of Klabin S.A., the largest paper manufacturer and exporter in Brazil, headquartered in Sao Paulo. They manufacture packaging paper and board, corrugated boxes, industrial sacks and timber, with 22 industrial plants in Brazil and one in Argentina. Klabin S.A. are also the largest paper recycler in Brazil, holding 11% of the country's recycling market. They have been selected as a powerbroker for timber and pulp and paper.

The Aldi Group is a German discount retailer split into two companies, Aldi Nord and Aldi SÃ¼d, both of which have an international presence. Although both companies are independent of one another, they operate under the same umbrella brand. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. In 2015, Aldi was one of the top five retailers of own-brand edible groceries in the world and in Europe, and among the top ten in the US.

PT Rajawali Corpora is an investment holding company of the Rajawali Group, an Indonesian conglomerate active in a variety of industries, including telecommunications, hotels, consumer goods, retail, transportation, coal, gold and iron mining, and agriculture. The Group's agricultural activities comprise palm, sugar, rubber and corn plantations. Founded in 1984, the company is based in Jakarta and employs some 30,000 people. It was founded and is owned by Peter Sondakh, who is among the richest men in Indonesia and also ranks among the top billionaires globally. 
The company has a growing presence in the agricultural industry. PT Jaya Madiri Sukses (JMS Group) is the plantation arm of the Rajawali Group, and is a holding company comprising of a total of seven plantation companies in South and East Kalimantan. In 2010, Rajawali was reported to begin planting its 200,000 hectare land bank with oil palm. In 2011 Rajawali entered into a joint venture with commodities trader Louis Dreyfus called Green Eagle Plantations Pte Ltd. In 2012, the venture was reported to operate in four regions in Indonesia (South, West and East Kalimantan, and Papua), with concessions of around 50,000 hectares. However, in 2014, Louis Dreyfus Commodities Asia Pte left the joint venture, selling its 50% share of Green Eagle to the Rajawali Group. More recently, in September 2014, through a purchase of two investment firms, Matacuna Group and Pegasus CP One, Rajawali reportedly has acquired a 21% stake in crude palm oil producer, BW Plantation.

rows.coprofile: Minerva is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.  MINERVA is selected as a powerbroker for beef and leather and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Marfrig Global Foods SA (Marfrig GF) is a multinational company with operations in Brazil, where it is headquartered, as well as in 15 other countries around the world. The company's main business activities include the production, processing, preparation, sale and distribution of meat (beef, pork, lamb and poultry), pasta and processed foods (including pizzas, lasagnas, breaded products and desserts), ready meals and frozen vegetables, as well as the distribution of other food products (including frozen foods, sausages and fish) and semi-finished and finished leather.
Marfrig GF began distributing meats and imported vegetables in 1986, over the past two decades it has grown rapidly and diversified through organic growth and acquisitions of Brazilian and overseas companies. Marfrig GF operates through a number of wholly and part owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. The largest shareholders are CEO Marcos Antonio Molina dos Santos, and his wife, via a holding company and the Brazilian development bank. In 2013 Marfrig GF sold Seara Brazil and Zenda (non-beef operations) to fellow Brazilian meat processor JBS and refocused on beef and food service in its home market of Brazil. Internationally, however, it retained a broader food focus through its MoyPark and Keystone operations.
Today Marfrig GF is one of Brazil's three largest beef exporters. It employs 46,000 people across its 78 production units and distribution centres, and it has offices in Europe, South America, North America, Asia and Oceania.
Marfrig is divided into three principle segments: Marfrig Beef produces beef and lamb for the South American and export markets, brand include GJ and Aberdeen Angus; the Moy Park segment's primary focus is on Europe where it provides poultry and prepared meals to retailers and food service chains using both the Moy Park and Jamie Oliver brands; and the Keystone segment supplies restaurant chains with meat products, focussing on the US and Asian markets and with a number of joint ventures in China. 
The company has a daily slaughtering capacity of 20,730 head of cattle (as well as numerous chickens, heads of pork and lambs) and also produces 294,000 leather articles per month. In 2013 Marfrig GF launched the world's first Rainforest Alliance Certified beef. The group's poultry and feed operations also use significant amounts of soya within poultry feed.
Marfrig GF claims to participate in the Grupo de Trabalho da Pecuária Sustentável (GTPS) - Sustainable Beef Working Group - a World Bank initiative implemented by IFC - International Finance Corporation with the purpose of promoting the sustainability of the beef and veal commodity supply chain. It is also a member of the Leather Working Group and a signatory to numerous sustainability initiatives, including: the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; the public commitment Criteria for Industrial-Scale Operations with Livestock and Bovine Products in the Amazon Biome, in partnership with Greenpeace; and the Corporate Pact for Sustainable Connections. In addition Marfrig GF has contributed to some reforestation projects, including giving over 9,776,000 eucalyptus saplings to 780 rural producers in order to foster biosafety and the "green barrier" on poultry and pork farms.

Tesco is a leading British retailer with around 4,800 stores aross the UK and Europe. The company specialises in groceries but also sells personal care items, apparel and furniture, as well as offering financial services through its subsidiary Tesco Bank. Amongst its product lines, Tesco sells a range of own brand products including packaged meats, dairy products and confectionary items. The company’s operations leave it exposed to several forest risk commodities. Tesco plc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: Commerzbank are a German retail, commercial and investment banking group, offering services to private and corporate customers. Their services include wealth management, investment banking, insurance, pensions, corporate finance and retail banking services. As of 2017, Commerzbank has more than 480 billion EUR in total assets, including over 215 billion EUR in claims on customers. Commerzbank are among the top 35 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 8 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

DLG Denmark, established in 1964, is one of Europe's biggest agricultural companies. It is owned by 30,000 Danish farmers and employs 7,500 people, 3,000 of whom are in Denmark. Through over 40 subsidiaries and associated companies, DLG Denmark is involved in a broad range of business and consumer sectors, with localised operations in in more than 20 countries. 
DLG Denmark is organised into four business areas: Premix and Nutrition, accounting for 4% of turnover, provides specialist animal feeds and minerals; Service and Energy, contributing 28% of turnover, provides a broad range of products and services including fuels, telecommunications and IT, and also operates DIY stores and petrol stations; Machinery, Flowers and Food, which accounts for 6% of turnover, provides industrial and agricultural machinery as well as a broad range of plants and food products, including oils and vegetables; and Farm Supply, the largest division, providing 62% turnover, encompasses animal feed production, poultry hatcheries, provision of fertiliser and pesticides, and crop production.
DLG Denmark produces compound feeds for farm animals at its mills in Europe and is one of Europe's top five largest producers of compound feeds. Soya is a significant feed production ingredient, accounting for around 15 to 20% composition. Consequently, DLG Denmark buys around half of Denmark's soymeal. DLG Denmark uses a similar amount of palm oil in its animal feed.
