They invest in international equity, fixed-income markets and real estate to provide security for Norway's economy against fluctuating oil prices. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 8 trillion NOK, with more than 4.8 trillion NOK in equities. The Norwegian Government Pension Fund are among the top 10 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with approximately 40 billion USD worth of shares across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Henkel is a manufacturing company based in Germany. Henkel operates worldwide with products within beauty care, laundry and home care, and adhesive technologies. These products expose the company to palm oil as a common ingredient. The company have a big portfolio of brands, including Loctite, Pritt, Dylan, and Schwarzkopf. According to Henkel, the company holds globally leading market positions both in consumer and industrial businesses.   Henkel AG & Co. KGaA is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.
RELX Group, headquartered in the UK, provides information in the form of electronic and printed publications for a range of industries worldwide.

Tetra Laval consists of three industry groups, Tetra Pak, Sidel and DeLaval.  The companies' activities focus on systems for the processing, packaging and distribution of food and accessories for dairy production and animal husbandry and are assessed due to their use of pulp and paper.

Grupo SLC was established in in 1945 and is the majority shareholder (with a 51.3% majority ownership) of SLC Agricola SA, a Brazilian agricultural company involved in the production of soya beans, as well as cotton, corn and coffee, among other commodities. SLC Grupo also owns: SLC Alimentos SA, a producer of rice, beans and lentils; Ferramentas Gerais, which provides maintenance and repair services and machinery and equipment for the industrial sector; and SLC Commercial, which sells farm machinery under the John Deere brand in the state of Rio Grande do Sul.
SLC Agricola was started in 1977 with the acquisition of Paineira Farm in the Coronel Bicaco municipality, under the name of Agropecuaria Schneider Logemann Ltda. The company now has its headquarters in Porto Alegre, Brazil and operates 16 farms in six states. In 2012/2013, these farms comprised a total planted area of over 340,000 hectares; including over 185,000 hectares of soya beans. SLC Agricola claims to be one of the largest producers of soya beans in Brazil, and sells soya beans in domestic and overseas markets. The company has multiple subsidiaries, which further to agricultural production, are also involved in: leasing agricultural land; offering services such as storage to other cereal producers; trading, importing and exporting agricultural products; and real estate.

LVMH’s primary revenue stream comes from its manufacture and sale of apparel and luggage, a trade which leaves it exposed to the forest risk commodity leather. Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd is a holding company for the Nippon Paper Group, which is comprised of around 180 affiliates and subsidiaries. The Group ranks among the top forest, paper and packaging companies globally, occupying sixth place in a worldwide ranking of the top 100 and the second position of such companies in Japan. The Group produces a variety of paper products, including newsprint, printing paper, copy paper, wrapping paper, linerboard, paperboard, tissue products, and healthcare products. For example, through its subsidiary Nippon Paper Crecia Co Ltd, the Group manufactures family care, personal care and professional products under a license agreement with leading hygiene products company, Kimberly-Clark.
The Group has diverse business interests on top of its activities in the paper sector, and several of Nippon Paper Groups's other operations also make use of wood products. For example, it has several subsidiaries active in the wood products and construction industry; in the procurement of lumber and the manufacture of construction materials. These subsidiaries include Nippon Paper Lumber Co., Ltd., PAL Co., Ltd., and Daishowa Uniboard Co., Ltd. Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd has a global network supplying logs and lumber from a variety of sources, including domestically and from the United States, Canada, Europe, New Zealand and some tropical regions. As well as supplying raw and sawn timber, Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd also manufactures plywood and laminated lumber products. Pal Co Ltd and Daishowa Uniboard Co Ltd manufacture products for use in the construction industry, such as doors, staircases, flooring and decorative laminates.

Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

The Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) offers financial services to Brazilian companies and financial institutions with the aim of stimulating industry and infrastructure growth in Brazil. Their services include corporate financing, non-reimbursable investments, and securities. As of 2017, the bank's total assets amount to more than 870 billion BRL, with loans of more than 590 billion BRL. BNDES are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

Mondelez International (Mondleez) was formed in 2012 as a spinoff of Kraft International. Mondelez is one of the world's largest snack companies with global net revenues of approximately $35 billion in 2013. 60% of the 2013 net revenue originated from biscuit and chocolate sales, with 40% of these sales in Europe and 20% in North Americai. It has over 100,000 employees and manufactures products for consumption in around 165 countries around the worldi.  In total, it has nine billion dollar brands, including Tang, Cadbury, Nabisco and Oreo biscuits. Further to that, the company also owns another 53 brands with annual revenues greater than $100 millioni. Through these brands, the company produces beverages, biscuits, cheese, chocolate and chewing gum. It also invests strongly in research and development, with numerous facilities across Europe, such as the chocolate centre for excellence in Bournville, UK, and its biscuits research and development centre in Saclay, France. The company is now focusing its attention on emerging markets through the expansion of existing manufacturing plants and the building of new ones. For example, Mondelez has expanded its chocolate factory in Curitiba, Brazil and spent $350 million on the construction of a new biscuit factory in Monteray, Mexicoi.
Mondelez International (formerly known as Kraft International) has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011. In 2012, the company used 285732 m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products. Of this 200,653 m3 was RSPO certified (crude palm oil plus palm kernel oil).
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum, Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner, Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, New York Declaration on Forests

rows.coprofile: Deckers Outdoor Corp is a footwear distributor based in the US made up of several well-known brands such as UGG.  Deckers Outdoor Corp is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Sumitomo Forestry Co. Ltd, is a timber company with operations in forestry, processing, materials provision and construction. The company is one of the world’s largest forestry companies and has subsidiaries operating across East and Southeast Asia, Oceania and North America.  Sumitomo Forestry is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest

rows.coprofile: ConAgra Foods is an American manufacturer of packaged food products as well as a provider of commercial products and foodservice. Its products are mostly frozen and refrigerated foods with well-known brands including Banquet, Blue Bonnet and Slim Jim, but it also produces cereals and snacks. ConAgra Foods is a major global player for oils and fats, sweet and savoury snacks, and ready meals.  ConAgra Brands Inc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Perkebunan Nusantara is an Indonesian state-owned plantation company comprised of fourteen individual but interrelated business enterprises. The group cultivates and processes several agricultural commodities, including rubber, tobacco, sugar cane, tea, and palm oil. It is a major producer and processor of palm oil, estimated to have more than 500,000 hectares for palm plantations and a processing capacity of more than 3,000 fresh fruit bunches per hour from more than 65 facilities.  Perkebunan Nusantara is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.
WestRock manufactures and sells paper and packaging solutions on a global scale, and ranked 194th on the 2018 Fortune 500 list by revenue in the United States.

JBS is a global company involved in the beef, lamb and poultry processing, and in pork production.  It is among the largest producer of protein products worldwide, and is also involved in the production of leather, hygiene and cleaning products, collagen, metal packaging, biodiesel and other goods. JBS has operations spanning 24 countries and serves around 300,000 customers in 150 countries. 
Initially, the company was a small operation, with the capacity of processing five head of cattle per day. However, since 1953, JBS has expanded hugely, with major acquisitions in South America, the US, Australia and Europe. In 2007 JBS was floated on the Brazilian stock exchange, making it the first meat processing company in Brazil to do so. Today it is headquartered in Sao Paulo and employs around 185,000 people in total. Its operations are split between the following business divisions: JBS Mercosul, which comprises the company's beef and leather and related industries in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay; JBS USA, which is responsible for overseeing JBS' activities in Australia, Canada, the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico; and finally, JBS Foods, which was established in 2013 and covers the company's poultry, pork and value-added products in Brazil. 
The variety of products, which include fresh and frozen cuts to ready meals and processed foods service a variety of markets, including the catering, supermarket and export markets. These are marketed under several brands, including Bertin, Swift, and Friboi, and packaged foods, including ready meals under the Seara brand.
As well as its extensive operations in the global meat production and processing industries, which make beef of obvious significance, soya is also important, given its use in animal feed. For example, JBS operates 13 poultry farms, two pig farms and over 40 hatcheries, which use large amounts of animal feed. On top of its own operations, JBS also has around 5000 pig and poultry partner producers, which it provides with technical support and materials including all feed. Similarly within its beef operations, JBS operates cattle feedlots in Brazil the US and Australia where it provides all feed. Further to this, JBS is a significant player in the global leather industry, and with a daily processing capacity of one hundred thousand hides, leather processing is one of JBS' primary activities.

Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV (Grupo Bimbo) was founded by Lorenzo Servitje in Mexico in 1945. International expansion began in 1989, resulting in Grupo Bimbo becoming the largest bakery company in the world in terms of sales and production volume. The company's main markets are the US and Mexico but it also operates in Central and Latin America, Canada, Asia and Europe. In 2014, net sales were $14.1 billion. The company has 167 manufacturing plants located largely in its key markets, with 85 plants in the US and 39 in Mexico. In addition to its global manufacturing facilities, the company operates a distribution network with over 52,000 routes, feeding into 2.2 million points of sale in 19 countries. Today, Grupo Bimbo employs over 21,000 individuals.
Grupo Bimbo produces more than 10,000 different products under 100 umbrella brands including Bimbo, New York Bakery Co., Marisela and Ricolino. It manufactures bread, potato crisps, pastries and a variety of other snacks, many of which contain palm oil. The company continues to expand its business in international markets; it recently completed the acquisition of the previously public-listed company, Canada Bread, for $1.83 billion.
initiatives: Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, New York Declaration on Forests, Consumer Goods Forum, UN Global Compact

Nine Dragons Paper Holdings Ltd (ND Paper) is a paper and paper packaging manufacturer that produces a variety of containerboard and paper products, including: linerboard; corrugating medium and coated duplex board; recycled printing and writing paper; and tissue paper. As well as paper products, ND Paper manufactures wood-, bamboo-, and unbleached kraft pulp. The company's products are manufactured under three brands: Nine Dragons, Land Dragon and Sea Dragon, each focusing on a different customer segment.  ND Paper is well known for its use of recovered paper; the company's main source of raw material. This is used in the manufacturing of some of its products, such as its testlinerboard, made from 100% recovered paper, and its Sea Dragon office paper. The company imports significant amounts of recovered paper from the US; however, this is not used exclusively in all products.
The company was established in 1995 and is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies, ranking among the top 30 globally and holding the leading position in China. ND Paper has six manufacturing bases across China, as well as in Vietnam and Mongolia, through joint ventures: Cheng Yang Paper and Nine Dragons Xing An Pulp & Paper (Inner Mongolia) Co Ltd. Originally, the company predominantly supplied packaging for manufacturers in southern China's export oriented industry; however, the business has increasingly tapped into the demand for packaging products from the domestic market as China's own consumer-demand has grown.

Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio with the RTL group, publishing with Penguin Random House, and magazines with Gruner + Jahr. The most important markets are the US and Western Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.

Mewah International Inc. (Mewah) is one of the dominant palm oil traders globally. It started operating in the 1950s with imports of palm oil from Malaysia to Singapore and is now involved in the production and distribution of a range of edible oils and fats. In 1987, Mewah opened its first refinery in Malaysia, producing 400 million tonnes per day, and has now opened a further two refineries, increasing its yearly capacity to 2.8 million tonnes. Mewah sources its raw materials from Malaysia and Indonesia before selling to the consumer and commercial markets in over 100 countries. It sells palm, soya bean, lauric, coconut, canola corn and sunflower oils commercially, and edible oils and fats on the consumer market. Mewah's consumer products are distributed via a range of different regional brands, such as Oki, Mona and Fry-ola, making it the world's leading edible oil company.
Mewah is also a key producer of food grade packaging for commercial and consumer markets. To continue to expand its business, Mewah is aiming to consolidate its position within the palm-based oil and fats business, expand its consumer product range, invest in efficient production facilities and expand its distribution network,. This has involved the construction of a new refinery in Sabah, Malaysia, which will increase Mewah's productivity to 3.5 million tonnes per year, along with the purchase of a new biodiesel facility in Westport, Malaysiaiv. Mewah has complemented these acquisitions with the installation of a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia, costing around $50 million, to produce a range of dairy products.
Mewah has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2006 and it expects to achieve 100% RSPO certification of all supply chains by 2015.

BASF is one of the world's leading chemical companies, operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF's home and personal care offerings. It is one of the top ten users of palm oil worldwide, using over 380,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products in 2015.

Beiersdorf is a global cosmetics and skin care company present in more than 65 countries worldwide. The company is a major global player with brands including Nivea, Eucerin and La Prairie. Palm oil is a significant ingredient in its products. Beiersdorf is one of the top global players for sun care and is especially important in Indonesia and Brazil. Furthermore, it is among the top ten in the world for beauty and personal care and among the top five in the world for skincare, being especially important in major importing markets such as Western Europe and China.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, Other intiative (add in further details)

rows.coprofile: Societe Generale are a banking group headquartered in France that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services span corporate finance, capital markets, insurance, wealth management, investments, securities and retail banking services. As of 2021, Societe Generale's total assets amount to more than 1.59 trillion EUR. Societe Generale are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Societe Generale was providing 115.4 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Tesco is a leading British retailer with around 4,800 stores aross the UK and Europe. The company specialises in groceries but also sells personal care items, apparel and furniture, as well as offering financial services through its subsidiary Tesco Bank. Amongst its product lines, Tesco sells a range of own brand products including packaged meats, dairy products and confectionary items. The company’s operations leave it exposed to several forest risk commodities. Tesco plc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: HSBC are an international banking group headquartered in London serving private and commercial clients. Their services include corporate finance, insurance, and investments, securities, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2021, HSBC's total assets amount to more than 2.9 trillion USD. HSBC are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2022 selection, HSBC was providing 115 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
Signatory to UN-convened Net-Zero Asset Owners Alliance, Commitment letter signatories. Church Commissioners for England not present in financing data

Viterra is a Swiss-based multi-national company producing and trading in the agriculture sectors, previously as part of Glencore.  Viterra is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile:
The Rougier Group is an international company, based in France and operating in the timber supply chain. It produces primary timber products, such as sawnwood, plywood and logs; and processed products, such as joists and decking, as well as other materials for the construction, packaging and furniture industries. 
Its main operations consist of natural forest harvesting and wood processing in Africa through Rougier Afrique International; imports and distribution of timber products in France through Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux; and management and investment in industrial forest plantations in Africa, through Lignafrica.
Rougier Group's production and processing operations in Africa through Rougier Afrique International are in the Republic of Congo, Cameroon and Gabon, where it is among the largest forestry companies, managing a total area of around 2 million hectares. In Gabon, Rougier Group exploits around 880,000 hectares of forests under four forest concessions, and also operates one plywood factory and three sawmills. In Cameroon, it operates through its subsidiary Societe ForestiÃ¨re et Industrielle de la Doume (SFID; Doume Forestry Company), which exploits 550,000 hectares of forests and operates two sawmills and a secondary timber processing workshop. Rougier Group also operates in the northern Republic of Congo through its subsidiary, Mokabi SA. Mokabi SA manages 586,000 hectares of forests and operates a sawmill.
Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux imports to France over 40,000 cubic metres per year from Africa, America, Europe and Asia. Rougier Sylvaco Panneax is the result of a merger between Rougier Group's two subsidiaries: Rougier Sylvaco and Rougier Panneaux. The merger aims to position Rougier Group better in the French market, which is experiencing increased concentration among its operators.

SHV Holdings is a Dutch trading company. The company owns Nutreco, which is one of the global leaders in animal nutrition and aquafeed. The company sells its products in more than 90 countries. According to Nutreco, its brand Skretting is the leading manufacturer of aquaculture feed in the world. Soy and palm oil are often used in animal feed products.   SHV holdings is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Empresas CMPC S.A. is a Chilean-based producer of forest products. The company operates in the businesses of forestry, pulp and paper, tissue and other products, including the production of paper-manufacture products.  Empresas CMPC S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group
The Forests Dialogue, New Generation Plantations and Forests Solution Group

rows.coprofile: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Holding are a financial services company headquartered in Japan serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include asset management, inheritance and succession, property administration, loans, investment support, and insurance. As of 2017, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Holding's total assets amount to over 63 trillion YEN with over 28 trillion YEN worth of loans. They are an important shareholder and lender in Forest 500 companies.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong (KLK) is a Malaysian agribusiness company active in the cultivation, processing and manufacturing of palm oil and rubber, as well as being involved in property development. The company has one of the largest landbanks among palm oil producers across Malaysia, Indonesia and Liberia. It also owns several mills and two refineries and is among the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to timber and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: The Yokohama Rubber Co Ltd was selected as a powerbroker for Rubber (Manufacturer, Trader)

Avon Products (Avon) is a global manufacturer and marketer of beauty and cosmetic products. Through its representatives system, it sells skincare products, fragrances, hair products, and fashion items. In 2015, the company had sales operations in 57 countries, excluding the US where it owns a minority stake in New Avon, with top markets including Brazil, Mexico, Russia and the United Kingdom. It was among the top ten beauty and personal care companies in the world by market share. In 2015, Avon used 20,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

Banco do Brasil are a state-controlled bank headquartered in Brazil serving private, corporate and government clients. Their services include investments, insurance, pensions, retail banking services, capital markets and corporate finance. As of 2017, Banco do Brasil's total assets amount to more than 1.4 trillion BRL, with more than 630 billion BRL in credit operations and leasing. Banco do Brasil are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

Bank of America are a US-based bank serving private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, wealth management, investments and retail banking services. As of 2017, the bank's total assets amount to more than 2 trillion USD, with more than 900 billion USD worth of loans and leases. Bank of America is among the top 5 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 75 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 15 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 28 billion USD worth of shares.

Nippon Paper Industries is a Japanese paper manufacturing company. The company produces newsprint, printing paper, paperboard, wrapping paper, and building materials among other products.   Nippon Paper Industries Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Rewe Group is a German retail company that operates within food retail, home improvement, pharmacies, discount stores, apparel shops, and travel. Rewe Group has over 15,000 stores in 20 European countries, and every week the company has 70 million customers visiting its shops. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities.   Rewe Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Yum! Brands Inc. develops franchises, operates and licenses restaurants. It is one of the world's largest restaurant companies, with over 42,500 companies in more than 130 countries and territories. The three globally recognised chains under the Yum! umbrella are KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell; which are the global leaders in their respective food categories of chicken, pizza and Mexican-style food .
Since its spinoff from PepsiCo. in 1997, Yum! Brands has expanded significantly internationally, with 65% of its profits now coming from non-US markets in 2015 compared to just 20% in 1997. In 2016, Yum! Brands opens on average over six new restaurants a day worldwide.
Yum! Brands' chicken restaurant chain, KFC, has 18,000 outlets in 115 countries and territories, serving over 12 million customers each day. Taco Bell serves Mexican style food through around 6,100 outlets in the US, serving more than 40 million customers each week. However, Yum! Brands is looking to expand the chain globally and currently has around 300 stores in 20 countries outside the US. By the end of 2014, there were over 15,600 Pizza Hut restaurants around the world.
Yum! Brands franchisees and company operated restaurants are significant purchasers of chicken, cheese, beef and pork products as well as paper and packaging materials. All three restaurant brands use palm oil, soy and beef in a variety of different products.

Oji Holdings is a corporation involved in the pulp and paper industry at a producing, processing and manufacturing level. Its products include packaging materials, household products, print materials and more. In 2014, it was among the top five largest companies for forest, paper and packaging products by annual sales value globally, with a supply capacity of 2.4 million metric tons of pulp to market. Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A, which was one of the largest timber, paper and packaging companies in Brazil in 2014. There were also plans announced in 2015 to establish operations in Myanmar.

Sumitomo Forestry Co. Ltd, is a timber company with operations in forestry, processing, materials provision and construction. The company has subsidiaries operating across East and Southeast Asia, Oceania and North America. In 2016 it had almost 250,000 hectares of planation forest under its management, of which over half was in Indonesia. Sumitomo is one of the world’s largest forestry companies, and in 2015 it ranked ninth on PwC’s top 100 Global Forest, Paper and Packaging Industry Companies.
Signatory to Net-Zero Asset Managers Initiative. Columbia Threadneedle Investments finances the Forest 500 with a total of 29319 USDM

Campbell Soup Co was founded in New Jersey, US, in 1869, when it began producing canned vegetables, soups, condiments and minced meats. The company now has annual sales of $8 billion and employs over 20,000 people. Its main business operations are divided into three divisions: simple meals (ready-made foods and soups); baked snacks; and health beverages and it has manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
The company's products are marketed under various brands, including Pepperidge Farms, which is the US division for cookies, crackers, bakery and frozen products and is led by 'Goldfish' crackers. However, the flagship Campbell's brand is the company's main source of revenue and is worth around US$2 billion. Through this brand, the company sells almost 2 billion cans of soup each year, accounting for 60% of the United States' market for canned soup. Campbell Soup Co continues to expand its range of products through investments into, and acquisitions of, other companies. For example, in 2013, the company acquired Bolthouse Farms, Plum Organics and Kelsen Group. During 2015, Campbell Soup Co. also plans to launch 200 new products, including protein drinks and bars.

Metro AG is a German wholesaler with operations across the world. The company’s portfolio caters to professional customers, through sales brands including METRO Cash & Carry and different FSD companies. With a diverse product range, Metro AG is exposed to a number of forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy, pulp and paper. Metro AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

IOI Corporation is a global, vertically integrated palm oil company active throughout the supply chain from cultivation to manufacturing. The company has one of the top ten largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with more than 225,000 hectares of plantation land in Indonesia and Malaysia. Its 15 mills have an annual capacity for more than 4.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches. IOI also owns four refineries in Malaysia and the Netherlands with an annual capacity of more than 3 million metric tons. Its products include oleochemicals and specialty oils and fats for the food industry.

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is an American company involved in the global cultivation, processing, manufacturing and trading of agricultural commodities, ingredients for food and animal feed, as well as biofuels. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soy in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. It is among the largest processors of soy in Brazil, and is a leading player in Bolivia and Paraguay. Additionally, ADM is one of the world's major biodiesel producers.  Archer Daniels Midland Co. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and paper packaging.

Standard Chartered are an international banking group headquartered in London, providing banking products and services for both personal and business customers. Their services include commercial banking and corporate finance, as well as retail banking, insurance, investment and wealth management. As of 2024, Standard Chartered's total assets stand at over 849 billion USD in 2024. Standard Chartered are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, predominantly in the food products and agriculture sectors. In the 2024 selection, Standard Chartered was providing 39.9 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Ahold Delhaize is a food retail group, formed from the merger of Ahold and the Delhaize Group in 2016. It has twenty-two store brands, including groceries, supermarkets, specialty stores and online stores across the US, the Netherlands, Belgium, and other European countries. It is one of the world's largest retailers and claims its subsidiaries include the top online retailer in the Benelux and leading online grocers in the Benelux and the US. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. In 2015, Ahold Delhaize used more than 10,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its own brand products.

Marfrig Global Foods is a multinational food company based in Brazil. Its primary business is in meat packing, but it also produces processed food and leather products. The company’s subsidiary Marfrig Beef has over 20 operational facilities spread across South America, with the capacity to slaughter over 3 million cattle per year.  Marfrig Global Foods is selected as a powerbroker for beef and is also assessed for its exposure to soy, leather and paper packaging.

The company is one of the world’s largest oil palm plantation owners and processors, and is also a major player in the soybean crushing industry with a global crushing capacity of 36 million metric tons per annum, the majority of which is in China. Wilmar International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including agribusiness, manufacturing, mining, and trading. The group’s palm oil subsidiary has one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers, it also has 5 palm oil mills and produces crude palm oil and palm kernel oil.  Triputra Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.
Kencana Agri is a palm oil plantation company based in Indonesia with a planted area of over 65,000 ha.

Toronto-Dominion Bank are a financial services company, headquartered in Canada serving private and corporate clients. Their services cover: personal and small business banking, insurance, asset management, auto financing, investing, commercial and wholesale banking. As of 2017, they have over 1.2 billion CAD in total assets with 270 billion CAD in assets under management.  Toronto-Dominion Bank are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 9 billion USD. They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 50, with shares worth more than 7.5 billion USD.

The Royal Bank of Canada are a banking and financial services group headquartered in Canada serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include wealth management, insurance, capital markets, investments, commercial banking and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.2 trillion CAD, with net loans worth nearly 480 billion CAD. The Royal Bank of Canada are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 11 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 50 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 7 billion USD worth of shares.

Prada SpA is the holding company of the Prada Group, which with its subsidiary companies, is involved in the design, manufacture and retail of leather goods, clothing, shoes, and accessories. Prada was founded in Italy in 1913 as a specialist retailer selling accessories, luggage and other luxury items. Today, the Prada brand forms a component of the Prada Group, which has become an international leader in the luxury goods industry. On top of the flagship Prada brand, the Group sells products under the Miu Miu, Car Shoe and Church's brands.  Prada and Miu Miu provide customers with a variety of high-end luxury items, including leatherwear, handbags, apparel, footwear and fragrances. The Car Shoe and Church's brands are more specialist and each offer high-end luxury footwear. Church's is a leading English leather footwear brand that dates back to 1873, while Car Shoe specialises in leather moccasins specifically designed for driving. The Prada Group's brands are sold through its own outlets in stores and online, and through wholesale distribution channels. The Group has a worldwide presence, including in the top fashion markets of London, Milan, Tokyo, Beijing, Hong Kong and New York.
Prada SpA is a significant player in the bags and luggage industry. It ranks among the top five bags and luggage companies globally, and in the top five in China and top three in the Western European market. It also plays an important role in the international footwear industry, particularly in the markets of China, the US and Europe.  Leather goods therefore form an important component of the Prada Group's business; accounting for over 65% of consolidated net sales in the year up to January 2014, totalling over 2 billion Euros.

Felda Global Ventures (FGV) is a Malaysian group of agribusiness companies active in the palm, rubber, sugar, and agri-services industries. The group is involved in both the cultivation and processing of oil palm as well as in the manufacturing of palm oil goods. In 2015, FGV had a total oil palm landbank of over 750,000 hectares across Indonesia and Malaysia which is one of the five largest landbanks for palm oil in the world. It also has major processing operations, processing about 15 million fresh fruit bunches in 2015, and claims to be the largest producer of crude palm oil in the world, producing more than 3 million metric tons in the same year.

MRV Engenharia e Participaces (MRV) is a construction company in Brazil focussed on the residential real estate market, building houses, apartment buildings and other properties. It is one of the largest Brazilian construction companies by units sold, revenue and sales value, and it operates in 134 cities and 19 states in Brazil. Timber is a major raw material for construction, and Brazil in general uses four times more tropical timber than China. In 2013, MRV used more than 1.4 million cubic metres of timber.

These products expose the company to palm oil as a common ingredient. The company have a big portfolio of brands, including Loctite, Pritt, Dylan, and Schwarzkopf. According to Henkel, the company holds globally leading market positions both in consumer and industrial businesses.   Henkel AG & Co. Mitsubishi Corp is a core company of the Mitsubishi Group; a group of autonomous companies made up of about 28 core enterprises and up to 600 member companies in all. The companies within the Mitsubishi Group conduct their operations independently of one another, but each honour the Group's three principles (of corporate social responsibility; integrity and fairness; and global understanding through business) and have their roots in the original shipping company, founded in 1870.
Mitsubishi Corp is a general trading company; the largest in Japan and the largest publicly-listed company of its kind in the world. The company's history extends back to 1954, when the Mitsubishi Shoji was established; however, Mitsubishi Corporation became the company's official English name in 1971. Mitsubishi Corp's activities now expand well beyond its original trading operations and it is involved in a wide variety of businesses, including energy, metals, food and environmental business.  Of particular relevance are Mitsubishi's operations in the production of food products that include soya and palm-based ingredients. Significantly, the Living Essentials department of Mitsubishi Corp also operates as a trading company in the palm oil industry, where it purchases predominantly Malaysian palm oil for export to Japan, the US and Taiwan, among others. The Living Essentials Group's activities in the production of consumer goods also include the procurement of raw materials and the manufacturing and distribution of a wide variety of products, including furniture, lumber, housing and construction materials, as well as many processed and frozen foods.
Mitsubishi Corp acquired UK-based food and drink manufacturer, Princes Ltd., in 1989. This is another particularly relevant component of Mitsubishi's operations. Founded in Liverpool, UK in 1880, Princes has since greatly increased its business portfolio diversifying from its original focus on the sale of canned goods. With a total of 19 mergers and acquisitions, it is now among the top food and drinks manufacturers in the UK.  Its tinned and canned products include meat pies, corned beef and stewed steak and the company is among the top five European beef importers from Brazil.

IOI also owns four refineries in Malaysia and the Netherlands with an annual capacity of more than 3 million metric tons. Its products include oleochemicals and specialty oils and fats for the food industry.

First Resources is a cultivator and processor of palm oil, active across Indonesia. The company's landbank for palm oil is one of the fifteen largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers, with more than 200,000 hectares in Indonesia. It also owns several mills and refineries with an annual processing capacity of 850,000 metric tons. First Resources sells a range of products including oleochemicals, biodiesel and palm kernel expeller which is used as animal feed.

Sinar Mas is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including pulp and paper, agriculture and food, energy, financial services, and real estate. The group’s agricultural business has one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It is also one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Its products include cooking oil and margarine. Additionally, the group crushes soy, with an annual capacity of 2.3 million metric tons. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.  Sinar Mas is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to pulp & paper.

Its products include milk, cheese, butter and cooking ingredients with brands such as Lurpak, Castello and Apetina. Arla Foods is one of the world’s largest ingredient producers. Soy plays an important role in the cooperative’s animal feed and palm oil is also used in its products.  Arla Foods is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

The Sime Darby Group is a Malaysian conglomerate involved in diverse industries, including logistics, industrial equipment, property and plantations. Sime Darby Plantation is the agribusiness arm of the group which has a landbank of approximately 1 million hectares with 600,000 hectares of planted oil palm. This is one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. In 2015, the group processed more than 10 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches and produced more than 2 million metric tons of crude palm oil. It also produces products such as oleochemicals, fats, biodiesel and other derivatives.

Kimberly-Clark is a leading personal care, health and hygiene company. The company manufactures a wide range of paper and pulp based products under well-known brand names such as Huggies, Kleenex, Scott and Pull-ups. Operating across the globe, Kimberly-Clark supplies over 175 country markets and has a large market share in its field.  Kimberly-Clark Group is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile:
LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA (LVMH) is a French company, with its headquarters in Paris, engaged in the luxury goods industry. The group was formed following the merger of the MoÃ«t Hennessy and Louis Vuitton companies in 1987; however its origins extend back much further in the history of the development of the French luxury goods industry. Louis Vuitton's flagship brand was launched in 1854, after which it continued to specialise solely in handmade leather bags for over 70 years, while, Moet Hennessy's origins are even earlier, as the company was involved in the wine industry for 100 years prior.
LVMH currently operates in five main segments: wines and spirits; fashion and leather goods; perfumes and cosmetics; watches and jewellery; and selective retailing. Within these five sectors, LVMH has a portfolio of more than 60 brands and an international network of more than 3,000 stores. Of particular importance is the company's fashion and leather goods division, which comprises well-known luggage, leather goods and apparel and accessories brands, such as Louis Vuitton, Givenchy and Marc Jacobs.
In 2013, the fashion and leather goods business accounted for the majority of the group's total revenue. The group is an industry leader in the bags and luggage market worldwide, occupying the top position globally in terms of market share and leading positions in the individual markets of China, Western Europe and the USA.

Inditex is a Spanish fashion retailer. It has eight brands, including Zara, Pull&Bear, Bershka, Massimo Dutti, and Stradivarius. Inditex has over 7000 stores in more than 90 countries, and employs over 160,000 people. The company claims to be one of the largest fashion retailers in the world. Inditex use cellulose and leather in its products.  Inditex S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Natuzzi S.p.A. (Natuzzi) is the parent company of the Natuzzi Group, an Italian furniture company, established in 1959. It is involved in the design, manufacture, and marketing of furniture, and specialises in leather and upholstered products such as sofas, armchairs and other living room accessories. Cattle hides and wood are among the key raw materials used by Natuzzi in the manufacture of its products, and significantly, sales of leather-upholstered furniture comprised over 94% of the company's net sales and 85% of the company's revenue in 2013.
The group has numerous subsidiaries, registered worldwide, including in Brazil, China, Italy and elsewhere in Europe, Japan, Russia, India and Australia.
As a leader in leather upholstery and the largest furniture manufacturer overall in Italy, Natuzzi plays a key role in the international leather trade, with customs data revealing that the company imports significant volumes of leather from Brazil. Further to this, Natuzzi owns one active manufacturing facility in Brazil, which aims to increase local sourcing from 2014 onwards.
Natuzzi offers products under several brands: Natuzzi Italia; Natuzzi Editions, also known as Leather Editions; Natuzzi Re-vive; and private label. Natuzzi Editions is the group's brand focusing on the medium-high end of the market. It was developed and is sold solely in the US market and its products are manufactured in China, Brazil and Romania. The Leather Editions brand offers similar leather products to Natuzzi Editions, but is marketed in Europe and the rest of the world, apart from in North and South America. Natuzzi Re-vive, launched in 2013, sells Natuzzi branded performance recliners.  Finally, the company has developed private label products to maintain its competitiveness in the low-end market segment.
The group's furniture products are sold through a range of retail outlets worldwide, including: franchised stores, Divani & Divani by Natuzzi and Natuzzi, which are all located in Italy and Portugal; its Natuzzi Editions and Leather Editions stores; and also through several large global furniture retailers, such as IKEA, Macy's, and Nitori.

As a leading producer of packaged foods, Kellanova uses significant quantities of soy, palm oil, pulp and paper throughout its product range. It is one of the largest poultry companies in Thailand and in the world. Its subsidiaries are also among the largest producers of animal feed globally. OCBC are among the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 4 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors, especially in agriculture and agriculture commodities.

With product lines spanning groceries, personal care items, apparel and furniture, Wal-Mart is exposed to a wide range of forest risk commodities, including palm oil, soy, beef, and timber. Mitsubishi Corp is a core company of the Mitsubishi Group; a group of autonomous companies made up of about 28 core enterprises and up to 600 member companies in all. The companies within the Mitsubishi Group conduct their operations independently of one another, but each honour the Group's three principles (of corporate social responsibility; integrity and fairness; and global understanding through business) and have their roots in the original shipping company, founded in 1870.
Mitsubishi Corp is a general trading company; the largest in Japan and the largest publicly-listed company of its kind in the world. The company's history extends back to 1954, when the Mitsubishi Shoji was established; however, Mitsubishi Corporation became the company's official English name in 1971. Mitsubishi Corp's activities now expand well beyond its original trading operations and it is involved in a wide variety of businesses, including energy, metals, food and environmental business.  Of particular relevance are Mitsubishi's operations in the production of food products that include soya and palm-based ingredients. Significantly, the Living Essentials department of Mitsubishi Corp also operates as a trading company in the palm oil industry, where it purchases predominantly Malaysian palm oil for export to Japan, the US and Taiwan, among others. The Living Essentials Group's activities in the production of consumer goods also include the procurement of raw materials and the manufacturing and distribution of a wide variety of products, including furniture, lumber, housing and construction materials, as well as many processed and frozen foods.
Mitsubishi Corp acquired UK-based food and drink manufacturer, Princes Ltd., in 1989. This is another particularly relevant component of Mitsubishi's operations. Founded in Liverpool, UK in 1880, Princes has since greatly increased its business portfolio diversifying from its original focus on the sale of canned goods. With a total of 19 mergers and acquisitions, it is now among the top food and drinks manufacturers in the UK.  Its tinned and canned products include meat pies, corned beef and stewed steak and the company is among the top five European beef importers from Brazil.

Minerva is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Together, these facilities have the capacity to slaughter more than 17,000 heads of cattle a day as of 2016. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.

Restaurant Brands International Inc. is the third largest fast food company in the world by market share, the second largest in western Europe and the fourth largest in the US. It was created in 2014 through the merging of two companies, Burger King Worldwide Inc. (Burger King) and Tim Hortons. The new company is headquartered in Canada, with 3G Capital being the majority shareholder. 
Burger King is the second largest fast food hamburger chain in the world, with 11 million customers visiting its stores every day. The company was founded in 1954 and in 2010, investment firm 3G Capital became the majority shareholder. The fast food giant is present in over 95 countries and US territories, and as of the end of 2013, comprised 13,667 restaurants, with the majority (54%) in the US and Canada and providing the bulk of the company's revenue. Having said this, Burger King is increasingly targeting expansion elsewhere, especially in high growth emerging markets. Burger King uses palm oil in its baked goods and as frying oil in the Asia/Pacific region and also uses soya in a number of its products, including baked goods.
Tim Hortons, with which Burger King merged to create Restaurant Brands International, is another multinational leader in the fast food industry. Tim Hortons franchises fast food restaurants primarily in Canada and the US. It is well known for its coffee and donuts, and also offers other sandwiches, bagels, cookies, muffins and pastries. Tim Horton's was started in Canada in the 1960s and now has around 4,304 restaurants, 3,468 in Canada, 807 in the US and 29 in the Gulf. Tim Horton's is one of the top ten largest fast food restaurant providers in the world and the largest in Canada. Tim Horton's demonstrates similar use of forest risk commodities to Burger King, purchasing both palm and soya bean oil for use in its products.
Note: In 2014 and 2015 this company was assessed under the name 'Burger King Worldwide Inc.'

R. R. Donnelley is a commercial printing company founded in 1864. It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. Their customers include some of the world's most well known companies including; Accenture, Barclays, IBM, and Microsoft. Despite offering a number of digital communication strategies, they are primarily known as a supplier of print material and is the leading company of its kind globally.  R. R. Donnelley also prints products for other companies involved in the printing and publishing sector. For example, it supplies print products to Pearson PLC and to HarperCollins, two of the world's largest publishers. In 2013 it employed roughly 57,000 people across four continents, in nearly 40 countries, leading to sales of $10.5 billion. It continues to expand through strategic acquisitions of companies specialising in both digital and commercial print. For example, in 2011, it acquired LibreDigital, a pioneering digital publishing and distribution company, and in 2014 acquired Consolidated Graphics in a deal worth over $600 million.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

Grupo Bimbo has more 100 brands in its portfolio, and produces over 10,000 different products. Through its products including bread, pastries and crisps Grupo Bimbo are exposed to palm oil and soy.   Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

COFCO is a leading agribusiness company in China producing, processing, manufacturing and trading in agricultural products and foodstuffs. It is one of the major players in the Chinese soy industry with two prominent Chinese subsidiaries. There are further processing facilities in Argentina and Brazil. The company is also a major exporter of soy from Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. COFCO’s animal feed production is among the largest globally. Another subsidiary has one of the largest forestry concessions in Gabon. The extent of its commodity trading and its food production also exposes the company to palm oil.  COFCO is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Staples Inc is an office supplies retailer that sells a variety of products to businesses and individual consumers. It is the world's largest specialist retailer of office supplies with key products lines in stationery, furniture, and technology products. Staples sells a wide variety of paper products, including copy paper, computer paper and POS rolls, photographic paper and letterheads.
Established in 1985, the company is headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts in the United States. The company's three operational segments are: North American Stores & Online; North American Commercial; and International Operations. The company operates around 2,200 stores globally, and also sells products online and via its catalogue service. It also has around 116 distribution centres throughout the US, Canada, Europe, China, South America, and elsewhere, in all serving customers in 26 countries worldwide.
Staples is the world's largest retailer of a wide range of wood- and paper-based office products, sourcing its products from a range of suppliers in different countries, including Argentina, Brazil, Canada, China and the US. In 2013, paper sales accounted for around 9% of Staples' total revenue; office furniture contributed around 5%; and core office supplies, which include paper and other core office products such as writing products, around 30%. Staples sells its own proprietary branded products under the Staples and Quill trademarks and also offers other manufactured branded items.

Lloyds Banking Group are financial services group headquartered in the UK serving individual and commercial clients. Their services include banking (retail, commercial and corporate), insurance, pensions and investments. As of 2024, their total assets amount to over £900 billion. Lloyds Banking Group are in top lenders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Lloyds Banking Group was providing 40.3 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd is a holding company for the Nippon Paper Group, which is comprised of around 180 affiliates and subsidiaries. The Group ranks among the top forest, paper and packaging companies globally, occupying sixth place in a worldwide ranking of the top 100 and the second position of such companies in Japan. The Group produces a variety of paper products, including newsprint, printing paper, copy paper, wrapping paper, linerboard, paperboard, tissue products, and healthcare products. For example, through its subsidiary Nippon Paper Crecia Co Ltd, the Group manufactures family care, personal care and professional products under a license agreement with leading hygiene products company, Kimberly-Clark.
The Group has diverse business interests on top of its activities in the paper sector, and several of Nippon Paper Groups's other operations also make use of wood products. For example, it has several subsidiaries active in the wood products and construction industry; in the procurement of lumber and the manufacture of construction materials. These subsidiaries include Nippon Paper Lumber Co., Ltd., PAL Co., Ltd., and Daishowa Uniboard Co., Ltd. Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd has a global network supplying logs and lumber from a variety of sources, including domestically and from the United States, Canada, Europe, New Zealand and some tropical regions. As well as supplying raw and sawn timber, Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd also manufactures plywood and laminated lumber products. Pal Co Ltd and Daishowa Uniboard Co Ltd manufacture products for use in the construction industry, such as doors, staircases, flooring and decorative laminates.

rows.coprofile: Tetra Laval consists of three industry groups, Tetra Pak, Sidel and DeLaval.  The companies' activities focus on systems for the processing, packaging and distribution of food and accessories for dairy production and animal husbandry and are assessed due to their use of pulp and paper.

The earliest foundations of the Oetker-Gruppe lie in 1891, when Dr August Oetker developed the baking powder, Backin, in Germany. The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. The Oetker-Gruppe sells its products to the consumer market under the brand, Dr Oetker. Its consumer products include; frozen pizzas, ready desserts and a number of other chilled and frozen products. Through the Martin Braun group, the Oetker-Gruppe sells a number of baking agents, glazes and decorations to baking and confectionary companies. The manufacturing of these products meant that the Oetker-Gruppe used 4,777 tonnes of palm oil or palm oil derivatives in 2013. Oetker-Gruppe has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011 and in 2012, four of its manufacturing facilities in Germany were certified as RSPO supply chain certified (all palm oil and palm oil derivatives used are RSPO-certified).

BTG Pactual are an investment bank and asset manager headquartered in Brazil. Their services include investment banking, corporate finance, asset and wealth management, and trading services. As of 2017, BTG Pactual's total assets under management amount to more than 125 billion BRL. BTG Pactual are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

Commerzbank are a German retail, commercial and investment banking group, offering services to private and corporate customers. Their services include wealth management, investment banking, insurance, pensions, corporate finance and retail banking services. As of 2017, Commerzbank has more than 480 billion EUR in total assets, including over 215 billion EUR in claims on customers. Commerzbank are among the top 35 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 8 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Natura Cosmeticos is a cosmetics company active throughout South America and which also has a consumer base in France. Its products range from make-up to fragrances and hair products, which exposes the company to forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soya. Natura Cosmeticos is one of the largest companies in Brazil for beauty and personal care as well as skin care.

Casino Guichard Perrachon (Casino) is a French retailer with more than 15,000 convenience stores, hypermarkets and supermarkets predominantly in France and Latin America. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. The group is among the edible grocery retailers globally and it has an especially strong presence in Latin America. Casino claims to be the top retailer in Brazil, Colombia and Vietnam.  Casino Guichard Perrachon S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: GlaxoSmithKline Plc is a United Kingdom-based healthcare company with business segments in pharmaceuticals, consumer healthcare and vaccines.  GlaxoSmithKline Plc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Target Corporation is a general merchandise retailer operating in the US. Established in 1902 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, it is one of North America's retail giants, ranking among the top fifty in the Fortune 500. Target offers a variety of products including: food, beauty and personal care items; cleaning and paper products; as well as apparel and furniture, among other products. The company operates over 1,792 stores in the US as well as 38 distribution centres. Target began operating stores in Canada in 2011 through the acquisition of Zellers; however in 2015 the company planned to discontinue operating stores in the country.
A significant component of Target's sales are made up of its owned and exclusive branded products, which account for around one third of the company's total sales. Its owned branded products include: Archers Farms groceries; luggage; travel accessories; furniture; other goods sold under the Embark brand; Smith & Hawken outdoor furniture; Sutton & Dodge meat products; and up & up health and beauty products.

Grupo Bimbo is a Mexican company that manufacture baked goods. The company sell products in most countries in America, and a few in Europe and Asia. Grupo Bimbo has more 100 brands in its portfolio, and produces over 10,000 different products. Through its products including bread, pastries and crisps Grupo Bimbo are exposed to palm oil and soy.   Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Daiwa House Industry is a Japanese construction company, constructing residential homes and flats, business premises, and hotels. It is one of the largest homebuilders in Japan, which is an industry that uses large amounts of timber.  Daiwa House Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Minerva is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. Together, these facilities have the capacity to slaughter more than 17,000 heads of cattle a day as of 2016. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.

rows.coprofile: DuPont is a US chemicals, materials and services company that provides scientific solutions to business challenges. It is active in agriculture, food and drinks, materials, electronics and other industries with operations in about 90 countries. The company’s nutrition business area is involved in the manufacturing of food ingredients which involves palm oil, and it also produces soy proteins and other soy based products. DuPont is a key vendor and manufacturer in the global food ingredient market.  DuPont is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Korindo Group is a diversified company based in Indonesia which produces, processes and manufacturers a range of products. Korindo has plantations of palm oil and timber

Hengan International is a Chinese manufacturer of paper products including sanitary napkins, disposable nappies and tissue paper.  Hengan International Group Co Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.
In addition to its major Starbucks brand the company also operates: Seattles Best Coffee, Teavana, Tazo, Evolution Fresh, La Boulange (bakery brand) and Torrefazione Italia Coffee. Starbucks is the largest cafe/bar owner in the world with revenues of $14.9bn. Starbucks uses paper in its packaging, soya (in milk) and palm oil (in its food products).

The Schwarz Group is a German retail group comprised of both wholesalers and multi-format retail stores. Its supermarkets operate under the brands Kaufland, Handelshof and Kaufmarkt, alongside the discount retailer Lidl. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. With the combined weight of these retailers, the Schwarz Group is among the top five retailers for edible groceries globally. It is also one of the largest edible grocery retailers in Europe.

Aditya Birla Group is one of the largest conglomerates in India with operations in 36 countries. The group operates in sectors including fashion, cement, mobiles and viscose filament yarn.  Aditya Birla Group is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

BASF is a German-based chemical company operating in over 80 countries. Its portfolio includes a wide range of products including chemicals, plastics, agricultural solutions, and even oil and gas. Palm kernel oil and its derivatives are key raw materials for BASF’s home and personal care offerings.  BASF Personal Care and Nutrition GmbH is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.

They are also among the top 15 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 28 billion USD worth of shares.

Globally it is one of the top 15 companies in the edible market, but it is also among the five largest in the APAC region. The store network comprises a total of 625 stores in 21 countries. With a diverse product range, Metro AG is exposed to a number of forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy, pulp and paper. Metro AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Estee Lauder is an American cosmetics company with products sold in 50 countries around the world. Products include skin care, hair care, makeup, and fragrances with well-known brands including Aveda, Jo Malone, and Estee Lauder itself. It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

Itaú Unibanco are banking group based in Brazil serving both private and commercial customers. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, wealth management, insurance, pensions and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.3 trillion BRL, including over 400 billion BRL in loans. Itaú Unibanco are one of the top 60 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 3 billion USD of loans to companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Aegon are an insurance company based in the Netherlands serving private, commercial and institutional customers. Their services include life insurance, pensions, and asset management. As of 2017, Aegon manage a combined value of 840 billion EUR of investments, including more than 325 billion EUR in assets under management. They are one of the top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with approximately 2 billion USD worth of bonds for companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group’s two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.6 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.  Royal Golden Eagle is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

COFCO is a leading agribusiness company in China producing, processing, manufacturing and trading in agricultural products and foodstuffs. It is one of the major players in the Chinese soy industry with two prominent Chinese subsidiaries. There are further processing facilities in Argentina and Brazil. The company is also a major exporter of soy from Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. COFCO’s animal feed production is among the largest globally. Another subsidiary has one of the largest forestry concessions in Gabon. The extent of its commodity trading and its food production also exposes the company to palm oil.  COFCO is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.
