rows.coprofile: The Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) offers financial services to Brazilian companies and financial institutions with the aim of stimulating industry and infrastructure growth in Brazil. Their services include corporate financing, non-reimbursable investments, and securities. As of 2017, the bank's total assets amount to more than 870 billion BRL, with loans of more than 590 billion BRL. BNDES are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

Kering SA is a French company engaged in the retail and distribution of luxury goods, primarily apparel and accessories. Until 2013, the company was known as PPR, short for Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, which in turn was its official name until 2005.  Established in 1963, the company has its origins in the building materials industry and in particular in the timber trade. It then became a leader in the retail sector, before entering into the world of luxury goods with the purchase of the Gucci brand in 1999. Today the company has 22 brands operating in two core divisions: Luxury, which designs, manufactures and markets luxury apparel, leather goods, accessories, watches, jewellery, fragrances and cosmetics; and Sport and Lifestyle, which designs and produces footwear, apparel and accessories under the company's sporting brands.
Kering SA is headquartered in Paris, France and its brands in its luxury and sports and lifestyle segments, include several world famous brands including Puma, Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen, Balenciaga and Stella McCartney, many of which have leather goods among their principal products,. Kering SA therefore plays a prominent role in the global trade in leather and animal skins, with several of the company's brands designing and selling leather goods. For example, it produces leather wallets and handbags under Saint Laurent  and Balenciaga. Through these and its numerous other brands, Kering SA holds the second largest market share in the bags and luggage sector globally. It also produces large amount s of leather footwear, for example under Sergio Rossi; a leading Italian shoe brand. Kering SA is among the top five manufacturers of footwear globally, occupying the fourth largest share of the global market in 2013, and in particular holding a leading position in the footwear market of Western Europe, especially in Italy. Kering SA is placing increasing emphasis on the direct sourcing of its raw materials, including leather. In 2013, it bought a majority stake in one the world's biggest producers of tanned skins and it has plans to build a new tanning facility in France, which could be operational by 2016.

Tesco is a leading British retailer with over 6,000 stores worldwide. The company specialises in groceries but also sells personal care items, apparel and furniture, as well as offering financial services through its subsidiary Tesco Bank. Amongst its product lines, Tesco sells a range of own brand products including packaged meats, dairy products and confectionary items. The company’s operations leave it exposed to several forest risk commodities.   Tesco plc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

It is a global market leader in many agricultural commodities such as cocoa and coffee, but also is a major player in African oil palm and forestry. Olam’s subsidiary, Congolaise Industrielle de Bois (CIB) operates forestry concessions in the Republic of Congo. The company is also active in soy cultivation and processing in South America and Africa.  Olam International  is selected as a powerbroker for soy and timber and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

The Aldi Group is a German discount retailer split into two companies, Aldi Nord and Aldi Sud, both of which have an international presence. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities.  Aldi Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

H&M Hennes and Mauritz AB is a Swedish clothing company operating under several brands, including its flagship brand H&M, as well as COS, Monki, Cheap Monday, and & Other Stories . The company, headquartered in Sweden, is involved in designing, manufacturing and marketing apparel, accessories and home textiles.  It was established in 1947, with the opening of its first Hennes store in VÃ¤sterÃ¥s, Sweden, which exclusively sold women's clothing. With the acquisition of hunting and fishing equipment store Mauritz Widforss in 1968, the company changed its name to Hennes & Mauritz and expanded its product range to also cover apparel for men and children. Since then, the company has expanded, opening stores throughout Europe as well as worldwide. For example, it expanded into the US in 2000, and opened stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2007. Further to this, the company established a new brand, COS, in 2007 and acquired the fashion firm, FaBric Scandinavien AB, in 2008, which holds the Weekday, Monki and Cheap Monday brands . In 2010, the full incorporation of FaBric Scandinavien was completed, when Hennes & Mauritz acquired the remaining 40% of shares.

rows.coprofile: Wilmar International Ltd. is a global agribusiness group involved in the cultivation, processing, refining, merchandising and trading of a wide range of agricultural products, including palm oil and soy. The company is one of the world’s largest oil palm plantation owners and processors, reportedly controlling around 45% of worldwide palm oil trade sourced from more than 80% of global palm oil growers. Wilmar is also a major player in the soybean crushing industry with a global crushing capacity of 36 million metric tons per annum, the majority of which is in China. The company claims to be one of the world’s largest producers of consumer edible oils.   Wilmar International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Domino's Pizza Inc. is a US pizza delivery and carry-out company serving the US and over 75 international markets. Worldwide, there are 11,700 stores that deliver over 1 million pizzas every day. Over 90% of stores are franchised, while Domino's Pizza Inc. owns around 377 stores in the US. It also runs dough manufacturing facilities and supply chain centres to supply stores in the US and in some overseas markets.  The US is Domino's Pizza Inc.'s single biggest market with 5,084 stores in Q1 2015, but over half of the company's sales come from outside the US. Domino's Pizza Inc. is the world's second biggest fast food pizza retailer. In addition to pizza, the company offers related products including sandwiches, chicken, salads, sauces, drinks and desserts. Beef is used as a pizza topping, soya is used in pizzas, and both soya and palm oil are used in side dishes and desserts.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating producer and distributor headquartered in Michigan, USA, employing more than 110,000 people. The key subsidiary of relevance to forest risk commodities owned by Lear Corp. is Eagle Ottawa, which produces leather upholstery products for the automotive industry. Eagle Ottawa was founded in 1865 and was formerly known as Eagle Tanning Works but changed its name to Eagle Ottawa, LLC in 1916.
 
Eagle Ottawa claims to be the largest supplier of premium automotive leather and produces a variety of leather products, including finished hides, cut leather, natural shrunken grain leather, and chrome- and non-chrome-tanned leather.  As well as these, it also produces leather for other interior uses, such as for door panels and instrument panels. The company engages in various activities in leather processing including pre-tanning and tanning as well as cutting and finishing. Aside from the subsidiary's headquarters, which are in the state of Michigan, in the US, Eagle Ottawa also has facilities in Mexico, Brazil, Hungary, China, South Korea and Thailand. It also has sales and design locations in China, Japan, Brazil, Germany, England, Sweden and Italy, as well as the US. The company's customers include some of the automobile industry's biggest players, including Mercedes, BMW, Toyota, Renault Chrysler, GMC and Volkswagen.

International Flavors & Fragrances, Inc (IFF) is an American corporation that manufactures products for the food and beverage, home and personal care, and health and wellness markets. They are headquartered in New York City, with manufacturing facilities in 44 different countries. They have been selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and soy. IFF and DuPont’s Nutrition & Biosciences Business completed their merger in 2021.

IKEA is a Swedish home furniture company. There are over 350 IKEA stores worldwide, with more than 180,000 employees. According to the company, it is the largest producer of wooden furniture in the world, meaning that its operations require large amounts of timber. It is also exposed to leather in furniture, and palm oil in candles and food.  IKEA Group is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

rows.coprofile: Kingfisher is a European home improvement company that operates chains of retail stores including B&Q, Castorama and Screwfix. Through its various subsidiaries, Kingfisher trades in a large number of timber products, ranging from garden sheds, to furniture and DIY supplies. It is also exposed to leather in some of its products.  Kingfisher Plc is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging.

Adecoagro is a leading agro-industrial company in South America, active in Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay. Its business involves the production of numerous grains and oilseeds, including soy. According to the company, Adecoagro is one of the largest owners of productive farmland in South America.  Adecoagro S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Marfrig Global Foods SA (Marfrig GF) is a multinational company with operations in Brazil, where it is headquartered, as well as in 15 other countries around the world. The company's main business activities include the production, processing, preparation, sale and distribution of meat (beef, pork, lamb and poultry), pasta and processed foods (including pizzas, lasagnas, breaded products and desserts), ready meals and frozen vegetables, as well as the distribution of other food products (including frozen foods, sausages and fish) and semi-finished and finished leather.
Marfrig GF began distributing meats and imported vegetables in 1986, over the past two decades it has grown rapidly and diversified through organic growth and acquisitions of Brazilian and overseas companies. Marfrig GF operates through a number of wholly and part owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. The largest shareholders are CEO Marcos Antonio Molina dos Santos, and his wife, via a holding company and the Brazilian development bank. In 2013 Marfrig GF sold Seara Brazil and Zenda (non-beef operations) to fellow Brazilian meat processor JBS and refocused on beef and food service in its home market of Brazil. Internationally, however, it retained a broader food focus through its MoyPark and Keystone operations.
Today Marfrig GF is one of Brazil's three largest beef exporters. It employs 46,000 people across its 78 production units and distribution centres, and it has offices in Europe, South America, North America, Asia and Oceania.
Marfrig is divided into three principle segments: Marfrig Beef produces beef and lamb for the South American and export markets, brand include GJ and Aberdeen Angus; the Moy Park segment's primary focus is on Europe where it provides poultry and prepared meals to retailers and food service chains using both the Moy Park and Jamie Oliver brands; and the Keystone segment supplies restaurant chains with meat products, focussing on the US and Asian markets and with a number of joint ventures in China. 
The company has a daily slaughtering capacity of 20,730 head of cattle (as well as numerous chickens, heads of pork and lambs) and also produces 294,000 leather articles per month. In 2013 Marfrig GF launched the world's first Rainforest Alliance Certified beef. The group's poultry and feed operations also use significant amounts of soya within poultry feed.
Marfrig GF claims to participate in the Grupo de Trabalho da Pecuária Sustentável (GTPS) - Sustainable Beef Working Group - a World Bank initiative implemented by IFC - International Finance Corporation with the purpose of promoting the sustainability of the beef and veal commodity supply chain. It is also a member of the Leather Working Group and a signatory to numerous sustainability initiatives, including: the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; the public commitment Criteria for Industrial-Scale Operations with Livestock and Bovine Products in the Amazon Biome, in partnership with Greenpeace; and the Corporate Pact for Sustainable Connections. In addition Marfrig GF has contributed to some reforestation projects, including giving over 9,776,000 eucalyptus saplings to 780 rural producers in order to foster biosafety and the "green barrier" on poultry and pork farms.

rows.coprofile: Deckers Outdoor Corp is a footwear distributor based in the US made up of several well-known brands such as UGG.  Deckers Outdoor Corp is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

JM Smucker is a Fortune 500 company who manufactures food and beverage products on a global scale. Famous brands include Crisco and Jif. JM Smucker is exposed to palm oil and soy as ingredients and to soy through animal feed for meat and dairy products.  JM Smucker  is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Credit Suisse are a global private bank based in Switzerland serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, capital markets, wealth management, investment banking, and consumer finance services. As of 2021, Credit Suisse have over 1.6 trillion CHF in assets under management. Credit Suisse are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2022 selection, Credit Suisse was providing 57 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

It is one of the top ten users of palm oil worldwide, using over 380,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products in 2015.

Natura Cosmeticos is a cosmetics company active throughout South America and which also has a consumer base in France. Its products range from make-up to fragrances and hair products, which exposes the company to forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soya. Natura Cosmeticos is one of the largest companies in Brazil for beauty and personal care as well as skin care.

Sinar Mas is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including pulp and paper, agriculture and food, energy, financial services, and real estate. The group’s agricultural business has one of the largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It is also one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Its products include cooking oil and margarine. Additionally, the group crushes soy, with an annual capacity of 2.3 million metric tons. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.  Sinar Mas is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to pulp & paper.

Target Corporation is a leading United States retailer with over 1,800 stores. The company is recognised as an industry leader, and in 2016 was ranked among the top 50 on the Fortune 500. It sells a variety of products including food, personal care items, paper products, furniture and apparel. Amongst these product lines Target sells several own-brand goods under labels including Market Pantry and Archer Farms. Through its retail and production operations Target is exposed to a variety of forest risk commodities.  Target Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef, leather, timber and paper packaging.
Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd. was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Producer, Processor, Trader) and is also assessed for Timber (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

rows.coprofile: UPM is a forest industry company based in Finland, with operations in 15 countries including Argentina, Uruguay and Indonesia. UPM produces, processes and trades timber and paper.  UPM is selected as a powerbroker for timber and pulp & paper.

Crédit Agricole are a European banking group headquartered in France serving private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, capital markets, investment banking, insurance, asset management, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2024, the group's total assets under management amount to more than 2.8 trillion EUR. Crédit Agricole are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Crédit Agricole was providing over 161 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Lloyds Banking Group plc are financial services group headquartered in the UK serving individual and commercial clients. Their services include banking (retail, commercial and corporate), insurance, pensions and investments. As of 2017, their total assets amount to over £810 billion with loans of over £450 billion. Lloyds Banking Group plc are in top lenders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

First Resources is a cultivator and processor of palm oil, active across Indonesia. The company's landbank for palm oil is one of the fifteen largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers, with more than 200,000 hectares in Indonesia. It also owns several mills and refineries with an annual processing capacity of 850,000 metric tons. First Resources sells a range of products including oleochemicals, biodiesel and palm kernel expeller which is used as animal feed.

Estee Lauder is an American cosmetics company with products sold in 50 countries around the world. Products include skin care, hair care, makeup, and fragrances with well-known brands including Aveda, Jo Malone, and Estee Lauder itself. It is among the top five largest companies for cosmetics and beauty and personal care by market share. The company has greatest presence in the US, Western Europe, and Hong Kong. In 2015, Estee Lauder used more than 3,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its products.

Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio, publishing and magazines. The most important markets are the US and Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.  Bertelsmann SE & Co. KGaA is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Starbucks Corp. was selected as a powerbroker for Coffee (Trader, Retailer, Manufacturer), Palm oil (Retailer), Cocoa (Retailer), Soy (Retailer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Beef (Retailer)

Target Corporation is a general merchandise retailer operating in the US. Established in 1902 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, it is one of North America's retail giants, ranking among the top fifty in the Fortune 500. Target offers a variety of products including: food, beauty and personal care items; cleaning and paper products; as well as apparel and furniture, among other products. The company operates over 1,792 stores in the US as well as 38 distribution centres. Target began operating stores in Canada in 2011 through the acquisition of Zellers; however in 2015 the company planned to discontinue operating stores in the country.
A significant component of Target's sales are made up of its owned and exclusive branded products, which account for around one third of the company's total sales. Its owned branded products include: Archers Farms groceries; luggage; travel accessories; furniture; other goods sold under the Embark brand; Smith & Hawken outdoor furniture; Sutton & Dodge meat products; and up & up health and beauty products.

Kraft Heinz Co. was selected as a powerbroker for Soy (Manufacturer), Beef (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Coffee (Manufacturer), Cocoa (Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer)

Sekisui House Ltd has operations in the housing construction industry, and in real estate brokerage and leasing. The company was established in 1960 and has its headquarters in Osaka, Japan. It claims to be Japan's largest and best known home builder and is listed among the largest companies globally as the second largest Japanese construction services company. 
Sekisui House Ltd has numerous subsidiaries across its various business segments, which comprise trade, brokerage and lease of real estate; remodelling; construction; surveying; and others including financial services and manufacturing. The company operates 19 construction subsidiaries across Japan under Sekisui Construction Ltd and as of January 2014 had constructed almost 2.2 million houses. Sekisui House Ltd has also been active in the Australian market since 2009, under Sekisui House Australia.
Sekisui House Ltd specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing and is the main player in Japan's prefabrication industry. Specifically, Sekisui House Ltd constructs and sells steel- and wooden-frame housing. The company's steel-frame housing was launched in the 1970's, marking the entrance of Sekisui House into the housing industry. This was followed by the launch of the company' wooden frame unit housing, Two-U Home, in 1982. The company now builds a variety of wooden frame housing, for example, the Gravis Bella wooden frame model, in its detached housing business. On top of its initial construction activities, Sekisui House Ltd also offers interior decoration and furnishing services.
The major shareholder of Sekisui House Ltd is Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, which has operations worldwide and also has business interests in urban infrastructure, environmental products and high performance plastics.

The Aldi Group is a German discount retailer split into two companies, Aldi Nord and Aldi Sud, both of which have an international presence. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities.  Aldi Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

AAK refines vegetable oils for specialised products mainly for foodservice, chocolate and confectionery, and technical products.  The Swedish company has 19 production facilities and sales offices in more than 25 countries, and claims to be the world’s leading manufacturer of specialty vegetable fats. AAK sources Soy from South America and Palm Oil from Southeast Asia and Central America.   AAK AB is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

ForFarmers B.V. is a major supplier of compound feed in the European market. The company also sells agricultural commodities such as fertilisers, seed and crop protection agents as well as advice services to its customers. With roots dating back to 1896, ForFarmers adopted its current name in 2005. The firm is transitioning its ownership structure from a cooperative to a shareholders structure. Presently, the firm remains majority-controlled (74%) by the cooperative FromFarmers and its members' accounts and certificates, with the remaining 26% under the ownership of other investors. In April 2016, ForFarmers will seek shareholders' approval to transfer to a technical listing on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange.
ForFarmers is the top feed supplier in both the Dutch and British markets, and is third and fourth in Belgium and Germany respectively. Also the company's biggest individual markets, the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany and Belgium account for 40%, 27% and 32% of sales respectively. The company sells around 8.9 million tons of feed per year, three quarters of which is compound feed.  In 2013, the largest proportion of its compound feed sales was pig feed at 37%, followed by cattle feed at 32%, and poultry feed at 22%. It employs over 2,300 people and has 42 manufacturing facilities at sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and the UK.
Acquisitions of feed businesses such as Hendrix, operating in Benelux and Germany, and BOCM Pauls, Wheyfeeds and HST Feeds in the UK, have helped to make ForFarmers Europe's largest compound feed producer. The company is looking at further acquisitions to enter new markets and to consolidate in existing European markets. ForFarmers also has strategic collaborations with direct competitors, including with Nutreco in the young animal feed business and with Agrifirm in the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and crop protection. As a major world compound feed producer, ForFarmers uses both soya and palm oil in its products.

Shell, headquartered in the Netherlands, is a group of energy and petrochemical companies operating globally. Segments of the business include the development of biofuels, using palm and soy products as a base.  Royal Dutch Shell is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and soy.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Operating across the United States, China and India, Tyson Foods Inc. has business in poultry, beef, pork and processed food products. The company’s poultry business is particularly noteworthy here, because it involves the provision of feed product to a network of independent poultry farmers that in 2015 exceeded 4,000. Animal feed uses significant quantities of soy, and in 2014 Tyson Food Inc’s operations in this field saw it ranked among the top ten feed producers worldwide.   Tyson Foods Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Hermès International S.A was selected as a powerbroker for Leather (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Manufacturer, Retailer) and is also assessed for Rubber (Manufacturer, Retailer), Timber (Retailer, Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer, Retailer), Soy (Manufacturer, Retailer)
initiatives: "Hermès demonstrates commitment to promoting biodiversity through its contributions to the Act4Nature initiative – of which it is a signatory –, its investment in the Livelihoods funds, and the actions it takes within the framework of the Fondation d’entreprise Hermès11"

rows.coprofile: Ahold Delhaize is a food retail group, formed from the merger of Ahold and the Delhaize Group in 2016. It has twenty-two store brands, including groceries, supermarkets, specialty stores and online stores across the US, the Netherlands, Belgium, and other European countries. It is one of the world's largest retailers and claims its subsidiaries include the top online retailer in the Benelux and leading online grocers in the Benelux and the US. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. In 2015, Ahold Delhaize used more than 10,000 metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in its own brand products.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum, New York Declaration on Forests, Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, UN Global Compact

rows.coprofile: Restaurant Brands International, created in 2014 after a merger of the two famous brands Burger King and Tim Hortons, is one of the world’s largest fast food companies. With its two brands, the company operates 19,000 restaurants in almost 100 countries. It is one of the top fast food companies in Europe, the US and in the world. The varied menu of both chains expose them to a range of forest risk commodities.  Restaurant Brands International is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Costco Wholesale Corporation as a global retailer and wholesaler. The company offers products such as groceries, apparel, furniture, houseware, office suppliers and health and beauty aids.  Costco Wholesale Corporation is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

The Hershey Company (Hershey's) was incorporated in Delaware, US in 1927, as a successor to a business founded in Philadelphia in 1894 by Milton S. Hershey. Today, the company sells and distributes its products in around 70 countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia. It claims to be the top chocolate and confectionary company in US by market share, where over 85% of Hershey's consolidated revenue is generated. Outside the US, the company's main countries of operation are Canada, Mexico, Brazil, China, India, Korea, and Japan. The company has 22,000 employees around the world and an annual turnover of over $7.4 billion. Hershey's has more than 80 brands  including Reese's, Mound, Almond Joy, Twizzlers , and it also shares a licensing agreement with Nestle to produce KitKat in America .  It has been a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member since 2011 and used 23,967 tonnes of palm oil in 2014, 100% of which is RSPO certified. Hershey's is focusing on expanding its business both through entry into new markets, such as the meat snack market through the acquisition of KRAVE Pure Foods, Inc., in March 2015, and through consolidating its operations in markets outside the US, such as through its acquisition in September 2015 of the remaining 49% of shares in its Bauducco/Pandurata Alimentos SA distribution joint venture in Brazil.

The Royal Bank of Canada are a banking and financial services group headquartered in Canada serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include wealth management, insurance, capital markets, investments, commercial banking and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.2 trillion CAD, with net loans worth nearly 480 billion CAD. The Royal Bank of Canada are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 11 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 50 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 7 billion USD worth of shares.
Harita Group was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Processor, Producer) and is also assessed for Timber (Producer, Processor)

Prada SpA is the holding company of the Prada Group, which with its subsidiary companies, is involved in the design, manufacture and retail of leather goods, clothing, shoes, and accessories. Prada was founded in Italy in 1913 as a specialist retailer selling accessories, luggage and other luxury items. Today, the Prada brand forms a component of the Prada Group, which has become an international leader in the luxury goods industry. On top of the flagship Prada brand, the Group sells products under the Miu Miu, Car Shoe and Church's brands.  Prada and Miu Miu provide customers with a variety of high-end luxury items, including leatherwear, handbags, apparel, footwear and fragrances. The Car Shoe and Church's brands are more specialist and each offer high-end luxury footwear. Church's is a leading English leather footwear brand that dates back to 1873, while Car Shoe specialises in leather moccasins specifically designed for driving. The Prada Group's brands are sold through its own outlets in stores and online, and through wholesale distribution channels. The Group has a worldwide presence, including in the top fashion markets of London, Milan, Tokyo, Beijing, Hong Kong and New York.
Prada SpA is a significant player in the bags and luggage industry. It ranks among the top five bags and luggage companies globally, and in the top five in China and top three in the Western European market. It also plays an important role in the international footwear industry, particularly in the markets of China, the US and Europe.  Leather goods therefore form an important component of the Prada Group's business; accounting for over 65% of consolidated net sales in the year up to January 2014, totalling over 2 billion Euros.
initiatives: No response to CDP for leather, reports total amount of material it uses for paper and packaging purposes

rows.coprofile:
DLG Denmark, established in 1964, is one of Europe's biggest agricultural companies. It is owned by 30,000 Danish farmers and employs 7,500 people, 3,000 of whom are in Denmark. Through over 40 subsidiaries and associated companies, DLG Denmark is involved in a broad range of business and consumer sectors, with localised operations in in more than 20 countries. 
DLG Denmark is organised into four business areas: Premix and Nutrition, accounting for 4% of turnover, provides specialist animal feeds and minerals; Service and Energy, contributing 28% of turnover, provides a broad range of products and services including fuels, telecommunications and IT, and also operates DIY stores and petrol stations; Machinery, Flowers and Food, which accounts for 6% of turnover, provides industrial and agricultural machinery as well as a broad range of plants and food products, including oils and vegetables; and Farm Supply, the largest division, providing 62% turnover, encompasses animal feed production, poultry hatcheries, provision of fertiliser and pesticides, and crop production.
DLG Denmark produces compound feeds for farm animals at its mills in Europe and is one of Europe's top five largest producers of compound feeds. Soya is a significant feed production ingredient, accounting for around 15 to 20% composition. Consequently, DLG Denmark buys around half of Denmark's soymeal. DLG Denmark uses a similar amount of palm oil in its animal feed.

Glencore is a Swiss-based multi-national company producing and trading in the agriculture, energy and metal sectors.  Glencore is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.
initiatives: World Business Council for Sustainable Development Forest Solutions Group

rows.coprofile: Essity is a Swedish company which manufacturers paper-based products including personal care, and hygiene products.  Essity is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum Deforestation resolution (being a member of the CGF is not sufficient)

rows.coprofile: Grupo Bimbo is a Mexican company that manufacture baked goods. The company sells products in most countries in America, and a few in Europe and Asia. Grupo Bimbo has more 100 brands in its portfolio, and produces over 10,000 different products. Through its products including bread, pastries and crisps Grupo Bimbo are exposed to palm oil and soy.   Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Signatory to Net-Zero Asset Managers Initiative. Nordea Investment Funds finances the Forest 500 with a total of 7 USDM
Sampoerna Agri Resources Pte. Ltd is one of the leading producers of palm oil and palm kernel in Indonesia.  Sampoerna Agri Resources Pte. Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

rows.coprofile: Norges Bank Investment Management are a Norwegian state-owned investment fund. They invest in international equity, fixed-income markets and real estate to provide security for Norway's economy against fluctuating oil prices. Norges Bank Investment Management are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with shares across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2022 selection, Norges Bank Investment Management was providing 111 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Musim Mas is a fully integrated palm oil corporation involved throughout the palm oil supply chain, from cultivation to processing, manufacturing and trading. The company's landbank is among the top fifteen largest landbanks globally for oil palm, with over 130,000 hectares of plantations in Indonesia as of 2016. In 2015, Musim Mas' processing facilities had an annual capacity of 900,000 metric tons for fresh fruit bunches and produced over 300,000 metric tons of palm oil products. Furthermore, it is among the top five importers and exporters of palm oil from Indonesia globally and among the top five producers of biodiesel in Indonesia.
initiatives: Fire Free Alliance, China Sustainable Palm Alliance,

rows.coprofile: Perkebunan Nusantara is an Indonesian state-owned plantation company comprised of fourteen individual but interrelated business enterprises. The group cultivates and processes several agricultural commodities, including rubber, tobacco, sugar cane, tea, and palm oil. It is a major producer and processor of palm oil, estimated to have more than 500,000 hectares for palm plantations and a processing capacity of more than 3,000 fresh fruit bunches per hour from more than 65 facilities.  Perkebunan Nusantara is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.
ConAgra Brands Inc was selected as a powerbroker for Soy (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Cocoa (Manufacturer), Beef (Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer)

CIMB Group is a Southeast Asian banking group headquartered in Malaysia serving private and commercial clients. Its services include corporate finance, treasury markets, investment banking, insurance, wealth management and retail banking. CIMB Group is one of the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, predominantly in the agriculture and agricultural commodity sectors.

Minerva S.A. is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. The meat processed by Minerva S.A. is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.  Minerva S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for beef and leather and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: WM Morrison Supermarkets PLC claims to be the UK’s fourth largest supermarket chain and operates approximately 500 stores. They have food manufacturing capabilities in meat, fish and bakery products.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong (KLK) is a Malaysian agribusiness company active in the cultivation, processing and manufacturing of palm oil and rubber, as well as being involved in property development. The company has one of the largest landbanks among palm oil producers across Malaysia, Indonesia and Liberia. It also owns several mills and two refineries and is among the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to timber and paper packaging.

Clariant AG is a Swiss multinational speciality chemicals company using both palm oil and soy in the manufacture of their various products. Clariant develops, produces, markets and sells specialty chemical products for various end markets including paints, cosmetics and oils.

optional_cols.heading: HRA applies to all supply chain

rows.coprofile: Sinar Mas is an Indonesian conglomerate active in diverse industries, including pulp and paper, agriculture and food, energy, financial services, and real estate. The group's agricultural business operates about 480,000 hectares of palm oil plantation as of 2016 and has one of the five largest landbanks globally among palm oil producers. It also has an annual processing capacity of more than 12 million fresh fruit bunches and is one of the largest importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia. Its products include cooking oil and margarine. Additionally, the group crushes soya, with an annual capacity of 2.3 million metric tons. Sinar Mas is also a major pulp and paper producer with its company Asia Pulp and Paper, having an annual capacity of more than 20 million metric tons across its mills in Indonesia and China.
Ferrero Group was selected as a powerbroker for Soy (Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer), Cocoa (Manufacturer) and is also assessed for Coffee (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

Nippon Paper Industries is a Japanese paper manufacturing company. The company produces newsprint, printing paper, paperboard, wrapping paper, and building materials among other products.  Nippon Paper Industries Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.
JBIC - the Japan Bank for International Cooperation is a Japanese financial institution which formed from the merger of the Japan Export-Import Bank and the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund.

PT Rajawali Corpora is an investment holding company of the Rajawali Group, an Indonesian conglomerate active in a variety of industries, including telecommunications, hotels, consumer goods, retail, transportation, coal, gold and iron mining, and agriculture. The Group's agricultural activities comprise palm, sugar, rubber and corn plantations. Founded in 1984, the company is based in Jakarta and employs some 30,000 people. It was founded and is owned by Peter Sondakh, who is among the richest men in Indonesia and also ranks among the top billionaires globally. 
The company has a growing presence in the agricultural industry. PT Jaya Madiri Sukses (JMS Group) is the plantation arm of the Rajawali Group, and is a holding company comprising of a total of seven plantation companies in South and East Kalimantan. In 2010, Rajawali was reported to begin planting its 200,000 hectare land bank with oil palm. In 2011 Rajawali entered into a joint venture with commodities trader Louis Dreyfus called Green Eagle Plantations Pte Ltd. In 2012, the venture was reported to operate in four regions in Indonesia (South, West and East Kalimantan, and Papua), with concessions of around 50,000 hectares. However, in 2014, Louis Dreyfus Commodities Asia Pte left the joint venture, selling its 50% share of Green Eagle to the Rajawali Group. More recently, in September 2014, through a purchase of two investment firms, Matacuna Group and Pegasus CP One, Rajawali reportedly has acquired a 21% stake in crude palm oil producer, BW Plantation.

H&M Hennes and Mauritz AB is a Swedish clothing company operating under several brands, including its flagship brand H&M, as well as COS, Monki, Cheap Monday, and & Other Stories . The company, headquartered in Sweden, is involved in designing, manufacturing and marketing apparel, accessories and home textiles.  It was established in 1947, with the opening of its first Hennes store in VÃ¤sterÃ¥s, Sweden, which exclusively sold women's clothing. With the acquisition of hunting and fishing equipment store Mauritz Widforss in 1968, the company changed its name to Hennes & Mauritz and expanded its product range to also cover apparel for men and children. Since then, the company has expanded, opening stores throughout Europe as well as worldwide. For example, it expanded into the US in 2000, and opened stores in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 2007. Further to this, the company established a new brand, COS, in 2007 and acquired the fashion firm, FaBric Scandinavien AB, in 2008, which holds the Weekday, Monki and Cheap Monday brands . In 2010, the full incorporation of FaBric Scandinavien was completed, when Hennes & Mauritz acquired the remaining 40% of shares.
With more than 3,700 stores in 55 countries, Hennes & Mauritz is one of the largest retailers of private label apparel globally. The company's brands sell a wide range of products, including shoes and accessories. H&M does not directly own or operate any manufacturing facilities and instead sources its products from around 900 independent suppliers, mostly in Europe and Asia. For example, the company's suppliers include manufacturers and processors in China and Italy, and manufacturers in Thailand.
Sucafina was selected as a powerbroker for Coffee (Trader)

rows.coprofile: Woolworths is an Australian retailer with stores across Australia and New Zealand offering food products, general merchandise and a home improvement range. Globally it is one of the top 15 companies in the edible market, but it is also among the five largest in the APAC region. As a diverse retailer, Woolworths carries the risk of exposure to many forest risk commodities, predominantly palm oil and soy, but also timber, beef, leather and paper.   Woolworths Group Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

It is one of the world's largest retailers, and the breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities.   Ahold Delhaize is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum Deforestation resolution (being a member of the CGF is not sufficient)

rows.coprofile: Sodrugestvo Group, based in Luxembourg, is an agro-industrial company, which specialise in soybean and rapeseed processing, purchasing of grains and oilseeds and distribution of those products to the end consumer. Sodrugestvo Group S.A is selected as a powerbroker for soy.
WestRock manufactures and sells paper and packaging solutions on a global scale.  Westrock is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

US Bancorp are a bank and asset management company, headquartered in the US serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include: commercial banking, investment banking, asset management, mortgage, and trust and payment services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to over 450 billion USD with 270 billion USD worth of loans. Unicredit SPA are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 11 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors . They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 150, with shares worth more than 2.9 billion USD.

Oji Holdings is a corporation involved in the pulp and paper industry at a producing, processing and manufacturing level. Its products include packaging materials, household products, print materials and more. Oji Holdings has paper production facilities throughout China, but also has operations in numerous countries, including Indonesia and Laos, and also owns the Brazilian Fibria Celulose S.A.  Oji Holdings corporation is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

General Mills is an American company that manufactures and distributes baking products, ready meals, ice cream, cereals, snacks, soup, and yoghurt among other products through retail stores. Its operatations span 6 continent and it offers over 100 brands, including Yoplait, Betty Crocker, and Cheerios.  General Mills Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: COFCO is a leading agribusiness company in China producing, processing, manufacturing and trading in agricultural products and foodstuffs. It is one of the major players in the Chinese soy industry with two prominent Chinese subsidiaries. There are further processing facilities in Argentina and Brazil. The company is also a major exporter of soy from Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. COFCO’s animal feed production is among the largest globally. Another subsidiary has one of the largest forestry concessions in Gabon. The extent of its commodity trading and its food production also exposes the company to palm oil.  COFCO is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: Lloyds Banking Group plc are financial services group headquartered in the UK serving individual and commercial clients. Their services include banking (retail, commercial and corporate), insurance, pensions and investments. As of 2017, their total assets amount to over £810 billion with loans of over £450 billion. Lloyds Banking Group plc are in top 50 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 5.3 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Allianz are a global financial services provider headquartered in Germany serving both private and corporate clients. Their services include a wide array of insurance products, such as property, health and life insurance, as well as a large asset management business. As of 2024, Allianz have over 1,920 billion EUR in assets under management. They are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies. In the 2024 selection, Allianz was providing 19.2 USD to the Forest 500 companies.

rows.coprofile: Agrifirm is a Dutch cooperative comprising around 17,500 farmers and horticulturalists which provides agricultural products and services. The cooperative has several subsidiaries which expands its operations across Europe and into Russia and China. Agrifirm represents an important part of Europe's soya imports and is also an importer of palm oil. It is also among the top thirty animal feed producers in the world, for which soya is a major ingredient.

Natura Cosmeticos is a cosmetics company active throughout South America and which also has a consumer base in France. Its products range from make-up to fragrances and hair products, which exposes the company to forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soya. Natura Cosmeticos is one of the largest companies in Brazil for beauty and personal care as well as skin care.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, Natural Capital Coalition

rows.coprofile:
Natuzzi S.p.A. (Natuzzi) is the parent company of the Natuzzi Group, an Italian furniture company, established in 1959. It is involved in the design, manufacture, and marketing of furniture, and specialises in leather and upholstered products such as sofas, armchairs and other living room accessories. Cattle hides and wood are among the key raw materials used by Natuzzi in the manufacture of its products, and significantly, sales of leather-upholstered furniture comprised over 94% of the company's net sales and 85% of the company's revenue in 2013.
The group has numerous subsidiaries, registered worldwide, including in Brazil, China, Italy and elsewhere in Europe, Japan, Russia, India and Australia.
As a leader in leather upholstery and the largest furniture manufacturer overall in Italy, Natuzzi plays a key role in the international leather trade, with customs data revealing that the company imports significant volumes of leather from Brazil. Further to this, Natuzzi owns one active manufacturing facility in Brazil, which aims to increase local sourcing from 2014 onwards.
Natuzzi offers products under several brands: Natuzzi Italia; Natuzzi Editions, also known as Leather Editions; Natuzzi Re-vive; and private label. Natuzzi Editions is the group's brand focusing on the medium-high end of the market. It was developed and is sold solely in the US market and its products are manufactured in China, Brazil and Romania. The Leather Editions brand offers similar leather products to Natuzzi Editions, but is marketed in Europe and the rest of the world, apart from in North and South America. Natuzzi Re-vive, launched in 2013, sells Natuzzi branded performance recliners.  Finally, the company has developed private label products to maintain its competitiveness in the low-end market segment.
The group's furniture products are sold through a range of retail outlets worldwide, including: franchised stores, Divani & Divani by Natuzzi and Natuzzi, which are all located in Italy and Portugal; its Natuzzi Editions and Leather Editions stores; and also through several large global furniture retailers, such as IKEA, Macy's, and Nitori.

Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio with the RTL group, publishing with Penguin Random House, and magazines with Gruner + Jahr. The most important markets are the US and Western Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. In 2015, the group processed and traded more than 1.6 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.

With product lines spanning groceries, personal care items, apparel and furniture, Wal-Mart is exposed to a wide range of forest risk commodities, including palm oil, soy, beef, and timber. It is one of the largest producer of wooden furniture in the world, meaning that its operations require large amounts of timber. It is also exposed to leather in furniture, and soy and palm oil in its candles and food. IKEA Group is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and soy.

rows.coprofile: Aditya Birla Group is one of the largest conglomerates in India with operations in 34 countries. The group operates in sectors including fashion, cement, mobiles and viscose filament yarn.  Aditya Birla Group is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Salim Group is a large Indonesian conglomerate. Its subsidiary Indofood Agri is a vertically integrated agribusiness company spanning the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivation to product manufacturing and marketing. Products produced include cooking oils and margarines under several brands which are sold both directly and through retailers.  Salim Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Daiwa House Industry is a Japanese construction company, constructing residential homes and flats, business premises, and hotels. The group's core business is in Japan, but it is expanding into China, the US, Australia and Southeast Asia. It is one of the largest homebuilders in, which is an industry that uses large amounts of timber, and claims to have been the largest Japanese construction company in 2014 with over 2 million units constructed as of 2015.

The group has many well-known brands, including not only Louis Vuitton, Moët & Chandon and Hennessy, but also Givenchy, TAG Heuer and Dior, amongst others. LVMH’s primary revenue stream comes from its manufacture and sale of apparel and luggage, a trade which leaves it exposed to the forest risk commodity leather.  LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, leather and paper packaging.

Campbell Soup Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Tesco started as a market stall in London in 1919, selling surplus groceries; its first store was opened ten years later in 1929. Following growth in the UK, Tesco floated on the London Stock Exchange in 1947. Today, Tesco is a multichannel grocery retailer active in eleven countries across Europe and Asia and also provides consumer financial services through its subsidiary, Tesco Bank. The company employs over 510,000 individuals and receives over 80 million shopping trips per week globally. In addition to its core grocery offering, in which it sells own branded and private label goods, Tesco sell a very broad range of other products including clothing, electronics, books and furniture. As a result of its large size and broad product range Tesco uses a range of forest risk commodities including, soy, beef, timber, paper and palm oil. In 2014, Tesco used 32,503 tons palm oil used in own brand products.
initiatives: Consumer Goods Forum, New York Declaration on Forests, Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, UN Global Compact

rows.coprofile:
Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

rows.coprofile: Toronto-Dominion Bank are a financial services company, headquartered in Canada serving private and corporate clients. Their services cover: personal and small business banking, insurance, asset management, auto financing, investing, commercial and wholesale banking. As of 2017, they have over 1.2 billion CAD in total assets with 270 billion CAD in assets under management.  Toronto-Dominion Bank are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 9 billion USD. They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 50, with shares worth more than 7.5 billion USD.

Sekisui House Ltd has operations in the housing construction industry, and in real estate brokerage and leasing. The company was established in 1960 and has its headquarters in Osaka, Japan. It claims to be Japan's largest and best known home builder and is listed among the largest companies globally as the second largest Japanese construction services company. 
Sekisui House Ltd has numerous subsidiaries across its various business segments, which comprise trade, brokerage and lease of real estate; remodelling; construction; surveying; and others including financial services and manufacturing. The company operates 19 construction subsidiaries across Japan under Sekisui Construction Ltd and as of January 2014 had constructed almost 2.2 million houses. Sekisui House Ltd has also been active in the Australian market since 2009, under Sekisui House Australia.
Sekisui House Ltd specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing and is the main player in Japan's prefabrication industry. Specifically, Sekisui House Ltd constructs and sells steel- and wooden-frame housing. The company's steel-frame housing was launched in the 1970's, marking the entrance of Sekisui House into the housing industry. This was followed by the launch of the company' wooden frame unit housing, Two-U Home, in 1982. The company now builds a variety of wooden frame housing, for example, the Gravis Bella wooden frame model, in its detached housing business. On top of its initial construction activities, Sekisui House Ltd also offers interior decoration and furnishing services.
The major shareholder of Sekisui House Ltd is Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, which has operations worldwide and also has business interests in urban infrastructure, environmental products and high performance plastics.

rows.coprofile: The earliest foundations of the Oetker-Gruppe lie in 1891, when Dr August Oetker developed the baking powder, Backin, in Germany. The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. The Oetker-Gruppe sells its products to the consumer market under the brand, Dr Oetker. Its consumer products include; frozen pizzas, ready desserts and a number of other chilled and frozen products. Through the Martin Braun group, the Oetker-Gruppe sells a number of baking agents, glazes and decorations to baking and confectionary companies. The manufacturing of these products meant that the Oetker-Gruppe used 4,777 tonnes of palm oil or palm oil derivatives in 2013. Oetker-Gruppe has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011 and in 2012, four of its manufacturing facilities in Germany were certified as RSPO supply chain certified (all palm oil and palm oil derivatives used are RSPO-certified).

Wilmar International Ltd. is a global agribusiness group involved in the cultivation, processing, refining, merchandising and trading of a wide range of agricultural products, including palm oil and soy. The company is one of the world’s largest oil palm plantation owners and processors, reportedly controlling around 45% of worldwide palm oil trade sourced from more than 80% of global palm oil growers. Wilmar is also a major player in the soybean crushing industry with a global crushing capacity of 36 million metric tons per annum, the majority of which is in China. The company claims to be one of the world’s largest producers of consumer edible oils.   Wilmar International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Mewah International Inc. (Mewah) is one of the dominant palm oil traders globally. It started operating in the 1950s with imports of palm oil from Malaysia to Singapore and is now involved in the production and distribution of a range of edible oils and fats. In 1987, Mewah opened its first refinery in Malaysia, producing 400 million tonnes per day, and has now opened a further two refineries, increasing its yearly capacity to 2.8 million tonnes. Mewah sources its raw materials from Malaysia and Indonesia before selling to the consumer and commercial markets in over 100 countries. It sells palm, soya bean, lauric, coconut, canola corn and sunflower oils commercially, and edible oils and fats on the consumer market. Mewah's consumer products are distributed via a range of different regional brands, such as Oki, Mona and Fry-ola, making it the world's leading edible oil company.
Mewah is also a key producer of food grade packaging for commercial and consumer markets. To continue to expand its business, Mewah is aiming to consolidate its position within the palm-based oil and fats business, expand its consumer product range, invest in efficient production facilities and expand its distribution network,. This has involved the construction of a new refinery in Sabah, Malaysia, which will increase Mewah's productivity to 3.5 million tonnes per year, along with the purchase of a new biodiesel facility in Westport, Malaysiaiv. Mewah has complemented these acquisitions with the installation of a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia, costing around $50 million, to produce a range of dairy products.
Mewah has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2006 and it expects to achieve 100% RSPO certification of all supply chains by 2015.

RELX Group, headquartered in the UK, prints publications for a range of industries worldwide. The large-scale printing operations require a vast amount of pulp and paper.  RELX Group is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Minerva is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. Together, these facilities have the capacity to slaughter more than 17,000 heads of cattle a day as of 2016. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving individuals and companies. Their services include banking, trust banking, securities, credit cards, and leasing. As of 2017, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group's total assets amount to over 300 trillion Yen with over 100 trillion Yen in loans. They are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

CIMB Group is a Southeast Asian banking group, headquartered in Malaysia, serving private and commercial clients. Its services include corporate finance, treasury markets, investment banking, insurance, wealth management and retail banking. As of 2022, CIMB Group have 653 billion MYR in total assets. In the 2022 selection, CIMB Group was providing 1.6 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
Signatory to Net Zero Banking Alliance. CIMB Bank Berhad finances the Forest 500 with a total of 1035 USDM
Signatory to Net-Zero Asset Managers Initiative, Commitment letter signatories. Legal & General Investment Management finances the Forest 500 with a total of 43574 USDM
Essity is a Swedish company which manufacturers paper-based products including personal care, and hygiene products.  Essity is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Shiseido Co Ltd is a multi-brand company comprising 105 companies in the following business divisions: Cosmetics; Healthcare; Professional; Frontier Sciences (manufactures raw materials for cosmetics and drugs); Food (restaurant operations); and Other (education/welfare). It was founded in Japan in 1872 and has grown into a global business; today it operates a domestic line and a global line of products. The global line operates in Europe, the US and Asia and consists of the cosmetics business, which manufactures and sells cosmetics, cosmetic tools and toiletry products; and the professional business, which manufactures and sells products to hair and beauty salons in Japan and overseas. Shiseido Co Ltd products are sold in over 89 overseas territories.
In addition to brands bearing the Shiseido name, the group also has other brands (each with its own brand values) that have been obtained through acquisitions and licensing agreements. These include bareEssentials (mineral make-up), NARS (make-up), Jean Paul-Gautier (fragrance) and Issey Mayake (fragrance).

Goldman Sachs are a global investment bank and financial services firm headquartered in the US serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, underwriting, investments, securities and wealth management. As of 2017, Goldman Sachs' total assets amount to more than 900 billion USD, including more than 50 billion USD in loans. Goldman Sachs are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.
