Their services include retail banking, insurance, pensions, asset management and corporate lending. As of 2024, BBVA have 801 billion EUR in total assets. BBVA are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans to companies across several sectors, including food retail and packaged food. In the 2024 selection, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA) was providing 51 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Starbucks Corp. is the owner of the Starbucks chain of coffee stores and several other subsidiaries operating across the food and beverage industry. In 2015 Starbucks was ranked as the largest chain of coffee shops in the world by number of stores. In 2017 it had over 24,000 outlets in 70 countries. In addition to coffee, Starbucks Corp. also trades in teas, bottled drinks, baked goods, snacks and other food items. Its range of products and packaging leave it exposed to various forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy and paper.   Starbucks Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

DBS are a financial services group headquartered in Singapore serving private and commercial clients. Their services include wealth management, corporate finance, institutional investment, insurance, and retail banking services. As of 2022, the group’s total assets amount to more than 745 billion SDG. In the 2022 selection, DBS was providing 7.9 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

ABN Amro is a Dutch bank engaged in providing banking products and services. The bank serves the retail, private banking and corporate banking sectors. In the 2022 selection, ABN Amro was providing 4.2 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Empresas CMPC S.A. is a Chilean-based producer of forest products. The company operates in the businesses of forestry, pulp and paper, tissue and other products which includes the production of paper-manufacture products. As of 2019, CMPC owns around 648,000 hectares of forest plantations across Latin America.

Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) is a leading processor and trader in agricultural commodities active in more than 100 countries. It is one of the major processors and exporters of soya in South America and one of the largest commodity traders globally. The company has significant oilseed crushing facilities in Brazil and Argentina, as well as having an annual capacity of several million metric tons in China. LDC is among the top ten soya exporters in Argentina and among the top five in Paraguay and Brazil. The company's palm oil operations are also significant with the company handling over 2 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives in 2015. It is also a major producer of biodiesel.

Felda Global Ventures (FGV) is a Malaysian group of agribusiness companies active in the palm, rubber, sugar, and agri-services industries. The group is involved in both the cultivation and processing of oil palm as well as in the manufacturing of palm oil goods. In 2015, FGV had a total oil palm landbank of over 750,000 hectares across Indonesia and Malaysia which is one of the five largest landbanks for palm oil in the world. It also has major processing operations, processing about 15 million fresh fruit bunches in 2015, and claims to be the largest producer of crude palm oil in the world, producing more than 3 million metric tons in the same year.

Goldman Sachs are a global investment bank and financial services firm headquartered in the US serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, underwriting, investments, securities and wealth management. As of 2017, Goldman Sachs' total assets amount to more than 900 billion USD, including more than 50 billion USD in loans. Goldman Sachs are among the top 10 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 45 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 30 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 12 billion USD worth of shares.

The first Walmart store opened in 1962 in Arkansas, US. The company floated in 1970 and since then has grown within the US and internationally. Now, in 2014, Walmart operates 11,500 stores, under 65 banners, in 28 countries and employs 2.2 million members of staff. Walmart is one of the world's largest retailers.
Walmart operates in four segments: Walmart US, Walmart International, Sam's Club and Global e-Commerce. Within the US, Walmart operates stores in a variety of different formats, the largest is the Supercenter. The approximately 180,000 square foot Supercenters provide grocery, fresh produce, clothing, electronics and home furnishings. Some Supercenters also include pharmacies, health clinics, restaurants and banks. At the other end of the scale Walmart's smallest format, Express stores, focus on groceries and general merchandise. Sam's Club is a wholesaler catering to consumer and small business members who want to buy both groceries and general merchandise in bulk. Sam's Club operates in the US and internationally.
Walmart is present in 27 countries outside of the US, operating grocery and retail operations both through wholly owned subsidiaries and joint ventures. Stores operate under Walmart and other banners: in the UK Walmart operates through ASDA; and in Asia (India, Japan and China) Walmart operates under banners such as Walmart and Seiyu. Walmart's 2011 acquisition of a majority stake of in Massmart Holdings Limited also gives it a presence in sub-Saharan Africa; the majority of its 350 stores are in South Africa. Walmart also operates throughout Latin America, again under both Walmart and local banners.
Walmart sells both private label and international brand goods. As one of the world's largest retailers,  Walmart uses significant volumes of forest risk commodities including beef, leather, pulp and paper, timber, soy and palm oil. In 2014, Walmart used 96,411 MT of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in its own brand products.

Sekisui House Ltd has operations in the housing construction industry, and in real estate brokerage and leasing. The company was established in 1960 and has its headquarters in Osaka, Japan. It claims to be Japan's largest and best known home builder and is listed among the largest companies globally as the second largest Japanese construction services company. 
Sekisui House Ltd has numerous subsidiaries across its various business segments, which comprise trade, brokerage and lease of real estate; remodelling; construction; surveying; and others including financial services and manufacturing. The company operates 19 construction subsidiaries across Japan under Sekisui Construction Ltd and as of January 2014 had constructed almost 2.2 million houses. Sekisui House Ltd has also been active in the Australian market since 2009, under Sekisui House Australia.
Sekisui House Ltd specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing and is the main player in Japan's prefabrication industry. Specifically, Sekisui House Ltd constructs and sells steel- and wooden-frame housing. The company's steel-frame housing was launched in the 1970's, marking the entrance of Sekisui House into the housing industry. This was followed by the launch of the company' wooden frame unit housing, Two-U Home, in 1982. The company now builds a variety of wooden frame housing, for example, the Gravis Bella wooden frame model, in its detached housing business. On top of its initial construction activities, Sekisui House Ltd also offers interior decoration and furnishing services.
The major shareholder of Sekisui House Ltd is Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, which has operations worldwide and also has business interests in urban infrastructure, environmental products and high performance plastics.

Natura & Co Holding SA is a Brazil-based personal care cosmetics manufacturer and sellers, made up of subsidaries including The Body Shop, Avon, and Aesop. Natura &Co operates in more than 100 countries, with over 3,700 stores. Its products range from make-up to fragrances and hair products, which exposes the company to forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soy. Natura&Co is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group's two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.6 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.
initiatives: Tropical Forest Alliance 2020 partner, UN Global Compact, New York Declaration on Forests, High Conservation Value Resource Network

rows.coprofile: Deutsche Bank are a major bank based in Germany serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, securities, wealth management, asset management, and retail banking services. As of 2024, the bank's total assets amount to more than 1.6 trillion EUR. Deutsche Bank is among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Deutsche Bank was providing 182 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Groupe Avril is an agro-industrial and financial group operating its business within the animal nutrition, renewable energy, food and chemistry sectors.  Groupe Avril is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd is a holding company for the Nippon Paper Group, which is comprised of around 180 affiliates and subsidiaries. The Group ranks among the top forest, paper and packaging companies globally, occupying sixth place in a worldwide ranking of the top 100 and the second position of such companies in Japan. The Group produces a variety of paper products, including newsprint, printing paper, copy paper, wrapping paper, linerboard, paperboard, tissue products, and healthcare products. For example, through its subsidiary Nippon Paper Crecia Co Ltd, the Group manufactures family care, personal care and professional products under a license agreement with leading hygiene products company, Kimberly-Clark.
The Group has diverse business interests on top of its activities in the paper sector, and several of Nippon Paper Groups's other operations also make use of wood products. For example, it has several subsidiaries active in the wood products and construction industry; in the procurement of lumber and the manufacture of construction materials. These subsidiaries include Nippon Paper Lumber Co., Ltd., PAL Co., Ltd., and Daishowa Uniboard Co., Ltd. Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd has a global network supplying logs and lumber from a variety of sources, including domestically and from the United States, Canada, Europe, New Zealand and some tropical regions. As well as supplying raw and sawn timber, Nippon Paper Lumber Co Ltd also manufactures plywood and laminated lumber products. Pal Co Ltd and Daishowa Uniboard Co Ltd manufacture products for use in the construction industry, such as doors, staircases, flooring and decorative laminates.
Fast Retailing are a Japanese clothing retailer operating through well-known brands such as UNIQLO and J Brand.

DLG Denmark, established in 1964, is one of Europe's biggest agricultural companies. It is owned by 30,000 Danish farmers and employs 7,500 people, 3,000 of whom are in Denmark. Through over 40 subsidiaries and associated companies, DLG Denmark is involved in a broad range of business and consumer sectors, with localised operations in in more than 20 countries. 
DLG Denmark is organised into four business areas: Premix and Nutrition, accounting for 4% of turnover, provides specialist animal feeds and minerals; Service and Energy, contributing 28% of turnover, provides a broad range of products and services including fuels, telecommunications and IT, and also operates DIY stores and petrol stations; Machinery, Flowers and Food, which accounts for 6% of turnover, provides industrial and agricultural machinery as well as a broad range of plants and food products, including oils and vegetables; and Farm Supply, the largest division, providing 62% turnover, encompasses animal feed production, poultry hatcheries, provision of fertiliser and pesticides, and crop production.
DLG Denmark produces compound feeds for farm animals at its mills in Europe and is one of Europe's top five largest producers of compound feeds. Soya is a significant feed production ingredient, accounting for around 15 to 20% composition. Consequently, DLG Denmark buys around half of Denmark's soymeal. DLG Denmark uses a similar amount of palm oil in its animal feed.

Kencana Agri is a palm oil plantation company based in Indonesia.  The Company has various oil palm estates, palm oil mills, kernel crushing plants, port and bulking terminals, and biomass power plant across Indonesia. Its subsidiaries include Kencana Logistics Pte. Ltd, and Kencana Plantations Pte. Ltd. Kencana Agri Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.
International Paper is one of the leading producers of fiber-based packaging, as well as pulp and paper, in the world.  International Paper is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

rows.coprofile: Mondelez International is an American manufacturer of snacks. The company sells chocolate, biscuits, beverages, candy, and meals. Some of the famous brands in Mondelez’s portfolio include Cadbury, Belvita, Mika, Ritz, and Oreo. According to the company, it is are one of the biggest snack companies in the world. Through its products Mondelez are exposed to palm oil and soy.  Mondelez International Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución is a forestry conglomerate based in Chile producing and trading in wood and timber products. The company is controlled by the Angelini Group through holding company, Empresas COPEC.  Angelini Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and is also assessed for its exposure to pulp & paper.

Nine Dragons Paper Holdings Ltd (ND Paper) is a paper and paper packaging manufacturer that produces a variety of containerboard and paper products, including: linerboard; corrugating medium and coated duplex board; recycled printing and writing paper; and tissue paper. As well as paper products, ND Paper manufactures wood-, bamboo-, and unbleached kraft pulp. The company's products are manufactured under three brands: Nine Dragons, Land Dragon and Sea Dragon, each focusing on a different customer segment.  ND Paper is well known for its use of recovered paper; the company's main source of raw material. This is used in the manufacturing of some of its products, such as its testlinerboard, made from 100% recovered paper, and its Sea Dragon office paper. The company imports significant amounts of recovered paper from the US; however, this is not used exclusively in all products.
The company was established in 1995 and is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies, ranking among the top 30 globally and holding the leading position in China. ND Paper has six manufacturing bases across China, as well as in Vietnam and Mongolia, through joint ventures: Cheng Yang Paper and Nine Dragons Xing An Pulp & Paper (Inner Mongolia) Co Ltd. Originally, the company predominantly supplied packaging for manufacturers in southern China's export oriented industry; however, the business has increasingly tapped into the demand for packaging products from the domestic market as China's own consumer-demand has grown.

Nordea Bank AB are a financial services group with headquarters in Sweden serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include: private banking, investment banking, securities, wealth management, asset management, capital markets, pensions and retail banking services. As of 2017, Nordea Bank AB's total assets amount to more than 600 billion EUR, with approximately 330 billion EUR in loans. Nordea Bank AB are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies.

rows.coprofile: The Hershey Company (Hershey's) was incorporated in Delaware, US in 1927, as a successor to a business founded in Philadelphia in 1894 by Milton S. Hershey. Today, the company sells and distributes its products in around 70 countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia. It claims to be the top chocolate and confectionary company in US by market share, where over 85% of Hershey's consolidated revenue is generated. Outside the US, the company's main countries of operation are Canada, Mexico, Brazil, China, India, Korea, and Japan. The company has 22,000 employees around the world and an annual turnover of over $7.4 billion. Hershey's has more than 80 brands  including Reese's, Mound, Almond Joy, Twizzlers , and it also shares a licensing agreement with Nestle to produce KitKat in America .  It has been a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member since 2011 and used 23,967 tonnes of palm oil in 2014, 100% of which is RSPO certified. Hershey's is focusing on expanding its business both through entry into new markets, such as the meat snack market through the acquisition of KRAVE Pure Foods, Inc., in March 2015, and through consolidating its operations in markets outside the US, such as through its acquisition in September 2015 of the remaining 49% of shares in its Bauducco/Pandurata Alimentos SA distribution joint venture in Brazil.

Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA) are a global financial services group based in Spain with activities in corporate, retail and investment banking. Their services include retail banking, insurance, pensions, asset management and corporate lending. As of 2024, BBVA have 801 billion EUR in total assets. BBVA are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans to companies across several sectors, including food retail and packaged food. In the 2024 selection, Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA) was providing 51 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Hengan International is a Chinese manufacturer of paper products including sanitary napkins, disposable nappies and tissue paper.  Hengan International Group Co Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Natuzzi S.p.A. (Natuzzi) is the parent company of the Natuzzi Group, an Italian furniture company, established in 1959. It is involved in the design, manufacture, and marketing of furniture, and specialises in leather and upholstered products such as sofas, armchairs and other living room accessories. Cattle hides and wood are among the key raw materials used by Natuzzi in the manufacture of its products, and significantly, sales of leather-upholstered furniture comprised over 94% of the company's net sales and 85% of the company's revenue in 2013.
The group has numerous subsidiaries, registered worldwide, including in Brazil, China, Italy and elsewhere in Europe, Japan, Russia, India and Australia.
As a leader in leather upholstery and the largest furniture manufacturer overall in Italy, Natuzzi plays a key role in the international leather trade, with customs data revealing that the company imports significant volumes of leather from Brazil. Further to this, Natuzzi owns one active manufacturing facility in Brazil, which aims to increase local sourcing from 2014 onwards.
Natuzzi offers products under several brands: Natuzzi Italia; Natuzzi Editions, also known as Leather Editions; Natuzzi Re-vive; and private label. Natuzzi Editions is the group's brand focusing on the medium-high end of the market. It was developed and is sold solely in the US market and its products are manufactured in China, Brazil and Romania. The Leather Editions brand offers similar leather products to Natuzzi Editions, but is marketed in Europe and the rest of the world, apart from in North and South America. Natuzzi Re-vive, launched in 2013, sells Natuzzi branded performance recliners.  Finally, the company has developed private label products to maintain its competitiveness in the low-end market segment.
The group's furniture products are sold through a range of retail outlets worldwide, including: franchised stores, Divani & Divani by Natuzzi and Natuzzi, which are all located in Italy and Portugal; its Natuzzi Editions and Leather Editions stores; and also through several large global furniture retailers, such as IKEA, Macy's, and Nitori.

Since its spinoff from PepsiCo. in 1997, Yum! Brands has expanded significantly internationally, with 65% of its profits now coming from non-US markets in 2015 compared to just 20% in 1997. In 2016, Yum! Brands opens on average over six new restaurants a day worldwide.
Yum! Brands' chicken restaurant chain, KFC, has 18,000 outlets in 115 countries and territories, serving over 12 million customers each day. Taco Bell serves Mexican style food through around 6,100 outlets in the US, serving more than 40 million customers each week. However, Yum! Brands is looking to expand the chain globally and currently has around 300 stores in 20 countries outside the US. By the end of 2014, there were over 15,600 Pizza Hut restaurants around the world.
Yum! Brands franchisees and company operated restaurants are significant purchasers of chicken, cheese, beef and pork products as well as paper and packaging materials. All three restaurant brands use palm oil, soy and beef in a variety of different products.

Mewah International Inc. (Mewah) is one of the dominant palm oil traders globally. It started operating in the 1950s with imports of palm oil from Malaysia to Singapore and is now involved in the production and distribution of a range of edible oils and fats. In 1987, Mewah opened its first refinery in Malaysia, producing 400 million tonnes per day, and has now opened a further two refineries, increasing its yearly capacity to 2.8 million tonnes. Mewah sources its raw materials from Malaysia and Indonesia before selling to the consumer and commercial markets in over 100 countries. It sells palm, soya bean, lauric, coconut, canola corn and sunflower oils commercially, and edible oils and fats on the consumer market. Mewah's consumer products are distributed via a range of different regional brands, such as Oki, Mona and Fry-ola, making it the world's leading edible oil company.
Mewah is also a key producer of food grade packaging for commercial and consumer markets. To continue to expand its business, Mewah is aiming to consolidate its position within the palm-based oil and fats business, expand its consumer product range, invest in efficient production facilities and expand its distribution network,. This has involved the construction of a new refinery in Sabah, Malaysia, which will increase Mewah's productivity to 3.5 million tonnes per year, along with the purchase of a new biodiesel facility in Westport, Malaysiaiv. Mewah has complemented these acquisitions with the installation of a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia, costing around $50 million, to produce a range of dairy products.
Mewah has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2006 and it expects to achieve 100% RSPO certification of all supply chains by 2015.

Wendy's restaurants specialise in hamburgers and sandwiches but also offer fries, salads and desserts. The majority of the company's restaurants are in North America; in 2014, 6,112 restaurants operated in the US and Canada, with the majority run by franchises. De Heus was founded in 1911 and has grown from a regional Dutch feed manufacturer into an international conglomerate. It is now Europe's fourth largest compound animal feed producer and cites itself as a global top 15 animal feed supplier. The company has activities in over 50 countries in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa and employs 3,000 people worldwide, operating around 30 feed mills. De Heus is still owned and managed by the De Heus Family.
De Heus manufactures feed for cattle, pigs, poultry and aquaculture; it also provides customised feed for individual farms. Subsidiaries include: Koudijis Animal Nutrition, which exports feed and related products to other European countries, Middle Eastern and African markets; and Agra-Matic, an agricultural consultancy operating in the Netherlands and Poland, providing advice in a number of areas including animal husbandry, the environment, technology and planning.
De Heus has focused upon expansion outside of Europe and entered a number of markets by establishing joint ventures in countries including China, Russia, Belgium, Ethiopia and Egypt. Further examples include an agreement with Brazilian firm, Nutrifarms LTDA, signed 2012, giving De Heus access to the Brazilian pig feed market. Investments expanding the company's infrastructure outside of Europe have also intensified DeHeus' international operations. For example, in 2013, the company opened a fourth feed factory in South Africa, manufacturing feed for not only traditional livestock but also ostrich and game. De Heus is currently investing in Vietnam, looking to become one of the top five largest feed producers. In March 2015, the company announced the opening of two new factories. Construction of a seventh Vietnamese factory is underway; a project that will cost around $30 million.

Yildiz Holding is a Turkish conglomerate active in the manufacturing of food products with operations around the world. Inditex SA owns the clothing and accessories retail brands Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Uterque and Zara Home. This Spanish company, formed by Amancio Ortega Gaona in 1963, is amongst the largest fashion retailers in the world, with a revenue of over €16 billion 2013.
Inditex SA started business with Zara in 1963, which is the largest and best known of all the company's brands; selling leather shoes and handbags, as well as mid-range clothes to men, women and children. Inditex was incorporated as the group's holding company in 1985 and in 1991 other brands were incorporated into the group. Today, Inditex has more than 6,000 stores in 88 countries around the world, with recent expansions into China and Russia. Outside of Zara, its other brands cover a wide range of markets, for example, Uterque is a dedicated accessory store, and Berksha and Pull&Bear target younger audiences.
Almost 90% of Inditex' suppliers come from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, India, South East Asia, Bangladesh, China, Brazil and Argentina, with over half of the company's manufacturing taking place in Spain or nearby countries, including Turkey and Morocco. This allows the company to respond to in-store demands and trends quickly, a model that has been dubbed 'Fast Fashion'. The company sells a range of apparel and accessories, including leather products, and notably, ranks in the top ten footwear companies in the western European market.

Tesco started as a market stall in London in 1919, selling surplus groceries; its first store was opened ten years later in 1929. Following growth in the UK, Tesco floated on the London Stock Exchange in 1947. Today, Tesco is a multichannel grocery retailer active in eleven countries across Europe and Asia and also provides consumer financial services through its subsidiary, Tesco Bank. The company employs over 510,000 individuals and receives over 80 million shopping trips per week globally. In addition to its core grocery offering, in which it sells own branded and private label goods, Tesco sell a very broad range of other products including clothing, electronics, books and furniture. As a result of its large size and broad product range Tesco uses a range of forest risk commodities including, soy, beef, timber, paper and palm oil. In 2014, Tesco used 32,503 tons palm oil used in own brand products.

First Resources sells a range of products including oleochemicals, biodiesel and palm kernel expeller which is used as animal feed.  Eight Capital is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Beiersdorf is one of the top global players for sun care, beauty and personal care and skincare. Target Corporation is a general merchandise retailer operating in the US. Established in 1902 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, it is one of North America's retail giants, ranking among the top fifty in the Fortune 500. Target offers a variety of products including: food, beauty and personal care items; cleaning and paper products; as well as apparel and furniture, among other products. The company operates over 1,792 stores in the US as well as 38 distribution centres. Target began operating stores in Canada in 2011 through the acquisition of Zellers; however in 2015 the company planned to discontinue operating stores in the country.
A significant component of Target's sales are made up of its owned and exclusive branded products, which account for around one third of the company's total sales. Its owned branded products include: Archers Farms groceries; luggage; travel accessories; furniture; other goods sold under the Embark brand; Smith & Hawken outdoor furniture; Sutton & Dodge meat products; and up & up health and beauty products.

LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA (LVMH) is a French company, with its headquarters in Paris, engaged in the luxury goods industry. The group was formed following the merger of the MoÃ«t Hennessy and Louis Vuitton companies in 1987; however its origins extend back much further in the history of the development of the French luxury goods industry. Louis Vuitton's flagship brand was launched in 1854, after which it continued to specialise solely in handmade leather bags for over 70 years, while, Moet Hennessy's origins are even earlier, as the company was involved in the wine industry for 100 years prior.
LVMH currently operates in five main segments: wines and spirits; fashion and leather goods; perfumes and cosmetics; watches and jewellery; and selective retailing. Within these five sectors, LVMH has a portfolio of more than 60 brands and an international network of more than 3,000 stores. Of particular importance is the company's fashion and leather goods division, which comprises well-known luggage, leather goods and apparel and accessories brands, such as Louis Vuitton, Givenchy and Marc Jacobs.
In 2013, the fashion and leather goods business accounted for the majority of the group's total revenue. The group is an industry leader in the bags and luggage market worldwide, occupying the top position globally in terms of market share and leading positions in the individual markets of China, Western Europe and the USA.

Its products are marketed principally under the company's own brands, within five business divisions: Outdoor and Action Sports, Jeanswear, Imagewear, Sportswear and Contemporary Brands. VF has a diverse portfolio of brands, including well-known names, such as outdoor apparel brand, The North Face, footwear, apparel and accessories brand, Timberland, and luggage and bag brands, Eastpak, JanSport and Kipling. In addition to brands bearing the Shiseido name, the group also has other brands (each with its own brand values) that have been obtained through acquisitions and licensing agreements. Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV (Grupo Bimbo) was founded by Lorenzo Servitje in Mexico in 1945. International expansion began in 1989, resulting in Grupo Bimbo becoming the largest bakery company in the world in terms of sales and production volume. The company's main markets are the US and Mexico but it also operates in Central and Latin America, Canada, Asia and Europe. In 2014, net sales were $14.1 billion. The company has 167 manufacturing plants located largely in its key markets, with 85 plants in the US and 39 in Mexico. In addition to its global manufacturing facilities, the company operates a distribution network with over 52,000 routes, feeding into 2.2 million points of sale in 19 countries. Today, Grupo Bimbo employs over 21,000 individuals.
Grupo Bimbo produces more than 10,000 different products under 100 umbrella brands including Bimbo, New York Bakery Co., Marisela and Ricolino. It manufactures bread, potato crisps, pastries and a variety of other snacks, many of which contain palm oil. The company continues to expand its business in international markets; it recently completed the acquisition of the previously public-listed company, Canada Bread, for $1.83 billion.

Asics Corporation was founded in 1949 in Kobe, Japan. It was incorporated twenty years later through the merger of three companies: Onitsuka, GTO and JELENK. The company has two business segments: sports product manufacture and sales; and outdoor products manufacture and sales. The sports segment is involved in the manufacture and sale of sportswear, sports shoes and equipment. This part of the business also oversees the management and delivery of products, the planning of products, and the factoring and sales support businesses. The other business segment is focused on the manufacture and sale of outdoor products through its subsidiaries, of which it has more than 50 globally. Asics Corporation employs more than 7,400 people worldwide.
Asics Corporation is among the top ten manufacturers of footwear globally and is particularly well known for its running shoes, which are marketed to both professional and amateur athletes.  The company is therefore a significant user of leather. Asics Corporation operates a number of flagship stores and the expansion of its retail network is a key strategy for the company. The company promotes its brands through participation in a number of high profile sporting events, for example through its sponsorship of major marathons and the use of Asics equipment by top sporting teams and federations on the world stage. On top of the Asics brand, the company sells fashion-oriented items under the Onitsuka Tiger brand.
Sampoerna Agri Resources Pte. Ltd was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Producer), Rubber (Producer) and is also assessed for Palm oil (Processor)
Triputra Group was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Processor, Producer), Rubber (Processor) and is also assessed for Rubber (Producer)

COFCO is a leading agribusiness company in China producing, processing, manufacturing and trading in agricultural products and foodstuffs. It is one of the major players in the Chinese soy industry with two prominent Chinese subsidiaries. There are further processing facilities in Argentina and Brazil. The company is also a major exporter of soy from Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. COFCO’s animal feed production is among the largest globally. Another subsidiary has one of the largest forestry concessions in Gabon. The extent of its commodity trading and its food production also exposes the company to palm oil.  COFCO is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Inditex SA owns the clothing and accessories retail brands Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Uterque and Zara Home. This Spanish company, formed by Amancio Ortega Gaona in 1963, is amongst the largest fashion retailers in the world, with a revenue of over €16 billion 2013.
Inditex SA started business with Zara in 1963, which is the largest and best known of all the company's brands; selling leather shoes and handbags, as well as mid-range clothes to men, women and children. Inditex was incorporated as the group's holding company in 1985 and in 1991 other brands were incorporated into the group. Today, Inditex has more than 6,000 stores in 88 countries around the world, with recent expansions into China and Russia. Outside of Zara, its other brands cover a wide range of markets, for example, Uterque is a dedicated accessory store, and Berksha and Pull&Bear target younger audiences.
Almost 90% of Inditex' suppliers come from Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Turkey, India, South East Asia, Bangladesh, China, Brazil and Argentina, with over half of the company's manufacturing taking place in Spain or nearby countries, including Turkey and Morocco. This allows the company to respond to in-store demands and trends quickly, a model that has been dubbed 'Fast Fashion'. The company sells a range of apparel and accessories, including leather products, and notably, ranks in the top ten footwear companies in the western European market.

The Kraft Heinz Company is a food and beverage company headquartered in North America but operating in over 45 countries. The company was formed in 2015 by a merger between Kraft Food Group, Inc. and H.J. Heinz Holding Corporation. According to the company, it is the third largest food and beverage company in North America and the fifth largest globally. The company has more than 200 brands sold in nearly 200 countries, with eight brands worth over $1 billion. Iconic brand names include Kraft, Heinz, Kool-Aid, Oscar Mayer and Planters.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

Precious Woods is a Swiss based company involved in the cultivation, processing and trading of tropical timber. It manages forests in both Brazil and Gabon. In 2016, its Brazilian forestry concessions amounted to more than 500,000 hectares, making Precious Woods one of the largest Brazilian forestry companies. In Gabon, Precious Woods' forestry concessions total more than 600,000 hectares as of 2016. The company has sawmills and manufacturing facilities in both regions, which processed more than 200,000 cubic metres of timber in 2015. Precious Woods is also a major timber trader in Europe.

Sekisui House Ltd has operations in the housing construction industry, and in real estate brokerage and leasing. The company was established in 1960 and has its headquarters in Osaka, Japan. It claims to be Japan's largest and best known home builder and is listed among the largest companies globally as the second largest Japanese construction services company. 
Sekisui House Ltd has numerous subsidiaries across its various business segments, which comprise trade, brokerage and lease of real estate; remodelling; construction; surveying; and others including financial services and manufacturing. The company operates 19 construction subsidiaries across Japan under Sekisui Construction Ltd and as of January 2014 had constructed almost 2.2 million houses. Sekisui House Ltd has also been active in the Australian market since 2009, under Sekisui House Australia.
Sekisui House Ltd specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing and is the main player in Japan's prefabrication industry. Specifically, Sekisui House Ltd constructs and sells steel- and wooden-frame housing. The company's steel-frame housing was launched in the 1970's, marking the entrance of Sekisui House into the housing industry. This was followed by the launch of the company' wooden frame unit housing, Two-U Home, in 1982. The company now builds a variety of wooden frame housing, for example, the Gravis Bella wooden frame model, in its detached housing business. On top of its initial construction activities, Sekisui House Ltd also offers interior decoration and furnishing services.
The major shareholder of Sekisui House Ltd is Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, which has operations worldwide and also has business interests in urban infrastructure, environmental products and high performance plastics.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

Samling Global Ltd group of companies is a Malaysian conglomerate with diverse operations, including in the timber and oil palm sectors.  Founded in 1963, Samling's core activities are in the forest products industry, where its operations span the length of the supply chain, from harvesting to processing, manufacturing and distribution.
Samling Global Ltd has a complicated corporate structure, with numerous subsidiaries and holding companies.  For example, Samling Global Ltd is an investment holding company incorporated in Bermuda, with numerous wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, the US, the British Virgin Islands and Japan. These companies in turn have a variety of subsidiaries, for example, in China, Malaysia, Guyana, Indonesia and India.
Of particular relevance, is Samling Global Ltd's involvement in the timber trade in Sarawak, Malaysia. Under Lingui Developments Bhd, Samling manages a total of 1.3 million hectares. Lingui Developments Bhd is an investment holding and forest resources and wood products company. It produces logs, plywood and veneer, fibreboard, doors and door facings, and kitchen counters and products, primarily for the export market and in particular for Japan, China, India, Korea and North America. Under its wholly owned subsidiary, Barama Company Ltd, Samling Global Ltd is also one of the biggest forestry companies in Guyana, where it holds 1.6 million hectares of forest concessions and produces sawnwood.
Samling Global Ltd is well established in the export markets of China and Japan. In China, it manufactures plywood, laminated veneer lumber and flooring and also distributes flooring through Elegant Living, one of China's major flooring distributors. Samling Global Ltd's access to the Japanese market is facilitated through its partnerships with Itochu Corporation, one of Japan's major traders and property developers, and Daiken Corporation, through which Samling Global Ltd supplies tropical logs and plywood for construction.
Samling Global Ltd has also expanded its operations into oil palm. Under Glenealy Plantations (Malaya) Bhd, it has plantations in Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, covering a total area of over 60,000 hectares; and also operates palm oil mills in Sabah and Sarawak. Samling Global Ltd is also part of a consortium developing acacia plantations in Malaysia to supply wood for the pulp and paper industry. This consortium is made up of Samling Strategic Corp Sdn Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, and KTS Timber Industries Bhd, all of which are major timber companies in Sarawak.

The company is also a significant player in the global leather industry, with over twenty tanneries in Brazil alone.  JBS is selected as a powerbroker for soy, beef, leather and paper packaging.

VF Corp (VF) is a US-based global apparel company, manufacturing and supplying apparel, footwear and accessories. Headquartered in North Carolina, in the US, VF's products are sold in more than 150 countries worldwide, through 47,000 retail outlets and 1,100 of the company's own stores.
Its products are marketed principally under the company's own brands, within five business divisions: Outdoor and Action Sports, Jeanswear, Imagewear, Sportswear and Contemporary Brands. VF has a diverse portfolio of brands, including well-known names, such as outdoor apparel brand, The North Face, footwear, apparel and accessories brand, Timberland, and luggage and bag brands, Eastpak, JanSport and Kipling. The company produces around 450 million items per year, and operates manufacturing facilities in the Middle East, Europe, Mexico, and Central and South America. As these facilities meet only a proportion of the company's production needs, especially for the company's footwear production, VF sources products from around 1,900 independently and company-run facilities. VF sources raw materials, including leather, from multiple international suppliers.
VF Corp is a leader in the global bags and luggage market, ranking in the top ten globally and occupying a leading position in the US, where it ranks third by market share. DLG Denmark, established in 1964, is one of Europe's biggest agricultural companies. It is owned by 30,000 Danish farmers and employs 7,500 people, 3,000 of whom are in Denmark. Through over 40 subsidiaries and associated companies, DLG Denmark is involved in a broad range of business and consumer sectors, with localised operations in in more than 20 countries. 
DLG Denmark is organised into four business areas: Premix and Nutrition, accounting for 4% of turnover, provides specialist animal feeds and minerals; Service and Energy, contributing 28% of turnover, provides a broad range of products and services including fuels, telecommunications and IT, and also operates DIY stores and petrol stations; Machinery, Flowers and Food, which accounts for 6% of turnover, provides industrial and agricultural machinery as well as a broad range of plants and food products, including oils and vegetables; and Farm Supply, the largest division, providing 62% turnover, encompasses animal feed production, poultry hatcheries, provision of fertiliser and pesticides, and crop production.
DLG Denmark produces compound feeds for farm animals at its mills in Europe and is one of Europe's top five largest producers of compound feeds. Soya is a significant feed production ingredient, accounting for around 15 to 20% composition. Consequently, DLG Denmark buys around half of Denmark's soymeal. DLG Denmark uses a similar amount of palm oil in its animal feed.

Natuzzi S.p.A. (Natuzzi) is the parent company of the Natuzzi Group, an Italian furniture company, established in 1959. It is involved in the design, manufacture, and marketing of furniture, and specialises in leather and upholstered products such as sofas, armchairs and other living room accessories. Cattle hides and wood are among the key raw materials used by Natuzzi in the manufacture of its products, and significantly, sales of leather-upholstered furniture comprised over 94% of the company's net sales and 85% of the company's revenue in 2013.
The group has numerous subsidiaries, registered worldwide, including in Brazil, China, Italy and elsewhere in Europe, Japan, Russia, India and Australia.
As a leader in leather upholstery and the largest furniture manufacturer overall in Italy, Natuzzi plays a key role in the international leather trade, with customs data revealing that the company imports significant volumes of leather from Brazil. Further to this, Natuzzi owns one active manufacturing facility in Brazil, which aims to increase local sourcing from 2014 onwards.
Natuzzi offers products under several brands: Natuzzi Italia; Natuzzi Editions, also known as Leather Editions; Natuzzi Re-vive; and private label. Natuzzi Editions is the group's brand focusing on the medium-high end of the market. It was developed and is sold solely in the US market and its products are manufactured in China, Brazil and Romania. The Leather Editions brand offers similar leather products to Natuzzi Editions, but is marketed in Europe and the rest of the world, apart from in North and South America. Natuzzi Re-vive, launched in 2013, sells Natuzzi branded performance recliners.  Finally, the company has developed private label products to maintain its competitiveness in the low-end market segment.
The group's furniture products are sold through a range of retail outlets worldwide, including: franchised stores, Divani & Divani by Natuzzi and Natuzzi, which are all located in Italy and Portugal; its Natuzzi Editions and Leather Editions stores; and also through several large global furniture retailers, such as IKEA, Macy's, and Nitori.

COFCO Group was founded in 1949 and operates in the edible seed market via China Agri Holdings Ltd. It is the second largest crusher of oilseeds (behind Wilmar International) and has 13% of the market share of oilseed crushing capability and over 9% of the market share for soybeans. Its manufacturing plants are located close to major food consumption markets including in Tianjin, Jiangsu, Shandong, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei and Xinjiang. Historically, the company has focused its business activities in downstream activities. However, in February 2014, COFCO bought a majority stake (51%) in Nidera, a Dutch commodities trader, in order to gain access to South American grain and oilseed goods, while in April 2014, the company acquired a controlling stake (51%) in Noble Agri, which owns oilseeds processing plants and a grain processing and distribution business. In May 2015, COFCO announced it will merge its holdings in Nidera and Noble Agri to create a new entity, COFCO International Holdings, in a joint venture with China Investment Corp, a sovereign wealth fund who will own 19.9% of the new business, with the ultimate intention of merging COFCO's own domestic business into COFCO International to combine COFCO's oil, grain and sugar assets.
COFCO Group retains a strong presence in the downstream market, with a number of branded goods sold across China. They sell shortening and margarine as well as a number of speciality products such as soybean milk fat. In total, their annual sales volume exceeds 120,000 tonnes across 31 Chinese provinces. Its brands include Sihai for soybean meal products and Fuzhiquan for cooking oils.
As well as being a major player in the processed food industry, COFCO Group has a long history in the timber sector and claims to be the largest integrated timber merchant in China. One of the Group's subsidiaries, China Timber Co. Ltd., has operated traded timber internationally for over fifty years. It imports a wide variety of timber and timber products from a range of countries, including raw timber from Papua New Guinea and Myanmar; and plywood, construction materials and furniture from Africa and South America. It also exports wood flooring and plywood and other manufactured wood products to the US, Europe, Japan and India.
Of particular relevance are China Timber's operations in the Republic of Gabon, where it holds five timber companies engaged in the direct harvesting of timber and timber processing activities. It has around one million hectares of tropical hardwood forests. Specifically, it operates Sunly Gabon, which is one of the largest Chinese firms operating in the Gabonese forestry sector and has several hundred thousand hectares of forest concessions in the north-east, east and southern parts of the country.

Nike Inc. was incorporated in 1969, and has grown to become the largest manufacturer of footwear in the world; it also claims to be one of the world's largest users of white leather for footwear.
Nike Inc. focuses on the design, development, and marketing of athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessory products, and sells its products worldwide to retail stores as well as through its own subsidiaries and distributors. It has five key brands: Nike, Converse, Hurley, Jordan and Nike Golf and in 2013, Nike ranked among the world's 25 most valuable brands. Nike Inc's subsidiary, Converse, also designs, distributes and licenses athletic and casual footwear as well as apparel under trademarks that include Converse, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron and Jack Purcell.
Nearly all of Nike Inc's footwear is manufactured outside of the United States by independent contract manufacturers. Most of these are based in Vietnam, China and Indonesia, which together account for 8% of the Nike brand footwear. Apparel is produced in 28 countries including China, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Malaysia, Turkey, Mexico and Cambodia. Globally, nearly 50,000 people work for Nike Inc. including in the 750 company-owned and operated retail stores.

Perum Perhutani is a state-owned enterprise, which manages the state forests in Java and Madua, Indonesia. The total area covers over 2.4 million hectares.  Perum Perhutani is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

Coty is a manufacturer and distributor of beauty products based in the US, with business segments in luxury, consumer beauty and professional beauty.  Coty Inc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

The Kraft Heinz Company is a food and beverage company headquartered in North America but operating in over 45 countries. The company was formed in 2015 by a merger between Kraft Food Group, Inc. and H.J. Heinz Holding Corporation. According to the company, it is the third largest food and beverage company in North America and the fifth largest globally. The company has more than 200 brands sold in nearly 200 countries, with eight brands worth over $1 billion. Iconic brand names include Kraft, Heinz, Kool-Aid, Oscar Mayer and Planters.

JBS is one of the world’s largest food companies and exporters of beef from Brazil. Across its meatpacking business it operates over 250 production facilities worldwide, with the capacity to process many tens of thousands of cattle per day. In addition to beef, JBS is exposed to soy, through its use of animal feed in cattle feedlots, poultry and swine farms. The company is also a significant player in the global leather industry, with over twenty tanneries in Brazil alone.  JBS is selected as a powerbroker for soy, beef, leather and paper packaging.

Felda Global Ventures (FGV) is a Malaysian group of agribusiness companies active in the palm, rubber, sugar, and agri-services industries. The group is involved in both the cultivation and processing of oil palm as well as in the manufacturing of palm oil goods. In 2015, FGV had a total oil palm landbank of over 750,000 hectares across Indonesia and Malaysia which is one of the five largest landbanks for palm oil in the world. It also has major processing operations, processing about 15 million fresh fruit bunches in 2015, and claims to be the largest producer of crude palm oil in the world, producing more than 3 million metric tons in the same year.

Natwest is a British banking and insurance holding company. As of 2024, Natwest have over 700 billion GBP in total assets. In the 2024 selection, Natwest was providing 36.2 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Rewe Group is a German retail company that operates within food retail, home improvement, pharmacies, discount stores, apparel shops, and travel. Rewe Group has over 15,000 stores in 20 European countries, and every week the company has 70 million customers visiting its shops. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities.   Rewe Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.

Walmart Inc was selected as a powerbroker for Rubber (Retailer), Leather (Retailer), Cocoa (Retailer), Coffee (Retailer), Beef (Retailer), Palm oil (Retailer), Soy (Retailer), Timber (Retailer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

rows.coprofile:
Hormel Foods Corp (Hormel) is a manufacturer of food and meat products, based in the US. The company currently has operations in six countries but it markets its thousands of products in over 40 countries from 44 manufacturing facilities, with a total workforce of 19,800 employees. Out of its 48 brands, the group claims that 35 hold either the top or second highest market share.
Since being founded in 1891, Hormel has risen to number 1057 on the Forbes Global 2000 list and is ranked at 311 in the Fortune 500. The business is split into: Grocery products; refrigerated foods; Jennie-O Turkey Store; specialty foods; and all others, each marketed under the wholly-owned subsidiary of Hormel Foods International Corporation (HFIC). HFIC operates in four spheres: the Americas, Asia-Pacific, China and Europe. These are reached through six joint ventures, three licensees and two wholly-owned subsidiaries (Hormel Foods Australia and Jennie-O Turkey Store Inc).
Particularly prevalent in overseas markets are its SPAM (chopped pork and ham) and Stagg (chili) (beef) brands, which both hold the primary market share in the UK and Ireland. Hormel Foods Corp. has recently expanded with the purchase of CytoSport Holdings Inc, which manufactures Muscle Milk, for $450 million in an effort to reach a younger market. In terms of rankings, Hormel is placed in the world top ten for ready meals and chilled processed food, the top five in the world for spreads, and second in the US for spreads and canned/preserved food.

MRV Engenharia e Participaces (MRV) is a construction company in Brazil focussed on the residential real estate market, building houses, apartment buildings and other properties. It is one of the largest Brazilian construction companies by units sold, revenue and sales value, and it operates in 134 cities and 19 states in Brazil. Timber is a major raw material for construction, and Brazil in general uses four times more tropical timber than China. In 2013, MRV used more than 1.4 million cubic metres of timber.

Dunkin' Brands Group is a franchisor of quick service restaurants including the two major chains Dunkin' Donuts and Baskin-Robbins. Dunkin' Donuts has more than 11,500 restaurants in 40 countries worldwide and offers coffee and baked goods including doughnuts and bagels. Baskin-Robbins has more than 7,000 shops in nearly 50 countries offering ice-cream and beverages. The diverse menus of both expose the group to several forest risk commodities. Dunkin' Brands is one of the ten largest food providers globally by market share.

Casino Guichard Perrachon (Casino) is a French retailer with more than 15,000 convenience stores, hypermarkets and supermarkets predominantly in France and Latin America. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Globally, the group is among the top twenty retailers for edible groceries, but it has an especially strong presence in Latin America where it is among the top five. Casino claims to be the top retailer in Brazil, Colombia and Vietnam.
initiatives: Cerrado Manifesto Statement of Support, UN Global Compact, Consumer Goods Forum

rows.coprofile:
Asics Corporation was founded in 1949 in Kobe, Japan. It was incorporated twenty years later through the merger of three companies: Onitsuka, GTO and JELENK. The company has two business segments: sports product manufacture and sales; and outdoor products manufacture and sales. The sports segment is involved in the manufacture and sale of sportswear, sports shoes and equipment. This part of the business also oversees the management and delivery of products, the planning of products, and the factoring and sales support businesses. The other business segment is focused on the manufacture and sale of outdoor products through its subsidiaries, of which it has more than 50 globally. Asics Corporation employs more than 7,400 people worldwide.
Asics Corporation is among the top ten manufacturers of footwear globally and is particularly well known for its running shoes, which are marketed to both professional and amateur athletes.  The company is therefore a significant user of leather. Asics Corporation operates a number of flagship stores and the expansion of its retail network is a key strategy for the company. The company promotes its brands through participation in a number of high profile sporting events, for example through its sponsorship of major marathons and the use of Asics equipment by top sporting teams and federations on the world stage. On top of the Asics brand, the company sells fashion-oriented items under the Onitsuka Tiger brand.

The Schwarz Group is a German retail group comprised of both wholesalers and multi-format retail stores. Its supermarkets operate over 12,900 stores (in 2021) across 33 countries under the brands Kaufland, Handelshof and Kaufmarkt, alongside the supermarket retailer Lidl. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. Schwarz Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: DBS are a financial services group headquartered in Singapore serving private and commercial clients. Their services include wealth management, corporate finance, institutional investment, insurance, and retail banking services. As of 2024, the groups assets under management amount to more than 426 billion SDG. In the 2024 selection, DBS was providing 20.9 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Aegon are an insurance company based in the Netherlands serving private, commercial and institutional customers. Their services include life insurance, pensions, and asset management. As of 2017, Aegon manage a combined value of 840 billion EUR of investments, including more than 325 billion EUR in assets under management. They are one of the top bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Unicharm Corporation manufactures and sells household care items, including baby, feminine, health and cosmetic products, through these products Unicharm uses pulp and paper.Unicharm Corporation has operations spanning the globe, and holds the top share of diaper sales in China and Indonesia.   Unicharm Corp is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group’s two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.8 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.  Royal Golden Eagle is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper.

Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses across the globe. The company offers products such as groceries, apparel, furniture, houseware, office suppliers and health and beauty aids across 762 warehouses as of 2018.

The Schwarz Group is a German retail group comprised of both wholesalers and multi-format retail stores. Its supermarkets operate under the brands Kaufland, Handelshof and Kaufmarkt, alongside the discount retailer Lidl. The breadth of its retail offerings exposes the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. With the combined weight of these retailers, the Schwarz Group is among the top five retailers for edible groceries globally. It is also one of the largest edible grocery retailers in Europe.

Associated British Foods is a diversified group with operations in food, ingredients and retail. The group’s business units include teas, cereals, sugars, and animal feed with such brands such as Twinings, Ryvita, and Blue Dragon. It is also a leading vendor in the baking ingredients market and the owner of the clothing retailer Primark. These diverse businesses expose the group to palm oil and soy in food production, soy in animal feed and leather in apparel. It is also among the largest producers of animal feed in Europe.  Associated British Foods Plc is selected as a powerbroker for soy, leather and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

Morgan Stanley are an international investment bank and financial services provider headquartered in the US that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Services include wealth management, investment banking, capital markets, sales and trading, and research and investment management. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 850 billion USD, with more than 130 billion USD worth of loans. Morgan Stanley are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 36 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 20 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 19 billion USD worth of shares.
Signatory to UN-convened Net-Zero Asset Owners Alliance, Net Zero Insurance Alliance, Commitment letter signatories. AXA Group finances the Forest 500 with a total of 6047 USDM

(Arauco) is controlled by the Angelini family through holding company, Empresas COPEC and is Chile's second largest pulp producer with a total capacity of 3.9 million tonnes of pulp. The company's product portfolio includes woodpulp, laminate panels, lumber, moulding and laminated beams. Its pulp products are used to produce paper, packaging material and diapers. Angelini Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and is also assessed for its exposure to pulp & paper.

Schroders are a financial services company headquartered in the UK offering wealth management and asset management services for private, corporate and institutional clients. As of 2024, Schroders have more than £535 billion of assets under management. They are one of the top shareholders in Forest 500 companies. In the 2024 selection, Schroders was providing 19.9 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
