rows.coprofile:
Mitsubishi Corp is a core company of the Mitsubishi Group; a group of autonomous companies made up of about 28 core enterprises and up to 600 member companies in all. The companies within the Mitsubishi Group conduct their operations independently of one another, but each honour the Group's three principles (of corporate social responsibility; integrity and fairness; and global understanding through business) and have their roots in the original shipping company, founded in 1870.
Mitsubishi Corp is a general trading company; the largest in Japan and the largest publicly-listed company of its kind in the world. The company's history extends back to 1954, when the Mitsubishi Shoji was established; however, Mitsubishi Corporation became the company's official English name in 1971. Mitsubishi Corp's activities now expand well beyond its original trading operations and it is involved in a wide variety of businesses, including energy, metals, food and environmental business.  Of particular relevance are Mitsubishi's operations in the production of food products that include soya and palm-based ingredients. Significantly, the Living Essentials department of Mitsubishi Corp also operates as a trading company in the palm oil industry, where it purchases predominantly Malaysian palm oil for export to Japan, the US and Taiwan, among others. The Living Essentials Group's activities in the production of consumer goods also include the procurement of raw materials and the manufacturing and distribution of a wide variety of products, including furniture, lumber, housing and construction materials, as well as many processed and frozen foods.
Mitsubishi Corp acquired UK-based food and drink manufacturer, Princes Ltd., in 1989. This is another particularly relevant component of Mitsubishi's operations. Founded in Liverpool, UK in 1880, Princes has since greatly increased its business portfolio diversifying from its original focus on the sale of canned goods. With a total of 19 mergers and acquisitions, it is now among the top food and drinks manufacturers in the UK.  Its tinned and canned products include meat pies, corned beef and stewed steak and the company is among the top five European beef importers from Brazil.

Arla Foods is a dairy cooperative with activities around the world. The company’s most prominent markets are the United Kingdom, Central Europe and Asia. Its products include milk, cheese, butter and cooking ingredients with brands such as Lurpak, Castello and Apetina. Arla Foods is one of the world’s largest ingredient producers. Soy plays an important role in the cooperative’s animal feed and palm oil is also used in its products.  Arla Foods is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Maxingvest AG was selected as a powerbroker for Pulp & Paper (Packaging), Coffee (Retailer) and is also assessed for Soy (Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer)

Gold Best Holdings is a manufacturing and trading pulp and paper company based in the British Virgin Islands. Its subsidiary, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd, operate in the business of packing paper.

The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.
In addition to its major Starbucks brand the company also operates: Seattles Best Coffee, Teavana, Tazo, Evolution Fresh, La Boulange (bakery brand) and Torrefazione Italia Coffee. Starbucks is the largest cafe/bar owner in the world with revenues of $14.9bn. Starbucks uses paper in its packaging, soya (in milk) and palm oil (in its food products).

Bertelsmann is a media and services company operating in 50 countries around the world. Its major operations are in television and radio, publishing and magazines. The most important markets are the US and Europe, but China, Brazil and India are growing markets. The company is one of the largest book publishers in the world and uses a significant amount of paper.  Bertelsmann SE & Co. KGaA is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Oji Holdings Corp was selected as a powerbroker for Pulp & Paper (Processor, Trader, Producer, Manufacturer) and is also assessed for Timber (Trader, Producer, Processor, Manufacturer), Rubber (Manufacturer)
JM Smucker is a Fortune 500 company who manufactures food and beverage products on a global scale. Famous brands include Crisco and Jif.

Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

Yum! Brands Inc. develops franchises, operates and licenses restaurants. It is one of the world's largest restaurant companies, with over 42,500 companies in more than 130 countries and territories. The three globally recognised chains under the Yum! umbrella are KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell; which are the global leaders in their respective food categories of chicken, pizza and Mexican-style food .
Since its spinoff from PepsiCo. in 1997, Yum! Brands has expanded significantly internationally, with 65% of its profits now coming from non-US markets in 2015 compared to just 20% in 1997. In 2016, Yum! Brands opens on average over six new restaurants a day worldwide.
Yum! Brands' chicken restaurant chain, KFC, has 18,000 outlets in 115 countries and territories, serving over 12 million customers each day. Taco Bell serves Mexican style food through around 6,100 outlets in the US, serving more than 40 million customers each week. However, Yum! Brands is looking to expand the chain globally and currently has around 300 stores in 20 countries outside the US. By the end of 2014, there were over 15,600 Pizza Hut restaurants around the world.
Yum! Brands franchisees and company operated restaurants are significant purchasers of chicken, cheese, beef and pork products as well as paper and packaging materials. All three restaurant brands use palm oil, soy and beef in a variety of different products.

Itaú Unibanco are banking group based in Brazil serving both private and commercial customers. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, wealth management, insurance, pensions and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.3 trillion BRL, including over 400 billion BRL in loans. Itaú Unibanco are one of the top 60 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 3 billion USD of loans to companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

SMBC Group are a global financial and banking group headquartered in Japan offering a broad range of financial services to private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, investment management and financial and operating leases, as well as retail banking and consumer finance. SMBC Group is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group. SMBC Group is the banking unit of the organisation. As of 2024, the group's total assets amount to more than 285 trillion Yen. SMBC Group are among the top loan providers to Forest 500 companies. In the 2024 selection, SMBC Group was providing 122.8 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group’s two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.6 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.  Royal Golden Eagle is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper.

Shiseido is a Japanese multinational company specialising in cosmetics and personal care. The company sells its products in over 100 countries under its own brand, and other well-known brand names including Elixir, NARS, bareMinerals and Issey Miyake. As a leading producer of cosmetic and personal care goods Shiseido is exposed to the forest risk commodity palm oil which is used in products such as lotions.   Shiseido Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

rows.coname: LVMH Moït Hennessy Louis Vuitton S.A.
rows.coprofile:
LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA (LVMH) is a French company, with its headquarters in Paris, engaged in the luxury goods industry. The group was formed following the merger of the MoÃ«t Hennessy and Louis Vuitton companies in 1987; however its origins extend back much further in the history of the development of the French luxury goods industry. Louis Vuitton's flagship brand was launched in 1854, after which it continued to specialise solely in handmade leather bags for over 70 years, while, Moet Hennessy's origins are even earlier, as the company was involved in the wine industry for 100 years prior.
LVMH currently operates in five main segments: wines and spirits; fashion and leather goods; perfumes and cosmetics; watches and jewellery; and selective retailing. Within these five sectors, LVMH has a portfolio of more than 60 brands and an international network of more than 3,000 stores. Of particular importance is the company's fashion and leather goods division, which comprises well-known luggage, leather goods and apparel and accessories brands, such as Louis Vuitton, Givenchy and Marc Jacobs.
In 2013, the fashion and leather goods business accounted for the majority of the group's total revenue. The group is an industry leader in the bags and luggage market worldwide, occupying the top position globally in terms of market share and leading positions in the individual markets of China, Western Europe and the USA.
initiatives: CDP Forests 2013-2015 are all submitted (not published)

rows.coprofile: Credit Agricole are a European banking group headquartered in France serving private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, capital markets, investment banking, insurance, asset management, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2017, the group's total assets amount to more than 1.7 trillion EUR, with more than 790 billion EUR of loans and advances. Credit Agricole are among the top 25 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 20 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 60 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 6 billion USD worth of shares.

Ajinomoto Co Inc is a Japanese multinational food and biotech company based in Tokyo. Ajinomoto Group has products in more than 130 countries and regions and sources raw materials, including beef, from Brazil, Japan, China, Thailand, India, Turkey, the United States, Canada, Mexico, Argentina, Uruguay, Australia and New Zealand. It has been selected as a powerbroker for beef, and is also assessed for it's exposure to palm oil, soy, and pulp and paper.

Sinar Mas Group Co. Ltd. was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Processor, Producer, Trader, Manufacturer), Soy (Processor, Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Manufacturer, Producer, Trader, Processor) and is also assessed for Cocoa (Manufacturer)

Societe Generale are a banking group headquartered in France that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services span corporate finance, capital markets, insurance, wealth management, investments, securities and retail banking services. As of 2021, Societe Generale's total assets amount to more than 1.46 trillion EUR, with a total of 78 Billion EUR of assets under management. Societe Generale are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2022 selection, Societe Generale was providing 51.6 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating manufacturer headquartered in the US. Its subsidiary Eagle Ottawa claims to be the world’s largest supplier of automotive leather. With customers including the likes of Mercedes, BMW, Toyoto and GMC, Eagle Ottawa has a high turnover of leather hides.  Lear Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Mewah International is an agri-business focused on edible oils and fats. The company has refineries and processing facilities in Malaysia and Singapore, and produce vegetable oils and fats from palm oil, soybean oil, canola oil, sunflower seed oil, and corn oil. The company has the capacity to refine 3.5 million tons of palm oil each year. Mewah International Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Malayan Banking is an international banking group headquartered in Malaysia operating several banking subsidiaries. The services it provides cover corporate finance, capital markets, securities, insurance, consumer and corporate banking. Malayan Banking is among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies,  predominantly in the agriculture and agricultural commodities sectors.

ConAgra Foods is an American manufacturer of packaged food products as well as a provider of commercial products and foodservice. The company is primarily focussed on North America but also has manufacturing facilities in Latin America and India. Its products are mostly frozen and refrigerated foods with well-known brands including Banquet, Blue Bonnet and Slim Jim, but it also produces cereals and snacks. ConAgra Foods is a major global player for oils and fats, sweet and savoury snacks, and ready meals. Palm oil and soya are both significant, and in 2015 more than 100,000 metric tons of palm oil products were used by the company.
Caramuru Alimentos was selected as a powerbroker for Soy (Processor, Trader, Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

Associated British Foods is a diversified group with operations in food, ingredients and retail. The group's business units include teas, cereals, sugars, and animal feed with such brands such as Twinings, Ryvita, and Blue Dragon. It is also a leading vendor in the baking ingredients market and the owner of the clothing retailer Primark. These diverse businesses expose the group to palm oil and soya in food production, soya in animal feed and leather in apparel. In 2015, for example, it used more than 24,000 metric tons of palm oil and palm oil derivatives in its products. It is also among the top fifteen producers of animal feed in Europe, with a production of over 2.2 million metric tons in 2014.

Saint Gobain is a French multinational corporation that designs, manufactures, and distributes building materials. Major brands include Jewson in the UK and Point P in France. It is one of the largest building material suppliers in Europe and operates in a total of 64 countries worldwide, including across Southeast Asia and South America. It is one of the largest European distributors of building materials.  Saint Gobain S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.
In addition to its major Starbucks brand the company also operates: Seattles Best Coffee, Teavana, Tazo, Evolution Fresh, La Boulange (bakery brand) and Torrefazione Italia Coffee. Starbucks is the largest cafe/bar owner in the world with revenues of $14.9bn. Starbucks uses paper in its packaging, soya (in milk) and palm oil (in its food products).

Nomura Partners Funds are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving private, corporate, government and institutional clients. Their services include retail, asset management, global markets and investment banking. As of 2017, Nomura Partners Funds' total assets amount to over 42 trillion Yen with over 3 trillion Yen in loans. They are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Mitsubishi Corp is a core company of the Mitsubishi Group; a group of autonomous companies made up of about 28 core enterprises and up to 600 member companies in all. The companies within the Mitsubishi Group conduct their operations independently of one another, but each honour the Group's three principles (of corporate social responsibility; integrity and fairness; and global understanding through business) and have their roots in the original shipping company, founded in 1870.
Mitsubishi Corp is a general trading company; the largest in Japan and the largest publicly-listed company of its kind in the world. The company's history extends back to 1954, when the Mitsubishi Shoji was established; however, Mitsubishi Corporation became the company's official English name in 1971. Mitsubishi Corp's activities now expand well beyond its original trading operations and it is involved in a wide variety of businesses, including energy, metals, food and environmental business.  Of particular relevance are Mitsubishi's operations in the production of food products that include soya and palm-based ingredients. Significantly, the Living Essentials department of Mitsubishi Corp also operates as a trading company in the palm oil industry, where it purchases predominantly Malaysian palm oil for export to Japan, the US and Taiwan, among others. The Living Essentials Group's activities in the production of consumer goods also include the procurement of raw materials and the manufacturing and distribution of a wide variety of products, including furniture, lumber, housing and construction materials, as well as many processed and frozen foods.
Mitsubishi Corp acquired UK-based food and drink manufacturer, Princes Ltd., in 1989. This is another particularly relevant component of Mitsubishi's operations. Founded in Liverpool, UK in 1880, Princes has since greatly increased its business portfolio diversifying from its original focus on the sale of canned goods. With a total of 19 mergers and acquisitions, it is now among the top food and drinks manufacturers in the UK.  Its tinned and canned products include meat pies, corned beef and stewed steak and the company is among the top five European beef importers from Brazil.

Power Financial Corporation are a diversified holding company headquartered in Canada with interests in the financial service providers Great-West Life co and IGM Financial. Services include investment, retirement, and insurance products and solutions. As of 2017, they have over 790 billion CAD in assets under management and 1.2 trillion CAD in assets under administration. Power Financial are among the top 40 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 10 billion USD worth of shares across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

rows.coprofile: Nordea are a financial services group with headquarters in Sweden serving private, corporate and institutional clients. As of 2022, Nordea's total assets amount to more than 570 billion EUR. Nordea are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, Nordea was providing 23.8 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

AAK is a Swedish agricultural processor and manufacturer of food ingredients, lipids, technical products, and animal feed with 19 production facilities and sales offices in over 25 countries. The company claims to be the world's leading manufacturer of specialty vegetable fats and is a major company in the global bakery ingredients market. Soya sourced from South America as well as palm oil and its derivatives sourced from Central America and Southeast Asia are used in these products by the company. In 2015, AAK used over 950,000 metric tons of palm oil and its derivatives in its products.

Minerva is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. The meat processed by Minerva is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.  MINERVA is selected as a powerbroker for beef and leather and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Operating across the United States, China and India, Tyson Foods Inc. has business in poultry, beef, pork and processed food products. The company’s poultry business involves the provision of feed product to a network of independent poultry farmers that exceeded 11,000 with animal feed using a significant quantity of soy. Tyson Foods Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile:
Staples Inc is an office supplies retailer that sells a variety of products to businesses and individual consumers. It is the world's largest specialist retailer of office supplies with key products lines in stationery, furniture, and technology products. Staples sells a wide variety of paper products, including copy paper, computer paper and POS rolls, photographic paper and letterheads.
Established in 1985, the company is headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts in the United States. The company's three operational segments are: North American Stores & Online; North American Commercial; and International Operations. The company operates around 2,200 stores globally, and also sells products online and via its catalogue service. It also has around 116 distribution centres throughout the US, Canada, Europe, China, South America, and elsewhere, in all serving customers in 26 countries worldwide.
Staples is the world's largest retailer of a wide range of wood- and paper-based office products, sourcing its products from a range of suppliers in different countries, including Argentina, Brazil, Canada, China and the US. In 2013, paper sales accounted for around 9% of Staples' total revenue; office furniture contributed around 5%; and core office supplies, which include paper and other core office products such as writing products, around 30%. Staples sells its own proprietary branded products under the Staples and Quill trademarks and also offers other manufactured branded items.

Nutreco N.V. (Nutreco) is an animal nutrition and feed company based in the Netherlands that manufactures feeds and additives for a range of animals and uses. It was created in 1994 by a private equity backed management buy-out of a number of firms involved in meat processing, animal nutrition and fish farming. Nutreco was floated on the NYSE Euronext Amsterdam exchange in 1997. In recent years, the company's strategy has been to focus more on animal nutrition and animal and aquaculture feed, moving away from meat processing and other downstream activities. It has also successfully targeted growth markets such as Russia, Asia, Africa and Latin America. Recently (October 2014), the Dutch investment firm, SHV Holdings, has entered into a conditional agreement to buy Nutreco.
The company currently employs around 10,000 people across more than 30 countries worldwide and serves markets in more than 80 countries. Operations are split into two main segments: Animal Nutrition and Fish Feed, which in 2013 accounted for 48% and 52% of revenue respectively. The Animal Nutrition division manufactures and sells farm minerals, concentrates, feed additives, animal health products, feeds and premixes. The segment contains multiple brands, each with different focuses and locations. These include Shur-Gain, which operates in Canada and some areas of the US, providing premixes, compound and speciality feeds pet foods and animal health products; Nanta, which focuses primarily on pigs, poultry and ruminants but also provides feed for horses and rabbits; and Skretting, Nutreco's fish feed company that provides feed for over 60 species of fish and shrimp. It has operations on five continents and manufactures feed in 14 countries.

Hormel Foods Corp (Hormel) is a manufacturer of food and meat products, based in the US. The company currently has operations in six countries but it markets its thousands of products in over 40 countries from 44 manufacturing facilities, with a total workforce of 19,800 employees. Out of its 48 brands, the group claims that 35 hold either the top or second highest market share.
Since being founded in 1891, Hormel has risen to number 1057 on the Forbes Global 2000 list and is ranked at 311 in the Fortune 500. The business is split into: Grocery products; refrigerated foods; Jennie-O Turkey Store; specialty foods; and all others, each marketed under the wholly-owned subsidiary of Hormel Foods International Corporation (HFIC). HFIC operates in four spheres: the Americas, Asia-Pacific, China and Europe. These are reached through six joint ventures, three licensees and two wholly-owned subsidiaries (Hormel Foods Australia and Jennie-O Turkey Store Inc).
Particularly prevalent in overseas markets are its SPAM (chopped pork and ham) and Stagg (chili) (beef) brands, which both hold the primary market share in the UK and Ireland. Hormel Foods Corp. has recently expanded with the purchase of CytoSport Holdings Inc, which manufactures Muscle Milk, for $450 million in an effort to reach a younger market. In terms of rankings, Hormel is placed in the world top ten for ready meals and chilled processed food, the top five in the world for spreads, and second in the US for spreads and canned/preserved food.

DSM is a Dutch based multinational company that manufactures products related to health, nutrition and materials. Within its nutrition division DSM produces a diverse range of products, from brewing enzymes, to animal feed formulation. Amongst its many products palm oil and soy are used in significant quantities.  Koninklijke DSM N.V. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA) are a global financial services group based in Spain with activities in corporate, retail and investment banking. Their services include retail banking, insurance, pensions, asset management and corporate lending. As of 2017, BBVA'a has more than 690 billion EUR in total assets and more than 416 billion EUR in loans and advances to customers. BBVA are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans to companies across several sectors, including food retail and packaged food.

Korindo Group is a diversified company based in Indonesia which produces, processes and manufacturers a range of products. Korindo has plantations of palm oil and timber.  Korindo Group PT is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and timber.
International Paper is one of the leading producers of fiber-based packaging, as well as pulp and paper, in the world.  International Paper is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

rows.coprofile: Metro AG is a German wholesaler with operations across the world. The company’s portfolio caters to professional customers, through sales brands including METRO Cash & Carry and different FSD companies. With a diverse product range, Metro AG is exposed to a number of forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy, pulp and paper. Metro AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Danzer is a German timber company based in Austria that produces veneer, lumber and other wood products from hardwood. It claims to be the largest producer of decorative veneer in the world.  Danzer Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

Its subsidiary Indofood Agri is a vertically integrated agribusiness company spanning the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivation to product manufacturing and marketing. Products produced include cooking oils and margarines under several brands which are sold both directly and through retailers.  Salim Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Clariant AG is a Swiss multinational speciality chemicals company using both palm oil and soy in the manufacture of their various products. Clariant develops, produces, markets and sells specialty chemical products for various end markets including paints, cosmetics and oils.

LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA (LVMH) is a French company, with its headquarters in Paris, engaged in the luxury goods industry. The group was formed following the merger of the MoÃ«t Hennessy and Louis Vuitton companies in 1987; however its origins extend back much further in the history of the development of the French luxury goods industry. Louis Vuitton's flagship brand was launched in 1854, after which it continued to specialise solely in handmade leather bags for over 70 years, while, Moet Hennessy's origins are even earlier, as the company was involved in the wine industry for 100 years prior.
LVMH currently operates in five main segments: wines and spirits; fashion and leather goods; perfumes and cosmetics; watches and jewellery; and selective retailing. Within these five sectors, LVMH has a portfolio of more than 60 brands and an international network of more than 3,000 stores. Of particular importance is the company's fashion and leather goods division, which comprises well-known luggage, leather goods and apparel and accessories brands, such as Louis Vuitton, Givenchy and Marc Jacobs.
In 2013, the fashion and leather goods business accounted for the majority of the group's total revenue. The group is an industry leader in the bags and luggage market worldwide, occupying the top position globally in terms of market share and leading positions in the individual markets of China, Western Europe and the USA.

Wilmar International Ltd. is a global agribusiness group involved in the cultivation, processing, refining, merchandising and trading of a wide range of agricultural products, including palm oil and soy. The company is one of the world’s largest oil palm plantation owners and processors, reportedly controlling around 45% of worldwide palm oil trade sourced from more than 80% of global palm oil growers. Wilmar is also a major player in the soybean crushing industry with a global crushing capacity of 36 million metric tons per annum, the majority of which is in China. The company claims to be one of the world’s largest producers of consumer edible oils.   Wilmar International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Associated British Foods is a diversified group with operations in food, ingredients and retail. The group’s business units include teas, cereals, sugars, and animal feed with such brands such as Twinings, Ryvita, and Blue Dragon. It is also a leading vendor in the baking ingredients market and the owner of the clothing retailer Primark. These diverse businesses expose the group to palm oil and soy in food production, soy in animal feed and leather in apparel. It is also among the largest producers of animal feed in Europe.  Associated British Foods Plc is selected as a powerbroker for soy, leather and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

The Wendy's Company (Wendy's) is the third largest quick service hamburger company in the world, with around 6,500 restaurants in the US and 29 other countries and US territories worldwide. Wendy's restaurants specialise in hamburgers and sandwiches but also offer fries, salads and desserts. The majority of the company's restaurants are in North America; in 2014, 6,112 restaurants operated in the US and Canada, with the majority run by franchises. The Wendy's Company has a joint venture with Restaurant Brands International covering around 100 restaurants in Canada. Outside of North America, there are 403 franchised restaurants in other countries and territories. In addition to beef and paper Wendy's uses soya (used in a range of spreads, dressings and baked products) and palm oil (used in snacks and desserts).

ING Group are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. The company has the capacity to refine 3.5 million tons of palm oil each year. Mewah International Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

Domino's Pizza Inc. is a US pizza delivery and carry-out company serving the US and over 75 international markets. Worldwide, there are 11,700 stores that deliver over 1 million pizzas every day. Over 90% of stores are franchised, while Domino's Pizza Inc. owns around 377 stores in the US. It also runs dough manufacturing facilities and supply chain centres to supply stores in the US and in some overseas markets.  The US is Domino's Pizza Inc.'s single biggest market with 5,084 stores in Q1 2015, but over half of the company's sales come from outside the US. Domino's Pizza Inc. is the world's second biggest fast food pizza retailer. In addition to pizza, the company offers related products including sandwiches, chicken, salads, sauces, drinks and desserts. Beef is used as a pizza topping, soya is used in pizzas, and both soya and palm oil are used in side dishes and desserts.

The cooperative has several subsidiaries which expand its operations across Europe and into Russia and China. Agrifirm represents a significant portion of Europe’s soy imports and is also an importer of palm oil.   Agrifirm is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

New Balance Athletic Shoes is a manufacturer of athletic footwear, apparel, and accessories and is present in more than 50 countries around the world. Its products include sports shoes, running, and hiking shoes, sports clothing and bags. Leather features in several of its footwear products. The company is one of the top footwear retailers globally, in China and Hong Kong, and in the US.  New Balance Athletic Shoe Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Nike is a manufacturer of sports shoes, sports apparel and accessories. The Company’s famous brands include Nike, Converse, Hurley, and Jordan. Many of Nike’s shoes are made using leather.  Nike Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather, pulp & paper and paper packaging.

Stichting Pensioenfonds ABP (ABP) are a pension fund based in the Netherlands for public and education sector employees. As of 2017, they have 403 billion EUR in available assets. They are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.
BioMar is a Danish fish feed producer for the aquaculture industry supplying over 80 countries.  BioMar is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Mizuho Financial Group Inc. are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include banking, securities, trust and asset management, credit cards, private banking, research and venture capital. As of 2024, Mizuho Financial Group Inc.'s total assets amount to over 270 trillion Yen. They are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Mizuho Financial Group Inc. was providing 182.5 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Aldi group (North) was selected as a powerbroker for Coffee (Retailer), Palm oil (Retailer), Soy (Retailer), Beef (Retailer), Cocoa (Retailer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Rubber (Retailer), Timber (Retailer), Leather (Retailer)

AXA are a financial services company headquartered in France serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include an array of insurance solutions, as well as a significant asset management business. As of 2017, AXA's total assets amount to more than 870 billion EUR, with more than 1.1 trillion EUR of assets under management. They are among the top 15 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 2 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. AXA are also among the top 30 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 13 billion USD worth of shares.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia are a financial services provider headquartered in Australia that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. They offer a range of products and services including retail, premium, business and institutional banking, funds management, pension programmes, insurance, and investment and share-broking products and services. As of 2017, Commonwealth Bank of Australia's total assets amount to over 970 billion AUD with over 730 billion AUD in loans. They are among the top 100 shareholders for Forest 500 Companies, with over 3 billion USD worth of shares.

Mewah International Inc. (Mewah) is one of the dominant palm oil traders globally. It started operating in the 1950s with imports of palm oil from Malaysia to Singapore and is now involved in the production and distribution of a range of edible oils and fats. In 1987, Mewah opened its first refinery in Malaysia, producing 400 million tonnes per day, and has now opened a further two refineries, increasing its yearly capacity to 2.8 million tonnes. Mewah sources its raw materials from Malaysia and Indonesia before selling to the consumer and commercial markets in over 100 countries. It sells palm, soya bean, lauric, coconut, canola corn and sunflower oils commercially, and edible oils and fats on the consumer market. Mewah's consumer products are distributed via a range of different regional brands, such as Oki, Mona and Fry-ola, making it the world's leading edible oil company.
Mewah is also a key producer of food grade packaging for commercial and consumer markets. To continue to expand its business, Mewah is aiming to consolidate its position within the palm-based oil and fats business, expand its consumer product range, invest in efficient production facilities and expand its distribution network,. This has involved the construction of a new refinery in Sabah, Malaysia, which will increase Mewah's productivity to 3.5 million tonnes per year, along with the purchase of a new biodiesel facility in Westport, Malaysiaiv. Mewah has complemented these acquisitions with the installation of a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia, costing around $50 million, to produce a range of dairy products.
Mewah has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2006 and it expects to achieve 100% RSPO certification of all supply chains by 2015.
Kencana Agri is a palm oil plantation company based in Indonesia with a planted area of over 65,000 ha.  Kencana Agri Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Doctor's Associates Inc. owns and operates the fast food sandwich chain Subway. Subway has more than 37,000 stores in over 100 countries around the world with the US and the UK as its largest markets. The company's breads, fillings and snacks expose it to a number of forest risk commodities. It is among the top five fast food restaurants in the world by market share.

Coamo Agroindustrial Cooperativa (Coamo) was founded in 1970 to enable Brazilian farmers to share the costs of wheat processing and storage. Today, Coamo operates 115 warehouses and, in 2014, the cooperative processed 7.0 million tons of agricultural products and was responsible for 3.6% of Brazil's total grain and fibre production. In addition to wheat and maize, the company deals with coffee, cotton and, most significantly, soya; processing 1.5 million tons of soybeans in 2014.
The company is among Brazil's top five crushers and exporters of soya. Its processing facilities include five soybean crushing mills, a soybean oil refinery, a hydrogenated fat mill, margarine processing facilities, and cotton wheat mills, which in total process around 1.7 million tons of products annually. The cooperative and processing complex are located in Parana, in Southern Brazil. It has over 6,700 employees and as well as processed products, also produces its own brand coffee and soybean oil that are sold in the region.

Hengan International is a Chinese manufacturer of paper products including sanitary napkins, disposable nappies and tissue paper.  Hengan International Group Co Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

JBS is a global company involved in the beef, lamb and poultry processing, and in pork production.  It is among the largest producer of protein products worldwide, and is also involved in the production of leather, hygiene and cleaning products, collagen, metal packaging, biodiesel and other goods. JBS has operations spanning 24 countries and serves around 300,000 customers in 150 countries. 
Initially, the company was a small operation, with the capacity of processing five head of cattle per day. However, since 1953, JBS has expanded hugely, with major acquisitions in South America, the US, Australia and Europe. In 2007 JBS was floated on the Brazilian stock exchange, making it the first meat processing company in Brazil to do so. Today it is headquartered in Sao Paulo and employs around 185,000 people in total. Its operations are split between the following business divisions: JBS Mercosul, which comprises the company's beef and leather and related industries in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay; JBS USA, which is responsible for overseeing JBS' activities in Australia, Canada, the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico; and finally, JBS Foods, which was established in 2013 and covers the company's poultry, pork and value-added products in Brazil. 
The variety of products, which include fresh and frozen cuts to ready meals and processed foods service a variety of markets, including the catering, supermarket and export markets. These are marketed under several brands, including Bertin, Swift, and Friboi, and packaged foods, including ready meals under the Seara brand.
As well as its extensive operations in the global meat production and processing industries, which make beef of obvious significance, soya is also important, given its use in animal feed. For example, JBS operates 13 poultry farms, two pig farms and over 40 hatcheries, which use large amounts of animal feed. On top of its own operations, JBS also has around 5000 pig and poultry partner producers, which it provides with technical support and materials including all feed. Similarly within its beef operations, JBS operates cattle feedlots in Brazil the US and Australia where it provides all feed. Further to this, JBS is a significant player in the global leather industry, and with a daily processing capacity of one hundred thousand hides, leather processing is one of JBS' primary activities.

It is also a major Chinese importer of palm oil.

Samling Global Ltd group of companies is a Malaysian conglomerate with diverse operations, including in the timber and oil palm sectors.  Founded in 1963, Samling's core activities are in the forest products industry, where its operations span the length of the supply chain, from harvesting to processing, manufacturing and distribution.
Samling Global Ltd has a complicated corporate structure, with numerous subsidiaries and holding companies.  For example, Samling Global Ltd is an investment holding company incorporated in Bermuda, with numerous wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, the US, the British Virgin Islands and Japan. These companies in turn have a variety of subsidiaries, for example, in China, Malaysia, Guyana, Indonesia and India.
Of particular relevance, is Samling Global Ltd's involvement in the timber trade in Sarawak, Malaysia. Under Lingui Developments Bhd, Samling manages a total of 1.3 million hectares. Lingui Developments Bhd is an investment holding and forest resources and wood products company. It produces logs, plywood and veneer, fibreboard, doors and door facings, and kitchen counters and products, primarily for the export market and in particular for Japan, China, India, Korea and North America. Under its wholly owned subsidiary, Barama Company Ltd, Samling Global Ltd is also one of the biggest forestry companies in Guyana, where it holds 1.6 million hectares of forest concessions and produces sawnwood.
Samling Global Ltd is well established in the export markets of China and Japan. In China, it manufactures plywood, laminated veneer lumber and flooring and also distributes flooring through Elegant Living, one of China's major flooring distributors. Samling Global Ltd's access to the Japanese market is facilitated through its partnerships with Itochu Corporation, one of Japan's major traders and property developers, and Daiken Corporation, through which Samling Global Ltd supplies tropical logs and plywood for construction.
Samling Global Ltd has also expanded its operations into oil palm. Under Glenealy Plantations (Malaya) Bhd, it has plantations in Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, covering a total area of over 60,000 hectares; and also operates palm oil mills in Sabah and Sarawak. Samling Global Ltd is also part of a consortium developing acacia plantations in Malaysia to supply wood for the pulp and paper industry. This consortium is made up of Samling Strategic Corp Sdn Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, and KTS Timber Industries Bhd, all of which are major timber companies in Sarawak.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating manufacturer headquartered in the US, operating in 39 countries. Its subsidiary Eagle Ottawa claims to be the world’s largest supplier of automotive leather. With customers including the likes of Mercedes, BMW, Toyoto and GMC, Eagle Ottawa has a high turnover of leather hides.  Lear Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: DuPont is a US chemicals, materials and services company that provides scientific solutions to business challenges. It is active in agriculture, food and drinks, materials, electronics and other industries with operations in about 90 countries. The company's nutrition business area is involved in the manufacturing of food ingredients which involves palm oil, and it also produces soy proteins and other soy based products. DuPont is a key vendor and manufacturer in the global food ingredient market.

The SIFCA Group is an agribusiness group based in the Ivory Coast active throughout the supply chain of several agricultural commodities, including rubber, sugar cane, and palm oil. SIFCA is a major palm oil producer in West Africa. It also processes palm oil and produces products such as margarine.  SIFCA Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

rows.coprofile: Daiwa House Industry is a Japanese construction company, constructing residential homes and flats, business premises, and hotels. It is one of the largest homebuilders in Japan, which is an industry that uses large amounts of timber.  Daiwa House Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Unigra is an Italian company in the production and distribution of food products containing soy and palm oil, including chocolate, drinking chocolate, sugar pastes, powder mixes and improvers for bakery and confectionery industry and artisans globally. Unigra is also assessed for pulp and paper due to volume of packaging involved in it's various products.

Capri Holdings Limited is a multinational luxury holding company, selling apparel, footwear and accessories. Brands operating under this parent company include Jimmy Choo, Michael Kors and Versace.  Capri Holdings Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

LBBW is a commerical and central bank, headquartered in Germany. It is among the largest lenders to Forest 500 companies, predominantly manufacturers and retailers that are exposed to several forest risk commodities.
Signatory to Commitment letter signatories. London LGPS CIV Ltd not present in financing data

Coach is an American manufacturer of accessories and lifestyle items such as bags, footwear, watches, and other leather goods. The company operates in America, Europe, and Asia both online and with physical stores. It is one of the top five bag and luggage retailers in the world by brand share. Coach is one of the leading such retailers in the US, and places among the top five in China and Hong Kong.
The Coca-Cola company was selected as a powerbroker for Coffee (Retailer) and is also assessed for Palm oil (Retailer), Cocoa (Retailer), Soy (Retailer, Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

Barclays are a multinational universal bank, headquartered in the UK serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services cover personal, corporate, offshore, private, and investment banking, wealth management, loans and mortgages, and corporate lending. As of 2021, Barclays have over 1.3 trillion GBP in assets under management. They are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2022 selection, Barclays was providing 95 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Uni-President Enterprises Corp (UPEC) manufactures and distributes a range of food products through its network of 200 affiliate companies and convenience stores. The company was incorporated in 1967 in Tainan County, Taiwan. It was originally established as a rural flour factory but over the decades has grown into an international conglomerate with operations across Asia Pacific. The manufacturing of food products is one of the company's core businesses and although it has a wide range of interests, including sports teams, retail operations and pharmaceuticals, the manufacture of food and feed are the group's largest operations. Its main products include feeds, edible oils, soya sauce, meat products, instant noodles, dairy products and frozen foods, among others.
The manufacture and marketing of food and feed products are undertaken by five main groups. The Provisions Group manufactures and markets flour, fertilizer, eggs, and animal and aquatic feeds to Asian and other international markets. The Dairy and Beverage Group manufactures dairy products, teas, soft drinks, coffee and other beverages under brands such as €œPure Tea€, €œRae-Shie€ and €œLa Gauche de la Seine€.  In addition to Taiwan, the Dairy and Beverage Group operates in mainland China, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Edible oils and instant noodles are produced by the Instant Food Group, which has a 50% market share of Taiwan's instant noodle market. Instant products are also sold outside of Taiwan with products available in 30 countries across five continents. Brands include Unif, Imperial, One More Cup, Kikkoman, A-HA, Juicymart and Pure Tea. The two smallest Groups are the General Foods and Health groups. The former provides meat products, ice cream, sauces and ready meals while the Health Group manufactures bakery and health products,.
Of particular relevance is President Nisshin Corp, a member of Uni-President that supplies oils and fats, including palm oil products, to the food industry. Furthermore, palm oil is also used in other products, for example in instant noodles, and is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soya, imported from both the US and South America, is used in Uni-President's feed and edible oil products.
JM Smucker is a Fortune 500 company who manufactures food and beverage products on a global scale. Famous brands include Crisco and Jif.

Oetker-Gruppe is a German manufacturer of packaged food. The majority of the company’s products are frozen pizzas, baking goods, desserts, dry ready meals, beverages, and snacks. Oetker-Gruppe operates internationally with around 350 companies working in a variety of different business segments. Oetker-Gruppe is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Nisshin OilliO is a Japanese company producing oil and oil-based products. The company produce edible oils, soy food, processed oils and fats, raw materials for cosmetics, food ingredients, and meals among other products.   Nisshin OilliO Group Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is the Japanese manufacturer of the well-known fermented probiotic milk drink Yakult. In addition to its namesake, Yakult also produces a variety of other food and beverage products, as well as pharmaceuticals and cosmetic goods. The company is a leading name in the packaged food industry with product lines spanning from health food to noodles. Through its various product lines Yakult is exposed to palm oil and soy. Yakult Honsha Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

DSM is a Dutch based multinational company that manufactures products related to health, nutrition and materials. Within its nutrition division DSM produces a diverse range of products, from brewing enzymes, to animal feed formulation. Amongst its many products palm oil and soy are used in significant quantities.  Koninklijke DSM N.V. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Groupe Lactalis was selected as a powerbroker for Timber (Manufacturer), Coffee (Manufacturer), Cocoa (Manufacturer), Palm oil (Manufacturer), Soy (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Manufacturer, Exposed)

Credit Agricole are a European banking group headquartered in France serving private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, capital markets, investment banking, insurance, asset management, wealth management and retail banking services. As of 2017, the group's total assets amount to more than 1.7 trillion EUR, with more than 790 billion EUR of loans and advances. Credit Agricole are among the top 25 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 20 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 60 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 6 billion USD worth of shares.

Allianz are a global financial services provider headquartered in Germany serving both private and corporate clients. Their services include a wide array of insurance products, such as property, health and life insurance, as well as a large asset management business. As of 2017, Allianz's total assets amount to more than 890 billion EUR, with over 1.9 trillion EUR in assets under management. They are among the top bondholders and shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors

Nine Dragons Paper Holdings Ltd (ND Paper) is a paper and paper packaging manufacturer that produces a variety of containerboard and paper products, including: linerboard; corrugating medium and coated duplex board; recycled printing and writing paper; and tissue paper. As well as paper products, ND Paper manufactures wood-, bamboo-, and unbleached kraft pulp. The company's products are manufactured under three brands: Nine Dragons, Land Dragon and Sea Dragon, each focusing on a different customer segment.  ND Paper is well known for its use of recovered paper; the company's main source of raw material. This is used in the manufacturing of some of its products, such as its testlinerboard, made from 100% recovered paper, and its Sea Dragon office paper. The company imports significant amounts of recovered paper from the US; however, this is not used exclusively in all products.
The company was established in 1995 and is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies, ranking among the top 30 globally and holding the leading position in China. ND Paper has six manufacturing bases across China, as well as in Vietnam and Mongolia, through joint ventures: Cheng Yang Paper and Nine Dragons Xing An Pulp & Paper (Inner Mongolia) Co Ltd. Originally, the company predominantly supplied packaging for manufacturers in southern China's export oriented industry; however, the business has increasingly tapped into the demand for packaging products from the domestic market as China's own consumer-demand has grown.

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

News Corporation (News Corp) is a media conglomerate with a network of companies in media, news, education and information services. In June 2013, News Corp's shareholders gave formal approval for the company to split its publishing and entertainment divisions, creating two new companies: News Corp, housing the company's publishing segment; 21st Century Fox housing the entertainment division. News Corp is now specifically a publishing company, producing newspaper, magazines, books and promotional inserts and coupons. The company was established in Australia in 1954, when Rupert Murdoch took control of the Australian corporation, News Limited, which had a majority interest in one of Adelaide's top daily newspapers. Since then, the company has grown dramatically and acquired numerous assets, beginning with newspapers in the UK: 'The Sun' and 'News of the World.' Established in Australia, News Corp is now based in the US and is the largest newspaper publishing company globally.
As of 2014, News Corp is comprised of the following businesses, with each housing several brands: News Corp Australia, News UK, Dow Jones & Company, New York Post, Harper Collins Publishers, Amplify, News America Marketing, and Storyful. News Corp Australia, for example, claims to be Australia's leading media and publishing company, selling over 10 million papers weekly, with titles including The Daily Telegraph, The Australian, and Herald Sun. News UK also publishes some of the UK's most well-known newspapers, including The Sun, The Times and The Sunday Times. Dow Jones & Company publishes The Wall Street Journal and specialises in the provision of news and business information via a variety of media outlets.  Finally, News Corp's subsidiary HarperCollins is one of the world's most prominent book publishing companies. In May 2014, HarperCollins acquired book publisher Harlequin; the acquisition of the Canadian company is the biggest deal in book publishing since the merger of two other publishing giants, Penguin and Random House in 2013.

The Godrej Group is an Indian conglomerate which, through its subsidiaries, operates in the consumer goods, real estate management, industrial engineering, furniture, appliances, security services, and agricultural products sectors. Established by Ardeshir Godrej in 1897, the Godrej family retain ownership of the group, although its subsidiaries Godrej Industries and Godrej Properties are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The company operates in 28 countries, with around three quarters of its business conducted in India where it is estimated that 500 million people use a Godrej product or service every day. In 2014, the group employed 28,000 people.
The Godrej Group is involved in palm oil through its subsidiaries at multiple stages within the supply chain. Godrej Industries, a holding company within the Godrej Group, is involved in a range of activities and sectors including the manufacture and marketing of oleo-chemicals as well as their precursors and derivatives, edible oils and bakery fats. Godrej International Limited, a subsidiary of Godrej Industries, trades vegetable oils such as palm oil internationally. Godrej Agrovet Ltd is an agribusiness subsidiary of Godrej Industries; it is India's largest animal feed manufacturer, producing over a million tons a year, and is also involved in palm oil production with 51,000 hectares of smallholder cultivation in India, four mills and a total land bank of 235,000 hectares. Finally, Godrej Consumer Products Ltd, the largest Indian personal care company, uses palm oil in its soaps. It is the largest Grade 1 quality soap and second largest toilet soap provider in India with brands such as Cinthol and No.1, and is currently seeking to increase its market share in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.

Hengan International is a Chinese manufacturer of paper products including sanitary napkins, disposable nappies and tissue paper.  Hengan International Group Co Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Coty is a manufacturer and distributor of beauty products based in the US, with business segments in luxury, consumer beauty and professional beauty.  Coty Inc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Royal Golden Eagle (RGE) is a holding company with interests in natural resources and manufacturing, operating around the world. Its businesses include pulp and paper, palm oil, specialty fibres, and energy. The group’s two pulp and paper subsidiaries, APRIL and Asia Symbol, together produce about 4.6 million metric tons of pulp and more than 1.7 million metric tons of paper products, making it one of the major producers in Indonesia. Asian Agri and Apical, its palm oil subsidiaries, have more than 160,000 hectares of palm oil landbank and an annual refinery capacity of 3.7 million metric tons. RGE is also one of the top importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.  Royal Golden Eagle is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp & paper.

Sumitomo Mitsui Trust are a financial services company headquartered in Japan serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include asset management, inheritance and succession, property administration, loans, investment support, and insurance. As of 2024, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust's total assets under management amount to over 450 billion USD. They are an important shareholder and lender in Forest 500 companies. In the 2024 selection, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust was providing 49.4 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

rows.coprofile: Olam international is a leading agricultural commodity business operating throughout the supply chain across 70 countries. It is a global market leader in many agricultural commodities such as cocoa and coffee, but also is a major player in African oil palm and forestry. Olam’s subsidiary, Congolaise Industrielle de Bois (CIB) operates forestry concessions in the Republic of Congo. The company is also active in soy cultivation and processing in South America and Africa.  Olam International  is selected as a powerbroker for soy and timber and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Fast Retailing isa Japanese clothing retailer operating through well-known brands such as UNIQLO and J Brand.  Fast Retailing is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper.

The Kroger Co. is a leading edible grocery retailer in the US. The company’s supermarkets and convenience stores operate under various banners including Smith’s, Fred Meyer’s and Food 4 Less. In addition to its retail operations, The Kroger Co. owns a string of food processing facilities. With sizeable operations in food processing and retail The Kroger Co. is exposed to forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy and beef.  Kroger Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: Restaurant Brands International, created in 2014 after a merger of the two famous brands Burger King and Tim Hortons, is one of the world’s largest fast food companies. With its two brands, the company operates 19,000 restaurants in almost 100 countries. It is one of the top fast food companies in Europe, the US and in the world. The varied menu of both chains expose them to a range of forest risk commodities.  Restaurant Brands International is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Groupe Auchan is an unlisted company, whose operations include hypermarkets and supermarkets. It is owned by the Mulliez Family through the holding company Association Familiale Mulliez (AFM), which owned an 87.8% stake in the Group as of 2011. Although Groupe Auchan's largest market is France, it also has a significant presence in mainland Europe and China, and operates in total in 16 countries. Its origins are in hypermarkets, which were established in 1961 by Gerard Mulliez. As of 31 December 2014, the group operates 888 fully-consolidated hypermarkets, 862 fully-consolidated supermarkets, and 370 shopping centres. Other smaller businesses of Groupe Auchan include a furniture and interior design chain, which has 26 French stores.
The group's hypermarkets operate under multiple banners such as Auchan and Alcampo, offering a broad range of products including groceries, clothing, furniture, DIY equipment and electronics. Groupe Auchan's supermarkets also operate through multiple banners such as Simply Markets, A2Pas, ATAK and Partisans de GoÃ»t. These offer a narrower range of products, concentrating on groceries. Together hypermarkets and supermarkets account for over 95% of group revenue.
In 1979, Groupe Auchan formed a stakeholder agreement making AFM the leading shareholder of ADEO.  ADEO SA is active in the international do-it-yourself (DIY) industry. It is the largest DIY retailer in Europe and among the top five DIY retailers globally in terms of net revenue. Through its numerous subsidiaries, it operates a chain of DIY stores providing construction materials, home decoration products, garden supplies, and kitchen and bathroom goods. Incorporated in 1986, ADEO is based in Lille, France and is comprised of 30 companies within 15 brands. It is a federation of autonomous companies, some of which are wholly-owned and some held under franchise, and comprises 391 franchise stores and 589 integrated stores in 12 countries, including Brazil and China and throughout Europe. Leroy Merlin is one the group's major companies; it is a major retail outlet in the home improvement sector, with almost 377 home improvement stores in 12 countries. The smaller, local chains run by ADEO include AKI, Bricocenter, and Weldom, and warehouse stores include Bricoman and Bricomart.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company that specialises in dairy products. The company has more than 266 production sites spanning over 51 countries. Under a range of different brands the company mainly produce cheese, milk, cream, butter, and milk powder. Lactalis claim to be the largest dairy group in the world, and the number one cheese group in Europe. Groupe Lactalis use palm oil in its products and is exposed to soy as a component of animal feed for dairy products.  Groupe Lactalis is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Through their subsidiaries their services cover: corporate finance, securities, wealth management, insurance, and retail banking services. As of 2022, NatWest Group's total assets amount to more than 1.07 Trillion GBP. NatWest Group are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, NatWest Group was providing 15 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Wilmar International Ltd. is a global agribusiness group involved in the cultivation, processing, refining, merchandising and trading of a wide range of agricultural products, including palm oil and soya. The company is one of the world's largest oil palm plantation owners and processors, reportedly controlling around 45% of worldwide palm oil trade sourced from more than 80% of global palm oil growers. Wilmar is also a major player in the soybean crushing industry with a global crushing capacity of 36 million metric tons per annum, the majority of which is in China. The company claims to be one of the world's largest producers of consumer edible oils.

Their services include investment banking, corporate finance, asset and wealth management, and trading services. As of 2017, BTG Pactual's total assets under management amount to more than 125 billion BRL. BTG Pactual are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

Campbell Soup is an American company that produces soups, snacks, beverages, ready meals, and packaged food. The company has many famous brands including Prego, V8, Pepperidge Farm, and Campbell’s. The company use palm oil, and soy in its products.  Campbell Soup Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Their services include investment banking, capital markets, wealth management, corporate finance and retail banking services. As of 2017, UBS' total assets amount to more than 910 billion CHF, with more than 310 billion CHF of gross loans. UBS are among the top shareholders and lenders for Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Wm Morrison Supermarkets PLC operates a chain of around 500 supermarkets in the UK. It has food manufacturing capabilities in meat, fish and bakery products and the breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Wm Morrison Supermarkets PLC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Clariant AG is a Swiss multinational speciality chemicals company using both palm oil and soy in the manufacture of their various products. Clariant develops, produces, markets and sells specialty chemical products for various end markets including paints, cosmetics and oils.

Danzer is a German timber company based in Austria that produces veneer, lumber and other wood products from hardwood. It claims to be the largest producer of decorative veneer in the world.  Danzer Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

Home Depot is an American home improvement retailer. The company sells building materials, flooring, hardware, storage solutions, furniture, paint, and electrical appliances among other products. Home Depot have over 2000 stores spread over the US, Mexico, and Canada. With more than 1 million products, Home Depot claims to be the biggest home improvement retailer in the world. The company’s retail operations require large amounts of timber.  Home Depot is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging.

TIAA-CREF are a financial services company headquartered in the US that primarily serves private and institutional investors in the not-for-profit sector including education, health care, government and research. Their services cover pensions, investments and insurance. In 2017, their total assets under management amount to more than 950 billion USD. TIAA-CREF are among the top 15 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 2.5 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 20 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 22 billion USD worth of shares.

Sekisui House is a Japanese construction company with numerous subsidiaries spanning real estate, remodelling, manufacturing and financial management, among others. It specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing, offering both steel and timber frame solutions. As a market leader in this field Sekisui House is exposed to the forest risk commodity timber.   Sekisui House Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Hormel Foods is one of the largest manufacturers of ready meals in the world.
