rows.coprofile:
LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA (LVMH) is a French company, with its headquarters in Paris, engaged in the luxury goods industry. The group was formed following the merger of the MoÃ«t Hennessy and Louis Vuitton companies in 1987; however its origins extend back much further in the history of the development of the French luxury goods industry. Louis Vuitton's flagship brand was launched in 1854, after which it continued to specialise solely in handmade leather bags for over 70 years, while, Moet Hennessy's origins are even earlier, as the company was involved in the wine industry for 100 years prior.
LVMH currently operates in five main segments: wines and spirits; fashion and leather goods; perfumes and cosmetics; watches and jewellery; and selective retailing. Within these five sectors, LVMH has a portfolio of more than 60 brands and an international network of more than 3,000 stores. Of particular importance is the company's fashion and leather goods division, which comprises well-known luggage, leather goods and apparel and accessories brands, such as Louis Vuitton, Givenchy and Marc Jacobs.
In 2013, the fashion and leather goods business accounted for the majority of the group's total revenue. The group is an industry leader in the bags and luggage market worldwide, occupying the top position globally in terms of market share and leading positions in the individual markets of China, Western Europe and the USA.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, Natural Capital Coalition

rows.coprofile:
The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

Asics Corporation was founded in 1949 in Kobe, Japan. It was incorporated twenty years later through the merger of three companies: Onitsuka, GTO and JELENK. The company has two business segments: sports product manufacture and sales; and outdoor products manufacture and sales. The sports segment is involved in the manufacture and sale of sportswear, sports shoes and equipment. This part of the business also oversees the management and delivery of products, the planning of products, and the factoring and sales support businesses. The other business segment is focused on the manufacture and sale of outdoor products through its subsidiaries, of which it has more than 50 globally. Asics Corporation employs more than 7,400 people worldwide.
Asics Corporation is among the top ten manufacturers of footwear globally and is particularly well known for its running shoes, which are marketed to both professional and amateur athletes.  The company is therefore a significant user of leather. Asics Corporation operates a number of flagship stores and the expansion of its retail network is a key strategy for the company. The company promotes its brands through participation in a number of high profile sporting events, for example through its sponsorship of major marathons and the use of Asics equipment by top sporting teams and federations on the world stage. On top of the Asics brand, the company sells fashion-oriented items under the Onitsuka Tiger brand.

Founded in 1927 in Cologne, Germany, the REWE Group employs over 330,000 individuals in 15,000 stores. Germany is REWE Group's largest market, generating 70% of the Group's revenue in 2014, but the company has operations across 11 other European countries.
REWE Group operates in the food sector through multiple chains and formats including; REWE, REWE Center, REWE City, Penny (a discount store) and TEMMA (an organic supermarket). Supermarkets offer a number of store (own) brands such as Penny, ja!, REWE, Muhlenhof and REWE Bio,  whose offerings include meat products, diary and bakery products. In 2014, REWE Group reported using 10,800 tonnes of palm oil in its own brand products.
REWE Group also operates DIY stores under the Toom Baumarkt and B1 Discount Baumarkt brands. Toom Baumarkt stores provide the Toom quality store branded products, with a broad range of items ranging from garden furniture to plant seeds. REWE Group is also active in the Travel & Tourism and Consumer Electronics retail sectors.

The Adidas Group is a footwear and sports apparel company operating in over 160 countries worldwide. Famous brands include Reebok, TaylorMade and Adidas itself. Processed leather is used in many of its footwear products. The group has one of the largest global brand shares for footwear retail in terms of global retail value. It is also one of the largest footwear retailers in Western Europe, China and Hong Kong, as well as placing among the top five in the US.
AmorePacific Corp is a Korean manufacturer of personal and household products. In 2015, it was reported that the company was the 14th largest cosmetics company in the world.

Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

IFFCO is an international business house, established in 1975 and based in the United Arab Emirates. IFFCO manufactures and markets a range of products for the mass consumer and industrial markets; producing around 7000 products and with a portfolio of 28 flagship brands, it sells its products in 84 countries worldwide, and has over 12,000 employees and offices in 21 countries.
The group's main business segments are: Impulse Foods; Agribusiness; Oils and Fats; Packaging; and Sales and Distribution. IFFCO therefore has multiple operations of relevance to forest risk commodity supply chain. For example, it's involvement in the production of packaged food, oils and fats, and in poultry farming, makes palm oil and soya of particular significance. Its Impulse Foods division manufactures and markets a range of convenience foods, including biscuits, savoury snacks, chocolates, confectionery, and ice creams, with brands such as London Dairy, Igloo, Tom and Break. While through its Agribusiness segment, IFFCO produces a range of food products, including poultry and eggs, bakery ingredients and frozen meat. IFFCO's joint venture with Oman Flour Mill is a fully-integrated poultry operation including a feed mill, parent bird and broiler farm, hatchery and processing facility. Finally, IFFCO's Oils and Fats segment manufactures products for the consumer and industrial markets, specialising in cooking oils, culinary products, and industrial fats for the food and personal care industries.
IFFCO has a worldwide presence, through its in-country offices, 33 manufacturing facilities and 6 distribution centres. Of particular note are IFFCO (Pakistan) Private Limited, IFFCO (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, and the group's various joint ventures, which include FELDA-IFFCO. FELDA-IFFCO is a partnership with plantation giant, FELDA; the largest producer of crude palm oil in Malaysia, with plantation land banks totalling 850,000 hectares, management of 530,000 hectares of plantations and a 7% share of the production market in 2011. FELDA-IFFCO also own 15 refineries in Malaysia, China, Turkey, Pakistan, South Africa and Canada, as well as four kernel crushing plants with a processing capacity of 8.4 million tonnes per year; producing around 20% of Malaysia's total crude palm kernel oil.
 IFFCO Pakistan is a major player in the edible oils and fats market. It operates the largest edible oil refinery in the country and is the only multinational company in Pakistan's edible oils industry. It procures raw materials domestically and internationally, including from Malaysia through FELDA-IFFCO. FINALLY, IFFCO Malaysia is an integrated oleo-chemical complex operating soap noodle and finishing plants that produce a variety of soap products and animal feed supplements.

rows.coprofile: Staples Inc is one of the world’s largest specialist retailers of office supplies, with key product lines in stationary, furniture and technology products. Amongst its products are a wide variety of paper goods, including copy paper, printer paper, POS rolls and letterheads. As a leading retailer of these goods Staples is exposed to the forest risk commodities paper, pulp and timber.   Staples Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and pulp & paper.

The Charoen Pokphand Group (C. P. Group) is a diverse Thai business conglomerate with 200 subsidiaries in 18 countries that cover the agribusiness, food, telecommunications, and retail industries, amongst others. The group operates integrated food supply chains for poultry and pork involving it heavily in the production of animal feed and food products. It is one of the largest poultry companies in Thailand and places among the ten largest poultry companies in the world. Its subsidiaries are also among the top fifteen global producers of animal feed.

Boparan Holdings is the parent company of the 2 Sisters Food Group, which produces around a third of all poultry products eaten every day in the United Kingdom. 2 Sisters Food Group operates in three divisions (protein, added value and chilled, and meals) and its main customers include restaurants such as KFC and supermarkets including Aldi, Asda, Co-op, Lidl, Marks & Spencer and Tesco. Boparan also owns restaurant groups including Giraffe and Carluccio's and other food companies including Bernard Matthews.   Boparan Holdings is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and beef.

Saint Gobain is a French multinational corporation that designs, manufactures, and distributes building materials. Major brands include Jewson in the UK and Point P in France. It is one of the largest building material suppliers in Europe and operates in a total of 64 countries worldwide, including across Southeast Asia and South America. It is one of the largest European distributors of building materials.  Saint Gobain S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Suzano Papel e Celulose SA produces paper and eucalyptus pulp, with operations across South and Central America, Asia and Africa. It has 1.2 million hectares of forest, of which 520,000 hectares are planted.

Dunkin' Brands Group is a franchisor of quick service restaurants including the two major chains Dunkin' Donuts and Baskin-Robbins. Dunkin' Donuts has more than 11,500 restaurants in 40 countries worldwide and offers coffee and baked goods including doughnuts and bagels. Baskin-Robbins has more than 7,000 shops in nearly 50 countries offering ice-cream and beverages. The diverse menus of both expose the group to several forest risk commodities. Dunkin' Brands is one of the ten largest food providers globally by market share.

Itaú Unibanco are banking group based in Brazil serving both private and commercial customers. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, wealth management, insurance, pensions and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.3 trillion BRL, including over 400 billion BRL in loans. Itaú Unibanco are one of the top 60 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 3 billion USD of loans to companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

The company is one of the largest producers of animal feed in the Netherlands and in the world. ForFarmers also claims to be the market leader for animal feed in Europe. Wilmar International Ltd. is a global agribusiness group involved in the cultivation, processing, refining, merchandising and trading of a wide range of agricultural products, including palm oil and soya. The company is one of the world's largest oil palm plantation owners and processors, reportedly controlling around 45% of worldwide palm oil trade sourced from more than 80% of global palm oil growers. Wilmar is also a major player in the soybean crushing industry with a global crushing capacity of 36 million metric tons per annum, the majority of which is in China. The company claims to be one of the world's largest producers of consumer edible oils.

Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is a Japanese company, established in 1935 and incorporated in 1955; it is involved in the manufacture and distribution of food and drink products. The company has three main business segments: Beverages and Food Manufacturing and Sale; Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing and Sale; and Others. The company's original and still most recognisable product is a probiotic fermented milk drink sold under the Yakult brand. This continues to be the company's main product, particularly in the overseas market, where average daily sales of Yakult products in early 2013 were over 22.5 million. However, aside from its fermented milk and yogurt products (which include the Joie, Sofuhl, and Purela, amongst others) Yakult also offers non-dairy beverages such as flavoured tea drinks and juices, a range of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food products, including noodles.
As of 2013, the company had around 79 subsidiaries and 18 associated companies. The company has overseas and domestic operations, with its operations outside of Japan starting in 1964, when its Taiwanese subsidiary was established. Since then, this has grown and the company is now active in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide, including in Europe, the US, Brazil, Mexico, China, South Korea, Hong Kong, Indonesia, and elsewhere in Asia.
Yakult is a significant player in the global packaged food market, demonstrated by its leading position in a variety of markets worldwide. For example, specifically, it ranks among the top three companies in the dairy products market in Japan, and among the top ten for the packaged food industry overall. It is also among the top five companies with the largest market shares in the South Korean noodle industry, and holds a similarly high market share in the market for noodles in the United States, and is in the top 25 companies in the world for the packaged food industry.
Signatory to UN-convened Net-Zero Asset Owners Alliance, Paris Aligned Investment Initiative. PKA finances the Forest 500 with a total of 934 USDM

The Godrej Group is an Indian conglomerate which, through its subsidiaries, operates in the consumer goods, real estate management, industrial engineering, furniture, appliances, security services, and agricultural products sectors. Established by Ardeshir Godrej in 1897, the Godrej family retain ownership of the group, although its subsidiaries Godrej Industries and Godrej Properties are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The company operates in 28 countries, with around three quarters of its business conducted in India where it is estimated that 500 million people use a Godrej product or service every day. In 2014, the group employed 28,000 people.
The Godrej Group is involved in palm oil through its subsidiaries at multiple stages within the supply chain. Godrej Industries, a holding company within the Godrej Group, is involved in a range of activities and sectors including the manufacture and marketing of oleo-chemicals as well as their precursors and derivatives, edible oils and bakery fats. Godrej International Limited, a subsidiary of Godrej Industries, trades vegetable oils such as palm oil internationally. Godrej Agrovet Ltd is an agribusiness subsidiary of Godrej Industries; it is India's largest animal feed manufacturer, producing over a million tons a year, and is also involved in palm oil production with 51,000 hectares of smallholder cultivation in India, four mills and a total land bank of 235,000 hectares. Finally, Godrej Consumer Products Ltd, the largest Indian personal care company, uses palm oil in its soaps. It is the largest Grade 1 quality soap and second largest toilet soap provider in India with brands such as Cinthol and No.1, and is currently seeking to increase its market share in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

The Gap Inc. is a leading global apparel retailer selling apparel, accessories and personal care products for men, women and children through its various brands. Gap Inc. was established with the opening of a single Gap store in San Francisco in the United States in 1969. Since then the company has expanded greatly through the establishment of several other retail brands, including Banana Republic, Old Navy, Athleta, and Intermix.
The company has around 3,300 company-operated stores and 400 franchise stores in more than 90 countries alongside e-commerce sales operations in almost 100 countries. Its company-operated stores are located in the US, Canada, the UK, France, Ireland, Japan, China, Italy and, since 2014, Taiwan. Gap Inc. also has franchise agreements with unaffiliated franchisees to operate Gap, Old Navy and Banana Republic stores throughout Asia, Australia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Gap Inc. employs around 140,000 full and part time individuals.
The company's flagship brand, Gap, which sells casual, American style apparel, continues to be the most prominent of the group's retail brands, with over 1,430 company stores and over 340 franchises worldwide. Gap Inc.'s retail brands vary in their retailing of own-brand and other designer brands. Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy and Athleta brands each sell their own own-label products, while the Intermix brands stocks both its own-label products and those of other designers.
Gap Inc is among the top three retailers of private-label apparel and the top five of all clothing retailers globally. Each of the company's brands stock a range of leather goods, including shoes, belts and bags. For example, Intermix, which was acquired by Gap Inc in 2012, offers a range of branded luxury accessories, including leather bags. Banana Republic and Gap brands similarly stock a range of leather goods, including leather jackets for men and women, and leather handbags, belts and shoes. Gap Inc. does not directly own or operate its own manufacturing facilities, and as of 2012, its branded apparel is produced in around 923 factories in 32 countries worldwide.

Association Familiale Mulliez (AFM) is a holding company for the businesses owned by the Mulliez family. Subsidiaries include Auchan Holding which  is one of the largest food retailers in the world and has hypermarkets and supermarkets in several countries, as well as operating a furniture and interior design chain in France. AFM also own restaurants including Carluccio's and Giraffe Restaurants, home improvement companies including Leroy Merlin and fashion brands including Orsay. Through its operations the company is exposed to several forest risk commodities.  Association Familiale Mulliez (AFM) is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Saint Gobain is a French multinational corporation that designs, manufactures, and distributes building materials. Major brands include Jewson in the UK and Point P in France. It is one of the largest building material suppliers in Europe and operates in a total of 64 countries worldwide, including across Southeast Asia and South America. It is one of the largest European distributors of building materials.  Saint Gobain S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Kraft Heinz is one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world. Its numerous iconic brands include Kraft, Heinz, Kool-Aid, Capri-Sun and Philadelphia. As one of the leading international food product manufacturers Kraft Heinz is exposed to a range of forest risk commodities. Notably, its product range involves the use of palm oil, soy, pulp and paper.   Kraft Heinz Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

The Royal Bank of Canada are a banking and financial services group headquartered in Canada serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include wealth management, insurance, capital markets, investments, commercial banking and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 1.2 trillion CAD, with net loans worth nearly 480 billion CAD. The Royal Bank of Canada are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.
Dai Nippon Printing is a Japanese printing company operating in publishing and commercial printing services. The company reported a total revenue of ¥1,412,252 million in 2018.

Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company with a substantial portfolio of businesses operating in a diverse range of sectors. Founded in 1938, it employs over 35,000 people across a number of sectors such as manufacturing; trading and ï¬nancial services; oil and gas exploration; print and packaging; agriculture; ï¬sheries; real estate; and mining. In addition to its core business activities in Yemen, the group operates as a manufacturing firm and trading company across four global regions: Africa; Asia; Europe; and the Middle East. Its global business focuses on non-food, and beverage and food products such as confectionery and biscuits. It has an extensive logistics infrastructure to manufacture and distribute its own and partners' products across its global markets.
Pacific Inter-Link (PIL), one of the group's Malaysia-based companies, is involved in the processing and trading of palm oil. It was incorporated in 1988 to export commodities and employs 1,750 people in Malaysia and Indonesia. Its refineries had an annual processing capacity of 1.3 million tonnes per annum in 2012. PIL is one of the major exporters of palm oil from Asia to Africa and the Middle East, exporting to around 64 countries in total. The company is currently looking to expand further into the African market, with the development of new refineries in Ethiopia and Kenya. The company's brands include Avena and Madina, which both sell various palm oil products, such as margarine, shortening, cooking oil, and vegetable ghee, as well as a range of packaged food, including canned fish and meat, and pasta products. On top of its core palm oil products, the group also supplies dairy products under the Milgro, Milac, and Sheeba brands.

Sekisui House is a Japanese construction company with numerous subsidiaries spanning real estate, remodelling, manufacturing and financial management, among others. It specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing, offering both steel and timber frame solutions. As a market leader in this field Sekisui House is exposed to the forest risk commodity timber.   Sekisui House Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.
Daio Paper Corporation are a Japanese manufacturer of paper products with business segments in paper and paperboard, and home and personal care.

Meredith Corporation is a leading American media and marketing company operating in publishing, printing as well as broadcasting. Their publications have a readership of over 120 million with a paid circulation of over 40 million having published magazines such as Sports Illustrated and Fortune Magazine. They also own various well-known national television stations such as CBS, FOX and ABC.

Asics Corporation was founded in 1949 in Kobe, Japan. It was incorporated twenty years later through the merger of three companies: Onitsuka, GTO and JELENK. The company has two business segments: sports product manufacture and sales; and outdoor products manufacture and sales. The sports segment is involved in the manufacture and sale of sportswear, sports shoes and equipment. This part of the business also oversees the management and delivery of products, the planning of products, and the factoring and sales support businesses. The other business segment is focused on the manufacture and sale of outdoor products through its subsidiaries, of which it has more than 50 globally. Asics Corporation employs more than 7,400 people worldwide.
Asics Corporation is among the top ten manufacturers of footwear globally and is particularly well known for its running shoes, which are marketed to both professional and amateur athletes.  The company is therefore a significant user of leather. Asics Corporation operates a number of flagship stores and the expansion of its retail network is a key strategy for the company. The company promotes its brands through participation in a number of high profile sporting events, for example through its sponsorship of major marathons and the use of Asics equipment by top sporting teams and federations on the world stage. On top of the Asics brand, the company sells fashion-oriented items under the Onitsuka Tiger brand.

Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is one of the world's leading marketers of branded casual, active lifestyle, work, outdoor sport, athletic, children's and uniform footwear and apparel. Wolverine owns a number of well-known brands, including Merrell, Sperry Top-Sider, Hush Puppies, Saucony, Wolverine, Keds, Stride Rite, Sebago, Cushe, Chaco, Bates, HYTEST and Soft Style. The company is also the licensee of other recognised brands, including Cat, Harley-Davidson and Patagonia. The company's products are sold by leading retailers in around 200 countries and territories. Wolverine also operates 463 retail stores through leases with various third-party landlords in the US, Canada and United Kingdom.
In addition to its footwear and apparel business, Wolverine markets pigskin leather through its Wolverine Leathers subsidiary. About 98% (based on pairs) of the company's footwear products are sourced from third-party suppliers located primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Until recently the rest came from company-owned sources in the US and the Dominican Republic but the latter was recently closed.
In October 2012, Wolverine acquired Collective Brands Inc. via a consortium that also includes Golden Gate Capital and Blum Capital Partners. Collective Brands is in itself a major player in the footwear industry (owning the Payless brand, amongst others); it is a very large footwear retailer with more than 4,400 stores in over 30 countries.

Sekisui House Ltd has operations in the housing construction industry, and in real estate brokerage and leasing. The company was established in 1960 and has its headquarters in Osaka, Japan. It claims to be Japan's largest and best known home builder and is listed among the largest companies globally as the second largest Japanese construction services company. 
Sekisui House Ltd has numerous subsidiaries across its various business segments, which comprise trade, brokerage and lease of real estate; remodelling; construction; surveying; and others including financial services and manufacturing. The company operates 19 construction subsidiaries across Japan under Sekisui Construction Ltd and as of January 2014 had constructed almost 2.2 million houses. Sekisui House Ltd has also been active in the Australian market since 2009, under Sekisui House Australia.
Sekisui House Ltd specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing and is the main player in Japan's prefabrication industry. Specifically, Sekisui House Ltd constructs and sells steel- and wooden-frame housing. The company's steel-frame housing was launched in the 1970's, marking the entrance of Sekisui House into the housing industry. This was followed by the launch of the company' wooden frame unit housing, Two-U Home, in 1982. The company now builds a variety of wooden frame housing, for example, the Gravis Bella wooden frame model, in its detached housing business. On top of its initial construction activities, Sekisui House Ltd also offers interior decoration and furnishing services.
The major shareholder of Sekisui House Ltd is Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, which has operations worldwide and also has business interests in urban infrastructure, environmental products and high performance plastics.

rows.coprofile: Celulosa Arauco y Constitución is a forestry conglomerate based in Chile producing and trading in wood and timber products. The company is controlled by the Angelini Group through holding company, Empresas COPEC.

Hillshire Brands Co. (Hillshire) is a food giant from Chicago which manufactures and markets meat-based products. Founded in 1939, Hillshire acquired many notable brands over the years, including Jimmy Dean and Ball Park Franks, which is reportedly the top hotdog brand in the US and worth over $500 million in revenue.  Hillshire has 9,500 employees and sales of $4.09 billion as of May 2013, placing it among the Forbes Global 2000 list of the world's largest public companies. Although the largest market for its six major brands is in the US, it also has a strong international presence, ranking in the top 20 in the world for frozen processed food, third globally for chilled processed food and second in the US in the same category. Outside of the US, it is amongst the five largest frozen processed food companies in Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Hillshire uses palm oil in its products; it sources palm-oil-containing raw materials for use in its manufacturing.
Hillshire itself has recently been acquired by Tyson Foods Inc., one of the largest producers and processors of meat, poultry and prepared foods in the world. Headquartered in Arkansas, Tyson was established in 1935 and remains under the ownership of the Tyson family. Although the majority of Tyson's operations are within the US, it also runs in country activities in poultry production in China, India, Mexico and Brazil, which utilise soya bean in poultry feed. The buyout of Hillshire by Tyson marks one of the biggest mergers in the packaged food industry and establishes Tyson firmly in the top two companies in the global processed meat market.
Frigol S.A was selected as a powerbroker for Beef (Trader, Processor) and is also assessed for Leather (Processor)

Sime Darby Bhd. was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Processor, Producer, Trader) and is also assessed for Soy (Processor), Leather (Manufacturer), Rubber (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)
Fast Retailing isa Japanese clothing retailer operating through well-known brands such as UNIQLO and J Brand.  Fast Retailing is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper.

Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is a leading international manufacturer of footwear and apparel, with product markets in approximately 200 countries worldwide. The company owns numerous well-known brands including Cat Footwear, Hush Puppies, Merrell, Saucony and Sebago. As a leading producer of apparel and footwear products Wolverine is exposed to the forest risk commodity leather, which is a key material in this sector.   Wolverine World Wide Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

R. R. Donnelley & Sons Co. is an American commercial printing company. The company offers services within commercial and digital printing, direct mail, printing labels, statement printing, and digital solutions. The large-scale printing operations require a vast amount of pulp and paper.  R. R. Donnelley & Sons Co. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Bank of Montreal are a financial services provider headquartered in Canada serving private and corporate clients, institutions, and governments. Their services include personal, commercial and investment banking, loans and mortgages, insurance, wealth management, corporate lending, bonds, equities, fixed income investing, research, risk management, and treasury and advisory services. As of 2017, Bank of Montreal's total assets amount to over 700 billion USD with 360 billion USD worth of loans. They are also among the top 70 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with shares amounting to over 4 billion USD.

COFCO Group was founded in 1949 and operates in the edible seed market via China Agri Holdings Ltd. It is the second largest crusher of oilseeds (behind Wilmar International) and has 13% of the market share of oilseed crushing capability and over 9% of the market share for soybeans. Its manufacturing plants are located close to major food consumption markets including in Tianjin, Jiangsu, Shandong, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei and Xinjiang. Historically, the company has focused its business activities in downstream activities. However, in February 2014, COFCO bought a majority stake (51%) in Nidera, a Dutch commodities trader, in order to gain access to South American grain and oilseed goods, while in April 2014, the company acquired a controlling stake (51%) in Noble Agri, which owns oilseeds processing plants and a grain processing and distribution business. In May 2015, COFCO announced it will merge its holdings in Nidera and Noble Agri to create a new entity, COFCO International Holdings, in a joint venture with China Investment Corp, a sovereign wealth fund who will own 19.9% of the new business, with the ultimate intention of merging COFCO's own domestic business into COFCO International to combine COFCO's oil, grain and sugar assets.
COFCO Group retains a strong presence in the downstream market, with a number of branded goods sold across China. They sell shortening and margarine as well as a number of speciality products such as soybean milk fat. In total, their annual sales volume exceeds 120,000 tonnes across 31 Chinese provinces. Its brands include Sihai for soybean meal products and Fuzhiquan for cooking oils.
As well as being a major player in the processed food industry, COFCO Group has a long history in the timber sector and claims to be the largest integrated timber merchant in China. One of the Group's subsidiaries, China Timber Co. Ltd., has operated traded timber internationally for over fifty years. It imports a wide variety of timber and timber products from a range of countries, including raw timber from Papua New Guinea and Myanmar; and plywood, construction materials and furniture from Africa and South America. It also exports wood flooring and plywood and other manufactured wood products to the US, Europe, Japan and India.
Of particular relevance are China Timber's operations in the Republic of Gabon, where it holds five timber companies engaged in the direct harvesting of timber and timber processing activities. It has around one million hectares of tropical hardwood forests. Specifically, it operates Sunly Gabon, which is one of the largest Chinese firms operating in the Gabonese forestry sector and has several hundred thousand hectares of forest concessions in the north-east, east and southern parts of the country.

As a market leader in this field Sekisui House is exposed to the forest risk commodity timber.   Sekisui House Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Mitsui & Co., Ltd. is a Japanese trading company operating worldwide. It sells canned and chilled foods, packaging materials, pharmaceuticals and feedstuffs, among others.  Mitsui & Co. Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

Campbell Soup is an American company that produces soups, snacks, beverages, ready meals, and packaged food. The company has many famous brands including Prego, V8, Pepperidge Farm, and Campbell’s. The Godrej Group is an Indian conglomerate which, through its subsidiaries, operates in the consumer goods, real estate management, industrial engineering, furniture, appliances, security services, and agricultural products sectors. Established by Ardeshir Godrej in 1897, the Godrej family retain ownership of the group, although its subsidiaries Godrej Industries and Godrej Properties are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The company operates in 28 countries, with around three quarters of its business conducted in India where it is estimated that 500 million people use a Godrej product or service every day. In 2014, the group employed 28,000 people.
The Godrej Group is involved in palm oil through its subsidiaries at multiple stages within the supply chain. Godrej Industries, a holding company within the Godrej Group, is involved in a range of activities and sectors including the manufacture and marketing of oleo-chemicals as well as their precursors and derivatives, edible oils and bakery fats. Godrej International Limited, a subsidiary of Godrej Industries, trades vegetable oils such as palm oil internationally. Godrej Agrovet Ltd is an agribusiness subsidiary of Godrej Industries; it is India's largest animal feed manufacturer, producing over a million tons a year, and is also involved in palm oil production with 51,000 hectares of smallholder cultivation in India, four mills and a total land bank of 235,000 hectares. Finally, Godrej Consumer Products Ltd, the largest Indian personal care company, uses palm oil in its soaps. It is the largest Grade 1 quality soap and second largest toilet soap provider in India with brands such as Cinthol and No.1, and is currently seeking to increase its market share in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

Samling Global Ltd group of companies is a Malaysian conglomerate with diverse operations, including in the timber and oil palm sectors.  Founded in 1963, Samling's core activities are in the forest products industry, where its operations span the length of the supply chain, from harvesting to processing, manufacturing and distribution.
Samling Global Ltd has a complicated corporate structure, with numerous subsidiaries and holding companies.  For example, Samling Global Ltd is an investment holding company incorporated in Bermuda, with numerous wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, the US, the British Virgin Islands and Japan. These companies in turn have a variety of subsidiaries, for example, in China, Malaysia, Guyana, Indonesia and India.
Of particular relevance, is Samling Global Ltd's involvement in the timber trade in Sarawak, Malaysia. Under Lingui Developments Bhd, Samling manages a total of 1.3 million hectares. Lingui Developments Bhd is an investment holding and forest resources and wood products company. It produces logs, plywood and veneer, fibreboard, doors and door facings, and kitchen counters and products, primarily for the export market and in particular for Japan, China, India, Korea and North America. Under its wholly owned subsidiary, Barama Company Ltd, Samling Global Ltd is also one of the biggest forestry companies in Guyana, where it holds 1.6 million hectares of forest concessions and produces sawnwood.
Samling Global Ltd is well established in the export markets of China and Japan. In China, it manufactures plywood, laminated veneer lumber and flooring and also distributes flooring through Elegant Living, one of China's major flooring distributors. Samling Global Ltd's access to the Japanese market is facilitated through its partnerships with Itochu Corporation, one of Japan's major traders and property developers, and Daiken Corporation, through which Samling Global Ltd supplies tropical logs and plywood for construction.
Samling Global Ltd has also expanded its operations into oil palm. Under Glenealy Plantations (Malaya) Bhd, it has plantations in Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, covering a total area of over 60,000 hectares; and also operates palm oil mills in Sabah and Sarawak. Samling Global Ltd is also part of a consortium developing acacia plantations in Malaysia to supply wood for the pulp and paper industry. This consortium is made up of Samling Strategic Corp Sdn Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, and KTS Timber Industries Bhd, all of which are major timber companies in Sarawak.

Societe Generale are a banking group headquartered in France that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services span corporate finance, capital markets, insurance, wealth management, investments, securities and retail banking services. As of 2021, Societe Generale's total assets amount to more than 1.59 trillion EUR. Societe Generale are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors. IFFCO is a business house based in the United Arab Emirates. The company have products within impulse food, agri-business, oils and fats, chemicals, and packaging. Well-known brands include Allana, Tiffany, London Dairy, and Igloo. IFFCO provides services to consumers in the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe, West Asia, Australia, and the US. Operations within packaged foods and oils and fats typically use forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soy. The company also has key palm oil processing operations in Pakistan and Indonesia.  IFFCO is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Minerva S.A. is a meat processing company active in the slaughtering, processing and trading of cattle products, as well as pork and poultry. Its processing operations are predominantly in Brazil where it is one of the top owners of slaughterhouses, but there are also facilities in Paraguay, Uruguay and Colombia. The meat processed by Minerva S.A. is exported to over a hundred countries and it is one of largest exporters of beef from Brazil. The company also produces and markets leather.  Minerva S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for beef and leather and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Itaú Unibanco are the largest private bank based in Brazil serving both private and commercial customers. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, wealth management, insurance, pensions and retail banking services. As of 2024, their total assets amount to more than 400 Billion USD. Itaú Unibanco are one of the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. Founded in 1927 in Cologne, Germany, the REWE Group employs over 330,000 individuals in 15,000 stores. Germany is REWE Group's largest market, generating 70% of the Group's revenue in 2014, but the company has operations across 11 other European countries.
REWE Group operates in the food sector through multiple chains and formats including; REWE, REWE Center, REWE City, Penny (a discount store) and TEMMA (an organic supermarket). Supermarkets offer a number of store (own) brands such as Penny, ja!, REWE, Muhlenhof and REWE Bio,  whose offerings include meat products, diary and bakery products. In 2014, REWE Group reported using 10,800 tonnes of palm oil in its own brand products.
REWE Group also operates DIY stores under the Toom Baumarkt and B1 Discount Baumarkt brands. Toom Baumarkt stores provide the Toom quality store branded products, with a broad range of items ranging from garden furniture to plant seeds. REWE Group is also active in the Travel & Tourism and Consumer Electronics retail sectors.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

Arcor is an Argentinian manufacturer of foodstuffs and packaged food operating in five South American countries and selling products in over 120 countries worldwide. Products it produces include confectionary, ice-cream, chocolates, canned food, sugars, and packaging. The company has a worldwide presence, and is an important player in Brazil.  Arcor SAIC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

The company operates in America, Europe, and Asia both online and with physical stores. It is one of the top five bag and luggage retailers in the world by brand share. Coach is one of the leading such retailers in the US, and places among the top five in China and Hong Kong.

Adidas Group is a manufacturer of footwear, sports apparel, and accessories. Its products are known under brands such as Adidas, Reebok, and TaylorMade. The company is present in over 160 countries, and is one of the largest footwear retailers in Europe, China and the US. Processed leather is commonly used in its footwear products. Costco Wholesale Corporation as a global retailer and wholesaler. The company offers products such as groceries, apparel, furniture, houseware, office suppliers and health and beauty aids.  Costco Wholesale Corporation is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong (KLK) is a Malaysian agribusiness company active in the cultivation, processing and manufacturing of palm oil and rubber, as well as being involved in property development. The company has one of the top ten largest landbanks among palm oil producers, with more than 200,000 hectares of palm plantations across Malaysia, Indonesia and Liberia. It owns several mills and two refineries and these processed more than 4.5 million metric tons of fresh fruit bunches in 2015. KLK is also among the top ten importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia.

Dai Nippon Printing is a Japanese printing company operating in publishing and commercial printing services.  The large-scale printing operations require a vast amount of pulp and paper.  Dai Nippon Printing is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

As of 2024, Banco do Brasil's total assets amount to more than 425.9 billion USD. Banco do Brasil are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading. Lindt & Sprungli is exposed to the forest risk commodities palm oil and soy, which are used in many of its chocolate products soy is also hidden in its supply chain of dairy ingredients as a key component of animal feed. rows.coprofile: Target Corporation is a leading United States retailer with over 1,900 stores. It sells a variety of products including food, personal care items, paper products, furniture and apparel. Amongst these product lines Target sells several own-brand goods under labels including Market Pantry and Archer Farms. Through its retail and production operations Target is exposed to a variety of forest risk commodities.  Target Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef, leather, timber and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Natura&Co is a cosmetics company active throughout South America and which also has a consumer base in France. Its products range from make-up to fragrances and hair products, which exposes the company to forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soy. Natura&Co is one of the largest companies in Brazil for beauty and personal care as well as skin care. Natura&Co is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is one of the world's leading marketers of branded casual, active lifestyle, work, outdoor sport, athletic, children's and uniform footwear and apparel. Wolverine owns a number of well-known brands, including Merrell, Sperry Top-Sider, Hush Puppies, Saucony, Wolverine, Keds, Stride Rite, Sebago, Cushe, Chaco, Bates, HYTEST and Soft Style. The company is also the licensee of other recognised brands, including Cat, Harley-Davidson and Patagonia. The company's products are sold by leading retailers in around 200 countries and territories. Wolverine also operates 463 retail stores through leases with various third-party landlords in the US, Canada and United Kingdom.
In addition to its footwear and apparel business, Wolverine markets pigskin leather through its Wolverine Leathers subsidiary. About 98% (based on pairs) of the company's footwear products are sourced from third-party suppliers located primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Until recently the rest came from company-owned sources in the US and the Dominican Republic but the latter was recently closed.
In October 2012, Wolverine acquired Collective Brands Inc. via a consortium that also includes Golden Gate Capital and Blum Capital Partners. Collective Brands is in itself a major player in the footwear industry (owning the Payless brand, amongst others); it is a very large footwear retailer with more than 4,400 stores in over 30 countries.

Lowe's Companies is a major home improvement company based in the US with operations in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. In 2015, Lowe's had one of largest market shares for DIY, furniture, and homeware in the world. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and is one of the top four leading home improvement companies worldwide.

Associated British Foods is a diversified group with operations in food, ingredients and retail. The group’s business units include teas, cereals, sugars, and animal feed with such brands such as Twinings, Ryvita, and Blue Dragon. It is also a leading vendor in the baking ingredients market and the owner of the clothing retailer Primark. These diverse businesses expose the group to palm oil and soy in food production, soy in animal feed and leather in apparel. It is also among the largest producers of animal feed in Europe.  Associated British Foods Plc is selected as a powerbroker for soy, leather and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia are a financial services provider headquartered in Australia that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. They offer a range of products and services including retail, premium, business and institutional banking, funds management, pension programmes, insurance, and investment and share-broking products and services. As of 2017, Commonwealth Bank of Australia's total assets amount to over 970 billion AUD with over 730 billion AUD in loans. They are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 Companies.

Costco Wholesale Corporation as a global retailer and wholesaler. The company offers products such as groceries, apparel, furniture, houseware, office suppliers and health and beauty aids.  Costco Wholesale Corporation is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

SLC Agricola is a producer company based in Brazil. The produce soybean, cotton, and corn across more than a dozen production sites in six Brazilian states: Goiás, Mato Grosso, Maranhão, Mato Grosso do Sul, Bahia and Piauí.  Grupo SLC is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

The Mitsubishi Corporation is a global business enterprise that operates businesses in approximately 110 countries and regions worldwide, with activities spanning multiple industries including fresh food retail, food ingredient manufacturing, animal feed production, and agricultural raw material production and trade. Mitsubishi Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil, beef and paper packaging through its various subsidiaries.

rows.coprofile: The Kroger Co. is a leading edible grocery retailer in the US. The company’s supermarkets and convenience stores operate under various banners including Smith’s, Fred Meyer’s and Food 4 Less. In addition to its retail operations, The Kroger Co. owns a string of food processing facilities. With sizeable operations in food processing and retail The Kroger Co. is exposed to forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy and beef.  Kroger Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

rows.coprofile: The Samling Group is a Malaysian conglomerate active in forestry, oil palm, and property development. It has been named one of the largest timber companies in Malaysia. It is also a processor of timber, turning its own logs into sawn wood, plywood, and veneer. The Samling Group also has oil palm plantations through its subsidiary Glenealy Plantations in Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea, and processes palm oil in Malaysian Borneo.  Samling Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

Allianz are a global financial services provider headquartered in Germany serving both private and corporate clients. Their services include a wide array of insurance products, such as property, health and life insurance, as well as a large asset management business. As of 2017, Allianz's total assets amount to more than 890 billion EUR, with over 1.9 trillion EUR in assets under management. They are among the top 5 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 5 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. Allianz are also among the top 50 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 7 billion USD worth of shares.
SIFCA Group was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Producer), Rubber (Producer, Processor, Trader) and is also assessed for Palm oil (Trader, Manufacturer, Processor), Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

Agrifirm is a Dutch agricultural cooperative consisting of over 17,000 farmers and horticulturalists. It combines the collective purchasing power of its members, making savings on the bulk purchase of products such as animal feed ingredients, seeds and fertilisers. The cooperative has several subsidiaries which expand its operations across Europe and into Russia and China. Agrifirm represents a significant portion of Europe’s soy imports and is also an importer of palm oil.   Agrifirm is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

SC Johnson & Son manufactures and sells household products such as home cleaning, pest control and home fragrance. Well-known brands include Mr Muscle and Glade.  SC Johnson & Son Inc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.

Danzer is a German timber company based in Austria that produces veneer, lumber and other wood products from hardwood. It claims to be the largest producer of decorative veneer in the world.  Danzer Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company that specialises in dairy products. The company has more than 266 production sites spanning over 51 countries. Under a range of different brands the company mainly produce cheese, milk, cream, butter, and milk powder. Lactalis claim to be the largest dairy group in the world, and the number one cheese group in Europe. Groupe Lactalis use palm oil in its products and is exposed to soy as a component of animal feed for dairy products.  Groupe Lactalis is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Toppan Printing Co. Ltd. is a printing company based in Japan with global reach. Products include packaging, commercial printing and publication printing.
Frialto is a Brazilian meat company producing and trading beef.  Frialto is selected as a powerbroker for beef.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving individuals and companies. Their services include banking, trust banking, securities, credit cards, and leasing. As of 2024, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial's total assets amount to over 2.6 trillion USD . They are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial was providing 173 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

US Bancorp are a bank and asset management company, headquartered in the US serving private, corporate and institutional clients. Their services include: commercial banking, investment banking, asset management, mortgage, and trust and payment services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to over 450 billion USD with 270 billion USD worth of loans. Unicredit SPA are among the top 30 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 11 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors . They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 150, with shares worth more than 2.9 billion USD.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia are a financial services provider headquartered in Australia that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. They offer a range of products and services including retail, premium, business and institutional banking, funds management, pension programmes, insurance, and investment and share-broking products and services. As of 2017, Commonwealth Bank of Australia's total assets amount to over 970 billion AUD with over 730 billion AUD in loans. They are among the top 100 shareholders for Forest 500 Companies, with over 3 billion USD worth of shares.

The Godrej Group is an Indian conglomerate which, through its subsidiaries, operates in the consumer goods, real estate management, industrial engineering, furniture, appliances, security services, and agricultural products sectors. Established by Ardeshir Godrej in 1897, the Godrej family retain ownership of the group, although its subsidiaries Godrej Industries and Godrej Properties are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The company operates in 28 countries, with around three quarters of its business conducted in India where it is estimated that 500 million people use a Godrej product or service every day. In 2014, the group employed 28,000 people.
The Godrej Group is involved in palm oil through its subsidiaries at multiple stages within the supply chain. Godrej Industries, a holding company within the Godrej Group, is involved in a range of activities and sectors including the manufacture and marketing of oleo-chemicals as well as their precursors and derivatives, edible oils and bakery fats. Godrej International Limited, a subsidiary of Godrej Industries, trades vegetable oils such as palm oil internationally. Godrej Agrovet Ltd is an agribusiness subsidiary of Godrej Industries; it is India's largest animal feed manufacturer, producing over a million tons a year, and is also involved in palm oil production with 51,000 hectares of smallholder cultivation in India, four mills and a total land bank of 235,000 hectares. Finally, Godrej Consumer Products Ltd, the largest Indian personal care company, uses palm oil in its soaps. It is the largest Grade 1 quality soap and second largest toilet soap provider in India with brands such as Cinthol and No.1, and is currently seeking to increase its market share in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

SC Johnson & Son manufactures and sells household products such as home cleaning, pest control and home fragrance. Well-known brands include Mr Muscle and Glade.  SC Johnson & Son Inc is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Shiseido is a Japanese multinational company specialising in cosmetics and personal care. The company sells its products in over 100 countries under its own brand, and other well-known brand names including Elixir, NARS, bareMinerals and Issey Miyake. As a leading producer of cosmetic and personal care goods Shiseido is exposed to the forest risk commodity palm oil which is used in products such as lotions.   Shiseido Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.
Grupo Nueva is a forestry company based in Chile. Its subsidiary, Masisa, operate in the business of wood boards across Latin America.

Gap is an American retailer of clothes and accessories operating 3,700 own brand and franchise stores around the world, as well as having an online presence. Well-known brands include Gap, Banana Republic, and Old Navy. Gap is one of the top clothing and footwear retailers selling exclusively own brand products in the world by brand share. It has significant presence in the US, Asia and Europe.  Gap Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper.

Arla Foods is a dairy cooperative with activities around the world. The company’s most prominent markets are the United Kingdom, Central Europe and Asia. Its products include milk, cheese, butter and cooking ingredients with brands such as Lurpak, Castello and Apetina. Arla Foods is one of the world’s largest ingredient producers. Soy plays an important role in the cooperative’s animal feed and palm oil is also used in its products.  Arla Foods is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Nissin Foods Holdings Co Ltd was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Manufacturer), Soy (Manufacturer) and is also assessed for Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

rows.coprofile: IFFCO is a business house based in the United Arab Emirates. The company have products within impulse food, agri-business, oils and fats, chemicals, and packaging. Well-known brands include Allana, Tiffany, London Dairy, and Igloo. IFFCO provides services to consumers in the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe, West Asia, Australia, and the US. Operations within packaged foods and oils and fats typically use forest risk commodities such as palm oil and soy. The company also has key palm oil processing operations in Pakistan and Indonesia.  IFFCO is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: RELX Group, headquartered in the UK, prints publications for a range of industries worldwide. The large-scale printing operations require a vast amount of pulp and paper.  RELX Group is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Daio Paper Corporation is a Japanese manufacturer of paper products with business segments in paper and paperboard, and home and personal care.  Daio Paper Corporation is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is a Japanese company, established in 1935 and incorporated in 1955; it is involved in the manufacture and distribution of food and drink products. The company has three main business segments: Beverages and Food Manufacturing and Sale; Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing and Sale; and Others. The company's original and still most recognisable product is a probiotic fermented milk drink sold under the Yakult brand. This continues to be the company's main product, particularly in the overseas market, where average daily sales of Yakult products in early 2013 were over 22.5 million. However, aside from its fermented milk and yogurt products (which include the Joie, Sofuhl, and Purela, amongst others) Yakult also offers non-dairy beverages such as flavoured tea drinks and juices, a range of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food products, including noodles.
As of 2013, the company had around 79 subsidiaries and 18 associated companies. The company has overseas and domestic operations, with its operations outside of Japan starting in 1964, when its Taiwanese subsidiary was established. Since then, this has grown and the company is now active in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide, including in Europe, the US, Brazil, Mexico, China, South Korea, Hong Kong, Indonesia, and elsewhere in Asia.
Yakult is a significant player in the global packaged food market, demonstrated by its leading position in a variety of markets worldwide. For example, specifically, it ranks among the top three companies in the dairy products market in Japan, and among the top ten for the packaged food industry overall. It is also among the top five companies with the largest market shares in the South Korean noodle industry, and holds a similarly high market share in the market for noodles in the United States, and is in the top 25 companies in the world for the packaged food industry.

Perkebunan Nusantara is an Indonesian state-owned plantation company comprised of fourteen individual but interrelated business enterprises. The group cultivates and processes several agricultural commodities, including rubber, tobacco, sugar cane, tea, and palm oil. It is a major producer and processor of palm oil, estimated to have more than 500,000 hectares for palm plantations and a processing capacity of more than 3,000 fresh fruit bunches per hour from more than 65 facilities.
Hengan International is a Chinese manufacturer of paper products including sanitary napkins, diapers and tissue paper.

Uni-President Enterprises Corp (UPEC) manufactures and distributes a range of food products through its network of 200 affiliate companies and convenience stores. The company was incorporated in 1967 in Tainan County, Taiwan. It was originally established as a rural flour factory but over the decades has grown into an international conglomerate with operations across Asia Pacific. The manufacturing of food products is one of the company's core businesses and although it has a wide range of interests, including sports teams, retail operations and pharmaceuticals, the manufacture of food and feed are the group's largest operations. Its main products include feeds, edible oils, soya sauce, meat products, instant noodles, dairy products and frozen foods, among others.
The manufacture and marketing of food and feed products are undertaken by five main groups. The Provisions Group manufactures and markets flour, fertilizer, eggs, and animal and aquatic feeds to Asian and other international markets. The Dairy and Beverage Group manufactures dairy products, teas, soft drinks, coffee and other beverages under brands such as €œPure Tea€, €œRae-Shie€ and €œLa Gauche de la Seine€.  In addition to Taiwan, the Dairy and Beverage Group operates in mainland China, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Edible oils and instant noodles are produced by the Instant Food Group, which has a 50% market share of Taiwan's instant noodle market. Instant products are also sold outside of Taiwan with products available in 30 countries across five continents. Brands include Unif, Imperial, One More Cup, Kikkoman, A-HA, Juicymart and Pure Tea. The two smallest Groups are the General Foods and Health groups. The former provides meat products, ice cream, sauces and ready meals while the Health Group manufactures bakery and health products,.
Of particular relevance is President Nisshin Corp, a member of Uni-President that supplies oils and fats, including palm oil products, to the food industry. Furthermore, palm oil is also used in other products, for example in instant noodles, and is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soya, imported from both the US and South America, is used in Uni-President's feed and edible oil products.
