rows.coprofile: Aldi encompasses two German family-owned discount supermarket chains that have over 10,000 stores across 20 countries. They have an estimated combined turnover of more than 50 million euros. The company has been selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and pulp & paper.

Lowe's Companies is a major home improvement company based in the US with operations in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. In 2015, Lowe's had one of largest market shares for DIY, furniture, and homeware in the world. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and is one of the top four leading home improvement companies worldwide.

Kraft Heinz is one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world. Its numerous iconic brands include Kraft, Heinz, Kool-Aid, Capri-Sun and Philadelphia. As one of the leading international food product manufacturers Kraft Heinz is exposed to a range of forest risk commodities. Notably, its product range involves the use of palm oil, soy, pulp and paper.   Kraft Heinz Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.

ForFarmers B.V. is a major supplier of compound feed in the European market. The company also sells agricultural commodities such as fertilisers, seed and crop protection agents as well as advice services to its customers. With roots dating back to 1896, ForFarmers adopted its current name in 2005. The firm is transitioning its ownership structure from a cooperative to a shareholders structure. Presently, the firm remains majority-controlled (74%) by the cooperative FromFarmers and its members' accounts and certificates, with the remaining 26% under the ownership of other investors. In April 2016, ForFarmers will seek shareholders' approval to transfer to a technical listing on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange.
ForFarmers is the top feed supplier in both the Dutch and British markets, and is third and fourth in Belgium and Germany respectively. Also the company's biggest individual markets, the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany and Belgium account for 40%, 27% and 32% of sales respectively. The company sells around 8.9 million tons of feed per year, three quarters of which is compound feed.  In 2013, the largest proportion of its compound feed sales was pig feed at 37%, followed by cattle feed at 32%, and poultry feed at 22%. It employs over 2,300 people and has 42 manufacturing facilities at sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and the UK.
Acquisitions of feed businesses such as Hendrix, operating in Benelux and Germany, and BOCM Pauls, Wheyfeeds and HST Feeds in the UK, have helped to make ForFarmers Europe's largest compound feed producer. The company is looking at further acquisitions to enter new markets and to consolidate in existing European markets. ForFarmers also has strategic collaborations with direct competitors, including with Nutreco in the young animal feed business and with Agrifirm in the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and crop protection. As a major world compound feed producer, ForFarmers uses both soya and palm oil in its products.

Coamo Agroindustrial Cooperativa (Coamo) was founded in 1970 to enable Brazilian farmers to share the costs of wheat processing and storage. Today, Coamo operates 115 warehouses and, in 2014, the cooperative processed 7.0 million tons of agricultural products and was responsible for 3.6% of Brazil's total grain and fibre production. In addition to wheat and maize, the company deals with coffee, cotton and, most significantly, soya; processing 1.5 million tons of soybeans in 2014.
The company is among Brazil's top five crushers and exporters of soya. Its processing facilities include five soybean crushing mills, a soybean oil refinery, a hydrogenated fat mill, margarine processing facilities, and cotton wheat mills, which in total process around 1.7 million tons of products annually. The cooperative and processing complex are located in Parana, in Southern Brazil. It has over 6,700 employees and as well as processed products, also produces its own brand coffee and soybean oil that are sold in the region.

ForFarmers B.V. is a major supplier of compound feed in the European market. The company also sells agricultural commodities such as fertilisers, seed and crop protection agents as well as advice services to its customers. With roots dating back to 1896, ForFarmers adopted its current name in 2005. The firm is transitioning its ownership structure from a cooperative to a shareholders structure. Presently, the firm remains majority-controlled (74%) by the cooperative FromFarmers and its members' accounts and certificates, with the remaining 26% under the ownership of other investors. In April 2016, ForFarmers will seek shareholders' approval to transfer to a technical listing on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange.
ForFarmers is the top feed supplier in both the Dutch and British markets, and is third and fourth in Belgium and Germany respectively. Also the company's biggest individual markets, the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany and Belgium account for 40%, 27% and 32% of sales respectively. The company sells around 8.9 million tons of feed per year, three quarters of which is compound feed.  In 2013, the largest proportion of its compound feed sales was pig feed at 37%, followed by cattle feed at 32%, and poultry feed at 22%. It employs over 2,300 people and has 42 manufacturing facilities at sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and the UK.
Acquisitions of feed businesses such as Hendrix, operating in Benelux and Germany, and BOCM Pauls, Wheyfeeds and HST Feeds in the UK, have helped to make ForFarmers Europe's largest compound feed producer. The company is looking at further acquisitions to enter new markets and to consolidate in existing European markets. ForFarmers also has strategic collaborations with direct competitors, including with Nutreco in the young animal feed business and with Agrifirm in the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and crop protection. As a major world compound feed producer, ForFarmers uses both soya and palm oil in its products.

BRF Brasil Foods (BRF) is a Brazilian food manufacturer with products including poultry, specialty meats, frozen food, and condiments. Its brands, including Sadia, serve customers in 120 countries. The company is one of the largest poultry manufacturers in the world and claims to be responsible for more than 14% of the global poultry trade with over 1.9 million metric tons of poultry products sold in 2015. It is one of the ten largest producers of animal feed in the world with over 10 million metric tons of feed produced in 2015. BRF currently has an annual slaughtering capacity of around 180,000 heads of cattle.

The Charoen Pokphand Group (C. P. Group) is a diverse Thai business conglomerate with 200 subsidiaries in 18 countries that cover the agribusiness, food, telecommunications, and retail industries, amongst others. The group operates integrated food supply chains for poultry and pork involving it heavily in the production of animal feed and food products. It is one of the largest poultry companies in Thailand and places among the ten largest poultry companies in the world. Its subsidiaries are also among the top fifteen global producers of animal feed.

Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.

New Balance Athletic Shoes is a manufacturer of athletic footwear, apparel, and accessories and is present in more than 50 countries around the world. Its products include sports shoes, running, and hiking shoes, sports clothing and bags. Leather features in several of its footwear products. The company is one of the top ten footwear retailers globally by brandshare. It is also among the top ten in China and Hong Kong, as well as in the US.

Coamo Agroindustrial Cooperativa (Coamo) was founded in 1970 to enable Brazilian farmers to share the costs of wheat processing and storage. Today, Coamo operates 115 warehouses and, in 2014, the cooperative processed 7.0 million tons of agricultural products and was responsible for 3.6% of Brazil's total grain and fibre production. In addition to wheat and maize, the company deals with coffee, cotton and, most significantly, soya; processing 1.5 million tons of soybeans in 2014.
The company is among Brazil's top five crushers and exporters of soya. Its processing facilities include five soybean crushing mills, a soybean oil refinery, a hydrogenated fat mill, margarine processing facilities, and cotton wheat mills, which in total process around 1.7 million tons of products annually. The cooperative and processing complex are located in Parana, in Southern Brazil. It has over 6,700 employees and as well as processed products, also produces its own brand coffee and soybean oil that are sold in the region.

Metro AG is a German wholesaler with operations across the world. The company’s portfolio caters to professional customers, through sales brands including METRO Cash & Carry and different FSD companies. With a diverse product range, Metro AG is exposed to a number of forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy, pulp and paper. Metro AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Starbucks Corp. is the owner of the Starbucks chain of coffee stores and several other subsidiaries operating across the food and beverage industry. As of 2023 it has 32,000 outlets in 80 countries. In addition to coffee, Starbucks Corp. also trades in teas, bottled drinks, baked goods, snacks and other food items. Its range of products and packaging leave it exposed to various forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy and paper.   Starbucks Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Lindt & Sprungli is a Swiss chocolatier that markets products in over 120 countries worldwide. Its key brand is Lindt, but it also sells under subsidiaries including Ghirardelli, Russel Stover and Whitman’s. Lindt & Sprungli is exposed to the forest risk commodities palm oil and soy, which are used in many of its chocolate products soy is also hidden in its supply chain of dairy ingredients as a key component of animal feed.  Lindt & Sprungli AG is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Groupe Avril is an agro-industrial and financial group operating its business within the animal nutrition, renewable energy, food and chemistry sectors.  Groupe Avril is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

Home Depot Inc. is a leading home improvement retailer, selling construction materials and products for the home and garden. It was founded in 1978 in Atlanta, Georgia in the US, where the company now has its headquarters. Since the opening of its first two stores in Atlanta in 1979, the company has grown to become the largest retailer in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector both in the US and globally. According to Home Depot, it is the fourth largest retailer in the US and the fifth largest in the world. Home Depot provides a range of products, including building materials, home improvement supplies, indoor and outdoor furniture, tools, and garden products for customers undertaking DIY activities.
The company has over 2,200 specialist stores throughout the US, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, China, Canada and Mexico. It entered the Canadian market in 1994 and now has 182 stores in ten of Canada's provinces. It entered the Mexican market in 2011, and has since become Mexico's largest home improvement retailer, with a total of 114 stores in the country. Home Depot's presence in China increased through its acquisition of The Home Way; China's first home improvement retailer. However, the company experienced slow growth in the Chinese market due to a low consumer appetite for DIY products and since then it has folded its store operations, closing its last store in Beijing in 2013.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating manufacturer headquartered in the US, operating in 39 countries. Its subsidiary Eagle Ottawa claims to be the world’s largest supplier of automotive leather. With customers including the likes of Mercedes, BMW, Toyoto and GMC, Eagle Ottawa has a high turnover of leather hides.  Lear Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Aditya Birla Group is one of the largest conglomerates in India with operations in 36 countries. The group operates in sectors including fashion, cement, mobiles and viscose filament yarn.  Aditya Birla Group is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

Toyo Suisan Kaisha Ltd (Toyo) is an international food producer specialising in ramen noodles and seafood. Toyo manufactures its products through various sub-divisions, such as the Domestic Instant Noodles segment and the Frozen and Refrigerated Foods segment. In addition to noodles, it also produces wontons, soup products, fish, ham, sausages and seasonings. It also has a Prepared Food section which manufactures sterile packaged rice, retort rice, soup and other products.
The company was founded in 1953, has its headquarters in Tokyo, and employs around 4,600 people. Its main overseas operations are in Mexico and the Us through its Overseas Instant Noodles Division, which sells noodles under the brand name Maruchan Inc. As of 2008, Toyo owns three food processing facilities in the US and has 32 subsidiaries.
By the 1970s, Toyo had become well-known in Japan and had branched out internationally. It is now the largest noodle company in the US, the second largest in Japan and third largest in the world. It is also in the top five companies in Japan for dried processed food and chilled processed food, and in the top 30 largest soup companies worldwide.
The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm oil and in 2013 was implicated by the Rainforest Action Network to be one of the 'Snack Food 20' responsible for using 'conflict' palm oil from unsustainable sources,.

Perkebunan Nusantara is an Indonesian state-owned plantation company comprised of fourteen individual but interrelated business enterprises. The group cultivates and processes several agricultural commodities, including rubber, tobacco, sugar cane, tea, and palm oil. It is a major producer and processor of palm oil, estimated to have more than 500,000 hectares for palm plantations and a processing capacity of more than 3,000 fresh fruit bunches per hour from more than 65 facilities.  Perkebunan Nusantara is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Hennes & Mauritz is a Swedish clothing company. It is mainly known through its own brand H&M, but it also has other brands such as Monki, Weekday, and Cheap Monday in its portfolio. H&M has over 4000 stores in more than 60 countries, and is one of the biggest clothing retailers in the world. Many of its products are made using cellulose or leather.   H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB  is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper.

rows.coprofile: Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings is a Chinese holding company for diverse industries but operates primarily in pulp and paper. It manufactures a variety of paper products including printing paper, packaging, newsprint, and specialty papers. Though the company primarily uses chips and recovered material in production, it also imports raw materials internationally. It therefore has a high risk of exposure to tropical wood in its supply chain.  Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co., Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

The first Starbucks coffee store opened in 1971 in Seattle US. Over the next two decades the company expanded across the US and it completed its initial public offering in 1992. Since then the coffee chain has grown dramatically, opening its first non-North American stores in Japan and Singapore in 1996. As well as organic growth, Starbucks has acquired other cafe and beverage companies and even a music company. In 2013, Starbucks had over 3 billion customer visits to its 19,000 plus stores operating in 62 countries across the globe.  Growth has continued with the company moving into a further three countries and expanding its portfolio to over 21,000 outlets.
As well as roasting, marketing and selling coffee, Starbucks also sells tea products, juices, pastries, sandwiches, salads and beverage making equipment. Products are sold through company operated stores, licensed stores, grocery stores, national food service accounts and some franchised stores.
In addition to its major Starbucks brand the company also operates: Seattles Best Coffee, Teavana, Tazo, Evolution Fresh, La Boulange (bakery brand) and Torrefazione Italia Coffee. Starbucks is the largest cafe/bar owner in the world with revenues of $14.9bn. Starbucks uses paper in its packaging, soya (in milk) and palm oil (in its food products).

Commerzbank are a German retail, commercial and investment banking group, offering services to private and corporate customers. Their services include wealth management, investment banking, insurance, pensions, corporate finance and retail banking services. As of 2017, Commerzbank has more than 480 billion EUR in total assets, including over 215 billion EUR in claims on customers. Commerzbank are among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

China Mengniu Dairy (Mengniu) is a Chinese manufacturer and distributor of dairy products. Its products include milk, ice-cream, cheese, and other dairy products. As of 2015, Mengniu had over 33 milk production facilities throughout China with an annual capacity of more than 8.5 million metric tons. The company is one of the top dairy companies in China and one of the top five in dairy globally, whilst also ranking highly for other dairy products and packaged food. It is also a major Chinese importer of palm oil.

Korindo Group PT was selected as a powerbroker for Pulp & Paper (Producer, Processor) and is also assessed for Palm oil (Processor, Producer), Timber (Manufacturer, Producer), Rubber (Processor, Producer)

Agrifirm is a Dutch cooperative comprising around 17,500 farmers and horticulturalists which provides agricultural products and services. The cooperative has several subsidiaries which expands its operations across Europe and into Russia and China. Agrifirm represents an important part of Europe's soya imports and is also an importer of palm oil. It is also among the top thirty animal feed producers in the world, for which soya is a major ingredient.

Prada is an Italian fashion retailer. Prada is a luxury brand producing leather goods, clothing, footwear, eyewear, fragrance, and confectionary. Famous brands include Prada, Miu Miu, and Church’s. The company is among the top fashion companies in the world and uses leather in its products.  Prada SpA is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

In addition to its retail operations, The Kroger Co. owns a string of food processing facilities. With sizeable operations in food processing and retail The Kroger Co. is exposed to forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy and beef.  Kroger Co. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Astra Agro Lestari is an Indonesian agribusiness company primarily involved in the cultivation of oil palm, but also with some processing capacity. The company’s landbank is one of the largest landbanks for palm oil globally, with approximately 300,000 hectares across Indonesia. It also owns a palm oil refinery alongside several processing and crushing facilities.   PT Astra International TBK is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Lowe’s Companies is a major home improvement company based in the US with operations in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and worldwide. Oetker-Gruppe is a German manufacturer of packaged food. The majority of the company’s products are frozen pizzas, baking goods, desserts, dry ready meals, beverages, and snacks. Oetker-Gruppe operates internationally with more than 400 companies working in a variety of different business segments.   Oetker-Gruppe is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is a Japanese company, established in 1935 and incorporated in 1955; it is involved in the manufacture and distribution of food and drink products. The company has three main business segments: Beverages and Food Manufacturing and Sale; Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing and Sale; and Others. The company's original and still most recognisable product is a probiotic fermented milk drink sold under the Yakult brand. This continues to be the company's main product, particularly in the overseas market, where average daily sales of Yakult products in early 2013 were over 22.5 million. However, aside from its fermented milk and yogurt products (which include the Joie, Sofuhl, and Purela, amongst others) Yakult also offers non-dairy beverages such as flavoured tea drinks and juices, a range of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food products, including noodles.
As of 2013, the company had around 79 subsidiaries and 18 associated companies. The company has overseas and domestic operations, with its operations outside of Japan starting in 1964, when its Taiwanese subsidiary was established. Since then, this has grown and the company is now active in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide, including in Europe, the US, Brazil, Mexico, China, South Korea, Hong Kong, Indonesia, and elsewhere in Asia.
Yakult is a significant player in the global packaged food market, demonstrated by its leading position in a variety of markets worldwide. For example, specifically, it ranks among the top three companies in the dairy products market in Japan, and among the top ten for the packaged food industry overall. It is also among the top five companies with the largest market shares in the South Korean noodle industry, and holds a similarly high market share in the market for noodles in the United States, and is in the top 25 companies in the world for the packaged food industry.

MRV Engenharia e Participaces (MRV) is a construction company in Brazil focussed on the residential real estate market, building houses, apartment buildings and other properties. It is one of the largest Brazilian construction companies by units sold, revenue and sales value, and it operates in 134 cities and 19 states in Brazil. Timber is a major raw material for construction, and Brazil in general uses four times more tropical timber than China. In 2013, MRV used more than 1.4 million cubic metres of timber.

rows.coprofile: Norges Bank Investment Management are a Norwegian state-owned investment fund. They invest in international equity, fixed-income markets and real estate to provide security for Norway's economy against fluctuating oil prices. Norges Bank Investment Management are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with shares across a broad range of forest risk sectors. The Gap Inc. is a leading global apparel retailer selling apparel, accessories and personal care products for men, women and children through its various brands. Gap Inc. was established with the opening of a single Gap store in San Francisco in the United States in 1969. Since then the company has expanded greatly through the establishment of several other retail brands, including Banana Republic, Old Navy, Athleta, and Intermix.
The company has around 3,300 company-operated stores and 400 franchise stores in more than 90 countries alongside e-commerce sales operations in almost 100 countries. Its company-operated stores are located in the US, Canada, the UK, France, Ireland, Japan, China, Italy and, since 2014, Taiwan. Gap Inc. also has franchise agreements with unaffiliated franchisees to operate Gap, Old Navy and Banana Republic stores throughout Asia, Australia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Gap Inc. employs around 140,000 full and part time individuals.
The company's flagship brand, Gap, which sells casual, American style apparel, continues to be the most prominent of the group's retail brands, with over 1,430 company stores and over 340 franchises worldwide. Gap Inc.'s retail brands vary in their retailing of own-brand and other designer brands. Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy and Athleta brands each sell their own own-label products, while the Intermix brands stocks both its own-label products and those of other designers.
Gap Inc is among the top three retailers of private-label apparel and the top five of all clothing retailers globally. Each of the company's brands stock a range of leather goods, including shoes, belts and bags. For example, Intermix, which was acquired by Gap Inc in 2012, offers a range of branded luxury accessories, including leather bags. Banana Republic and Gap brands similarly stock a range of leather goods, including leather jackets for men and women, and leather handbags, belts and shoes. Gap Inc. does not directly own or operate its own manufacturing facilities, and as of 2012, its branded apparel is produced in around 923 factories in 32 countries worldwide.

The Volkswagen Group are a German multinational automative manufacturer based in Wolfsburg, Germany. The Group comprises ten brands from five European countries: Volkswagen, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles, ŠKODA, SEAT, CUPRA, Audi, Lamborghini, Bentley, Porsche and Ducati. Leather is a critical component in the manufacture of cars as it is used to produce steering wheels, interior components and seats. The Volkswagen Group is selected as a powerbroker for leather.

rows.coprofile: Mitsui & Co., Ltd. is a Japanese trading company operating worldwide. It sells canned and chilled foods, packaging materials, pharmaceuticals and feedstuffs, among others.  Mitsui & Co. Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

Association Familiale Mulliez (AFM) is a holding company for the businesses owned by the Mulliez family. Subsidiaries include Auchan Holding which is one of the largest food retailers in the world and has hypermarkets and supermarkets in several countries, as well as operating a furniture and interior design chain in France. AFM also own restaurants including Carluccio's and Giraffe Restaurants, home improvement companies including Leroy Merlin and fashion brands including Orsay. Through its operations the company is exposed to several forest risk commodities. rows.coprofile: Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company that operates in a range of sectors across services, trading, and manufacturing. Its main business activities are edible oils, dairy products, baked goods, flour milling, printing, and packaging.  The company export products to more than 80 countries through many different brands. Its subsidiary, Pacific Inter-Link, processes and trades palm oil.  Hayel Saeed Anam Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy, pulp & paper and paper packaging.

Groupe Auchan is an unlisted company, whose operations include hypermarkets and supermarkets. It is owned by the Mulliez Family through the holding company Association Familiale Mulliez (AFM), which owned an 87.8% stake in the Group as of 2011. Although Groupe Auchan's largest market is France, it also has a significant presence in mainland Europe and China, and operates in total in 16 countries. Its origins are in hypermarkets, which were established in 1961 by Gerard Mulliez. As of 31 December 2014, the group operates 888 fully-consolidated hypermarkets, 862 fully-consolidated supermarkets, and 370 shopping centres. Other smaller businesses of Groupe Auchan include a furniture and interior design chain, which has 26 French stores.
The group's hypermarkets operate under multiple banners such as Auchan and Alcampo, offering a broad range of products including groceries, clothing, furniture, DIY equipment and electronics. Groupe Auchan's supermarkets also operate through multiple banners such as Simply Markets, A2Pas, ATAK and Partisans de GoÃ»t. These offer a narrower range of products, concentrating on groceries. Together hypermarkets and supermarkets account for over 95% of group revenue.
In 1979, Groupe Auchan formed a stakeholder agreement making AFM the leading shareholder of ADEO.  ADEO SA is active in the international do-it-yourself (DIY) industry. It is the largest DIY retailer in Europe and among the top five DIY retailers globally in terms of net revenue. Through its numerous subsidiaries, it operates a chain of DIY stores providing construction materials, home decoration products, garden supplies, and kitchen and bathroom goods. Incorporated in 1986, ADEO is based in Lille, France and is comprised of 30 companies within 15 brands. It is a federation of autonomous companies, some of which are wholly-owned and some held under franchise, and comprises 391 franchise stores and 589 integrated stores in 12 countries, including Brazil and China and throughout Europe. Leroy Merlin is one the group's major companies; it is a major retail outlet in the home improvement sector, with almost 377 home improvement stores in 12 countries. The smaller, local chains run by ADEO include AKI, Bricocenter, and Weldom, and warehouse stores include Bricoman and Bricomart.

Inditex is a Spanish fashion retailer. It has eight brands, including Zara, Pull&Bear, Bershka, Massimo Dutti, and Stradivarius. Inditex has over 7000 stores in more than 90 countries, and employs over 160,000 people. The company claims to be one of the largest fashion retailers in the world. Inditex use cellulose and leather in its products.  Inditex S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Wm Morrison Supermarkets PLC operates a chain of around 500 supermarkets in the UK. It has food manufacturing capabilities in meat, fish and bakery products and the breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Wm Morrison Supermarkets PLC is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Their services cover insurance, savings, investment management and pensions. As of 2022, their total assets amount to more than £582.6 billion and they hold over 1.6 Trillion USD of assets under management. Legal & General are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, Legal & General was providing 43.6 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

The Mitsubishi Corporation is a diversified business with activities across a wide range of sectors, including energy, industrial goods, metals, machinery, and finance, as well as food products. The breadth of its living essentials business group exposes the company to many forest risk commodities. Some of these businesses include agricultural traders, food processors, restaurant chains, and animal feed manufacturers. The Mitsubishi Corporation is a major trader of palm oil. Its subsidiaries also rank among the top five European importers of Brazilian beef.  Mitsubishi Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and beef.

Oetker-Gruppe is a German manufacturer of packaged food. The majority of the company’s products are frozen pizzas, baking goods, desserts, dry ready meals, beverages, and snacks. Oetker-Gruppe operates internationally with around 350 companies working in a variety of different business segments. Oetker-Gruppe is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Vicentin is an Argentinian agro-industrial company active in textiles, agriculture, and agricultural products. It is a major player in the Argentinian soya market with a significant market share for soya crushing. The company's three crushing facilities have an annual capacity of just under 10 million metric tons as of 2015. Vicentin is also one of the largest exporters of soya from Argentina and among the top ten from Paraguay. Additionally, the company is involved in biodiesel production with a daily production of 500 tons and has a feed lot holding 20,000 heads of cattle.

Vicentin is also one of the largest exporters of soya from Argentina and among the top ten from Paraguay. COFCO Group was founded in 1949 and operates in the edible seed market via China Agri Holdings Ltd. It is the second largest crusher of oilseeds (behind Wilmar International) and has 13% of the market share of oilseed crushing capability and over 9% of the market share for soybeans. Its manufacturing plants are located close to major food consumption markets including in Tianjin, Jiangsu, Shandong, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei and Xinjiang. Historically, the company has focused its business activities in downstream activities. However, in February 2014, COFCO bought a majority stake (51%) in Nidera, a Dutch commodities trader, in order to gain access to South American grain and oilseed goods, while in April 2014, the company acquired a controlling stake (51%) in Noble Agri, which owns oilseeds processing plants and a grain processing and distribution business. In May 2015, COFCO announced it will merge its holdings in Nidera and Noble Agri to create a new entity, COFCO International Holdings, in a joint venture with China Investment Corp, a sovereign wealth fund who will own 19.9% of the new business, with the ultimate intention of merging COFCO's own domestic business into COFCO International to combine COFCO's oil, grain and sugar assets.
COFCO Group retains a strong presence in the downstream market, with a number of branded goods sold across China. They sell shortening and margarine as well as a number of speciality products such as soybean milk fat. In total, their annual sales volume exceeds 120,000 tonnes across 31 Chinese provinces. Its brands include Sihai for soybean meal products and Fuzhiquan for cooking oils.
As well as being a major player in the processed food industry, COFCO Group has a long history in the timber sector and claims to be the largest integrated timber merchant in China. One of the Group's subsidiaries, China Timber Co. Ltd., has operated traded timber internationally for over fifty years. It imports a wide variety of timber and timber products from a range of countries, including raw timber from Papua New Guinea and Myanmar; and plywood, construction materials and furniture from Africa and South America. It also exports wood flooring and plywood and other manufactured wood products to the US, Europe, Japan and India.
Of particular relevance are China Timber's operations in the Republic of Gabon, where it holds five timber companies engaged in the direct harvesting of timber and timber processing activities. It has around one million hectares of tropical hardwood forests. Specifically, it operates Sunly Gabon, which is one of the largest Chinese firms operating in the Gabonese forestry sector and has several hundred thousand hectares of forest concessions in the north-east, east and southern parts of the country.

Hillshire Brands Co. (Hillshire) is a food giant from Chicago which manufactures and markets meat-based products. Founded in 1939, Hillshire acquired many notable brands over the years, including Jimmy Dean and Ball Park Franks, which is reportedly the top hotdog brand in the US and worth over $500 million in revenue.  Hillshire has 9,500 employees and sales of $4.09 billion as of May 2013, placing it among the Forbes Global 2000 list of the world's largest public companies. Although the largest market for its six major brands is in the US, it also has a strong international presence, ranking in the top 20 in the world for frozen processed food, third globally for chilled processed food and second in the US in the same category. Outside of the US, it is amongst the five largest frozen processed food companies in Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Hillshire uses palm oil in its products; it sources palm-oil-containing raw materials for use in its manufacturing.
Hillshire itself has recently been acquired by Tyson Foods Inc., one of the largest producers and processors of meat, poultry and prepared foods in the world. Headquartered in Arkansas, Tyson was established in 1935 and remains under the ownership of the Tyson family. Although the majority of Tyson's operations are within the US, it also runs in country activities in poultry production in China, India, Mexico and Brazil, which utilise soya bean in poultry feed. The buyout of Hillshire by Tyson marks one of the biggest mergers in the packaged food industry and establishes Tyson firmly in the top two companies in the global processed meat market.

Franklin Resources are an investment management firm headquartered in the US that serves private and institutional clients. Their services cover equity, fixed-income, multi-asset and alternative funds. As of 2017, Franklin Resources' total assets under management amount to more than 700 billion USD. They are among the top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with over 1 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with approximately 15 billion USD worth of shares.

rows.coprofile: Petros are a non-profit foundation headquartered in Brazil operating solely in pensions. They offer several different pension plans and manage corporate pensions for companies and organisations. As of 2017, their total investments amount to more than 60 billion BRL. Petros are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

Lindt & Sprungli AG (Lindt) is a Swiss chocolatier founded in 1845, which describes itself as the market leader in the premium chocolates industry. The company sells in over 100 countries worldwide, with products under the brand names Ghirardelli, Caffarel, Hofbauer and Kufferle. Lindt employs a total of 8,949 people, has eight production sites (six in Europe and two in the USA) and distributes globally (including in China, Australia, South Africa, North America and Europe), with its largest markets being the European and NAFTA countries. The company distributes its products through a variety of avenues, including duty free retail outlets in airports, department stores, its own stores and Chocolate Cafes.
As a confectionery company, Lindt is ranked 7th in the world and 6th in Western Europe, and is also ranked among the top 50 packaged food companies globally. Further to this, Lindt is placed among the Forbes Global 2000 list. As a manufacturer of sweet snacks, Lindt uses palm oil in a number of its products and also includes soya derivatives, such as soya lecithin, as an ingredient in most of its chocolates.
Lindt has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2008. In 2012 it used 2,565m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products; and it aims to be sourcing 100% RSPO-certified sustainable palm oil by 2015.

Macquarie Group are a financial services group headquartered in Australia serving institutional, corporate, government and retail clients. Their services cover: asset management, asset and corporate finance, banking, advisory services and global, commodity, and capital markets. As of 2017, their total assets amount to over 180 billion AUD with over 470 billion AUD of assets under management. Macquarie Group are among the top 10 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with over 3 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors . They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 80 with shares worth more than 4 billion USD.

Coamo Agroindustrial Cooperativa (Coamo) was founded in 1970 to enable Brazilian farmers to share the costs of wheat processing and storage. Today, Coamo operates 115 warehouses and, in 2014, the cooperative processed 7.0 million tons of agricultural products and was responsible for 3.6% of Brazil's total grain and fibre production. In addition to wheat and maize, the company deals with coffee, cotton and, most significantly, soya; processing 1.5 million tons of soybeans in 2014.
The company is among Brazil's top five crushers and exporters of soya. Its processing facilities include five soybean crushing mills, a soybean oil refinery, a hydrogenated fat mill, margarine processing facilities, and cotton wheat mills, which in total process around 1.7 million tons of products annually. The cooperative and processing complex are located in Parana, in Southern Brazil. It has over 6,700 employees and as well as processed products, also produces its own brand coffee and soybean oil that are sold in the region.

Nike is a manufacturer of sports shoes, sports apparel and accessories. The Company’s famous brands include Nike, Converse, Hurley, and Jordan. Many of Nike’s shoes are made using leather.  Nike Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather, pulp & paper and paper packaging.

Associated British Foods is a diversified group with operations in food, ingredients and retail. The group’s business segments include grocery, ingredients, agriculture, sugar, and retail with such brands such as Twinings and Ryvita. It is also a leading vendor in the baking ingredients market and the owner of the clothing retailer Primark. These diverse businesses expose the group to palm oil and soy in food production, soy in animal feed and leather in apparel. It is also among the largest producers of animal feed in Europe.  Associated British Foods Plc is selected as a powerbroker for soy, leather and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

TIAA-CREF are a financial services company headquartered in the US that primarily serves private and institutional investors in the not-for-profit sector including education, health care, government and research. Their services cover pensions, investments and insurance. In 2017, their total assets under management amount to more than 950 billion USD. TIAA-CREF are among the top bondholders and shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with bonds and shares across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

C&J Clark International (Clarks) is a UK footwear company operating in over 75 countries. It designs, manufactures, and sells a wide range of footwear. The company is a major European footwear retailer and is one of largest footwear retailers globally.  C & J Clark International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) are an international bank headquartered in Australia providing services to private, retail, small business and corporate clients. Their services include pensions, insurance, investments, corporate finance, financial market products and retail banking. As of 2024, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) have over 59.3 billion USD in assets under management. They are among the top lenders to companies in the Forest 500. In the 2024 selection, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) was providing 19.5 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Meiji Holdings Co. Ltd. (Meiji Holdings) is a Japanese holding company, headquartered in Tokyo, that through its subsidiaries has operations in the manufacture of dairy products, confectionery, health food and pharmaceuticals. The company, in its current holding company structure, was established in 2008; however, its origins extend back to the early 1900s, with the establishment of Meiji Sugar Co. Ltd. and Meiji Dairies Corporation in 1906, and then Meiji Co. Ltd. (a manufacturer of confectionery) in 1916.  
Meiji Holdings' business activities now fall under Meiji Co. Ltd. and Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd. Meiji Co. Ltd. produces a variety of food products, under its confectionery, dairy, healthcare & nutritionals, and international business units. Whereas Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd manufactures pharmaceuticals in three main segments: anti-infective drugs, therapeutic drugs for neural disorders, and generic drugs. The company is active within Japan and internationally, through its overseas network of companies, which can be found throughout Asia, Europe and North America. Meiji Holdings ranks among the top 2,000 public companies in the world and has over 14,000 employees.
The company's operations in packaged food manufacturing, in particular its use of palm and soya products in the production of sweets, chocolate and ice cream, are of particular importance with respect to forest risk commodities. For example, palm oil and palm kernel oil can be found in Meiji's brands of chocolate cookies and crackers, Chococones and Chocorooms, which it markets in the United States. Similarly, palm oil and soya derivatives can be found in other products, such as Meiji's Apollo Strawberry Chocolate Candy.
Meiji Holdings is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

As of 2022, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial's total assets amount to over 3.1 trillion USD with over 776 Billion USD assets under management. Domino's Pizza Inc. is a US pizza delivery and carry-out company serving the US and over 75 international markets. Worldwide, there are 11,700 stores that deliver over 1 million pizzas every day. Over 90% of stores are franchised, while Domino's Pizza Inc. owns around 377 stores in the US. It also runs dough manufacturing facilities and supply chain centres to supply stores in the US and in some overseas markets.  The US is Domino's Pizza Inc.'s single biggest market with 5,084 stores in Q1 2015, but over half of the company's sales come from outside the US. Domino's Pizza Inc. is the world's second biggest fast food pizza retailer. In addition to pizza, the company offers related products including sandwiches, chicken, salads, sauces, drinks and desserts. Beef is used as a pizza topping, soya is used in pizzas, and both soya and palm oil are used in side dishes and desserts.

Nutreco N.V. (Nutreco) is an animal nutrition and feed company based in the Netherlands that manufactures feeds and additives for a range of animals and uses. It was created in 1994 by a private equity backed management buy-out of a number of firms involved in meat processing, animal nutrition and fish farming. Nutreco was floated on the NYSE Euronext Amsterdam exchange in 1997. In recent years, the company's strategy has been to focus more on animal nutrition and animal and aquaculture feed, moving away from meat processing and other downstream activities. It has also successfully targeted growth markets such as Russia, Asia, Africa and Latin America. Recently (October 2014), the Dutch investment firm, SHV Holdings, has entered into a conditional agreement to buy Nutreco.
The company currently employs around 10,000 people across more than 30 countries worldwide and serves markets in more than 80 countries. Operations are split into two main segments: Animal Nutrition and Fish Feed, which in 2013 accounted for 48% and 52% of revenue respectively. The Animal Nutrition division manufactures and sells farm minerals, concentrates, feed additives, animal health products, feeds and premixes. The segment contains multiple brands, each with different focuses and locations. These include Shur-Gain, which operates in Canada and some areas of the US, providing premixes, compound and speciality feeds pet foods and animal health products; Nanta, which focuses primarily on pigs, poultry and ruminants but also provides feed for horses and rabbits; and Skretting, Nutreco's fish feed company that provides feed for over 60 species of fish and shrimp. It has operations on five continents and manufactures feed in 14 countries.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, New York Declaration on Forests

Unigra is also assessed for pulp and paper due to volume of packaging involved in it's various products.

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

Founded in Hong Kong in the 1800s, CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd (CK Hutchison) operates five core businesses: ports and related services, retail, infrastructure, energy and telecommunication. The company was formed in its present structure in 2015 following the restructuring of Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd. and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd. to separate the property business into a new holding company and subsume Hutchison Whampoa's other operations under the direction of CK Hutchison. CK Hutchison employs around 270,000 people across 50 countries.
CK Hutchison's retail operations are led by A.S. Watson Group, which was started in 1828 as a small dispensary in Guangzhou, China. Today, the Group has more than 12,000 stores in 22 countries worldwide and claims to be the world's largest international health and beauty retailer. The company operates multiple brands in the health and beauty sector, including: Watsons, which has over 4,800 stores and 1,400 pharmacies in Asia and Europe; Kruidvat, which has over 1,000 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium; and Superdrug, which operates in the UK and Ireland and has over 870 stores. A.S. Watson also sells food, wine and electronics under multiple brands, which include: PARKnSHOP, which operates 340 supermarkets in Greater China; and SU-PA-DE-PA, which combines supermarket food products with department store ranges, such as clothing and entertainment. The Group's portfolio also includes over 500 European perfume and cosmetics shops.

Koninklijke DSM is a Dutch-based multinational company that focuses on the manufacturing of products related to health, nutrition and materials. These products cover 17 global markets, including the food and dietary supplements, personal care, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, paints, electronics, life protection, automotive, feed, alternative energy and bio-based materials markets. It is one of the top ten manufacturers of food and drinks ingredients in the world.
Koninklijke DSM operates globally, with a most of its workforce based in the Netherlands, the rest of Europe, North and Latin America and China. Over half of its total sales come from Western Europe and North America but the company also has aims to increase sales in high growth economies such as China, Brazil, Russia and India. Over half of the company's sales come from its nutrition products, with most of these sales occurring in Europe and North and Latin America. Koninklijke DSM uses palm oil based derivatives in the manufacture of its food, beverages and dietary supplements. The nutrition cluster of the company DSM Nutritional Products AG - became a Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) member in 2008.  
In 2013, DSM Nutritional Products formed a strategic partnership with Monsanto (who develops soya bean varieties and sells seeds to farmers) to develop the first stearidonate (SDA) omega-3 soya bean oil for use in foods in North American. The SDA soya bean oil could offer a vegetarian alternative to fatty fish acids as a source of omega-3, and it will add to the company's growing portfolio of nutritional lipids.

SIFCA Group was founded in 1964 and is a conglomerate of four companies specialising in the production of palm oil, rubber and sugar in Africa. 27% of the group's shares are held by a company jointly owned by Wilmar International and Olam International, 44% are owned by Parme Investment, MMORIV owns 21% and the remaining 8% of SIFCA Group is owned by private shareholders.
Overall, the company employs around 30,000 people in 5 countries, with oil palm representing 40% of the group's turnover. PALMCI and SANIA are the two companies in the conglomerate that take part in the oil palm supply chain. PALMCI is responsible for the management of 39,000 hectares of industrial oil palm plantations and over 130,000 hectares of village plantations. SANIA is then responsible for utilising these upstream derivatives to produce final products that are used internally and also exported overseas. Through its refineries, SANIA has a production capability of approximately 280,000 MT of refined palm oil per year. Much of that capacity is provided by the SANIA processing plant in Abidjan, which has a crude palm oil capacity of 1,500 MT per day. Furthermore, through SAPH, SIFCA is the largest producer of rubber in Africa with over 20,000 hectares of industrial plantations. SANIA produces several edible oil and margarine products and markets them under different brands, including Palme d'Or, Dora, Saint Ave and Delicia. 
At the time of writing, SIFCA Group's website pages on sustainable development are many years out of date and do not appear to specifically address the issues of deforestation or sustainable palm oil production. None of the group companies appear to be members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

SHV Holdings is a Dutch trading company. The company owns Nutreco, which is one of the global leaders in animal nutrition and aquafeed. The company sells its products in more than 90 countries. According to Nutreco, its brand Skretting is the leading manufacturer of aquaculture feed in the world. Soy and palm oil are often used in animal feed products.   SHV holdings is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company that operates in a range of sectors across services, trading, and manufacturing. Its main business activities are edible oils, dairy products, baked goods, flour milling, printing, and packaging.  The company export products to more than 80 countries through many different brands. Its subsidiary, Pacific Inter-Link, processes and trades palm oil.  Hayel Saeed Anam Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy, pulp & paper and paper packaging.

COFCO Group was founded in 1949 and operates in the edible seed market via China Agri Holdings Ltd. It is the second largest crusher of oilseeds (behind Wilmar International) and has 13% of the market share of oilseed crushing capability and over 9% of the market share for soybeans. Its manufacturing plants are located close to major food consumption markets including in Tianjin, Jiangsu, Shandong, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei and Xinjiang. Historically, the company has focused its business activities in downstream activities. However, in February 2014, COFCO bought a majority stake (51%) in Nidera, a Dutch commodities trader, in order to gain access to South American grain and oilseed goods, while in April 2014, the company acquired a controlling stake (51%) in Noble Agri, which owns oilseeds processing plants and a grain processing and distribution business. In May 2015, COFCO announced it will merge its holdings in Nidera and Noble Agri to create a new entity, COFCO International Holdings, in a joint venture with China Investment Corp, a sovereign wealth fund who will own 19.9% of the new business, with the ultimate intention of merging COFCO's own domestic business into COFCO International to combine COFCO's oil, grain and sugar assets.
COFCO Group retains a strong presence in the downstream market, with a number of branded goods sold across China. They sell shortening and margarine as well as a number of speciality products such as soybean milk fat. In total, their annual sales volume exceeds 120,000 tonnes across 31 Chinese provinces. Its brands include Sihai for soybean meal products and Fuzhiquan for cooking oils.
As well as being a major player in the processed food industry, COFCO Group has a long history in the timber sector and claims to be the largest integrated timber merchant in China. One of the Group's subsidiaries, China Timber Co. Ltd., has operated traded timber internationally for over fifty years. It imports a wide variety of timber and timber products from a range of countries, including raw timber from Papua New Guinea and Myanmar; and plywood, construction materials and furniture from Africa and South America. It also exports wood flooring and plywood and other manufactured wood products to the US, Europe, Japan and India.
Of particular relevance are China Timber's operations in the Republic of Gabon, where it holds five timber companies engaged in the direct harvesting of timber and timber processing activities. It has around one million hectares of tropical hardwood forests. Specifically, it operates Sunly Gabon, which is one of the largest Chinese firms operating in the Gabonese forestry sector and has several hundred thousand hectares of forest concessions in the north-east, east and southern parts of the country.

Meiji Holdings Co. Ltd. (Meiji Holdings) is a Japanese holding company, headquartered in Tokyo, that through its subsidiaries has operations in the manufacture of dairy products, confectionery, health food and pharmaceuticals. The company, in its current holding company structure, was established in 2008; however, its origins extend back to the early 1900s, with the establishment of Meiji Sugar Co. Ltd. and Meiji Dairies Corporation in 1906, and then Meiji Co. Ltd. (a manufacturer of confectionery) in 1916.  
Meiji Holdings' business activities now fall under Meiji Co. Ltd. and Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd. Meiji Co. Ltd. produces a variety of food products, under its confectionery, dairy, healthcare & nutritionals, and international business units. Whereas Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd manufactures pharmaceuticals in three main segments: anti-infective drugs, therapeutic drugs for neural disorders, and generic drugs. The company is active within Japan and internationally, through its overseas network of companies, which can be found throughout Asia, Europe and North America. Meiji Holdings ranks among the top 2,000 public companies in the world and has over 14,000 employees.
The company's operations in packaged food manufacturing, in particular its use of palm and soya products in the production of sweets, chocolate and ice cream, are of particular importance with respect to forest risk commodities. For example, palm oil and palm kernel oil can be found in Meiji's brands of chocolate cookies and crackers, Chococones and Chocorooms, which it markets in the United States. Similarly, palm oil and soya derivatives can be found in other products, such as Meiji's Apollo Strawberry Chocolate Candy.
Meiji Holdings is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Hillshire Brands Co. (Hillshire) is a food giant from Chicago which manufactures and markets meat-based products. Founded in 1939, Hillshire acquired many notable brands over the years, including Jimmy Dean and Ball Park Franks, which is reportedly the top hotdog brand in the US and worth over $500 million in revenue.  Hillshire has 9,500 employees and sales of $4.09 billion as of May 2013, placing it among the Forbes Global 2000 list of the world's largest public companies. Although the largest market for its six major brands is in the US, it also has a strong international presence, ranking in the top 20 in the world for frozen processed food, third globally for chilled processed food and second in the US in the same category. Outside of the US, it is amongst the five largest frozen processed food companies in Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Hillshire uses palm oil in its products; it sources palm-oil-containing raw materials for use in its manufacturing.
Hillshire itself has recently been acquired by Tyson Foods Inc., one of the largest producers and processors of meat, poultry and prepared foods in the world. Headquartered in Arkansas, Tyson was established in 1935 and remains under the ownership of the Tyson family. Although the majority of Tyson's operations are within the US, it also runs in country activities in poultry production in China, India, Mexico and Brazil, which utilise soya bean in poultry feed. The buyout of Hillshire by Tyson marks one of the biggest mergers in the packaged food industry and establishes Tyson firmly in the top two companies in the global processed meat market.

The company operates multiple brands in the health and beauty sector, including: Watsons, which has over 4,800 stores and 1,400 pharmacies in Asia and Europe; Kruidvat, which has over 1,000 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium; and Superdrug, which operates in the UK and Ireland and has over 870 stores. Watson also sells food, wine and electronics under multiple brands, which include: PARKnSHOP, which operates 340 supermarkets in Greater China; and SU-PA-DE-PA, which combines supermarket food products with department store ranges, such as clothing and entertainment. The company is a major European footwear retailer and is one of largest footwear retailers globally.  C & J Clark International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

The Wendy's Company (Wendy's) is the third largest quick service hamburger company in the world, with around 6,500 restaurants in the US and 29 other countries and US territories worldwide. Wendy's restaurants specialise in hamburgers and sandwiches but also offer fries, salads and desserts. The majority of the company's restaurants are in North America; in 2014, 6,112 restaurants operated in the US and Canada, with the majority run by franchises. The Wendy's Company has a joint venture with Restaurant Brands International covering around 100 restaurants in Canada. Outside of North America, there are 403 franchised restaurants in other countries and territories. In addition to beef and paper Wendy's uses soya (used in a range of spreads, dressings and baked products) and palm oil (used in snacks and desserts).

Home Depot Inc. is a leading home improvement retailer, selling construction materials and products for the home and garden. It was founded in 1978 in Atlanta, Georgia in the US, where the company now has its headquarters. Since the opening of its first two stores in Atlanta in 1979, the company has grown to become the largest retailer in the do-it-yourself (DIY) sector both in the US and globally. According to Home Depot, it is the fourth largest retailer in the US and the fifth largest in the world. Home Depot provides a range of products, including building materials, home improvement supplies, indoor and outdoor furniture, tools, and garden products for customers undertaking DIY activities.
The company has over 2,200 specialist stores throughout the US, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, China, Canada and Mexico. It entered the Canadian market in 1994 and now has 182 stores in ten of Canada's provinces. It entered the Mexican market in 2011, and has since become Mexico's largest home improvement retailer, with a total of 114 stores in the country. Home Depot's presence in China increased through its acquisition of The Home Way; China's first home improvement retailer. However, the company experienced slow growth in the Chinese market due to a low consumer appetite for DIY products and since then it has folded its store operations, closing its last store in Beijing in 2013.

AFM also own restaurants including Carluccio's and Giraffe Restaurants, home improvement companies including Leroy Merlin and fashion brands including Orsay. Well-known brands include Gap, Banana Republic, and Old Navy. Gap is one of the top clothing and footwear retailers selling exclusively own brand products in the world by brand share. It has significant presence in the US, Asia and Europe.  Gap Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and pulp & paper.

BRF Brasil Foods (BRF) is a Brazilian food manufacturer with products including poultry, specialty meats, frozen food, and condiments. Its brands, including Sadia, serve customers in 120 countries. The company is one of the largest poultry manufacturers in the world and claims to be responsible for more than 14% of the global poultry trade with over 1.9 million metric tons of poultry products sold in 2015. It is one of the ten largest producers of animal feed in the world with over 10 million metric tons of feed produced in 2015. BRF currently has an annual slaughtering capacity of around 180,000 heads of cattle.

SIFCA Group was founded in 1964 and is a conglomerate of four companies specialising in the production of palm oil, rubber and sugar in Africa. 27% of the group's shares are held by a company jointly owned by Wilmar International and Olam International, 44% are owned by Parme Investment, MMORIV owns 21% and the remaining 8% of SIFCA Group is owned by private shareholders.
Overall, the company employs around 30,000 people in 5 countries, with oil palm representing 40% of the group's turnover. PALMCI and SANIA are the two companies in the conglomerate that take part in the oil palm supply chain. PALMCI is responsible for the management of 39,000 hectares of industrial oil palm plantations and over 130,000 hectares of village plantations. SANIA is then responsible for utilising these upstream derivatives to produce final products that are used internally and also exported overseas. Through its refineries, SANIA has a production capability of approximately 280,000 MT of refined palm oil per year. Much of that capacity is provided by the SANIA processing plant in Abidjan, which has a crude palm oil capacity of 1,500 MT per day. Furthermore, through SAPH, SIFCA is the largest producer of rubber in Africa with over 20,000 hectares of industrial plantations. SANIA produces several edible oil and margarine products and markets them under different brands, including Palme d'Or, Dora, Saint Ave and Delicia. 
At the time of writing, SIFCA Group's website pages on sustainable development are many years out of date and do not appear to specifically address the issues of deforestation or sustainable palm oil production. None of the group companies appear to be members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Grupo SLC was established in in 1945 and is the majority shareholder (with a 51.3% majority ownership) of SLC Agricola SA, a Brazilian agricultural company involved in the production of soya beans, as well as cotton, corn and coffee, among other commodities. SLC Grupo also owns: SLC Alimentos SA, a producer of rice, beans and lentils; Ferramentas Gerais, which provides maintenance and repair services and machinery and equipment for the industrial sector; and SLC Commercial, which sells farm machinery under the John Deere brand in the state of Rio Grande do Sul.
SLC Agricola was started in 1977 with the acquisition of Paineira Farm in the Coronel Bicaco municipality, under the name of Agropecuaria Schneider Logemann Ltda. The company now has its headquarters in Porto Alegre, Brazil and operates 16 farms in six states. In 2012/2013, these farms comprised a total planted area of over 340,000 hectares; including over 185,000 hectares of soya beans. SLC Agricola claims to be one of the largest producers of soya beans in Brazil, and sells soya beans in domestic and overseas markets. The company has multiple subsidiaries, which further to agricultural production, are also involved in: leasing agricultural land; offering services such as storage to other cereal producers; trading, importing and exporting agricultural products; and real estate.

Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is one of the world's leading marketers of branded casual, active lifestyle, work, outdoor sport, athletic, children's and uniform footwear and apparel. Wolverine owns a number of well-known brands, including Merrell, Sperry Top-Sider, Hush Puppies, Saucony, Wolverine, Keds, Stride Rite, Sebago, Cushe, Chaco, Bates, HYTEST and Soft Style. The company is also the licensee of other recognised brands, including Cat, Harley-Davidson and Patagonia. The company's products are sold by leading retailers in around 200 countries and territories. Wolverine also operates 463 retail stores through leases with various third-party landlords in the US, Canada and United Kingdom.
In addition to its footwear and apparel business, Wolverine markets pigskin leather through its Wolverine Leathers subsidiary. About 98% (based on pairs) of the company's footwear products are sourced from third-party suppliers located primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Until recently the rest came from company-owned sources in the US and the Dominican Republic but the latter was recently closed.
In October 2012, Wolverine acquired Collective Brands Inc. via a consortium that also includes Golden Gate Capital and Blum Capital Partners. Collective Brands is in itself a major player in the footwear industry (owning the Payless brand, amongst others); it is a very large footwear retailer with more than 4,400 stores in over 30 countries.

Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company with a substantial portfolio of businesses operating in a diverse range of sectors. Founded in 1938, it employs over 35,000 people across a number of sectors such as manufacturing; trading and ï¬nancial services; oil and gas exploration; print and packaging; agriculture; ï¬sheries; real estate; and mining. In addition to its core business activities in Yemen, the group operates as a manufacturing firm and trading company across four global regions: Africa; Asia; Europe; and the Middle East. Its global business focuses on non-food, and beverage and food products such as confectionery and biscuits. It has an extensive logistics infrastructure to manufacture and distribute its own and partners' products across its global markets.
Pacific Inter-Link (PIL), one of the group's Malaysia-based companies, is involved in the processing and trading of palm oil. It was incorporated in 1988 to export commodities and employs 1,750 people in Malaysia and Indonesia. Its refineries had an annual processing capacity of 1.3 million tonnes per annum in 2012. PIL is one of the major exporters of palm oil from Asia to Africa and the Middle East, exporting to around 64 countries in total. The company is currently looking to expand further into the African market, with the development of new refineries in Ethiopia and Kenya. The company's brands include Avena and Madina, which both sell various palm oil products, such as margarine, shortening, cooking oil, and vegetable ghee, as well as a range of packaged food, including canned fish and meat, and pasta products. On top of its core palm oil products, the group also supplies dairy products under the Milgro, Milac, and Sheeba brands.

As such, Wendy’s  exposed to the forest risk commodities palm oil and soy, which are used as ingredients in its food products and as feed to its meat products, and paper which is used in its packaging. Mitsubishi Corp is a core company of the Mitsubishi Group; a group of autonomous companies made up of about 28 core enterprises and up to 600 member companies in all. The companies within the Mitsubishi Group conduct their operations independently of one another, but each honour the Group's three principles (of corporate social responsibility; integrity and fairness; and global understanding through business) and have their roots in the original shipping company, founded in 1870.
Mitsubishi Corp is a general trading company; the largest in Japan and the largest publicly-listed company of its kind in the world. The company's history extends back to 1954, when the Mitsubishi Shoji was established; however, Mitsubishi Corporation became the company's official English name in 1971. Mitsubishi Corp's activities now expand well beyond its original trading operations and it is involved in a wide variety of businesses, including energy, metals, food and environmental business.  Of particular relevance are Mitsubishi's operations in the production of food products that include soya and palm-based ingredients. Significantly, the Living Essentials department of Mitsubishi Corp also operates as a trading company in the palm oil industry, where it purchases predominantly Malaysian palm oil for export to Japan, the US and Taiwan, among others. The Living Essentials Group's activities in the production of consumer goods also include the procurement of raw materials and the manufacturing and distribution of a wide variety of products, including furniture, lumber, housing and construction materials, as well as many processed and frozen foods.
Mitsubishi Corp acquired UK-based food and drink manufacturer, Princes Ltd., in 1989. This is another particularly relevant component of Mitsubishi's operations. Founded in Liverpool, UK in 1880, Princes has since greatly increased its business portfolio diversifying from its original focus on the sale of canned goods. With a total of 19 mergers and acquisitions, it is now among the top food and drinks manufacturers in the UK.  Its tinned and canned products include meat pies, corned beef and stewed steak and the company is among the top five European beef importers from Brazil.
