rows.coprofile: H. Schmidt Holding were founded in 1780. They produce a range of leather products for cars, planes, trains and public seating areas. It is a world-leading manufacturer of high-class upholstery leather. They focus on the core areas of manufacturing and processing high-end upholstery leather for upmarket and interior sector. Sekisui House Ltd has operations in the housing construction industry, and in real estate brokerage and leasing. The company was established in 1960 and has its headquarters in Osaka, Japan. It claims to be Japan's largest and best known home builder and is listed among the largest companies globally as the second largest Japanese construction services company. 
Sekisui House Ltd has numerous subsidiaries across its various business segments, which comprise trade, brokerage and lease of real estate; remodelling; construction; surveying; and others including financial services and manufacturing. The company operates 19 construction subsidiaries across Japan under Sekisui Construction Ltd and as of January 2014 had constructed almost 2.2 million houses. Sekisui House Ltd has also been active in the Australian market since 2009, under Sekisui House Australia.
Sekisui House Ltd specialises in the construction of prefabricated housing and is the main player in Japan's prefabrication industry. Specifically, Sekisui House Ltd constructs and sells steel- and wooden-frame housing. The company's steel-frame housing was launched in the 1970's, marking the entrance of Sekisui House into the housing industry. This was followed by the launch of the company' wooden frame unit housing, Two-U Home, in 1982. The company now builds a variety of wooden frame housing, for example, the Gravis Bella wooden frame model, in its detached housing business. On top of its initial construction activities, Sekisui House Ltd also offers interior decoration and furnishing services.
The major shareholder of Sekisui House Ltd is Sekisui Chemical Co Ltd, which has operations worldwide and also has business interests in urban infrastructure, environmental products and high performance plastics.

IFFCO is an international business house, established in 1975 and based in the United Arab Emirates. IFFCO manufactures and markets a range of products for the mass consumer and industrial markets; producing around 7000 products and with a portfolio of 28 flagship brands, it sells its products in 84 countries worldwide, and has over 12,000 employees and offices in 21 countries.
The group's main business segments are: Impulse Foods; Agribusiness; Oils and Fats; Packaging; and Sales and Distribution. IFFCO therefore has multiple operations of relevance to forest risk commodity supply chain. For example, it's involvement in the production of packaged food, oils and fats, and in poultry farming, makes palm oil and soya of particular significance. Its Impulse Foods division manufactures and markets a range of convenience foods, including biscuits, savoury snacks, chocolates, confectionery, and ice creams, with brands such as London Dairy, Igloo, Tom and Break. While through its Agribusiness segment, IFFCO produces a range of food products, including poultry and eggs, bakery ingredients and frozen meat. IFFCO's joint venture with Oman Flour Mill is a fully-integrated poultry operation including a feed mill, parent bird and broiler farm, hatchery and processing facility. Finally, IFFCO's Oils and Fats segment manufactures products for the consumer and industrial markets, specialising in cooking oils, culinary products, and industrial fats for the food and personal care industries.
IFFCO has a worldwide presence, through its in-country offices, 33 manufacturing facilities and 6 distribution centres. Of particular note are IFFCO (Pakistan) Private Limited, IFFCO (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, and the group's various joint ventures, which include FELDA-IFFCO. FELDA-IFFCO is a partnership with plantation giant, FELDA; the largest producer of crude palm oil in Malaysia, with plantation land banks totalling 850,000 hectares, management of 530,000 hectares of plantations and a 7% share of the production market in 2011. FELDA-IFFCO also own 15 refineries in Malaysia, China, Turkey, Pakistan, South Africa and Canada, as well as four kernel crushing plants with a processing capacity of 8.4 million tonnes per year; producing around 20% of Malaysia's total crude palm kernel oil.
 IFFCO Pakistan is a major player in the edible oils and fats market. It operates the largest edible oil refinery in the country and is the only multinational company in Pakistan's edible oils industry. It procures raw materials domestically and internationally, including from Malaysia through FELDA-IFFCO. FINALLY, IFFCO Malaysia is an integrated oleo-chemical complex operating soap noodle and finishing plants that produce a variety of soap products and animal feed supplements.

Saint-Gobain SA is a multinational corporation that manufactures and distributes construction materials.  Established in France in 1665 as the first company to produce glass on an industrial scale, Saint-Gobain has a long history in the sector and is now a leading company in the distribution of building materials. Specifically, it is among the top five industry leaders in Europe's increasingly consolidated building products distribution sector. Saint-Gobain claims to be the largest of these industry players; with over 4,000 sales outlets and over 17,000 employees in the manufacturing and distribution sectors in the UK and Ireland alone.
Saint-Gobain houses several enterprises in the construction and building materials distribution industries. The company's construction products activities include the production of cast iron pipe systems, plasterboard and plaster products, insulation, industrial mortars and exterior products. Saint-Gobain's building distribution activities operate under several trading brands in 27 countries, including 16 brands in France, 12 in Germany and 18 in the UK.
International Timber is one of Saint-Gobain's brands in the UK, supplying timber and timber products to a range of industry sectors.  International Timber produces a variety of wood products, including hardwoods, softwoods, decking, flooring and engineered timber components. The company imports tropical sawnwood from South America, including from Brazil; from West Africa, including Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo; and from Asia, including Indonesia. Another of Saint-Gobain's subsidiaries in the UK is Jewson. Jewson is the UK's leading supplier of building materials and timber products, which it sources from International Timber.

Prada SpA is the holding company of the Prada Group, which with its subsidiary companies, is involved in the design, manufacture and retail of leather goods, clothing, shoes, and accessories. Prada was founded in Italy in 1913 as a specialist retailer selling accessories, luggage and other luxury items. Today, the Prada brand forms a component of the Prada Group, which has become an international leader in the luxury goods industry. On top of the flagship Prada brand, the Group sells products under the Miu Miu, Car Shoe and Church's brands.  Prada and Miu Miu provide customers with a variety of high-end luxury items, including leatherwear, handbags, apparel, footwear and fragrances. The Car Shoe and Church's brands are more specialist and each offer high-end luxury footwear. Church's is a leading English leather footwear brand that dates back to 1873, while Car Shoe specialises in leather moccasins specifically designed for driving. The Prada Group's brands are sold through its own outlets in stores and online, and through wholesale distribution channels. The Group has a worldwide presence, including in the top fashion markets of London, Milan, Tokyo, Beijing, Hong Kong and New York.
Prada SpA is a significant player in the bags and luggage industry. It ranks among the top five bags and luggage companies globally, and in the top five in China and top three in the Western European market. It also plays an important role in the international footwear industry, particularly in the markets of China, the US and Europe.  Leather goods therefore form an important component of the Prada Group's business; accounting for over 65% of consolidated net sales in the year up to January 2014, totalling over 2 billion Euros.

Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.

The WTK Group of companies has diverse business interests in forestry and timber processing, oil palm, land development, trading, and manufacturing, as well as other services, including insurance and shipping. Established in 1940, the group has its origins in timber activities and is the oldest of the top logging companies operating in Sarawak, Malaysia. One of the group's subsidiaries, WTK Holdings Berhad, is a publicly listed investment holding company, whose subsidiaries in turn are involved in timber harvesting and in downstream timber processing. WTK Group operates five sawmills and three plywood mills and is therefore involved in manufacturing and trading plywood, sawn timber, logs and other timber products for domestic and overseas markets. As well as producing and trading timber products, the group is also active in the trade of other goods, including adhesives.
As well as being one of the oldest logging operators in Sarawak, WTK Group is also one of the largest; it has a total of 850,000 hectares of timber concessions, 320,000 hectares of which are managed under WTK Holdings Bhd. The organisation also has 400,000 hectares of concessions in Papua New Guinea and further forestry operations in Indonesia. In Malaysia, WTK Group is well established, with further activities outside of the timber industry, including in tourism, hotels and shipping.
With regards to other forest risk commodities, WTK Group is increasingly diversifying into oil palm. The group has a total palm oil land bank of around 120,000 hectares in Sarawak, Malaysia. It also owns three oil mills and plans to enter into the refinery business in the future.

Coamo Agroindustrial Cooperativa (Coamo) was founded in 1970 to enable Brazilian farmers to share the costs of wheat processing and storage. Today, Coamo operates 115 warehouses and, in 2014, the cooperative processed 7.0 million tons of agricultural products and was responsible for 3.6% of Brazil's total grain and fibre production. In addition to wheat and maize, the company deals with coffee, cotton and, most significantly, soya; processing 1.5 million tons of soybeans in 2014.
The company is among Brazil's top five crushers and exporters of soya. Its processing facilities include five soybean crushing mills, a soybean oil refinery, a hydrogenated fat mill, margarine processing facilities, and cotton wheat mills, which in total process around 1.7 million tons of products annually. The cooperative and processing complex are located in Parana, in Southern Brazil. It has over 6,700 employees and as well as processed products, also produces its own brand coffee and soybean oil that are sold in the region.

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

ForFarmers B.V. is a major supplier of compound feed in the European market. The company also sells agricultural commodities such as fertilisers, seed and crop protection agents as well as advice services to its customers. With roots dating back to 1896, ForFarmers adopted its current name in 2005. The firm is transitioning its ownership structure from a cooperative to a shareholders structure. Presently, the firm remains majority-controlled (74%) by the cooperative FromFarmers and its members' accounts and certificates, with the remaining 26% under the ownership of other investors. In April 2016, ForFarmers will seek shareholders' approval to transfer to a technical listing on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange.
ForFarmers is the top feed supplier in both the Dutch and British markets, and is third and fourth in Belgium and Germany respectively. Also the company's biggest individual markets, the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany and Belgium account for 40%, 27% and 32% of sales respectively. The company sells around 8.9 million tons of feed per year, three quarters of which is compound feed.  In 2013, the largest proportion of its compound feed sales was pig feed at 37%, followed by cattle feed at 32%, and poultry feed at 22%. It employs over 2,300 people and has 42 manufacturing facilities at sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and the UK.
Acquisitions of feed businesses such as Hendrix, operating in Benelux and Germany, and BOCM Pauls, Wheyfeeds and HST Feeds in the UK, have helped to make ForFarmers Europe's largest compound feed producer. The company is looking at further acquisitions to enter new markets and to consolidate in existing European markets. ForFarmers also has strategic collaborations with direct competitors, including with Nutreco in the young animal feed business and with Agrifirm in the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and crop protection. As a major world compound feed producer, ForFarmers uses both soya and palm oil in its products.

Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

Lindt & Sprungli AG (Lindt) is a Swiss chocolatier founded in 1845, which describes itself as the market leader in the premium chocolates industry. The company sells in over 100 countries worldwide, with products under the brand names Ghirardelli, Caffarel, Hofbauer and Kufferle. Lindt employs a total of 8,949 people, has eight production sites (six in Europe and two in the USA) and distributes globally (including in China, Australia, South Africa, North America and Europe), with its largest markets being the European and NAFTA countries. The company distributes its products through a variety of avenues, including duty free retail outlets in airports, department stores, its own stores and Chocolate Cafes.
As a confectionery company, Lindt is ranked 7th in the world and 6th in Western Europe, and is also ranked among the top 50 packaged food companies globally. Further to this, Lindt is placed among the Forbes Global 2000 list. As a manufacturer of sweet snacks, Lindt uses palm oil in a number of its products and also includes soya derivatives, such as soya lecithin, as an ingredient in most of its chocolates.
Lindt has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2008. In 2012 it used 2,565m3 of palm oil and palm oil derived products; and it aims to be sourcing 100% RSPO-certified sustainable palm oil by 2015.

Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacture of a variety of paper products, including art paper, liquid packaging board, paying card, newsprint and copier paper. On top of its principal activities, making and selling paper products, the company also provides electricity, chemicals for paper manufacturing and construction materials. For example, through its subsidiaries Shandong Chenming Panels Co Ltd and Shouguang Chenming Floor Board Co Ltd, the company manufactures engineered wood products, including high-density fibreboard and wood flooring.
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd has manufacturing facilities located throughout China and distributes its products both domestically and to the international market, with overseas sales offices worldwide; in Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Brazil, and in Europe, India and Africa.  It is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies globally, ranking among the top 50, and as the second largest in China. The company produces around four million tonnes of paper products annually and until 2012 relied mostly on purchased chips and recovered fibre as the raw materials for its products. The company has since become increasingly integrated, developing a production base of plantation forests in China.

Grupo Bimbo SAB de CV (Grupo Bimbo) was founded by Lorenzo Servitje in Mexico in 1945. International expansion began in 1989, resulting in Grupo Bimbo becoming the largest bakery company in the world in terms of sales and production volume. The company's main markets are the US and Mexico but it also operates in Central and Latin America, Canada, Asia and Europe. In 2014, net sales were $14.1 billion. The company has 167 manufacturing plants located largely in its key markets, with 85 plants in the US and 39 in Mexico. In addition to its global manufacturing facilities, the company operates a distribution network with over 52,000 routes, feeding into 2.2 million points of sale in 19 countries. Today, Grupo Bimbo employs over 21,000 individuals.
Grupo Bimbo produces more than 10,000 different products under 100 umbrella brands including Bimbo, New York Bakery Co., Marisela and Ricolino. It manufactures bread, potato crisps, pastries and a variety of other snacks, many of which contain palm oil. The company continues to expand its business in international markets; it recently completed the acquisition of the previously public-listed company, Canada Bread, for $1.83 billion.

Mewah International Inc. (Mewah) is one of the dominant palm oil traders globally. It started operating in the 1950s with imports of palm oil from Malaysia to Singapore and is now involved in the production and distribution of a range of edible oils and fats. In 1987, Mewah opened its first refinery in Malaysia, producing 400 million tonnes per day, and has now opened a further two refineries, increasing its yearly capacity to 2.8 million tonnes. Mewah sources its raw materials from Malaysia and Indonesia before selling to the consumer and commercial markets in over 100 countries. It sells palm, soya bean, lauric, coconut, canola corn and sunflower oils commercially, and edible oils and fats on the consumer market. Mewah's consumer products are distributed via a range of different regional brands, such as Oki, Mona and Fry-ola, making it the world's leading edible oil company.
Mewah is also a key producer of food grade packaging for commercial and consumer markets. To continue to expand its business, Mewah is aiming to consolidate its position within the palm-based oil and fats business, expand its consumer product range, invest in efficient production facilities and expand its distribution network,. This has involved the construction of a new refinery in Sabah, Malaysia, which will increase Mewah's productivity to 3.5 million tonnes per year, along with the purchase of a new biodiesel facility in Westport, Malaysiaiv. Mewah has complemented these acquisitions with the installation of a new manufacturing facility in Malaysia, costing around $50 million, to produce a range of dairy products.
Mewah has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2006 and it expects to achieve 100% RSPO certification of all supply chains by 2015.

Nitori Holdings Co Ltd is a furniture company based in Hokkaido, Japan. The company dates back to 1967 when it opened its first furniture store and in 2010 the company was restructured: Nitori Holdings Co Ltd was established, marking the transition of Nitori Co Ltd to a holding company structure whereby Nitori Holdings Co Ltd oversees the Nitori group of companies,.The company operates a chain of furniture stores, and sells its own brand, manufactured as well as imported merchandise. It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand. Around 80% of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are sourced from overseas and as part of its expansion outside of Japan, the company also supports the operations of two furniture factories in Indonesia (since 1994) and Vietnam (since 2004). Some of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are manufactured at externally-owned facilities; however, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd maintains close contact with and involvement in all its business operations through the establishment of regional offices. Furthermore, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is directly responsible for the import and distribution of all products to its stores, with its subsidiary Home Logistics Co Ltd responsible for all domestic distribution.
In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.

Nitori Holdings Co Ltd is a furniture company based in Hokkaido, Japan. The company dates back to 1967 when it opened its first furniture store and in 2010 the company was restructured: Nitori Holdings Co Ltd was established, marking the transition of Nitori Co Ltd to a holding company structure whereby Nitori Holdings Co Ltd oversees the Nitori group of companies,.The company operates a chain of furniture stores, and sells its own brand, manufactured as well as imported merchandise. It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand. Around 80% of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are sourced from overseas and as part of its expansion outside of Japan, the company also supports the operations of two furniture factories in Indonesia (since 1994) and Vietnam (since 2004). Some of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are manufactured at externally-owned facilities; however, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd maintains close contact with and involvement in all its business operations through the establishment of regional offices. Furthermore, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is directly responsible for the import and distribution of all products to its stores, with its subsidiary Home Logistics Co Ltd responsible for all domestic distribution.
In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.

ForFarmers B.V. is a major supplier of compound feed in the European market. The company also sells agricultural commodities such as fertilisers, seed and crop protection agents as well as advice services to its customers. With roots dating back to 1896, ForFarmers adopted its current name in 2005. The firm is transitioning its ownership structure from a cooperative to a shareholders structure. Presently, the firm remains majority-controlled (74%) by the cooperative FromFarmers and its members' accounts and certificates, with the remaining 26% under the ownership of other investors. In April 2016, ForFarmers will seek shareholders' approval to transfer to a technical listing on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange.
ForFarmers is the top feed supplier in both the Dutch and British markets, and is third and fourth in Belgium and Germany respectively. Also the company's biggest individual markets, the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany and Belgium account for 40%, 27% and 32% of sales respectively. The company sells around 8.9 million tons of feed per year, three quarters of which is compound feed.  In 2013, the largest proportion of its compound feed sales was pig feed at 37%, followed by cattle feed at 32%, and poultry feed at 22%. It employs over 2,300 people and has 42 manufacturing facilities at sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and the UK.
Acquisitions of feed businesses such as Hendrix, operating in Benelux and Germany, and BOCM Pauls, Wheyfeeds and HST Feeds in the UK, have helped to make ForFarmers Europe's largest compound feed producer. The company is looking at further acquisitions to enter new markets and to consolidate in existing European markets. ForFarmers also has strategic collaborations with direct competitors, including with Nutreco in the young animal feed business and with Agrifirm in the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and crop protection. As a major world compound feed producer, ForFarmers uses both soya and palm oil in its products.

IFFCO is an international business house, established in 1975 and based in the United Arab Emirates. IFFCO manufactures and markets a range of products for the mass consumer and industrial markets; producing around 7000 products and with a portfolio of 28 flagship brands, it sells its products in 84 countries worldwide, and has over 12,000 employees and offices in 21 countries.
The group's main business segments are: Impulse Foods; Agribusiness; Oils and Fats; Packaging; and Sales and Distribution. IFFCO therefore has multiple operations of relevance to forest risk commodity supply chain. For example, it's involvement in the production of packaged food, oils and fats, and in poultry farming, makes palm oil and soya of particular significance. Its Impulse Foods division manufactures and markets a range of convenience foods, including biscuits, savoury snacks, chocolates, confectionery, and ice creams, with brands such as London Dairy, Igloo, Tom and Break. While through its Agribusiness segment, IFFCO produces a range of food products, including poultry and eggs, bakery ingredients and frozen meat. IFFCO's joint venture with Oman Flour Mill is a fully-integrated poultry operation including a feed mill, parent bird and broiler farm, hatchery and processing facility. Finally, IFFCO's Oils and Fats segment manufactures products for the consumer and industrial markets, specialising in cooking oils, culinary products, and industrial fats for the food and personal care industries.
IFFCO has a worldwide presence, through its in-country offices, 33 manufacturing facilities and 6 distribution centres. Of particular note are IFFCO (Pakistan) Private Limited, IFFCO (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, and the group's various joint ventures, which include FELDA-IFFCO. FELDA-IFFCO is a partnership with plantation giant, FELDA; the largest producer of crude palm oil in Malaysia, with plantation land banks totalling 850,000 hectares, management of 530,000 hectares of plantations and a 7% share of the production market in 2011. FELDA-IFFCO also own 15 refineries in Malaysia, China, Turkey, Pakistan, South Africa and Canada, as well as four kernel crushing plants with a processing capacity of 8.4 million tonnes per year; producing around 20% of Malaysia's total crude palm kernel oil.
 IFFCO Pakistan is a major player in the edible oils and fats market. It operates the largest edible oil refinery in the country and is the only multinational company in Pakistan's edible oils industry. It procures raw materials domestically and internationally, including from Malaysia through FELDA-IFFCO. FINALLY, IFFCO Malaysia is an integrated oleo-chemical complex operating soap noodle and finishing plants that produce a variety of soap products and animal feed supplements.
initiatives: Awarded full points as FELDA-IFFCO are the main subsidary of interest

The Kroger Co. is one of the world's largest grocery retailers, operating a number of store formats including grocery and multi-department stores, discount stores, convenience stores and jewellery stores. Food stores are the company's primary business and account for around 94% of total sales. As of December 2015, in the US Kroger Co. operated 2,774 grocery retail stores, 786 convenience stores and 326 jewellery stores. The company also operates 37 food processing and manufacturing facilities producing for the company's private-label brands.
In 2013, the 2,640 supermarkets accounted for 93% of Kroger Co.'s revenue and they are split into four major formats across multiple different banners: Combination stores; Multi-department stores; Market place stores; and Price impact warehouse stores.
Combinations stores make up the bulk of the estate (85%) and provide a complete supermarket offering, many including pharmacies, bakeries, delis, seafood, meat and florist shops. The combination stores operate under 15 different banners, including Ralphs, King Soopers, City Market and Kroger. Multi-Department Stores are Kroger Co's largest format stores and operate under the Fred Meyer / Freddy's banner. They typically comprise food and pharmacy departments, as well as a broad range of clothing, shoes, accessories, electronics, homewares, furniture, garden furniture, toys, sporting and automotive goods. Fred Meyer is the third largest supercentre operator in the US. The Market Place Stores, which have a smaller offering than the Multi-Department Stores, operate under multiple banners such as King Soopers Market Place, Kroger's Market Place and Dillons Market Place. They provide a full grocery offering with some also selling clothing and furniture. Finally, the Price Impact Warehouse stores offer lower cost grocery and health and beauty items under the Food 4 Less, Foods Co, Ruler Foods and PriceRite banners.     
Convenience stores accounted for 5% of Kroger Co's total sales in 2013 and offer a variety of Kroger branded products. Around 90% of convenience stores are operated by subsidiaries with the remainder being run through franchise agreements.
Kroger Co manufactures approximately 40% of its corporate brand products, which accounted for 27% of units sold in 2013. Kroger Co's manufacturing plants produce dairy products, meat, bakery products, salads, spices and drinks. Kroger has committed to using only 100% sustainably sourced palm oil in its own brand products by the end of 2015 and to work with its private label suppliers to improve their supply chains as well. In addition, Kroger uses significant amounts of packaging in its products and it recently announced that it would stop using Asia Pulp and Paper as a supplier due to concerns over its connections with deforestation.

It is ones of the largest companies across the Republic of Congo, Cameroon, and Gabon, as of 2016.  All of these regions also have sawmills and manufacturing facilities which process  timber products.  Rougier Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

As a market leader in this field Sekisui House is exposed to the forest risk commodity timber.   Sekisui House Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

The SIFCA Group is an agribusiness group based in the Ivory Coast active throughout the supply chain of several agricultural commodities, including rubber, sugar cane, and palm oil. SIFCA is a major palm oil producer in West Africa. It also processes palm oil and produces products such as margarine.  SIFCA Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

DLG Denmark, established in 1964, is one of Europe's biggest agricultural companies. It is owned by 30,000 Danish farmers and employs 7,500 people, 3,000 of whom are in Denmark. Through over 40 subsidiaries and associated companies, DLG Denmark is involved in a broad range of business and consumer sectors, with localised operations in in more than 20 countries. 
DLG Denmark is organised into four business areas: Premix and Nutrition, accounting for 4% of turnover, provides specialist animal feeds and minerals; Service and Energy, contributing 28% of turnover, provides a broad range of products and services including fuels, telecommunications and IT, and also operates DIY stores and petrol stations; Machinery, Flowers and Food, which accounts for 6% of turnover, provides industrial and agricultural machinery as well as a broad range of plants and food products, including oils and vegetables; and Farm Supply, the largest division, providing 62% turnover, encompasses animal feed production, poultry hatcheries, provision of fertiliser and pesticides, and crop production.
DLG Denmark produces compound feeds for farm animals at its mills in Europe and is one of Europe's top five largest producers of compound feeds. Soya is a significant feed production ingredient, accounting for around 15 to 20% composition. Consequently, DLG Denmark buys around half of Denmark's soymeal. DLG Denmark uses a similar amount of palm oil in its animal feed.

BCA are a top financier in Indonesia, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

SHV Holdings is a Dutch trading company. The company owns Nutreco, which is one of the global leaders in animal nutrition and aquafeed. The company sells its products in more than 90 countries. According to Nutreco, its brand Skretting is the leading manufacturer of aquaculture feed in the world. Soy and palm oil are often used in animal feed products.   SHV holdings is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB) are a leading bank in Northern Europe with a history dating back to 1856. SEB claim they are a thought leader and pioneer, having collaborated with the World Bank in 2008 to issue its first green bond. SEB hold 3.579 trillion SEK of assets under management. In the 2024 selection, Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB) was providing 29.6 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses across the globe. The company offers products such as groceries, apparel, furniture, houseware, office suppliers and health and beauty aids across 762 warehouses as of 2018.

China Mengniu Dairy (Mengniu) is a Chinese manufacturer and distributor of dairy products. Its products include milk, ice-cream, cheese, and other dairy products. The company is one of the top dairy companies in China and globally, whilst also ranking highly for other dairy products and packaged food. It is also a major Chinese importer of palm oil.  China Mengniu Dairy Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Paper Excellence Group was selected as a powerbroker for Pulp & Paper (Manufacturer)

De Heus was founded in 1911 and has grown from a regional Dutch feed manufacturer into an international conglomerate. It is now Europe's fourth largest compound animal feed producer and cites itself as a global top 15 animal feed supplier. The company has activities in over 50 countries in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa and employs 3,000 people worldwide, operating around 30 feed mills. De Heus is still owned and managed by the De Heus Family.
De Heus manufactures feed for cattle, pigs, poultry and aquaculture; it also provides customised feed for individual farms. Subsidiaries include: Koudijis Animal Nutrition, which exports feed and related products to other European countries, Middle Eastern and African markets; and Agra-Matic, an agricultural consultancy operating in the Netherlands and Poland, providing advice in a number of areas including animal husbandry, the environment, technology and planning.
De Heus has focused upon expansion outside of Europe and entered a number of markets by establishing joint ventures in countries including China, Russia, Belgium, Ethiopia and Egypt. Further examples include an agreement with Brazilian firm, Nutrifarms LTDA, signed 2012, giving De Heus access to the Brazilian pig feed market. Investments expanding the company's infrastructure outside of Europe have also intensified DeHeus' international operations. For example, in 2013, the company opened a fourth feed factory in South Africa, manufacturing feed for not only traditional livestock but also ostrich and game. De Heus is currently investing in Vietnam, looking to become one of the top five largest feed producers. In March 2015, the company announced the opening of two new factories. Construction of a seventh Vietnamese factory is underway; a project that will cost around $30 million.
initiatives: As in 7.1, the commitment to sustainable palm oil and soya are only for the suppliers producing for the Dutch market. It is not stated what their demands are for suppliers that supply for their products produced and sold elsewhere in the world.
Does not mention that they recognise the role of forest in climate regulation.

rows.coprofile: The earliest foundations of the Oetker-Gruppe lie in 1891, when Dr August Oetker developed the baking powder, Backin, in Germany. The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. The Oetker-Gruppe sells its products to the consumer market under the brand, Dr Oetker. Its consumer products include; frozen pizzas, ready desserts and a number of other chilled and frozen products. Through the Martin Braun group, the Oetker-Gruppe sells a number of baking agents, glazes and decorations to baking and confectionary companies. The manufacturing of these products meant that the Oetker-Gruppe used 4,777 tonnes of palm oil or palm oil derivatives in 2013. Oetker-Gruppe has been a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) since 2011 and in 2012, four of its manufacturing facilities in Germany were certified as RSPO supply chain certified (all palm oil and palm oil derivatives used are RSPO-certified).

Lowe’s Companies is a major home improvement company based in the US with operations in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and worldwide.  Lowe's Companies Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging.

Prada is an Italian fashion retailer. Prada is a luxury brand producing leather goods, clothing, footwear, eyewear, fragrance, and confectionary. Famous brands include Prada, Miu Miu, and Church’s. The company is among the top fashion companies in the world and uses leather in its products.  Prada SpA is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.
Anta Sports was selected as a powerbroker for Leather (Manufacturer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Rubber (Manufacturer)

Association Familiale Mulliez (AFM) was selected as a powerbroker for Palm oil (Retailer), Beef (Retailer), Cocoa (Retailer), Coffee (Retailer), Soy (Retailer), Pulp & Paper (Packaging) and is also assessed for Timber (Retailer)

Nomura are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving private, corporate, government and institutional clients. Their services include retail, asset management, global markets and investment banking. As of 2021, Nomura's total assets amount to over 42.5 trillion Yen and 64.7 trillion Yen of assets under management. They are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2022 selection, Nomura was providing 38.7 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Nike Inc is one of the world's largest athletic apparel company and designs, markets, and distributes athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, and accessories. The Company’s famous brands include Nike, Converse, Hurley, and Jordan. Many of Nike’s shoes are made using leather.  Nike Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather, pulp & paper and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Banco do Brasil are a state-controlled bank headquartered in Brazil serving private, corporate and government clients. Their services include investments, insurance, pensions, retail banking services, capital markets and corporate finance. As of 2022, Banco do Brasil's total assets amount to more than 362 billion USD. Banco do Brasil are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading. In the 2022 selection, Banco do Brasil was providing 3.2 bilion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

The Mitsubishi Corporation is a global business enterprise that operates businesses in approximately 110 countries and regions worldwide, with activities spanning multiple industries including fresh food retail, food ingredient manufacturing, animal feed production, and agricultural raw material production and trade. Mitsubishi Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil, beef and paper packaging through its various subsidiaries.

Staples Inc is one of the world’s largest specialist retailers of office supplies, with key product lines in stationary, furniture and technology products. Amongst its products are a wide variety of paper goods, including copy paper, printer paper, POS rolls and letterheads. As a leading retailer of these goods Staples is exposed to the forest risk commodities paper, pulp and timber.   Staples Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and pulp & paper.

Its products include building materials, appliances, furniture and flooring. Of its sales, the vast majority are in the US. It is one of the largest home improvement chains in the US and worldwide. Lowe's Companies Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather, timber and paper packaging.

Grupo Nueva is a Chilean holding company that operates through its subsidiaries specialized in the forestry and wood derivatives industries. Its subsidiary, Masisa, operates in the business of wood boards across Latin America.  Grupo Nueva is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Restaurant Brands International is one of the world’s largest fast food companies, operating over 30,000  restaurants in almost 100 countries. Through it's brands Tim Hortons, Burger King, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs, it is one of the top fast food companies in Europe, the US and in the world. The varied menu of both chains expose them to a range of forest risk commodities.  Restaurant Brands International is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

rows.coprofile: Bata is a footwear retailer and manufacturer active in more than 90 countries around the world. The company produces more than 140 million pairs of shoes a year from sandals to smart leather shoes and women's heels. Major brands include Marie Claire, North Star and Sandak. It is one of the largest footwear retailers in Italy and is among the top fifteen globally by brand share. Bata is also one of Europe's largest footwear and leather retailers.

Steve Madden Ltd., based in the US, manufactures and sells footwear on a global scale, as such it is exposed to the forest risk commodity leather.   Steve Madden Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Samko Timber is an Indonesian company involved in the production and processing of forestry products. Samko Timber is a major processor of timber, claiming to be one of the world’s top tropical hardwood plywood producers.  Samko Timber Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.
Toyota Group was selected as a powerbroker for Rubber (Manufacturer, Retailer), Leather (Manufacturer, Retailer)

The Mitsubishi Corporation is a diversified business with activities across a wide range of sectors, including energy, industrial goods, metals, machinery, and finance, as well as food products. The breadth of its living essentials business group exposes the company to many forest risk commodities. Some of these businesses include agricultural traders, food processors, restaurant chains, and animal feed manufacturers. The Mitsubishi Corporation is a major trader of palm oil. Its subsidiaries also rank among the top five European importers of Brazilian beef.  Mitsubishi Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and beef.

California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) is a public pension fund headquartered in the US serving private and corporate clients. Its services include investment management, actuarial services, and retirement, death benefit and health benefit programmes. CalPERS are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, CalPERS was providing 28 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

BRF Brasil Foods is a Brazilian food manufacturer with products including poultry, specialty meats, frozen food, and condiments. Its brands, including Sadia, serve customers in 120 countries. The company is one of the largest poultry manufacturers in the world and is one of the largest producers of animal feed in the world.  BRF Brasil Foods S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

The Godrej Group is a conglomerate active in diverse industries, including agriculture, consumer and industrial goods, food, furniture, and construction. The breadth of its portfolio exposes the group to a number of forest risk commodities. Godrej’s subsidiary Godrej Industries produces crude palm oil and oleo-chemical products. The group is also involved in the production of animal feed and is one of the largest producers of annual feed in India. Moreover, the group’s home care consumer goods business, with brands such as Good Knight and Hit, is one of the largest in India and Indonesia. It is also a significant player in India for packaged food and personal care.  Godrej Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy, beef, timber and pulp & paper.

Oetker-Gruppe is a German manufacturer of packaged food. The majority of the company’s products are frozen pizzas, baking goods, desserts, dry ready meals, beverages, and snacks. Oetker-Gruppe operates internationally with more than 400 companies working in a variety of different business segments.   Oetker-Gruppe is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Seven & i is a Japanese holding company with over 87,000 stores worldwide as of 2022. Its main subsidiary is the convenience store 7-Eleven, with the others operating in the fields of real estate, food services, financial services, manufacturing and processing. As a leading retailer with a diversified product portfolio, Seven & I Holdings is exposed to several forest risk commodities and is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to leather and timber.

IFFCO is an international business house, established in 1975 and based in the United Arab Emirates. IFFCO manufactures and markets a range of products for the mass consumer and industrial markets; producing around 7000 products and with a portfolio of 28 flagship brands, it sells its products in 84 countries worldwide, and has over 12,000 employees and offices in 21 countries.
The group's main business segments are: Impulse Foods; Agribusiness; Oils and Fats; Packaging; and Sales and Distribution. IFFCO therefore has multiple operations of relevance to forest risk commodity supply chain. For example, it's involvement in the production of packaged food, oils and fats, and in poultry farming, makes palm oil and soya of particular significance. Its Impulse Foods division manufactures and markets a range of convenience foods, including biscuits, savoury snacks, chocolates, confectionery, and ice creams, with brands such as London Dairy, Igloo, Tom and Break. While through its Agribusiness segment, IFFCO produces a range of food products, including poultry and eggs, bakery ingredients and frozen meat. IFFCO's joint venture with Oman Flour Mill is a fully-integrated poultry operation including a feed mill, parent bird and broiler farm, hatchery and processing facility. Finally, IFFCO's Oils and Fats segment manufactures products for the consumer and industrial markets, specialising in cooking oils, culinary products, and industrial fats for the food and personal care industries.
IFFCO has a worldwide presence, through its in-country offices, 33 manufacturing facilities and 6 distribution centres. Of particular note are IFFCO (Pakistan) Private Limited, IFFCO (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, and the group's various joint ventures, which include FELDA-IFFCO. FELDA-IFFCO is a partnership with plantation giant, FELDA; the largest producer of crude palm oil in Malaysia, with plantation land banks totalling 850,000 hectares, management of 530,000 hectares of plantations and a 7% share of the production market in 2011. FELDA-IFFCO also own 15 refineries in Malaysia, China, Turkey, Pakistan, South Africa and Canada, as well as four kernel crushing plants with a processing capacity of 8.4 million tonnes per year; producing around 20% of Malaysia's total crude palm kernel oil.
 IFFCO Pakistan is a major player in the edible oils and fats market. It operates the largest edible oil refinery in the country and is the only multinational company in Pakistan's edible oils industry. It procures raw materials domestically and internationally, including from Malaysia through FELDA-IFFCO. FINALLY, IFFCO Malaysia is an integrated oleo-chemical complex operating soap noodle and finishing plants that produce a variety of soap products and animal feed supplements.
Hain Celestial Group, Inc. is an American food and personal care manufacturing company operating across North America and Europe.

Agrifirm is a Dutch agricultural cooperative consisting of over 17,000 farmers and horticulturalists. It combines the collective purchasing power of its members, making savings on the bulk purchase of products such as animal feed ingredients, seeds and fertilisers. The cooperative has several subsidiaries which expand its operations across Europe, North and South America, Asia and Africa. Agrifirm represents a significant portion of Europe’s soy imports and is also an importer of palm oil. Agrifirm is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Boparan Holdings is the parent company of the 2 Sisters Food Group, which produces around a third of all poultry products eaten every day in the United Kingdom. 2 Sisters Food Group operates in three divisions (protein, added value and chilled, and meals) and its main customers include restaurants such as KFC and supermarkets including Aldi, Asda, Co-op, Lidl, Marks & Spencer and Tesco. Boparan also owns restaurant groups including Giraffe and Carluccio's and other food companies including Bernard Matthews.   Boparan Holdings is selected as a powerbroker for soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and beef.

AmorePacific Corp is a Korean manufacturer of beauty, personal care and household products. It has business operations in China, France, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, India, Australia, Russia, Indonesia, Thailand, Japan,  Canada, and the US. AmorePacific Corp is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to soy.

Walgreens Boots Alliance is an Anglo-Swiss-American pharmaceutical company based in Illinois with over 12,500 locations across the U.S., Europe and Latin America. They own the retail pharmacy chains Walgreens and Boots as well as other manufacturing and distribution companies. They have been selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and pulp and paper.

Dekeloil is a palm oil company operating in Côte d’Ivoire. The company engages in both the development and cultivation of palm oil plantations, and the processing and manufacture of crude palm oil.  DekelOil is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil.

Granol is a Brazilian agribusiness company operating solely in Brazil that processes and refines agricultural products. The company is a major processor of soy and is also involved in the production of biodiesel. Granol is among the largest exporters of soy from Brazil.  Granol is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Pertamina Persero PT is a state-owned Indonesian company focussing on oil, gas, renewable energy and new energy. This involves the exploration and extraction of oil and gas as well as the development of geothermal energy and coal bed methane as alternate energy sources. In addition, the company is involved in crude oil processing and the marketing, trade and shipping of oil products, gas and petrochemicals. The company is also involved in the domestic retail of gasoline and diesel and has an extensive network of over 5000 retail gas stations across Indonesia.
As per a government mandate in 2013, all diesel for industry and transportation in Indonesia must contain 10% biofuel. This has led to Pertamina Persero PT issuing a number of tenders for palm oil-based biodiesel to meet these requirements. Palm oil companies Wilmar International and Musim Mas have already won tenders to supply biodiesel to Pertamina Persero PT and more tenders are planned for the future. A total of 5.3 million kilolitres (around 4.7 million MT) of palm-based biodiesel will be procured for 2014-2015.

Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.

R. R. Donnelley is a commercial printing company founded in 1864. It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. Their customers include some of the world's most well known companies including; Accenture, Barclays, IBM, and Microsoft. Despite offering a number of digital communication strategies, they are primarily known as a supplier of print material and is the leading company of its kind globally.  R. R. Donnelley also prints products for other companies involved in the printing and publishing sector. For example, it supplies print products to Pearson PLC and to HarperCollins, two of the world's largest publishers. In 2013 it employed roughly 57,000 people across four continents, in nearly 40 countries, leading to sales of $10.5 billion. It continues to expand through strategic acquisitions of companies specialising in both digital and commercial print. For example, in 2011, it acquired LibreDigital, a pioneering digital publishing and distribution company, and in 2014 acquired Consolidated Graphics in a deal worth over $600 million.

Nine Dragons Paper Holdings Ltd (ND Paper) is a paper and paper packaging manufacturer that produces a variety of containerboard and paper products, including: linerboard; corrugating medium and coated duplex board; recycled printing and writing paper; and tissue paper. As well as paper products, ND Paper manufactures wood-, bamboo-, and unbleached kraft pulp. The company's products are manufactured under three brands: Nine Dragons, Land Dragon and Sea Dragon, each focusing on a different customer segment.  ND Paper is well known for its use of recovered paper; the company's main source of raw material. This is used in the manufacturing of some of its products, such as its testlinerboard, made from 100% recovered paper, and its Sea Dragon office paper. The company imports significant amounts of recovered paper from the US; however, this is not used exclusively in all products.
The company was established in 1995 and is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies, ranking among the top 30 globally and holding the leading position in China. ND Paper has six manufacturing bases across China, as well as in Vietnam and Mongolia, through joint ventures: Cheng Yang Paper and Nine Dragons Xing An Pulp & Paper (Inner Mongolia) Co Ltd. Originally, the company predominantly supplied packaging for manufacturers in southern China's export oriented industry; however, the business has increasingly tapped into the demand for packaging products from the domestic market as China's own consumer-demand has grown.
Blondeau Group are the parent company of German firelighter manufacturer, Boomex. Boomex are a leading supplier of grill and coal lighters in Europe.

BRF Brasil Foods (BRF) is a Brazilian food manufacturer with products including poultry, specialty meats, frozen food, and condiments. Its brands, including Sadia, serve customers in 120 countries. The company is one of the largest poultry manufacturers in the world and claims to be responsible for more than 14% of the global poultry trade with over 1.9 million metric tons of poultry products sold in 2015. It is one of the ten largest producers of animal feed in the world with over 10 million metric tons of feed produced in 2015. BRF currently has an annual slaughtering capacity of around 180,000 heads of cattle.

Japan based Seven & I Holdings Co Ltd (Seven & I Holdings) is a holding company that established from the merger of Ito-Yokado Co, Seven Eleven Japan Co, and Denny's Japan. Through its subsidiaries, Seven & I Holdings operates convenience stores, food supermarkets, department stores, general merchandise stores, food services, financial services and IT services.
As of 2014, there were around 56,000 Seven & I Holdings stores in 16 different countries in Asia, Scandinavia, the Americas and Australia, serving, on average, 58 million customers per day, 20.5 million of which were in Japan. The bulk of the portfolio is made up of over 56,600 7-Eleven convenience stores, the world's largest franchise chain store. In addition to the 7-Eleven banner Seven & I Holdings operate Sogo & Seibu department stores; several hundred food supermarkets under the York Mart and York-Benimaru banners; superstores predominantly using the Ito Yokado banner; a number of speciality stores; and restaurants, including around 470 Denny's restaurants in Japan. Seven & I Holdings also have a number of consumer financial services subsidiaries. Within the food sector, Seven & I subsidiaries have a number of own or private brand labels including 7-Select, Seven Premium and Seven Gold; these brands include meat products, baked goods, desserts and confectionary.

rows.coprofile: AEON is a Japanese based company primarily focused on retail with more than 300 subsidiaries across 13 countries. Its business is primarily focussed in the Asia-Pacific region and includes supermarkets, convenience stores, and home stores amongst others. This range of shops exposes the group to a wide range of forest risk commodities. In the Asia-Pacific region it is one of the largest retailers of edible groceries. It also has a significant global market share, making AEON a major player on both the regional and global scale. Its grocery business is especially prominent in Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Thailand.

OCBC are among the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 4 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors, especially in agriculture and agriculture commodities.

Vicentin is an Argentinian agro-industrial company active in textiles, agriculture, and agricultural products. It is a major player in the Argentinian soy market with a significant market share for soy crushing. Vicentin is also one of the largest exporters of soy from Argentina and among the top ten from Paraguay. Uni-President Enterprises Corp (UPEC) manufactures and distributes a range of food products through its network of 200 affiliate companies and convenience stores. The company was incorporated in 1967 in Tainan County, Taiwan. It was originally established as a rural flour factory but over the decades has grown into an international conglomerate with operations across Asia Pacific. The manufacturing of food products is one of the company's core businesses and although it has a wide range of interests, including sports teams, retail operations and pharmaceuticals, the manufacture of food and feed are the group's largest operations. Its main products include feeds, edible oils, soya sauce, meat products, instant noodles, dairy products and frozen foods, among others.
The manufacture and marketing of food and feed products are undertaken by five main groups. The Provisions Group manufactures and markets flour, fertilizer, eggs, and animal and aquatic feeds to Asian and other international markets. The Dairy and Beverage Group manufactures dairy products, teas, soft drinks, coffee and other beverages under brands such as €œPure Tea€, €œRae-Shie€ and €œLa Gauche de la Seine€.  In addition to Taiwan, the Dairy and Beverage Group operates in mainland China, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Edible oils and instant noodles are produced by the Instant Food Group, which has a 50% market share of Taiwan's instant noodle market. Instant products are also sold outside of Taiwan with products available in 30 countries across five continents. Brands include Unif, Imperial, One More Cup, Kikkoman, A-HA, Juicymart and Pure Tea. The two smallest Groups are the General Foods and Health groups. The former provides meat products, ice cream, sauces and ready meals while the Health Group manufactures bakery and health products,.
Of particular relevance is President Nisshin Corp, a member of Uni-President that supplies oils and fats, including palm oil products, to the food industry. Furthermore, palm oil is also used in other products, for example in instant noodles, and is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soya, imported from both the US and South America, is used in Uni-President's feed and edible oil products.

Morgan Stanley are an international investment bank and financial services provider headquartered in the US that serves private, corporate and institutional clients. Services include wealth management, investment banking, capital markets, sales and trading, and research and investment management. As of 2024 their total assets under management amount to 1.6 trillion USD. Morgan Stanley are among the top lenders and shareholders to Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors. In the 2024 selection, Morgan Stanley was providing 232.2 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

The Kroger Co. is one of the world's largest grocery retailers, operating a number of store formats including grocery and multi-department stores, discount stores, convenience stores and jewellery stores. Food stores are the company's primary business and account for around 94% of total sales. As of December 2015, in the US Kroger Co. operated 2,774 grocery retail stores, 786 convenience stores and 326 jewellery stores. The company also operates 37 food processing and manufacturing facilities producing for the company's private-label brands.
In 2013, the 2,640 supermarkets accounted for 93% of Kroger Co.'s revenue and they are split into four major formats across multiple different banners: Combination stores; Multi-department stores; Market place stores; and Price impact warehouse stores.
Combinations stores make up the bulk of the estate (85%) and provide a complete supermarket offering, many including pharmacies, bakeries, delis, seafood, meat and florist shops. The combination stores operate under 15 different banners, including Ralphs, King Soopers, City Market and Kroger. Multi-Department Stores are Kroger Co's largest format stores and operate under the Fred Meyer / Freddy's banner. They typically comprise food and pharmacy departments, as well as a broad range of clothing, shoes, accessories, electronics, homewares, furniture, garden furniture, toys, sporting and automotive goods. Fred Meyer is the third largest supercentre operator in the US. The Market Place Stores, which have a smaller offering than the Multi-Department Stores, operate under multiple banners such as King Soopers Market Place, Kroger's Market Place and Dillons Market Place. They provide a full grocery offering with some also selling clothing and furniture. Finally, the Price Impact Warehouse stores offer lower cost grocery and health and beauty items under the Food 4 Less, Foods Co, Ruler Foods and PriceRite banners.     
Convenience stores accounted for 5% of Kroger Co's total sales in 2013 and offer a variety of Kroger branded products. Around 90% of convenience stores are operated by subsidiaries with the remainder being run through franchise agreements.
Kroger Co manufactures approximately 40% of its corporate brand products, which accounted for 27% of units sold in 2013. Kroger Co's manufacturing plants produce dairy products, meat, bakery products, salads, spices and drinks. Kroger has committed to using only 100% sustainably sourced palm oil in its own brand products by the end of 2015 and to work with its private label suppliers to improve their supply chains as well. In addition, Kroger uses significant amounts of packaging in its products and it recently announced that it would stop using Asia Pulp and Paper as a supplier due to concerns over its connections with deforestation.

De Heus is a Dutch conglomerate producing animal feed and active in more than 50 countries around the world. The group produces animal feed for poultry, cattle, pigs, and other animals, as well as providing support services and company solutions. It is one of the largest animal feed producers in the Netherlands and the world.  De Heus is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

The Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group are a global financial and banking group headquartered in Japan offering a broad range of financial services to private and corporate clients. Their services include corporate finance, investment management and financial and operating leases, as well as retail banking and consumer finance. As of 2017, the group's total assets amount to more than 190 trillion Yen. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial are among the top 20 loan providers to Forest 500 companies, with more than 25 billion USD of loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Hormel Foods is an American food manufacturer. The company has a range of different products including ready meals, meat products, snacks, and beverages. Hormel Foods is one of the largest manufacturers of ready meals in the world. The large-scale operations within food manufacturing require the use of forest risk commodities such as palm oil, soy, and beef.  Hormel Foods Corp. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Bank Mandiri are a bank and financial service provider headquartered in Indonesia serving corporate and private clients. Their services span consumer, corporate, commercial, micro, retail, treasury and international banking including loans and mortgages. As of 2022, Bank Mandiri's total consolidated assets amount to more than 1,700 trillion IDR with more than 1,100 trillion IDR in loans. In the 2022 selection, Bank Mandiri was providing 3.7 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

De Heus was founded in 1911 and has grown from a regional Dutch feed manufacturer into an international conglomerate. It is now Europe's fourth largest compound animal feed producer and cites itself as a global top 15 animal feed supplier. The company has activities in over 50 countries in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa and employs 3,000 people worldwide, operating around 30 feed mills. De Heus is still owned and managed by the De Heus Family.
De Heus manufactures feed for cattle, pigs, poultry and aquaculture; it also provides customised feed for individual farms. Subsidiaries include: Koudijis Animal Nutrition, which exports feed and related products to other European countries, Middle Eastern and African markets; and Agra-Matic, an agricultural consultancy operating in the Netherlands and Poland, providing advice in a number of areas including animal husbandry, the environment, technology and planning.
De Heus has focused upon expansion outside of Europe and entered a number of markets by establishing joint ventures in countries including China, Russia, Belgium, Ethiopia and Egypt. Further examples include an agreement with Brazilian firm, Nutrifarms LTDA, signed 2012, giving De Heus access to the Brazilian pig feed market. Investments expanding the company's infrastructure outside of Europe have also intensified DeHeus' international operations. For example, in 2013, the company opened a fourth feed factory in South Africa, manufacturing feed for not only traditional livestock but also ostrich and game. De Heus is currently investing in Vietnam, looking to become one of the top five largest feed producers. In March 2015, the company announced the opening of two new factories. Construction of a seventh Vietnamese factory is underway; a project that will cost around $30 million.

Stichting Pensioenfonds ABP (ABP) are a pension fund based in the Netherlands for public and education sector employees. As of 2017, they have 403 billion EUR in available assets. They are among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies, across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Agrifirm is a Dutch agricultural cooperative consisting of over 17,000 farmers and horticulturalists. It combines the collective purchasing power of its members, making savings on the bulk purchase of products such as animal feed ingredients, seeds and fertilisers. The cooperative has several subsidiaries which expand its operations across Europe and into Russia and China. Agrifirm represents a significant portion of Europe’s soy imports and is also an importer of palm oil.   Agrifirm is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Though the company primarily uses chips and recovered material in production, it also imports raw materials internationally. It therefore has a high risk of exposure to tropical wood in its supply chain.  Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co., Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.
