Skechers USA is a company that manufactures and markets footwear, which is sold in both company-owned retail stores as well as through other retail channels. The company has two categories of footwear, lifestyle and performance, which are available in 160 countries around the world. Skechers was one of the top footwear companies in the world by brand share. It is also one of the largest in the US and among the five largest in China.

Caramuru Alimentos are a Brazilian company specialising in the processing and manufacture of soy, corn, sunflower and canola. The company operate across Brazil in animal, biodiesel, commodity, industrial, consumer products and logistics segments.

Meiji Holdings Co. Ltd. (Meiji Holdings) is a Japanese holding company, headquartered in Tokyo, that through its subsidiaries has operations in the manufacture of dairy products, confectionery, health food and pharmaceuticals. The company, in its current holding company structure, was established in 2008; however, its origins extend back to the early 1900s, with the establishment of Meiji Sugar Co. Ltd. and Meiji Dairies Corporation in 1906, and then Meiji Co. Ltd. (a manufacturer of confectionery) in 1916.  
Meiji Holdings' business activities now fall under Meiji Co. Ltd. and Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd. Meiji Co. Ltd. produces a variety of food products, under its confectionery, dairy, healthcare & nutritionals, and international business units. Whereas Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd manufactures pharmaceuticals in three main segments: anti-infective drugs, therapeutic drugs for neural disorders, and generic drugs. The company is active within Japan and internationally, through its overseas network of companies, which can be found throughout Asia, Europe and North America. Meiji Holdings ranks among the top 2,000 public companies in the world and has over 14,000 employees.
The company's operations in packaged food manufacturing, in particular its use of palm and soya products in the production of sweets, chocolate and ice cream, are of particular importance with respect to forest risk commodities. For example, palm oil and palm kernel oil can be found in Meiji's brands of chocolate cookies and crackers, Chococones and Chocorooms, which it markets in the United States. Similarly, palm oil and soya derivatives can be found in other products, such as Meiji's Apollo Strawberry Chocolate Candy.
Meiji Holdings is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

The WTK Group of companies has diverse business interests in forestry and timber processing, oil palm, land development, trading, and manufacturing, as well as other services, including insurance and shipping. Established in 1940, the group has its origins in timber activities and is the oldest of the top logging companies operating in Sarawak, Malaysia. One of the group's subsidiaries, WTK Holdings Berhad, is a publicly listed investment holding company, whose subsidiaries in turn are involved in timber harvesting and in downstream timber processing. WTK Group operates five sawmills and three plywood mills and is therefore involved in manufacturing and trading plywood, sawn timber, logs and other timber products for domestic and overseas markets. As well as producing and trading timber products, the group is also active in the trade of other goods, including adhesives.
As well as being one of the oldest logging operators in Sarawak, WTK Group is also one of the largest; it has a total of 850,000 hectares of timber concessions, 320,000 hectares of which are managed under WTK Holdings Bhd. The organisation also has 400,000 hectares of concessions in Papua New Guinea and further forestry operations in Indonesia. In Malaysia, WTK Group is well established, with further activities outside of the timber industry, including in tourism, hotels and shipping.
With regards to other forest risk commodities, WTK Group is increasingly diversifying into oil palm. The group has a total palm oil land bank of around 120,000 hectares in Sarawak, Malaysia. It also owns three oil mills and plans to enter into the refinery business in the future.

Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.

Prada SpA is the holding company of the Prada Group, which with its subsidiary companies, is involved in the design, manufacture and retail of leather goods, clothing, shoes, and accessories. Prada was founded in Italy in 1913 as a specialist retailer selling accessories, luggage and other luxury items. Today, the Prada brand forms a component of the Prada Group, which has become an international leader in the luxury goods industry. On top of the flagship Prada brand, the Group sells products under the Miu Miu, Car Shoe and Church's brands.  Prada and Miu Miu provide customers with a variety of high-end luxury items, including leatherwear, handbags, apparel, footwear and fragrances. The Car Shoe and Church's brands are more specialist and each offer high-end luxury footwear. Church's is a leading English leather footwear brand that dates back to 1873, while Car Shoe specialises in leather moccasins specifically designed for driving. The Prada Group's brands are sold through its own outlets in stores and online, and through wholesale distribution channels. The Group has a worldwide presence, including in the top fashion markets of London, Milan, Tokyo, Beijing, Hong Kong and New York.
Prada SpA is a significant player in the bags and luggage industry. It ranks among the top five bags and luggage companies globally, and in the top five in China and top three in the Western European market. It also plays an important role in the international footwear industry, particularly in the markets of China, the US and Europe.  Leather goods therefore form an important component of the Prada Group's business; accounting for over 65% of consolidated net sales in the year up to January 2014, totalling over 2 billion Euros.

The Rougier Group is an international company, based in France and operating in the timber supply chain. It produces primary timber products, such as sawnwood, plywood and logs; and processed products, such as joists and decking, as well as other materials for the construction, packaging and furniture industries. 
Its main operations consist of natural forest harvesting and wood processing in Africa through Rougier Afrique International; imports and distribution of timber products in France through Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux; and management and investment in industrial forest plantations in Africa, through Lignafrica.
Rougier Group's production and processing operations in Africa through Rougier Afrique International are in the Republic of Congo, Cameroon and Gabon, where it is among the largest forestry companies, managing a total area of around 2 million hectares. In Gabon, Rougier Group exploits around 880,000 hectares of forests under four forest concessions, and also operates one plywood factory and three sawmills. In Cameroon, it operates through its subsidiary Societe ForestiÃ¨re et Industrielle de la Doume (SFID; Doume Forestry Company), which exploits 550,000 hectares of forests and operates two sawmills and a secondary timber processing workshop. Rougier Group also operates in the northern Republic of Congo through its subsidiary, Mokabi SA. Mokabi SA manages 586,000 hectares of forests and operates a sawmill.
Rougier Sylvaco Panneaux imports to France over 40,000 cubic metres per year from Africa, America, Europe and Asia. Rougier Sylvaco Panneax is the result of a merger between Rougier Group's two subsidiaries: Rougier Sylvaco and Rougier Panneaux. The merger aims to position Rougier Group better in the French market, which is experiencing increased concentration among its operators.

Hillshire Brands Co. (Hillshire) is a food giant from Chicago which manufactures and markets meat-based products. Founded in 1939, Hillshire acquired many notable brands over the years, including Jimmy Dean and Ball Park Franks, which is reportedly the top hotdog brand in the US and worth over $500 million in revenue.  Hillshire has 9,500 employees and sales of $4.09 billion as of May 2013, placing it among the Forbes Global 2000 list of the world's largest public companies. Although the largest market for its six major brands is in the US, it also has a strong international presence, ranking in the top 20 in the world for frozen processed food, third globally for chilled processed food and second in the US in the same category. Outside of the US, it is amongst the five largest frozen processed food companies in Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Hillshire uses palm oil in its products; it sources palm-oil-containing raw materials for use in its manufacturing.
Hillshire itself has recently been acquired by Tyson Foods Inc., one of the largest producers and processors of meat, poultry and prepared foods in the world. Headquartered in Arkansas, Tyson was established in 1935 and remains under the ownership of the Tyson family. Although the majority of Tyson's operations are within the US, it also runs in country activities in poultry production in China, India, Mexico and Brazil, which utilise soya bean in poultry feed. The buyout of Hillshire by Tyson marks one of the biggest mergers in the packaged food industry and establishes Tyson firmly in the top two companies in the global processed meat market.

WH Group, formerly Shuanghui International is headquartered in Hong Kong and has business operations in three segments: packaged meat, fresh pork and hog production. Its global portfolio includes Shuanghui Development, Smithfield Foods and Campofrio Food Group. The anglicised name for Shuanghui Group is Shineway Group and it holds the top market positions for canned or preserved, and chilled processed food in China and is also among the top ten globally for chilled processed foods and the top 40 for packaged food.
The Shineway Group is the largest meat processing company in China, occupying a significant share of the market and employing some 60,000 people. Shanghui/Shineway is the company's original Chinese brand; manufacturing fresh pork and retorted and pasteurised packaged meat products in more than ten product ranges (including King of Kings and Spicy Crispy Sausage) and over 200 cuts and styles of fresh and chilled meat. However, although it advertises itself as the largest pork company in the world and therefore focuses on hog slaughtering and processing, the company's operations in the beef and poultry sectors have recently expanded.
Within the United States, Smithfield Food manufactures pork products and exports them as far as China, Mexico, Russia, Japan and Canada. Brand names include Smithfield, Margherita, Farmland, Armour and Curly's, amongst others; and products include smoked and boiled hams, bacon, sausage, deli meats, hot dogs, luncheon meats, pepperoni, dry meat, and finally pre-prepared foods (supplying grocery stores and restaurants alike). Smithfield is one of the five largest chilled processed food companies in the world and supplies to brands in around 50 countries.
Finally, Campofrio Food Group, in which WH Group owns a 37% share, (the largest packaged meat company in Europe) is the European branch of WH Group's business; it operates in Spain, France, Belgium, Holland, Germany, Italy, Portugal and the US.

COFCO Group was founded in 1949 and operates in the edible seed market via China Agri Holdings Ltd. It is the second largest crusher of oilseeds (behind Wilmar International) and has 13% of the market share of oilseed crushing capability and over 9% of the market share for soybeans. Its manufacturing plants are located close to major food consumption markets including in Tianjin, Jiangsu, Shandong, Guangdong, Guangxi, Hubei and Xinjiang. Historically, the company has focused its business activities in downstream activities. However, in February 2014, COFCO bought a majority stake (51%) in Nidera, a Dutch commodities trader, in order to gain access to South American grain and oilseed goods, while in April 2014, the company acquired a controlling stake (51%) in Noble Agri, which owns oilseeds processing plants and a grain processing and distribution business. In May 2015, COFCO announced it will merge its holdings in Nidera and Noble Agri to create a new entity, COFCO International Holdings, in a joint venture with China Investment Corp, a sovereign wealth fund who will own 19.9% of the new business, with the ultimate intention of merging COFCO's own domestic business into COFCO International to combine COFCO's oil, grain and sugar assets.
COFCO Group retains a strong presence in the downstream market, with a number of branded goods sold across China. They sell shortening and margarine as well as a number of speciality products such as soybean milk fat. In total, their annual sales volume exceeds 120,000 tonnes across 31 Chinese provinces. Its brands include Sihai for soybean meal products and Fuzhiquan for cooking oils.
As well as being a major player in the processed food industry, COFCO Group has a long history in the timber sector and claims to be the largest integrated timber merchant in China. One of the Group's subsidiaries, China Timber Co. Ltd., has operated traded timber internationally for over fifty years. It imports a wide variety of timber and timber products from a range of countries, including raw timber from Papua New Guinea and Myanmar; and plywood, construction materials and furniture from Africa and South America. It also exports wood flooring and plywood and other manufactured wood products to the US, Europe, Japan and India.
Of particular relevance are China Timber's operations in the Republic of Gabon, where it holds five timber companies engaged in the direct harvesting of timber and timber processing activities. It has around one million hectares of tropical hardwood forests. Specifically, it operates Sunly Gabon, which is one of the largest Chinese firms operating in the Gabonese forestry sector and has several hundred thousand hectares of forest concessions in the north-east, east and southern parts of the country.

rows.coprofile: The Charoen Pokphand Group (C. P. Group) is a diverse Thai business conglomerate with 200 subsidiaries in 18 countries that cover the agribusiness, food, telecommunications, and retail industries, amongst others. The group operates integrated food supply chains for poultry and pork involving it heavily in the production of animal feed and food products. It is one of the largest poultry companies in Thailand and places among the ten largest poultry companies in the world. Its subsidiaries are also among the top fifteen global producers of animal feed.

WH Group, formerly Shuanghui International is headquartered in Hong Kong and has business operations in three segments: packaged meat, fresh pork and hog production. Its global portfolio includes Shuanghui Development, Smithfield Foods and Campofrio Food Group. The anglicised name for Shuanghui Group is Shineway Group and it holds the top market positions for canned or preserved, and chilled processed food in China and is also among the top ten globally for chilled processed foods and the top 40 for packaged food.
The Shineway Group is the largest meat processing company in China, occupying a significant share of the market and employing some 60,000 people. Shanghui/Shineway is the company's original Chinese brand; manufacturing fresh pork and retorted and pasteurised packaged meat products in more than ten product ranges (including King of Kings and Spicy Crispy Sausage) and over 200 cuts and styles of fresh and chilled meat. However, although it advertises itself as the largest pork company in the world and therefore focuses on hog slaughtering and processing, the company's operations in the beef and poultry sectors have recently expanded.
Within the United States, Smithfield Food manufactures pork products and exports them as far as China, Mexico, Russia, Japan and Canada. Brand names include Smithfield, Margherita, Farmland, Armour and Curly's, amongst others; and products include smoked and boiled hams, bacon, sausage, deli meats, hot dogs, luncheon meats, pepperoni, dry meat, and finally pre-prepared foods (supplying grocery stores and restaurants alike). Smithfield is one of the five largest chilled processed food companies in the world and supplies to brands in around 50 countries.
Finally, Campofrio Food Group, in which WH Group owns a 37% share, (the largest packaged meat company in Europe) is the European branch of WH Group's business; it operates in Spain, France, Belgium, Holland, Germany, Italy, Portugal and the US.

DBS are a financial services group headquartered in Singapore serving private and commercial clients. Their services include wealth management, corporate finance, institutional investment, insurance, and retail banking services. As of 2017, the group's total assets amount to more than 480 billion SGD, with over 300 billion SGD in customer loans. DBS are among the top 35 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 8 billion USD across the agriculture, agricultural commodities and consumer goods sectors.

The company has been selected as a powerbroker for leather.

One of its subsidiaries is Molinos Río de la Plata, an agribusiness company in Argentina involved in the procurement of agricultural raw materials as well as producing several branded products such as vegetable oils. The company is a major exporter of soy from Argentina.  Perez Companc Family Group is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil.

The Triputra Group is an Indonesian company, headquartered in Jakarta. The group is comprised of four main business segments: agribusiness, manufacturing, mining and, trading and services. Of most relevance are the company's operations in the production of agricultural commodities, which include rubber and palm oil. The group's subsidiary, Triputra Agro Persada (established in 2005) and its affiliates have a land bank of around 388,000 hectares and plan to increase this to 600,000 hectares by 2020.
Triputra Agro Persada began with the acquisition of PT Brahma Binabakti in Jambi province in Sumatra. In 2007, the company established a partnership with Union Sampoerna, marking the acquisition of 63,000 hectares of plantations in Central Kalimantan. The following year, in 2008, a partnership was formed with Yudha Group, further expanding the company's acreage with 20,000 hectares in East Kalimantan. The company continued to grow through other partnerships and with the support of a total of 13 national and international financial institutions, including ANZ, Bank Mandiri, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubushi and Rabobank. Triputra Agro Persada produced around 200,000 tons of crude palm oil in 2011 and employed around 24,000 people. It claims to be one of the largest oil palm companies in Indonesia.
PT Triputra Agro Persada is a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). In 2013 it reported to have 14,500 hectares of area under palm oil plantation and to have produced 90,000 MT of crude palm oil, 14,400 MT of palm kernel. It expects to achieve 100% certification of its estates by the end of 2015.

rows.coname: Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co. Ltd.
rows.coprofile:
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacture of a variety of paper products, including art paper, liquid packaging board, paying card, newsprint and copier paper. On top of its principal activities, making and selling paper products, the company also provides electricity, chemicals for paper manufacturing and construction materials. For example, through its subsidiaries Shandong Chenming Panels Co Ltd and Shouguang Chenming Floor Board Co Ltd, the company manufactures engineered wood products, including high-density fibreboard and wood flooring.
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd has manufacturing facilities located throughout China and distributes its products both domestically and to the international market, with overseas sales offices worldwide; in Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Brazil, and in Europe, India and Africa.  It is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies globally, ranking among the top 50, and as the second largest in China. The company produces around four million tonnes of paper products annually and until 2012 relied mostly on purchased chips and recovered fibre as the raw materials for its products. The company has since become increasingly integrated, developing a production base of plantation forests in China.

SIFCA Group was founded in 1964 and is a conglomerate of four companies specialising in the production of palm oil, rubber and sugar in Africa. 27% of the group's shares are held by a company jointly owned by Wilmar International and Olam International, 44% are owned by Parme Investment, MMORIV owns 21% and the remaining 8% of SIFCA Group is owned by private shareholders.
Overall, the company employs around 30,000 people in 5 countries, with oil palm representing 40% of the group's turnover. PALMCI and SANIA are the two companies in the conglomerate that take part in the oil palm supply chain. PALMCI is responsible for the management of 39,000 hectares of industrial oil palm plantations and over 130,000 hectares of village plantations. SANIA is then responsible for utilising these upstream derivatives to produce final products that are used internally and also exported overseas. Through its refineries, SANIA has a production capability of approximately 280,000 MT of refined palm oil per year. Much of that capacity is provided by the SANIA processing plant in Abidjan, which has a crude palm oil capacity of 1,500 MT per day. Furthermore, through SAPH, SIFCA is the largest producer of rubber in Africa with over 20,000 hectares of industrial plantations. SANIA produces several edible oil and margarine products and markets them under different brands, including Palme d'Or, Dora, Saint Ave and Delicia. 
At the time of writing, SIFCA Group's website pages on sustainable development are many years out of date and do not appear to specifically address the issues of deforestation or sustainable palm oil production. None of the group companies appear to be members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Hillshire Brands Co. (Hillshire) is a food giant from Chicago which manufactures and markets meat-based products. Founded in 1939, Hillshire acquired many notable brands over the years, including Jimmy Dean and Ball Park Franks, which is reportedly the top hotdog brand in the US and worth over $500 million in revenue.  Hillshire has 9,500 employees and sales of $4.09 billion as of May 2013, placing it among the Forbes Global 2000 list of the world's largest public companies. Although the largest market for its six major brands is in the US, it also has a strong international presence, ranking in the top 20 in the world for frozen processed food, third globally for chilled processed food and second in the US in the same category. Outside of the US, it is amongst the five largest frozen processed food companies in Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Hillshire uses palm oil in its products; it sources palm-oil-containing raw materials for use in its manufacturing.
Hillshire itself has recently been acquired by Tyson Foods Inc., one of the largest producers and processors of meat, poultry and prepared foods in the world. Headquartered in Arkansas, Tyson was established in 1935 and remains under the ownership of the Tyson family. Although the majority of Tyson's operations are within the US, it also runs in country activities in poultry production in China, India, Mexico and Brazil, which utilise soya bean in poultry feed. The buyout of Hillshire by Tyson marks one of the biggest mergers in the packaged food industry and establishes Tyson firmly in the top two companies in the global processed meat market.

De Heus was founded in 1911 and has grown from a regional Dutch feed manufacturer into an international conglomerate. It is now Europe's fourth largest compound animal feed producer and cites itself as a global top 15 animal feed supplier. The company has activities in over 50 countries in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa and employs 3,000 people worldwide, operating around 30 feed mills. De Heus is still owned and managed by the De Heus Family.
De Heus manufactures feed for cattle, pigs, poultry and aquaculture; it also provides customised feed for individual farms. Subsidiaries include: Koudijis Animal Nutrition, which exports feed and related products to other European countries, Middle Eastern and African markets; and Agra-Matic, an agricultural consultancy operating in the Netherlands and Poland, providing advice in a number of areas including animal husbandry, the environment, technology and planning.
De Heus has focused upon expansion outside of Europe and entered a number of markets by establishing joint ventures in countries including China, Russia, Belgium, Ethiopia and Egypt. Further examples include an agreement with Brazilian firm, Nutrifarms LTDA, signed 2012, giving De Heus access to the Brazilian pig feed market. Investments expanding the company's infrastructure outside of Europe have also intensified DeHeus' international operations. For example, in 2013, the company opened a fourth feed factory in South Africa, manufacturing feed for not only traditional livestock but also ostrich and game. De Heus is currently investing in Vietnam, looking to become one of the top five largest feed producers. In March 2015, the company announced the opening of two new factories. Construction of a seventh Vietnamese factory is underway; a project that will cost around $30 million.

C&J Clark International (Clarks) is a UK footwear company operating in over 75 countries. It designs, manufactures, and sells a wide range of footwear. The company is a major European footwear retailer and is one of largest footwear retailers globally.  C & J Clark International Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

ForFarmers B.V. is a major supplier of compound feed in the European market. The company also sells agricultural commodities such as fertilisers, seed and crop protection agents as well as advice services to its customers. With roots dating back to 1896, ForFarmers adopted its current name in 2005. The firm is transitioning its ownership structure from a cooperative to a shareholders structure. Presently, the firm remains majority-controlled (74%) by the cooperative FromFarmers and its members' accounts and certificates, with the remaining 26% under the ownership of other investors. In April 2016, ForFarmers will seek shareholders' approval to transfer to a technical listing on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange.
ForFarmers is the top feed supplier in both the Dutch and British markets, and is third and fourth in Belgium and Germany respectively. Also the company's biggest individual markets, the Netherlands, the UK, and Germany and Belgium account for 40%, 27% and 32% of sales respectively. The company sells around 8.9 million tons of feed per year, three quarters of which is compound feed.  In 2013, the largest proportion of its compound feed sales was pig feed at 37%, followed by cattle feed at 32%, and poultry feed at 22%. It employs over 2,300 people and has 42 manufacturing facilities at sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and the UK.
Acquisitions of feed businesses such as Hendrix, operating in Benelux and Germany, and BOCM Pauls, Wheyfeeds and HST Feeds in the UK, have helped to make ForFarmers Europe's largest compound feed producer. The company is looking at further acquisitions to enter new markets and to consolidate in existing European markets. ForFarmers also has strategic collaborations with direct competitors, including with Nutreco in the young animal feed business and with Agrifirm in the purchase of seeds, fertilisers and crop protection. As a major world compound feed producer, ForFarmers uses both soya and palm oil in its products.

Natuzzi S.p.A. (Natuzzi) is the parent company of the Natuzzi Group, an Italian furniture company, established in 1959. It is involved in the design, manufacture, and marketing of furniture, and specialises in leather and upholstered products such as sofas, armchairs and other living room accessories. Cattle hides and wood are among the key raw materials used by Natuzzi in the manufacture of its products, and significantly, sales of leather-upholstered furniture comprised over 94% of the company's net sales and 85% of the company's revenue in 2013.
The group has numerous subsidiaries, registered worldwide, including in Brazil, China, Italy and elsewhere in Europe, Japan, Russia, India and Australia.
As a leader in leather upholstery and the largest furniture manufacturer overall in Italy, Natuzzi plays a key role in the international leather trade, with customs data revealing that the company imports significant volumes of leather from Brazil. Further to this, Natuzzi owns one active manufacturing facility in Brazil, which aims to increase local sourcing from 2014 onwards.
Natuzzi offers products under several brands: Natuzzi Italia; Natuzzi Editions, also known as Leather Editions; Natuzzi Re-vive; and private label. Natuzzi Editions is the group's brand focusing on the medium-high end of the market. It was developed and is sold solely in the US market and its products are manufactured in China, Brazil and Romania. The Leather Editions brand offers similar leather products to Natuzzi Editions, but is marketed in Europe and the rest of the world, apart from in North and South America. Natuzzi Re-vive, launched in 2013, sells Natuzzi branded performance recliners.  Finally, the company has developed private label products to maintain its competitiveness in the low-end market segment.
The group's furniture products are sold through a range of retail outlets worldwide, including: franchised stores, Divani & Divani by Natuzzi and Natuzzi, which are all located in Italy and Portugal; its Natuzzi Editions and Leather Editions stores; and also through several large global furniture retailers, such as IKEA, Macy's, and Nitori.

Groupe Blattner Elwyn is a conglomerate based in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), active in a variety of sectors, including agribusiness, logistics and distribution, and timber processing . Agriculture is at the core of Groupe Blattner Elwyn's operations and the group's agribusiness activities are in the production and processing of rubber, palm oil and cocoa. The Group's industrial operations are in: The production of crown corks and metal cans; timber processing and harvesting; and in the production of laminated table-tops, through a company based in France. Finally, Groupe Blattner Elwyn has a variety of distribution and services companies, which include medical operations, chemical production, the automotive industry, and importing and exporting activities.
Groupe Blattner Elwyn has six subsidiaries involved in the cultivation and processing of palm oil managing some 28,311 hectares of land, 17,196 of which are currently in production. The group operates six oil palm factories and provides employment for around 10,000 permanent and temporary workers and sharecroppers.
Regarding the group's timber operations, Groupe Blattner Elwyn acquired SIFORCO from Danzer Group in February 2012. This acquisition was Groupe Blattner Elwyn's first step into the forestry sector, which the Group views as an investment in the growing timber industry in the DRC. SIFORCO, which was established in 1972, manages an area of over 1.9 million hectares in the DRC, making it one of the largest logging companies in the country in terms of forest area. SIFORCO has 600 employees and the majority of its concessions are located in the Equateur and Orientale provinces. The company harvests its natural forests for the production of logs and also has timber processing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer, and a joiner's workshop. It harvests and processes timber mainly for the European and American markets.

The WTK Group of companies has diverse business interests in forestry and timber processing, oil palm, land development, trading, and manufacturing, as well as other services, including insurance and shipping. Established in 1940, the group has its origins in timber activities and is the oldest of the top logging companies operating in Sarawak, Malaysia. One of the group's subsidiaries, WTK Holdings Berhad, is a publicly listed investment holding company, whose subsidiaries in turn are involved in timber harvesting and in downstream timber processing. WTK Group operates five sawmills and three plywood mills and is therefore involved in manufacturing and trading plywood, sawn timber, logs and other timber products for domestic and overseas markets. As well as producing and trading timber products, the group is also active in the trade of other goods, including adhesives.
As well as being one of the oldest logging operators in Sarawak, WTK Group is also one of the largest; it has a total of 850,000 hectares of timber concessions, 320,000 hectares of which are managed under WTK Holdings Bhd. The organisation also has 400,000 hectares of concessions in Papua New Guinea and further forestry operations in Indonesia. In Malaysia, WTK Group is well established, with further activities outside of the timber industry, including in tourism, hotels and shipping.
With regards to other forest risk commodities, WTK Group is increasingly diversifying into oil palm. The group has a total palm oil land bank of around 120,000 hectares in Sarawak, Malaysia. It also owns three oil mills and plans to enter into the refinery business in the future.

Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. PT Rajawali Corpora is an investment holding company of the Rajawali Group, an Indonesian conglomerate active in a variety of industries, including telecommunications, hotels, consumer goods, retail, transportation, coal, gold and iron mining, and agriculture. The Group's agricultural activities comprise palm, sugar, rubber and corn plantations. Founded in 1984, the company is based in Jakarta and employs some 30,000 people. It was founded and is owned by Peter Sondakh, who is among the richest men in Indonesia and also ranks among the top billionaires globally. 
The company has a growing presence in the agricultural industry. PT Jaya Madiri Sukses (JMS Group) is the plantation arm of the Rajawali Group, and is a holding company comprising of a total of seven plantation companies in South and East Kalimantan. In 2010, Rajawali was reported to begin planting its 200,000 hectare land bank with oil palm. In 2011 Rajawali entered into a joint venture with commodities trader Louis Dreyfus called Green Eagle Plantations Pte Ltd. In 2012, the venture was reported to operate in four regions in Indonesia (South, West and East Kalimantan, and Papua), with concessions of around 50,000 hectares. However, in 2014, Louis Dreyfus Commodities Asia Pte left the joint venture, selling its 50% share of Green Eagle to the Rajawali Group. More recently, in September 2014, through a purchase of two investment firms, Matacuna Group and Pegasus CP One, Rajawali reportedly has acquired a 21% stake in crude palm oil producer, BW Plantation.

It also has a significant global market share, making AEON a major player on both the regional and global scale. Its grocery business is especially prominent in Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Thailand.

Sodefor (Société de Développement Forestier) is the largest logging company in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with concessions of over 2 million hectares. The company harvests timber from its concession areas and processes timber for the production of sawn wood and plywood. Sodefor and three other major forestry companies in DRC, Societe Forestiere et des Matieres Ligneuses Africaines (Soforma), Compagnie Forestière de Transformation (CFT) and Societe Forestière et Agricole de la M'Bola (Forabola), are all linked via a common shareholder (Norsudtimber S.A.), however are managed separately. These are among the most significant forestry companies in the country. Soforma operates the third largest area of concessions and oversees around 996,000 hectares of forest in the Cuvette Centrale region, while Forabola and CFT rank fourth and fifth respectively, in terms of area under concession.
Norsudtimber is a private Portuguese-owned company registered in Liechtenstein.

Hillshire Brands Co. (Hillshire) is a food giant from Chicago which manufactures and markets meat-based products. Founded in 1939, Hillshire acquired many notable brands over the years, including Jimmy Dean and Ball Park Franks, which is reportedly the top hotdog brand in the US and worth over $500 million in revenue.  Hillshire has 9,500 employees and sales of $4.09 billion as of May 2013, placing it among the Forbes Global 2000 list of the world's largest public companies. Although the largest market for its six major brands is in the US, it also has a strong international presence, ranking in the top 20 in the world for frozen processed food, third globally for chilled processed food and second in the US in the same category. Outside of the US, it is amongst the five largest frozen processed food companies in Australia, Hong Kong and Malaysia. Hillshire uses palm oil in its products; it sources palm-oil-containing raw materials for use in its manufacturing.
Hillshire itself has recently been acquired by Tyson Foods Inc., one of the largest producers and processors of meat, poultry and prepared foods in the world. Headquartered in Arkansas, Tyson was established in 1935 and remains under the ownership of the Tyson family. Although the majority of Tyson's operations are within the US, it also runs in country activities in poultry production in China, India, Mexico and Brazil, which utilise soya bean in poultry feed. The buyout of Hillshire by Tyson marks one of the biggest mergers in the packaged food industry and establishes Tyson firmly in the top two companies in the global processed meat market.

The Nisshin OilliO Group Ltd (Nisshin OilliO) is a Japanese company involved in the processing and manufacturing of oils and oil-based products. Established in 1907, it claims to be the largest vegetable oil company in Japan and today operates a number of companies involved in the manufacture, processing and distribution of manufactured goods, including oils, fats and chemical products. Its main business segments are: Oils and Meals; Processed Oils and Fats; Healthy Foods; Fine Chemicals; and Soya Foods and Materials. Nisshin OilliO's main oil-based products include: edible oils for household and commercial use, and food processing; margarines, shortenings, and other processed and speciality oils and fats; healthy oil products, premium oils and soya bean oil; and finally, dressings, and other healthy food products. However, its business operations also extend to a variety of other sectors, with the group also active in the insurance, marketing and restaurant industries, among others.
The Nisshin OilliO Group has four manufacturing facilities in Japan, as well as overseas subsidiaries in China, Taiwan, Malaysia, Singapore, Europe and North America. In 2005, the Group acquired Malaysian company, Intercontinental Speciality Fats Sdn. Bhd (ISF), an edible oils and fats manufacturer, supplying products for the chocolate and confectionery, bakery, dairy, and convenience food industries. ISF operates two refineries in Malaysia , where it occupies a 5% of the oil palm refinery market.

Meiji Holdings Co. Ltd. (Meiji Holdings) is a Japanese holding company, headquartered in Tokyo, that through its subsidiaries has operations in the manufacture of dairy products, confectionery, health food and pharmaceuticals. The company, in its current holding company structure, was established in 2008; however, its origins extend back to the early 1900s, with the establishment of Meiji Sugar Co. Ltd. and Meiji Dairies Corporation in 1906, and then Meiji Co. Ltd. (a manufacturer of confectionery) in 1916.  
Meiji Holdings' business activities now fall under Meiji Co. Ltd. and Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd. Meiji Co. Ltd. produces a variety of food products, under its confectionery, dairy, healthcare & nutritionals, and international business units. Whereas Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd manufactures pharmaceuticals in three main segments: anti-infective drugs, therapeutic drugs for neural disorders, and generic drugs. The company is active within Japan and internationally, through its overseas network of companies, which can be found throughout Asia, Europe and North America. Meiji Holdings ranks among the top 2,000 public companies in the world and has over 14,000 employees.
The company's operations in packaged food manufacturing, in particular its use of palm and soya products in the production of sweets, chocolate and ice cream, are of particular importance with respect to forest risk commodities. For example, palm oil and palm kernel oil can be found in Meiji's brands of chocolate cookies and crackers, Chococones and Chocorooms, which it markets in the United States. Similarly, palm oil and soya derivatives can be found in other products, such as Meiji's Apollo Strawberry Chocolate Candy.
Meiji Holdings is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Bright Food Group (Bright Food) is a Chinese food industry group involved in agriculture, food processing, and manufacturing, as well as retailing. It is involved in diverse business areas, but its main food businesses include packaged foods, dairy, sugar and vegetables. The group is a major player in China ranking highly in several categories, including dairy and packaged foods. It is also a global player, ranking among the top ten in the world for dairy and the top twenty for packaged foods.

Uni-President Enterprises Corp (UPEC) manufactures and distributes a range of food products through its network of 200 affiliate companies and convenience stores. The company was incorporated in 1967 in Tainan County, Taiwan. It was originally established as a rural flour factory but over the decades has grown into an international conglomerate with operations across Asia Pacific. The manufacturing of food products is one of the company's core businesses and although it has a wide range of interests, including sports teams, retail operations and pharmaceuticals, the manufacture of food and feed are the group's largest operations. Its main products include feeds, edible oils, soya sauce, meat products, instant noodles, dairy products and frozen foods, among others.
The manufacture and marketing of food and feed products are undertaken by five main groups. The Provisions Group manufactures and markets flour, fertilizer, eggs, and animal and aquatic feeds to Asian and other international markets. The Dairy and Beverage Group manufactures dairy products, teas, soft drinks, coffee and other beverages under brands such as €œPure Tea€, €œRae-Shie€ and €œLa Gauche de la Seine€.  In addition to Taiwan, the Dairy and Beverage Group operates in mainland China, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Edible oils and instant noodles are produced by the Instant Food Group, which has a 50% market share of Taiwan's instant noodle market. Instant products are also sold outside of Taiwan with products available in 30 countries across five continents. Brands include Unif, Imperial, One More Cup, Kikkoman, A-HA, Juicymart and Pure Tea. The two smallest Groups are the General Foods and Health groups. The former provides meat products, ice cream, sauces and ready meals while the Health Group manufactures bakery and health products,.
Of particular relevance is President Nisshin Corp, a member of Uni-President that supplies oils and fats, including palm oil products, to the food industry. Furthermore, palm oil is also used in other products, for example in instant noodles, and is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soya, imported from both the US and South America, is used in Uni-President's feed and edible oil products.

Their services include: commercial banking, investment banking, asset management, and advisory services. Bright Food Group (Bright Food) is a Chinese food industry group involved in agriculture, food processing, and manufacturing, as well as retailing. It is involved in diverse business areas, but its main food businesses include packaged foods, dairy, sugar and vegetables. The group is a major player in China ranking highly in several categories, including dairy and packaged foods. It is also a global player, ranking among the top ten in the world for dairy and the top twenty for packaged foods.

Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

WH Group, formerly Shuanghui International is headquartered in Hong Kong and has business operations in three segments: packaged meat, fresh pork and hog production. Its global portfolio includes Shuanghui Development, Smithfield Foods and Campofrio Food Group. The anglicised name for Shuanghui Group is Shineway Group and it holds the top market positions for canned or preserved, and chilled processed food in China and is also among the top ten globally for chilled processed foods and the top 40 for packaged food.
The Shineway Group is the largest meat processing company in China, occupying a significant share of the market and employing some 60,000 people. Shanghui/Shineway is the company's original Chinese brand; manufacturing fresh pork and retorted and pasteurised packaged meat products in more than ten product ranges (including King of Kings and Spicy Crispy Sausage) and over 200 cuts and styles of fresh and chilled meat. However, although it advertises itself as the largest pork company in the world and therefore focuses on hog slaughtering and processing, the company's operations in the beef and poultry sectors have recently expanded.
Within the United States, Smithfield Food manufactures pork products and exports them as far as China, Mexico, Russia, Japan and Canada. Brand names include Smithfield, Margherita, Farmland, Armour and Curly's, amongst others; and products include smoked and boiled hams, bacon, sausage, deli meats, hot dogs, luncheon meats, pepperoni, dry meat, and finally pre-prepared foods (supplying grocery stores and restaurants alike). Smithfield is one of the five largest chilled processed food companies in the world and supplies to brands in around 50 countries.
Finally, Campofrio Food Group, in which WH Group owns a 37% share, (the largest packaged meat company in Europe) is the European branch of WH Group's business; it operates in Spain, France, Belgium, Holland, Germany, Italy, Portugal and the US.

Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

It is headquartered in Illinois, USA and provides a range of communication services to corporate customers, enabling them disperse messages using various types of media. rows.coprofile: Seven & i is a Japanese holding company with over 60,000 stores worldwide as of 2017. Its main subsidiary is the convenience store 7-Eleven, which in 2015 ranked among the top franchises in the world. In addition to 7-Eleven, the company has subsidiaries operating in the fields of real estate, food services, financial services, manufacturing and processing. As a leading retailer with a diversified product portfolio, Seven & i Holdings is exposed to forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy, beef and paper.  Seven & I Holdings Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to leather and timber.

Natuzzi S.p.A. (Natuzzi) is the parent company of the Natuzzi Group, an Italian furniture company, established in 1959. It is involved in the design, manufacture, and marketing of furniture, and specialises in leather and upholstered products such as sofas, armchairs and other living room accessories. Cattle hides and wood are among the key raw materials used by Natuzzi in the manufacture of its products, and significantly, sales of leather-upholstered furniture comprised over 94% of the company's net sales and 85% of the company's revenue in 2013.
The group has numerous subsidiaries, registered worldwide, including in Brazil, China, Italy and elsewhere in Europe, Japan, Russia, India and Australia.
As a leader in leather upholstery and the largest furniture manufacturer overall in Italy, Natuzzi plays a key role in the international leather trade, with customs data revealing that the company imports significant volumes of leather from Brazil. Further to this, Natuzzi owns one active manufacturing facility in Brazil, which aims to increase local sourcing from 2014 onwards.
Natuzzi offers products under several brands: Natuzzi Italia; Natuzzi Editions, also known as Leather Editions; Natuzzi Re-vive; and private label. Natuzzi Editions is the group's brand focusing on the medium-high end of the market. It was developed and is sold solely in the US market and its products are manufactured in China, Brazil and Romania. The Leather Editions brand offers similar leather products to Natuzzi Editions, but is marketed in Europe and the rest of the world, apart from in North and South America. Natuzzi Re-vive, launched in 2013, sells Natuzzi branded performance recliners.  Finally, the company has developed private label products to maintain its competitiveness in the low-end market segment.
The group's furniture products are sold through a range of retail outlets worldwide, including: franchised stores, Divani & Divani by Natuzzi and Natuzzi, which are all located in Italy and Portugal; its Natuzzi Editions and Leather Editions stores; and also through several large global furniture retailers, such as IKEA, Macy's, and Nitori.

IFFCO is an international business house, established in 1975 and based in the United Arab Emirates. IFFCO manufactures and markets a range of products for the mass consumer and industrial markets; producing around 7000 products and with a portfolio of 28 flagship brands, it sells its products in 84 countries worldwide, and has over 12,000 employees and offices in 21 countries.
The group's main business segments are: Impulse Foods; Agribusiness; Oils and Fats; Packaging; and Sales and Distribution. IFFCO therefore has multiple operations of relevance to forest risk commodity supply chain. For example, it's involvement in the production of packaged food, oils and fats, and in poultry farming, makes palm oil and soya of particular significance. Its Impulse Foods division manufactures and markets a range of convenience foods, including biscuits, savoury snacks, chocolates, confectionery, and ice creams, with brands such as London Dairy, Igloo, Tom and Break. While through its Agribusiness segment, IFFCO produces a range of food products, including poultry and eggs, bakery ingredients and frozen meat. IFFCO's joint venture with Oman Flour Mill is a fully-integrated poultry operation including a feed mill, parent bird and broiler farm, hatchery and processing facility. Finally, IFFCO's Oils and Fats segment manufactures products for the consumer and industrial markets, specialising in cooking oils, culinary products, and industrial fats for the food and personal care industries.
IFFCO has a worldwide presence, through its in-country offices, 33 manufacturing facilities and 6 distribution centres. Of particular note are IFFCO (Pakistan) Private Limited, IFFCO (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, and the group's various joint ventures, which include FELDA-IFFCO. FELDA-IFFCO is a partnership with plantation giant, FELDA; the largest producer of crude palm oil in Malaysia, with plantation land banks totalling 850,000 hectares, management of 530,000 hectares of plantations and a 7% share of the production market in 2011. FELDA-IFFCO also own 15 refineries in Malaysia, China, Turkey, Pakistan, South Africa and Canada, as well as four kernel crushing plants with a processing capacity of 8.4 million tonnes per year; producing around 20% of Malaysia's total crude palm kernel oil.
 IFFCO Pakistan is a major player in the edible oils and fats market. It operates the largest edible oil refinery in the country and is the only multinational company in Pakistan's edible oils industry. It procures raw materials domestically and internationally, including from Malaysia through FELDA-IFFCO. FINALLY, IFFCO Malaysia is an integrated oleo-chemical complex operating soap noodle and finishing plants that produce a variety of soap products and animal feed supplements.

Lotte is a multinational holding company with businesses spanning food manufacture, retail, tourism, petrochemicals, construction and real estate. Headquartered in South Korea, the company’s origins are in the food industry, where it operates both production facilities and supermarkets. As a leading food manufacturer and retailer Lotte is exposed to forest risk commodities including palm oil, soy and beef.  Lotte Co. DLG Denmark, established in 1964, is one of Europe's biggest agricultural companies. It is owned by 30,000 Danish farmers and employs 7,500 people, 3,000 of whom are in Denmark. Through over 40 subsidiaries and associated companies, DLG Denmark is involved in a broad range of business and consumer sectors, with localised operations in in more than 20 countries. 
DLG Denmark is organised into four business areas: Premix and Nutrition, accounting for 4% of turnover, provides specialist animal feeds and minerals; Service and Energy, contributing 28% of turnover, provides a broad range of products and services including fuels, telecommunications and IT, and also operates DIY stores and petrol stations; Machinery, Flowers and Food, which accounts for 6% of turnover, provides industrial and agricultural machinery as well as a broad range of plants and food products, including oils and vegetables; and Farm Supply, the largest division, providing 62% turnover, encompasses animal feed production, poultry hatcheries, provision of fertiliser and pesticides, and crop production.
DLG Denmark produces compound feeds for farm animals at its mills in Europe and is one of Europe's top five largest producers of compound feeds. Soya is a significant feed production ingredient, accounting for around 15 to 20% composition. Consequently, DLG Denmark buys around half of Denmark's soymeal. DLG Denmark uses a similar amount of palm oil in its animal feed.

Lotte Co. Ltd was founded in Japan in 1948 and has since grown into a global company group of 50 companies. One of the group's major subsidiary companies is Lotte Confectionery, established in south Korea in 1967; it quickly became the country's biggest food manufacturer. Lotte Confectionary is not only the largest domestic producer of candies, biscuits, chocolates, chewing gum and ice cream, it also has operations overseas including in the US, Russia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Belgium, India and othes. Today Lotte Co. Ltd is a vast organisation, which has diverse business interests in food, retail, petrochemicals, finance and communications. Additional food related operations in Korea include businesses involved in fats and oils, bakeries, milk processing, baby food and meat processing products. Lotte Co. Ltd also has number of fast food franchise operations in South Korea with separate entities for doughnuts, cafes, hamburgers, desserts and family restaurants.
Lotte Shopping Co., Ltd. is a listed subsidiary of the company, operating department stores and discount stores. It is amongst the 20 largest grocery retailers globally. Lotte Mart is a chain of discount stores that operates more than 60 stores in Korea but has also opened stores oversea including in China, Indonesia (where it is one of the top three supermarket retailers), and Vietnam. In Korea, Lotte Co. Ltd is the leading supermarket operator and also operates a chain of 7-Eleven stores through their Korea Seven subsidiary.
Due to its involvement in processed foods, retail, and meat processing the most relevant forest risk commodities for Lotte Co. Ltd are soya, palm oil, beef, and paper & packaging. Lotte Co. Ltd is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

The Gap Inc. is a leading global apparel retailer selling apparel, accessories and personal care products for men, women and children through its various brands. Gap Inc. was established with the opening of a single Gap store in San Francisco in the United States in 1969. Since then the company has expanded greatly through the establishment of several other retail brands, including Banana Republic, Old Navy, Athleta, and Intermix.
The company has around 3,300 company-operated stores and 400 franchise stores in more than 90 countries alongside e-commerce sales operations in almost 100 countries. Its company-operated stores are located in the US, Canada, the UK, France, Ireland, Japan, China, Italy and, since 2014, Taiwan. Gap Inc. also has franchise agreements with unaffiliated franchisees to operate Gap, Old Navy and Banana Republic stores throughout Asia, Australia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Gap Inc. employs around 140,000 full and part time individuals.
The company's flagship brand, Gap, which sells casual, American style apparel, continues to be the most prominent of the group's retail brands, with over 1,430 company stores and over 340 franchises worldwide. Gap Inc.'s retail brands vary in their retailing of own-brand and other designer brands. Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy and Athleta brands each sell their own own-label products, while the Intermix brands stocks both its own-label products and those of other designers.
Gap Inc is among the top three retailers of private-label apparel and the top five of all clothing retailers globally. Each of the company's brands stock a range of leather goods, including shoes, belts and bags. For example, Intermix, which was acquired by Gap Inc in 2012, offers a range of branded luxury accessories, including leather bags. Banana Republic and Gap brands similarly stock a range of leather goods, including leather jackets for men and women, and leather handbags, belts and shoes. Gap Inc. does not directly own or operate its own manufacturing facilities, and as of 2012, its branded apparel is produced in around 923 factories in 32 countries worldwide.

Target Corporation is a general merchandise retailer operating in the US. Established in 1902 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, it is one of North America's retail giants, ranking among the top fifty in the Fortune 500. Target offers a variety of products including: food, beauty and personal care items; cleaning and paper products; as well as apparel and furniture, among other products. The company operates over 1,792 stores in the US as well as 38 distribution centres. Target began operating stores in Canada in 2011 through the acquisition of Zellers; however in 2015 the company planned to discontinue operating stores in the country.
A significant component of Target's sales are made up of its owned and exclusive branded products, which account for around one third of the company's total sales. Its owned branded products include: Archers Farms groceries; luggage; travel accessories; furniture; other goods sold under the Embark brand; Smith & Hawken outdoor furniture; Sutton & Dodge meat products; and up & up health and beauty products.

Li Ning Company Limited is a publicly owned, China-based investment holding company whose subsidiaries manufacture, distribute and sell sports shoes, clothes and equipment.  Its main market is in China, where its products are sold under its core Li-Ning brand. It also manufactures and sells sports equipment under the Double Happiness brand, badminton equipment under the Kason brand, and products under the Lotto brand, and sells outdoor sports products under French brand AIGLE. Its annual revenue is HKD 7.64bn.

Deichmann Group is a German shoe manufacturer and retailer founded in 1913 by Heinreich Deichmann. The company was established in Essen, North Rhine Westphalia, where the headquarters are still located. Currently, Deichmann Group has around 3,600 stores across 23 European countries and the USA; 1,360 stores are in Germany and over 80 in the UK. Deichmann Group is the top shoe retail company in Europe and sold around 172 million pairs of shoes worldwide in 2014. The company aims to produce fashionable shoes at affordable prices and sells shoes for men, women and children as well as accessories, including bags. The company stocks many of their own brands such as Graceland and 5th Avenue but also has collaborations with other brands, particularly in the children's sector, for example with Hello Kitty, Disney and Peppa Pig. In addition, Deichmann stores stock sports shoes from other brands, including Adidas, Fila and Pumav.
Deichmann Group began opening stores in European countries other than Germany during the early 1990s, including in the UK in 2001 and most recently in Russia in 2014. Acquisitions have also assisted brand development. In 2002, Deichmann Group bought the US chain Off Broadway Shoes, which has over 75 stores across the US, and the company has owned Rack Room Shoes since 1984. The company continues to expand its retail presence in Germany, with the planned opening of 66 new stores in the country during 2015 alongside 150 new retail branches internationally.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating producer and distributor headquartered in Michigan, USA, employing more than 110,000 people. The key subsidiary of relevance to forest risk commodities owned by Lear Corp. is Eagle Ottawa, which produces leather upholstery products for the automotive industry. Eagle Ottawa was founded in 1865 and was formerly known as Eagle Tanning Works but changed its name to Eagle Ottawa, LLC in 1916.
 
Eagle Ottawa claims to be the largest supplier of premium automotive leather and produces a variety of leather products, including finished hides, cut leather, natural shrunken grain leather, and chrome- and non-chrome-tanned leather.  As well as these, it also produces leather for other interior uses, such as for door panels and instrument panels. The company engages in various activities in leather processing including pre-tanning and tanning as well as cutting and finishing. Aside from the subsidiary's headquarters, which are in the state of Michigan, in the US, Eagle Ottawa also has facilities in Mexico, Brazil, Hungary, China, South Korea and Thailand. It also has sales and design locations in China, Japan, Brazil, Germany, England, Sweden and Italy, as well as the US. The company's customers include some of the automobile industry's biggest players, including Mercedes, BMW, Toyota, Renault Chrysler, GMC and Volkswagen.
