The Nisshin OilliO Group Ltd (Nisshin OilliO) is a Japanese company involved in the processing and manufacturing of oils and oil-based products. Established in 1907, it claims to be the largest vegetable oil company in Japan and today operates a number of companies involved in the manufacture, processing and distribution of manufactured goods, including oils, fats and chemical products. Its main business segments are: Oils and Meals; Processed Oils and Fats; Healthy Foods; Fine Chemicals; and Soya Foods and Materials. Nisshin OilliO's main oil-based products include: edible oils for household and commercial use, and food processing; margarines, shortenings, and other processed and speciality oils and fats; healthy oil products, premium oils and soya bean oil; and finally, dressings, and other healthy food products. However, its business operations also extend to a variety of other sectors, with the group also active in the insurance, marketing and restaurant industries, among others.
The Nisshin OilliO Group has four manufacturing facilities in Japan, as well as overseas subsidiaries in China, Taiwan, Malaysia, Singapore, Europe and North America. In 2005, the Group acquired Malaysian company, Intercontinental Speciality Fats Sdn. Bhd (ISF), an edible oils and fats manufacturer, supplying products for the chocolate and confectionery, bakery, dairy, and convenience food industries. ISF operates two refineries in Malaysia , where it occupies a 5% of the oil palm refinery market.

Deichmann Group is a German shoe manufacturer and retailer founded in 1913 by Heinreich Deichmann. The company was established in Essen, North Rhine Westphalia, where the headquarters are still located. Currently, Deichmann Group has around 3,600 stores across 23 European countries and the USA; 1,360 stores are in Germany and over 80 in the UK. Deichmann Group is the top shoe retail company in Europe and sold around 172 million pairs of shoes worldwide in 2014. The company aims to produce fashionable shoes at affordable prices and sells shoes for men, women and children as well as accessories, including bags. The company stocks many of their own brands such as Graceland and 5th Avenue but also has collaborations with other brands, particularly in the children's sector, for example with Hello Kitty, Disney and Peppa Pig. In addition, Deichmann stores stock sports shoes from other brands, including Adidas, Fila and Pumav.
Deichmann Group began opening stores in European countries other than Germany during the early 1990s, including in the UK in 2001 and most recently in Russia in 2014. Acquisitions have also assisted brand development. In 2002, Deichmann Group bought the US chain Off Broadway Shoes, which has over 75 stores across the US, and the company has owned Rack Room Shoes since 1984. The company continues to expand its retail presence in Germany, with the planned opening of 66 new stores in the country during 2015 alongside 150 new retail branches internationally.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating producer and distributor headquartered in Michigan, USA, employing more than 110,000 people. The key subsidiary of relevance to forest risk commodities owned by Lear Corp. is Eagle Ottawa, which produces leather upholstery products for the automotive industry. Eagle Ottawa was founded in 1865 and was formerly known as Eagle Tanning Works but changed its name to Eagle Ottawa, LLC in 1916.
 
Eagle Ottawa claims to be the largest supplier of premium automotive leather and produces a variety of leather products, including finished hides, cut leather, natural shrunken grain leather, and chrome- and non-chrome-tanned leather.  As well as these, it also produces leather for other interior uses, such as for door panels and instrument panels. The company engages in various activities in leather processing including pre-tanning and tanning as well as cutting and finishing. Aside from the subsidiary's headquarters, which are in the state of Michigan, in the US, Eagle Ottawa also has facilities in Mexico, Brazil, Hungary, China, South Korea and Thailand. It also has sales and design locations in China, Japan, Brazil, Germany, England, Sweden and Italy, as well as the US. The company's customers include some of the automobile industry's biggest players, including Mercedes, BMW, Toyota, Renault Chrysler, GMC and Volkswagen.

Li Ning Company Limited is a publicly owned, China-based investment holding company whose subsidiaries manufacture, distribute and sell sports shoes, clothes and equipment.  Its main market is in China, where its products are sold under its core Li-Ning brand. It also manufactures and sells sports equipment under the Double Happiness brand, badminton equipment under the Kason brand, and products under the Lotto brand, and sells outdoor sports products under French brand AIGLE. Its annual revenue is HKD 7.64bn.

Meiji Holdings Co. Ltd. (Meiji Holdings) is a Japanese holding company, headquartered in Tokyo, that through its subsidiaries has operations in the manufacture of dairy products, confectionery, health food and pharmaceuticals. The company, in its current holding company structure, was established in 2008; however, its origins extend back to the early 1900s, with the establishment of Meiji Sugar Co. Ltd. and Meiji Dairies Corporation in 1906, and then Meiji Co. Ltd. (a manufacturer of confectionery) in 1916.  
Meiji Holdings' business activities now fall under Meiji Co. Ltd. and Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd. Meiji Co. Ltd. produces a variety of food products, under its confectionery, dairy, healthcare & nutritionals, and international business units. Whereas Meiji Seika Pharma Co. Ltd manufactures pharmaceuticals in three main segments: anti-infective drugs, therapeutic drugs for neural disorders, and generic drugs. The company is active within Japan and internationally, through its overseas network of companies, which can be found throughout Asia, Europe and North America. Meiji Holdings ranks among the top 2,000 public companies in the world and has over 14,000 employees.
The company's operations in packaged food manufacturing, in particular its use of palm and soya products in the production of sweets, chocolate and ice cream, are of particular importance with respect to forest risk commodities. For example, palm oil and palm kernel oil can be found in Meiji's brands of chocolate cookies and crackers, Chococones and Chocorooms, which it markets in the United States. Similarly, palm oil and soya derivatives can be found in other products, such as Meiji's Apollo Strawberry Chocolate Candy.
Meiji Holdings is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Pertamina Persero PT is a state-owned Indonesian company focussing on oil, gas, renewable energy and new energy. This involves the exploration and extraction of oil and gas as well as the development of geothermal energy and coal bed methane as alternate energy sources. In addition, the company is involved in crude oil processing and the marketing, trade and shipping of oil products, gas and petrochemicals. The company is also involved in the domestic retail of gasoline and diesel and has an extensive network of over 5000 retail gas stations across Indonesia.
As per a government mandate in 2013, all diesel for industry and transportation in Indonesia must contain 10% biofuel. This has led to Pertamina Persero PT issuing a number of tenders for palm oil-based biodiesel to meet these requirements. Palm oil companies Wilmar International and Musim Mas have already won tenders to supply biodiesel to Pertamina Persero PT and more tenders are planned for the future. A total of 5.3 million kilolitres (around 4.7 million MT) of palm-based biodiesel will be procured for 2014-2015.

Yamazaki Baking Co (Yamazaki) is a Japanese group of companies involved in the manufacture and sale of baked goods and was founded in 1948. The company has four main business segments: Food, Overseas Food, Retail and Other. The food divisions manufacture a range of baked products and confectionary, whilst the retail division operates supermarkets, cafeterias and convenience stores. The full range of products manufactured includes breads, pastries, biscuits, rice balls, noodles, sandwiches, packed meals and snacks such as rice crackers and Japanese crackers. Jam, desserts, side dishes and prepared food in retort pouches are also being produced alongside both Japanese and Western-style confectionary. The Others division deals with logistics; it manages the design, supervision and construction of food manufacturing facilities, the non-life insurance agency business, as well as the manufacture and sale of cleaning agents for baking equipment.
Yamazaki is the largest baking company in Japan, the third largest packaged food company in Japan and ranks in the top 60 in the worldwide packaged food and sweet and savoury snacks categories. More importantly, it is among the top five baking companies in the world.
Yamazaki grow successfully through the implementation of high-tech equipment imported from Europe and North America in the post-war period. Over the last 60 years it has diversified its product range, including introduction of foreign foods into the Japanese market. Yamazaki claims that the development of its own licensed stores allows it to respond to changing markets and customer desires (particularly its bakeshops, which manufacture products on-site, as well as selling goods made elsewhere). The company now has 17,521 employees and 105,000 stores across Japan.

Plukon Food Group play a significant role in the European poultry market, with a weekly slaughter volume of 9 million chickens. The group also process, package and market these products for the food processing industry.

Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.
Aviva is the UK’s largest insurance provider. The company provides life insurance, general insurance and asset management products and services to individuals and small and medium-sized businesses.

Nine Dragons Paper Holdings is a Chinese company producing packaging paperboard and paper products. According to the company, it is the largest producer of containerboard in China, and in terms of production capacity the company is one of the biggest in the world. Nine Dragons Paper Holding’s operations require large amounts of pulp and paper. Nine Dragons Paper Holdings is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.

AEON is a Japanese retail group operating more than 300 subsidiaries across 13 countries. Its business includes supermarkets, convenience stores and home stores. It is one of the largest retailers of edible groceries in the Asia Pacific region, which exposes it to palm oil, soy and beef.  AEON Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging.

Swedbank Robur Fonder AB is Sweden's largest asset management firm, managing the savings of over three million people. Swedbank Robur Fonder AB aims to 'create sustainable, long-term return for their investors whilst also contributing to the development of society and the environment'. Swedbank Robur Fonder AB serves more than 4 million retail, institutional and corporate clients and currently has 166billion euros of assets under management. As of 2024, Bank Mandiri's total consolidated assets amount to more than 165 billion USD with more than 86.3 billion in loans. In the 2024 selection, Bank Mandiri was providing 7.9 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

BTG Pactual are an investment bank and asset manager headquartered in Brazil. Their services include investment banking, corporate finance, asset and wealth management, and trading services. As of 2017, BTG Pactual's total assets under management amount to more than 125 billion BRL. BTG Pactual are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

MRV Engenharia e Participaces (MRV) is a construction company in Brazil and the United States, focussed on the residential real estate market, building houses, apartment buildings and other properties. It is one of the largest Brazilian construction companies by units sold, revenue and sales value, and it operates in 160 cities and 22 states in Brazil. Timber is a major raw material for construction, and Brazil in general uses four times more tropical timber than China.  MRV Engenharia e Participacoes S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Savencia SA is a French cheese and dairy company which sends products to market in 120 countries worldwide. The company has many well-known brands including Coeur de Lion, Saint Agur, Géramont and Lucina. Through its various cheese and dairy products Savencia is exposed to the forest risk commodity palm oil and soy which is used in animal feed. Groupe Savencia S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

ORIX Corporation are a diversified financial services firm based in Japan. The corporation and its group has approximately $400 billion in AUM* through various asset management companies. In the 2022 selection, ORIX Corporation was providing 12 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
Coty is a manufacturer and distributor of beauty products based in the US, with business segments in luxury, consumer beauty and professional beauty.

Bradesco are a banking and financial services group based in Brazil serving private, commercial and institutional customers. Bradesco are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading. As of 2024 Bradesco has a total of 386 billion USD in total assets. In the 2024 selection, Bradesco was providing 11.5 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
Kasikornbank is a banking group based in Thailand. It was previously known as the Thai Farmers Bank. In the 2022 selection, Kasikornbank was providing 772 million USD to the Forest 500 companies.

JBJ Investimentos is the parent company of JBJ Agropecuári, whose line of business is in cattle raising and exporting in Brazil. JBJ Agropecuári processes 200,000 heads per year and uses 80,000 hectares of land.  JBJ Investimentos is selected as a powerbroker for beef.

Samsonite is an American manufacturer of suitcases, backpacks, handbags, wallets, laptop bags, and toiletry bags. Samsonite sells its products in more than one hundred countries in North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia. According to the company, Samsonite is the largest travel luggage company in the world. The company use leather in its products.   Samsonite International S.A. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

SIFCA Group was founded in 1964 and is a conglomerate of four companies specialising in the production of palm oil, rubber and sugar in Africa. 27% of the group's shares are held by a company jointly owned by Wilmar International and Olam International, 44% are owned by Parme Investment, MMORIV owns 21% and the remaining 8% of SIFCA Group is owned by private shareholders.
Overall, the company employs around 30,000 people in 5 countries, with oil palm representing 40% of the group's turnover. PALMCI and SANIA are the two companies in the conglomerate that take part in the oil palm supply chain. PALMCI is responsible for the management of 39,000 hectares of industrial oil palm plantations and over 130,000 hectares of village plantations. SANIA is then responsible for utilising these upstream derivatives to produce final products that are used internally and also exported overseas. Through its refineries, SANIA has a production capability of approximately 280,000 MT of refined palm oil per year. Much of that capacity is provided by the SANIA processing plant in Abidjan, which has a crude palm oil capacity of 1,500 MT per day. Furthermore, through SAPH, SIFCA is the largest producer of rubber in Africa with over 20,000 hectares of industrial plantations. SANIA produces several edible oil and margarine products and markets them under different brands, including Palme d'Or, Dora, Saint Ave and Delicia. 
At the time of writing, SIFCA Group's website pages on sustainable development are many years out of date and do not appear to specifically address the issues of deforestation or sustainable palm oil production. None of the group companies appear to be members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Frigorifico Concepción is a meat processing company in Paraguay that is involved throughout the beef supply chain, from production to processing, distribution and exporting. Though primarily dealing in beef, the company also processes cattle for leather.   Frigorifico Concepcion S A is selected as a powerbroker for beef and is also assessed for its exposure to leather.

Malayan Banking is an international banking group headquartered in Malaysia operating several banking subsidiaries. Malayan Banking is among the top lenders to Forest 500 companies,  predominantly in the agriculture and agricultural commodities sectors.

In the 2022 selection, Algemeen Burgerlijk Pensioenfonds (ABP) was providing 14.8 bilion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Ruchi Soya is a subsidiary of Ruchi Group, an Indian conglomerate with diverse business interests. Founded in 1986 as a trading company, Ruchi Soya is now a leading manufacturer and India's largest marketer of edible oils, condiments, and soya-based food. It runs 21 manufacturing facilities across India to create products for its portfolio of brands, which includes Nutrela, Mahakosh, and Sunrich. During 2013 to 2014, it had a turnover of US$4 billion. The company is a member of both the Round Table on Responsible Soy and the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil. In 2014, Ruchi Soya extracted over 3 million tonnes of soya meal and handled over 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil.

Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is one of the world's leading marketers of branded casual, active lifestyle, work, outdoor sport, athletic, children's and uniform footwear and apparel. Wolverine owns a number of well-known brands, including Merrell, Sperry Top-Sider, Hush Puppies, Saucony, Wolverine, Keds, Stride Rite, Sebago, Cushe, Chaco, Bates, HYTEST and Soft Style. The company is also the licensee of other recognised brands, including Cat, Harley-Davidson and Patagonia. The company's products are sold by leading retailers in around 200 countries and territories. Wolverine also operates 463 retail stores through leases with various third-party landlords in the US, Canada and United Kingdom.
In addition to its footwear and apparel business, Wolverine markets pigskin leather through its Wolverine Leathers subsidiary. About 98% (based on pairs) of the company's footwear products are sourced from third-party suppliers located primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Until recently the rest came from company-owned sources in the US and the Dominican Republic but the latter was recently closed.
In October 2012, Wolverine acquired Collective Brands Inc. via a consortium that also includes Golden Gate Capital and Blum Capital Partners. Collective Brands is in itself a major player in the footwear industry (owning the Payless brand, amongst others); it is a very large footwear retailer with more than 4,400 stores in over 30 countries.

Uni-President Enterprises Corp (UPEC) manufactures and distributes a range of food products through its network of 200 affiliate companies and convenience stores. The company was incorporated in 1967 in Tainan County, Taiwan. It was originally established as a rural flour factory but over the decades has grown into an international conglomerate with operations across Asia Pacific. The manufacturing of food products is one of the company's core businesses and although it has a wide range of interests, including sports teams, retail operations and pharmaceuticals, the manufacture of food and feed are the group's largest operations. Its main products include feeds, edible oils, soya sauce, meat products, instant noodles, dairy products and frozen foods, among others.
The manufacture and marketing of food and feed products are undertaken by five main groups. The Provisions Group manufactures and markets flour, fertilizer, eggs, and animal and aquatic feeds to Asian and other international markets. The Dairy and Beverage Group manufactures dairy products, teas, soft drinks, coffee and other beverages under brands such as €œPure Tea€, €œRae-Shie€ and €œLa Gauche de la Seine€.  In addition to Taiwan, the Dairy and Beverage Group operates in mainland China, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Edible oils and instant noodles are produced by the Instant Food Group, which has a 50% market share of Taiwan's instant noodle market. Instant products are also sold outside of Taiwan with products available in 30 countries across five continents. Brands include Unif, Imperial, One More Cup, Kikkoman, A-HA, Juicymart and Pure Tea. The two smallest Groups are the General Foods and Health groups. The former provides meat products, ice cream, sauces and ready meals while the Health Group manufactures bakery and health products,.
Of particular relevance is President Nisshin Corp, a member of Uni-President that supplies oils and fats, including palm oil products, to the food industry. Furthermore, palm oil is also used in other products, for example in instant noodles, and is sourced from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soya, imported from both the US and South America, is used in Uni-President's feed and edible oil products.

Compañía Bernal SA is one of the largest beef processing companies in Argentina. Their own brand beef product "Finexcor" sells within supermarkets across Latin America, whilst other frozen beef products export out internationally through company owned distribution networks.

Nine Dragons Paper Holdings Ltd (ND Paper) is a paper and paper packaging manufacturer that produces a variety of containerboard and paper products, including: linerboard; corrugating medium and coated duplex board; recycled printing and writing paper; and tissue paper. As well as paper products, ND Paper manufactures wood-, bamboo-, and unbleached kraft pulp. The company's products are manufactured under three brands: Nine Dragons, Land Dragon and Sea Dragon, each focusing on a different customer segment.  ND Paper is well known for its use of recovered paper; the company's main source of raw material. This is used in the manufacturing of some of its products, such as its testlinerboard, made from 100% recovered paper, and its Sea Dragon office paper. The company imports significant amounts of recovered paper from the US; however, this is not used exclusively in all products.
The company was established in 1995 and is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies, ranking among the top 30 globally and holding the leading position in China. ND Paper has six manufacturing bases across China, as well as in Vietnam and Mongolia, through joint ventures: Cheng Yang Paper and Nine Dragons Xing An Pulp & Paper (Inner Mongolia) Co Ltd. Originally, the company predominantly supplied packaging for manufacturers in southern China's export oriented industry; however, the business has increasingly tapped into the demand for packaging products from the domestic market as China's own consumer-demand has grown.

The earliest foundations of the Oetker-Gruppe lie in 1891, when Dr August Oetker developed the baking powder, Backin, in Germany. The Oetker-Gruppe now employs over 27,000 people and has a turnover of approximately 11 billion euros. The company operates in a number of different sectors and are split into six divisions: food; beer and non-alcoholic beverages; wine and spirits; shipping; banking; and a further division responsible for the production of phosphate-based products, management of four hotels and also publishing. The food division currently has annual sales of 2.6 billion euros from 350 products marketed in Germany and approximately 3,500 products internationally. Six plants in Germany manufacture the group's products but they also operate manufacturing plants across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. The Oetker-Gruppe sells its products to the consumer market under the brand, Dr Oetker. Its consumer products include; frozen pizzas, ready desserts and a number of other chilled and frozen products. Through the Martin Braun group, the Oetker-Gruppe sells a number of baking agents, glazes and decorations to baking and confectionary companies. The manufacturing of these products meant that the Oetker-Gruppe used 4,777 tonnes of palm oil or palm oil derivatives in 2013. Toyo Suisan Kaisha Ltd (Toyo) is an international food producer specialising in ramen noodles and seafood. Toyo manufactures its products through various sub-divisions, such as the Domestic Instant Noodles segment and the Frozen and Refrigerated Foods segment. In addition to noodles, it also produces wontons, soup products, fish, ham, sausages and seasonings. It also has a Prepared Food section which manufactures sterile packaged rice, retort rice, soup and other products.
The company was founded in 1953, has its headquarters in Tokyo, and employs around 4,600 people. Its main overseas operations are in Mexico and the Us through its Overseas Instant Noodles Division, which sells noodles under the brand name Maruchan Inc. As of 2008, Toyo owns three food processing facilities in the US and has 32 subsidiaries.
By the 1970s, Toyo had become well-known in Japan and had branched out internationally. It is now the largest noodle company in the US, the second largest in Japan and third largest in the world. It is also in the top five companies in Japan for dried processed food and chilled processed food, and in the top 30 largest soup companies worldwide.
The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm oil and in 2013 was implicated by the Rainforest Action Network to be one of the 'Snack Food 20' responsible for using 'conflict' palm oil from unsustainable sources,.

Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.

Groupe Blattner Elwyn is a conglomerate based in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), active in a variety of sectors, including agribusiness, logistics and distribution, and timber processing . Agriculture is at the core of Groupe Blattner Elwyn's operations and the group's agribusiness activities are in the production and processing of rubber, palm oil and cocoa. The Group's industrial operations are in: The production of crown corks and metal cans; timber processing and harvesting; and in the production of laminated table-tops, through a company based in France. Finally, Groupe Blattner Elwyn has a variety of distribution and services companies, which include medical operations, chemical production, the automotive industry, and importing and exporting activities.
Groupe Blattner Elwyn has six subsidiaries involved in the cultivation and processing of palm oil managing some 28,311 hectares of land, 17,196 of which are currently in production. The group operates six oil palm factories and provides employment for around 10,000 permanent and temporary workers and sharecroppers.
Regarding the group's timber operations, Groupe Blattner Elwyn acquired SIFORCO from Danzer Group in February 2012. This acquisition was Groupe Blattner Elwyn's first step into the forestry sector, which the Group views as an investment in the growing timber industry in the DRC. SIFORCO, which was established in 1972, manages an area of over 1.9 million hectares in the DRC, making it one of the largest logging companies in the country in terms of forest area. SIFORCO has 600 employees and the majority of its concessions are located in the Equateur and Orientale provinces. The company harvests its natural forests for the production of logs and also has timber processing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer, and a joiner's workshop. It harvests and processes timber mainly for the European and American markets.

Want Want is a Chinese investment holding company with subsidiaries engaged in the manufacture and distribution of packaged food products, including rice crackers, dairy goods, confectionary items and other snacks. The company primarily serves the domestic market in China, but also exports its products to locations such as the United States and Canada. As a leading producer of packaged food products, Want Want is exposed to the forest risk commodities palm oil and soy which are commonly used ingredients in this sector.   Want Want is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Formed in 2017 from the merger between Janus Capital Group and Henderson Global Investors, Janus Henderson Group plc are an asset manager headquartered in the UK serving private and institutional clients. Their services include trusts, investment funds, equities, fixed income, and multi-asset investments. As of 2017, Janus Henderson Group plc has over 360 billion USD in assets under management. They are among the top 40 shareholders for Forest 500 companies with over 10 billion USD worth of shares.

WH Group, formerly Shuanghui International is headquartered in Hong Kong and has business operations in three segments: packaged meat, fresh pork and hog production. Its global portfolio includes Shuanghui Development, Smithfield Foods and Campofrio Food Group. The anglicised name for Shuanghui Group is Shineway Group and it holds the top market positions for canned or preserved, and chilled processed food in China and is also among the top ten globally for chilled processed foods and the top 40 for packaged food.
The Shineway Group is the largest meat processing company in China, occupying a significant share of the market and employing some 60,000 people. Shanghui/Shineway is the company's original Chinese brand; manufacturing fresh pork and retorted and pasteurised packaged meat products in more than ten product ranges (including King of Kings and Spicy Crispy Sausage) and over 200 cuts and styles of fresh and chilled meat. However, although it advertises itself as the largest pork company in the world and therefore focuses on hog slaughtering and processing, the company's operations in the beef and poultry sectors have recently expanded.
Within the United States, Smithfield Food manufactures pork products and exports them as far as China, Mexico, Russia, Japan and Canada. Brand names include Smithfield, Margherita, Farmland, Armour and Curly's, amongst others; and products include smoked and boiled hams, bacon, sausage, deli meats, hot dogs, luncheon meats, pepperoni, dry meat, and finally pre-prepared foods (supplying grocery stores and restaurants alike). Smithfield is one of the five largest chilled processed food companies in the world and supplies to brands in around 50 countries.
Finally, Campofrio Food Group, in which WH Group owns a 37% share, (the largest packaged meat company in Europe) is the European branch of WH Group's business; it operates in Spain, France, Belgium, Holland, Germany, Italy, Portugal and the US.
initiatives: Listed on CDP, but no Forests reports. Climate report forthcoming. Campofrio also listed on CDP - but again no response. Smithfield Foods listed on CDP with 2014 Forests report, but no volumes of products. Not listed on RSPO. No other info on website.

rows.coprofile: The Wendy's Company (Wendy's) is the third largest quick service hamburger company in the world, with around 6,500 restaurants in the US and 29 other countries and US territories worldwide. Wendy's restaurants specialise in hamburgers and sandwiches but also offer fries, salads and desserts. The majority of the company's restaurants are in North America; in 2014, 6,112 restaurants operated in the US and Canada, with the majority run by franchises. The Wendy's Company has a joint venture with Restaurant Brands International covering around 100 restaurants in Canada. Outside of North America, there are 403 franchised restaurants in other countries and territories. In addition to beef and paper Wendy's uses soya (used in a range of spreads, dressings and baked products) and palm oil (used in snacks and desserts).

Cyrela Brazil Realty is a Brazilian property development company in the residential, commercial and corporate segments focused on high-end and luxury residential and commercial properties and mid-tier residences. Cyrela Brazil Realty is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Skechers USA is a company that manufactures and markets footwear, which is sold in both company-owned retail stores as well as through other retail channels. The company has two categories of footwear, lifestyle and performance, which are available in 180 countries around the world. Skechers is one of the top footwear companies in the world by brand share, as such it is exposed to the forest risk commodity leather. Skechers USA Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Granol is a Brazilian agribusiness company operating solely in Brazil that processes and refines agricultural products. The company is a major processor of soy and is also involved in the production of biodiesel. Granol is among the largest exporters of soy from Brazil.  Granol is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Inspire Brands, Inc. is an American holding company and the owner and franchisor of the Arby's, Buffalo Wild Wings, Sonic Drive-In, Jimmy John's, Rusty Taco, Mister Donut, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins restaurant chains. Dunkin’ Donuts has more than 11,500 restaurants in 40 countries worldwide and offers coffee and baked goods including doughnuts and bagels. Baskin-Robbins has more than 7,000 shops in nearly 50 countries offering ice-cream and beverages. Arby's has more than 3,300 fast food restaurants in the USA, offering sandwiches with a focus on roast beef. The diverse group of restaurants expose the group to several forest risk commodities. Inspire Brands is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging, and is also assessed for beef..

Li Ning Company is a Chinese holding company with subsidiaries involved in the manufacture, distribution and sale of sports shoes, clothes and equipment.  Its main market is in China, where its products are sold under the Li-Ning brand. It also markets products under other well-known brands including Double Happiness, Kason, Lotto and AIGLE. As a leading footwear and luggage manufacturer Li Ning is exposed to the forest risk commodity leather.  Li Ning Company Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

Samko Timber Ltd is a forest products company listed in Singapore and based in Indonesia. It produces a variety of timber products, including plywood, decking, doors, window frames, piano parts, laminated veneer lumber, laminated veneer board, and truck body parts. One of the largest and well established logging and plywood companies in Indonesia, the company was founded in 1978 and has since become a major player in the processed timber products industry in Indonesia; it also claims to be among the top five tropical hardwood producers in the world.
Samko Timber Ltd has numerous subsidiaries, with the majority of its operations in Indonesia. For example, Bioforest Pte Ltd is based in Singapore but its 99.9% owned subsidiary, PT Bioforest Indonesia is based and operates in Indonesia. Similarly, Samko Trading Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, has operations through its 100% owned subsidiaries in Indonesia and Malaysia (Samkowood Product Sdn Bhd). On top of its activities in Southeast Asia, Samko Timber Ltd has established a joint venture in the US under Samko USA LLC, to market its products in North America. 
Within Indonesia, the company has procurement, processing, manufacturing and distribution operations. Specifically, Samko Timber Ltd has five processing units in Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi; ten veneer plants in Java and Sumatra; a 9,400 hectare industrial tree plantation in Jambi, Sumatra; and through its associate company, in Kalimantan it has 4 forest plantations of 125,000 hectares and four natural forest logging concessions covering a total of 450,000 hectares.

Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.
initiatives: UN Global Compact, Consumer Goods Forum

rows.coprofile: Daiwa Securities is a holding company headquartered in Japan. The Group provides financial services which includes dealing, brokerage, underwriting, the distribution of securities and asset management. As of 2022, Daiwa Securities have over 28 trillion JPY in total assets.

Japan based Seven & I Holdings Co Ltd (Seven & I Holdings) is a holding company that established from the merger of Ito-Yokado Co, Seven Eleven Japan Co, and Denny's Japan. Through its subsidiaries, Seven & I Holdings operates convenience stores, food supermarkets, department stores, general merchandise stores, food services, financial services and IT services.
As of 2014, there were around 56,000 Seven & I Holdings stores in 16 different countries in Asia, Scandinavia, the Americas and Australia, serving, on average, 58 million customers per day, 20.5 million of which were in Japan. The bulk of the portfolio is made up of over 56,600 7-Eleven convenience stores, the world's largest franchise chain store. In addition to the 7-Eleven banner Seven & I Holdings operate Sogo & Seibu department stores; several hundred food supermarkets under the York Mart and York-Benimaru banners; superstores predominantly using the Ito Yokado banner; a number of speciality stores; and restaurants, including around 470 Denny's restaurants in Japan. Seven & I Holdings also have a number of consumer financial services subsidiaries. Within the food sector, Seven & I subsidiaries have a number of own or private brand labels including 7-Select, Seven Premium and Seven Gold; these brands include meat products, baked goods, desserts and confectionary.

The Brazilian facility alone has an annual production capacity of 7 million square metres of leather from bovine hide.  Gruppo Mastrotto Spa is selected as a powerbroker for leather.

Cencosud is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to leather and timber.

Their services include corporate finance, pensions, international trading and retail banking services. As of 2021, BNI have over 964 trillion IDR in assets under management. Ting Hsin is a Taiwanese based company that is predominantly active in the production and distribution of food and beverage products. Products include instant noodles, baked goods, and soft drinks, and its Master Kong brand is well-known in China. Alongside its manufacturing, the company also has an extensive sales network in China with more than 100,000 retail outlets as of 2013, as well as distributing products globally. Ting Hsin isone of the five largest packaged food companies in China, and as a leading manufacturer of packaged food products Ting Hsin is exposed to palm oil and soy. Toyo Suisan Kaisha Ltd (Toyo) is an international food producer specialising in ramen noodles and seafood. Toyo manufactures its products through various sub-divisions, such as the Domestic Instant Noodles segment and the Frozen and Refrigerated Foods segment. In addition to noodles, it also produces wontons, soup products, fish, ham, sausages and seasonings. It also has a Prepared Food section which manufactures sterile packaged rice, retort rice, soup and other products.
The company was founded in 1953, has its headquarters in Tokyo, and employs around 4,600 people. Its main overseas operations are in Mexico and the Us through its Overseas Instant Noodles Division, which sells noodles under the brand name Maruchan Inc. As of 2008, Toyo owns three food processing facilities in the US and has 32 subsidiaries.
By the 1970s, Toyo had become well-known in Japan and had branched out internationally. It is now the largest noodle company in the US, the second largest in Japan and third largest in the world. It is also in the top five companies in Japan for dried processed food and chilled processed food, and in the top 30 largest soup companies worldwide.
The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm oil and in 2013 was implicated by the Rainforest Action Network to be one of the 'Snack Food 20' responsible for using 'conflict' palm oil from unsustainable sources,.

BMO Financial Group are a financial services provider headquartered in Canada, they are the 8th largest bank in North America by assets, serving private and corporate clients, institutions, and governments. Their services include personal, commercial and investment banking, loans and mortgages, insurance, wealth management, corporate lending, bonds, equities, fixed income investing, research, risk management, and treasury and advisory services. As of 2022, BMO Financial Group have over 1,000 billion USD in total assets. They are also among the top shareholders for Forest 500 companies. In the 2022 selection, BMO Financial Group was providing 29 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Groupe Blattner Elwyn is a conglomerate based in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), active in a variety of sectors, including agribusiness, logistics and distribution, and timber processing . Agriculture is at the core of Groupe Blattner Elwyn's operations and the group's agribusiness activities are in the production and processing of rubber, palm oil and cocoa. The Group's industrial operations are in: The production of crown corks and metal cans; timber processing and harvesting; and in the production of laminated table-tops, through a company based in France. Finally, Groupe Blattner Elwyn has a variety of distribution and services companies, which include medical operations, chemical production, the automotive industry, and importing and exporting activities.
Groupe Blattner Elwyn has six subsidiaries involved in the cultivation and processing of palm oil managing some 28,311 hectares of land, 17,196 of which are currently in production. The group operates six oil palm factories and provides employment for around 10,000 permanent and temporary workers and sharecroppers.
Regarding the group's timber operations, Groupe Blattner Elwyn acquired SIFORCO from Danzer Group in February 2012. This acquisition was Groupe Blattner Elwyn's first step into the forestry sector, which the Group views as an investment in the growing timber industry in the DRC. SIFORCO, which was established in 1972, manages an area of over 1.9 million hectares in the DRC, making it one of the largest logging companies in the country in terms of forest area. SIFORCO has 600 employees and the majority of its concessions are located in the Equateur and Orientale provinces. The company harvests its natural forests for the production of logs and also has timber processing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer, and a joiner's workshop. It harvests and processes timber mainly for the European and American markets.

The group is one of the top leather and footwear retailers in Europe and globally.  Deichmann Group is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

It is a major player in the Argentinian soy market with a significant market share in  soy crushing. Vicentin is also one of the largest exporters of soy from Argentina and among the top 10 sourcers from Paraguay. Additionally, the company is involved in biodiesel production with a daily production of 500 tons and has a feed lot holding 20,000 heads of cattle.  Vicentin S.A.I.C. is selected as a powerbroker for soy and is also assessed for its exposure to beef.

Established in 1968, NICE Group is the largest soap and detergent manufacturer in China; it also produces dishwasher soap and toothpaste. It's best known brand is the detergent, DIAO; further brands include Supra, Soling, 100 Years Hare Care and Lizi. Since 1994, the group's sales of laundry powder, soap and liquid detergent have been number one in China; and in 2005, NICE Group ranked in the top 8 worldwide. Each year the company produces 1 million tonnes of washing powder, 540,000 tonnes of liquid detergent, 280,000 tonnes of soap bars, 20,000 tonnes of industrial glycerine and 400 million tubes of toothpaste.  The Group has over 10,000 employees, operates 10 brands, and has more than 50 sales branches and 3 overseas subsidiaries. The Group's products are sold in China, the Middle East, Africa, Oceania, Europe and the US.

Voya Financial are a financial services company headquartered in the US with a focus on retirement. Offerings include retirement plants, annuities, investment management, life insurance and workplace benefits schemes. As of June 2017, Voya Financial's total assets amount to more than 510 billion USD with more than 300 billion USD in assets under management. Voya Financial are among the top 15 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 2 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 100 with shares worth more than 3 billion USD.

Kikkoman Corporation (Kikkoman) is a holding company concerned with the manufacture of food, mainly soy sauce and alcohols. It is a Japanese company and was founded in 1917, though its website claims its soy sauce manufacturing history dates back a further 200 years. Aside from soy sauce, the company also produces related seasonings and drinks (mainly alcoholic); it also produces enzymes and other biochemical products. There are 67 companies in the group and it has a total of 5,622 employees.
There are four segments to the business. The domestic food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce and soya related seasonings, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, as well as cans, soya milk drinks and health food products. The domestic 'other products' segment includes drugs, chemicals, real estate, logistic and indirect services. The overseas food manufacturing and sale segment provides soy sauce, processed tomato products under the Del Monte brand, cans, soya milk drinks and health food products, in overseas markets. Finally, the overseas food wholesales segment purchases and sells oriental food products.
Outside of Japan, Kikkoman produces soy sauce in the US, Europe, Singapore and Taiwan. It is the largest sauce, dressings and condiments company in Japan, the second largest in Hong Kong for canned and preserved food, and one of the top ten largest sauce, dressings and condiments manufacturers in the World.

Pertamina Persero PT is a state-owned Indonesian company focussing on oil, gas, renewable energy and new energy. This involves the exploration and extraction of oil and gas as well as the development of geothermal energy and coal bed methane as alternate energy sources. In addition, the company is involved in crude oil processing and the marketing, trade and shipping of oil products, gas and petrochemicals. The company is also involved in the domestic retail of gasoline and diesel and has an extensive network of over 5000 retail gas stations across Indonesia.
As per a government mandate in 2013, all diesel for industry and transportation in Indonesia must contain 10% biofuel. This has led to Pertamina Persero PT issuing a number of tenders for palm oil-based biodiesel to meet these requirements. Palm oil companies Wilmar International and Musim Mas have already won tenders to supply biodiesel to Pertamina Persero PT and more tenders are planned for the future. A total of 5.3 million kilolitres (around 4.7 million MT) of palm-based biodiesel will be procured for 2014-2015.

Yamazaki Baking Co (Yamazaki) is a Japanese group of companies involved in the manufacture and sale of baked goods and was founded in 1948. The company has four main business segments: Food, Overseas Food, Retail and Other. The food divisions manufacture a range of baked products and confectionary, whilst the retail division operates supermarkets, cafeterias and convenience stores. The full range of products manufactured includes breads, pastries, biscuits, rice balls, noodles, sandwiches, packed meals and snacks such as rice crackers and Japanese crackers. Jam, desserts, side dishes and prepared food in retort pouches are also being produced alongside both Japanese and Western-style confectionary. The Others division deals with logistics; it manages the design, supervision and construction of food manufacturing facilities, the non-life insurance agency business, as well as the manufacture and sale of cleaning agents for baking equipment.
Yamazaki is the largest baking company in Japan, the third largest packaged food company in Japan and ranks in the top 60 in the worldwide packaged food and sweet and savoury snacks categories. More importantly, it is among the top five baking companies in the world.
Yamazaki grow successfully through the implementation of high-tech equipment imported from Europe and North America in the post-war period. Over the last 60 years it has diversified its product range, including introduction of foreign foods into the Japanese market. Yamazaki claims that the development of its own licensed stores allows it to respond to changing markets and customer desires (particularly its bakeshops, which manufacture products on-site, as well as selling goods made elsewhere). The company now has 17,521 employees and 105,000 stores across Japan.

Established in 1968, NICE Group is the largest soap and detergent manufacturer in China; it also produces dishwasher soap and toothpaste. It's best known brand is the detergent, DIAO; further brands include Supra, Soling, 100 Years Hare Care and Lizi. Since 1994, the group's sales of laundry powder, soap and liquid detergent have been number one in China; and in 2005, NICE Group ranked in the top 8 worldwide. Each year the company produces 1 million tonnes of washing powder, 540,000 tonnes of liquid detergent, 280,000 tonnes of soap bars, 20,000 tonnes of industrial glycerine and 400 million tubes of toothpaste.  The Group has over 10,000 employees, operates 10 brands, and has more than 50 sales branches and 3 overseas subsidiaries. The Group's products are sold in China, the Middle East, Africa, Oceania, Europe and the US.

The Japan Agricultural Cooperatives Group (JA Group) is an agricultural cooperative, established to support its members by selling their products rather than each of its members selling products independently. On top of this, JA Group provides its members with production materials and agrochemicals. The group is a politically powerful organisation and is comprised of almost ten million regular and associate members. 
The JA Group is made up of several constituent parts, including ZEN-NOH, which is the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations. ZEN-NOH manages the business and distribution operations of the JA Group and is responsible for the marketing and supply business side of the group. Of particular relevance, are ZEN-NOH's operations in the animal feed sector. Of the total 24 to 25 million tonnes of compound feed used per year in Japan, ZEN-NOH handles around 30%, making ZEN-NOH Japan's largest compound feed producer and one of the top ten in the world. Through its subsidiaries, ZEN-NOH imports large volumes of soya from overseas producers including Brazil, India and China for use in compound animal feeds.
Also of relevance, is the group's Daily Necessities business unit, through which ZEN-NOH and JA run around 800 A-Coop supermarkets. The stores sell clothing, food products and consumer durables, and prioritise goods produced by members and sell A-Coop branded goods. Currently there are around 1,300 A-Coop branded goods, which include packaged food and clothing.

United Overseas Bank (UOB) are banking group headquartered in Singapore serving both private and commercial customers. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, capital markets, insurance, asset management, pensions, venture capital, and retail banking services. As of 2017, UOB's total assets amount to more than 340 billion SGD, with more than 220 billion SGD of net customer loans. UOB are one of the top 60 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 3 billion USD worth of loans to companies predominantly in the agriculture, agricultural commodities, food retail and animal feed sectors.

Legg Mason are an international asset management company headquartered in the US serving individual and institutional clients. Their services cover mutual and close-end funds, ETFs, saving plans and collective investment funds. As of 2017, their total assets under management amount to over £750 billion. Legg Mason are in top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 1.6 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also among the top 60 shareholders for Forest 500 companies with over 6 billion USD worth of shares.

SIFCA Group was founded in 1964 and is a conglomerate of four companies specialising in the production of palm oil, rubber and sugar in Africa. 27% of the group's shares are held by a company jointly owned by Wilmar International and Olam International, 44% are owned by Parme Investment, MMORIV owns 21% and the remaining 8% of SIFCA Group is owned by private shareholders.
Overall, the company employs around 30,000 people in 5 countries, with oil palm representing 40% of the group's turnover. PALMCI and SANIA are the two companies in the conglomerate that take part in the oil palm supply chain. PALMCI is responsible for the management of 39,000 hectares of industrial oil palm plantations and over 130,000 hectares of village plantations. SANIA is then responsible for utilising these upstream derivatives to produce final products that are used internally and also exported overseas. Through its refineries, SANIA has a production capability of approximately 280,000 MT of refined palm oil per year. Much of that capacity is provided by the SANIA processing plant in Abidjan, which has a crude palm oil capacity of 1,500 MT per day. Furthermore, through SAPH, SIFCA is the largest producer of rubber in Africa with over 20,000 hectares of industrial plantations. SANIA produces several edible oil and margarine products and markets them under different brands, including Palme d'Or, Dora, Saint Ave and Delicia. 
At the time of writing, SIFCA Group's website pages on sustainable development are many years out of date and do not appear to specifically address the issues of deforestation or sustainable palm oil production. None of the group companies appear to be members of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Lotte Co. Ltd was founded in Japan in 1948 and has since grown into a global company group of 50 companies. One of the group's major subsidiary companies is Lotte Confectionery, established in south Korea in 1967; it quickly became the country's biggest food manufacturer. Lotte Confectionary is not only the largest domestic producer of candies, biscuits, chocolates, chewing gum and ice cream, it also has operations overseas including in the US, Russia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Belgium, India and othes. Today Lotte Co. Ltd is a vast organisation, which has diverse business interests in food, retail, petrochemicals, finance and communications. Additional food related operations in Korea include businesses involved in fats and oils, bakeries, milk processing, baby food and meat processing products. Lotte Co. Ltd also has number of fast food franchise operations in South Korea with separate entities for doughnuts, cafes, hamburgers, desserts and family restaurants.
Lotte Shopping Co., Ltd. is a listed subsidiary of the company, operating department stores and discount stores. It is amongst the 20 largest grocery retailers globally. Lotte Mart is a chain of discount stores that operates more than 60 stores in Korea but has also opened stores oversea including in China, Indonesia (where it is one of the top three supermarket retailers), and Vietnam. In Korea, Lotte Co. Ltd is the leading supermarket operator and also operates a chain of 7-Eleven stores through their Korea Seven subsidiary.
Due to its involvement in processed foods, retail, and meat processing the most relevant forest risk commodities for Lotte Co. Ltd are soya, palm oil, beef, and paper & packaging. Lotte Co. Ltd is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

MetLife are a financial services provider headquartered in the US with offerings for private and commercial clients. Their services include various forms of insurance, corporate retirement and benefit solutions, and institutional investments. As of 2017, MetLife's total assets amount to more than 925 billion USD, with more than 360 billion USD in various forms of securities. MetLife are one of the top 10 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 2.5 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Thomson Reuters is a worldwide printing and publishing company, both online and in print, and headquartered in Canada.

The Htoo Group of Companies is one of Myanmar's largest and most influential conglomerates. The group has more than fourteen subsidiaries engaged in a variety of operations. Its extensive influence is shown through the diversity of its business activities, which include ventures in the airline industry (Air Bagan); banking (AGD Bank); the tourism industry through its luxury resorts and hotels; mining; logistics; construction; agriculture; trading; radio (FM Bagan); and petroleum (Htoo Petrol), amongst others. Air Bagan was the country's first private airline, launched in 2004, and Htoo Group of Companies has since added to its portfolio in the air travel industry, through the establishment of Asian Wings Airways.
The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

rows.coname: Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co Ltd.
rows.coprofile:
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacture of a variety of paper products, including art paper, liquid packaging board, paying card, newsprint and copier paper. On top of its principal activities, making and selling paper products, the company also provides electricity, chemicals for paper manufacturing and construction materials. For example, through its subsidiaries Shandong Chenming Panels Co Ltd and Shouguang Chenming Floor Board Co Ltd, the company manufactures engineered wood products, including high-density fibreboard and wood flooring.
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd has manufacturing facilities located throughout China and distributes its products both domestically and to the international market, with overseas sales offices worldwide; in Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Brazil, and in Europe, India and Africa.  It is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies globally, ranking among the top 50, and as the second largest in China. The company produces around four million tonnes of paper products annually and until 2012 relied mostly on purchased chips and recovered fibre as the raw materials for its products. The company has since become increasingly integrated, developing a production base of plantation forests in China.

Allstate are a US-based insurance company that offers a variety of insurance solutions. Their services include insurance, financial planning, annuities and investments. As of 2017, Allstate's total assets amount to more than 110 billion USD, with more than 60 billion USD in securities. They are one of the top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 1.5 billion USD worth of bonds for companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

The Godrej Group is an Indian conglomerate which, through its subsidiaries, operates in the consumer goods, real estate management, industrial engineering, furniture, appliances, security services, and agricultural products sectors. Established by Ardeshir Godrej in 1897, the Godrej family retain ownership of the group, although its subsidiaries Godrej Industries and Godrej Properties are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The company operates in 28 countries, with around three quarters of its business conducted in India where it is estimated that 500 million people use a Godrej product or service every day. In 2014, the group employed 28,000 people.
The Godrej Group is involved in palm oil through its subsidiaries at multiple stages within the supply chain. Godrej Industries, a holding company within the Godrej Group, is involved in a range of activities and sectors including the manufacture and marketing of oleo-chemicals as well as their precursors and derivatives, edible oils and bakery fats. Godrej International Limited, a subsidiary of Godrej Industries, trades vegetable oils such as palm oil internationally. Godrej Agrovet Ltd is an agribusiness subsidiary of Godrej Industries; it is India's largest animal feed manufacturer, producing over a million tons a year, and is also involved in palm oil production with 51,000 hectares of smallholder cultivation in India, four mills and a total land bank of 235,000 hectares. Finally, Godrej Consumer Products Ltd, the largest Indian personal care company, uses palm oil in its soaps. It is the largest Grade 1 quality soap and second largest toilet soap provider in India with brands such as Cinthol and No.1, and is currently seeking to increase its market share in Africa, Asia and Latin America.

Macquarie Group are a financial services group headquartered in Australia serving institutional, corporate, government and retail clients. Their services cover: asset management, asset and corporate finance, banking, advisory services and global, commodity, and capital markets. As of 2017, their total assets amount to over 180 billion AUD with over 470 billion AUD of assets under management. Macquarie Group are among the top 10 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with over 3 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors . They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 80 with shares worth more than 4 billion USD.

Swedbank AB is a Swedish multinational banking group. Swedbank offers services including retail banking and asset management. In the 2024 selection, Swedbank was providing 15.8 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Cyrela Brazil Realty is a Brazilian property development company in the residential, commercial and corporate segments focused on high-end and luxury residential and commercial properties and mid-tier residences. Cyrela Brazil Realty is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Cencosud is a Chilean retail conglomerate with operations throughout Latin America. Its sales outlets include supermarkets, home improvement stores, shopping centres and department stores. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities.  Cencosud is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy, beef and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to leather and timber.

Inspire Brands, Inc. is an American holding company and the owner and franchisor of the Arby's, Buffalo Wild Wings, Sonic Drive-In, Jimmy John's, Rusty Taco, Mister Donut, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins restaurant chains. Dunkin’ Donuts has more than 11,500 restaurants in 40 countries worldwide and offers coffee and baked goods including doughnuts and bagels. Baskin-Robbins has more than 7,000 shops in nearly 50 countries offering ice-cream and beverages. Arby's has more than 3,300 fast food restaurants in the USA, offering sandwiches with a focus on roast beef. The diverse group of restaurants expose the group to several forest risk commodities. Inspire Brands is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging, and is also assessed for beef..

Wolverine World Wide Inc (Wolverine) is one of the world's leading marketers of branded casual, active lifestyle, work, outdoor sport, athletic, children's and uniform footwear and apparel. Wolverine owns a number of well-known brands, including Merrell, Sperry Top-Sider, Hush Puppies, Saucony, Wolverine, Keds, Stride Rite, Sebago, Cushe, Chaco, Bates, HYTEST and Soft Style. The company is also the licensee of other recognised brands, including Cat, Harley-Davidson and Patagonia. The company's products are sold by leading retailers in around 200 countries and territories. Wolverine also operates 463 retail stores through leases with various third-party landlords in the US, Canada and United Kingdom.
In addition to its footwear and apparel business, Wolverine markets pigskin leather through its Wolverine Leathers subsidiary. About 98% (based on pairs) of the company's footwear products are sourced from third-party suppliers located primarily in the Asia Pacific region. Until recently the rest came from company-owned sources in the US and the Dominican Republic but the latter was recently closed.
In October 2012, Wolverine acquired Collective Brands Inc. via a consortium that also includes Golden Gate Capital and Blum Capital Partners. Collective Brands is in itself a major player in the footwear industry (owning the Payless brand, amongst others); it is a very large footwear retailer with more than 4,400 stores in over 30 countries.

Gruppo Mastrotto is an Italian based processor and manufacturer of leather for use in products such as footwear, upholstery and other leather goods. Most the group’s operations are in Italy, making it a major importer of leather, and it also has operations in Brazil, Tunisia and Indonesia. The Brazilian facility alone has an annual production capacity of 7 million square metres of leather from bovine hide.  Gruppo Mastrotto Spa is selected as a powerbroker for leather.

Yildiz Holding is a Turkish conglomerate active in the manufacturing of food products with operations around the world. Its subsidiaries have more than 320 brands across a broad range of products, including biscuits, margarine, dairy products, confectionary, and instant foods. Two of its major subsidiaries are United Biscuits and Ülker. Yildiz is a major worldwide food manufacturer, especially for biscuits and snack bars for which it is one of the largest manufacturers in Europe and among the top five worldwide and as such is exposed to palm oil and soy.  Yildiz Holding is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Advance Publications is an American communications company that publishes magazines, newspapers, and journals, as well as online publishing and television. Advance Publications is one of the largest magazine publishers globally, and one of the company’s subsidiaries is Condé Nast, whose magazine portfolio includes brands such as Vogue, Vanity Fair, GQ, and Wired. The publishing operations require a large amount of pulp and paper.  Advance Publications Inc. is selected as a powerbroker for pulp & paper.
Karex Berhad was selected as a powerbroker for Rubber (Manufacturer) and is also assessed for Pulp & Paper (Packaging)

ORIX Corporation are a diversified financial services firm based in Japan. The corporation and its group has approximately $400 billion in AUM* through various asset management companies. In the 2022 selection, ORIX Corporation was providing 12 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Sodrugestvo Group, based in Luxembourg, is an agro-industrial company, which specialise in soybean and rapeseed processing, purchasing of grains and oilseeds and distribution of those products to the end consumer.

AFA (Agric. Federados Args.) is an Argentinean cooperative that produces and trades in agricultural products, with the majority including soy. In addition to this, AFA offers farmers a wide range of other services including logistic services, insurance products, technical assistance and financing solutions. AFA is one of the largest cooperations in Latin America, generating millions of tons of soybean per year, the main portion of which are used for the production of biodiesel for North America.

BTG Pactual are an investment bank and asset manager headquartered in Brazil. Their services include investment banking, corporate finance, asset and wealth management, and trading services. As of 2024, BTG Pactual's total assets amount to more than 100.3 billion USD. BTG Pactual are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading. In the 2024 selection, BTG Pactual was providing 3.6 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group Co Ltd (Yili Group) is a packaged food manufacturer, specialising in the production of dairy products. Its principal products include milk and other dairy-based foods, and can be classified into five major business divisions: liquid milk, powdered milk, ice cream, yogurt; and raw milk. As well as these, the company's products include other frozen foods, noodles, cheese, and soya bean powder. In total Yili Group has around 100 subsidiary companies and manufactures over 1000 products.
Since it was founded in Hohhot, China, in 1956, the company has established itself as a key player in the global packaged food industry. In 1993 the company was restructured as a group of companies under its current name and in 2005 it became China's leading company in the supply of milk powder and milk tea powder. Today, it ranks as both the top dairy and packaged food company on the Chinese market, and is among the top 20 packaged food companies overall worldwide. Furthermore, being listed on the Forbes 2000, it is also among the top public companies in the world.
Palm oil is commonly used as a base oil in ice cream, making it the most relevant forest risk commodity to Yili Group's operations. The Chinese ice cream industry consumed over 110,000 tonnes of palm oil in 2011. Yili holds the leading market share in the Chinese ice cream market, with its ice cream products including the Chocliz and Yili Pastureland brands.

The WTK Group of companies has diverse business interests in forestry and timber processing, oil palm, land development, trading, and manufacturing, as well as other services, including insurance and shipping. Established in 1940, the group has its origins in timber activities and is the oldest of the top logging companies operating in Sarawak, Malaysia. One of the group's subsidiaries, WTK Holdings Berhad, is a publicly listed investment holding company, whose subsidiaries in turn are involved in timber harvesting and in downstream timber processing. WTK Group operates five sawmills and three plywood mills and is therefore involved in manufacturing and trading plywood, sawn timber, logs and other timber products for domestic and overseas markets. As well as producing and trading timber products, the group is also active in the trade of other goods, including adhesives.
As well as being one of the oldest logging operators in Sarawak, WTK Group is also one of the largest; it has a total of 850,000 hectares of timber concessions, 320,000 hectares of which are managed under WTK Holdings Bhd. The organisation also has 400,000 hectares of concessions in Papua New Guinea and further forestry operations in Indonesia. In Malaysia, WTK Group is well established, with further activities outside of the timber industry, including in tourism, hotels and shipping.
With regards to other forest risk commodities, WTK Group is increasingly diversifying into oil palm. The group has a total palm oil land bank of around 120,000 hectares in Sarawak, Malaysia. It also owns three oil mills and plans to enter into the refinery business in the future.

Samling Global Ltd group of companies is a Malaysian conglomerate with diverse operations, including in the timber and oil palm sectors.  Founded in 1963, Samling's core activities are in the forest products industry, where its operations span the length of the supply chain, from harvesting to processing, manufacturing and distribution.
Samling Global Ltd has a complicated corporate structure, with numerous subsidiaries and holding companies.  For example, Samling Global Ltd is an investment holding company incorporated in Bermuda, with numerous wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, the US, the British Virgin Islands and Japan. These companies in turn have a variety of subsidiaries, for example, in China, Malaysia, Guyana, Indonesia and India.
Of particular relevance, is Samling Global Ltd's involvement in the timber trade in Sarawak, Malaysia. Under Lingui Developments Bhd, Samling manages a total of 1.3 million hectares. Lingui Developments Bhd is an investment holding and forest resources and wood products company. It produces logs, plywood and veneer, fibreboard, doors and door facings, and kitchen counters and products, primarily for the export market and in particular for Japan, China, India, Korea and North America. Under its wholly owned subsidiary, Barama Company Ltd, Samling Global Ltd is also one of the biggest forestry companies in Guyana, where it holds 1.6 million hectares of forest concessions and produces sawnwood.
Samling Global Ltd is well established in the export markets of China and Japan. In China, it manufactures plywood, laminated veneer lumber and flooring and also distributes flooring through Elegant Living, one of China's major flooring distributors. Samling Global Ltd's access to the Japanese market is facilitated through its partnerships with Itochu Corporation, one of Japan's major traders and property developers, and Daiken Corporation, through which Samling Global Ltd supplies tropical logs and plywood for construction.
Samling Global Ltd has also expanded its operations into oil palm. Under Glenealy Plantations (Malaya) Bhd, it has plantations in Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, covering a total area of over 60,000 hectares; and also operates palm oil mills in Sabah and Sarawak. Samling Global Ltd is also part of a consortium developing acacia plantations in Malaysia to supply wood for the pulp and paper industry. This consortium is made up of Samling Strategic Corp Sdn Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, and KTS Timber Industries Bhd, all of which are major timber companies in Sarawak.
