rows.coname: Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co. Ltd.
rows.coprofile:
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacture of a variety of paper products, including art paper, liquid packaging board, paying card, newsprint and copier paper. On top of its principal activities, making and selling paper products, the company also provides electricity, chemicals for paper manufacturing and construction materials. For example, through its subsidiaries Shandong Chenming Panels Co Ltd and Shouguang Chenming Floor Board Co Ltd, the company manufactures engineered wood products, including high-density fibreboard and wood flooring.
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd has manufacturing facilities located throughout China and distributes its products both domestically and to the international market, with overseas sales offices worldwide; in Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Brazil, and in Europe, India and Africa.  It is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies globally, ranking among the top 50, and as the second largest in China. The company produces around four million tonnes of paper products annually and until 2012 relied mostly on purchased chips and recovered fibre as the raw materials for its products. The company has since become increasingly integrated, developing a production base of plantation forests in China.

The Htoo Group of Companies is one of Myanmar's largest and most influential conglomerates. The group has more than fourteen subsidiaries engaged in a variety of operations. Its extensive influence is shown through the diversity of its business activities, which include ventures in the airline industry (Air Bagan); banking (AGD Bank); the tourism industry through its luxury resorts and hotels; mining; logistics; construction; agriculture; trading; radio (FM Bagan); and petroleum (Htoo Petrol), amongst others. Air Bagan was the country's first private airline, launched in 2004, and Htoo Group of Companies has since added to its portfolio in the air travel industry, through the establishment of Asian Wings Airways.
The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

Kewpie Corp (Kewpie) is a Japanese food manufacturer that produces a variety of processed and packaged food products for commercial and consumer use. Palm oil and soya are the most relevant forest risk commodities to Kewpie's operations, as vegetable oils are commonly used in these products. The Kewpie group of companies consists of the Kewpie Corp and 65 consolidated subsidiaries, which together are involved in the manufacturing, wholesale, transport and storage of food products. The group's operations can be divided into five business segments: Condiments and Processed Foods; Health Function Products; Egg Products; Salad and Prepared Foods; and Distribution System.
The condiments products category is a core part of the Group's operations, principally producing mayonnaise and dressings. The company's processed foods segment produces a variety of canned and bottled foods, such as jams, pasta sauces, canned sweetcorn and baby food. Through these two business segments, the sales of these products have positioned Kewpie in a leading position in the domestic and international spreads market, where its holds the top market share in Japan, and is among the top 20 globally. Kewpie is also among the top five manufacturers of baby food in Japan, and places within the top 50 on the global market. Kewpie also has a business division specialising in egg products, such as liquid, frozen and dried eggs, which are used by food manufacturers in the production of confectionery, meat products and fish cakes, among others. Kewpie uses a large amount of egg products itself, for example as a main ingredient in its mayonnaise, and accounts for the use of about 9% of all eggs produced in Japan.  As well as the above divisions, Kewpie has operations in the production of fine chemical products, such as hyaluronic acid; and delicatessen products, such as salads. Finally, the company also provides food distribution services for the domestic market, including under K.R.S. Corporation. Kewpie has a well-established overseas presence, with subsidiaries is in the United States, the Netherlands, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand.
Kewpie is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO).

rows.coname: Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Co. Ltd.
rows.coprofile:
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacture of a variety of paper products, including art paper, liquid packaging board, paying card, newsprint and copier paper. On top of its principal activities, making and selling paper products, the company also provides electricity, chemicals for paper manufacturing and construction materials. For example, through its subsidiaries Shandong Chenming Panels Co Ltd and Shouguang Chenming Floor Board Co Ltd, the company manufactures engineered wood products, including high-density fibreboard and wood flooring.
Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd has manufacturing facilities located throughout China and distributes its products both domestically and to the international market, with overseas sales offices worldwide; in Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Brazil, and in Europe, India and Africa.  It is one of the largest forest, paper and packaging companies globally, ranking among the top 50, and as the second largest in China. The company produces around four million tonnes of paper products annually and until 2012 relied mostly on purchased chips and recovered fibre as the raw materials for its products. The company has since become increasingly integrated, developing a production base of plantation forests in China.

Savencia SA, formerly Bongrain SA, is a French cheese and dairy producer founded in the 1950s. It is the second largest cheese company in France and the fifth largest in the world, using around 4.2 billion litres of milk annually. The company has over 19,000 employees and its products are sold in 120 countries, with production and sales subsidiaries in Europe, North and South America, Asia and Australia. Savencia SA also has production facilities worldwide, in countries such as Russia, Ireland, France, US, Argentina, Egypt, China and India. There are many brands within the company, such as UK-based Coeur de Lion and Saint Agur. The company's global expansion began in 1962 with entries into the Belgian, German and Swiss markets, and in 1975 the company expanded beyond Europe into Brazil, the US and Australia. Groupe Blattner Elwyn is a conglomerate based in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), active in a variety of sectors, including agribusiness, logistics and distribution, and timber processing . Agriculture is at the core of Groupe Blattner Elwyn's operations and the group's agribusiness activities are in the production and processing of rubber, palm oil and cocoa. The Group's industrial operations are in: The production of crown corks and metal cans; timber processing and harvesting; and in the production of laminated table-tops, through a company based in France. Finally, Groupe Blattner Elwyn has a variety of distribution and services companies, which include medical operations, chemical production, the automotive industry, and importing and exporting activities.
Groupe Blattner Elwyn has six subsidiaries involved in the cultivation and processing of palm oil managing some 28,311 hectares of land, 17,196 of which are currently in production. The group operates six oil palm factories and provides employment for around 10,000 permanent and temporary workers and sharecroppers.
Regarding the group's timber operations, Groupe Blattner Elwyn acquired SIFORCO from Danzer Group in February 2012. This acquisition was Groupe Blattner Elwyn's first step into the forestry sector, which the Group views as an investment in the growing timber industry in the DRC. SIFORCO, which was established in 1972, manages an area of over 1.9 million hectares in the DRC, making it one of the largest logging companies in the country in terms of forest area. SIFORCO has 600 employees and the majority of its concessions are located in the Equateur and Orientale provinces. The company harvests its natural forests for the production of logs and also has timber processing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer, and a joiner's workshop. It harvests and processes timber mainly for the European and American markets.

The Gap Inc. is a leading global apparel retailer selling apparel, accessories and personal care products for men, women and children through its various brands. Gap Inc. was established with the opening of a single Gap store in San Francisco in the United States in 1969. Since then the company has expanded greatly through the establishment of several other retail brands, including Banana Republic, Old Navy, Athleta, and Intermix.
The company has around 3,300 company-operated stores and 400 franchise stores in more than 90 countries alongside e-commerce sales operations in almost 100 countries. Its company-operated stores are located in the US, Canada, the UK, France, Ireland, Japan, China, Italy and, since 2014, Taiwan. Gap Inc. also has franchise agreements with unaffiliated franchisees to operate Gap, Old Navy and Banana Republic stores throughout Asia, Australia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Gap Inc. employs around 140,000 full and part time individuals.
The company's flagship brand, Gap, which sells casual, American style apparel, continues to be the most prominent of the group's retail brands, with over 1,430 company stores and over 340 franchises worldwide. Gap Inc.'s retail brands vary in their retailing of own-brand and other designer brands. Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy and Athleta brands each sell their own own-label products, while the Intermix brands stocks both its own-label products and those of other designers.
Gap Inc is among the top three retailers of private-label apparel and the top five of all clothing retailers globally. Each of the company's brands stock a range of leather goods, including shoes, belts and bags. For example, Intermix, which was acquired by Gap Inc in 2012, offers a range of branded luxury accessories, including leather bags. Banana Republic and Gap brands similarly stock a range of leather goods, including leather jackets for men and women, and leather handbags, belts and shoes. Gap Inc. does not directly own or operate its own manufacturing facilities, and as of 2012, its branded apparel is produced in around 923 factories in 32 countries worldwide.

Emami Ltd. was founded in 1974 and is a leading personal and healthcare business headquartered in India. Through its subsidiaries it has a presence in a numerous markets and in various segments of the supply chain. One of its subsidiaries, Emami Biotech Ltd., is a key trader and processor of a range of raw materials, including oil palm, soybeans and jatropha. Emami Biotech has been central to the growth of India's capability in the biodiesel market, with the installation of the largest biodiesel plant in eastern India at Haldia. This plant has recently been upgraded so that it can process 2,000 tonnes of soybean and palm oil per day. This complements another refinery in Andhra Pradesh which adds a further 1,200 tonnes per day for the production of palm and sunflower oils. To further fill Emami's down-market needs, Emami Biotech imports a large amount of raw product into India, with over 4% of the total Indian market share in crude palm oil imports.
In terms of upstream activities, Emani Biotech owns a plantation in Ethiopia for the production of edible and non-edible oils and is looking to purchase plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia. In recent years, Emami Biotech has invested in the development of its marketing network to distribute its products under its Healthy and Tasty brand. Through this network, the company is able to supply goods to over 4,500 distributors and 12,000 retailers. Another subsidiary of Emami is Starmark, which owns a chain of seven retail stores in Kolkata and Chennai. These retail stores sell a range of books, toys, music and stationary. The sale of stationary and books is complemented by the production of newsprint, writing and printing paper by another subsidiary, Emami Paper Mills Ltd. Emami Paper Mills manufacturers these products from waste paper in two plants, one in Orissa and the other in Kolkata.

Lotte Confectionary is not only the largest domestic producer of candies, biscuits, chocolates, chewing gum and ice cream, it also has operations overseas including in the US, Russia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Belgium, India and othes. Today Lotte Co. Ltd is a vast organisation, which has diverse business interests in food, retail, petrochemicals, finance and communications. Additional food related operations in Korea include businesses involved in fats and oils, bakeries, milk processing, baby food and meat processing products. Lotte Co. Ltd also has number of fast food franchise operations in South Korea with separate entities for doughnuts, cafes, hamburgers, desserts and family restaurants.
Lotte Shopping Co., Ltd. is a listed subsidiary of the company, operating department stores and discount stores. It is amongst the 20 largest grocery retailers globally. Lotte Mart is a chain of discount stores that operates more than 60 stores in Korea but has also opened stores oversea including in China, Indonesia (where it is one of the top three supermarket retailers), and Vietnam. In Korea, Lotte Co. Ltd is the leading supermarket operator and also operates a chain of 7-Eleven stores through their Korea Seven subsidiary.
Due to its involvement in processed foods, retail, and meat processing the most relevant forest risk commodities for Lotte Co. Ltd are soya, palm oil, beef, and paper & packaging. Lotte Co. Ltd is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil.

Schroder Investment Management Ltd. are a financial services company headquartered in the UK offering wealth management and asset management services for private, corporate and institutional clients. As of 2017, Schroder have more than £410 billion of assets under management and total assets of £21 billion. They are one of the top 40 shareholders in Forest 500 companies with over 9.6 billion USD worth of shares in companies in a variety of forest risk sectors.

Gruppo Mastrotto is an Italian based processor and manufacturer of leather for use in products such as footwear, upholstery and other leather goods. Most the group's operations are in Italy, making it a major importer of leather, and it also has operations in Brazil, Tunisia and Indonesia. The Brazilian facility alone has an annual production capacity of 7 million square metres of leather from bovine hide.

The Htoo Group of Companies is one of Myanmar's largest and most influential conglomerates. The group has more than fourteen subsidiaries engaged in a variety of operations. Its extensive influence is shown through the diversity of its business activities, which include ventures in the airline industry (Air Bagan); banking (AGD Bank); the tourism industry through its luxury resorts and hotels; mining; logistics; construction; agriculture; trading; radio (FM Bagan); and petroleum (Htoo Petrol), amongst others. Air Bagan was the country's first private airline, launched in 2004, and Htoo Group of Companies has since added to its portfolio in the air travel industry, through the establishment of Asian Wings Airways.
The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of America's largest cooperatives, employing 9,000 people and with 3,200 producer-members and 1,000 member-cooperatives serving over 300,000 agricultural producers. In 2013 it had annual sales of $14.2 billion, and it ranks #194 on the Fortune 500. The company has four business segments: dairy foods, crop inputs, animal feed and business services. Dairy foods products are provided by its Dairy Foods and Kozy Shack businesses. Crop inputs are provided by its Winfield Solutions business, and its animal feeds are provided by its Purina Animal Nutrition LLC, Land O'Lakes Feed LLC and Purina Mills LLC businesses.
Dairy Foods sells mainly butter and cheese, under the under the Land O Lakes and Alpine Lace brands. It claims to produce America's #1 brand of butter and deli american cheese. The Land O Lakes brand is also licensed to a small number of partner companies who produce milk, creams, juices, eggs, cottage cheese, sour cream, yogurt and cocoa mixes, such as the WhiteWaves Food Company. Kozy Shack, acquired in 2012, produces chilled desserts such as rice pudding, tapioca pudding and flans and claims to be America's #1 brand of tapioca and rice pudding.
Purina Animal Nutrition LLC provides supplements, ingredients, complete feeds and speciality technologies to farmers and the consumer (pet) markets via several thousand local cooperatives, independent dealers and other retailers in the US. The company is heavily involved in research and development and has over 100 patents worldwide. Land O'Lakes Inc. animal feed production began with feed for mules and horses in 1894, and today its feed products are produced for an extremely broad range of animals from farm animals, during multiple lifecycle stages, to fish, pets and exotic animals. Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers and therefore purchases large quantities of soya, some of which is used in animal feed production,. As some animal feeds also use palm oil, Land O'Lakes Inc. may also source palm oil for use as an ingredient.
Land O'Lakes Inc. is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil or the Roundtable on Responsible Soy.

X5 Retail Group NV is a Russian food retailer, with retail operations in four different formats and brands: Economy stores under the Pyaterochka brand (4,789 stores); supermarkets under the Perekrestok brand (403 stores); hypermarkets under the Karusel brand (82 stores); convenience stores under a range of different brand names (209 stores); and an online retail channel under the E5.ru brand. The company has its origins in 1995, when the Perekrestok supermarket brand was established. The chain of Pyaterochka stores was launched a few years later in 1999, and in 2006 these two brands merged and adopted the X5 Retail Group NV name.
X5 Retail Group's Pyaterochka economy convenience stores provide over 69% of the group's total revenue in 2014 . The Group has been steadily increasing its marketing of private label products and, through its various retail formats, offers a wide range of products, including dairy products, canned goods and groceries, confectionery and bakery products, and fresh and processed meat, among others.

Cencosud is a Chilean retail conglomerate with operations throughout Latin America. Its sales outlets include supermarkets, home improvement stores, shopping centres and department stores. It is especially prominent in Argentina where it ranks among the top three retailers for edible groceries.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating producer and distributor headquartered in Michigan, USA, employing more than 110,000 people. The key subsidiary of relevance to forest risk commodities owned by Lear Corp. is Eagle Ottawa, which produces leather upholstery products for the automotive industry. Eagle Ottawa was founded in 1865 and was formerly known as Eagle Tanning Works but changed its name to Eagle Ottawa, LLC in 1916.
 
Eagle Ottawa claims to be the largest supplier of premium automotive leather and produces a variety of leather products, including finished hides, cut leather, natural shrunken grain leather, and chrome- and non-chrome-tanned leather.  As well as these, it also produces leather for other interior uses, such as for door panels and instrument panels. The company engages in various activities in leather processing including pre-tanning and tanning as well as cutting and finishing. Aside from the subsidiary's headquarters, which are in the state of Michigan, in the US, Eagle Ottawa also has facilities in Mexico, Brazil, Hungary, China, South Korea and Thailand. It also has sales and design locations in China, Japan, Brazil, Germany, England, Sweden and Italy, as well as the US. The company's customers include some of the automobile industry's biggest players, including Mercedes, BMW, Toyota, Renault Chrysler, GMC and Volkswagen.

Deichmann Group is a German shoe manufacturer and retailer founded in 1913 by Heinreich Deichmann. The company was established in Essen, North Rhine Westphalia, where the headquarters are still located. Currently, Deichmann Group has around 3,600 stores across 23 European countries and the USA; 1,360 stores are in Germany and over 80 in the UK. Deichmann Group is the top shoe retail company in Europe and sold around 172 million pairs of shoes worldwide in 2014. The company aims to produce fashionable shoes at affordable prices and sells shoes for men, women and children as well as accessories, including bags. The company stocks many of their own brands such as Graceland and 5th Avenue but also has collaborations with other brands, particularly in the children's sector, for example with Hello Kitty, Disney and Peppa Pig. In addition, Deichmann stores stock sports shoes from other brands, including Adidas, Fila and Pumav.
Deichmann Group began opening stores in European countries other than Germany during the early 1990s, including in the UK in 2001 and most recently in Russia in 2014. Acquisitions have also assisted brand development. In 2002, Deichmann Group bought the US chain Off Broadway Shoes, which has over 75 stores across the US, and the company has owned Rack Room Shoes since 1984. The company continues to expand its retail presence in Germany, with the planned opening of 66 new stores in the country during 2015 alongside 150 new retail branches internationally.

Ruchi Soya is a subsidiary of Ruchi Group, an Indian conglomerate with diverse business interests. Founded in 1986 as a trading company, Ruchi Soya is now a leading manufacturer and India's largest marketer of edible oils, condiments, and soya-based food. It runs 21 manufacturing facilities across India to create products for its portfolio of brands, which includes Nutrela, Mahakosh, and Sunrich. During 2013 to 2014, it had a turnover of US$4 billion. The company is a member of both the Round Table on Responsible Soy and the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil. In 2014, Ruchi Soya extracted over 3 million tonnes of soya meal and handled over 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil.

China Mengniu Dairy (Mengniu) is a Chinese manufacturer and distributor of dairy products. Its products include milk, ice-cream, cheese, and other dairy products. As of 2015, Mengniu had over 33 milk production facilities throughout China with an annual capacity of more than 8.5 million metric tons. The company is one of the top dairy companies in China and one of the top five in dairy globally, whilst also ranking highly for other dairy products and packaged food. It is also a major Chinese importer of palm oil.

Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group Co Ltd (Yili Group) is a packaged food manufacturer, specialising in the production of dairy products. Its principal products include milk and other dairy-based foods, and can be classified into five major business divisions: liquid milk, powdered milk, ice cream, yogurt; and raw milk. As well as these, the company's products include other frozen foods, noodles, cheese, and soya bean powder. In total Yili Group has around 100 subsidiary companies and manufactures over 1000 products.
Since it was founded in Hohhot, China, in 1956, the company has established itself as a key player in the global packaged food industry. In 1993 the company was restructured as a group of companies under its current name and in 2005 it became China's leading company in the supply of milk powder and milk tea powder. Today, it ranks as both the top dairy and packaged food company on the Chinese market, and is among the top 20 packaged food companies overall worldwide. Furthermore, being listed on the Forbes 2000, it is also among the top public companies in the world.
Palm oil is commonly used as a base oil in ice cream, making it the most relevant forest risk commodity to Yili Group's operations. The Chinese ice cream industry consumed over 110,000 tonnes of palm oil in 2011. Yili holds the leading market share in the Chinese ice cream market, with its ice cream products including the Chocliz and Yili Pastureland brands.

Products include instant noodles, baked goods, and soft drinks, and its Master Kong brand is well-known in China. Alongside its manufacturing, the company also has an extensive sales network in China with more than 100,000 retail outlets as of 2013, as well as distributing products globally. Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

Japfa is one of Indonesia’s largest agri-food companies. The company produces animal feed and operates industrial beef, poultry and aquaculture shrimp farms. Its feed and meat brands include Comfeed, Benefeed, Santori Beef, Best Chicken and the Tora-Tora brands. Japfa is one of the largest animal feed and chicken producers in Indonesia. Japfa are exposed to soy as a key ingredient in animal feed.  Japfa Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to beef.

The Rougier Group is a French company primarily involved in the logging, processing, and trade of tropical timber from Africa. From its headquarters in Niort, in the Poitou-Charentes province of France, Rougier presides over a vast forestry concession in the African countries (and former French colonies) of Gabon and Cameroon. All of these regions also have sawmills and manufacturing facilities which process timber products.  Rougier Group is selected as a powerbroker for timber and paper packaging.

Savencia SA, formerly Bongrain SA, is a French cheese and dairy producer founded in the 1950s. It is the second largest cheese company in France and the fifth largest in the world, using around 4.2 billion litres of milk annually. The company has over 19,000 employees and its products are sold in 120 countries, with production and sales subsidiaries in Europe, North and South America, Asia and Australia. Savencia SA also has production facilities worldwide, in countries such as Russia, Ireland, France, US, Argentina, Egypt, China and India. There are many brands within the company, such as UK-based Coeur de Lion and Saint Agur. The company's global expansion began in 1962 with entries into the Belgian, German and Swiss markets, and in 1975 the company expanded beyond Europe into Brazil, the US and Australia. Amongst others, the company's subsidiaries include: Alouette Cheese (US); Bresse Blue Japon (Japan); and Ich Leibe Kaese (Germany), which provides recipes and information about cheese.

Want Want is a Chinese investment holding company with subsidiaries engaged in the manufacture and distribution of packaged food products, including rice crackers, dairy goods, confectionary items and other snacks. The company primarily serves the domestic market in China, but also exports its products to locations such as the United States and Canada. As a leading producer of packaged food products, Want Want is exposed to the forest risk commodities palm oil and soy which are commonly used ingredients in this sector.   Want Want is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

rows.coname: Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group Co. Ltd.
rows.coprofile:
Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group Co Ltd (Yili Group) is a packaged food manufacturer, specialising in the production of dairy products. Its principal products include milk and other dairy-based foods, and can be classified into five major business divisions: liquid milk, powdered milk, ice cream, yogurt; and raw milk. As well as these, the company's products include other frozen foods, noodles, cheese, and soya bean powder. In total Yili Group has around 100 subsidiary companies and manufactures over 1000 products.
Since it was founded in Hohhot, China, in 1956, the company has established itself as a key player in the global packaged food industry. In 1993 the company was restructured as a group of companies under its current name and in 2005 it became China's leading company in the supply of milk powder and milk tea powder. Today, it ranks as both the top dairy and packaged food company on the Chinese market, and is among the top 20 packaged food companies overall worldwide. Furthermore, being listed on the Forbes 2000, it is also among the top public companies in the world.
Palm oil is commonly used as a base oil in ice cream, making it the most relevant forest risk commodity to Yili Group's operations. The Chinese ice cream industry consumed over 110,000 tonnes of palm oil in 2011. Yili holds the leading market share in the Chinese ice cream market, with its ice cream products including the Chocliz and Yili Pastureland brands.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company specialising in dairy products, including milk powder and nutrition products, cheese, liquid milk, fats and chilled dairy goods. The company, originally known as Societe Laitiere Besnier, was established in 1939 and changed its name to Groupe Lactalis S.A. in 1999. Visible in 150 countries and with on the ground operations in 70 countries (as of 2011), Lactalis has grown to have a global presence and ranks itself the world's leading dairy group. The company employs around 61,000 people and operates a total of 200 industrial plants.  The majority of its operations are in Europe, where it employs almost 40,000 people, however it is active worldwide, with operations in America, Africa and Asia/Oceania.  In September 2014, the Group, through its Parmalat subsidiary, agreed to buy the dairy units of Brazilian food company BRF, and has also agreed to buy units of Brazilian dairy company, LBR-Lacteos (which previously held license to use the Parmalat brand name in Brazil).
The group's branded products include President cheese, Rachel's yoghurt, Roquefort Socieite and Munch Bunch. It also has a long history with Nestle and took over a subsidiary, Claudel Roustang, in 1985. In 2006 Groupe Lactalis and Nestle created a subsidiary, Lactalis Nestle, which deals with Nestle's fresh dairy produce and owns yoghurt brands, Munch Bunch and Ski, in the UK. In addition to its recognisable dairy brands, Groupe Lactalis also provides ingredients for industry, including whey products, lactose and milk powder, to be used in the manufacture of products such as ice-cream, ready meals and confectionery.
Groupe Lactalis also uses palm oil in some of its products. For example, its Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division, produces butters, creams and margarines, some of which contain palm oil, as do the products of the Lactalis Nutrition Sante division. The Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division does not currently measure how much palm oil it uses but it plans to start sourcing RSPO-certified oil palm products in 2015 and to be using 100% RSPO-certified oil palm by 2018 (on own-brand products). Further to this, some of Groupe Lactalis products also contain soya.

Perez Companc Family Group is an Argentinian holding company primarily involved the energy business, such as oil and gas, petrochemicals and electricity. One of its subsidiaries is Molinos Río de la Plata, an agribusiness company in Argentina involved in the procurement of agricultural raw materials as well as producing several branded products such as vegetable oils. The company is a major exporter of soya from Argentina.

Toyo Suisan Kaisha Ltd (Toyo) is an international food producer specialising in ramen noodles and seafood. Toyo manufactures its products through various sub-divisions, such as the Domestic Instant Noodles segment and the Frozen and Refrigerated Foods segment. In addition to noodles, it also produces wontons, soup products, fish, ham, sausages and seasonings. It also has a Prepared Food section which manufactures sterile packaged rice, retort rice, soup and other products.
The company was founded in 1953, has its headquarters in Tokyo, and employs around 4,600 people. Its main overseas operations are in Mexico and the Us through its Overseas Instant Noodles Division, which sells noodles under the brand name Maruchan Inc. As of 2008, Toyo owns three food processing facilities in the US and has 32 subsidiaries.
By the 1970s, Toyo had become well-known in Japan and had branched out internationally. It is now the largest noodle company in the US, the second largest in Japan and third largest in the world. It is also in the top five companies in Japan for dried processed food and chilled processed food, and in the top 30 largest soup companies worldwide.
The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm oil and in 2013 was implicated by the Rainforest Action Network to be one of the 'Snack Food 20' responsible for using 'conflict' palm oil from unsustainable sources,.

The Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) offers financial services to Brazilian companies and financial institutions with the aim of stimulating industry and infrastructure growth in Brazil. Their services include corporate financing, non-reimbursable investments, and securities. As of 2024, the bank's total assets amount to more than 737 billion BRL. BNDES are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading. In the 2024 selection, BNDES was providing 3.5 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.

The company has many well-known brands including Coeur de Lion, Saint Agur, Géramont and Lucina. Samling Global Ltd group of companies is a Malaysian conglomerate with diverse operations, including in the timber and oil palm sectors.  Founded in 1963, Samling's core activities are in the forest products industry, where its operations span the length of the supply chain, from harvesting to processing, manufacturing and distribution.
Samling Global Ltd has a complicated corporate structure, with numerous subsidiaries and holding companies.  For example, Samling Global Ltd is an investment holding company incorporated in Bermuda, with numerous wholly owned subsidiaries in Australia, the US, the British Virgin Islands and Japan. These companies in turn have a variety of subsidiaries, for example, in China, Malaysia, Guyana, Indonesia and India.
Of particular relevance, is Samling Global Ltd's involvement in the timber trade in Sarawak, Malaysia. Under Lingui Developments Bhd, Samling manages a total of 1.3 million hectares. Lingui Developments Bhd is an investment holding and forest resources and wood products company. It produces logs, plywood and veneer, fibreboard, doors and door facings, and kitchen counters and products, primarily for the export market and in particular for Japan, China, India, Korea and North America. Under its wholly owned subsidiary, Barama Company Ltd, Samling Global Ltd is also one of the biggest forestry companies in Guyana, where it holds 1.6 million hectares of forest concessions and produces sawnwood.
Samling Global Ltd is well established in the export markets of China and Japan. In China, it manufactures plywood, laminated veneer lumber and flooring and also distributes flooring through Elegant Living, one of China's major flooring distributors. Samling Global Ltd's access to the Japanese market is facilitated through its partnerships with Itochu Corporation, one of Japan's major traders and property developers, and Daiken Corporation, through which Samling Global Ltd supplies tropical logs and plywood for construction.
Samling Global Ltd has also expanded its operations into oil palm. Under Glenealy Plantations (Malaya) Bhd, it has plantations in Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, covering a total area of over 60,000 hectares; and also operates palm oil mills in Sabah and Sarawak. Samling Global Ltd is also part of a consortium developing acacia plantations in Malaysia to supply wood for the pulp and paper industry. This consortium is made up of Samling Strategic Corp Sdn Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, and KTS Timber Industries Bhd, all of which are major timber companies in Sarawak.

Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is a Japanese company, established in 1935 and incorporated in 1955; it is involved in the manufacture and distribution of food and drink products. The company has three main business segments: Beverages and Food Manufacturing and Sale; Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing and Sale; and Others. The company's original and still most recognisable product is a probiotic fermented milk drink sold under the Yakult brand. This continues to be the company's main product, particularly in the overseas market, where average daily sales of Yakult products in early 2013 were over 22.5 million. However, aside from its fermented milk and yogurt products (which include the Joie, Sofuhl, and Purela, amongst others) Yakult also offers non-dairy beverages such as flavoured tea drinks and juices, a range of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food products, including noodles.
As of 2013, the company had around 79 subsidiaries and 18 associated companies. The company has overseas and domestic operations, with its operations outside of Japan starting in 1964, when its Taiwanese subsidiary was established. Since then, this has grown and the company is now active in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide, including in Europe, the US, Brazil, Mexico, China, South Korea, Hong Kong, Indonesia, and elsewhere in Asia.
Yakult is a significant player in the global packaged food market, demonstrated by its leading position in a variety of markets worldwide. For example, specifically, it ranks among the top three companies in the dairy products market in Japan, and among the top ten for the packaged food industry overall. It is also among the top five companies with the largest market shares in the South Korean noodle industry, and holds a similarly high market share in the market for noodles in the United States, and is in the top 25 companies in the world for the packaged food industry.

Danish Agro is a cooperative of Danish agribusinesses active across 16 countries. The company operates in the purchase and sale of feedstuff, ingredients and vitamin mixes, fertiliser, crop protection and energy.

Calbee is a Japanese snack and cereal company that has overseas sales and operations in ten countries. It is a major sweet and savoury snack company. Major markets include Hong Kong, South Korea, and the US, and its products include a wide variety of potato and other vegetable crisps. In Hong Kong and China, it is one of the largest such companies by market share and it is one of the five largest in the world.

Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company with a substantial portfolio of businesses operating in a diverse range of sectors. Founded in 1938, it employs over 35,000 people across a number of sectors such as manufacturing; trading and ï¬nancial services; oil and gas exploration; print and packaging; agriculture; ï¬sheries; real estate; and mining. In addition to its core business activities in Yemen, the group operates as a manufacturing firm and trading company across four global regions: Africa; Asia; Europe; and the Middle East. Its global business focuses on non-food, and beverage and food products such as confectionery and biscuits. It has an extensive logistics infrastructure to manufacture and distribute its own and partners' products across its global markets.
Pacific Inter-Link (PIL), one of the group's Malaysia-based companies, is involved in the processing and trading of palm oil. It was incorporated in 1988 to export commodities and employs 1,750 people in Malaysia and Indonesia. Its refineries had an annual processing capacity of 1.3 million tonnes per annum in 2012. PIL is one of the major exporters of palm oil from Asia to Africa and the Middle East, exporting to around 64 countries in total. The company is currently looking to expand further into the African market, with the development of new refineries in Ethiopia and Kenya. The company's brands include Avena and Madina, which both sell various palm oil products, such as margarine, shortening, cooking oil, and vegetable ghee, as well as a range of packaged food, including canned fish and meat, and pasta products. On top of its core palm oil products, the group also supplies dairy products under the Milgro, Milac, and Sheeba brands.

The Htoo Group of Companies is one of Myanmar's largest and most influential conglomerates. The group has more than fourteen subsidiaries engaged in a variety of operations. Its extensive influence is shown through the diversity of its business activities, which include ventures in the airline industry (Air Bagan); banking (AGD Bank); the tourism industry through its luxury resorts and hotels; mining; logistics; construction; agriculture; trading; radio (FM Bagan); and petroleum (Htoo Petrol), amongst others. Air Bagan was the country's first private airline, launched in 2004, and Htoo Group of Companies has since added to its portfolio in the air travel industry, through the establishment of Asian Wings Airways.
The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

Frigorifico Concepcion S.A. is a meat processing company in Paraguay that is involved throughout the beef supply chain, from production to processing, distribution and exporting. Though primarily dealing in beef, the company also processes cattle for leather and biodiesel. It was among the top five exporters of beef from Latin America and is one of the largest exporters of beef in Paraguay and Brazil. Frigorifico Concepcion also owns three ranches totalling 40,000 heads of cattle and also has a monthly slaughter capacity of 40,000 heads of cattle as of 2016.

Want Want China Holdings Limited is a Chinese investment holding company, which through its main company and subsidiaries engages in the manufacture and distribution of packaged food products, including beverages, dairy products, rice crackers, confectionery and other snacks.
Want Want Holdings China Limited was incorporated in 2007, but has its origins in the 1960s in Taiwan, when the company began as a manufacturer of canned goods, under the name of I Lan Foods Industrial Co Ltd. The Want Want trademark was registered in China in1989 and its first Chinese subsidiary followed in 1992. In 2007, Want Want Holdings Limited was delisted from the Singapore Stock Exchange and the company was restructured, with the incorporation of Want Want China Holdings Limited; the new holding company responsible for the group's operations in the food and drinks industry.
The company is headquartered in Shanghai and the majority of its operations are in mainland China, although it also is active in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore and Japan. The company's subsidiaries include Want Want Holdings Ltd., Want Want Foods Limited, and Long Wave Foods Limited. These produce a variety of food and drink products, including sugar coated and savoury rice crackers, flavoured milk, coffee, yoghurt drinks, confectionery and nuts and other snacks. The company has around 95 factories and 36 production bases in China.
In 2010, the company was China's largest manufacturer of rice cakes and flavoured dairy drinks. Want Want is particularly well-established in the sweet and savoury snacks market, where it is among the top ten manufacturers in the world, and the market leader in China. It also occupies a significant market share of the Chinese dairy and bakery products industries, and China's packaged food industry as a whole. The most relevant forest risk commodities its uses are palm oil and soya, which are commonly used in packaged and processed food products. The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO).

Pertamina Persero PT is a state-owned Indonesian company focussing on oil, gas, renewable energy and new energy. This involves the exploration and extraction of oil and gas as well as the development of geothermal energy and coal bed methane as alternate energy sources. In addition, the company is involved in crude oil processing and the marketing, trade and shipping of oil products, gas and petrochemicals. The company is also involved in the domestic retail of gasoline and diesel and has an extensive network of over 5000 retail gas stations across Indonesia.
As per a government mandate in 2013, all diesel for industry and transportation in Indonesia must contain 10% biofuel. This has led to Pertamina Persero PT issuing a number of tenders for palm oil-based biodiesel to meet these requirements. Palm oil companies Wilmar International and Musim Mas have already won tenders to supply biodiesel to Pertamina Persero PT and more tenders are planned for the future. A total of 5.3 million kilolitres (around 4.7 million MT) of palm-based biodiesel will be procured for 2014-2015.

Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company with a substantial portfolio of businesses operating in a diverse range of sectors. Founded in 1938, it employs over 35,000 people across a number of sectors such as manufacturing; trading and ï¬nancial services; oil and gas exploration; print and packaging; agriculture; ï¬sheries; real estate; and mining. In addition to its core business activities in Yemen, the group operates as a manufacturing firm and trading company across four global regions: Africa; Asia; Europe; and the Middle East. Its global business focuses on non-food, and beverage and food products such as confectionery and biscuits. It has an extensive logistics infrastructure to manufacture and distribute its own and partners' products across its global markets.
Pacific Inter-Link (PIL), one of the group's Malaysia-based companies, is involved in the processing and trading of palm oil. It was incorporated in 1988 to export commodities and employs 1,750 people in Malaysia and Indonesia. Its refineries had an annual processing capacity of 1.3 million tonnes per annum in 2012. PIL is one of the major exporters of palm oil from Asia to Africa and the Middle East, exporting to around 64 countries in total. The company is currently looking to expand further into the African market, with the development of new refineries in Ethiopia and Kenya. The company's brands include Avena and Madina, which both sell various palm oil products, such as margarine, shortening, cooking oil, and vegetable ghee, as well as a range of packaged food, including canned fish and meat, and pasta products. On top of its core palm oil products, the group also supplies dairy products under the Milgro, Milac, and Sheeba brands.

Nitori Holdings Co Ltd is a furniture company based in Hokkaido, Japan. The company dates back to 1967 when it opened its first furniture store and in 2010 the company was restructured: Nitori Holdings Co Ltd was established, marking the transition of Nitori Co Ltd to a holding company structure whereby Nitori Holdings Co Ltd oversees the Nitori group of companies,.The company operates a chain of furniture stores, and sells its own brand, manufactured as well as imported merchandise. It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand. Around 80% of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are sourced from overseas and as part of its expansion outside of Japan, the company also supports the operations of two furniture factories in Indonesia (since 1994) and Vietnam (since 2004). Some of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are manufactured at externally-owned facilities; however, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd maintains close contact with and involvement in all its business operations through the establishment of regional offices. Furthermore, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is directly responsible for the import and distribution of all products to its stores, with its subsidiary Home Logistics Co Ltd responsible for all domestic distribution.
In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.

It is one of China's largest construction and real estate companies, but also operates globally in 20 countries and is one of the leading construction companies globally. Housing construction is a very timber heavy industry and CSCEC has a dominant market share. Housing construction also comprises the majority of their contracts by value.

Cresud SA is an agricultural company based in Argentina, involved in the production of crops, and beef and dairy cattle. As of June 2013, the company has a beef cattle stock of over 60,000 heads, which are primarily destined for the domestic Argentine market and not for export. Crop production includes soya, corn, sunflower and wheat. Soya accounts for over half of the company's total crop production, with 220,000 tons produced in 2013. Almost half of this soya was produced in Brazil, with a large amount also produced in Argentina.
Cresud SA owns almost 1 million hectares of its own land and nearly 50,000 hectares of land under lease agreements. Of this land more than 400,000 hectares is currently productive, with a further 135,000 hectares under development. Although largely based in Argentina, since 2005 the company has been expanding into other Latin American countries including Brazil, Paraguay and Bolivia. Currently, 66% of the company's land area is in Argentina, 19% in Brazil, 13% in Paraguay and 2% in Bolivia.

Emami Ltd. was founded in 1974 and is a leading personal and healthcare business headquartered in India. Through its subsidiaries it has a presence in a numerous markets and in various segments of the supply chain. One of its subsidiaries, Emami Biotech Ltd., is a key trader and processor of a range of raw materials, including oil palm, soybeans and jatropha. Emami Biotech has been central to the growth of India's capability in the biodiesel market, with the installation of the largest biodiesel plant in eastern India at Haldia. This plant has recently been upgraded so that it can process 2,000 tonnes of soybean and palm oil per day. This complements another refinery in Andhra Pradesh which adds a further 1,200 tonnes per day for the production of palm and sunflower oils. To further fill Emami's down-market needs, Emami Biotech imports a large amount of raw product into India, with over 4% of the total Indian market share in crude palm oil imports.
In terms of upstream activities, Emani Biotech owns a plantation in Ethiopia for the production of edible and non-edible oils and is looking to purchase plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia. In recent years, Emami Biotech has invested in the development of its marketing network to distribute its products under its Healthy and Tasty brand. Through this network, the company is able to supply goods to over 4,500 distributors and 12,000 retailers. Another subsidiary of Emami is Starmark, which owns a chain of seven retail stores in Kolkata and Chennai. These retail stores sell a range of books, toys, music and stationary. The sale of stationary and books is complemented by the production of newsprint, writing and printing paper by another subsidiary, Emami Paper Mills Ltd. Emami Paper Mills manufacturers these products from waste paper in two plants, one in Orissa and the other in Kolkata.

Deichmann Group is a German shoe manufacturer and retailer founded in 1913 by Heinreich Deichmann. The company was established in Essen, North Rhine Westphalia, where the headquarters are still located. Currently, Deichmann Group has around 3,600 stores across 23 European countries and the USA; 1,360 stores are in Germany and over 80 in the UK. Deichmann Group is the top shoe retail company in Europe and sold around 172 million pairs of shoes worldwide in 2014. The company aims to produce fashionable shoes at affordable prices and sells shoes for men, women and children as well as accessories, including bags. The company stocks many of their own brands such as Graceland and 5th Avenue but also has collaborations with other brands, particularly in the children's sector, for example with Hello Kitty, Disney and Peppa Pig. In addition, Deichmann stores stock sports shoes from other brands, including Adidas, Fila and Pumav.
Deichmann Group began opening stores in European countries other than Germany during the early 1990s, including in the UK in 2001 and most recently in Russia in 2014. Acquisitions have also assisted brand development. In 2002, Deichmann Group bought the US chain Off Broadway Shoes, which has over 75 stores across the US, and the company has owned Rack Room Shoes since 1984. The company continues to expand its retail presence in Germany, with the planned opening of 66 new stores in the country during 2015 alongside 150 new retail branches internationally.

Emami Ltd. was founded in 1974 and is a leading personal and healthcare business headquartered in India. Through its subsidiaries it has a presence in a numerous markets and in various segments of the supply chain. One of its subsidiaries, Emami Biotech Ltd., is a key trader and processor of a range of raw materials, including oil palm, soybeans and jatropha. Emami Biotech has been central to the growth of India's capability in the biodiesel market, with the installation of the largest biodiesel plant in eastern India at Haldia. This plant has recently been upgraded so that it can process 2,000 tonnes of soybean and palm oil per day. This complements another refinery in Andhra Pradesh which adds a further 1,200 tonnes per day for the production of palm and sunflower oils. To further fill Emami's down-market needs, Emami Biotech imports a large amount of raw product into India, with over 4% of the total Indian market share in crude palm oil imports.
In terms of upstream activities, Emani Biotech owns a plantation in Ethiopia for the production of edible and non-edible oils and is looking to purchase plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia. In recent years, Emami Biotech has invested in the development of its marketing network to distribute its products under its Healthy and Tasty brand. Through this network, the company is able to supply goods to over 4,500 distributors and 12,000 retailers. Another subsidiary of Emami is Starmark, which owns a chain of seven retail stores in Kolkata and Chennai. These retail stores sell a range of books, toys, music and stationary. The sale of stationary and books is complemented by the production of newsprint, writing and printing paper by another subsidiary, Emami Paper Mills Ltd. Emami Paper Mills manufacturers these products from waste paper in two plants, one in Orissa and the other in Kolkata.

Deichmann Group is a German shoe manufacturer and retailer founded in 1913 by Heinreich Deichmann. The company was established in Essen, North Rhine Westphalia, where the headquarters are still located. Currently, Deichmann Group has around 3,600 stores across 23 European countries and the USA; 1,360 stores are in Germany and over 80 in the UK. Deichmann Group is the top shoe retail company in Europe and sold around 172 million pairs of shoes worldwide in 2014. The company aims to produce fashionable shoes at affordable prices and sells shoes for men, women and children as well as accessories, including bags. The company stocks many of their own brands such as Graceland and 5th Avenue but also has collaborations with other brands, particularly in the children's sector, for example with Hello Kitty, Disney and Peppa Pig. In addition, Deichmann stores stock sports shoes from other brands, including Adidas, Fila and Pumav.
Deichmann Group began opening stores in European countries other than Germany during the early 1990s, including in the UK in 2001 and most recently in Russia in 2014. Acquisitions have also assisted brand development. In 2002, Deichmann Group bought the US chain Off Broadway Shoes, which has over 75 stores across the US, and the company has owned Rack Room Shoes since 1984. The company continues to expand its retail presence in Germany, with the planned opening of 66 new stores in the country during 2015 alongside 150 new retail branches internationally.

Rimbunan Hijau Group (RH Group) is among Malaysia's largest conglomerates. The group operates in a variety of sectors including forestry, oil palm, media, information communication technologies and hospitality, and also holds diverse business interests, such as aquaculture and mining. RH Group's operations are found internationally, including in Cambodia, China, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Korea, Malaysia, Myanmar, Papua New Guinea, Singapore and the US. The group is complex in structure, with numerous publicly-listed and privately-held subsidiaries operating under various holding companies.
RH Group is a key player in the international timber industry, involved in forestry and the processing and manufacturing of timber products. It is one of the two largest forestry enterprises in Malaysia, where it has extensive concessions in Sarawak of over 1 million hectares. These include the concessions of subsidiary Jaya Tiasa Holdings Berhad, which comprises about 12% of Sarawak's production forest. It also claims to be the largest veneer and plywood manufacturer in the country, accounting for 10% of total production.
RH Group is also involved in timber processing in Africa, China, Papua New Guinea, and outside of the tropics in Russia and New Zealand. In Gabon, RH Group manages the largest forestry enterprise, with a total area of over 900,000 hectares. The group also plays a central role in timber trade between Africa and China. For example, it has been reported that almost all timber from the Republic of Congo is exported through RH Group , with the majority destined for the Chinese market.
Under Rimbunan Hijau (PNG) Limited, RH Group dominates the forestry industry in Papua New Guinea (PNG), where it is responsible for about one third of all PNG's log exports. RH Group has timber processing and manufacturing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer and plywood, primarily for the export market. The group also owns one of PNG's two major newspapers: The National, and is one of the country's largest employers in the private sector.
RH Group is also active in the palm oil sector. Its subsidiary, investment holding company Rimbunan Sawit Berhad (RSB) is a key player in the industry in Sarawak and has several subsidiaries with plantation and processing operations. RSB has around 93,500 hectares of plantations in Sarawak and one mill, with a second expected to be commissioned in 2015. Further to this, RH Group has about 31,000 hectares allocated for oil palm development in East New Britain in PNG.

Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company specialising in dairy products, including milk powder and nutrition products, cheese, liquid milk, fats and chilled dairy goods. The company, originally known as Societe Laitiere Besnier, was established in 1939 and changed its name to Groupe Lactalis S.A. in 1999. Visible in 150 countries and with on the ground operations in 70 countries (as of 2011), Lactalis has grown to have a global presence and ranks itself the world's leading dairy group. The company employs around 61,000 people and operates a total of 200 industrial plants.  The majority of its operations are in Europe, where it employs almost 40,000 people, however it is active worldwide, with operations in America, Africa and Asia/Oceania.  In September 2014, the Group, through its Parmalat subsidiary, agreed to buy the dairy units of Brazilian food company BRF, and has also agreed to buy units of Brazilian dairy company, LBR-Lacteos (which previously held license to use the Parmalat brand name in Brazil).
The group's branded products include President cheese, Rachel's yoghurt, Roquefort Socieite and Munch Bunch. It also has a long history with Nestle and took over a subsidiary, Claudel Roustang, in 1985. In 2006 Groupe Lactalis and Nestle created a subsidiary, Lactalis Nestle, which deals with Nestle's fresh dairy produce and owns yoghurt brands, Munch Bunch and Ski, in the UK. In addition to its recognisable dairy brands, Groupe Lactalis also provides ingredients for industry, including whey products, lactose and milk powder, to be used in the manufacture of products such as ice-cream, ready meals and confectionery.
Groupe Lactalis also uses palm oil in some of its products. For example, its Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division, produces butters, creams and margarines, some of which contain palm oil, as do the products of the Lactalis Nutrition Sante division. The Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division does not currently measure how much palm oil it uses but it plans to start sourcing RSPO-certified oil palm products in 2015 and to be using 100% RSPO-certified oil palm by 2018 (on own-brand products). Bank Central Asia (BCA) is a banking group based in Indonesia serving private and corporate clients. Their services include consumer and corporate financing, settlements, securities, insurance and a variety of retail banking services. As of 2017, BCA's total assets amount to more than 700 trillion IDR with more than 100 trillion IDR worth of securities. BCA are a top financier in Indonesia, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.

New York Life Insurance are a mutual based in the US offering a range of financial solutions. Offerings include life insurance, annuities, mutual funds and workplace insurance schemes. As of 2017, New York Life Insurance's total consolidated assets amount to more than 280 billion USD and they had more than 170 billion USD worth of bonds. New York Life Insurance are among the top 10 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 3 billion USD worth of bonds across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Nomura Partners Funds are a financial services group headquartered in Japan serving private, corporate, government and institutional clients. Their services include retail, asset management, global markets and investment banking. As of 2017, Nomura Partners Funds' total assets amount to over 42 trillion Yen with over 3 trillion Yen in loans. They are among the top 15 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with loans amounting to more than 13 billion USD across a broad range of forest risk sectors. They are also an important shareholder in Forest 500 companies, ranking among the top 60 with shares worth over 6 billion USD.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company specialising in dairy products, including milk powder and nutrition products, cheese, liquid milk, fats and chilled dairy goods. The company, originally known as Societe Laitiere Besnier, was established in 1939 and changed its name to Groupe Lactalis S.A. in 1999. Visible in 150 countries and with on the ground operations in 70 countries (as of 2011), Lactalis has grown to have a global presence and ranks itself the world's leading dairy group. The company employs around 61,000 people and operates a total of 200 industrial plants.  The majority of its operations are in Europe, where it employs almost 40,000 people, however it is active worldwide, with operations in America, Africa and Asia/Oceania.  In September 2014, the Group, through its Parmalat subsidiary, agreed to buy the dairy units of Brazilian food company BRF, and has also agreed to buy units of Brazilian dairy company, LBR-Lacteos (which previously held license to use the Parmalat brand name in Brazil).
The group's branded products include President cheese, Rachel's yoghurt, Roquefort Socieite and Munch Bunch. It also has a long history with Nestle and took over a subsidiary, Claudel Roustang, in 1985. In 2006 Groupe Lactalis and Nestle created a subsidiary, Lactalis Nestle, which deals with Nestle's fresh dairy produce and owns yoghurt brands, Munch Bunch and Ski, in the UK. New Hope Group is one of the largest agribusiness enterprises in China. The company started in 1982 when founder, Liu Yonghao, and his three brothers left their jobs and sold their bicycles and watches to raise money to buy poultry.

Both the feed sales volume and meat processing volume were ranked No. 1 in China.

A high proportion of timber in China is consumed in the industrial and construction sector, which accounted for over 75% of total wood consumption in 2010. Shanghai Construction Group ranks as the second largest construction firm in China in terms of market share and as well as playing a key role in China's domestic construction industry, the group is active overseas, having completed more than 100 projects in 30 different countries and regions worldwide. In 2013, the group's overseas activities contributed over 15% to its total revenue. It is comprised of a number of subsidiaries and business departments. It has 17 subsidiaries involved in construction, engineering, real estate and landscaping, and 13 supporting business departments. The group also provides engineering and renovation services and has further business interests, for example in trading through its import and export operations. Shanghai Construction Group is a state-owned enterprise, whose majority shareholder is the Shanghai Municipal Government.
The group as a whole has been active in the Chinese construction sector for over fifty years. Shanghai Construction Group's subsidiary, Shanghai Construction Co Ltd, is involved exclusively in construction. It was established in 1994 and was listed on Shanghai stock exchange in 1998. The company is engaged in contracting, designing and constructing a variety of projects; including the development of residential, industrial, and municipal buildings, and public infrastructure facilities.
China's affordable housing programme aims for the construction of 36 million units of affordable housing in the five years leading up to 2015, as part of the country's 12th five-year plan. It is expected that the government's housing plan will drive increasing consumption and imports of wood products. Shanghai Construction Group has previously been involved in this programme, for example with the Sanlin Affordable Housing Development.

Ting Hsin is a Taiwanese based company that is predominantly active in the production and distribution of food and beverage products. Products include instant noodles, baked goods, and soft drinks, and its Master Kong brand is well-known in China. Alongside its manufacturing, the company also has an extensive sales network in China with more than 100,000 retail outlets as of 2013, as well as distributing products globally. Ting Hsin isone of the five largest packaged food companies in China.

JVL Agro Industries Ltd (JVL), formally Jhunjhunwala Vanaspati Limited, is an Indian edible oil manufacturer. The company was incorporated in 1989, and was established initially in Northern India as a manufacturer of hydrogenated vegetable oils and refined oils, with the capacity to produce around 25 tonnes per day. The company has since grown to be the largest vegetable oil manufacturer in the country, with four plants producing 300 tonnes a day, with products including palm oil and soya bean oil.
The company's mid- and downstream activities require a large amount of raw material, therefore JVL are responsible for around 5% of India's total crude palm oil imports. JVL is also taking steps to acquire new land in Indonesia and Ethiopia for the production of palm oil and, as of 2013, had signed an agreement for the use of 12,500 acres of land in Ethiopia, with the potential of extending this to 62,000 acres.
JVL has a number of brands under which products are distributed to the consumer market across 18 Indian states. For example, refined soya bean oil is sold under the Jhoola health brand, while blended oils are sold under the Joohi active brand. JVL are working towards the development of rapid revenue growth partly by diversifying into new markets. For example, in 2012, they began to market bakery products, and in 2013-14 were set to commission a rice mill in Bihar with a production capacity of 12 metric tonnes per hour.

It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand.
