In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.

Domino's Pizza Inc. is a US pizza delivery and carry-out company serving the US and over 75 international markets. Worldwide, there are 11,700 stores that deliver over 1 million pizzas every day. Over 90% of stores are franchised, while Domino's Pizza Inc. owns around 377 stores in the US. It also runs dough manufacturing facilities and supply chain centres to supply stores in the US and in some overseas markets.  The US is Domino's Pizza Inc.'s single biggest market with 5,084 stores in Q1 2015, but over half of the company's sales come from outside the US. Domino's Pizza Inc. is the world's second biggest fast food pizza retailer. In addition to pizza, the company offers related products including sandwiches, chicken, salads, sauces, drinks and desserts. Beef is used as a pizza topping, soya is used in pizzas, and both soya and palm oil are used in side dishes and desserts.

The Japan Agricultural Cooperatives Group (JA Group) is an agricultural cooperative, established to support its members by selling their products rather than each of its members selling products independently. On top of this, JA Group provides its members with production materials and agrochemicals. The group is a politically powerful organisation and is comprised of almost ten million regular and associate members. 
The JA Group is made up of several constituent parts, including ZEN-NOH, which is the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations. ZEN-NOH manages the business and distribution operations of the JA Group and is responsible for the marketing and supply business side of the group. Of particular relevance, are ZEN-NOH's operations in the animal feed sector. Of the total 24 to 25 million tonnes of compound feed used per year in Japan, ZEN-NOH handles around 30%, making ZEN-NOH Japan's largest compound feed producer and one of the top ten in the world. Through its subsidiaries, ZEN-NOH imports large volumes of soya from overseas producers including Brazil, India and China for use in compound animal feeds.
Also of relevance, is the group's Daily Necessities business unit, through which ZEN-NOH and JA run around 800 A-Coop supermarkets. The stores sell clothing, food products and consumer durables, and prioritise goods produced by members and sell A-Coop branded goods. Currently there are around 1,300 A-Coop branded goods, which include packaged food and clothing.

Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of America's largest cooperatives, employing 9,000 people and with 3,200 producer-members and 1,000 member-cooperatives serving over 300,000 agricultural producers. In 2013 it had annual sales of $14.2 billion, and it ranks #194 on the Fortune 500. The company has four business segments: dairy foods, crop inputs, animal feed and business services. Dairy foods products are provided by its Dairy Foods and Kozy Shack businesses. Crop inputs are provided by its Winfield Solutions business, and its animal feeds are provided by its Purina Animal Nutrition LLC, Land O'Lakes Feed LLC and Purina Mills LLC businesses.
Dairy Foods sells mainly butter and cheese, under the under the Land O Lakes and Alpine Lace brands. It claims to produce America's #1 brand of butter and deli american cheese. The Land O Lakes brand is also licensed to a small number of partner companies who produce milk, creams, juices, eggs, cottage cheese, sour cream, yogurt and cocoa mixes, such as the WhiteWaves Food Company. Kozy Shack, acquired in 2012, produces chilled desserts such as rice pudding, tapioca pudding and flans and claims to be America's #1 brand of tapioca and rice pudding.
Purina Animal Nutrition LLC provides supplements, ingredients, complete feeds and speciality technologies to farmers and the consumer (pet) markets via several thousand local cooperatives, independent dealers and other retailers in the US. The company is heavily involved in research and development and has over 100 patents worldwide. Land O'Lakes Inc. animal feed production began with feed for mules and horses in 1894, and today its feed products are produced for an extremely broad range of animals from farm animals, during multiple lifecycle stages, to fish, pets and exotic animals. Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers and therefore purchases large quantities of soya, some of which is used in animal feed production,. As some animal feeds also use palm oil, Land O'Lakes Inc. may also source palm oil for use as an ingredient.
Land O'Lakes Inc. is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil or the Roundtable on Responsible Soy.

Both the feed sales volume and meat processing volume were ranked No. 1 in China.

Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

Nong Shim Holdings Co., Ltd. is a South Korean investment holding company. Through its subsidiaries, it operates in the food and beverage industry. Subsidiaries include NongShim Co Ltd which manufactures and markets instant noodles and snacks as well as producing refined palm oil ingredients; Youlchon Chemical Co. Ltd. which is engaged in packaging material manufacturing; and Tae Kyung Nong San Co. Ltd., engaged in the processing of agricultural and seafood products.

Cresud SA is an agricultural company based in Argentina, involved in the production of crops, and beef and dairy cattle. As of June 2013, the company has a beef cattle stock of over 60,000 heads, which are primarily destined for the domestic Argentine market and not for export. Crop production includes soya, corn, sunflower and wheat. Soya accounts for over half of the company's total crop production, with 220,000 tons produced in 2013. Almost half of this soya was produced in Brazil, with a large amount also produced in Argentina.
Cresud SA owns almost 1 million hectares of its own land and nearly 50,000 hectares of land under lease agreements. Of this land more than 400,000 hectares is currently productive, with a further 135,000 hectares under development. Although largely based in Argentina, since 2005 the company has been expanding into other Latin American countries including Brazil, Paraguay and Bolivia. Currently, 66% of the company's land area is in Argentina, 19% in Brazil, 13% in Paraguay and 2% in Bolivia.

Established in 1968, NICE Group is the largest soap and detergent manufacturer in China; it also produces dishwasher soap and toothpaste. It's best known brand is the detergent, DIAO; further brands include Supra, Soling, 100 Years Hare Care and Lizi. Since 1994, the group's sales of laundry powder, soap and liquid detergent have been number one in China; and in 2005, NICE Group ranked in the top 8 worldwide. Each year the company produces 1 million tonnes of washing powder, 540,000 tonnes of liquid detergent, 280,000 tonnes of soap bars, 20,000 tonnes of industrial glycerine and 400 million tubes of toothpaste.  The Group has over 10,000 employees, operates 10 brands, and has more than 50 sales branches and 3 overseas subsidiaries. The Group's products are sold in China, the Middle East, Africa, Oceania, Europe and the US.

New Hope Group is one of the largest agribusiness enterprises in China. The company started in 1982 when founder, Liu Yonghao, and his three brothers left their jobs and sold their bicycles and watches to raise money to buy poultry.
The group is involved in four main sectors: Chemicals and Resources, which has operations and interests in potassium, nickel, coal, phosphorous (including for use in animal feeds) and PVC production; Finance and Investment, which has investments in commercial banks, life insurers, investment companies and funds; Real Estate and Infrastructure; and Agribusiness and Food. Agribusiness and Food is the group's most significant area; it has operations throughout the supply chain, including animal breeding, feed production, dairy, technology services, abattoirs and meat processing. New Hope Group is one of the largest suppliers of poultry, eggs, pork and dairy products in China. Through subsidiaries such as New Hope Liuhe Co Ltd it is also one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers. It has 184 feed mills, based in China and other markets including Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia and the Philippines. The mills are capable of producing 26.6 million tonnes of feed annually, with sales of 12 million tonnes.
Based in Qingdao, China and founded in 1995, New Hope Liuhe Co Ltd (Liuhe) is the listed company of New Hope Group. The company is engaged in animal feed manufacturing, meat processing and cooking, livestock and poultry breeding, importing and exporting trade, animal production and financial guarantee. It currently owns more than 265 subsidiary companies nationwide with a total employee number exceeding 50,000 persons. In 2009, Liuhe produced 10.1 million metric tons of animal feed, processed 1.25 million metric tons of poultry meat and hatched 216 million day-old poults with total sales revenue of 40.2 billion RMB Yuan. Both the feed sales volume and meat processing volume were ranked No. 1 in China.

Yue Yuen Industrial Holdings Ltd (Yue Yuen), a subsidiary of Pou Chen Group, is a publicly listed investment holding company with its headquarters in Taiwan. Through its subsidiaries, Yueyuen engages in the manufacture, marketing, distribution and sale of footwear. It is one of the world's top five footwear manufacturers.
Its products consist mainly of athletic and casual footwear, for international brands such as Nike, Adidas, Reebok and Timberland. Yueyuen's retailing segment sells sportswear products under some of these brands within China, through its subsidiary Pou Sheng International. It has about 3,665 counters and stores throughout the Greater China region.
The company's factories are located in China, Indonesia and other parts of Asia, as well as Mexico, the US and Vietnam.

Lenta is a major Russian retail chain operating approximately 200 hypermarkets and supermarkets across Russia in major cities. The company operates as a low-price/low-cost retailer and is seeking to expand its Russian footprint. The breadth of its retail offerings expose the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. It is one of the largest Russian retailers by edible grocery retail market share and has links to beef produced in Brazil and Argentina.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company specialising in dairy products, including milk powder and nutrition products, cheese, liquid milk, fats and chilled dairy goods. The company, originally known as Societe Laitiere Besnier, was established in 1939 and changed its name to Groupe Lactalis S.A. in 1999. Visible in 150 countries and with on the ground operations in 70 countries (as of 2011), Lactalis has grown to have a global presence and ranks itself the world's leading dairy group. The company employs around 61,000 people and operates a total of 200 industrial plants.  The majority of its operations are in Europe, where it employs almost 40,000 people, however it is active worldwide, with operations in America, Africa and Asia/Oceania.  In September 2014, the Group, through its Parmalat subsidiary, agreed to buy the dairy units of Brazilian food company BRF, and has also agreed to buy units of Brazilian dairy company, LBR-Lacteos (which previously held license to use the Parmalat brand name in Brazil).
The group's branded products include President cheese, Rachel's yoghurt, Roquefort Socieite and Munch Bunch. It also has a long history with Nestle and took over a subsidiary, Claudel Roustang, in 1985. In 2006 Groupe Lactalis and Nestle created a subsidiary, Lactalis Nestle, which deals with Nestle's fresh dairy produce and owns yoghurt brands, Munch Bunch and Ski, in the UK. In addition to its recognisable dairy brands, Groupe Lactalis also provides ingredients for industry, including whey products, lactose and milk powder, to be used in the manufacture of products such as ice-cream, ready meals and confectionery.
Groupe Lactalis also uses palm oil in some of its products. For example, its Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division, produces butters, creams and margarines, some of which contain palm oil, as do the products of the Lactalis Nutrition Sante division. The Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division does not currently measure how much palm oil it uses but it plans to start sourcing RSPO-certified oil palm products in 2015 and to be using 100% RSPO-certified oil palm by 2018 (on own-brand products). Further to this, some of Groupe Lactalis products also contain soya.

Gruppo Mastrotto is an Italian based processor and manufacturer of leather for use in products such as footwear, upholstery and other leather goods. Most the group's operations are in Italy, making it a major importer of leather, and it also has operations in Brazil, Tunisia and Indonesia. The Brazilian facility alone has an annual production capacity of 7 million square metres of leather from bovine hide.

Hayel Saeed Anam Group is a Yemen-based company with a substantial portfolio of businesses operating in a diverse range of sectors. Founded in 1938, it employs over 35,000 people across a number of sectors such as manufacturing; trading and ï¬nancial services; oil and gas exploration; print and packaging; agriculture; ï¬sheries; real estate; and mining. In addition to its core business activities in Yemen, the group operates as a manufacturing firm and trading company across four global regions: Africa; Asia; Europe; and the Middle East. Its global business focuses on non-food, and beverage and food products such as confectionery and biscuits. It has an extensive logistics infrastructure to manufacture and distribute its own and partners' products across its global markets.
Pacific Inter-Link (PIL), one of the group's Malaysia-based companies, is involved in the processing and trading of palm oil. It was incorporated in 1988 to export commodities and employs 1,750 people in Malaysia and Indonesia. Its refineries had an annual processing capacity of 1.3 million tonnes per annum in 2012. PIL is one of the major exporters of palm oil from Asia to Africa and the Middle East, exporting to around 64 countries in total. The company is currently looking to expand further into the African market, with the development of new refineries in Ethiopia and Kenya. The company's brands include Avena and Madina, which both sell various palm oil products, such as margarine, shortening, cooking oil, and vegetable ghee, as well as a range of packaged food, including canned fish and meat, and pasta products. On top of its core palm oil products, the group also supplies dairy products under the Milgro, Milac, and Sheeba brands.

Calbee is a Japanese snack and cereal company that has overseas sales and operations in ten countries. It is a major sweet and savoury snack company. Major markets include Hong Kong, South Korea, and the US, and its products include a wide variety of potato and other vegetable crisps. In Hong Kong and China, it is one of the largest such companies by market share and it is one of the five largest in the world.

It is especially prominent in Argentina where it ranks among the top three retailers for edible groceries.

CIMB Group are a Southeast Asian banking group headquartered in Malaysia serving private and commercial clients. Their services include corporate finance, treasury markets, investment banking, insurance, wealth management and retail banking. As of 2017, the group's total assets amount to more than 500 billion MYR, with more than 310 billion MYR in loans, advances and financing. CIMB Group are one of the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 4 billion USD worth of loans to companies predominantly in the agriculture and agricultural commodity sectors.

Blackrock are an asset management firm headquartered in the US serving private, corporate, institutional, governmental, and intermediary clients. Their services span equities and fixed income investments, mutual funds, collective investment funds, risk analytics, advisory and technology services, and wealth management. As of 2017, Blackrock's total assets under management stand at over 5.9 trillion USD. They are the largest shareholder for Forest 500 companies with over 167 billion USD worth of shares. Blackrock are also among the top 5 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with over 6 billion USD worth of bonds across a range of forest risk sectors.

Pictet Funds are an international asset management company headquartered in Switzerland that serves private, sovereign and institutional clients. Their services cover wealth management, private banking, asset management and asset related services. As of 2017, their total assets amount to more than 38 billion CHF, with more than 460 billion CHF in assets under management. Pictet Funds are among the top 80 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with nearly 5 billion USD worth of shares.

Aberdeen Asset management are a global asset management company headquartered in the UK, serving private and institutional clients and external investment advisors. Their services cover equities, fixed income, quantitative, property and hedge fund investments. As of 2017, Aberdeen Asset Management have over 395 billion USD in assets under management. They are also among the top 50 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 8 billion USD worth of shares.

Lear Corp. is an automotive seating producer and distributor headquartered in Michigan, USA, employing more than 110,000 people. The key subsidiary of relevance to forest risk commodities owned by Lear Corp. is Eagle Ottawa, which produces leather upholstery products for the automotive industry. Eagle Ottawa was founded in 1865 and was formerly known as Eagle Tanning Works but changed its name to Eagle Ottawa, LLC in 1916.
 
Eagle Ottawa claims to be the largest supplier of premium automotive leather and produces a variety of leather products, including finished hides, cut leather, natural shrunken grain leather, and chrome- and non-chrome-tanned leather.  As well as these, it also produces leather for other interior uses, such as for door panels and instrument panels. The company engages in various activities in leather processing including pre-tanning and tanning as well as cutting and finishing. Aside from the subsidiary's headquarters, which are in the state of Michigan, in the US, Eagle Ottawa also has facilities in Mexico, Brazil, Hungary, China, South Korea and Thailand. It also has sales and design locations in China, Japan, Brazil, Germany, England, Sweden and Italy, as well as the US. The company's customers include some of the automobile industry's biggest players, including Mercedes, BMW, Toyota, Renault Chrysler, GMC and Volkswagen.

China Resources (CR) is a diversified business group with its main business in consumer products, energy, and pharmaceuticals as well as being involved in retail, chemicals, and textiles, amongst other industries. Food products include rice, meat, and frozen foods. The group's retail chain, CR Vanguard, is also one of the largest retail chains in China. It is one of the largest retailers in China by edible grocery sales and one of the largest in the Asia-Pacific region overall.
Grupo Viz is a Mexican meat processor. The company also operates in the business of leather accessories, and bioorganic and pet food products.

China State Construction Engineering Corp. (CSCEC) is a state-owned corporation involved in housing and infrastructure construction, as well as real estate development and international contracting. It is one of China's largest construction and real estate companies, but also operates globally in 20 countries and is one of the leading construction companies globally. Housing construction is a very timber heavy industry and CSCEC has a dominant market share. Housing construction also comprises the majority of their contracts by value.

A high proportion of timber in China is consumed in the industrial and construction sector, which accounted for over 75% of total wood consumption in 2010. Shanghai Construction Group ranks as the second largest construction firm in China in terms of market share and as well as playing a key role in China's domestic construction industry, the group is active overseas, having completed more than 100 projects in 30 different countries and regions worldwide. In 2013, the group's overseas activities contributed over 15% to its total revenue. It is comprised of a number of subsidiaries and business departments. It has 17 subsidiaries involved in construction, engineering, real estate and landscaping, and 13 supporting business departments. The group also provides engineering and renovation services and has further business interests, for example in trading through its import and export operations. Shanghai Construction Group is a state-owned enterprise, whose majority shareholder is the Shanghai Municipal Government.
The group as a whole has been active in the Chinese construction sector for over fifty years. Shanghai Construction Group's subsidiary, Shanghai Construction Co Ltd, is involved exclusively in construction. It was established in 1994 and was listed on Shanghai stock exchange in 1998. The company is engaged in contracting, designing and constructing a variety of projects; including the development of residential, industrial, and municipal buildings, and public infrastructure facilities.
China's affordable housing programme aims for the construction of 36 million units of affordable housing in the five years leading up to 2015, as part of the country's 12th five-year plan. It is expected that the government's housing plan will drive increasing consumption and imports of wood products. Shanghai Construction Group has previously been involved in this programme, for example with the Sanlin Affordable Housing Development.

JVL Agro Industries Ltd (JVL), formally Jhunjhunwala Vanaspati Limited, is an Indian edible oil manufacturer. The company was incorporated in 1989, and was established initially in Northern India as a manufacturer of hydrogenated vegetable oils and refined oils, with the capacity to produce around 25 tonnes per day. The company has since grown to be the largest vegetable oil manufacturer in the country, with four plants producing 300 tonnes a day, with products including palm oil and soya bean oil.
The company's mid- and downstream activities require a large amount of raw material, therefore JVL are responsible for around 5% of India's total crude palm oil imports. JVL is also taking steps to acquire new land in Indonesia and Ethiopia for the production of palm oil and, as of 2013, had signed an agreement for the use of 12,500 acres of land in Ethiopia, with the potential of extending this to 62,000 acres.
JVL has a number of brands under which products are distributed to the consumer market across 18 Indian states. For example, refined soya bean oil is sold under the Jhoola health brand, while blended oils are sold under the Joohi active brand. JVL are working towards the development of rapid revenue growth partly by diversifying into new markets. For example, in 2012, they began to market bakery products, and in 2013-14 were set to commission a rice mill in Bihar with a production capacity of 12 metric tonnes per hour.

The company's factories are located in China, Indonesia and other parts of Asia, as well as Mexico, the US and Vietnam.
initiatives: Listed on CDP, but no response to any reports. No other info on website.

Toyo Suisan Kaisha Ltd (Toyo) is an international food producer specialising in ramen noodles and seafood. Toyo manufactures its products through various sub-divisions, such as the Domestic Instant Noodles segment and the Frozen and Refrigerated Foods segment. In addition to noodles, it also produces wontons, soup products, fish, ham, sausages and seasonings. It also has a Prepared Food section which manufactures sterile packaged rice, retort rice, soup and other products.
The company was founded in 1953, has its headquarters in Tokyo, and employs around 4,600 people. Its main overseas operations are in Mexico and the Us through its Overseas Instant Noodles Division, which sells noodles under the brand name Maruchan Inc. As of 2008, Toyo owns three food processing facilities in the US and has 32 subsidiaries.
By the 1970s, Toyo had become well-known in Japan and had branched out internationally. It is now the largest noodle company in the US, the second largest in Japan and third largest in the world. It is also in the top five companies in Japan for dried processed food and chilled processed food, and in the top 30 largest soup companies worldwide.
The company does not appear to be a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm oil and in 2013 was implicated by the Rainforest Action Network to be one of the 'Snack Food 20' responsible for using 'conflict' palm oil from unsustainable sources,.
State Bank of India is a commercial bank providing services to individuals, corporations, institutions, commercial enterprises and the agricultural sector.

Cencosud is a Chilean retail conglomerate with operations throughout Latin America. Its sales outlets include supermarkets, home improvement stores, shopping centres and department stores. The breadth of its retail market means it is exposed to several forest risk commodities. Cencosud is the one of the five largest retailers for edible groceries in Latin America. It is especially prominent in Argentina where it ranks among the top three retailers for edible groceries.
YPF are an energy company whose headquarters are in Argentina, and refine and distribute bio-fuels.

Lenta is a major Russian retail chain operating approximately 200 hypermarkets and supermarkets across Russia in major cities. The company operates as a low-price/low-cost retailer and is seeking to expand its Russian footprint. The breadth of its retail offerings expose the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. It is one of the largest Russian retailers by edible grocery retail market share and has links to beef produced in Brazil and Argentina.

The Japan Agricultural Cooperatives Group (JA Group) is an agricultural cooperative, established to support its members by selling their products rather than each of its members selling products independently. On top of this, JA Group provides its members with production materials and agrochemicals. The group is a politically powerful organisation and is comprised of almost ten million regular and associate members. 
The JA Group is made up of several constituent parts, including ZEN-NOH, which is the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations. ZEN-NOH manages the business and distribution operations of the JA Group and is responsible for the marketing and supply business side of the group. Of particular relevance, are ZEN-NOH's operations in the animal feed sector. Of the total 24 to 25 million tonnes of compound feed used per year in Japan, ZEN-NOH handles around 30%, making ZEN-NOH Japan's largest compound feed producer and one of the top ten in the world. Through its subsidiaries, ZEN-NOH imports large volumes of soya from overseas producers including Brazil, India and China for use in compound animal feeds.
Also of relevance, is the group's Daily Necessities business unit, through which ZEN-NOH and JA run around 800 A-Coop supermarkets. The stores sell clothing, food products and consumer durables, and prioritise goods produced by members and sell A-Coop branded goods. Currently there are around 1,300 A-Coop branded goods, which include packaged food and clothing.
initiatives: Not listed on CDP or RSPO. No other info on website.

rows.coprofile: Norinchukin Bank are a financial institution with headquarters in Japan founded by Japanese agriculture, forestry and fishery cooperatives. Enshrined in law, Norinchukin Bank's services include deposit services, securities, corporate finance, investments and debentures for companies related to agriculture, forestry and fishery. As of March 2017, their total assets amount to over 980 billion USD with more than 100 billion USD of loans and bills discounted. Norinchukin Bank are one of the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 4 billion USD worth of loans to companies across the agricultural, forestry, construction and packaged food sectors.

The Beidahuang Group is China's largest agricultural and agribusiness group. It is involved in a variety of business, such as pharmaceuticals, food products, oils, and agriculture. The group's soya subsidiary has an annual processing capacity of 10 million metric tons which the company claims makes it the largest processor of soya in China. This is turned into meal and oil for food products and edible oils. It is also a leading importer of Brazilian soya. In 2014, it imported over 8 million metric tons of soya, accounting for almost 15% of Chinese imports.

Belle International Holdings is a Chinese business primarily involved in the manufacturing and retail of footwear and apparel. It owns several brands including Belle, Staccato, and Tata, and manufactures shoes for other brands including Clarks and Mephisto. Its apparel business is focussed on retail distribution, including with brands such as Nike, Adidas, and Puma. It is one of the largest global footwear manufacturers and is also one of the largest Chinese shoe stores.

Bright Food Group (Bright Food) is a Chinese food industry group involved in agriculture, food processing, and manufacturing, as well as retailing. It is involved in diverse business areas, but its main food businesses include packaged foods, dairy, sugar and vegetables. The group is a major player in China ranking highly in several categories, including dairy and packaged foods. It is also a global player, ranking among the top ten in the world for dairy and the top twenty for packaged foods.

X5 Retail Group NV is a Russian food retailer, with retail operations in four different formats and brands: Economy stores under the Pyaterochka brand (4,789 stores); supermarkets under the Perekrestok brand (403 stores); hypermarkets under the Karusel brand (82 stores); convenience stores under a range of different brand names (209 stores); and an online retail channel under the E5.ru brand. The company has its origins in 1995, when the Perekrestok supermarket brand was established. The chain of Pyaterochka stores was launched a few years later in 1999, and in 2006 these two brands merged and adopted the X5 Retail Group NV name.
X5 Retail Group's Pyaterochka economy convenience stores provide over 69% of the group's total revenue in 2014 . The Group has been steadily increasing its marketing of private label products and, through its various retail formats, offers a wide range of products, including dairy products, canned goods and groceries, confectionery and bakery products, and fresh and processed meat, among others.

It produces and markets womenÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s shoes under its own brands, which include ST&SAT, FONDBERYL, SAFIYA, IIXVIIX, GAVAKLAS and D:FUSE, and acts as the agent in China for the Italian Killah and Stonefly footwear brands . It also has one subsidiary, also in China, which designs, produces and sells leather shoes and other leather products. The company operates has a design and development centre, a manufacturing centre, 13 regional marketing centres, 30 liaison offices, and over 250 stores across China.

The company operates as a low-price/low-cost retailer and is seeking to expand its Russian footprint. The breadth of its retail offerings expose the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. It is one of the largest Russian retailers by edible grocery retail market share and has links to beef produced in Brazil and Argentina.

Samsonite International SA is a US based luggage company involved in the design, manufacturing, marketing and sale of luggage and travel accessories. Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

Domino's Pizza Inc. is a US pizza delivery and carry-out company serving the US and over 75 international markets. Worldwide, there are 11,700 stores that deliver over 1 million pizzas every day. Over 90% of stores are franchised, while Domino's Pizza Inc. owns around 377 stores in the US. It also runs dough manufacturing facilities and supply chain centres to supply stores in the US and in some overseas markets.  The US is Domino's Pizza Inc.'s single biggest market with 5,084 stores in Q1 2015, but over half of the company's sales come from outside the US. Domino's Pizza Inc. is the world's second biggest fast food pizza retailer. In addition to pizza, the company offers related products including sandwiches, chicken, salads, sauces, drinks and desserts. Beef is used as a pizza topping, soya is used in pizzas, and both soya and palm oil are used in side dishes and desserts.

It also has one subsidiary, also in China, which designs, produces and sells leather shoes and other leather products. The company operates has a design and development centre, a manufacturing centre, 13 regional marketing centres, 30 liaison offices, and over 250 stores across China.

A high proportion of timber in China is consumed in the industrial and construction sector, which accounted for over 75% of total wood consumption in 2010. Shanghai Construction Group ranks as the second largest construction firm in China in terms of market share and as well as playing a key role in China's domestic construction industry, the group is active overseas, having completed more than 100 projects in 30 different countries and regions worldwide. In 2013, the group's overseas activities contributed over 15% to its total revenue. It is comprised of a number of subsidiaries and business departments. It has 17 subsidiaries involved in construction, engineering, real estate and landscaping, and 13 supporting business departments. The group also provides engineering and renovation services and has further business interests, for example in trading through its import and export operations. Shanghai Construction Group is a state-owned enterprise, whose majority shareholder is the Shanghai Municipal Government.
The group as a whole has been active in the Chinese construction sector for over fifty years. Shanghai Construction Group's subsidiary, Shanghai Construction Co Ltd, is involved exclusively in construction. It was established in 1994 and was listed on Shanghai stock exchange in 1998. The company is engaged in contracting, designing and constructing a variety of projects; including the development of residential, industrial, and municipal buildings, and public infrastructure facilities.
China's affordable housing programme aims for the construction of 36 million units of affordable housing in the five years leading up to 2015, as part of the country's 12th five-year plan. It is expected that the government's housing plan will drive increasing consumption and imports of wood products. Shanghai Construction Group has previously been involved in this programme, for example with the Sanlin Affordable Housing Development.

rows.coprofile: Established in 1968, NICE Group is the largest soap and detergent manufacturer in China; it also produces dishwasher soap and toothpaste. It's best known brand is the detergent, DIAO; further brands include Supra, Soling, 100 Years Hare Care and Lizi. Since 1994, the group's sales of laundry powder, soap and liquid detergent have been number one in China; and in 2005, NICE Group ranked in the top 8 worldwide. Each year the company produces 1 million tonnes of washing powder, 540,000 tonnes of liquid detergent, 280,000 tonnes of soap bars, 20,000 tonnes of industrial glycerine and 400 million tubes of toothpaste.  The Group has over 10,000 employees, operates 10 brands, and has more than 50 sales branches and 3 overseas subsidiaries. The Group's products are sold in China, the Middle East, Africa, Oceania, Europe and the US.

Ting Hsin is a Taiwanese based company that is predominantly active in the production and distribution of food and beverage products. Products include instant noodles, baked goods, and soft drinks, and its Master Kong brand is well-known in China. Alongside its manufacturing, the company also has an extensive sales network in China with more than 100,000 retail outlets as of 2013, as well as distributing products globally. Ting Hsin isone of the five largest packaged food companies in China.

JVL Agro Industries Ltd (JVL), formally Jhunjhunwala Vanaspati Limited, is an Indian edible oil manufacturer. The company was incorporated in 1989, and was established initially in Northern India as a manufacturer of hydrogenated vegetable oils and refined oils, with the capacity to produce around 25 tonnes per day. The company has since grown to be the largest vegetable oil manufacturer in the country, with four plants producing 300 tonnes a day, with products including palm oil and soya bean oil.
The company's mid- and downstream activities require a large amount of raw material, therefore JVL are responsible for around 5% of India's total crude palm oil imports. JVL is also taking steps to acquire new land in Indonesia and Ethiopia for the production of palm oil and, as of 2013, had signed an agreement for the use of 12,500 acres of land in Ethiopia, with the potential of extending this to 62,000 acres.
JVL has a number of brands under which products are distributed to the consumer market across 18 Indian states. For example, refined soya bean oil is sold under the Jhoola health brand, while blended oils are sold under the Joohi active brand. JVL are working towards the development of rapid revenue growth partly by diversifying into new markets. For example, in 2012, they began to market bakery products, and in 2013-14 were set to commission a rice mill in Bihar with a production capacity of 12 metric tonnes per hour.

Granol, headquartered in São Paulo, is one of the top three soybean crushers in Brazil and is also one of the top ten exporters from the country. The company began in 1965 as a vegetable oil producer and two years later began expansion through the acquisition other companies and plants. Now with 2,000 employees, 23 warehouses, two biodiesel production plants and five soybean processing factories, Granol is the largest producer of biodiesel (and its by-product, glycerine) from soybean in Brazil and can produce 2 million tons of soybean oil per year. It currently has approximately 7,000 clients globally.
Granol's products include: biodiesel; glycerine, which is used as an ingredient in the food and pharmaceuticals ingredient; lecithin, a biodegradable food ingredient that can act as an antioxidant or stabilizer; soybean meal, which is primarily used as animal feed; and soybean oil. Most of the company's facilities are located in southern and central Brazil.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. In 2015, the group processed and traded more than 1.6 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.

New Hope Group is one of the largest agribusiness enterprises in China. The company started in 1982 when founder, Liu Yonghao, and his three brothers left their jobs and sold their bicycles and watches to raise money to buy poultry.
The group is involved in four main sectors: Chemicals and Resources, which has operations and interests in potassium, nickel, coal, phosphorous (including for use in animal feeds) and PVC production; Finance and Investment, which has investments in commercial banks, life insurers, investment companies and funds; Real Estate and Infrastructure; and Agribusiness and Food. Agribusiness and Food is the group's most significant area; it has operations throughout the supply chain, including animal breeding, feed production, dairy, technology services, abattoirs and meat processing. New Hope Group is one of the largest suppliers of poultry, eggs, pork and dairy products in China. Through subsidiaries such as New Hope Liuhe Co Ltd it is also one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers. It has 184 feed mills, based in China and other markets including Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia and the Philippines. The mills are capable of producing 26.6 million tonnes of feed annually, with sales of 12 million tonnes.
Based in Qingdao, China and founded in 1995, New Hope Liuhe Co Ltd (Liuhe) is the listed company of New Hope Group. The company is engaged in animal feed manufacturing, meat processing and cooking, livestock and poultry breeding, importing and exporting trade, animal production and financial guarantee. It currently owns more than 265 subsidiary companies nationwide with a total employee number exceeding 50,000 persons. In 2009, Liuhe produced 10.1 million metric tons of animal feed, processed 1.25 million metric tons of poultry meat and hatched 216 million day-old poults with total sales revenue of 40.2 billion RMB Yuan. Both the feed sales volume and meat processing volume were ranked No. 1 in China.
initiatives: Not listed on CDP or RSPO, no info on website.

rows.coprofile: Gold Best Holdings is a manufacturing and trading pulp and paper company based in the British Virgin Islands. Its subsidiary, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd, operate in the business of packing paper. Gold Best Holdings is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and pulp & paper and is also assessed for its exposure to pulp & paper packaging.

Foundation to Support Research of the Northern Export Corridor (FAPCEN) was established in April 1993 as an NGO by entrepreneurs and rural producers with the aim of undertaking agricultural research and promoting sustainable development in the 'Northern Export Corridor' region i.e. the states of Maranhao, Tocantins and Piaui. The company has been selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Gruppo Mastrotto is an Italian based processor and manufacturer of leather for use in products such as footwear, upholstery and other leather goods. Most the group’s operations are in Italy, making it a major importer of leather, and it also has operations in Brazil, Tunisia and Indonesia. The Brazilian facility alone has an annual production capacity of 7 million square metres of leather from bovine hide.  Gruppo Mastrotto Spa is selected as a powerbroker for leather.
YPF is an energy company whose headquarters are in Argentina, and refine and distribute biofuels. YPF uses soy in its biofuel production.  YPF is selected as a powerbroker for soy.

Aviva is a UK-based multinational insurance company serving both individual and corporate clients. Their services include a wide range of insurance products, such as life, health, general, and asset protection, as well as retirement and investment solutions. As of 2024, Aviva have over 407 billion GBP in assets under management. In the 2024 selection, Aviva was providing 12.1 billion USD to the Forest 500 companies.
initiatives: Financial Sector Deforestation Action initiative (FSDA), Biodiversity Pledge and the Terra Carta Initiative, TNFD

rows.coprofile: Norinchukin Bank are a financial institution with headquarters in Japan founded by Japanese agriculture, forestry and fishery cooperatives. Enshrined in law, Norinchukin Bank's services include deposit services, securities, corporate finance, investments and debentures for companies related to agriculture, forestry and fishery. As of March 2017, their total assets amount to over 980 billion USD with more than 100 billion USD of loans and bills discounted. Norinchukin Bank are one of the top 55 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with more than 4 billion USD worth of loans to companies across the agricultural, forestry, construction and packaged food sectors.

Bank of New York Mellon Corp. are a financial services provider headquartered in the US serving governments, institutions, asset managers and corporate and private clients.  Their services include asset and investment management, trusts, treasury services, capital markets, foreign exchange and wealth management. As of 2017, Bank of New York Mellon Corp. has 1.8 trillion USD in assets under management. They are among the top 10 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with over 36 billion USD worth of shares. Bank of New York Mellon Corp. are also among the top 50 lenders to Forest 500 companies, with over 4.7 billion USD worth of loans across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Allstate are a US-based insurance company that offers a variety of insurance solutions. Their services include insurance, financial planning, annuities and investments. As of 2017, Allstate's total assets amount to more than 110 billion USD, with more than 60 billion USD in securities. They are one of the top 20 bondholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 1.5 billion USD worth of bonds for companies across a broad range of forest risk sectors.

Banco Bradesco S.A. are a banking and financial services group based in Brazil serving private, commercial and institutional customers. Their services include corporate finance, investment banking, asset management, insurance, pensions and retail banking services. As of 2017, their total assets under management amount to more than 475 billion BRL. Banco Bradesco S.A. are a top financier in Brazil, an important forest jurisdiction in terms of tropical forest cover and agricultural commodity production and trading.
Export-Import Bank of Malaysia is a government-owned financial institution, providing banking products and services in Malaysia.

Aberdeen Asset management are a global asset management company headquartered in the UK, serving private and institutional clients and external investment advisors. Their services cover equities, fixed income, quantitative, property and hedge fund investments. As of 2017, Aberdeen Asset Management have over 395 billion USD in assets under management. They are also among the top 50 shareholders for Forest 500 companies, with more than 8 billion USD worth of shares.

Pictet Funds are an international asset management company headquartered in Switzerland that serves private, sovereign and institutional clients. Their services cover wealth management, private banking, asset management and asset related services. The Land O Lakes brand is also licensed to a small number of partner companies who produce milk, creams, juices, eggs, cottage cheese, sour cream, yogurt and cocoa mixes, such as the WhiteWaves Food Company. Kozy Shack, acquired in 2012, produces chilled desserts such as rice pudding, tapioca pudding and flans and claims to be America's #1 brand of tapioca and rice pudding.
Purina Animal Nutrition LLC provides supplements, ingredients, complete feeds and speciality technologies to farmers and the consumer (pet) markets via several thousand local cooperatives, independent dealers and other retailers in the US. The company is heavily involved in research and development and has over 100 patents worldwide. Land O'Lakes Inc. animal feed production began with feed for mules and horses in 1894, and today its feed products are produced for an extremely broad range of animals from farm animals, during multiple lifecycle stages, to fish, pets and exotic animals. Land O'Lakes Inc. is one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers and therefore purchases large quantities of soya, some of which is used in animal feed production,. As some animal feeds also use palm oil, Land O'Lakes Inc. may also source palm oil for use as an ingredient.

Agriculture is at the core of Groupe Blattner Elwyn's operations and the group's agribusiness activities are in the production and processing of rubber, palm oil and cocoa. The Group's industrial operations are in: The production of crown corks and metal cans; timber processing and harvesting; and in the production of laminated table-tops, through a company based in France. Finally, Groupe Blattner Elwyn has a variety of distribution and services companies, which include medical operations, chemical production, the automotive industry, and importing and exporting activities.
Groupe Blattner Elwyn has six subsidiaries involved in the cultivation and processing of palm oil managing some 28,311 hectares of land, 17,196 of which are currently in production. The group operates six oil palm factories and provides employment for around 10,000 permanent and temporary workers and sharecroppers.
Regarding the group's timber operations, Groupe Blattner Elwyn acquired SIFORCO from Danzer Group in February 2012. This acquisition was Groupe Blattner Elwyn's first step into the forestry sector, which the Group views as an investment in the growing timber industry in the DRC. SIFORCO, which was established in 1972, manages an area of over 1.9 million hectares in the DRC, making it one of the largest logging companies in the country in terms of forest area. SIFORCO has 600 employees and the majority of its concessions are located in the Equateur and Orientale provinces. The company harvests its natural forests for the production of logs and also has timber processing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer, and a joiner's workshop. It harvests and processes timber mainly for the European and American markets.

The WTK Group of companies has diverse business interests in forestry and timber processing, oil palm, land development, trading, and manufacturing, as well as other services, including insurance and shipping. Established in 1940, the group has its origins in timber activities and is the oldest of the top logging companies operating in Sarawak, Malaysia. One of the group's subsidiaries, WTK Holdings Berhad, is a publicly listed investment holding company, whose subsidiaries in turn are involved in timber harvesting and in downstream timber processing. WTK Group operates five sawmills and three plywood mills and is therefore involved in manufacturing and trading plywood, sawn timber, logs and other timber products for domestic and overseas markets. As well as producing and trading timber products, the group is also active in the trade of other goods, including adhesives.
As well as being one of the oldest logging operators in Sarawak, WTK Group is also one of the largest; it has a total of 850,000 hectares of timber concessions, 320,000 hectares of which are managed under WTK Holdings Bhd. The organisation also has 400,000 hectares of concessions in Papua New Guinea and further forestry operations in Indonesia. In Malaysia, WTK Group is well established, with further activities outside of the timber industry, including in tourism, hotels and shipping.
With regards to other forest risk commodities, WTK Group is increasingly diversifying into oil palm. The group has a total palm oil land bank of around 120,000 hectares in Sarawak, Malaysia. It also owns three oil mills and plans to enter into the refinery business in the future.

The Group's industrial operations are in: The production of crown corks and metal cans; timber processing and harvesting; and in the production of laminated table-tops, through a company based in France. Finally, Groupe Blattner Elwyn has a variety of distribution and services companies, which include medical operations, chemical production, the automotive industry, and importing and exporting activities.
Groupe Blattner Elwyn has six subsidiaries involved in the cultivation and processing of palm oil managing some 28,311 hectares of land, 17,196 of which are currently in production. The group operates six oil palm factories and provides employment for around 10,000 permanent and temporary workers and sharecroppers.
Regarding the group's timber operations, Groupe Blattner Elwyn acquired SIFORCO from Danzer Group in February 2012. This acquisition was Groupe Blattner Elwyn's first step into the forestry sector, which the Group views as an investment in the growing timber industry in the DRC. SIFORCO, which was established in 1972, manages an area of over 1.9 million hectares in the DRC, making it one of the largest logging companies in the country in terms of forest area. SIFORCO has 600 employees and the majority of its concessions are located in the Equateur and Orientale provinces. The company harvests its natural forests for the production of logs and also has timber processing facilities for the production of sawn timber and veneer, and a joiner's workshop. It harvests and processes timber mainly for the European and American markets.

Yakult Honsha Co Ltd (Yakult) is a Japanese company, established in 1935 and incorporated in 1955; it is involved in the manufacture and distribution of food and drink products. The company has three main business segments: Beverages and Food Manufacturing and Sale; Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing and Sale; and Others. The company's original and still most recognisable product is a probiotic fermented milk drink sold under the Yakult brand. This continues to be the company's main product, particularly in the overseas market, where average daily sales of Yakult products in early 2013 were over 22.5 million. However, aside from its fermented milk and yogurt products (which include the Joie, Sofuhl, and Purela, amongst others) Yakult also offers non-dairy beverages such as flavoured tea drinks and juices, a range of cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and food products, including noodles.
As of 2013, the company had around 79 subsidiaries and 18 associated companies. The company has overseas and domestic operations, with its operations outside of Japan starting in 1964, when its Taiwanese subsidiary was established. Since then, this has grown and the company is now active in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide, including in Europe, the US, Brazil, Mexico, China, South Korea, Hong Kong, Indonesia, and elsewhere in Asia.
Yakult is a significant player in the global packaged food market, demonstrated by its leading position in a variety of markets worldwide. For example, specifically, it ranks among the top three companies in the dairy products market in Japan, and among the top ten for the packaged food industry overall. It is also among the top five companies with the largest market shares in the South Korean noodle industry, and holds a similarly high market share in the market for noodles in the United States, and is in the top 25 companies in the world for the packaged food industry.

Kewpie Corp (Kewpie) is a Japanese food manufacturer that produces a variety of processed and packaged food products for commercial and consumer use. Palm oil and soya are the most relevant forest risk commodities to Kewpie's operations, as vegetable oils are commonly used in these products. The Kewpie group of companies consists of the Kewpie Corp and 65 consolidated subsidiaries, which together are involved in the manufacturing, wholesale, transport and storage of food products. The group's operations can be divided into five business segments: Condiments and Processed Foods; Health Function Products; Egg Products; Salad and Prepared Foods; and Distribution System.
The condiments products category is a core part of the Group's operations, principally producing mayonnaise and dressings. The company's processed foods segment produces a variety of canned and bottled foods, such as jams, pasta sauces, canned sweetcorn and baby food. Through these two business segments, the sales of these products have positioned Kewpie in a leading position in the domestic and international spreads market, where its holds the top market share in Japan, and is among the top 20 globally. Kewpie is also among the top five manufacturers of baby food in Japan, and places within the top 50 on the global market. Kewpie also has a business division specialising in egg products, such as liquid, frozen and dried eggs, which are used by food manufacturers in the production of confectionery, meat products and fish cakes, among others. Kewpie uses a large amount of egg products itself, for example as a main ingredient in its mayonnaise, and accounts for the use of about 9% of all eggs produced in Japan.  As well as the above divisions, Kewpie has operations in the production of fine chemical products, such as hyaluronic acid; and delicatessen products, such as salads. Finally, the company also provides food distribution services for the domestic market, including under K.R.S. Corporation. Kewpie has a well-established overseas presence, with subsidiaries is in the United States, the Netherlands, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand.
Kewpie is not a member of the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO).

Founded in Hong Kong in the 1800s, CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd (CK Hutchison) operates five core businesses: ports and related services, retail, infrastructure, energy and telecommunication. The company was formed in its present structure in 2015 following the restructuring of Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd. and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd. to separate the property business into a new holding company and subsume Hutchison Whampoa's other operations under the direction of CK Hutchison. CK Hutchison employs around 270,000 people across 50 countries.
CK Hutchison's retail operations are led by A.S. Watson Group, which was started in 1828 as a small dispensary in Guangzhou, China. Today, the Group has more than 12,000 stores in 22 countries worldwide and claims to be the world's largest international health and beauty retailer. The company operates multiple brands in the health and beauty sector, including: Watsons, which has over 4,800 stores and 1,400 pharmacies in Asia and Europe; Kruidvat, which has over 1,000 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium; and Superdrug, which operates in the UK and Ireland and has over 870 stores. A.S. Watson also sells food, wine and electronics under multiple brands, which include: PARKnSHOP, which operates 340 supermarkets in Greater China; and SU-PA-DE-PA, which combines supermarket food products with department store ranges, such as clothing and entertainment. The Group's portfolio also includes over 500 European perfume and cosmetics shops.

Sodefor (Société de Développement Forestier) is the largest logging company in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with concessions of over 2 million hectares. The company harvests timber from its concession areas and processes timber for the production of sawn wood and plywood. Sodefor and three other major forestry companies in DRC, Societe Forestiere et des Matieres Ligneuses Africaines (Soforma), Compagnie Forestière de Transformation (CFT) and Societe Forestière et Agricole de la M'Bola (Forabola), are all linked via a common shareholder (Norsudtimber S.A.), however are managed separately. These are among the most significant forestry companies in the country. Soforma operates the third largest area of concessions and oversees around 996,000 hectares of forest in the Cuvette Centrale region, while Forabola and CFT rank fourth and fifth respectively, in terms of area under concession.
Norsudtimber is a private Portuguese-owned company registered in Liechtenstein.
Grupo Bom Retiro is a Brazilian company operating in the business of industrialising salted hides and finished leather.

China Resources (CR) is a diversified business group with its main business in consumer products, energy, and pharmaceuticals as well as being involved in retail, chemicals, and textiles, amongst other industries. Food products include rice, meat, and frozen foods. The group's retail chain, CR Vanguard, is also one of the largest retail chains in China. It is one of the largest retailers in China by edible grocery sales and one of the largest in the Asia-Pacific region overall.

WH Group, formerly Shuanghui International is headquartered in Hong Kong and has business operations in three segments: packaged meat, fresh pork and hog production. Its global portfolio includes Shuanghui Development, Smithfield Foods and Campofrio Food Group. The anglicised name for Shuanghui Group is Shineway Group and it holds the top market positions for canned or preserved, and chilled processed food in China and is also among the top ten globally for chilled processed foods and the top 40 for packaged food.
The Shineway Group is the largest meat processing company in China, occupying a significant share of the market and employing some 60,000 people. Shanghui/Shineway is the company's original Chinese brand; manufacturing fresh pork and retorted and pasteurised packaged meat products in more than ten product ranges (including King of Kings and Spicy Crispy Sausage) and over 200 cuts and styles of fresh and chilled meat. However, although it advertises itself as the largest pork company in the world and therefore focuses on hog slaughtering and processing, the company's operations in the beef and poultry sectors have recently expanded.
Within the United States, Smithfield Food manufactures pork products and exports them as far as China, Mexico, Russia, Japan and Canada. Brand names include Smithfield, Margherita, Farmland, Armour and Curly's, amongst others; and products include smoked and boiled hams, bacon, sausage, deli meats, hot dogs, luncheon meats, pepperoni, dry meat, and finally pre-prepared foods (supplying grocery stores and restaurants alike). Smithfield is one of the five largest chilled processed food companies in the world and supplies to brands in around 50 countries.
Finally, Campofrio Food Group, in which WH Group owns a 37% share, (the largest packaged meat company in Europe) is the European branch of WH Group's business; it operates in Spain, France, Belgium, Holland, Germany, Italy, Portugal and the US.

Aceitera General Deheza (AGD Group) is a soy producer, processor and trader based in Argentina. Products include crude and refined vegetable oils, protein meals and biodiesel. AGD is one of the largest soy exporters from Argentina and exports soybean oil and soy-based protein meals, among other products to 45 countries.

Established in 1968, NICE Group is the largest soap and detergent manufacturer in China; it also produces dishwasher soap and toothpaste. It's best known brand is the detergent, DIAO; further brands include Supra, Soling, 100 Years Hare Care and Lizi. Since 1994, the group's sales of laundry powder, soap and liquid detergent have been number one in China; and in 2005, NICE Group ranked in the top 8 worldwide. Each year the company produces 1 million tonnes of washing powder, 540,000 tonnes of liquid detergent, 280,000 tonnes of soap bars, 20,000 tonnes of industrial glycerine and 400 million tubes of toothpaste.  The Group has over 10,000 employees, operates 10 brands, and has more than 50 sales branches and 3 overseas subsidiaries. The Group's products are sold in China, the Middle East, Africa, Oceania, Europe and the US.

The Permata Hijau Group (PHG) is a palm oil company that has operations across the entire palm oil supply chain from cultivating to manufacturing and distribution. Its products include crude palm oil, oleochemicals, biodiesel, specialty fats and cooking oil. In 2015, the group processed and traded more than 1.6 million metric tons of palm oil and derivatives. PHG is one of the top five importers and exporters of palm oil in Indonesia and is among the top ten importers of palm oil into China.
Coop Col Multiactiva Fernheim Ltda is a Paraguayan cooperative with operations in dairy and agricultural products, and beef production.
Camera Agroalimentos S.A. is a prominent Brazilian agribusiness. The company produce, process and trade in soybean and manufacture biodiesel.

Pertamina Persero PT is a state-owned Indonesian company focussing on oil, gas, renewable energy and new energy. This involves the exploration and extraction of oil and gas as well as the development of geothermal energy and coal bed methane as alternate energy sources. In addition, the company is involved in crude oil processing and the marketing, trade and shipping of oil products, gas and petrochemicals. The company is also involved in the domestic retail of gasoline and diesel and has an extensive network of over 5000 retail gas stations across Indonesia.
As per a government mandate in 2013, all diesel for industry and transportation in Indonesia must contain 10% biofuel. This has led to Pertamina Persero PT issuing a number of tenders for palm oil-based biodiesel to meet these requirements. Palm oil companies Wilmar International and Musim Mas have already won tenders to supply biodiesel to Pertamina Persero PT and more tenders are planned for the future. A total of 5.3 million kilolitres (around 4.7 million MT) of palm-based biodiesel will be procured for 2014-2015.

Cresud SA is an agricultural company based in Argentina, involved in the production of crops, and beef and dairy cattle. As of June 2013, the company has a beef cattle stock of over 60,000 heads, which are primarily destined for the domestic Argentine market and not for export. Crop production includes soya, corn, sunflower and wheat. Soya accounts for over half of the company's total crop production, with 220,000 tons produced in 2013. Almost half of this soya was produced in Brazil, with a large amount also produced in Argentina.
Cresud SA owns almost 1 million hectares of its own land and nearly 50,000 hectares of land under lease agreements. Of this land more than 400,000 hectares is currently productive, with a further 135,000 hectares under development. Although largely based in Argentina, since 2005 the company has been expanding into other Latin American countries including Brazil, Paraguay and Bolivia. Currently, 66% of the company's land area is in Argentina, 19% in Brazil, 13% in Paraguay and 2% in Bolivia.
InVivo, an agricultural cooperative in France , operates in agriculture and consumer retail .

Total Enterprise Ltd. is a Hong Kong-based distributor of quick-frozen food products, including beef, pork and chicken. They primarily sell to the Chinese market and import frozen meat from Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina, among others.

New Hope Group is one of the largest agribusiness enterprises in China. The company started in 1982 when founder, Liu Yonghao, and his three brothers left their jobs and sold their bicycles and watches to raise money to buy poultry.
The group is involved in four main sectors: Chemicals and Resources, which has operations and interests in potassium, nickel, coal, phosphorous (including for use in animal feeds) and PVC production; Finance and Investment, which has investments in commercial banks, life insurers, investment companies and funds; Real Estate and Infrastructure; and Agribusiness and Food. Agribusiness and Food is the group's most significant area; it has operations throughout the supply chain, including animal breeding, feed production, dairy, technology services, abattoirs and meat processing. New Hope Group is one of the largest suppliers of poultry, eggs, pork and dairy products in China. Through subsidiaries such as New Hope Liuhe Co Ltd it is also one of the world's top five largest animal feed producers. It has 184 feed mills, based in China and other markets including Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia and the Philippines. The mills are capable of producing 26.6 million tonnes of feed annually, with sales of 12 million tonnes.
Based in Qingdao, China and founded in 1995, New Hope Liuhe Co Ltd (Liuhe) is the listed company of New Hope Group. The company is engaged in animal feed manufacturing, meat processing and cooking, livestock and poultry breeding, importing and exporting trade, animal production and financial guarantee. It currently owns more than 265 subsidiary companies nationwide with a total employee number exceeding 50,000 persons. In 2009, Liuhe produced 10.1 million metric tons of animal feed, processed 1.25 million metric tons of poultry meat and hatched 216 million day-old poults with total sales revenue of 40.2 billion RMB Yuan. Both the feed sales volume and meat processing volume were ranked No. 1 in China.

The Japan Agricultural Cooperatives Group (JA Group) is an agricultural cooperative, established to support its members by selling their products rather than each of its members selling products independently. On top of this, JA Group provides its members with production materials and agrochemicals. The group is a politically powerful organisation and is comprised of almost ten million regular and associate members. 
The JA Group is made up of several constituent parts, including ZEN-NOH, which is the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations. ZEN-NOH manages the business and distribution operations of the JA Group and is responsible for the marketing and supply business side of the group. Of particular relevance, are ZEN-NOH's operations in the animal feed sector. Of the total 24 to 25 million tonnes of compound feed used per year in Japan, ZEN-NOH handles around 30%, making ZEN-NOH Japan's largest compound feed producer and one of the top ten in the world. Through its subsidiaries, ZEN-NOH imports large volumes of soya from overseas producers including Brazil, India and China for use in compound animal feeds.
Also of relevance, is the group's Daily Necessities business unit, through which ZEN-NOH and JA run around 800 A-Coop supermarkets. The stores sell clothing, food products and consumer durables, and prioritise goods produced by members and sell A-Coop branded goods. Currently there are around 1,300 A-Coop branded goods, which include packaged food and clothing.

Yamazaki Baking Co (Yamazaki) is a Japanese group of companies involved in the manufacture and sale of baked goods and was founded in 1948. The company has four main business segments: Food, Overseas Food, Retail and Other. The food divisions manufacture a range of baked products and confectionary, whilst the retail division operates supermarkets, cafeterias and convenience stores. The full range of products manufactured includes breads, pastries, biscuits, rice balls, noodles, sandwiches, packed meals and snacks such as rice crackers and Japanese crackers. Jam, desserts, side dishes and prepared food in retort pouches are also being produced alongside both Japanese and Western-style confectionary. The Others division deals with logistics; it manages the design, supervision and construction of food manufacturing facilities, the non-life insurance agency business, as well as the manufacture and sale of cleaning agents for baking equipment.
Yamazaki is the largest baking company in Japan, the third largest packaged food company in Japan and ranks in the top 60 in the worldwide packaged food and sweet and savoury snacks categories. More importantly, it is among the top five baking companies in the world.
Yamazaki grow successfully through the implementation of high-tech equipment imported from Europe and North America in the post-war period. Over the last 60 years it has diversified its product range, including introduction of foreign foods into the Japanese market. Yamazaki claims that the development of its own licensed stores allows it to respond to changing markets and customer desires (particularly its bakeshops, which manufacture products on-site, as well as selling goods made elsewhere). The company now has 17,521 employees and 105,000 stores across Japan.

Founded in Hong Kong in the 1800s, CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd (CK Hutchison) operates five core businesses: ports and related services, retail, infrastructure, energy and telecommunication. The company was formed in its present structure in 2015 following the restructuring of Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd. and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd. to separate the property business into a new holding company and subsume Hutchison Whampoa's other operations under the direction of CK Hutchison. CK Hutchison employs around 270,000 people across 50 countries.
CK Hutchison's retail operations are led by A.S. Watson Group, which was started in 1828 as a small dispensary in Guangzhou, China. Today, the Group has more than 12,000 stores in 22 countries worldwide and claims to be the world's largest international health and beauty retailer. The company operates multiple brands in the health and beauty sector, including: Watsons, which has over 4,800 stores and 1,400 pharmacies in Asia and Europe; Kruidvat, which has over 1,000 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium; and Superdrug, which operates in the UK and Ireland and has over 870 stores. A.S. Watson also sells food, wine and electronics under multiple brands, which include: PARKnSHOP, which operates 340 supermarkets in Greater China; and SU-PA-DE-PA, which combines supermarket food products with department store ranges, such as clothing and entertainment. The Group's portfolio also includes over 500 European perfume and cosmetics shops.

Nitori Holdings Co Ltd is a furniture company based in Hokkaido, Japan. The company dates back to 1967 when it opened its first furniture store and in 2010 the company was restructured: Nitori Holdings Co Ltd was established, marking the transition of Nitori Co Ltd to a holding company structure whereby Nitori Holdings Co Ltd oversees the Nitori group of companies,.The company operates a chain of furniture stores, and sells its own brand, manufactured as well as imported merchandise. It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand. Around 80% of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are sourced from overseas and as part of its expansion outside of Japan, the company also supports the operations of two furniture factories in Indonesia (since 1994) and Vietnam (since 2004). Some of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are manufactured at externally-owned facilities; however, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd maintains close contact with and involvement in all its business operations through the establishment of regional offices. Furthermore, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is directly responsible for the import and distribution of all products to its stores, with its subsidiary Home Logistics Co Ltd responsible for all domestic distribution.
In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.
