Nitori Holdings Co Ltd is a furniture company based in Hokkaido, Japan. The company dates back to 1967 when it opened its first furniture store and in 2010 the company was restructured: Nitori Holdings Co Ltd was established, marking the transition of Nitori Co Ltd to a holding company structure whereby Nitori Holdings Co Ltd oversees the Nitori group of companies,.The company operates a chain of furniture stores, and sells its own brand, manufactured as well as imported merchandise. It is the largest home furnishings company in Japan and the third largest globally. As a manufacturer and retailer of furniture and interior products, the company has operations at multiple stages of the supply chain.
Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is the manufacturing arm of the Nitori group and produces a variety of furniture products, including cupboards, beds, and kitchen storage units. Nitori Furniture Co Ltd sources raw materials from around the world and has procurement facilities in seven countries, including in China, Malaysia and Thailand. Around 80% of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are sourced from overseas and as part of its expansion outside of Japan, the company also supports the operations of two furniture factories in Indonesia (since 1994) and Vietnam (since 2004). Some of Nitori Furniture Co Ltd's products are manufactured at externally-owned facilities; however, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd maintains close contact with and involvement in all its business operations through the establishment of regional offices. Furthermore, Nitori Furniture Co Ltd is directly responsible for the import and distribution of all products to its stores, with its subsidiary Home Logistics Co Ltd responsible for all domestic distribution.
In terms of the group's retail activities, Nitori Co Ltd operates over 300 stores, both in Japan and abroad. Although the group was originally inspired by the developed furniture and home interiors markets of the United States and Europe, Nitori Co Ltd's growth is well demonstrated by its entrance into the US market, where in 2013, it opened its first store under the Aki-Home brand in California.

Established in 1968, NICE Group is the largest soap and detergent manufacturer in China; it also produces dishwasher soap and toothpaste. It's best known brand is the detergent, DIAO; further brands include Supra, Soling, 100 Years Hare Care and Lizi. Since 1994, the group's sales of laundry powder, soap and liquid detergent have been number one in China; and in 2005, NICE Group ranked in the top 8 worldwide. Each year the company produces 1 million tonnes of washing powder, 540,000 tonnes of liquid detergent, 280,000 tonnes of soap bars, 20,000 tonnes of industrial glycerine and 400 million tubes of toothpaste.  The Group has over 10,000 employees, operates 10 brands, and has more than 50 sales branches and 3 overseas subsidiaries. Yamazaki Baking Co (Yamazaki) is a Japanese group of companies involved in the manufacture and sale of baked goods and was founded in 1948. The company has four main business segments: Food, Overseas Food, Retail and Other. The food divisions manufacture a range of baked products and confectionary, whilst the retail division operates supermarkets, cafeterias and convenience stores. The full range of products manufactured includes breads, pastries, biscuits, rice balls, noodles, sandwiches, packed meals and snacks such as rice crackers and Japanese crackers. Jam, desserts, side dishes and prepared food in retort pouches are also being produced alongside both Japanese and Western-style confectionary. The Others division deals with logistics; it manages the design, supervision and construction of food manufacturing facilities, the non-life insurance agency business, as well as the manufacture and sale of cleaning agents for baking equipment.
Yamazaki is the largest baking company in Japan, the third largest packaged food company in Japan and ranks in the top 60 in the worldwide packaged food and sweet and savoury snacks categories. More importantly, it is among the top five baking companies in the world.
Yamazaki grow successfully through the implementation of high-tech equipment imported from Europe and North America in the post-war period. Over the last 60 years it has diversified its product range, including introduction of foreign foods into the Japanese market. Yamazaki claims that the development of its own licensed stores allows it to respond to changing markets and customer desires (particularly its bakeshops, which manufacture products on-site, as well as selling goods made elsewhere). The company now has 17,521 employees and 105,000 stores across Japan.

PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia (Japfa) is a vertically integrated Indonesian agri-food company,. The company started in 1971 and floated on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges in 1989. Since then, acquisitions of animal feed, shrimp feed, poultry breeding and processing, and shrimp farming companies have helped to make Japfa one of the largest and most highly integrated poultry and shrimp producers in Indonesia.
The company is split into four divisions: Beef; Strategic Business; Aquaculture; and Poultry. The beef division is a vertically integrated cattle breeding, fattening and processing operation that operates Asia's biggest feedlot and produces finished products under the Santori Beef brand. Japfa's strategic business division contains a number of businesses and operations that support or complement Japfa's other divisions. Activities within this division include poultry vaccine research and production, poultry processing, and trading of raw materials to support Japfa's core animal feed business. The aquaculture division is run through PT Suri Tani Pemuka, a 100% owned subsidiary. The division breeds, farms and processes shrimp for export market. It also produces over 50,000 tons of fish and shrimp feed annually and has plans to further expand this area of the business. Finally, the vertically integrated poultry division is Japfa's largest division accounting for 83% of sales; Japfa is one of the largest poultry producers in Indonesia. Feed production is a key area of the business; Japfa is the second largest chicken feed producer in Indonesia, with approximately a 33% market share. The company's 19 mills across Indonesia, have capacity of 3.6 million tonnes. The poultry feed unit accounted for more than 50% of gross sales in 2013. Japfa's scale is important in helping it to secure commodities such as corn and soya at favourable prices.

Amul is an Indian dairy company operating throughout India that manufactures products such as milk, butter, cheese, ice-cream, and other food and beverages. The company also produces its own cattle feed. These products involve significant amounts of palm oil and soy, as well as paper for packaging. It is one of the largest companies in India by market share for packaged food, dairy, and ice-cream and frozen desserts as well as oils and fats.  Amul is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Major brands include Marie Claire, North Star and Sandak. Bata is also one of Europe’s largest footwear and leather retailers.  Bata Corporation is selected as a powerbroker for leather and paper packaging.

The New Hope Group is a Chinese conglomerate with 600 subsidiaries across 20 countries active in agriculture, consumer goods, industrial resources, and real estate. The company is especially prominent in livestock and animal feed. The New Hope Group is one of the top producers of poultry in the world. In addition, it is one of the world’s largest producers of animal feed and one of the largest in China. New Hope Group is exposed to palm oil and soy in the animal feed.  New Hope Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.
Mercurio Alimentos is a food production company based in Brazil. The company exports to over 40 countries. They have been selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and beef.

Nice Group is a Chinese manufacturer of cleaning products. The company sells laundry powder, liquid detergents, bath soaps, toothpastes, and dishwasher liquids among other products. Well-known brands include DIAO, NICE, and Supra. Nice Group claims to be the number one company in China for laundry powder, soap, and liquid detergent. These products are known to use palm oil.    Nice Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and paper packaging.

Parker-Migliorini International is a company that supplies food products to the global market. The company is a partnership between two international food distributors, Parker International and Meridional Meat. Parker-Migliorini’s products include beef, poultry, pork, lamb, seafood, game meat, equine, and dairy. The company imports beef from Brazil and other countries in South America.  Parker-Migliorini International Gmbh is selected as a powerbroker for beef.

Soyuz Corporation, based in Russia, processes vegetable fats and oils for the food industry, including confectionary, bakery and ice cream production. Soyuz Corporation is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Tangrenshen Group Co. Ltd. controls more than 100 subsidaries throughout China, and sells feed products including TRS and Camel brands. Animal feed exposes Tangrenshen Group to the forest risk commodities soy and palm oil. Tangrenshen Group (TRS) is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Total Enterprise Ltd. is a Hong Kong-based distributor of frozen food products, including beef. It primarily sells to the Chinese market and import frozen meat from Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina, among others.   Total Enterprise Ltd is selected as a powerbroker for beef.

Unifood Industrial Group is based in China with overseas branches in New Zealand, Hong Kong and the Netherlands. The company specialises in meat manufacturing and processing. Unifood Industrial Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and beef.

Bright Food Group is a Chinese food industry group involved in agriculture, food processing, and manufacturing, as well as retailing. It is involved in diverse business areas, but its main food businesses include packaged foods, dairy, sugar and vegetables. The group is a major player in China and globally including in dairy and packaged foods.   Bright Food (Group) Co. Ltd. is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging.

Dalian Huafeng Furniture is a Chinese company specialising in furniture manufacturing, producing solid wood furniture. East Hope Group is a Chinese company that primarily produces animal feed but also produces chemicals and other products. The group operates 111 animal feed subsidiaries in China, Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, Cambodia, and other countries. Its animal feed products include feed for cattle, poultry, pigs, and aquaculture. Important brands include “East Hope”, “Golden Bean” and “Red Gate”. It is one of the largest producers of animal feed in the world.  East Hope Group is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil, soy and paper packaging and is also assessed for its exposure to timber.

Groupe Blattner Elwyn (GBE) is an industrial group operating in the Democratic Republic of Congo and active in diverse industries, including agriculture, mining, and other industries. Its agricultural businesses include the cultivation and processing of palm oil, livestock and the production of animal feed, as well as logging forestry concessions. The company is one of the major palm oil producers in the Democratic Republic of Congo and owns the logging company SIFORCO, which operates forestry concessions in the DRC.  Groupe Blattner Elwyn is selected as a powerbroker for timber and is also assessed for its exposure to palm oil and paper packaging.

Parker-Migliorini International (PMI) is a partnership between two international food distribution companies, Parker International and Meridional Meat. It is a major global food trader, specialising in a wide range of beef products, as well as pork, poultry, seafood, some fruits and vegetables, and animal feed (predominantly hay and straw). PMI operates globally and reports that it ships thousands of containers internationally every year. The company has a worldwide presence, with offices in North, Central and South America, including in Mexico and Brazil; Asia, in China and Japan; and Europe, in Switzerland. PMI Hong Kong Food Services Ltd is the Hong Kong office of PMI.
PMI, through its Hong Kong Food Services Ltd office, is one of China's top importers of beef from Brazil, ranking as the number one company responsible for over 25% of total imports from Brazil in 2013. It also imports beef from other countries, including Mexico.

PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia (Japfa) is a vertically integrated Indonesian agri-food company,. The company started in 1971 and floated on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges in 1989. Since then, acquisitions of animal feed, shrimp feed, poultry breeding and processing, and shrimp farming companies have helped to make Japfa one of the largest and most highly integrated poultry and shrimp producers in Indonesia.
The company is split into four divisions: Beef; Strategic Business; Aquaculture; and Poultry. The beef division is a vertically integrated cattle breeding, fattening and processing operation that operates Asia's biggest feedlot and produces finished products under the Santori Beef brand. Japfa's strategic business division contains a number of businesses and operations that support or complement Japfa's other divisions. Activities within this division include poultry vaccine research and production, poultry processing, and trading of raw materials to support Japfa's core animal feed business. The aquaculture division is run through PT Suri Tani Pemuka, a 100% owned subsidiary. The division breeds, farms and processes shrimp for export market. It also produces over 50,000 tons of fish and shrimp feed annually and has plans to further expand this area of the business. Finally, the vertically integrated poultry division is Japfa's largest division accounting for 83% of sales; Japfa is one of the largest poultry producers in Indonesia. Feed production is a key area of the business; Japfa is the second largest chicken feed producer in Indonesia, with approximately a 33% market share. The company's 19 mills across Indonesia, have capacity of 3.6 million tonnes. The poultry feed unit accounted for more than 50% of gross sales in 2013. Japfa's scale is important in helping it to secure commodities such as corn and soya at favourable prices.

OJSC Magnit is a Russian holding company, operating in the Russian food retail sector. Magnit is an Open Joint Stock Company (OJSC) and is among Russia's largest retailers. The company operates four types of stores: Magnit convenience stores, of which it runs almost 7700; Magnit hypermarkets, of which it has 170; Magnit Family stores, of which is operates over 60; and Magnit cosmetics stores, of which it runs 816.
The company began in household chemical wholesale in the mid-1990s, and has since expanded into the retail market. Today it ranks as the top retailer in the Russian market in terms of its sales and its presence across Russia, and employs around 230,000 people. Magnit produces around 700 private label products for its stores, amounting to 13% of total sales in 2012. Included in Magnit's ranges of goods are a variety of meat products, including a range of unbranded and branded private label frozen and chilled meat products, including beef.
Between 2007 and 2012, Russia imported over 23% of Brazil's total beef exports, which accounted for around 40% of Russia's total beef and veal import market (in 2010); therefore, as a leading retailer and stockist of meat products in Russia, Magnit is at significant risk of supplying beef products linked to tropical deforestation. In 2009 Magnit began to import goods from abroad run by its subsidiary company Tander. By the end of 2013, company's import accounted for 10% of its turnover. During the first six months of 2014, Tander was in top 10 Russia's importers with total volume of import in amount of $830.58 million.

The Htoo Group of Companies is one of Myanmar's largest and most influential conglomerates. The group has more than fourteen subsidiaries engaged in a variety of operations. Its extensive influence is shown through the diversity of its business activities, which include ventures in the airline industry (Air Bagan); banking (AGD Bank); the tourism industry through its luxury resorts and hotels; mining; logistics; construction; agriculture; trading; radio (FM Bagan); and petroleum (Htoo Petrol), amongst others. Air Bagan was the country's first private airline, launched in 2004, and Htoo Group of Companies has since added to its portfolio in the air travel industry, through the establishment of Asian Wings Airways.
The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

JVL Agro Industries Ltd (JVL), formally Jhunjhunwala Vanaspati Limited, is an Indian edible oil manufacturer. The company was incorporated in 1989, and was established initially in Northern India as a manufacturer of hydrogenated vegetable oils and refined oils, with the capacity to produce around 25 tonnes per day. The company has since grown to be the largest vegetable oil manufacturer in the country, with four plants producing 300 tonnes a day, with products including palm oil and soya bean oil.
The company's mid- and downstream activities require a large amount of raw material, therefore JVL are responsible for around 5% of India's total crude palm oil imports. JVL is also taking steps to acquire new land in Indonesia and Ethiopia for the production of palm oil and, as of 2013, had signed an agreement for the use of 12,500 acres of land in Ethiopia, with the potential of extending this to 62,000 acres.
JVL has a number of brands under which products are distributed to the consumer market across 18 Indian states. For example, refined soya bean oil is sold under the Jhoola health brand, while blended oils are sold under the Joohi active brand. JVL are working towards the development of rapid revenue growth partly by diversifying into new markets. For example, in 2012, they began to market bakery products, and in 2013-14 were set to commission a rice mill in Bihar with a production capacity of 12 metric tonnes per hour.

Grupo Jari, founded in 1994, is a prominent company in the forestry, paper and packaging sectors in Brazil. It claims to be one of the largest producers of corrugated cardboard packaging in Brazil and is responsible for 3% of eucalyptus pulp on the international market.
In 2010, the Group reported that it was responsible for 1.3 million hectares of forest in the Brazilian Amazon, including 545,000 hectares of native forest and 120,000 hectares authorised for plantations. The Group's native forests are located in the Vale do Jari, on the border of the states of ParÃ¡ and AmapÃ¡. According to Brazil's National Confederation of Industry (CNI), Grupo Jari is responsible for the largest area of natural forests under sustainable management in the Brazilian Amazon and is one of the country's principal producers of sawnwood. Grupo Jari produces sawn timber for the furniture and construction industries. Although it represented just 0.3% of total sawnwood production from the Brazilian Amazon in 2010, this is significant given that Brazil is the top producer of tropical sawnwood globally, responsible for 37.54% of total production from all ITTO producer countries (2007-2012). 
Jari was initially made up of three companies: Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A.; Jari Florestal; and Ouro Verde Amazonia. In 2012, however, Jari Celulose, Papel e Embalagens S.A. and US-based firm, International Paper, formed a joint corrugated packaging venture: Orsa International Paper Embalagens S.A. Having originally owned 75% of the joint venture, International Paper acquired the remainder in 2014 and is therefore is now in charge of Jari Celulose's packaging assets. Groupo Jari also partners with a number of companies manufacturing construction materials, such as wooden decks and flooring, for overseas retailers.

A high proportion of timber in China is consumed in the industrial and construction sector, which accounted for over 75% of total wood consumption in 2010. Shanghai Construction Group ranks as the second largest construction firm in China in terms of market share and as well as playing a key role in China's domestic construction industry, the group is active overseas, having completed more than 100 projects in 30 different countries and regions worldwide. In 2013, the group's overseas activities contributed over 15% to its total revenue. It is comprised of a number of subsidiaries and business departments. It has 17 subsidiaries involved in construction, engineering, real estate and landscaping, and 13 supporting business departments. The group also provides engineering and renovation services and has further business interests, for example in trading through its import and export operations. Shanghai Construction Group is a state-owned enterprise, whose majority shareholder is the Shanghai Municipal Government.
The group as a whole has been active in the Chinese construction sector for over fifty years. Shanghai Construction Group's subsidiary, Shanghai Construction Co Ltd, is involved exclusively in construction. It was established in 1994 and was listed on Shanghai stock exchange in 1998. The company is engaged in contracting, designing and constructing a variety of projects; including the development of residential, industrial, and municipal buildings, and public infrastructure facilities.
China's affordable housing programme aims for the construction of 36 million units of affordable housing in the five years leading up to 2015, as part of the country's 12th five-year plan. It is expected that the government's housing plan will drive increasing consumption and imports of wood products. Shanghai Construction Group has previously been involved in this programme, for example with the Sanlin Affordable Housing Development.

The Vicwood Group is a Hong Kong based timber company manufacturing plywood, parquet and other timber-based products. Alongside manufacturing facilities in China, the company also has forestry concessions and sawmills in Central Africa. In 2005, it had over 700,000 hectares in the Central African Republic and a further 1,000,000 hectares across Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Vicwood Group claims to have expanded on these 1.7 million hectares to now have forestry concessions covering a total area of about 2 million hectares as of 2016. It is one of the largest forestry concession operators in Cameroon.

Guangdong Wen's Group is a Chinese agricultural company. Founded in 1983 by seven farmers, it is active in a variety of sectors including research and development; animal feed production; poultry and pig farming; food processing; bio-pharmaceuticals; real estate development; industrial investment; and other activities relating to the agricultural sector. The group is comprised of around 160 subsidiaries, employs some 3.68 million workers and is active across 23 Chinese provinces.
Guangdong Wen's Group is active throughout the agricultural supply chain. The group is also one of the ten largest animal feed manufacturers globally, producing close to 10 million metric tons of feed annually. As well as being a top producer of animal feed, it is among the largest pig and poultry producers in China and therefore also a large buyer of animal feed products, including soybean and corn. It also provides livestock and agricultural equipment to farmers and produces a range of milk products, and cooked and chilled foods for consumers.
Le Gouessant, an agricultural cooperative in France, has its core business in animal feed, producing over 800,000 tons in 2017.

China's furniture industry is the country's highest export earner of all finished timber products and a significant consumer of timber, using around 19 million cubic metres (roundwood equivalent) in 2010. Dalian Huafeng Furniture Co. Ltd. is a Chinese furniture manufacturer, established in 1952 and located in the city of Zhuanghe in Dalian, China. The company claims to be the largest furniture manufacturer in China and to have the largest storage base for raw materials of the furniture industry globally. By market share it is also the largest manufacturer of wooden furniture, producing around 10 million units of furniture, including bedroom, dining room, living room, office, and hotel furniture per annum.
As well as supplying the domestic market, through its 300 stores, Dalian Huafeng Furniture also exports products to Japan, the US, Europe and Southeast Asia via a specialised industrial zone established in 2002. Despite its long history in the Chinese market, the company only became a prominent exporter of furniture products in 2000, when it became established in the US export market. The company continues to increase its presence in the export market, for example, with plans to open 300 stores in the US in five years from 2012.
Dalian Huafeng Furniture has expanded its furniture manufacturing operations to include production of wooden boards into its business activities. This was achieved in 2008 through a partnership with Jilin Forest Industry Co. Ltd., which manufactures and markets a range of timber products.

OJSC Magnit is a Russian holding company, operating in the Russian food retail sector. Magnit is an Open Joint Stock Company (OJSC) and is among Russia's largest retailers. The company began in household chemical wholesale in the mid-1990s, and has since expanded into the retail market. Today it ranks as the top retailer in the Russian market in terms of its sales and its presence across Russia, and employs around 230,000 people. Magnit produces around 700 private label products for its stores, amounting to 13% of total sales in 2012. Included in Magnit's ranges of goods are a variety of meat products, including a range of unbranded and branded private label frozen and chilled meat products, including beef.
Between 2007 and 2012, Russia imported over 23% of Brazil's total beef exports, which accounted for around 40% of Russia's total beef and veal import market (in 2010); therefore, as a leading retailer and stockist of meat products in Russia, Magnit is at significant risk of supplying beef products linked to tropical deforestation. In 2009 Magnit began to import goods from abroad run by its subsidiary company Tander. By the end of 2013, company's import accounted for 10% of its turnover. During the first six months of 2014, Tander was in top 10 Russia's importers with total volume of import in amount of $830.58 million.

De Heus was founded in 1911 and has grown from a regional Dutch feed manufacturer into an international conglomerate. It is now Europe's fourth largest compound animal feed producer and cites itself as a global top 15 animal feed supplier. The company has activities in over 50 countries in Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa and employs 3,000 people worldwide, operating around 30 feed mills. De Heus is still owned and managed by the De Heus Family.
De Heus manufactures feed for cattle, pigs, poultry and aquaculture; it also provides customised feed for individual farms. Subsidiaries include: Koudijis Animal Nutrition, which exports feed and related products to other European countries, Middle Eastern and African markets; and Agra-Matic, an agricultural consultancy operating in the Netherlands and Poland, providing advice in a number of areas including animal husbandry, the environment, technology and planning.
De Heus has focused upon expansion outside of Europe and entered a number of markets by establishing joint ventures in countries including China, Russia, Belgium, Ethiopia and Egypt. Further examples include an agreement with Brazilian firm, Nutrifarms LTDA, signed 2012, giving De Heus access to the Brazilian pig feed market. Investments expanding the company's infrastructure outside of Europe have also intensified DeHeus' international operations. For example, in 2013, the company opened a fourth feed factory in South Africa, manufacturing feed for not only traditional livestock but also ostrich and game. De Heus is currently investing in Vietnam, looking to become one of the top five largest feed producers. In March 2015, the company announced the opening of two new factories. Construction of a seventh Vietnamese factory is underway; a project that will cost around $30 million.

Housing construction is a very timber heavy industry and CSCEC has a dominant market share. Housing construction also comprises the majority of their contracts by value.

Samsonite International SA is a US based luggage company involved in the design, manufacturing, marketing and sale of luggage and travel accessories. Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

Air Bagan was the country's first private airline, launched in 2004, and Htoo Group of Companies has since added to its portfolio in the air travel industry, through the establishment of Asian Wings Airways.
The agricultural and timber sectors are important divisions of the Htoo Group of Companies' activities. Myanmar's large domestic conglomerates are highly influential in the country's timber trade. The Group's timber export unit was established in 1993, making it the earliest of its business operations.  The Group has several subsidiaries active in the sector, including Htoo Wood Products Ltd. and Htoo Trading Company Ltd., which are engaged in logging and the export of timber products, most notably teak, and are among the most dominant private timber companies in the country.
Within the agricultural sector, the Htoo Group is involved in the cultivation of several commodities, including oranges, mangoes, and oil palm. It is an important major player in the country's growing oil palm industry, with operations in the Tanintharyi Region in southern Myanmar. Its Myeik Palm Oil Plantation was established in 2004 and the company has plans for the development of 330,000 acres of plantations.

PT Rajawali Corpora is an investment holding company of the Rajawali Group, an Indonesian conglomerate active in a variety of industries, including telecommunications, hotels, consumer goods, retail, transportation, coal, gold and iron mining, and agriculture. The Group's agricultural activities comprise palm, sugar, rubber and corn plantations. Founded in 1984, the company is based in Jakarta and employs some 30,000 people. It was founded and is owned by Peter Sondakh, who is among the richest men in Indonesia and also ranks among the top billionaires globally. 
The company has a growing presence in the agricultural industry. PT Jaya Madiri Sukses (JMS Group) is the plantation arm of the Rajawali Group, and is a holding company comprising of a total of seven plantation companies in South and East Kalimantan. In 2010, Rajawali was reported to begin planting its 200,000 hectare land bank with oil palm. In 2011 Rajawali entered into a joint venture with commodities trader Louis Dreyfus called Green Eagle Plantations Pte Ltd. In 2012, the venture was reported to operate in four regions in Indonesia (South, West and East Kalimantan, and Papua), with concessions of around 50,000 hectares. However, in 2014, Louis Dreyfus Commodities Asia Pte left the joint venture, selling its 50% share of Green Eagle to the Rajawali Group. More recently, in September 2014, through a purchase of two investment firms, Matacuna Group and Pegasus CP One, Rajawali reportedly has acquired a 21% stake in crude palm oil producer, BW Plantation.

The company has more than 90 branches throughout Hong Kong, making it a major player in the Hong Kong market. As of 2016, it was among the top 10 largest importers globally for Brazilian beef, exposing the company to deforestation risks.

The company operates as a low-price/low-cost retailer and is seeking to expand its Russian footprint. The breadth of its retail offerings expose the group to a variety of forest risk commodities. It is one of the largest Russian retailers by edible grocery retail market share and has links to beef produced in Brazil and Argentina.

Emami Ltd. was founded in 1974 and is a leading personal and healthcare business headquartered in India. Through its subsidiaries it has a presence in a numerous markets and in various segments of the supply chain. One of its subsidiaries, Emami Biotech Ltd., is a key trader and processor of a range of raw materials, including oil palm, soybeans and jatropha. Emami Biotech has been central to the growth of India's capability in the biodiesel market, with the installation of the largest biodiesel plant in eastern India at Haldia. This plant has recently been upgraded so that it can process 2,000 tonnes of soybean and palm oil per day. This complements another refinery in Andhra Pradesh which adds a further 1,200 tonnes per day for the production of palm and sunflower oils. To further fill Emami's down-market needs, Emami Biotech imports a large amount of raw product into India, with over 4% of the total Indian market share in crude palm oil imports.
In terms of upstream activities, Emani Biotech owns a plantation in Ethiopia for the production of edible and non-edible oils and is looking to purchase plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia. In recent years, Emami Biotech has invested in the development of its marketing network to distribute its products under its Healthy and Tasty brand. Through this network, the company is able to supply goods to over 4,500 distributors and 12,000 retailers. Another subsidiary of Emami is Starmark, which owns a chain of seven retail stores in Kolkata and Chennai. These retail stores sell a range of books, toys, music and stationary. The customer base of Conde Nast is over 100 million consumers. Advance Publications is one of the largest magazine publishers globally.

According to Kontragent, an official database on Russian legal entities, in 2012, Reserve Food Company made net profit of 145,000 million RUB (343 million USD), that is 25 million RUB or 13% less than the previous year, likely due to an increase in the cost of products.

PMI operates globally and reports that it ships thousands of containers internationally every year. The company has a worldwide presence, with offices in North, Central and South America, including in Mexico and Brazil; Asia, in China and Japan; and Europe, in Switzerland. PMI Hong Kong Food Services Ltd is the Hong Kong office of PMI.
PMI, through its Hong Kong Food Services Ltd office, is one of China's top importers of beef from Brazil, ranking as the number one company responsible for over 25% of total imports from Brazil in 2013. It also imports beef from other countries, including Mexico.

Emami Ltd. was founded in 1974 and is a leading personal and healthcare business headquartered in India. Through its subsidiaries it has a presence in a numerous markets and in various segments of the supply chain. One of its subsidiaries, Emami Biotech Ltd., is a key trader and processor of a range of raw materials, including oil palm, soybeans and jatropha. Emami Biotech has been central to the growth of India's capability in the biodiesel market, with the installation of the largest biodiesel plant in eastern India at Haldia. This plant has recently been upgraded so that it can process 2,000 tonnes of soybean and palm oil per day. This complements another refinery in Andhra Pradesh which adds a further 1,200 tonnes per day for the production of palm and sunflower oils. To further fill Emami's down-market needs, Emami Biotech imports a large amount of raw product into India, with over 4% of the total Indian market share in crude palm oil imports.
In terms of upstream activities, Emani Biotech owns a plantation in Ethiopia for the production of edible and non-edible oils and is looking to purchase plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia. In recent years, Emami Biotech has invested in the development of its marketing network to distribute its products under its Healthy and Tasty brand. Through this network, the company is able to supply goods to over 4,500 distributors and 12,000 retailers. Another subsidiary of Emami is Starmark, which owns a chain of seven retail stores in Kolkata and Chennai. These retail stores sell a range of books, toys, music and stationary. The sale of stationary and books is complemented by the production of newsprint, writing and printing paper by another subsidiary, Emami Paper Mills Ltd. Emami Paper Mills manufacturers these products from waste paper in two plants, one in Orissa and the other in Kolkata.

OJSC Magnit is a Russian holding company, operating in the Russian food retail sector. Magnit is an Open Joint Stock Company (OJSC) and is among Russia's largest retailers. The company operates four types of stores: Magnit convenience stores, of which it runs almost 7700; Magnit hypermarkets, of which it has 170; Magnit Family stores, of which is operates over 60; and Magnit cosmetics stores, of which it runs 816.
The company began in household chemical wholesale in the mid-1990s, and has since expanded into the retail market. Today it ranks as the top retailer in the Russian market in terms of its sales and its presence across Russia, and employs around 230,000 people. Magnit produces around 700 private label products for its stores, amounting to 13% of total sales in 2012. Included in Magnit's ranges of goods are a variety of meat products, including a range of unbranded and branded private label frozen and chilled meat products, including beef.
Between 2007 and 2012, Russia imported over 23% of Brazil's total beef exports, which accounted for around 40% of Russia's total beef and veal import market (in 2010); therefore, as a leading retailer and stockist of meat products in Russia, Magnit is at significant risk of supplying beef products linked to tropical deforestation. In 2009 Magnit began to import goods from abroad run by its subsidiary company Tander. By the end of 2013, company's import accounted for 10% of its turnover. During the first six months of 2014, Tander was in top 10 Russia's importers with total volume of import in amount of $830.58 million.

The Vicwood Group is a Hong Kong based timber company manufacturing plywood, parquet and other timber-based products. Alongside manufacturing facilities in China, the company also has forestry concessions and sawmills in Central Africa. In 2005, it had over 700,000 hectares in the Central African Republic and a further 1,000,000 hectares across Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Vicwood Group claims to have expanded on these 1.7 million hectares to now have forestry concessions covering a total area of about 2 million hectares as of 2016. It is one of the largest forestry concession operators in Cameroon.

Amul is an Indian dairy company operating throughout India that manufactures products such as milk, butter, cheese, ice-cream, and other food and beverages. The company also produces its own cattle feed. These products involve significant amounts of palm oil and soya, as well as paper for packaging. It is one of the largest companies in India by market share for packaged food, dairy, and ice-cream and frozen desserts. Additionally, it is among the top five Indian companies by market share for oils and fats.

Bright Food Group (Bright Food) is a Chinese food industry group involved in agriculture, food processing, and manufacturing, as well as retailing. It is involved in diverse business areas, but its main food businesses include packaged foods, dairy, sugar and vegetables. The group is a major player in China ranking highly in several categories, including dairy and packaged foods. It is also a global player, ranking among the top ten in the world for dairy and the top twenty for packaged foods.

rows.coprofile: The Corporación De Abastecimiento Y Servicios Agrícolas S.A. (CASA) is a Venezuelan state-owned food company, involved in the purchasing and supply of food and agricultural products. The company is the main supplier of the state-owned retailer MERCAL, involving it in the purchase of a variety of basic foodstuffs, including dry milk, beans, vegetable oils and margarine. It is also one of the top importers of Brazilian beef. CASA also sells own-brand products such as lentils, dry milk and vegetable oils.

The Vicwood Group claims to have expanded on these 1.7 million hectares to now have forestry concessions covering a total area of about 2 million hectares as of 2016. It is one of the largest forestry concession operators in Cameroon.

Groupe Lactalis is a French company specialising in dairy products, including milk powder and nutrition products, cheese, liquid milk, fats and chilled dairy goods. The company, originally known as Societe Laitiere Besnier, was established in 1939 and changed its name to Groupe Lactalis S.A. in 1999. Visible in 150 countries and with on the ground operations in 70 countries (as of 2011), Lactalis has grown to have a global presence and ranks itself the world's leading dairy group. The company employs around 61,000 people and operates a total of 200 industrial plants.  The majority of its operations are in Europe, where it employs almost 40,000 people, however it is active worldwide, with operations in America, Africa and Asia/Oceania.  In September 2014, the Group, through its Parmalat subsidiary, agreed to buy the dairy units of Brazilian food company BRF, and has also agreed to buy units of Brazilian dairy company, LBR-Lacteos (which previously held license to use the Parmalat brand name in Brazil).
The group's branded products include President cheese, Rachel's yoghurt, Roquefort Socieite and Munch Bunch. It also has a long history with Nestle and took over a subsidiary, Claudel Roustang, in 1985. In 2006 Groupe Lactalis and Nestle created a subsidiary, Lactalis Nestle, which deals with Nestle's fresh dairy produce and owns yoghurt brands, Munch Bunch and Ski, in the UK. In addition to its recognisable dairy brands, Groupe Lactalis also provides ingredients for industry, including whey products, lactose and milk powder, to be used in the manufacture of products such as ice-cream, ready meals and confectionery.
Groupe Lactalis also uses palm oil in some of its products. For example, its Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division, produces butters, creams and margarines, some of which contain palm oil, as do the products of the Lactalis Nutrition Sante division. The Lactalis Beurres & Cremes division does not currently measure how much palm oil it uses but it plans to start sourcing RSPO-certified oil palm products in 2015 and to be using 100% RSPO-certified oil palm by 2018 (on own-brand products). Further to this, some of Groupe Lactalis products also contain soya.

It is one of the top five footwear manufactures in China and is also among the top fifteen retailers of footwear in China and Hong Kong by brand share.

Darmex Agro Holdings is a private holding company also known as Duta Palma, after the subsidiary through which it was established in 1987, Dutapalma Nusantara. It is one of the largest palm oil producers and traders in Indonesia and, in 2012, the subsidiary Duta Palma Nusantara Group was ranked among the top 100 groups in Indonesia. The group has a total of seven subsidiaries and both upstream and downstream operations.
As of 2009, it had around 155,000 hectares of oil palm plantations in Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo, and Riau, in Sumatra, as well as 8 palm oil mills in the provinces of Riau, Jambi and Kalimantan, with a combined monthly production capacity of 36,000 metric tonnes of crude palm oil (CPO). Much of the CPO produced is further processed in Darmex Agro Holdings' refineries in order to produce palm derivatives, including palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) and refined bleached and deodorised palm stearin and palm oil (RBDPS and RBDPO) . Further to these core business divisions, Darmex Agro Holdings has expanded its business to cover other processing, storage and shipping activities.

Belle International Holdings is a Chinese business primarily involved in the manufacturing and retail of footwear and apparel. It owns several brands including Belle, Staccato, and Tata, and manufactures shoes for other brands including Clarks and Mephisto. Its apparel business is focussed on retail distribution, including with brands such as Nike, Adidas, and Puma. It is one of the largest global footwear manufacturers and is also one of the largest Chinese shoe stores.

Yunnan Huijia Import & Export Co Ltd is a privately owned company based in China. In 2012, it was the biggest importer of palm oil in China, and it continues to be one of the country's largest importers of palm oil. The company imports and exports palm oil, edible oil, animal feed and other agricultural products, including soya bean meal. Yunnan Huijia Import & Export Co Ltd is one of several subsidiaries of the Huijia Group, which imports feedstuffs, carries out domestic trading, processes feedstuffs, and engages in genetics and breeding.
Yunnan Huijia Import & Export Co Ltd has direct cooperative relations with producers and suppliers in America, Canada, Australia, Singapore, Vietnam, Uruguay, Peru, Chile and Hong Kong. These include the billion dollar agreements signed in 2013 between Huijia Group and Malaysia's 101 Group, and between Yunnan Huijia Import & Export Co Ltd and Singapore-based Wilmar international Ltd.

Samsonite International SA is a US based luggage company involved in the design, manufacturing, marketing and sale of luggage and travel accessories. Its products include luggage, business accessories, such as laptop cases, and outdoor and casual bags. The company was established in 1910 in the state of Colorado, and has since grown to be a leader in the luggage and bags industry; manufacturing products under multiple brands and selling them worldwide.
The company's products are sold under several brands, including Samsonite, American Tourister, High Sierra, Hartmann, Lipault, and Speck, as well as other owned and licensed brand names. Samsonite International claims to be the largest travel luggage company in the world, and in 2013 sold its products through over 46,000 sales points in more than 100 countries worldwide. The company is one of the few luggage groups to sell its products across the globe, in North America, Europe, Latin America, and throughout Asia, including India and China. In 2012, at 12%, Samsonite International occupied the largest market share in the global luggage industry, making it three times larger than its closest competitor.  Several of Samsonite International's brands produce leather products, such as the Business Leather line under the Samsonite brand, as well as business cases, tote bags and other leather accessories under the Hartmann brand.
Samsonite's products are predominantly manufactured in Asia. The company outsources around 94% of its manufacturing, with manufacturing facilities in China producing up to 84% of the total, and the rest produced throughout Asia, predominantly in Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Thailand.

X5 Retail Group NV is a Russian food retailer, with retail operations in four different formats and brands: Economy stores under the Pyaterochka brand (4,789 stores); supermarkets under the Perekrestok brand (403 stores); hypermarkets under the Karusel brand (82 stores); convenience stores under a range of different brand names (209 stores); and an online retail channel under the E5.ru brand. The company has its origins in 1995, when the Perekrestok supermarket brand was established. The chain of Pyaterochka stores was launched a few years later in 1999, and in 2006 these two brands merged and adopted the X5 Retail Group NV name.
X5 Retail Group's Pyaterochka economy convenience stores provide over 69% of the group's total revenue in 2014 . The Group has been steadily increasing its marketing of private label products and, through its various retail formats, offers a wide range of products, including dairy products, canned goods and groceries, confectionery and bakery products, and fresh and processed meat, among others.

This is turned into meal and oil for food products and edible oils. It is also a leading importer of Brazilian soya. In 2014, it imported over 8 million metric tons of soya, accounting for almost 15% of Chinese imports.

JVL Agro Industries Ltd (JVL), formally Jhunjhunwala Vanaspati Limited, is an Indian edible oil manufacturer. The company was incorporated in 1989, and was established initially in Northern India as a manufacturer of hydrogenated vegetable oils and refined oils, with the capacity to produce around 25 tonnes per day. The company has since grown to be the largest vegetable oil manufacturer in the country, with four plants producing 300 tonnes a day, with products including palm oil and soya bean oil.
The company's mid- and downstream activities require a large amount of raw material, therefore JVL are responsible for around 5% of India's total crude palm oil imports. JVL is also taking steps to acquire new land in Indonesia and Ethiopia for the production of palm oil and, as of 2013, had signed an agreement for the use of 12,500 acres of land in Ethiopia, with the potential of extending this to 62,000 acres.
JVL has a number of brands under which products are distributed to the consumer market across 18 Indian states. For example, refined soya bean oil is sold under the Jhoola health brand, while blended oils are sold under the Joohi active brand. JVL are working towards the development of rapid revenue growth partly by diversifying into new markets. For example, in 2012, they began to market bakery products, and in 2013-14 were set to commission a rice mill in Bihar with a production capacity of 12 metric tonnes per hour.

China's furniture industry is the country's highest export earner of all finished timber products and a significant consumer of timber, using around 19 million cubic metres (roundwood equivalent) in 2010. Dalian Huafeng Furniture Co. Ltd. is a Chinese furniture manufacturer, established in 1952 and located in the city of Zhuanghe in Dalian, China. The company claims to be the largest furniture manufacturer in China and to have the largest storage base for raw materials of the furniture industry globally. By market share it is also the largest manufacturer of wooden furniture, producing around 10 million units of furniture, including bedroom, dining room, living room, office, and hotel furniture per annum.
As well as supplying the domestic market, through its 300 stores, Dalian Huafeng Furniture also exports products to Japan, the US, Europe and Southeast Asia via a specialised industrial zone established in 2002. Despite its long history in the Chinese market, the company only became a prominent exporter of furniture products in 2000, when it became established in the US export market. The company continues to increase its presence in the export market, for example, with plans to open 300 stores in the US in five years from 2012.
Dalian Huafeng Furniture has expanded its furniture manufacturing operations to include production of wooden boards into its business activities. This was achieved in 2008 through a partnership with Jilin Forest Industry Co. Ltd., which manufactures and markets a range of timber products.

rows.coname: Guangdong Wens Foodstuff Group Co., Ltd
rows.coprofile:
Guangdong Wen's Group is a Chinese agricultural company. Founded in 1983 by seven farmers, it is active in a variety of sectors including research and development; animal feed production; poultry and pig farming; food processing; bio-pharmaceuticals; real estate development; industrial investment; and other activities relating to the agricultural sector. The group is comprised of around 160 subsidiaries, employs some 3.68 million workers and is active across 23 Chinese provinces.
Guangdong Wen's Group is active throughout the agricultural supply chain. The group is also one of the ten largest animal feed manufacturers globally, producing close to 10 million metric tons of feed annually. As well as being a top producer of animal feed, it is among the largest pig and poultry producers in China and therefore also a large buyer of animal feed products, including soybean and corn. It also provides livestock and agricultural equipment to farmers and produces a range of milk products, and cooked and chilled foods for consumers.

Wings Corp are a manufacturer of soaps and detergents, including personal care products and are exposed to palm oil and soy. It operates in Indonesia, Nigeria and the Philippines as well as internationally.  Wings Corp is selected as a powerbroker for palm oil and is also assessed for its exposure to soy and paper packaging.

Darmex Agro Holdings is a private holding company also known as Duta Palma, after the subsidiary through which it was established in 1987, Dutapalma Nusantara. It is one of the largest palm oil producers and traders in Indonesia and, in 2012, the subsidiary Duta Palma Nusantara Group was ranked among the top 100 groups in Indonesia. The group has a total of seven subsidiaries and both upstream and downstream operations.
As of 2009, it had around 155,000 hectares of oil palm plantations in Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo, and Riau, in Sumatra, as well as 8 palm oil mills in the provinces of Riau, Jambi and Kalimantan, with a combined monthly production capacity of 36,000 metric tonnes of crude palm oil (CPO). Much of the CPO produced is further processed in Darmex Agro Holdings' refineries in order to produce palm derivatives, including palm fatty acid distillate (PFAD) and refined bleached and deodorised palm stearin and palm oil (RBDPS and RBDPO) . Further to these core business divisions, Darmex Agro Holdings has expanded its business to cover other processing, storage and shipping activities.

The Vicwood Group is a Hong Kong based timber company manufacturing plywood, parquet and other timber-based products. Alongside manufacturing facilities in China, the company also has forestry concessions and sawmills in Central Africa. In 2005, it had over 700,000 hectares in the Central African Republic and a further 1,000,000 hectares across Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Vicwood Group claims to have expanded on these 1.7 million hectares to now have forestry concessions covering a total area of about 2 million hectares as of 2016. It is one of the largest forestry concession operators in Cameroon.

A high proportion of timber in China is consumed in the industrial and construction sector, which accounted for over 75% of total wood consumption in 2010. Shanghai Construction Group ranks as the second largest construction firm in China in terms of market share and as well as playing a key role in China's domestic construction industry, the group is active overseas, having completed more than 100 projects in 30 different countries and regions worldwide. In 2013, the group's overseas activities contributed over 15% to its total revenue. It is comprised of a number of subsidiaries and business departments. It has 17 subsidiaries involved in construction, engineering, real estate and landscaping, and 13 supporting business departments. The group also provides engineering and renovation services and has further business interests, for example in trading through its import and export operations. Shanghai Construction Group is a state-owned enterprise, whose majority shareholder is the Shanghai Municipal Government.
The group as a whole has been active in the Chinese construction sector for over fifty years. Shanghai Construction Group's subsidiary, Shanghai Construction Co Ltd, is involved exclusively in construction. It was established in 1994 and was listed on Shanghai stock exchange in 1998. The company is engaged in contracting, designing and constructing a variety of projects; including the development of residential, industrial, and municipal buildings, and public infrastructure facilities.
China's affordable housing programme aims for the construction of 36 million units of affordable housing in the five years leading up to 2015, as part of the country's 12th five-year plan. It is expected that the government's housing plan will drive increasing consumption and imports of wood products. Shanghai Construction Group has previously been involved in this programme, for example with the Sanlin Affordable Housing Development.
